title: fix(cli): raw stack trace on ConfigNotFoundError instead of friendly message
body:
## Issue

`ao session ls` (and other subcommands that call `loadConfig()`) throws a raw Node.js stack trace when `agent-orchestrator.yaml` is missing. The error message is helpful — `No agent-orchestrator.yaml found. Run 'ao start' to create one.` — but it is buried in an unreadable stack trace. The CLI should catch known error types and display a clean, actionable message instead.

## Environment

- AO version: `0.2.2`
- OS: macOS 26.4
- Node.js: `v22.22.1`

## Evidence

![User runs ao session ls](https://github.com/yyovil/storage/releases/download/agent-orchestrator%2F981/agent-orchestrator-__s03__final-state.png)

Here's the [**video proof**](https://github.com/yyovil/storage/releases/download/agent-orchestrator%2F981/agent-orchestrator-__recording.mp4)

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the fix spec for AI agents.

## Steps

1. **Read `packages/cli/src/index.ts`** and `packages/cli/src/program.ts` to understand the CLI entrypoint and how `createProgram()` works.

2. **Edit `packages/cli/src/index.ts`** to use `parseAsync()` with a `.catch()` handler:
   ```typescript
   #!/usr/bin/env node

   import { ConfigNotFoundError } from "@composio/ao-core";
   import { createProgram } from "./program.js";

   createProgram()
     .parseAsync()
     .catch((err) => {
       if (err instanceof ConfigNotFoundError) {
         console.error(err.message);
         process.exit(1);
       }
       throw err;
     });
   ```
   - Use `parseAsync()` instead of `parse()` so the promise chain works.
   - Only catch `ConfigNotFoundError` — re-throw everything else so other errors still surface with full stack traces.
   - No chalk styling needed — the message is already descriptive.

3. **Verify** that `createProgram()` returns a Commander `Command` instance that supports `parseAsync()`. Read `packages/cli/src/program.ts` to confirm.

4. **Run `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-cli typecheck`** to confirm no type errors.

5. **Test manually:** rename `agent-orchestrator.yaml` out of the way, run `ao session ls`, confirm a single clean error line with no stack trace, then restore the file.

## Constraints

- Do not touch unrelated files.
- Prefer minimal, surgical edits.
- The global handler in `index.ts` should only catch `ConfigNotFoundError` (and any other error subclasses that set a user-facing `.message`). Unknown errors should still throw with their full stack trace for debugging.
- Do not add error handling inside individual command action handlers — a single top-level handler is the correct fix.
- Note follow-up work separately instead of expanding scope inside this issue.

## Acceptance

Running `ao session ls` in a directory without `agent-orchestrator.yaml` prints:

```
Error: No agent-orchestrator.yaml found. Run `ao start` to create one.
```

No stack trace. Exit code 1.

## Problem

When running `ao start` in an unconfigured repo, there's no guided setup flow. Running `ao start --init` fails with `error: unknown option '--init'`.

- **Agent (non-interactive):** `ao start` should detect the missing config and print a clear message telling the agent to run `ao init` first, then exit with a non-zero code.

### Interactive (TTY detected)
```
$ ao start
No agent-orchestrator.yaml found. Would you like to initialize? (Y/n) y

```

$ ao start
Error: No agent-orchestrator.yaml found. Run `ao init` first to configure.
```

## Current Behavior

```
$ ao start --init
error: unknown option '--init'
```

No guidance is provided when config is missing.

Detection of human vs agent can use `process.stdout.isTTY` — if truthy, show interactive prompt; otherwise, print the command and exit.

title: ao start: clear stale Next.js cache on version upgrade
body:
## Problem

After upgrading `@aoagents/ao` via `npm install -g`, running `ao start` serves the old UI because Next.js uses a cached `.next` build from the previous version. Users have to manually find and delete the cache.

## Expected Behavior

`ao start` (or the npm postinstall hook) should detect a version mismatch and automatically clear the stale `.next` cache before starting the dashboard server.

## Suggested Fix

Either:
1. **postinstall hook**: In the `@aoagents/ao` or `@aoagents/ao-web` postinstall script, delete any existing `.next` cache directory so the next start uses the fresh build.
2. **ao start**: Before launching the web server, compare the cached build version (e.g. a `.next/BUILD_ID` or a stamped version file) against the current package version. If mismatched, wipe `.next` and rebuild/use the pre-built assets.

Option 1 is simpler and ensures the cache is always clean after install.

title: node-pty posix_spawnp failure on global install (npm/pnpm)
body:
## Problem

After installing `@aoagents/ao` globally via `npm install -g` or `pnpm add -g`, the web terminal fails with:

```
Error: posix_spawnp failed.
    at new UnixTerminal (node-pty/lib/unixTerminal.js:92:24)
```

This happens because `node-pty` ships a pre-built native binary that may not match the user's Node.js version or architecture. The repo has a `scripts/rebuild-node-pty.js` postinstall script, but it only runs for source installs — the published npm packages don't trigger a native rebuild on the consumer's machine.

## Who's affected

Any user installing globally, especially those using Node version managers (nvm, fnm, volta) where the runtime Node version differs from what the pre-built binary was compiled against.

## Current workaround

```bash
cd $(npm root -g)/node-pty  # or pnpm equivalent
npx node-gyp rebuild
```

## Suggested fix

Add a `postinstall` script to the published `@aoagents/ao` or `@aoagents/ao-web` package that runs `node-gyp rebuild` on `node-pty` if the pre-built binary fails a sanity check. Something like:

```js
try {
  require('node-pty');
} catch (e) {
  // Pre-built binary doesn't work, trigger rebuild
  execSync('npx node-gyp rebuild', { cwd: path.dirname(require.resolve('node-pty/package.json')) });
}
```

This ensures the native binary always matches the user's Node.js version after install.

title: Orchestrator session immediately marked as 'killed' despite running fine
fix: prevent race condition marking new sessions as killed
body:
## Why

New orchestrator (and worker) sessions are immediately marked as "killed" / "Exited" in the dashboard even though the tmux session and agent are running fine. This is a race condition between session creation and the first lifecycle poll.

## What

- Add a 60-second startup grace period in `agent-claude-code` `getActivityState()`
- If `isProcessRunning()` returns false but the session was created less than 60s ago, return `"idle"` instead of `"exited"` to give the agent process time to launch
- Updated tests to cover both the grace period case and the post-grace-period exited case

## Root Cause

1. `spawnOrchestrator()` creates tmux session and writes `status=working`
2. Lifecycle worker polls within seconds
3. `runtime.isAlive()` → tmux exists → `true` ✅
4. `agent.getActivityState()` → `findClaudeProcess()` scans `ps` for `claude` on the TTY → Claude hasn't started yet → returns `null`
5. `isProcessRunning()` returns `false` → returns `{ state: "exited" }`
6. Lifecycle manager writes `status=killed` to metadata
7. Dashboard shows "Exited"

## How to Test

1. `ao start` in a configured repo
2. New orchestrator session should show "Working" or "Idle" instead of "Exited"
3. Run tests: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test`

Fixes #989

title: web terminal UI breaks when interacted with terminal on mobile
ao start spawns duplicate orchestrator sessions on every run
body:
## Problem

Every time `ao start` is run, it spawns a brand new orchestrator session (`int-orchestrator`, `int-orchestrator-1`, `int-orchestrator-2`, etc.) without checking if a previous orchestrator is already running. The dashboard ends up showing multiple orchestrator sessions, most of which are stale or redundant.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ao start` → spawns `int-orchestrator`
2. Kill the `ao` process (Ctrl-C), tmux session survives
3. `ao start` again → spawns `int-orchestrator-1` (does NOT reuse the existing one)
4. Repeat → `int-orchestrator-2`, etc.
5. Dashboard shows all of them

## Expected Behavior

`ao start` should:
1. Check if an orchestrator session already exists for this project
2. If the tmux session is alive, reattach/reuse it instead of spawning a new one
3. If the tmux session is dead but metadata exists, clean up the stale metadata first
4. Only spawn a new orchestrator if none exists

## Current Behavior

```
$ tmux list-sessions | grep orchestrator
8474d6f29887-integrator-orchestrator: 1 windows (created Wed Mar 11)
c13a0108f64e-int-orchestrator: 1 windows (created Tue Apr 7 20:37)
c13a0108f64e-int-orchestrator-1: 1 windows (created Tue Apr 7 20:48)
c13a0108f64e-int-orchestrator-2: 1 windows (created Tue Apr 7 20:50)

title: feat(windows): cross-platform adapter (platform.ts)
body:
Parent: #956

## What

Create `packages/core/src/platform.ts` with 6 functions that centralize all platform-branching logic. Export from `packages/core/src/index.ts`.

This is the foundation for all other Windows compatibility work. Every other sub-issue imports from this module instead of doing ad-hoc `process.platform` checks.

## Functions

- `isWindows(): boolean`
- `getDefaultRuntime(): "tmux" | "process"`
- `getShell(): { cmd: string, args: (command: string) => string[] }` — resolves pwsh > powershell.exe > cmd.exe on Windows, `$SHELL` or `/bin/sh` on Unix
- `killProcessTree(pid, signal): Promise<void>` — `taskkill /T /F /PID` on Windows, `process.kill(-pid)` on Unix
- `findPidByPort(port): Promise<string | null>` — `netstat -ano` on Windows, `lsof -ti` on Unix
- `getEnvDefaults(): { HOME, SHELL, TMPDIR, PATH, USER }` — platform-appropriate defaults

## Files

- Create: `packages/core/src/platform.ts`
- Create: `packages/core/src/__tests__/platform.test.ts`
- Modify: `packages/core/src/index.ts` (add exports)

## Tests (`packages/core/src/__tests__/platform.test.ts`)

- `isWindows()` returns true on win32, false on linux
- `getDefaultRuntime()` returns "process" on win32, "tmux" on linux
- `getShell()` returns sh/bash on Unix, pwsh/powershell/cmd on win32
- `getShell()` pwsh > powershell.exe > cmd.exe fallback chain
- `killProcessTree()` calls `process.kill(-pid)` on Unix
- `killProcessTree()` calls `taskkill` on win32
- `killProcessTree()` handles already-dead process without throwing
- `findPidByPort()` calls `lsof` on Unix
- `findPidByPort()` calls `netstat` on win32
- `findPidByPort()` returns null when port not in use
- `getEnvDefaults()` returns Unix paths on linux
- `getEnvDefaults()` returns Windows paths on win32

## Design constraints

- Zero behavior change on Linux/macOS. Every function returns existing Unix behavior on non-Windows.
- No new dependencies. Uses Node built-ins (`child_process`, `os`) and Windows system tools (`taskkill`, `netstat`).
- Shell resolution is cached after first call for performance.
- `_resetShellCache()` exported for testing.

title: fix(windows): skip tmux preflight + per-project runtime check
body:
Parent: #956
Depends on: #993

## What

Two related fixes in the CLI startup path:

1. `start.ts:919` has a hardcoded fallback `config.defaults?.runtime ?? "tmux"` that should use `getDefaultRuntime()` from the platform adapter. On Windows with no explicit runtime, this causes `ensureTmux()` to be called unnecessarily.

2. (B21) `start.ts:919` only checks `config.defaults.runtime`, not per-project runtime. If a project has `runtime: tmux` explicitly set on Windows, `ensureTmux()` won't fire and the user gets a confusing error later.

Note: `spawn.ts:74` already gates correctly (`if (runtime === "tmux")`) — no change needed there. B03 from the original proposal is not a real blocker.

## Current behavior

On Windows with no explicit runtime in config, the fallback resolves to `"tmux"` and `ensureTmux()` is called, which hard-exits with a WSL install hint.

## Expected behavior

- On Windows with no explicit runtime, fallback resolves to `"process"` and `ensureTmux()` is skipped.
- If any project has `runtime: tmux`, `ensureTmux()` fires with the early warning.

## Files

- Modify: `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` (line 919, change fallback + add per-project check)

## Tests

- Modify: `packages/cli/__tests__/commands/start.test.ts`
  - `ensureTmux()` is NOT called when platform is win32 and no explicit runtime is set
  - `ensureTmux()` IS called when runtime is explicitly "tmux" on any platform

feat: file lock registry — detect and warn on cross-session file conflicts
body:
## Problem

Multiple interns edit the same files (e.g., `LapTimingViewModel.kt`, `strings.xml`), causing merge conflicts when their branches are rebased. During the 2026-04-06 marathon, multiple interns independently fixed the same gnssSatelliteProvider mock.

## Solution

Track which files each session modifies in a SQLite table. Warn at spawn time if files overlap with other active sessions. Clear locks when sessions reach terminal status.

## Implementation

### File 1: `packages/core/src/session-db.ts`

Add to `SCHEMA_SQL` (~line 410):
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS file_locks (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  file_path TEXT NOT NULL,
  first_seen TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  UNIQUE(session_id, file_path)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_file_locks_session ON file_locks(session_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_file_locks_active ON file_locks(file_path);
```

Add CRUD functions:
- `updateFileLocks(sessionId, files[])` — upsert modified files (INSERT OR IGNORE, in transaction)
- `getConflictingFiles(sessionId)` — returns `{ file, heldBy }[]` for files held by OTHER active sessions
- `clearFileLocks(sessionId)` — DELETE all locks for session

### File 2: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-switch.ts`

In `handleImplementing()`, after detecting commits (~line 158):
```typescript
const { stdout } = await execFileAsync("git", [
  "diff", "--name-only", `origin/${defaultBranch}..HEAD`,
], { cwd: row.workspace_path!, timeout: 5_000 });
const files = stdout.trim().split("\n").filter(Boolean);
if (files.length > 0) updateFileLocks(row.id, files);
```

In terminal transitions (merged, killed): call `clearFileLocks(row.id)`

### File 3: `packages/core/src/services/session-spawn.ts`

After worktree creation, before agent launch:
```typescript
const conflicts = getConflictingFiles(sessionId);
if (conflicts.length > 0) {
  const fileList = conflicts.map(c => `  ${c.file} (held by ${c.heldBy})`).join("\n");
  console.warn(`[spawn] ${sessionId}: potential file conflicts:\n${fileList}`);
}
```

### File 4: CLI visibility

Add to `ao status` or new `ao file-locks <project>` command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `file_locks` table created on DB init
- [ ] `updateFileLocks()` populates table from `git diff --name-only`
- [ ] `getConflictingFiles()` returns overlapping files from other active sessions
- [ ] `clearFileLocks()` removes all locks for a session
- [ ] Spawn logs warning when file conflicts detected
- [ ] Locks cleared on merged/killed transitions
- [ ] Unit tests for CRUD functions
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm typecheck` passes

## Files

- `packages/core/src/session-db.ts`
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-switch.ts`
- `packages/core/src/services/session-spawn.ts`
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-db.test.ts` or new test file
- `packages/cli/src/commands/` (status or new command)

title: feat(core): add worker session persistence on respawn
body:
## Summary

Closes #899

When an AO worker session dies (crash, rate limit, OOM, manual kill) and a new worker is spawned for the same issue, the new worker previously started completely from scratch — zero conversation history, no knowledge of previous attempts, no awareness of commits already made. This PR fixes that by teaching `spawn()` to detect previous sessions and resume them, using a three-tier fallback chain.

## Problem

AO already had a fully working session restore system (`ao session restore <id>`), but it was only available as a manual CLI command. The automated respawn path (`spawn()`) completely ignored it — always calling `getLaunchCommand()` fresh, never checking for previous sessions, and never reusing workspaces. Additionally, after a machine crash/restart, sessions stuck in `working` state were never detected or recovered.

## What Changed

### 1. Resume Fallback Chain in `spawn()` (core)

`spawn()` now implements a three-tier fallback before launching a new agent:

```
1. Is workerRespawnStrategy "fresh"? → skip everything, launch fresh
2. Does a previous archived session exist for this issue + agent?
   → NO → launch fresh
   → YES ↓
3. Is session resumable (killed/errored/terminated) AND agent has getRestoreCommand()?
   → YES → native resume (claude --resume, codex resume, opencode --session)
   → NO ↓
4. Build context from archived metadata + git history
   → Context available → prepend to prompt, launch with context
   → No context → launch completely fresh
```

**Key design decision:** Archive lookup runs BEFORE workspace creation. When resuming, `workspace.restore()` recreates the worktree from the existing branch (preserving commits and worktree path), which is critical for agents like Codex that match session files by CWD.

### 2. `findArchivedSessionForIssue()` Helper (core)

New general-purpose function in `session-manager.ts` that searches archived sessions by issue ID and agent name with status filtering:

- **Resumable** (`killed`, `errored`, `terminated`): eligible for native resume + context injection
- **Completed** (`done`, `cleanup`): eligible for context injection only (uses "check for review feedback" language)
- **Merged**: excluded entirely — work already landed

### 3. Context Injection Module (core — new file)

`packages/core/src/session-context-builder.ts` — `buildPreviousSessionContext()` extracts a structured context summary from archived metadata:

- Previous session status and agent summary (capped at 500 chars)
- Git commits on the branch (`origin/{defaultBranch}..HEAD`, capped at 10)
- PR link and status
- Tailored instructions: "completed" sessions get "check for review feedback", interrupted sessions get "do NOT start over"
- Total context capped at 4000 chars to stay within ARG_MAX

### 4. Active Session Dedup Guard (core)

`spawn()` now checks for existing active sessions with the same `issueId` before any resource allocation. Prevents spawning duplicate workers that would make conflicting commits on the same branch. Uses `isOrchestratorSessionRecord()` to exclude orchestrator sessions. Agent name comparison falls back to `config.defaults.agent` for sessions without a persisted agent name.

### 5. Per-Project Configuration (core)

New `workerRespawnStrategy` field in `ProjectConfig`:

```yaml
projects:
  my-app:
    workerRespawnStrategy: "resume"   # default — try native resume, fall back to context injection
    # workerRespawnStrategy: "context-inject"  # skip native resume, always inject context
    # workerRespawnStrategy: "fresh"           # always start fresh (previous behavior)
```

Added to both the TypeScript type (`types.ts`) and Zod validation schema (`config.ts`).

### 6. Session Lineage Tracking (core)

`spawn()` writes a `resumedFrom` metadata field when resuming from a previous session, creating a lineage chain: `app-3` → `app-2` → `app-1`.

### 7. Machine-Restart Persistence (core + cli)

**Dead session recovery** (`recoverDeadSessions` in `lifecycle-manager.ts`):
- On lifecycle-worker startup, scans all active (non-terminal) sessions
- Skips PR-managed sessions (`pr_open`, `review_pending`, `changes_requested`, `approved`, `mergeable`, `ci_failed`) — lifecycle poll tracks these via PR state, not a running agent
- Skips orchestrator sessions (role check, suffix check, `prefix-orchestrator-N` regex)
- Checks if the agent process is still running via runtime + agent plugin
- Dead sessions → transition to `terminated`, archive metadata
- Pre-checks for existing active sessions before respawning (prevents dedup conflicts)
- Auto-respawns dead sessions that had an `issueId` — the resume chain above kicks in automatically

**System service** (`ao service install/uninstall` in `service.ts`):
- Generates and installs launchd plist (macOS) or systemd unit (Linux)
- Lifecycle-worker auto-starts on boot, triggering dead-session recovery
- Proper escaping: XML entities for plist, `%%` for systemd percent specifiers, `$$` for dollar signs
- Uses canonical `sanitizeProjectId` from core for consistent service naming

### 8. OpenCode `getRestoreCommand()` (plugin)

OpenCode agent plugin now implements `getRestoreCommand()`, using `--session <id>` for native session resume. Looks up session ID from metadata first, falls back to `findOpenCodeSession()` API.

## Files Changed

| Area | Files | What |
|------|-------|------|
| **Core engine** | `session-manager.ts` | `findArchivedSessionForIssue()`, dedup guard, resume chain in `spawn()` |
| | `session-context-builder.ts` | **New** — context extraction from archived sessions |
| | `lifecycle-manager.ts` | `recoverDeadSessions()` with pre-check and auto-respawn |
| | `types.ts` | `workerRespawnStrategy`, `RESUMABLE_STATUSES`, `PR_MANAGED_STATUSES` |
| | `config.ts` | Zod schema for `workerRespawnStrategy` |
| | `metadata.ts` | `resumedFrom` field |
| **CLI** | `service.ts` | **New** — `ao service install/uninstall/status` |
| | `lifecycle-worker.ts` | Boot-time dead-session recovery integration |
| **Plugin** | `agent-opencode/index.ts` | `getRestoreCommand()` implementation |
| **Tests** | `spawn-resume.test.ts` | 31+ test cases for resume chain |
| | `session-context-builder.test.ts` | 13+ test cases for context extraction |
| | `lifecycle-recovery.test.ts` | 15+ test cases for dead-session recovery |
| | `service.test.ts`, `service-command.test.ts` | 61+ test cases for service management |
| | `lifecycle-worker.test.ts` | 5 test cases for CLI integration |
| | `config-validation.test.ts` | Schema validation tests |

## Test Plan

- [x] `findArchivedSessionForIssue()` — matches by issue+agent, filters merged, picks most recent
- [x] `buildPreviousSessionContext()` — includes status/summary/commits/PR, caps lengths, different language for done vs interrupted
- [x] Active session dedup guard — throws on duplicate, allows different issues, no resources created on rejection
- [x] `spawn()` resume chain — native resume → context injection → fresh launch for all three strategies
- [x] `workerRespawnStrategy` config — accepts valid values, rejects invalid, defaults to undefined
- [x] `recoverDeadSessions()` — skips terminal/PR-managed/orchestrator sessions, archives dead ones, auto-respawns
- [x] Service generation — correct plist/systemd output, proper escaping, install/uninstall/status commands
- [x] All CI checks passing (lint, typecheck, test, integration tests, diff coverage)

title: Follow-ups for file based communication protocol
body:
Follow up to #968. Tracks the next part of the work that was scoped out of the initial transport PR to keep it focused. None of these blocks the v1 file-based protocol while all of them build on top of it.

## Scoped out of #968

### 1. Orchestrator-side context injection
A background process in the orchestrator agent session that watches event files and injects them into the orchestrator's context. The current AO orchestrator is a Node daemon, not an agent with a context window, so the framing needs a design pass before implementation. Tied to the broader \"orchestrator as an agent\" question.

### 2. `comms.json` for user-spawned runtimes
The original issue mentioned a `comms.json` file for runtime discovery when sessions are spawned outside AO. Deferred — needs its own design.

### 3. Cross-runtime sidecar
The inbox sidecar (`fs.watch` on `inbox.jsonl` with single-writer mutex) currently lives inside `runtime-file`. To get the same idle-delivery behavior for `runtime-tmux` and any future runtime, the sidecar should be lifted into a shared layer (probably `runtime-process` base or session-manager).

### 4. Epoch replay on respawn
Inbox messages carry an `epoch` field but we don't currently re-deliver missed messages when an agent restarts mid-session. After a respawn, the sidecar should replay entries since the last acknowledged ID.

### 5. Activity log specification
`activity.jsonl` exists and is written to, but the schema isn't formally documented and there's no consumer reading it for analytics or stuck-detection beyond the existing fallback path.

## New Phase 2 features

### 6. Message TTL / expiry
Inbox entries get an `expiresAt` field. The sidecar skips expired messages. Enables semantics like \"fix this CI failure within 10 min or escalate.\"

### 7. Priority queue in inbox
`priority: \"urgent\"` field on inbox entries. Sidecar drains urgent messages before normal-priority ones, regardless of id order.

### 8. Backpressure
If `lastDeliveredId` falls more than N behind the latest write, pause new sends and notify a human. Signals that the agent isn't keeping up.

### 9. Inbox archival / rotation
When `inbox.jsonl` exceeds a size threshold, rotate to `inbox.jsonl.1` and start fresh. Required eventually because the file grows unbounded.

### 10. Cross-session messaging
Agent A writes to Agent B's inbox via a `target_session` field. Enables agent-to-agent coordination without orchestrator routing.

### 11. Replay on agent restart
When an agent respawns, re-deliver inbox entries from the last-acked ID, not from the epoch start. Related to # 4 above, but specifically about the ack contract.

### 12. Structured tool input in events
`agent-events.jsonl` carries richer data so the lifecycle worker can make smarter routing decisions (e.g. \"agent failed because dependency X is missing\" -> auto-install reaction).

### 13. Dedup by content hash
Currently, dedup keys are random. Switching to content hashes would automatically collapse identical messages.

## Phase 3: coordination and reliability

### 14. File conflict detection beyond rebase
The auto-rebase coordinator handles file overlap on merge. Phase 3 would add proactive conflict detection — warn agents in real time when they're about to touch a file another agent is already modifying.

### 15. Cross runtime support for Codex turn-steer / OpenCode plugins
Codex has a `turn/steer` JSON-RPC method for mid-turn redirects. OpenCode has a plugin tool hook. Both could be wired to the inbox sidecar for richer interruption semantics.

Refs #853, #968

title: feat(windows): Node.js metadata wrappers + pwsh shell for runtime-process
body:
Parent: #956
Depends on: #993

## What

Two related blockers that prevent agents from functioning on Windows:

### B16: Wrapper scripts are bash-only

`packages/core/src/agent-workspace-hooks.ts` generates ~/.ao/bin/gh and ~/.ao/bin/git as bash scripts. These intercept git/gh commands to write metadata (PR tracking, branch info). Without them, PRs created by agents don't appear in the dashboard.

On Windows: bash doesn't exist, : PATH delimiter is wrong (Windows uses ;), /tmp and /usr/bin don't exist.

**Fix:** Dual wrapper generation. On Unix, emit bash scripts (unchanged). On Windows, emit Node.js wrapper scripts with .cmd shims.

### B18: Launch commands use bash $(cat ...) substitution

runtime-process spawns with shell: true (line 64) which resolves to cmd.exe on Windows. Agent launch commands use $(cat file) which is bash syntax.

**Fix:** Change shell: true to shell: getShell().cmd. On Windows this gives pwsh, which supports $(cat file) natively.

## Files

- Modify: packages/core/src/agent-workspace-hooks.ts (wrapper generation, PATH delimiter)
- Modify: packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/index.ts (line 64, shell option)

## Tests

- packages/core/src/__tests__/agent-workspace-hooks.test.ts
  - On win32, generates .cmd shims and .js wrapper scripts (not bash)
  - Node.js wrapper writes metadata JSONL and forwards to real binary
  - PATH delimiter is ; on win32, : on Unix
  - On Unix, generates bash scripts (existing behavior preserved)
- packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/__tests__/index.test.ts
  - Spawns with pwsh (or resolved shell) on win32
  - Spawns with shell: true on Unix (existing behavior preserved)

title: feat(windows): Node.js metadata hook for Claude Code
body:
Parent: #956
Depends on: #993

## What

The Claude Code PostToolUse hook is a bash script that uses jq, grep, sed, tr, and chmod 0o755 to update session metadata. None of these work on Windows.

Evidence:
- packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:34 - METADATA_UPDATER_SCRIPT starts with #!/usr/bin/env bash
- Line 576 - await chmod(hookScriptPath, 0o755) (Unix file permissions)
- Lines 619-624 - Script body uses set -euo pipefail, jq, grep, sed, tr

Without this hook, Claude Code sessions on Windows won't update metadata (summary, cost, PR status).

## Fix

Generate a Node.js hook script on Windows instead of bash. The hook does JSON parsing and file writes, which Node.js handles with built-ins (JSON.parse, fs.writeFileSync). No external tools needed.

On Unix: keep existing bash hook (unchanged).
On Windows: write Node.js script, skip chmod (Windows uses file extension for executability).

## Files

- Modify: packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts (setupWorkspaceHooks method)

## Tests (packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/__tests__/index.test.ts)

- On win32, writes a Node.js hook script (starts with #!/usr/bin/env node, no bash-isms)
- On win32, does NOT call chmod
- On Unix, writes bash hook script (existing behavior preserved)
- On Unix, calls chmod 0o755 (existing behavior preserved)
- Node.js hook correctly parses metadata JSON and writes updates

title: fix(windows): project builds on Windows (cp -r + Next.js EPERM)
body:
Parent: #956

## What

Two build failures prevent the project from compiling on native Windows.

### 1. CLI build uses Unix cp command

packages/cli/package.json uses cp -r to copy assets, which is not available on Windows cmd.exe.

Error: 'cp' is not recognized as an internal or external command

Fix: Replace with Node.js built-in fs.cpSync (available Node 16+):

"build": "tsc && node -e \"require('fs').cpSync('src/assets','dist/assets',{recursive:true})\""

### 2. Next.js webpack hits EPERM on Windows home directory junctions

Next.js scans the user home directory during transpilePackages resolution and hits
C:\Users\<user>\Application Data, a legacy Windows junction point that denies access.

Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, scandir 'C:\Users\priya\Application Data'

Fix: Add webpack snapshot config to next.config.js that limits module scanning on Windows:

webpack: (config) => {
  if (process.platform === "win32") {
    config.snapshot = {
      ...config.snapshot,
      managedPaths: [/^(.+?[\\/]node_modules[\\/])/],
    };
  }
  return config;
},

## Files

- Modify: packages/cli/package.json (line 28, build script)
- Modify: packages/web/next.config.js (add webpack config)

## Tests

- pnpm build completes successfully on Windows
- pnpm build still completes successfully on Linux/macOS (no behavior change)
- Both fixes are gated: cpSync is cross-platform, webpack change only activates on win32

## Note

23 packages also have "clean": "rm -rf dist" which fails on Windows cmd.exe.
Not blocking (clean is manual, not part of build pipeline). Can be fixed separately
by replacing with node -e "require('fs').rmSync('dist',{recursive:true,force:true})".

Fixes #986. After upgrading `@composio/ao` via npm, `ao start` served the old dashboard UI because Next.js runtime cache (`.next/cache`) persisted from the previous version.

title: feat(windows): complete Windows support
body:
## Summary

Adds first-class Windows support to AO. Same `ao` install, same dashboard, same agents — Windows users get all of it natively without WSL.

110 commits, ~9k LOC across 140 files. Zero behaviour change on macOS / Linux: every Windows path is gated behind `isWindows()`, and the existing `runtime-tmux` + bash hook flows are untouched.

## What is new

**Cross-platform core (`packages/core/src/platform.ts`)** — the single home for every platform branch. Exports: `isWindows`, `getDefaultRuntime` (`process` on Windows, `tmux` elsewhere), `getShell` (pwsh → powershell.exe → cmd.exe with `AO_SHELL` override), `killProcessTree` (`taskkill /T /F` vs POSIX group kill), `findPidByPort` (`netstat -ano` vs `lsof`), `getEnvDefaults` (USERPROFILE / TEMP / USERNAME). Path equality helpers (`pathsEqual`, `canonicalCompareKey`) handle NTFS case-insensitivity.

**Native PTY via ConPTY** — `runtime-process` is the default runtime on Windows. Each session owns a small detached **pty-host** helper process (`packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/pty-host.ts`) that wraps a `node-pty` ConPTY behind a named pipe (`\\.\pipe\ao-pty-<sessionId>`). Binary 8-message frame protocol with chunked input (≤512-char pieces, 15ms gaps) to dodge ConPTY input-buffer truncation, 1000-line rolling output buffer for scrollback-on-attach, full signal interception so `conpty_console_list_agent.exe` does not orphan and trigger WER `0x800700e8`. Pty-hosts register in `~/.agent-orchestrator/windows-pty-hosts.json` so `ao stop` can reach detached children that `taskkill /T` cannot. `sweepWindowsPtyHosts()` cooperatively kills, polls (with EPERM-vs-ESRCH disambiguation), then force-kills stragglers.

**Mux WS Windows branch** — `handleWindowsPipeMessage` in `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` relays terminal traffic to/from named pipes, scoped by `(projectId, sessionId)`. `direct-terminal-ws.ts` skips tmux entirely on Windows. `resolvePipePath` reads each session's metadata (V2 layout with V1 fallback) to find its pipe.

**Shell + script-runner** — `getShell()` everywhere we used to assume `/bin/sh`. `script-runner.ts` runs `.ps1` siblings of `.sh` scripts via PowerShell (`-File` mode, not `-Command`); falls through to `AO_BASH_PATH` / Git Bash (WSL bash explicitly excluded — wrong filesystem semantics). New `ao-doctor.ps1` / `ao-update.ps1` shipped, both invoked transparently by `ao doctor` / `ao update` on Windows.

**Agent plugins** — every agent (claude-code, codex, kimicode, aider, opencode, cursor) updated for Windows. PATH wrappers (`gh`, `git`) are now `.cjs` + `.cmd` shims via `setupPathWrapperWorkspace` instead of bash scripts. Claude Code's PostToolUse metadata-updater is a `.cjs` Node script (no bash/jq/grep/sed). Codex/kimicode prepend `& ` to launch commands so PowerShell parses quoted absolute binary paths as call expressions. `systemPromptFile` content is inlined as `--append-system-prompt` (no `$(cat …)`). `detect()` calls use `shell: isWindows()` + `windowsHide: true`. `isProcessRunning` short-circuits POSIX-only paths and applies EPERM-aware signal-0 probing. Cursor-specific stderr suppression. Drive-letter slug encoding preserved (`C:` → `C-`) so Claude Code's session-JSONL lookup works.

**CLI** — `ao start` no longer detaches the dashboard child on Windows (Ctrl+C reaches the whole console group natively). `ao stop` calls `sweepWindowsPtyHosts()` before tearing down the parent. `startup-preflight` offers to switch the YAML config from `runtime: tmux` to `runtime: process` on Windows. `winget install --id Git.Git` for Windows Git install hints. Worktree `rmSync` gets a retry loop for file-handle drain races. Multi-merge race conditions in pipe-relay close hardened.

## Docs

- `docs/CROSS_PLATFORM.md` — full developer reference. Golden Rule (no raw `process.platform` checks; use `isWindows()`), complete helper inventory with import paths, EPERM-vs-ESRCH pattern, PowerShell/bash differences, IPv6 `localhost` stalls, agent-plugin specifics, 10-point pre-merge checklist.
- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` — Cross-Platform sections with the helper quick-reference, point at `CROSS_PLATFORM.md`.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — new "Windows Runtime Architecture" section (pty-host mermaid, pipe protocol message-type table, registry, sweep, Windows process map). All existing diagrams updated to show both runtimes.
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/BUGBOT.md`, `packages/core/README.md`, `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/README.md`, `packages/core/src/prompts/orchestrator.md` — outdated tmux/POSIX-only claims removed.
- `README.md`, `SETUP.md`, `docs/CLI.md` — Quick-Start prerequisites split per OS, runtime defaults annotated, Remote Access section flags Linux/Windows as no-ops for `power.preventIdleSleep`, `tmux not found` troubleshooting includes a Windows clause.
- `skills/agent-orchestrator/SKILL.md` — declares Windows support (`os: ["darwin", "linux", "win32"]`), drops tmux from required bins.

## Behaviour on existing platforms

Zero regression intended. All Windows code paths gated by `isWindows()`. Shell, runtime, agent, and CLI changes either branch cleanly or are opt-in via config. No new dependencies on Unix.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all packages
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm test` — Linux CI green
- [ ] Live test on macOS (reviewer)
- [ ] Live test on Linux (reviewer)
- [x] Live test on Windows — author has been dogfooding throughout

## Related

Closes #993, #994, #995, #998, #999, #1014, #1015, #1019. Incorporates earlier Windows PRs in the series (#1028, #1031, #1032, #1033) plus follow-ups.

title: Fix/shared terminal resize
body:
Closes #991 

## Summary
Fixes a shared terminal resize bug when the same session is open on multiple devices at once.

## Root cause

The direct terminal WebSocket server treated every connected viewer as resize-authoritative for the same tmux session. Each client sent its own `cols/rows`, and the server immediately applied that resize to the PTY. With a narrow mobile viewport and a wide desktop viewport attached to the same session, the mobile resize could override the desktop layout.

## What changed

- `packages/web/server/direct-terminal-ws.ts`
  - track multiple viewers per AO session instead of assuming a single active viewer
  - keep per-viewer terminal dimensions
  - compute a shared terminal size across connected viewers
  - apply the largest connected viewport size instead of letting a smaller viewer shrink the session for everyone
  - keep compatibility with existing `activeSessions` behavior by maintaining a representative session entry

- `packages/web/server/__tests__/direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts`
  - added a regression test covering a wide desktop viewer and a narrower mobile viewer connected to the same session
  - verifies that a smaller second resize does not collapse the shared terminal size

## Why this fixes the bug

A smaller mobile viewer is no longer allowed to reduce the effective tmux size seen by a larger desktop viewer. The shared session stays sized for the largest connected viewport, which prevents the desktop terminal from collapsing when the mobile terminal is used.

## Testing

```bash
pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web exec vitest run server/__tests__/direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts
pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web build

title: spawn: branch/worktree conflict gives no recovery path when re-spawning an existing issue
body:
## Summary

When `ao spawn <issue>` is interrupted (process killed, terminal closed, tracker fetch fails mid-flow) **after** the worktree has already been created but **before** the session reaches a stable state, the next `ao spawn <issue>` attempt hard-fails with:

```
✗ Failed to checkout branch "feat/issue-9215" in worktree:
  Command failed: git checkout feat/issue-9215
  fatal: 'feat/issue-9215' is already used by worktree at '/home/priyanshu/.worktrees/sktime/skt-1'
```

There is no recovery path. The user is stuck:

- `ao spawn <issue>` → fails with the worktree conflict error
- The agent may have already done meaningful work in that worktree


---

## Root Cause

The spawn flow creates the worktree early (step 4 of \`session-manager.ts:spawn()\`), but session metadata is written much later (step 8). If anything fails in between — or if the user interrupts the process — the worktree remains on disk with no corresponding session record.

On a retry:

1. \`sm.spawn()\` computes the same branch name (e.g. \`feat/issue-9215\`) from the issue ID
2. The workspace-worktree plugin's \`create()\` hits the \`"already exists"\` branch in its fallback path
3. \`git worktree add {newPath} {baseRef}\` + \`git checkout {branch}\` — this fails if \`{branch}\` is **already checked out** in the orphaned worktree
4. The plugin throws, spawn aborts — no cleanup, no guidance

Batch-spawn deduplication only checks existing **session metadata** for the issue ID. It does not check git for existing branches or worktrees, so orphaned worktrees are invisible to it.

---

## Affected Scenarios

Scenario A — Orphaned worktree, no session metadata
Scenario B — Session in terminal state, worktree still on disk
Scenario C — Multiple stale worktrees for the same issue
Scenario D — Tracker fetch fails after worktree is created


---


## Steps to Reproduce



1. Spawn an issue where the tracker repo has issues disabled
```
ao spawn 9215   # fails mid-way; worktree created at ~/.worktrees/sktime/skt-1
```

2. Try again
```
ao spawn 9215
# ✗ Failed to checkout branch "feat/issue-9215" in worktree:
#   fatal: 'feat/issue-9215' is already used by worktree at '/home/priyanshu/.worktrees/sktime/skt-1'
```

**Manual workaround until fixed:**
```
git worktree remove ~/.worktrees/sktime/skt-1 --force
git branch -D feat/issue-9215
ao spawn 9215
```

title: feat(web): intuitive kbd shortcuts for dashboard navigation
body:
> [!CAUTION]
> This issue is **WIP**. Agent is working on making kbd shortcuts feel most intuitive.

## Issue

We need kbd shortcuts so bad to navigate the dashboard. Everything(reaching to the worker agents terminal to start prompting, shifting from one terminal to another, know project status) is 2-3 clicks away.

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the implementation spec for AI agents.

## V1 Shortcuts

| # | Action | Shortcut | Rationale |
|---|--------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | Go to all projects | `g p` | Two-key sequence (à la GitHub). `g` = "go to", `p` = "projects". No OS conflict. Single keys like `p` are too easy to misfire. |
| 2 | Toggle fullscreen terminal | `f` | Mnemonic, no OS conflict. Single key is fine — it's a toggle on a view you're already looking at, low misfire risk. |
| 3 | Switch sessions (command panel) | `Mod+k` | Universal command palette shortcut (VS Code, Slack, Linear). `react-hotkeys-hook` supports `mod+k` natively — maps to Cmd on macOS, Ctrl on Windows/Linux. Use `preventDefault` to override browser address bar focus. |
| 4 | Show shortcuts | `?` | Industry standard (GitHub, Gmail, YouTube). Requires Shift on most layouts, hard to hit accidentally. |
| 5 | Toggle theme | `g t` | "Go to" sequence — `t` for theme. Infrequent action, so a sequence prevents accidental triggers. |
| 6 | View PRs for current project | `g r` | "Go to" sequence — `r` for review/PRs. Fits the `g` prefix pattern. |
| 7 | Toggle sidebar | `[` | Matches VS Code convention. Visually suggestive of a collapsing panel. Single key is fine — structural toggle, easy to undo. |

### Cross-platform design decisions

- **No `Cmd+w/s/c/v/t/n`** — all browser-reserved, would cause poor UX
- **`g + _` sequences** are safe everywhere — two plain keys, no modifier, no OS meaning
- **`Mod+k`** is the only modifier combo — justified because command palette is universally expected at this binding. `react-hotkeys-hook` handles the Cmd/Ctrl abstraction natively
- All keys exist on every standard keyboard layout

## Steps

1. Install `react-hotkeys-hook` in `packages/web`:
   ```bash
   pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web add react-hotkeys-hook
   ```

2. Create `packages/web/src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts` — registers all 7 bindings via `useHotkeys`. All shortcuts must be disabled when focus is inside `<input>`, `<textarea>`, or `contentEditable`.

3. Wire the hook into the layout component that wraps all dashboard views.

4. Create `packages/web/src/components/CommandPanel.tsx` — session switcher opened by `Mod+k`. Lists orchestrator and worker sessions, supports fuzzy text filtering, navigates on Enter, closes on Escape. Call `preventDefault` on the key event.

5. Create `packages/web/src/components/KeyboardShortcutsHelp.tsx` — modal overlay listing all bindings. Dismissed with Escape or `?` again.

6. Add tests (see Testing section below).

7. Verify:
   ```bash
   pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web typecheck && pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test
   ```

## Testing

**Stack:** Vitest 2.1 + jsdom + `fireEvent.keyDown` from `@testing-library/react` (matches existing repo patterns — no `user-event`).

**Do NOT mock `react-hotkeys-hook`.** Let it bind real `keydown` listeners on jsdom's `document`. Mocking the library means testing the mock, not the shortcuts. The only mocks needed are `next/navigation` (same `vi.mock` pattern used across all existing component tests) and callback props.

### `packages/web/src/hooks/__tests__/useKeyboardShortcuts.test.ts`

Hook unit tests. Use `renderHook` + `fireEvent.keyDown(document, ...)`.

| # | Test case | Fire | Assert |
|---|-----------|------|--------|
| 1 | `g p` navigates to all projects | `keyDown {key:"g"}` then `keyDown {key:"p"}` | `router.push` called with projects path |
| 2 | `g r` navigates to PRs | `keyDown {key:"g"}` then `keyDown {key:"r"}` | `router.push` called with PRs path |
| 3 | `g t` toggles theme | `keyDown {key:"g"}` then `keyDown {key:"t"}` | theme toggle callback invoked |
| 4 | `f` toggles fullscreen terminal | `keyDown {key:"f"}` | fullscreen callback invoked |
| 5 | `[` toggles sidebar | `keyDown {key:"["}` | sidebar callback invoked |
| 6 | `?` opens shortcuts overlay | `keyDown {key:"?"}` | overlay callback invoked |
| 7 | `Mod+k` opens command panel (Ctrl) | `keyDown {key:"k", ctrlKey:true}` | panel callback invoked |
| 8 | `Mod+k` opens command panel (Meta) | `keyDown {key:"k", metaKey:true}` | panel callback invoked |
| 9 | sequence timeout — `g` then 600ms then `p` | `keyDown {key:"g"}`, `vi.advanceTimersByTime(600)`, `keyDown {key:"p"}` | nothing happens |
| 10 | inert when `<input>` focused | render `<input>`, focus it, fire all shortcuts on it | no callbacks invoked |
| 11 | inert when `<textarea>` focused | render `<textarea>`, focus it, fire all shortcuts on it | no callbacks invoked |

### `packages/web/src/components/__tests__/KeyboardShortcutsHelp.test.tsx`

| # | Test case | Assert |
|---|-----------|--------|
| 1 | renders all 7 shortcuts with correct keys and descriptions | screen.getByText for each shortcut |
| 2 | Escape closes the overlay | fire `keyDown {key:"Escape"}`, verify `onClose` called |
| 3 | `?` closes the overlay | fire `keyDown {key:"?"}`, verify `onClose` called |
| 4 | does not render when closed | pass `isOpen={false}`, verify nothing in DOM |

### `packages/web/src/components/__tests__/CommandPanel.test.tsx`

| # | Test case | Assert |
|---|-----------|--------|
| 1 | renders session list (orchestrator + worker) | sessions visible in list |
| 2 | filters sessions on text input | type in search, verify list narrows to matches |
| 3 | Enter on selected session navigates | `router.push` called with session path |
| 4 | Escape closes the panel | verify `onClose` called |
| 5 | empty state when no sessions match filter | "no results" message visible |

### CI risk & mitigation

`react-hotkeys-hook` attaches `document.addEventListener("keydown", ...)`. If listeners leak across test suites, shortcuts from one test fire in another. **Mitigation:** each test uses `renderHook`/`render` and relies on React's cleanup on unmount. Add an explicit `afterEach(() => cleanup())` if flakiness appears.

## Constraints

- Write as less verbose code.
- Do not add any UI component library (constraint C-01).
- No inline `style=` attributes — Tailwind utility classes only.
- Dark theme must be preserved (constraint C-05).
- Component files max 400 lines (constraint C-04).
- Test files for all new components (constraint C-12).
- Shortcuts must be inert when a text input is focused.
- No `Cmd+<letter>` or `Ctrl+<letter>` combos beyond `Mod+k`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `g p` navigates to the all-projects view.
- [ ] `f` toggles fullscreen terminal on session detail view.
- [ ] `Mod+k` opens command panel to fuzzy-search and switch sessions; Escape closes it.
- [ ] `?` opens help overlay listing all 7 shortcuts; `?` or Escape dismisses it.
- [ ] `g t` toggles light/dark theme.
- [ ] `g r` navigates to the PRs view for the current project.
- [ ] `[` toggles the sidebar.
- [ ] All shortcuts are inert when focus is in a text input.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web typecheck` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test` passes — all 20 new tests green.

title: Dashboard should expose exact session state and memory state directly, without requiring terminal commands or orchestrator prompts
body:
## Summary

  AO currently has the underlying data needed to understand session lifecycle state, but the user experience is still too terminal-centric and orchestrator-dependent.

  In practice, I had to:

  - inspect session metadata files directly
  - run ao status
  - ask the orchestrator/agent to show status

  This should instead be visible directly in the dashboard.

  ## Problem

  The underlying session metadata already contains important fields such as:

  - session status
  - activity
  - PR URL
  - branch
  - agent
  - memory artifacts on disk

  But the dashboard does not make these states first-class or obvious enough for normal operation.

  As a result:

  - users need to go through Claude/Codex or the terminal to understand what AO is doing
  - status debugging is harder than it should be
  - memory behavior is opaque even though the data exists on disk

  ## Expected behavior

  The dashboard should directly show, per session:

  - exact session status
  - exact activity state
  - PR URL / PR number
  - branch
  - agent
  - whether session memory exists
  - whether project memory exists
  - latest memory extraction outcome / failure reason if extraction failed

  This should be visible without:

  - asking the orchestrator agent
  - inspecting metadata files manually
  - relying on ao status output only

  ## Why this matters

  AO already has a state machine and metadata model.
  The issue is visibility, not missing backend state.

  If the dashboard exposed this directly:

  - users could trust AO state without terminal debugging
  - memory-system debugging would be much easier
  - status mismatches would be easier to spot
  - the product would feel like an orchestrator, not a thin wrapper around tmux and CLI commands

  ## Suggested improvements

  1. Add explicit session status and activity fields side-by-side in the dashboard.
  2. Add a memory section per session:
      - session memory exists / missing
      - extraction last succeeded / failed
      - failure reason
  3. Add project memory summary per project:
      - file exists / missing
      - session count
      - last updated timestamp
  4. Make PR state and lifecycle state clearer:
      - working
      - pr_open
      - ci_failed
      - changes_requested
      - approved
      - mergeable
      - merged
  5. Show the data directly from AO metadata/state instead of expecting users to ask the orchestrator session.

  ## Current impact observed

  In testing, it was difficult to tell from the UI alone:

  - whether a session had reached a memory-triggering status
  - whether memory extraction had run
  - whether extraction failed
  - whether session memory and project memory files were actually created

  The data existed, but the dashboard did not surface it clearly enough.

title: Existing orchestrator sessions do not pick up agent changes from agent-orchestrator.yaml
body:
## Summary

  If the configured agent is changed in agent-orchestrator.yaml, existing orchestrator sessions continue running with the old agent instead of picking up the new configuration.

  This makes the config change appear ineffective until the old orchestrator session is manually killed and a new one is started.

  ## Repro

  1. Start AO with a project configured to use one agent, for example:
      - defaults.agent: claude-code
  2. Let AO create an orchestrator session.
  3. Change the config to use a different agent, for example:
      - defaults.agent: codex
        or
      - projects.<id>.orchestrator.agent: codex
  4. Restart with ao start.
  5. Observe that the existing orchestrator session is reused and still runs with the old agent.

  ## Actual behavior

  - Existing orchestrator sessions keep the agent they were originally created with.
  - Config changes to orchestrator agent selection are not applied to already-running orchestrators.
  - From the user perspective, changing YAML does not seem to work.

  ## Expected behavior

  One of the following should happen clearly and consistently:

  1. AO should recreate the orchestrator when the configured orchestrator agent changes.
  2. Or AO should warn clearly that an existing orchestrator is pinned to the old agent.
  3. Or AO should expose a first-class command/flow to refresh the orchestrator from current config.

  ## Why this matters

  Users expect agent-orchestrator.yaml to be the source of truth for orchestrator behavior.

  Right now:

  - the persisted old orchestrator session effectively overrides the new config
  - the system feels inconsistent
  - debugging is confusing, especially when switching between Claude and Codex due to limits or testing

  ## Suspected cause

  ao start prefers reusing an existing non-terminal orchestrator session for the project, and that session already has persisted metadata including the agent it was launched with.

  As a result, the new YAML config is not applied to that existing orchestrator instance.

  ## Suggested fixes

  - Detect orchestrator agent config drift and recreate the orchestrator automatically.
  - Or print a clear message like:
      - “Existing orchestrator is using claude-code; config now requests codex. Kill/recreate to apply changes.”
  - Or add a --refresh-orchestrator / --recreate-orchestrator option to ao start.
  - Consider making orchestrator reuse conditional on config compatibility, not just session existence.

title: ao spawn --decompose crashes when Anthropic API key is unset
body:
## Problem
Running `ao spawn <issue> --decompose` without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set crashes the entire process instead of failing gracefully.

### Reproduction
```bash
ao spawn 843 --decompose
```

### Actual behavior
```text
✗ Could not resolve authentication method. Expected either apiKey or authToken to be set.
```

### Notes
- The decomposition path currently depends on Anthropic authentication being present in the environment.
- In practice this means `--decompose` can hard-fail before a session is created when the key is missing.
- The current behavior is abrupt and gives no fallback behavior for users who can otherwise use `ao spawn` successfully.

title: ao spawn --decompose creates multiple branches and PRs for one issue
body:
## Problem
When `ao spawn --decompose` splits a single issue into subtasks, each leaf agent creates its own branch and PR.

### Observed behavior
For one issue, the decomposition flow can produce multiple PRs such as:

```text
Issue #42 → PR #101 (feat/42-ao-1)
          → PR #102 (feat/42-ao-2)
          → PR #103 (feat/42-ao-3)
```

### Why this is a problem
- Multiple PRs are linked to one issue, which makes issue tracking messy.
- Reviewers have to review several PRs in the correct order.
- Merges become sequential and brittle because later PRs can depend on earlier ones landing cleanly.
- Git history for one issue ends up fragmented across multiple branches.

title: fix(web): stale .next cache causes false PageNotFoundError build failures
body:
## Problem

`pnpm build` (specifically `next build` for `@composio/ao-web`) intermittently fails with `PageNotFoundError` errors when the `.next` cache is stale. The errors reference API routes that actually exist in the source tree but aren't found during the "Collecting page data" phase.

### Error Output

```
[Error [PageNotFoundError]: Cannot find module for page: /api/issues] {
  code: 'ENOENT'
}
[Error [PageNotFoundError]: Cannot find module for page: /api/orchestrators] {
  code: 'ENOENT'
}
[Error [PageNotFoundError]: Cannot find module for page: /api/projects] {
  code: 'ENOENT'
}
> Build error occurred
[Error: Failed to collect page data for /api/issues] { type: 'Error' }
```

The specific routes that fail vary between runs — sometimes it's `/api/issues`, `/api/orchestrators`, `/api/projects`; other times it's `/api/runtime/terminal`, `/api/prs/[id]/merge`, `/api/sessions/[id]/kill`.

### Reproduction

1. Run `pnpm build` (succeeds on first clean build)
2. Checkout a different branch or merge new commits that modify API routes
3. Run `pnpm build` again without clearing `.next` cache

The build fails with `PageNotFoundError` for routes that were added/changed.

### Workaround

Delete `.next` cache before building:

```bash
rm -rf packages/web/.next
pnpm build
```

### Root Cause

Next.js 15's build cache retains route manifests from previous builds. When new API routes are added (e.g., `/api/orchestrators` from PR #886, error boundaries from PR #929), the stale cache conflicts with the new route structure during the "Collecting page data" phase.

### Suggested Fix

Add a `prebuild` script to `packages/web/package.json` that cleans the `.next` directory:

```json
"prebuild": "rm -rf .next"
```

Or add `.next` cleanup to the CI workflow before the build step.

### Environment

- Next.js 15.5.12
- Node.js 20+
- macOS (also reproducible in CI)

### Impact

- Blocks `pnpm build` for contributors working across branches
- Can cause CI false positives if cache leaks between workflow runs
- Web unit tests (`pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test`) are not affected — only `next build`

title: fix(web): critical dependency warning from dynamic import in plugin-registry.js
body:
## Problem

`next build` emits a **"Critical dependency: the request of a dependency is an expression"** warning twice during compilation. This is triggered by dynamic `import()` calls in `packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts` where the package name is a runtime variable.

### Warning Output

```
⚠ Compiled with warnings

../core/dist/plugin-registry.js
Critical dependency: the request of a dependency is an expression

Import trace for requested module:
../core/dist/plugin-registry.js
../core/dist/index.js
./src/app/api/orchestrators/route.ts
```

The warning appears twice (once per `import()` site in plugin-registry.ts).

### Root Cause

`plugin-registry.ts` has two dynamic import sites where the package specifier is a variable:

```typescript
// Line 389 — loadBuiltins()
const doImport = importFn ?? ((pkg: string) => import(pkg));
// ...
mod = normalizeImportedPluginModule(await doImport(builtin.pkg));

// Line 421 — loadFromConfig()
const doImport = importFn ?? ((pkg: string) => import(pkg));
```

Webpack (used by Next.js) cannot statically analyze `import(pkg)` when `pkg` is a variable, so it flags it as a critical dependency. This is expected behavior for a plugin system that discovers packages at runtime.

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator.git
cd agent-orchestrator
pnpm install
pnpm build  # or: pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web build
# Observe "Critical dependency" warnings in output
```

### Impact

- **Build warnings** — clutters CI output, makes it harder to spot real issues
- **No runtime impact** — the dynamic imports work correctly at runtime since these are server-side API routes
- The warning appears on every build, cannot be suppressed without changes

### Suggested Fix

Options (in order of least invasive):

1. **Suppress the webpack warning** in `next.config.js`:
   ```js
   webpack: (config) => {
     config.module.exprContextCritical = false;
     return config;
   }
   ```

2. **Add `@composio/ao-core` to `serverExternalPackages`** — it's already there (`"@composio/core"` is listed but the actual package is `@composio/ao-core`). The current entry `"@composio/core"` may be incorrect. Marking core as external would prevent webpack from bundling it and eliminate the warning.

3. **Use `createRequire()` instead of dynamic `import()`** for the plugin loading path when running in the web context.

### Environment

- Next.js 15.5.12
- Webpack 5 (via Next.js)
- `packages/web/next.config.js` has `serverExternalPackages: ["@composio/core"]` but the actual package name is `@composio/ao-core`

title: fix(web): tracker-linear cannot resolve @composio/core during next build
body:
## Problem

`next build` emits a **"Module not found: Can't resolve '@composio/core'"** warning from `tracker-linear/dist/index.js`. The tracker-linear plugin has `@composio/core` (the Composio SDK, not `@composio/ao-core`) as an optional peer dependency that it dynamically imports at runtime, but webpack tries to resolve it at build time and fails.

### Warning Output

```
../plugins/tracker-linear/dist/index.js
Module not found: Can't resolve '@composio/core' in
  '/Users/dj/sj/agent-orchestrator/packages/plugins/tracker-linear/dist'

Import trace for requested module:
../plugins/tracker-linear/dist/index.js
./src/lib/services.ts
./src/app/api/orchestrators/route.ts
```

### Root Cause

`tracker-linear/src/index.ts` has a dynamic import for the optional Composio SDK:

```typescript
// Line 140
const { Composio } = await import("@composio/core");
```

This is intentionally optional — the plugin gracefully handles the missing dependency at runtime:

```typescript
} catch {
  throw new Error(
    "Composio SDK (@composio/core) is not installed. " +
    "Install it with: pnpm add @composio/core",
  );
}
```

However, the `tracker-linear` package is listed in `transpilePackages` in `next.config.js`, so webpack tries to resolve all its imports at build time, including the optional `@composio/core`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator.git
cd agent-orchestrator
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web build
# Observe "Module not found: Can't resolve '@composio/core'" warning
```

### Impact

- **Build warning** — does not block the build (compiled successfully despite the warning)
- **No runtime impact** — the import is wrapped in try/catch and only called when Linear tracker is configured with Composio auth
- Adds noise to CI output

### Suggested Fix

Options:

1. **Move `tracker-linear` to `serverExternalPackages`** instead of `transpilePackages` — prevents webpack from trying to bundle it and resolve its optional deps.

2. **Add `@composio/core` to `serverExternalPackages`** — it's already listed there but as `"@composio/core"`. Verify this is the correct package name the Composio SDK publishes under (not `@composio/ao-core`).

3. **Use a webpack `IgnorePlugin`** to skip resolution of `@composio/core` in the tracker-linear context:
   ```js
   webpack: (config) => {
     config.plugins.push(
       new webpack.IgnorePlugin({ resourceRegExp: /^@composio\/core$/ })
     );
     return config;
   }
   ```

### Environment

- Next.js 15.5.12
- `packages/web/next.config.js` lists `@composio/ao-plugin-tracker-linear` in `transpilePackages`
- `@composio/core` is NOT installed in the workspace (it's an external optional dep)

## Summary
- route configured self-hosted GitLab hosts through `GL_HOST` for non-API `glab` commands
- accept both `/-/issues/:id` and `/-/work_items/:id` when parsing GitLab issue URLs
- bundle the built-in GitLab SCM and tracker plugins in the CLI package so registry-backed commands can load them

Self-hosted GitLab issue commands were still resolving against `gitlab.com` because the shared helper only applied the configured host to `glab api`. Recent GitLab instances can also surface issue URLs under `/-/work_items/:id`, which broke issue parsing during creation and labeling.

title: Intermittent race: orchestrator session can be falsely marked killed during startup while tmux is still alive
body:
Summary
We observed an intermittent startup race where an orchestrator session is marked killed even though its tmux session is alive and the agent is still running. When this happens, the web session detail page shows Terminal session has ended for a live orchestrator.

This does not appear to be deterministic on every machine or every startup. It looks timing-dependent.

Symptoms
Orchestrator session detail page shows:
Terminal session has ended
tmux ls still shows the orchestrator session
tmux capture-pane shows the agent is alive and waiting at the prompt
Session metadata/API reports:
status: "killed"
activity: "exited"
Expected
If the orchestrator tmux session is alive, the session should remain non-terminal and the web UI should attach to the terminal normally.

Actual
A just-starting orchestrator can be transitioned to killed during startup, even though the backing tmux session is alive.

Repro
This appears to be intermittent and timing-sensitive, so repro is not guaranteed every time.

Probable repro path:

Start the app in optimized mode:
ao start
Let AO create or reuse an orchestrator session.
Open the orchestrator session page quickly:
http://localhost:3000/sessions/ao-orchestrator-<n>
If the race triggers, the page shows Terminal session has ended.
Verify the tmux session is actually alive:
tmux ls
tmux capture-pane -pt <tmux-session-name> | tail -40
Why this seems timing-dependent
The failure window seems to be during orchestrator startup, before its real runtime metadata is fully persisted but after the session is already visible to the lifecycle poller.

Suspected root cause
During orchestrator spawn, the session can exist briefly before its real runtime identity is fully written to metadata.

sessionManager can fabricate a temporary runtime handle while enriching/loading sessions. The lifecycle worker may then treat that temporary handle as a real runtime identity and run runtime.isAlive() against it.

If that fabricated handle does not map to the real tmux session yet, lifecycle can incorrectly conclude the session is dead and transition it to killed.

So the likely race is:

orchestrator session reserved / partially visible
lifecycle poll runs
temporary runtime handle is treated as authoritative
isAlive() returns false
lifecycle persists status=killed
UI then correctly renders the session as ended
Observed evidence
We observed cases where:

tmux session existed and was interactive
session API returned status: "killed"
lifecycle observability showed early transition like:
spawning -> killed
We also saw a suspicious timing pattern where lifecycle transitioned the session before the recorded createdAt timestamp that ended up in metadata, which further suggests a spawn/setup window race.

Scope
This appears to affect orchestrator startup specifically and may be more likely when:

using ao start in optimized/production-style mode
lifecycle worker is already running
startup timing causes polling to overlap with orchestrator creation
stale local AO state/worktrees/session records exist
Suggested fix
Lifecycle should only use runtime liveness checks when the runtime identity is actually persisted in metadata, for example via:

persisted runtimeHandle
persisted tmuxName
It should not treat temporary/fabricated runtime handles as authoritative during the spawn window.

Suggested regression coverage
Add tests for:

spawning/orchestrator session without persisted runtime metadata
lifecycle polling during startup
ensure such sessions do not transition to killed prematurely
ensure real persisted dead runtimes still transition to killed
Notes
This does not look like:

a tmux bug
a frontend-only bug
The frontend was reflecting persisted session state correctly. The incorrect terminal-ended state appears to originate in lifecycle/session startup coordination.

title: fix(web): correct xterm.js terminal width rendering in session detail
body:
## Summary

- **Remove padding from xterm container**: The `p-1.5` (6px) padding on the `terminalRef` div caused `FitAddon` to miscalculate column count because `clientWidth` includes padding but the terminal renders in the content area only.
- **Replace `window` resize listener with `ResizeObserver`**: The old `window.addEventListener('resize', ...)` only fired on window resizes, missing container-level changes like sidebar collapse or panel layout shifts. `ResizeObserver` observes the terminal container directly.
- **Defer initial `fit.fit()` with `requestAnimationFrame`**: Calling `fit.fit()` synchronously after `terminal.open()` can calculate dimensions before the DOM has fully settled. Deferring to the next animation frame ensures correct initial sizing.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a session detail page — terminal renders at correct width filling the container
- [ ] Resize the browser window — terminal reflows correctly
- [ ] Collapse/expand the sidebar — terminal reflows correctly without a window resize
- [ ] Verify no visual padding gap between terminal content and container edge
