title: feat: code-review plugin slot — AI-powered peer review for worker PRs (#1275)
body:
## Summary

Adds the **9th plugin slot** — `code-review` — to Agent Orchestrator. When a coding agent opens a PR, AO can auto-spawn a lightweight reviewer workspace (just a detached git worktree, no tmux/agent/runtime), run the configured CodeReview plugin in it, persist structured findings, and loop until the code is clean or a human intervenes.

Closes #1275 (the tracking issue for this feature).

## What's included

### Core (`packages/core/`)

- **Plugin slot types** (`types.ts`): `CodeReview` interface, `CodeReviewRun`, `CodeReviewFinding`, `CodeReviewThread`, `CodeReviewConfig`. `PluginSlot` and `ExternalPluginLocation` extended for the new slot.
- **Config** (`config.ts`): Zod `CodeReviewConfigSchema` on `ProjectConfig.codeReview` with `mode`, `prompt`, `autoSendNewFindingsToAgent`, `routing.publishToScm`, `limits` (`maxReviewRounds`, `maxBudgetPerRun`, `confidenceThreshold`, `stallWindow`), `severityThreshold`, `trigger.onPullRequestOpen/Update/manual`. External plugin collection honors the new slot.
- **Paths** (`paths.ts`): `getReviewsDir` and `getReviewWorkspacesDir` under the per-project base dir.
- **Plugin registry** (`plugin-registry.ts`): builtin `code-review-codex` registration; `updateConfigWithManifestName` handles the new `codeReview` project location.
- **Fingerprint + convergence** (`code-review-fingerprint.ts`): stable 16-hex `sha256(filePath\\0category\\0severity\\0anchor)` fingerprint, sliding-window union, stalled-detection per the spec, dismissal carry-forward.
- **Flat-file review store** (`review-store.ts`): CRUD for runs/findings/threads. Reviewer IDs (`{sessionPrefix}-rev-N`) allocated project-wide to prevent collisions across workers.
- **Review manager** (`review-manager.ts`): serializes at most one in-flight reviewer per worker+SHA, marks prior runs ``outdated``, creates detached reviewer worktrees, carries forward dismissed findings via fingerprint matching, runs convergence check, terminates with structured reasons (`cycle_cap`, `reviewer_failure`, `manual_cancel`, etc.), cleans up workspaces for done/stalled/failed runs (keeps `awaiting_context` alive for chat).
- **Lifecycle integration** (`lifecycle-manager.ts` + `code-review-trigger.ts`): generic `onSessionPolled` hook on `LifecycleManagerDeps` so the review manager can piggyback on the existing poll loop without entangling the lifecycle state machine in review internals. `createReviewTrigger` skips disabled/manual-only projects and dedupes per worker HEAD SHA via `git rev-parse`.

### Reference plugin (`packages/plugins/code-review-codex/`)

- Wraps `codex exec review --base <branch> --json`. Parses structured findings into `CodeReviewFindingInput` (flexible field mapping for codex/review shape drift). Maps P0/P1/P2/P3 priority to error/warning/info. Persists the codex session inside the reviewer workspace so `sendFollowUp` can reattach for chat.

### CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/review.ts`)

- `ao review run <session>` — trigger a review
- `ao review list [session]` — list review runs
- `ao review show <runId>` — display findings
- `ao review dismiss <runId> <findingId>` — dismiss (persists across re-reviews)
- `ao review send <runId> [findingId]` — route findings to the coding agent
- `ao review cancel <runId>` — terminate a running review

### Web (`packages/web/`)

- `services.ts` registers the Codex code-review plugin, builds a `ReviewManager`, and wires `createReviewTrigger` into the lifecycle's new `onSessionPolled` hook.
- `/reviews` page: 5-column Kanban (Running, Awaiting context, Done, Stalled, Terminated) grouped by `loopState` with finding previews.
- `GET /api/reviews` — list review runs with findings (filterable by project/session)
- `POST /api/reviews/runs` — manually trigger a review
- `PATCH /api/reviews/findings/[runId]/[findingId]` — dismiss/reopen/send actions

### Tests

- Core: fingerprint stability, reviewer ID allocation (project-scoped), store CRUD, triage carry-forward, convergence (including flip-flop detection)
- Codex plugin: manifest, JSON payload extraction, finding normalization, priority-to-severity mapping
- Full test run: **812 core tests** and **483 CLI tests** green.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` — all packages
- [ ] `pnpm test` — unit + integration
- [ ] `pnpm lint` — no new errors
- [ ] `ao review run <session>` works against a real codex install
- [ ] Review Workbench (`/reviews`) renders grouped runs with findings
- [ ] Dismissing a finding on one run keeps it dismissed on the next re-review for the same worker (fingerprint match)
- [ ] A stalled loop (`maxReviewRounds: 3` with no convergence) transitions to STALLED and records `terminationReason: cycle_cap`
- [ ] `awaiting_context` keeps the reviewer workspace; `done` / `stalled` / `failed` / `outdated` cleans it up

title: feat(cli): filter terminated sessions from ao session ls / ao status by default
body:
Closes #1310.

## Summary

- `ao session ls` and `ao status` now hide terminated sessions (`killed`, `terminated`, `done`, `merged`, `errored`, `cleanup`, plus lifecycle-driven terminal states like `runtime.state=exited` and `pr.state=merged`) by default.
- A dim footer reports how many were hidden: `N terminated sessions hidden. Use --include-terminated to show.`
- New flag `--include-terminated` on both commands restores the pre-change behavior.
- Keeps `-a, --all` orthogonal — it still only governs orchestrator visibility on `ao session ls`. Combine the two flags when you want both.

## Breaking change: JSON shape

`ao session ls --json` and `ao status --json` now emit `{ data: [...], meta: { hiddenTerminatedCount: number } }` instead of a bare array. Scripts consuming the JSON must read `.data`. `--include-terminated` restores the full data set and reports `hiddenTerminatedCount: 0`.

A Changeset entry (`.changeset/filter-terminated-sessions-from-ls.md`) calls this out as a minor bump with migration guidance. `SETUP.md` and `docs/CLI.md` updated to match the new shape and flag.

## Scope & rationale

- **CLI-only.** Does not touch lifecycle auto-archival (that's #536 — different risk surface, different rollback story).
- **`ao session restore <id>` unchanged.** That path goes through `sm.get`, not `sm.list`, so terminated sessions remain restorable by id.
- **`--watch` respects the filter each tick** (recomputes `hiddenTerminatedCount` each render so transitions to terminal state are reflected live).
- **Web dashboard unaffected** — already handled via `packages/web/src/lib/orchestrator-utils.ts`.

## Review input

Planned with `/codex` consult before implementation, then reviewed with `/codex` against the diff. Codex flagged three nits, all addressed:

1. ✅ Stale JSON examples in `SETUP.md` and `docs/CLI.md` — updated.
2. ✅ Missing tests for the lifecycle branch of `isTerminalSession` (vs. the flat-status branch) — added on both commands.
3. Deferred (nit, not blocker): per-project "(no active sessions)" message still prints when a project has only hidden terminals. Global footer already discloses the count. Happy to follow up if preferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all packages.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 486 passed (6 new tests: 3 per command covering filter, flag, JSON meta; 1 new lifecycle-branch test per command).
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 new warnings or errors.
- [ ] Manual smoke against a config with a mix of active + terminated sessions:
  - `ao session ls` / `ao status` → active-only with footer.
  - `ao session ls --include-terminated` / `ao status --include-terminated` → full list, no footer.
  - `ao session ls --json` / `ao status --json` → `{data, meta.hiddenTerminatedCount > 0}`, `data` filtered.
  - `ao session restore <terminated-id>` still works.
  - `ao status --watch` → footer updates when a session transitions terminal mid-watch.

title: Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots
body:
## Overview

Performed a comprehensive architecture analysis of the AO backend to map complexity and identify simplification targets. This issue documents the raw findings.

## 1. Spider Files (High Coupling)

Two files reference 14+ other core modules, making them central coupling points:

| File | LOC | Direct References |
|------|-----|-------------------|
| `session-manager.ts` | 2801 | 16 modules |
| `lifecycle-manager.ts` | 1997 | 14 modules |

**session-manager.ts imports from:**
- types, metadata (8 functions), lifecycle-state (4 functions), prompt-builder, activity-signal (2 functions), paths (4 functions), opencode-session-id, opencode-agents-md, orchestrator-session-strategy, utils/session-from-metadata, utils/validation (2 functions), utils, agent-selection (2 functions)

**lifecycle-manager.ts imports from:**
- types (20+ items), lifecycle-state (3 functions), metadata, paths, lifecycle-transition, observability (2 functions), notifier-resolution, agent-selection (2 functions), activity-signal (5 functions), agent-report (3 functions), report-watcher (3 functions), lifecycle-status-decisions (7 functions)

These two files alone account for ~4,800 LOC (33% of core package).

## 2. Fan-In Analysis (Everything Depends on These)

| File | Fan-In Count | Notes |
|------|--------------|-------|
| `types.ts` | 26 importers | Every core file, all 22 plugins, CLI, web |
| `metadata.ts` | 8 importers | session-manager, lifecycle-manager, lifecycle-transition, agent-report |
| `lifecycle-state.ts` | 7 importers | session-manager, lifecycle-manager, lifecycle-transition, metadata, agent-report |
| `paths.ts` | 6 importers | |
| `utils/validation.ts` | 6 importers | |

Changes to high fan-in files ripple across the entire codebase.

## 3. Serialization Hops

Traced data flow from `ao spawn` to dashboard appearance. Found multiple serialization/deserialization cycles:

1. **Config**: YAML → JS object → Zod validated → OrchestratorConfig
2. **Metadata**: SessionMetadata → key=value string → file → key=value string → Record<string,string> → Session
3. **Lifecycle**: CanonicalSessionLifecycle → JSON string (statePayload) → metadata file → JSON parse → lifecycle object
4. **PR data**: GraphQL response → PREnrichmentData → in-memory cache → status derivation
5. **Activity**: JSONL file → parse → ActivityLogEntry → classify → ActivitySignal

The lifecycle state round-trips through JSON serialization inside the key=value metadata file (statePayload field).

## 4. State Machine Complexity

The session lifecycle has **16 states** and **~40 transitions**:

```
States: spawning, detecting, working, pr_open, ci_failed, review_pending, 
        changes_requested, approved, mergeable, merged, needs_input, stuck, 
        errored, killed, done, cleanup
```

The `detecting` state exists purely as a "we don't know yet" intermediate state with retry logic (max 3 attempts, 5min timeout).

State derivation in `determineStatus()` (lifecycle-manager.ts:475-926) is 450 lines of nested conditionals checking:
- Runtime probe (alive/dead/unknown)
- Process probe (alive/dead/unknown) 
- Activity signal (6 states × 5 sources)
- PR state (4 states)
- CI status (4 states)
- Review decision (4 states)
- Agent reports
- Idle thresholds

## 5. Interface Surface Area

`types.ts` defines **95+ interfaces/types/constants** at 1725 LOC.

Plugin interfaces have varying method counts:
| Interface | Methods | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| SCM | 14+ | Largest interface |
| Agent | 10 | 5 required, 5 optional |
| Tracker | 8 | |
| Runtime | 6 | |
| Workspace | 4 | |
| Terminal | 4 | |
| Notifier | 2 | Simplest |

The `SCM` interface grew to accommodate both GitHub and GitLab patterns (GraphQL batch enrichment, webhooks, merge methods, automated comments, etc.).

## 6. Potentially Over-Abstracted

Found interfaces with 1 implementation and 1 consumer:

| Interface | Implementation | Consumer |
|-----------|---------------|----------|
| `RuntimeMetrics` | runtime plugins | (unused in core) |
| `OpenCodeAgentConfig` | config | agent-opencode only |
| `OpenCodeSessionManager` | session-manager | CLI only |

## 7. Plugin Slot Utilization

| Slot | Built-in Plugins | External Plugins |
|------|------------------|------------------|
| runtime | 2 (tmux, process) | 0 |
| agent | 5 (claude-code, codex, aider, cursor, opencode) | 0 |
| workspace | 2 (worktree, clone) | 0 |
| tracker | 3 (github, linear, gitlab) | 0 |
| scm | 2 (github, gitlab) | 0 |
| notifier | 6 (desktop, slack, webhook, discord, composio, openclaw) | 0 |
| terminal | 2 (iterm2, web) | 0 |

All 22 plugins are built-in. Config supports external plugins via `package`/`path` but none exist.

## 8. CLI Command Sizes

| Command | LOC |
|---------|-----|
| `start.ts` | 1731 |
| `plugin.ts` | 602 |
| `setup.ts` | 591 |
| `status.ts` | 528 |
| `doctor.ts` | 466 |

`start.ts` is larger than most core modules because it bundles the lifecycle polling loop, SSE server, WebSocket terminal bridge, and caffeinate/power management.

feat: pipeline execution model — configurable per-PR stages backed by agent plugins
body:
> ⚠️ **This issue captures the end-state vision.** Types, scope, and implementation details are authoritatively defined in the delivery sub-issues:
> - **v0 (foundation)** — #1346 — single-stage pipeline engine, CLI + runtime parity with PR #1339
> - **v1 (multi-stage + routing + conditional exits)** — #1349 — `dependsOn`, `command` executor, `builtin` stages, workspace classes, `Stage.routes`, `exitPredicates`
> - **v2 (user-facing completeness)** — #1350 — Pipeline Workbench UI, conversational follow-up, composed findings bundling, worker-alive check, human-readable reviewer IDs (closes remaining #1275 feature-parity gap)
> - **v3 (orchestrator + workstream pipelines)** — #1351 — three-scope model (`worker` / `orchestrator` / `workstream`), workstream concept (sibling workers sharing a base branch), cross-worker triggers (`workstream.all_pr_opened`, `workstream.all_merged`, etc.), workstream predicates for fan-in, `spawn-workstream` builtin; release-gate example shows all three scopes coordinating
>
> **The roadmap is v0 → v1 → v2 → v3.** v3 adds orchestrator-aware pipelines additively — v0/v1/v2 semantics are unchanged. `cron` and `session.started` lifecycle triggers remain dropped; post-merge pipelines were absorbed into v1 (#1349). No Phase 3.
>
> When this document disagrees with #1346, #1349, or #1350, **the sub-issues win.** #1345 predates the v0/v1/v2 restructure in places — the "Delivery plan," `TaskContext` shape (missing `signal`/`stageRunId`), `Stage` fields (no `routes`/`exitPredicates`), trigger enum (still lists `session.started`/`cron`), `StagePolicy.autoSendFindingsToAgent` (removed), concurrency defaults, and the "Open questions" below are historical. Read here for motivation and design intent; read the sub-issues for what will actually be built.

## Summary

Replace the hardcoded "code → PR → review" flow with a **declarative pipeline** defined per project. Each pipeline is an ordered set of **stages**; each stage names an **executor** (usually an agent plugin in a specific *mode*) plus a **task** that tells the executor what to do. The same agent plugin (codex, claude-code, aider) can appear in multiple stages with different modes.

This generalizes the recently-added code-review slot (#1275 / PR #1339) so adding new capabilities (security review, test synthesis, doc updates, post-merge tasks, nightly audits) is a config change instead of a new plugin slot.

## Motivation

The code-review plugin slot was a one-off. Every future check — typecheck, lint, security scan, test synthesis, post-merge changelog, follow-up refactor — would need either its own slot or a verifier shim. That doesn't scale.

A pipeline model lets us:
- Sequence stages with explicit dependencies (`dependsOn: [review]`)
- Reuse one agent plugin across multiple stages (codex as reviewer AND as fixer)
- Mix AI and non-AI stages (`command` executor covers typecheck/lint/test)
- Run multiple pipelines per project (PR pipeline + post-merge pipeline + nightly pipeline)
- **Run multiple reviewers in parallel** — each is just another stage

## Delivery plan

Rescoped since initial draft. Current plan is **v0 + v1 + v2 + v3** — authoritatively tracked in the sub-issues. Summary:

### v0 — foundation — #1346
- `Agent.executeTask` + `supportedModes` + mandatory `AbortSignal`
- Pipeline types, Zod config, flat-file store
- Pure state machine reducer + FIFO effect-interpreter driver + engine hydration
- **Strictly single-stage** pipelines (validator enforces `stages.length === 1`)
- `agent` executor only
- Codex `executeTask` reference implementation
- `codeReview:` shim → single-stage pipeline; feature parity with #1339
- "Send findings to worker" as a reducer `SEND_TO_AGENT` command (not a stage)
- CLI: `ao pipeline runs/show/run/cancel/resume/migrate` + `ao stage` + `ao artifact`

### v1 — multi-stage + routing + conditional exits — #1349
- `dependsOn` + DAG resolution + cycle detection + outdated propagation
- Parallel execution (tests at `maxConcurrentStages = 4`; production cap lifts gradually)
- `command` executor + JSON-over-stdout contract + fork-PR gating (adds `PRInfo.isFromFork`)
- `builtin` executors (`router`, `compose`) with narrow `BuiltinTaskContext` (has `sendToSession`)
- Workspace classes (`shared-ro` / `isolated-rw`) + WorkspaceGuard
- Structural vs tuning `CONFIG_CHANGED` classifier
- **Conditional routing** via `Stage.routes` — dynamic activation of dependents; unrouted dependents transition to `skipped`
- **Conditional exits** via `Pipeline.exitPredicates` — typed `Predicate` DSL (`all_pass`, `any_pass`, `no_open_findings`, `finding_count_below`, etc., composable via `and/or/not`)
- Multiple pipelines per project + `ao pipeline list` (configs)

### v2 — user-facing completeness — #1350
- Pipeline Workbench UI (`/pipelines` — supersedes `/reviews` from #1339)
- Review strip on existing Dashboard session cards
- Dismiss / reopen / send UI actions with SSE live updates
- `Agent.sendFollowUpToTask?` plugin extension + Codex implementation
- Conversational chat panel with reviewer stages in `awaiting_context`
- Composed findings delivery: bundles AO findings with SCM `getPendingComments()`
- Proactive worker-alive pre-send check
- Human-readable reviewer IDs: `{sessionPrefix}-rev-N`

### v3 — orchestrator + workstream pipelines — #1351
- **Three-scope model:** `Pipeline.scope: "worker" | "orchestrator" | "workstream"` (default `"worker"`; v0/v1/v2 unchanged)
- **Workstream** as a first-class grouping: sibling workers spawned by one orchestrator sharing a base branch, stamped with a shared `workstreamId`. Session metadata gains `parentSessionId` and `workstreamId`
- **Orchestrator triggers:** `orchestrator.started`, `orchestrator.manual`
- **Workstream triggers (cross-worker fan-in):** `workstream.created`, `workstream.worker_pr_opened`, `workstream.all_pr_opened`, `workstream.worker_pr_merged`, `workstream.all_merged`, `workstream.any_stalled`, `workstream.manual`
- **Workstream predicates** for `when` clauses / routes / exit predicates: `all_workstream_workers_in_state`, `all_workstream_workers_match`, `workstream_member_count`
- **`spawn-workstream` builtin** lets pipelines declaratively spawn a workstream from an upstream `json` artifact describing the tasks. Orchestrator agents can also use `ao spawn --workstream <id>` from the CLI
- **Workbench workstream view** groups member workers under their workstream card
- **Concrete end-to-end example** in the issue: release-v2.5 coordinating three feature workers — orchestrator pipeline plans and spawns, each worker runs its own pr-review, a workstream pipeline runs integrated-review + waits for all-merged + bumps version + tags release. All three scopes interact.

### Removed from roadmap
- `cron` trigger — speculative; no use case argued. Open a focused issue if demand appears.
- `session.started` trigger — YAGNI; worker-spawn setup is the worker agent's job (or `project.postCreate` commands), not a pipeline trigger.
- Post-merge pipelines with fresh-workspace semantics — **moved into v1 (#1349)**. v1's multi-pipeline support enables them; the engine creates a fresh detached worktree at `origin/{defaultBranch}` for `pr.merged`-triggered runs.

## Core model

```
Pipeline = ordered list of Stages with declarative dependencies
Stage    = { name, trigger, dependsOn, executor, task, inputs, policy }
Executor = plugin + mode    ← an Agent plugin, run in a specific mode
Task     = what the executor should do, in a stage-appropriate shape
```

A pipeline instance runs against a **pipeline context** (worker session, PR, HEAD SHA). Each stage produces **artifacts** (findings, generic JSON). Downstream stages read upstream artifacts via `inputs`. Runs are persisted flat-file so they survive restart and replay.

## Agent plugin changes

Agent plugins today only support **interactive session mode** (launch → attach → chat). Pipelines require a second mode: **task mode** — one-shot, headless, with structured input and structured output.

Extend `Agent` minimally:

```typescript
interface Agent {
  // existing interactive session API stays as-is

  /**
   * Optional: execute a one-shot pipeline task and return structured results.
   * Plugins that don't implement this are only usable in interactive stages.
   */
  executeTask?(task: AgentTask, ctx: TaskContext): Promise<TaskResult>

  /**
   * Advertise which task modes this agent can run. Used at config-validation
   * time to reject stages whose executor/mode the plugin doesn't support.
   */
  readonly supportedModes?: AgentMode[]
}

// Advisory — plugins use this as capability advertisement. The prompt is what
// actually steers the agent. Users can pass custom strings for novel modes.
type AgentMode = "code" | "review" | "answer" | string

interface AgentTask {
  mode: AgentMode
  prompt: string
  outputSchema?: "findings" | "json"
  budget?: { maxUsd?: number; maxDurationMs?: number }
  inputs?: Record<string, Artifact[]>    // upstream artifacts, resolved
  config?: Record<string, unknown>
}

interface TaskContext {
  workspacePath: string       // isolated detached worktree, READ-ONLY contract
  baseBranch: string
  headSha: string
  linkedSessionId: SessionId
  projectId: string
  pipelineRunId: string
  stageName: string
}

interface TaskResult {
  outcome: "completed" | "failed" | "skipped"
  verdict?: "pass" | "fail" | "neutral"
  artifacts: ArtifactInput[]
  summary: string
  cost?: CostEstimate
  errorMessage?: string
}
```

Agents that can't execute tasks headless simply omit `executeTask`. Existing interactive-only agents keep working.

## Stages

```typescript
interface Stage {
  name: string                            // unique within pipeline
  trigger?: StageTrigger                  // optional; inherit pipeline-level trigger if omitted
  dependsOn?: string[]                    // other stage names; forms the DAG
  executor: ExecutorRef
  task: TaskSpec
  inputs?: Record<string, InputBinding>   // references to upstream stages' artifacts
  policy?: StagePolicy
  timeout?: string                        // "15m", "2h"
  retries?: number                        // retry on outcome=failed, same inputs, no loopRounds increment
}

interface StageTrigger {
  on: TriggerEvent[]
  dedupeBy?: "sha" | "branch" | "none"
}

// External events only — inter-stage ordering is expressed via dependsOn.
type TriggerEvent =
  | "session.started"
  | "pr.opened"
  | "pr.updated"
  | "pr.merge_ready"
  | "pr.merged"
  | "manual"
  | "cron"

interface ExecutorRef {
  kind: "agent" | "command" | "builtin"
  plugin?: string                         // "codex", "claude-code", ...
  mode?: AgentMode                        // for kind=agent
  command?: string                        // for kind=command
  config?: Record<string, unknown>
}

interface StagePolicy {
  blocksMerge?: boolean                   // whether fail verdict blocks merge
  autoSendFindingsToAgent?: string        // stage name of coding agent to route to
  maxRounds?: number                      // per-stage loop cap
  stallWindow?: number                    // per-stage sliding window
}

interface InputBinding {
  from: string                            // "stage:review.findings"
  filter?: Record<string, unknown>        // e.g. { status: "open", severity: "error" }
}

interface TaskSpec {
  prompt?: string                         // for agent executors
  promptFile?: string                     // path to prompt template
  outputSchema?: "findings" | "json"
}
```

**Dependency rules:**
- `dependsOn` forms a DAG over stage names. Config validation **must reject cycles** with a clear error listing the offending names.
- A stage runs when: its trigger fired AND every `dependsOn` stage is terminal (any outcome — the stage decides via `inputs.filter` whether to skip or proceed).
- Stages with no `dependsOn` and a matching trigger run in parallel.
- `maxConcurrentStages` (default 4) caps parallel execution within a single run.

**Plugin-not-installed:** if `executor.plugin` references an unknown plugin, **fail loud at config load**, not at runtime.

## Artifacts

```typescript
type ArtifactInput =
  | { kind: "finding"; filePath?: string; startLine?: number; endLine?: number;
      title: string; description: string; category: string;
      severity: "error" | "warning" | "info"; confidence: number;
      anchorSignature?: string }
  | { kind: "json"; name: string; value: unknown }

interface Artifact extends ArtifactInput {
  artifactId: string
  stageName: string
  pipelineRunId: string
  fingerprint?: string                    // for findings, scoped by stageName
  status?: "open" | "dismissed" | "sent_to_agent" | "resolved"
  createdAt: string
}
```

Only two artifact kinds in v1 — `finding` and a generic `json` bucket. More kinds (`patch`, `summary`, `metric`) added only when a concrete stage needs them.

Fingerprint algorithm (from #1275) stays: `sha256(stageName\0filePath\0category\0severity\0anchor)[:16]` — **scoped by `stageName`** so findings from different stages don't collide. Dismissals persist across pipeline runs via fingerprint match.

## Pipeline runtime

- **DAG resolution.** Stages run when trigger fired AND all `dependsOn` are terminal. No cycles — rejected at config load.
- **Serialization.** One pipeline run per `(worker session, headSha, pipeline name)`. New commits mark prior runs `outdated`, cancel in-flight stages, start fresh.
- **Shared workspace.** All stages in one run share one isolated detached worktree at `headSha`. Contract: **read-only during stage execution.** Stages that produce code changes emit artifacts a later stage applies — no direct writes to the shared tree.
- **Budget.** Per-stage and per-pipeline caps. Remaining stages skip (`outcome: skipped`) on cap breach.
- **Concurrency.** `maxConcurrentStages` default 4 per pipeline run.
- **Retries.** `retries: N` on a stage retries on `outcome: failed` only, same inputs, does not increment `loopRounds`, counts against `budget`.

## Pipeline selection

Projects may declare multiple pipelines. When a `TriggerEvent` fires:
- **Every pipeline whose stage(s) subscribe to that event fires** — pipelines are independent.
- `defaultPipeline` is a **UX hint** (which pipeline the Workbench surfaces first); it does NOT gate execution.

## `command` executor contract

The `command` executor runs a shell command in the stage's read-only worktree and expects **a single JSON object on stdout** matching the `TaskResult` shape:

```json
{
  "outcome": "completed",
  "verdict": "fail",
  "summary": "2 type errors",
  "artifacts": [
    { "kind": "finding", "filePath": "src/a.ts", "startLine": 12,
      "title": "Type 'string' is not assignable to 'number'",
      "description": "...", "category": "typecheck", "severity": "error", "confidence": 1.0 }
  ]
}
```

Tools that don't natively emit this (tsc, trivy, eslint) need a shim script. Exit code 0 required for a valid `TaskResult`; non-zero collapses to `{ outcome: "failed" }` regardless of stdout. No auto-parsing of SARIF/JUnit/etc. in v1.

## Post-merge workspace

`pr.merged` and `cron` triggers don't have a worker workspace to attach to. Stages on those triggers run in a **fresh detached worktree at the default branch HEAD**, created by the pipeline engine, destroyed after the run completes.

## Security — fork PRs and `command` executors

`command` stages execute arbitrary shell in the worktree. For PRs opened from a fork, this is untrusted code execution. **Default:** `command` executors do not run on fork PRs. Override per-project via `pipelines.{name}.allowForkPRs: true` — explicit opt-in, documented risk.

`agent` executors inherit the coding agent's existing sandbox/permission model (unchanged).

## Exit semantics & loop termination

Three levels of exit:

### 1. Stage exit (single execution)
One executor invocation returns with `verdict: pass | fail | neutral` plus `outcome: completed | failed | skipped`. Bounded by the stage's `timeout`.

### 2. Pipeline run exit (single SHA)
A `PipelineRun` is terminal when every stage is `completed | failed | skipped | outdated`.

Aggregate verdict:
- `fail` if any `blocksMerge: true` stage has verdict `fail`
- `pass` if every `blocksMerge: true` stage has verdict `pass`
- `neutral` otherwise (no blocking stages failed, but not all passed either)

### 3. Pipeline loop exit (across SHAs)
Tracked per `(worker session, pipeline name)`:

| Loop state | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `running` | Any stage in the current run is not terminal |
| `awaiting_context` | All stages terminal for the current SHA, at least one has open findings waiting on human triage |
| `done` | All stages `verdict=pass` AND zero open findings across all stages |
| `stalled` | Any `blocksMerge: true` stage hit its per-stage stalled check OR pipeline-level `maxLoopRounds` reached without `done` |
| `terminated` | `manual_cancel` / `worker_dead` / `config_change` / `stage_failure` |

**Exit predicates:**
```
done          = ∀ stages: verdict == pass ∧ open_findings == 0
stalled       = ∃ blocking stage: stage.loopState == stalled
                OR loopRounds ≥ pipeline.maxLoopRounds ∧ ¬done
awaiting_ctx  = all stages terminal for current SHA ∧ ∃ stage: open_findings > 0
running       = any stage not terminal
```

**Re-trigger rule (new commit):**
- Loop state `awaiting_context` or `done` AND HEAD changed → mark prior run `outdated`, start new PipelineRun, increment `loopRounds`
- Loop state `stalled` → no automatic re-trigger; requires explicit `ao pipeline resume <session>` (resets `loopRounds`)
- Loop state `terminated` → no re-trigger
- Loop state `running` → new commits queue; do NOT preempt an in-flight run

**Two convergence mechanisms:**
1. **Per-stage stalled detection** (from #1275): sliding-window union of open fingerprints over last `stallWindow` runs. If `n ≥ stage.maxRounds` AND `|W(n)| ≥ |W(n-1)|`, the stage is `stalled`. Catches persistent findings AND flip-flops (`{a}→{b}→{a}`).
2. **Pipeline-level safety cap**: `pipeline.maxLoopRounds` (default 5) bounds total re-triggers regardless of per-stage state. Prevents a cheap stage from retriggering the whole pipeline forever.

### Multi-reviewer convergence rule

**Stages don't compare findings with each other.** Each stage's convergence is isolated:
- Finding fingerprints are scoped by `stageName`, so codex-review's `{a}` and claude-review's `{a}` are distinct artifacts with distinct fingerprints
- Dismissing a codex-review finding does not dismiss the matching claude-review finding
- Pipeline `done` requires every stage done — not "any stage agrees"

This avoids the ambiguous questions #1275 deferred:
- "If reviewer A dismissed and reviewer B raised the same location, is it dismissed?" → they're different findings
- "Do reviewers run in parallel or serialize?" → parallel; each stage is independent
- "Does pipeline `done` require all reviewers done, or just one?" → all

The tradeoff: a noisy reviewer stage can block a pipeline indefinitely if never dismissed. Policy escape: set `policy.blocksMerge: false` on advisory stages so they don't keep the pipeline out of `done`.

### Termination reasons

| Reason | Meaning | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `cycle_cap` | Per-stage `maxRounds` or pipeline `maxLoopRounds` reached | `ao pipeline resume` resets counter |
| `worker_dead` | Linked worker session exited/killed | Informational |
| `stage_failure` | Blocking stage's executor crashed unrecoverably | `ao stage retry <stageRunId>` |
| `manual_cancel` | Human cancelled | Intentional |
| `config_change` | Pipeline config changed mid-flight (in-flight runs finish, loop state resets on next trigger) | Re-enable via config |

## Storage

Flat files under `~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/pipelines/`:
- `runs/{runId}.json` — PipelineRun
- `stages/{runId}/{stageRunId}.json` — StageRun
- `artifacts/{runId}/{stageRunId}.jsonl` — **one JSONL per stage**, not per artifact; scales to 1000+ findings per stage without filesystem pain
- `loops/{sessionId}-{pipelineName}.json` — loop state (loopRounds, lastSha, current run pointer)

## Config

```yaml
projects:
  my-app:
    pipelines:
      pr-review:
        maxLoopRounds: 5
        maxConcurrentStages: 4

        stages:
          - name: review-codex
            trigger:
              on: [pr.opened, pr.updated]
              dedupeBy: sha
            executor:
              kind: agent
              plugin: codex
              mode: review
            task:
              prompt: |
                Review the diff against main. Focus on correctness and security.
                Emit findings with file/line/severity.
              outputSchema: findings
            policy:
              blocksMerge: false          # advisory
              maxRounds: 3
              stallWindow: 3

          # Second reviewer, runs in parallel with codex — no interaction between them
          - name: review-claude
            trigger: { on: [pr.opened, pr.updated] }
            executor: { kind: agent, plugin: claude-code, mode: review }
            task: { outputSchema: findings }
            policy: { blocksMerge: false, maxRounds: 3, stallWindow: 3 }

          - name: security-scan
            trigger: { on: [pr.opened, pr.updated] }
            executor:
              kind: command
              command: ./scripts/trivy-shim.sh    # shim emits TaskResult JSON on stdout
            task: { outputSchema: findings }
            policy: { blocksMerge: true }

          - name: typecheck
            trigger: { on: [pr.opened, pr.updated] }
            executor:
              kind: command
              command: ./scripts/typecheck-shim.sh
            policy: { blocksMerge: true }

          - name: route-findings
            dependsOn: [review-codex, review-claude, security-scan]
            executor: { kind: builtin, plugin: router }
            inputs:
              codex_findings:  { from: stage:review-codex.findings,   filter: { status: open } }
              claude_findings: { from: stage:review-claude.findings,  filter: { status: open } }
              scan_findings:   { from: stage:security-scan.findings,  filter: { severity: error } }

          - name: fix
            dependsOn: [route-findings]
            executor:
              kind: agent
              plugin: codex         # same plugin as review-codex, different mode
              mode: code
            task:
              prompt: "Fix the routed findings, push, and reply to the review."
            inputs:
              findings: { from: stage:route-findings.json, filter: { name: "delivered" } }

      post-merge-docs:
        stages:
          - name: update-changelog
            trigger: { on: [pr.merged] }   # runs in a fresh default-branch worktree
            executor: { kind: agent, plugin: aider, mode: code }
            task: { prompt: "Update CHANGELOG.md with the merged PR summary." }

    defaultPipeline: pr-review   # UX hint for Workbench; does not gate execution
```

## Triggers → lifecycle hook

Extend the lifecycle manager with a **pipeline engine** that subscribes to existing lifecycle events:
- `session.status == pr_open` first time → `pr.opened`
- `git rev-parse HEAD` changes → `pr.updated`
- SCM reports merged → `pr.merged`
- CLI `ao pipeline run` → `manual`

Engine resolves which pipelines and stages fire, queues them, and dispatches to executors.

## Executor implementations

### `kind: "agent"`
Uses existing Agent plugin registry. Calls `agent.executeTask(task, ctx)`. Plugin must declare the `mode` in `supportedModes`. Interactive-only plugins error at config validation.

### `kind: "command"`
Runs a shell command in the stage's read-only worktree. Expects a single JSON object on stdout matching `TaskResult` shape (see command executor contract above). Exit-code 0 required for a valid result.

### `kind: "builtin"`
Core-provided stages for plumbing. v1 ships:
- `router` — composes open findings from input stages into a prompt and delivers via `session_manager.send()` to the linked worker session; emits a `json` artifact named `delivered` containing the message and finding IDs
- `compose` — merges artifacts from multiple inputs into a single bundle for downstream consumption

`merge` and `notify` deferred to phase 3.

## Human triage — Pipeline Workbench

Replaces the Review Workbench. Each worker PR card shows a mini pipeline diagram with per-stage status:

```
┌ app-1 @ abc123 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ review-codex ⚠  review-claude ✓  security-scan ✗  typecheck ✓  │
│ route-findings ⏳  fix ○                                         │
│                                                                   │
│ security-scan: 2 errors                         [Dismiss] [Send] │
│ review-codex: 3 open / 1 dismissed              [Dismiss] [Send] │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Pipeline-level loop state ribbon at the top: `running | awaiting_context | done | stalled | terminated` with `loopRounds/maxLoopRounds` counter.

## CLI

```bash
ao pipeline list [session]
ao pipeline show <runId>
ao pipeline run <session> [--pipeline X]
ao pipeline cancel <runId>
ao pipeline resume <session>             # resets loopRounds, clears stalled
ao stage retry <stageRunId>
ao artifact list <runId> [--stage X]
ao artifact dismiss <artifactId>
ao artifact send <artifactId> [--to session]
```

## Migration from PR #1339

| Today (#1339) | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `code-review` plugin slot | Removed — code review is a stage with `executor: {kind: agent, mode: review}` |
| `CodeReview.runReview` | `Agent.executeTask({ mode: "review", outputSchema: "findings" })` |
| `code-review-codex` plugin | `codex` agent plugin gains `executeTask` supporting `mode: "review"` |
| `CodeReviewRun` | `PipelineRun` with a `review-codex` stage |
| `CodeReviewFinding` | `Artifact` of kind `finding` |
| `projects.*.codeReview` config | `projects.*.pipelines.{name}.stages[]` |
| Review Workbench | Pipeline Workbench |
| `onSessionPolled` hook | Pipeline engine subscribes to lifecycle events |
| Per-worker loop states | Per-`(session, pipeline)` loop states |
| `maxReviewRounds` | `stage.policy.maxRounds` + `pipeline.maxLoopRounds` |

**Compatibility shim:** accept the `codeReview:` block for one release, compile to an equivalent single-stage `review-only` pipeline internally. Remove shim after one release.

## What this unlocks

- **Sequencing.** `review → route-findings → fix → re-review` declaratively via `dependsOn`.
- **Cross-stage artifacts.** `fix` reads findings from `review`; post-merge pipelines fire on `pr.merged`.
- **Agent reuse.** One `codex` plugin serves `review` and `code` stages via different modes.
- **Non-AI stages.** `command` covers typecheck/lint/test via shim scripts.
- **Multiple pipelines per project.** `pr-review` on PR, `post-merge-docs` after merge, `nightly-audit` on cron.
- **Multiple reviewers in parallel.** Each is a stage with its own fingerprint scope and convergence.

## Explicit non-goals for v1

- `when:` expression language — cut entirely. Use `dependsOn` for ordering and `inputs.filter` for data-based conditions.
- Arbitrary `stage:X.completed` triggers — replaced by `dependsOn`.
- Fan-out/fan-in beyond simple dependency edges.
- Cross-project pipelines.
- Human-approval stages as explicit kind (workaround: `awaiting_input` loop state).
- Pipeline versioning / dry-run.
- Cross-stage finding deduplication (deliberate — see Multi-reviewer rule).
- Auto-parsing SARIF / JUnit / custom formats in `command` executor.
- Artifact kinds beyond `finding` and `json`.

## Open questions (resolved — see sub-issues for current answers)

1. ~~**Default pipeline** for existing projects~~ → **Resolved in v0 (#1346):** the `codeReview:` shim synthesizes a `legacy-code-review` pipeline; no built-in default for greenfield projects.
2. ~~**Agent mode discovery**~~ → **Resolved in v0 (#1346):** static `supportedModes` manifest field; validated at config load.
3. ~~**Router stage access to core services**~~ → **Resolved in v1 (#1349):** `BuiltinTaskContext extends TaskContext` with a narrow `sendToSession` channel. Only builtin executors receive it.
4. ~~**Cron triggers**~~ → **Removed from roadmap.** Speculative; reopen as a focused issue if real demand appears.
5. **`maxLoopRounds` default = 5** — kept as v0's default; still TBD whether real usage wants a different number.

## References

- Supersedes (partially) #1275 — code-review plugin slot
- Builds on PR #1339 — code-review implementation (migrated into a `review` stage)

title: feat(pipeline): implementation plan — engine, executors, and config shim
body:
**This is the v0 foundation issue.** Ships the minimum pipeline machinery needed to replace #1339's code-review engine as a single-stage pipeline — **CLI and runtime behavior only**. v1 (#1349) extends this with multi-stage, `command` executor, workspace classes, and conditional routing / exit predicates. v2 (#1350) closes the remaining #1275 feature-parity gap: Pipeline Workbench UI, conversational follow-up, composed findings bundling, worker-alive checks, and human-readable reviewer IDs.

Sub-issue of #1345.

## Goal

Replace PR #1339's code-review engine with a pipeline-shaped foundation. A project configured with `codeReview:` continues to work via a compatibility shim that synthesizes a **one-stage pipeline**. v0 delivers **CLI + runtime parity** with #1339: same findings, same dismissal persistence, same stalled detection, same `autoSendNewFindingsToAgent` routing.

**What v0 does NOT preserve from #1339** (tracked in v2 #1350):
- Review Workbench UI at `/reviews` — deferred to v2; v0 is CLI-only for human triage
- Conversational follow-up (`sendFollowUp`) — deferred to v2
- Composed findings bundle with SCM pending comments — deferred to v2
- Proactive worker-alive pre-send check — v0 is reactive (send-fails-leaves-finding-open); proactive check is v2
- `{sessionPrefix}-rev-N` human-readable reviewer IDs — v0 uses opaque `PipelineRunId`; human alias is v2

A user upgrading from #1339 to v0 alone loses the Web UI and chat capability. v0 + v2 is the full replacement.

## Scope

**In:**
- `Agent.executeTask` plugin interface extension + `supportedModes` + mandatory `AbortSignal`
- `Pipeline` + `Stage` types (minimal fields; extensible in v1)
- Pipeline store (flat-file, JSONL per stage)
- Pipeline engine: pure state machine + effect interpreter, two-level state model (`EngineState` + `RunState`)
- Strictly single-stage execution per run (shim produces one-stage pipelines only)
- `agent` executor (only kind shipped in v0)
- Codex plugin `executeTask` reference implementation (review + code + answer modes)
- `codeReview:` → single-stage pipeline compatibility shim
- Lifecycle integration (trigger emission from existing events)
- Engine hydration from persistent store on startup
- "Send findings to coding agent" as a **reducer-level command**, not a stage
- Fingerprint-based convergence ported from #1275
- CLI: `ao pipeline runs/show/cancel/resume/run/migrate`
- Observability events
- Tests (unit + integration + property-based on reducer)

**Not in v0 (moved to v1 #1349):**
- Multi-stage support: `dependsOn`, DAG resolution, cycle detection, parallel execution
- `command` executor + JSON-over-stdout contract + fork-PR gating
- `builtin` executors (`router`, `compose`) as first-class stages
- `BuiltinTaskContext` + `sendToSession` capability
- Workspace classes (`shared-ro` / `isolated-rw`), WorkspaceGuard
- Outdated propagation (moot with single-stage)
- Structural vs tuning `CONFIG_CHANGED` distinction (v0: any config change terminates)
- `PRInfo.isFromFork` (only needed by command executor)
- Multiple pipelines per project / `ao pipeline list` (configs)
- Per-stage `cache` directories
- Conditional exit predicates (`exitPredicates`)

## Module-by-module breakdown

### 1. Core type extensions — `packages/core/src/types.ts`

~120 LOC.

```typescript
interface Agent {
  // ... existing fields unchanged
  executeTask?(task: AgentTask, ctx: TaskContext): Promise<TaskResult>
  readonly supportedModes?: AgentMode[]
}

type AgentMode = "code" | "review" | "answer" | string

interface AgentTask { mode; prompt; outputSchema?; budget?; inputs?; config? }

interface TaskContext {
  workspacePath: string
  baseBranch: string
  headSha: string
  linkedSessionId: SessionId
  projectId: string
  pipelineRunId: PipelineRunId
  stageRunId: StageRunId
  stageName: string
  signal: AbortSignal              // MANDATORY
}

interface TaskResult { outcome; verdict?; artifacts; summary; cost?; errorMessage? }

type ArtifactId    = string & { __brand: "ArtifactId" }
type StageRunId    = string & { __brand: "StageRunId" }
type PipelineRunId = string & { __brand: "PipelineRunId" }

interface Pipeline {
  name: string
  maxLoopRounds: number        // default 5
  stages: Stage[]              // single-stage only in v0; validator enforces
}

interface Stage {
  name: string
  trigger: StageTrigger        // required in v0 (no dependsOn yet)
  executor: { kind: "agent"; plugin: string; mode: AgentMode; config?: Record<string, unknown> }
  task: TaskSpec
  policy?: StagePolicy
  timeout?: string
  retries?: number
  budget?: { maxUsd?: number; maxDurationMs?: number }
}

interface StagePolicy { blocksMerge?; maxRounds?; stallWindow? }

type ArtifactInput = FindingArtifact | JsonArtifact

// FindingArtifact shape (inline for clarity):
//   kind: "finding"
//   filePath, startLine, endLine, title, description
//   category: string          // "security" | "correctness" | "style" | ... | "general"
//   severity: "error" | "warning" | "info"
//   confidence: number        // 0.0–1.0
//   anchorSignature?: string  // structural anchor (function/class name) for fingerprint
//   belowConfidenceThreshold?: boolean
//     // Set by the reducer when finding.confidence < pipeline/stage confidenceThreshold.
//     // Finding stays open, but UI filters it from the default view.
//     // "Deprioritize without dismissing" — preserves audit vs silently hiding.

interface Artifact extends ArtifactInput { artifactId; stageName; stageRunId; pipelineRunId; fingerprint?; status?; createdAt }

interface LoopState {
  sessionId; pipelineName; loopState: LoopStateName
  loopRounds: number; lastSha: string
  currentRunId?: PipelineRunId; updatedAt: string
}

type TriggerEvent     = "pr.opened" | "pr.updated" | "pr.merge_ready" | "pr.merged" | "manual"
type LoopStateName    = "running" | "awaiting_context" | "done" | "stalled" | "terminated"
type TerminationReason = "cycle_cap" | "worker_dead" | "stage_failure" | "manual_cancel" | "config_change"
```

**Practical trigger support in v0:** the enum includes `pr.merged` and `pr.merge_ready` for forward compatibility with v1, but v0's shim only synthesizes pipelines with `pr.opened` / `pr.updated` triggers. A user hand-authoring a v0 pipeline with `pr.merged` would fail at workspace creation (v0 has no fresh-worktree story — that lands in v1 §8.5). Config validator should warn, not block, so v1 upgrades don't require a trigger-enum migration.

Fields reserved for v1 (`dependsOn`, `inputs`, `workspace`) are **intentionally absent** in v0 — adding them lands with v1.

### 2. Config schema — `packages/core/src/config.ts`

Zod schema (~60 LOC) + validator (~80 LOC):
- `stages.length === 1` enforced (v0 is single-stage; multi-stage is v1)
- Plugin-not-installed check
- `executor.plugin + mode` validated against `supportedModes`
- Reject stages without a `trigger`

Shim (`code-review-shim.ts`, ~100 LOC):
- Per-project: `codeReview:` present and `pipelines:` absent → synthesize `legacy-code-review` pipeline with one `review` stage
- Both present → loud error at config load (per-project rule)
- Fingerprints synthesized with `stageName: "review"` so existing dismissals carry forward

**Field mapping from legacy `codeReview:` to `pipelines:`:**

| Legacy field | Pipeline target |
|---|---|
| `codeReview.plugin` | `stage.executor.plugin` (with `kind: "agent"`, `mode: "review"`) |
| `codeReview.prompt` | `stage.task.prompt` (verbatim; the 1st of three customization layers) |
| `codeReview.limits.maxBudgetPerRun` | `stage.budget.maxUsd` |
| `codeReview.limits.maxReviewRounds` | `pipeline.maxLoopRounds` |
| `codeReview.limits.stallWindow` | `stage.policy.stallWindow` |
| `codeReview.limits.confidenceThreshold` | Applied by reducer when enriching findings — sets `belowConfidenceThreshold: true` on findings below the threshold (2nd customization layer) |
| `codeReview.severityThreshold` | Reducer post-filter — findings with severity below the threshold are dropped before fingerprinting, matching #1339's behavior |
| `codeReview.trigger.onPullRequestOpen/Update` | `stage.trigger.on` entries (`pr.opened` / `pr.updated`) |
| `codeReview.autoSendNewFindingsToAgent` | Controls whether the reducer emits `SEND_TO_AGENT` on terminal-with-open-findings. Default `true` (autonomous-by-capability, matching #1339). |
| `.agent-rules.md` (repo file) | Read by the Codex plugin at runtime — unchanged, automatic (3rd customization layer; no shim work needed) |

The three **customization layers** users see: (1) `severityThreshold` filters post-review, (2) `prompt` appends custom instructions to the review stage's task, (3) `.agent-rules.md` in the repo is read automatically by the reviewer agent.

### 3. Pipeline store — `packages/core/src/pipeline-store.ts`

~200 LOC. Mirrors `review-store.ts`:

```
~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/pipelines/
  runs/{runId}.json                     PipelineRun (with frozen pipelineConfigSnapshot)
  stages/{runId}/{stageRunId}.json      StageRun
  artifacts/{runId}/{stageRunId}.jsonl  Artifact[]
  loops/{sessionId}-{pipelineName}.json LoopState
```

Operations: `createRun`, `updateRun`, `getRun`, `listRuns(sessionId?)`, `createStageRun`, `updateStageRun`, `getStageRun`, `listStageRuns(runId)`, `appendArtifacts(stageRunId, inputs[])`, `listArtifacts(stageRunId, filter?)`, `updateArtifactStatus(id, status, meta?)`, `readLoopState(sessionId, pipelineName)`, `writeLoopState(...)`, `loadEngineStateSnapshot()`, `pruneRuns(policy)`.

All writes via `atomic-write.ts`.

### 4. Pipeline engine — `packages/core/src/pipeline-engine/`

#### 4a. Two-level state model

The reducer operates over `EngineState` wrapping multiple `RunState`s — even in single-stage v0, multi-run tracking is required because `NEW_SHA_DETECTED` marks the current run outdated AND spawns a new run.

```typescript
interface EngineState {
  runs: Map<PipelineRunId, RunState>
  currentRunByLoop: Map<string, PipelineRunId>        // "{sessionId}:{pipelineName}"
  historySummaries: Map<string, RunSummary[]>         // for convergence across runs
}

interface RunState {
  runId; sessionId; pipelineName
  pipelineConfigSnapshot: Pipeline                     // frozen at run-create
  headSha; loopState; terminationReason?; loopRounds
  stages: Map<string, StageState>                      // one entry in v0; map for v1 extension
  createdAt: string
}

interface StageState {
  status: "pending" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "skipped" | "outdated"
  attempt: number
  verdict?: "pass" | "fail" | "neutral"
  artifacts: ArtifactId[]
  startedAt?: string; completedAt?: string
}
// Note: "ready" status deferred to v1 (only meaningful with concurrency > 1)
```

Every event carries `now: number` (driver stamps at enqueue); reducer stays pure.

```typescript
type Event =
  | { type: "TRIGGER_FIRED"; now; name: TriggerEvent; ctx: EventContext }
  | { type: "NEW_SHA_DETECTED"; now; sessionId; pipelineName; sha }
  | { type: "STAGE_DONE"; now; runId; stageName; result: TaskResult }
  | { type: "STAGE_FAILED"; now; runId; stageName; error }
  | { type: "STAGE_TIMEOUT"; now; runId; stageName }
  | { type: "CLI_CANCEL"; now; runId; reason?: TerminationReason }
  | { type: "SYSTEM_CANCEL"; now; runId; reason: TerminationReason }    // hydration / worker_dead
  | { type: "CLI_RESUME"; now; sessionId; pipelineName }
  | { type: "CONFIG_CHANGED"; now; sessionId; pipelineName; newConfig: Pipeline }
  | { type: "TICK"; now }

type Command =
  | { type: "START_STAGE"; async: true; runId; stageName; ctx: TaskContext }
  | { type: "CANCEL_STAGE"; async: true; runId; stageName }
  | { type: "CREATE_WORKTREE"; async: true; runId; path; sha }          // single class in v0
  | { type: "DESTROY_WORKTREE"; async: true; path }
  | { type: "PERSIST_RUN"; async: false; runId }
  | { type: "PERSIST_LOOP_STATE"; async: false; sessionId; pipelineName; state: LoopState }
  | { type: "APPEND_ARTIFACTS"; async: false; stageRunId; artifacts: ArtifactInput[] }
  | { type: "SEND_TO_AGENT"; async: true; sessionId; message: string; findingIds: ArtifactId[] }
  | { type: "EMIT_OBSERVATION"; async: false; event: ObservabilityEvent }
```

`SEND_TO_AGENT` is the v0 replacement for a `router` stage: after the review stage terminates with open findings, the reducer emits this command. Driver calls `sessionManager.send()` and enqueues a follow-up event to update artifact statuses to `sent_to_agent`. When v1 ships `builtin/router`, this command becomes unused (the stage takes over).

**Emission semantics (avoids spamming the worker on retries / re-reviews):**
- Reducer emits `SEND_TO_AGENT` only for findings where `status === "open"` AND `sentToAgentAt` is unset
- After the driver confirms delivery, reducer emits artifact-status updates flipping those findings to `sent_to_agent` with `sentToAgentAt: now`
- Retries that re-produce the same fingerprints → findings carry forward with `sentToAgentAt` already set → not resent
- A new run at a new SHA creates new artifacts with matching fingerprints → fingerprint-match inherits triage state (including `sentToAgentAt`) from the prior run → already-sent findings don't resend
- If the driver's send call fails, the finding stays `open` with `sentToAgentAt` unset; next poll cycle retries

**Reducer:** `update(state: EngineState, event: Event): [EngineState, Command[]]`. Pure, synchronous, no clock.

#### 4b. Event queue and command ordering

Driver maintains strictly FIFO queue; reducer never re-entrant. On each `step()`:
1. Dequeue one event (stamped `now` at enqueue)
2. Call `update()` synchronously
3. Execute commands **in array order**: sync commands complete before next; async are fire-and-forget
4. Commit new EngineState
5. Return

Async command completions enqueue fresh events (`STAGE_DONE`, `STAGE_FAILED`, etc.). Single processing loop → no concurrent reducer calls.

Concurrency: **hardcoded serial in v0** — driver runs at most one `START_STAGE` at a time. (Single-stage pipelines trivially satisfy this.)

#### 4c. Workspace management

Single class in v0: a **detached git worktree per run** at `headSha`, shared by the (one) stage. Destroyed on run terminal transition to `done | stalled | failed | outdated`; kept for `awaiting_context` so follow-up chat works.

No isolation concerns because there's no second stage running concurrently. Multi-class workspace (shared-ro / isolated-rw) + WorkspaceGuard arrive in v1 with multi-stage.

#### 4d. Cancellation contract

`TaskContext.signal` is mandatory. Driver owns the `AbortController`; signal fires on `CANCEL_STAGE`. Agent plugins must respect signal — blocking review gate on new plugin PRs.

#### 4e. Convergence and config snapshots

- Per-stage sliding-window stalled detection (reuse `detectStalled` from `code-review-fingerprint.ts`). Runs against `RunSummary` entries in `historySummaries`.
- Pipeline-level `maxLoopRounds` cap.
- `RunState.pipelineConfigSnapshot` frozen at run-create.
- Any `CONFIG_CHANGED` → in-flight runs terminate with `config_change`. v0 does not distinguish structural vs tuning (that's v1).

#### 4f. Budget semantics

- `stage.budget > no cap` (no pipeline-level default in v0; one-line addition in v1)
- `maxUsd` and `maxDurationMs` per-run, summed across retries
- Breach → driver aborts via `signal`; `STAGE_FAILED(errorMessage: "budget exceeded")`
- Cost from `TaskResult.cost` (agents) + wall-clock

#### 4g. Engine hydration on startup

Driver startup rebuilds `EngineState` synchronously (no event queue round-trip):
1. Read all `PipelineRun` records
2. For each terminated run → build `RunSummary`, insert into `historySummaries`
3. For each in-flight run (loopState not in `{done, stalled, terminated}`): directly construct terminal state with `terminationReason: "worker_dead"`, clear `currentRunId` in its LoopState
4. Read `loops/` files → populate `currentRunByLoop`, skipping entries whose `currentRunId` now points to a terminal run
5. Engine ready

Without this, stalled detection silently breaks after any restart.

### 5. Agent executor — `packages/core/src/executors/agent-executor.ts`

~80 LOC. Only executor kind in v0.

- Resolves plugin from registry
- Validates `supportedModes` at dispatch time
- Invokes `agent.executeTask(task, ctx)` with `ctx.signal` wired to the driver's `AbortController`
- Wraps plugin errors into `STAGE_FAILED` events; abort-while-running → clean cancellation

### 6. Codex `executeTask` — `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/execute-task.ts`

~150 LOC.

**Invocation:**
- `mode: "review"` → `codex exec review --base {baseBranch} --json --output-last-message {tempFile} --full-auto`
- `mode: "code"` → `codex exec --json {prompt}`
- `mode: "answer"` → same as code but returns `{ answer: string }`
- `supportedModes` manifest: `["review", "code", "answer"]`

**`--ephemeral` is intentionally NOT used.** The Codex session must persist in the workspace so v2's `sendFollowUpToTask` (via `codex exec --continue`) can re-attach to the same review context. Using `--ephemeral` would discard the session and break follow-up chat. Review gate on the Codex plugin PR.

**Signal handling:** `ctx.signal` → spawned codex process killed on abort (SIGTERM → 5s → SIGKILL).

**Lenient parser:** unknown fields ignored; missing required keys → `outcome: failed` with detected codex version + first 500 bytes of stdout in `errorMessage`.

**Codex `review` output → AO `finding` artifact mapping** (spec: match `code-review-codex` plugin behavior from #1339 so the shim-equivalence tests pass):

| Codex field | AO `finding` field | Transform |
|---|---|---|
| `code_location.absolute_file_path` | `filePath` | Direct |
| `code_location.line_range.start` | `startLine` | Direct |
| `code_location.line_range.end` | `endLine` | Direct |
| `title` | `title` | Strip `[P0]`–`[P3]` prefix; e.g. `"[P1] Missing null check in auth handler"` → `"Missing null check in auth handler"` |
| `body` | `description` | Markdown preserved |
| `priority` | `severity` | P0/P1 → `error`, P2 → `warning`, P3 → `info` |
| `confidence_score` | `confidence` | Direct (0.0–1.0) |
| — | `category` | Inferred from title keywords (`security`, `correctness`, `performance`, `style`) or default `"general"` |
| — | `fingerprint` | Computed in the reducer: `sha256(stageName\0filePath\0category\0severity\0anchorSignature)[:16]` |

`overall_explanation` and `overall_confidence_score` from Codex's run-level output map to `TaskResult.summary` and `TaskResult.overallConfidence`.

Existing `@aoagents/ao-plugin-code-review-codex` deprecated; shim resynthesizes its behavior.

### 7. Lifecycle integration — `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`

~40 LOC diff. Extend `LifecycleManagerDeps` with `pipelineEngine?: PipelineEngine`, replacing `onSessionPolled` from #1339.

Trigger emission:
- `pr_open` first time → `TRIGGER_FIRED("pr.opened", ctx)`
- HEAD SHA delta → `NEW_SHA_DETECTED(sessionId, pipelineName, sha)`
- PR merged → `TRIGGER_FIRED("pr.merged", ctx)`
- CLI → `TRIGGER_FIRED("manual", ctx)`
- Config reload with pipeline-relevant diff → `CONFIG_CHANGED` (v0: any diff, no structural/tuning distinction)

v0 emits one event per configured pipeline for the session (single pipeline per project means at most one).

### 8. CLI — `packages/cli/src/commands/pipeline.ts`, `stage.ts`, `artifact.ts`

~300 LOC total. v0 subset:

```bash
ao pipeline runs [session] [--limit N]        # list runs, newest first
ao pipeline show <runId>                      # run detail
ao pipeline run <session>                     # manual trigger
ao pipeline cancel <runId>
ao pipeline resume <session>                  # clears stalled
ao pipeline migrate                           # prints pipelines: block from legacy codeReview:

ao stage retry <stageRunId>                   # retry one stage

ao artifact list <runId>
ao artifact show <artifactId>
ao artifact dismiss <artifactId> [--by USER]
ao artifact reopen <artifactId>
ao artifact send <artifactId>
```

`ao pipeline list` (configs), `ao pipeline run --pipeline X`, `ao stage logs`, `ao artifact --stage`, and `--project` flags are v1 (multi-pipeline / command-executor features).

### 9. Observability

Reducer emits `EMIT_OBSERVATION` on transitions; driver forwards to `observer.recordOperation`.

v0 events:
- `pipeline.run.created` / `pipeline.run.terminated` (reason, duration)
- `pipeline.stage.terminated` (stage name, status, verdict, duration, artifact count, cost)
- `pipeline.cancellation` (runId, trigger source)

v1 adds: `pipeline.workspace.guard_warning`, `pipeline.fork_pr_blocked`.

### 10. Tests

**Unit (`packages/core/src/__tests__/`):**
- `pipeline-config-validator.test.ts` — plugin-not-installed, mode validation, single-stage enforcement, per-project shim check
- `pipeline-store.test.ts` — CRUD, JSONL artifacts, config snapshot round-trip, GC
- `pipeline-engine/reducer.test.ts` — target ≥ 40 tests on meaningful (state × event) transitions
- `pipeline-engine/reducer.property.test.ts` — fast-check property tests for 6 invariants (see below)
- `pipeline-engine/driver.test.ts` — FIFO queue, sync/async command ordering, hydration
- `pipeline-engine/hydration.test.ts` — historySummaries rebuild + worker_dead orphaning
- `pipeline-engine/config-snapshot.test.ts` — CONFIG_CHANGED terminates in-flight
- `executors/agent-executor.test.ts` — signal propagation, mode validation
- `pipeline-engine/send-to-agent.test.ts` — reducer emits SEND_TO_AGENT on terminal-with-findings; driver updates artifact status

**Plugin:**
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/__tests__/execute-task.test.ts` — three modes, signal abort, lenient parser

**Integration:**
- `pipeline-review-only.integration.test.ts` — shim path; verifies #1339 behavior preserved (same findings, dismissals, transitions)
- `pipeline-cancellation.integration.test.ts` — `pr.updated` mid-stage cancels and restarts at new SHA
- `pipeline-restart.integration.test.ts` — kill/restart driver mid-run, verify hydration

## Property-based invariants

Target 10k random event sequences per invariant (1k locally, 10k in CI):

1. No stage transitions `pending → succeeded` (must pass through `running`)
2. Every `CANCEL_STAGE` command is followed (eventually) by the stage reaching a terminal state
3. `NEW_SHA_DETECTED` during a running run → old run terminates as `outdated`, new run created at new SHA
4. Retries count at most exactly `stage.retries`, never more
5. `loopRounds` increments on `TRIGGER_FIRED(pr.updated)` only, never on retry
6. Every `pipeline.stage.terminated` has a matching prior `stage.started` observation (no dropped events)

v1 adds four more invariants (dependents propagation, structural vs tuning CONFIG, workspace creation bounds, isolated-rw destruction).

## Migration plan

1. Land #1345 (spec)
2. **Type-only PR 2a:** `Agent.executeTask` (optional), `AgentMode`, `supportedModes`, `TaskContext`, branded IDs
3. **Type-only PR 2b:** `Pipeline`, `Stage`, `EngineState`, `RunState`, `Event`, `Command`, `LoopState`
4. Pipeline store (reviewable standalone)
5. Pipeline engine reducer (pure function + property tests — PR-reviewable but not behaviorally verifiable without driver; call this out)
6. Driver + agent executor + hydration — behind `AO_PIPELINE_ENGINE=1` flag
7. Codex `executeTask` + code-review-codex plugin deprecation — behind flag
8. Shim — behind flag; without flag, #1339 code path continues
9. Flip flag default to on in follow-up release — **gated on v2 (#1350) having landed**, so users don't lose the Review Workbench UI when v0 becomes the default path. If v2 isn't ready, extend the opt-in window rather than force a UI regression.
10. Remove shim one release after default-on. **Persisted legacy-code-review runs remain queryable** via `ao pipeline runs` / `ao pipeline show`; only new runs require `pipelines:` config.

## Risks

**Risk 1 — Codex CLI output drift:** lenient parser, version-annotated errors, opt-in weekly smoke test.

**Risk 2 — Scheduler correctness:** addressed by pure state machine + property tests. Risk is lower in v0 than previously scoped because concurrency is hardcoded serial and single-stage eliminates dependents/outdated-propagation complexity.

**Risk 3 — Shim drift:** 3-release window, `ao pipeline migrate`, persisted data survives shim removal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All tests pass (unit + integration + property-based)
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [ ] A project with only `codeReview:` works identically to #1339 under the shim — verified by shim-equivalence tests against #1339's fixtures
- [ ] Mid-stage `pr.updated` cancels and restarts at new SHA — verified by cancellation test
- [ ] `CONFIG_CHANGED` mid-run terminates cleanly — verified by config-change test
- [ ] Driver restart: historySummaries rebuilt from store; in-flight orphaned as `worker_dead` — verified by hydration test
- [ ] Stage with no `trigger` fails config load
- [ ] Multi-stage pipeline fails config load (`stages.length > 1`) with a v1-reference pointer
- [ ] Plugin-not-installed fails config load with plugin name
- [ ] Reducer never observes an I/O result synchronously — ESLint rule restricting reducer imports
- [ ] Every event carries `now`; reducer makes no clock calls — test mocks `Date.now`
- [ ] Property tests assert 6 invariants across 10k random sequences
- [ ] Cancellation test asserts abort handler fires AND work ceases within 5s
- [ ] `SEND_TO_AGENT` command fires for findings with `status === "open"` AND `sentToAgentAt` unset; already-sent findings don't resend on retries or new-SHA runs — verified by dedicated unit test
- [ ] Observability emits 3 named event types
- [ ] Shim-removal release: persisted legacy-code-review runs queryable

## Task checklist

### Core types
- [ ] 2a — `Agent.executeTask` (optional), `AgentMode`, `supportedModes`, `TaskContext`, branded IDs
- [ ] 2b — `Pipeline`, `Stage`, engine internals (`EngineState`, `RunState`, `Event`, `Command`, `LoopState`)

### Config
- [ ] Zod schemas for `pipelines:` (single-stage enforcement)
- [ ] Validator (plugin-not-installed, mode, trigger required, per-project shim conflict)
- [ ] Validator emits warning (not error) when a v0 pipeline uses `pr.merged` or `pr.merge_ready` triggers — notes that v1 unblocks the post-merge workspace story
- [ ] `code-review-shim.ts`

### Store
- [ ] `pipeline-store.ts` with JSONL artifacts + config snapshot + GC + `loadEngineStateSnapshot`

### Engine
- [ ] `pipeline-engine/state.ts`
- [ ] `pipeline-engine/reducer.ts` — pure, every event `now`-stamped, emits `SEND_TO_AGENT` on terminal-with-findings
- [ ] `pipeline-engine/driver.ts` — FIFO, command ordering, AbortController ownership, startup hydration, `SEND_TO_AGENT` dispatch
- [ ] Reducer-imports ESLint rule

### Executor
- [ ] `agent-executor` (only kind in v0)

### Plugin
- [ ] Codex `executeTask` (review + code + answer, lenient parser, signal)
- [ ] Codex `supportedModes` manifest entry
- [ ] Deprecate `@aoagents/ao-plugin-code-review-codex`

### Lifecycle
- [ ] `LifecycleManagerDeps.pipelineEngine`
- [ ] Trigger emission with `now` stamping, `CONFIG_CHANGED` on reload
- [ ] Remove `onSessionPolled`

### CLI
- [ ] `ao pipeline runs/show/run/cancel/resume/migrate`
- [ ] `ao stage retry`
- [ ] `ao artifact list/show/dismiss/reopen/send`

### Observability
- [ ] 3 event types wired through `EMIT_OBSERVATION` → `observer.recordOperation`

### Tests
- [ ] Reducer unit tests (≥ 40 meaningful transitions)
- [ ] Reducer property tests (6 invariants via fast-check)
- [ ] Driver tests (FIFO, command ordering, hydration)
- [ ] Config-snapshot + CONFIG_CHANGED test
- [ ] Shim-equivalence tests against #1339 fixtures
- [ ] Executor tests (signal, mode validation)
- [ ] Integration: review-only, cancellation, restart

### Docs
- [ ] `docs/pipelines.md` — v0 schema + shim walkthrough + migration to v1 when it lands
- [ ] Update `CLAUDE.md` plugin standards (`executeTask` + `signal` contract)
- [ ] Changeset entry

## References

title: fix(webhooks): restore killed sessions and auto-spawn on CI failure
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1290

When a CI webhook fires for a PR, `findAffectedSessions` only matches sessions in non-terminal states. If the session was previously killed or errored, the event was silently dropped with a bare `continue`. This means the CI failure signal never reached the agent.

- Add `findRestorableSessions()` in `scm-webhooks.ts` using the existing `isRestorable()` predicate from `ao-core` (covers killed/terminated/done/errored, excludes merged)
- In the webhook route handler, when `findAffectedSessions` returns empty for a CI event, restore any matching terminal sessions and re-run `lifecycle.check()` so the existing reaction engine handles the `ci-failed` signal
- If no restorable session exists and `autoSpawnOnCIFailure` is enabled in project config, spawn a new session with a targeted prompt to investigate and fix the CI failure
- Add `autoSpawnOnCIFailure?: boolean` to `SCMWebhookConfig` in `types.ts`
- Add 4 unit tests for `findRestorableSessions` covering: non-CI events, CI events without prNumber, matched killed session, and skipping merged sessions

## Test plan

- All 601 web package tests pass
- All 432 non-web tests pass
- Typecheck and build clean across all packages
- New tests in `scm-webhooks.test.ts` cover the added function directly
