title: feat(pipeline): v3 — orchestrator-aware pipelines (scope + lifecycle triggers)
body:
**This is the v3 expansion issue.** Makes pipelines orchestrator-aware AND workstream-aware — an orchestrator spawns a group of workers on the same base branch, pipelines coordinate across them, a release-gate pipeline fires when every member merges. v0/v1/v2 semantics unchanged; v3 is additive.

Sub-issue of #1345.

## Why

The concrete motivating scenario: a human runs an orchestrator agent to ship release v2.5, which needs features A, B, and C landed together. The orchestrator wants to:

1. Decide what work to do (read the planning doc, issues list, etc.)
2. Spawn three workers W_A, W_B, W_C — each on its own feature branch off `main`
3. Let each worker open a PR and get reviewed individually
4. Run an **integrated review** across the three PRs to catch cross-feature interactions
5. Wait for all three to merge
6. Run a release-gate pipeline that bumps the version and tags

v0/v1/v2 pipelines are worker-scoped and PR-driven — no place to express "check all three workers' PRs together" or "fire when every member merges." The orchestrator agent has no pipeline primitive to coordinate sibling workers. Today the orchestrator would have to track the workstream manually and poll via CLI for everything.

v3 adds:
- **Workstream** as a first-class grouping of worker sessions sharing an orchestrator and a base branch
- **Three-scope pipeline model** — `scope: "worker" | "orchestrator" | "workstream"`
- **Workstream trigger events** — fired by the engine when aggregate conditions hold across member workers
- **Workstream predicates** for exit conditions / routes / `when` clauses that reason about member state
- Workstream creation via the existing `ao spawn --workstream <id>` CLI path — the orchestrator agent loops over its task list and spawns workers directly. No pipeline-driven spawn in v3.
- **Workbench workstream view** grouping worker cards under their workstream

The end-to-end example later in this spec shows all three scopes interacting: an orchestrator pipeline plans and spawns, each worker runs its own review pipeline, the workstream pipeline coordinates integrated review and release gating.

## Delivery phases

v3 as specified is larger than one PR. Suggested split (each phase shippable and useful on its own):

- **v3.0 — workstream tracking + orchestrator scope.** Session metadata extensions, `parentSessionId` / `workstreamId`, `ao spawn --workstream`, workstream aggregate events fired by lifecycle, `Pipeline.scope` enum with orchestrator + workstream, new predicate kinds, validator scope×trigger matrix. No UI. No `ao workstream forgive`. CLI-only triage. This is the functional core.
- **v3.1 — Workbench workstream view.** UI grouping of workers under their workstream card, scope filter extension, `ao workstream list` / `show`, `ao workstream forgive` CLI. Builds on v2's Workbench.
- **v3.2 — pipeline-driven spawn (optional, only if demanded).** `spawn-workstream` builtin + narrow `OrchestratorTaskContext.spawnWorker` capability + per-workstream member caps enforced at pipeline layer. Not necessarily shipped — only if CLI-only spawning in v3.0 turns out to be insufficient.

Phase boundaries line up with reviewable PR-scale chunks. Skipping v3.2 is explicit.

## Scope

**In:**
- Session metadata extensions: `parentSessionId?: SessionId` and `workstreamId?: string` on worker sessions
- `SessionSpawnConfig` accepts `parentSessionId` and `workstreamId` at spawn time
- `Pipeline.scope: "worker" | "orchestrator" | "workstream"` (default `"worker"` — v0/v1/v2 behavior preserved)
- Triggers:
  - `orchestrator.started`, `orchestrator.manual`
  - `workstream.created`, `workstream.worker_pr_opened`, `workstream.worker_pr_updated`, `workstream.all_pr_opened`, `workstream.worker_pr_merged`, `workstream.all_merged`, `workstream.any_stalled`, `workstream.manual`
- Predicate DSL additions (available in `routes[].when`, `exitPredicates`, and v1's existing sites):
  - `{ kind: "all_workstream_workers_in_state"; state: CanonicalSessionState }`
  - `{ kind: "all_workstream_workers_match"; predicate: Predicate }` (recursively evaluated over each member's latest run)
  - `{ kind: "workstream_member_count"; op: "eq" | "ge" | "le"; value: number }`
- Engine extensions: `EngineState.workstreams: Map<workstreamId, WorkstreamState>` with aggregate state tracked per workstream; workstream-scoped `RunState` has `linkedSessionId = workstreamId` + `memberSessionIds: SessionId[]`
- `ao spawn --workstream <id> --issue <issueId> --prompt <string>` — stamps the new worker with the given workstream ID; first spawn creates the workstream, subsequent spawns join. Orchestrator agents loop this command from their conversation turn; no new pipeline-level capability required.
- Workbench: workstream grouping view — worker cards nested under workstream cards with aggregate status
- CLI extensions:
  - `ao workstream list [project]`
  - `ao workstream show <workstreamId>` — lists members, aggregate state, pipeline runs at each scope
  - `ao spawn --workstream <id> --issue <issueId>` — spawn a worker stamped with the workstream
  - `ao pipeline run <scope-id> --pipeline X` (works for session IDs and workstream IDs uniformly)

**Not in v3:**
- **Pipeline-driven worker spawn** (`spawn-workstream` builtin, `OrchestratorTaskContext.spawnWorker`) — deferred to v3.1 if real demand appears. Orchestrator agents spawn via `ao spawn --workstream <id>` from their own turn; the pipeline engine stays out of SessionManager mutation.
- Workstream hierarchies (workstream-of-workstreams)
- Cross-project workstreams
- Pipeline-driven orchestrator spawn (orchestrator is spawned by human via `ao start`, not by a pipeline)
- Automatic workstream-level merge squashing
- Conflict resolution semantics (conflicts surface as findings; resolution is the worker's job)
- Workstream cancellation cascade policy beyond "terminate member pipelines" (the actual worker sessions continue; orchestrator agent decides what to do with them)

## Three-scope model

| Scope | linkedSessionId | Triggered by | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `worker` (default) | worker session ID | `pr.opened`, `pr.updated`, `pr.merged`, `manual` | Per-PR review (today's pr-review) |
| `orchestrator` | orchestrator session ID | `orchestrator.started`, `orchestrator.manual` | Orchestrator bootstrap, preflight checks, manual gates |
| `workstream` | workstream ID (not a session) | `workstream.*` events, `manual` | Cross-worker coordination: integrated review, release gates, fan-in |

`RunState.linkedSessionId` remains a single string. For workstream scope, it holds the `workstreamId` (which is a user-chosen string, namespaced per project). The reducer treats it opaquely.

**But `sessionManager.send(linkedSessionId, ...)` does not work for workstream IDs** — they aren't sessions. Callers that currently assume `linkedSessionId` is a real session must branch on `scope`:

- `SEND_TO_AGENT` command (v0): fires only for `scope: "worker"` runs. Workstream-scoped runs do NOT emit `SEND_TO_AGENT` — there's no single worker to notify
- `builtin/router` (v1): when invoked in a workstream-scoped run, routes to the **workstream's creating orchestrator session** (`WorkstreamState.orchestratorSessionId`) instead of `linkedSessionId`. If the orchestrator is dead or absent, the router emits a `routing.orchestrator_absent` observation and returns a `neutral` verdict — findings remain in the store for human triage
- Worker-alive pre-send check (v2): bypassed entirely for workstream-scoped runs (no single target session to check); its equivalent for routing to an orchestrator is the existing "session not found → skip" logic
- `ao pipeline show <runId>` / Workbench: for workstream-scoped runs, displays `memberSessionIds` and `orchestratorSessionId` instead of a single linked session

**What workstream-scoped runs cannot do:** send a composed prompt to "the worker" — there isn't one. If a workstream-scoped pipeline needs to dispatch work back to members, it must go through the orchestrator agent (which polls, decides, and invokes CLI) OR through worker-scoped pipelines triggered separately. The split is deliberate: workstream pipelines coordinate and produce artifacts; worker pipelines act on individual PRs.

Workstream-scoped `RunState` gains one optional field:
```typescript
interface RunState {
  // ... v0/v1/v2 fields
  memberSessionIds?: SessionId[]   // workstream scope: snapshot of members at run-create
}
```

The snapshot means workstream runs are deterministic even if new workers join mid-run.

## Workstream lifecycle

```
Workstream created (via `ao spawn --workstream <id>` with a previously-unseen ID)
  → workstream.created event

First member worker's PR opens
  → workstream.worker_pr_opened event (per member)

All member workers have an open PR
  → workstream.all_pr_opened event (fires once per workstream per transition)

Any member worker's pipeline stalls
  → workstream.any_stalled event

Any member worker merges
  → workstream.worker_pr_merged event

All member workers merged
  → workstream.all_merged event

Workstream is terminal (all_merged reached OR manually closed)
  → workstream closed; state retained for audit
```

The lifecycle manager computes workstream aggregate state on each poll cycle by walking member sessions. "All member" events are edge-triggered (fire on the transition, not on every poll after).

**Workstream closure:** a workstream closes when all members reach a terminal session state (merged, killed, done). No automatic cleanup of member sessions — the orchestrator agent decides what to do with them post-closure.

**Orchestrator death doesn't close workstreams.** A workstream outlives the orchestrator session that created it. Concrete semantics:

- Member workers continue running — they're their own sessions
- Workstream-scoped pipelines continue firing on aggregate events (lifecycle polls member sessions, not the orchestrator)
- **Orchestrator-scoped pipelines** for the dead orchestrator cannot re-trigger (no `orchestrator.manual`, no `orchestrator.started`) — but any in-flight run completes normally under the v0 run-snapshot model
- No new workers can join (no orchestrator to call `ao spawn --workstream`). A human can still invoke `ao spawn --workstream <id>` directly; the workstream accepts the new member
- Workstream records `orchestratorSessionId` but doesn't hard-depend on that session being alive; the field is reference metadata, not a foreign key constraint

This matches the "orchestrator coordinates, pipeline executes" design — the pipeline engine and workstream state are independent of whichever agent happens to be managing them at any moment.

## Session metadata additions

```
~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/sessions/{sessionName}/meta
  # existing fields: worktree, branch, status, ...
  # v3 additions:
  parentSessionId: ao-orchestrator-2         # who spawned this worker
  workstreamId: release-v2.5                 # which workstream (optional)
```

`SessionSpawnConfig` extended:
```typescript
interface SessionSpawnConfig {
  // ... existing fields
  parentSessionId?: SessionId
  workstreamId?: string          // if present, worker joins this workstream
  workstreamBaseBranch?: string  // override project default; captured per-workstream
}
```

Workstream identity is a namespaced string. The first spawn with a given `workstreamId` creates the workstream; subsequent spawns join it. Uniqueness is per-project; validator rejects spawn against a closed workstream.

## Predicates

Three new kinds compose over v1's existing Predicate DSL:

```typescript
type Predicate =
  // ... v1 kinds

  // True when every workstream member's canonical session state matches.
  | { kind: "all_workstream_workers_in_state"; state: CanonicalSessionState }

  // True when every workstream member's most recent pipeline run of the specified
  // pipeline satisfies the inner predicate. If a member has no run for that
  // pipeline, the predicate is false.
  | { kind: "all_workstream_workers_match"; pipeline: string; predicate: Predicate }

  // Size check on workstream membership.
  | { kind: "workstream_member_count"; op: "eq" | "ge" | "le"; value: number }
```

These are evaluated against the extended `PredicateCtx`:
```typescript
interface PredicateCtx {
  run: RunState
  history: RunSummary[]
  findings: Map<string, Artifact[]>
  // v3 addition — only populated for workstream-scoped runs
  workstream?: {
    id: string
    members: Array<{
      sessionId: SessionId
      canonicalState: CanonicalSessionState
      latestRunByPipeline: Map<string, RunSummary>   // for cross-pipeline predicates
    }>
  }
}
```

For worker/orchestrator-scoped runs, `workstream` is absent; workstream predicates evaluate false.

## Engine extensions

### `EngineState.workstreams`

```typescript
interface WorkstreamState {
  workstreamId: string
  orchestratorSessionId: SessionId
  projectId: string
  baseBranch: string
  memberSessionIds: Set<SessionId>
  forgivenMemberIds: Set<SessionId>              // via `ao workstream forgive`
  createdAt: string
  closed?: string                                 // ISO timestamp
  currentRunByPipeline: Map<string, PipelineRunId>
  historySummaries: Map<string, RunSummary[]>

  // Aggregate-event emission tracking. Each poll cycle, the lifecycle
  // computes current aggregate state over (memberSessionIds \ forgivenMemberIds)
  // and compares against this set. Emits workstream.* trigger events for
  // signals that hold now but didn't last cycle. Hydration on startup clears
  // this set and recomputes on next poll, which may re-emit events — consumers
  // must be idempotent OR rely on dedupe via loop-state tracking in the reducer.
  lastAggregateSignals: Set<
    | "created"
    | "all_pr_opened"
    | "all_merged"
    | "any_stalled"
  >
}
```

The `forgivenMemberIds` set is explicitly separate from `memberSessionIds` so aggregate events fired after a `forgive` operation are based on `members \ forgiven`, but history (membership records, run histories keyed on original member IDs) remains intact for audit.

### New events

```typescript
type Event =
  // ... v1 events

  // v3 additions
  | { type: "WORKSTREAM_CREATED"; now; workstreamId; orchestratorSessionId; projectId; baseBranch }
  | { type: "WORKSTREAM_MEMBER_ADDED"; now; workstreamId; memberSessionId }
  | { type: "WORKSTREAM_MEMBER_STATE_CHANGED"; now; workstreamId; memberSessionId; newState: CanonicalSessionState }
  | { type: "TRIGGER_FIRED"; now; name: TriggerEvent; ctx }   // existing; new TriggerEvent values flow through
```

### Lifecycle manager

- Detects new spawn with `workstreamId` → emits `WORKSTREAM_CREATED` (if first) or `WORKSTREAM_MEMBER_ADDED`
- On every poll cycle, walks workstream members; when aggregate state transitions (e.g., last member just opened a PR → `all_pr_opened`), emits the corresponding `TRIGGER_FIRED(workstream.*, ctx)`
- Edge-triggered: events fire once per transition, not repeatedly

### Reducer

Workstream scope adds one new code path: when a `TRIGGER_FIRED(workstream.*)` arrives, the reducer resolves `workstreamId` from the event context, looks up `EngineState.workstreams[workstreamId]` for the member snapshot, and creates a workstream-scoped `RunState` with `memberSessionIds` from the snapshot. From there, DAG resolution / executor dispatch / convergence all work identically to worker-scoped runs.

Predicate evaluator: when evaluating a workstream-scoped run's predicate, the driver populates `PredicateCtx.workstream` by reading from `EngineState.workstreams` and each member's `historySummaries`. Pure function, same determinism guarantees as v1/v2.

## Workstream creation — CLI-only in v3

v3 does **not** introduce a pipeline-level way to spawn workers. The orchestrator agent spawns workers from its own conversation turn:

```bash
ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 101 --prompt "Implement feature A"
ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 102 --prompt "Implement feature B"
ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 103 --prompt "Implement feature C"
```

The first invocation (with a workstream ID not seen before) creates the workstream and emits `WORKSTREAM_CREATED`. Subsequent invocations emit `WORKSTREAM_MEMBER_ADDED`. Both flow through the lifecycle manager to the pipeline engine.

This keeps the pipeline engine out of SessionManager mutation. If a "pipeline stage that spawns workers declaratively" turns out to matter in practice, it's a focused v3.1 addition — a `spawn-workstream` builtin with a narrow `OrchestratorTaskContext.spawnWorker` capability gated by project-level caps. Out of scope for v3.0.

## End-to-end example: release v2.5

This shows all three scopes interacting to coordinate a release across three features.

```yaml
projects:
  myapp:
    pipelines:

      # 1. WORKER-SCOPED — per-PR review (v0/v1 behavior, unchanged)
      pr-review:
        stages:
          - name: review
            trigger: { on: [pr.opened, pr.updated] }
            executor: { kind: agent, plugin: codex, mode: review }

      # 2. ORCHESTRATOR-SCOPED — bootstrap the release
      release-bootstrap:
        scope: orchestrator
        stages:
          - name: plan
            trigger: { on: [orchestrator.manual] }
            executor: { kind: agent, plugin: codex, mode: answer }
            task:
              prompt: |
                Read docs/release-v2.5.md. Produce a task list (one entry per issue
                to ship). For each: issueId, one-line title, implementation prompt.
              outputSchema: json
            # Produces: a json artifact the orchestrator agent reads to spawn
            # workers via CLI in its next turn — no pipeline-driven spawn in v3.

      # Orchestrator agent (after release-bootstrap.plan completes) reads the
      # task list and executes from its own turn:
      #
      #   ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 101 --prompt "..."
      #   ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 102 --prompt "..."
      #   ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 103 --prompt "..."
      #
      # This stamps workers with workstreamId=release-v2.5, emits
      # WORKSTREAM_CREATED + 2x WORKSTREAM_MEMBER_ADDED, and each worker's
      # pr-review pipeline fires when its PR opens.

      # 3. WORKSTREAM-SCOPED — coordinate across the release's workers
      release-gate:
        scope: workstream
        stages:
          - name: integrated-review
            trigger: { on: [workstream.all_pr_opened] }
            executor: { kind: agent, plugin: codex, mode: review }
            task:
              prompt: |
                Review the combined diff of all member worker branches.
                Focus on cross-feature interactions that per-PR review can't catch.
              outputSchema: findings

          # Gate stage — fires when all members merge, then routes to release
          # only if every member's pr-review also converged (no open findings).
          # Per v1's routes model — no stage-level `when:` field exists; routing
          # from the gate stage is how conditional activation is expressed.
          - name: gate
            trigger: { on: [workstream.all_merged] }
            executor: { kind: builtin, plugin: compose }   # no-op; this stage is a routing hinge
            routes:
              - when:
                  kind: all_workstream_workers_match
                  pipeline: pr-review
                  predicate: { kind: no_open_findings }
                to: [bump-version]
              - to: []      # default: reviews still have open findings → halt release branch

          - name: bump-version
            dependsOn: [gate]
            executor: { kind: agent, plugin: codex, mode: code }
            task:
              prompt: "Bump semver minor, update CHANGELOG with links to the merged PRs."

          - name: tag-release
            dependsOn: [bump-version]
            executor: { kind: command, command: ./scripts/tag-release.sh }

    # Per-project workstream settings (optional)
    workstreams:
      defaultBaseBranch: main
      maxConcurrent: 3             # at most 3 open workstreams per project
```

### Flow

```
Human runs ao start → orchestrator session spawns
Human: ao pipeline run ao-orchestrator-1 --pipeline release-bootstrap
                                  ↓
  [release-bootstrap] plan stage emits JSON task list artifact
                                  ↓
  Orchestrator agent reads the task list from its turn, loops:
    ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 101 --prompt "..."
    ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 102 --prompt "..."
    ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 103 --prompt "..."
                                  ↓
  Engine emits WORKSTREAM_CREATED + 2x WORKSTREAM_MEMBER_ADDED (first spawn creates; 2 more join)
                                  ↓
  Each worker W_A, W_B, W_C begins working on its issue
                                  ↓
  Each worker opens a PR → per-worker pr-review pipeline runs (3 runs, independent)
  Each emits workstream.worker_pr_opened; last one also emits workstream.all_pr_opened
                                  ↓
  [release-gate] integrated-review fires on workstream.all_pr_opened
                                  ↓
  Workers address review findings (both per-PR and integrated-review)
                                  ↓
  When all PRs merge:
    - workstream.all_merged fires
    - [release-gate] gate stage runs; its route evaluates all_workstream_workers_match
      against pr-review's per-worker runs. Routes to bump-version when every
      worker's review converged (no_open_findings); otherwise halts the release.
                                  ↓
  [release-gate] bump-version commits semver + CHANGELOG
                                  ↓
  [release-gate] tag-release tags the merge commit
                                  ↓
  Workstream closes (all members terminal); state retained in Workbench for audit
```

### What the human sees in the Workbench

```
Projects > myapp > Workstreams
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ release-v2.5                                    3 members · ⏳ │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│  W_A (ao-1)   feature A    pr_open    review: 2 findings open │
│  W_B (ao-2)   feature B    pr_open    review: 0 findings      │
│  W_C (ao-3)   feature C    pr_open    review: 0 findings      │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ Workstream pipelines:                                          │
│  release-gate  integrated-review ✓  gate ⏸ (waiting on reviews)│
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Migration and compatibility

- v0/v1/v2 configs work unchanged. `Pipeline.scope` absent = `"worker"`.
- Existing worker sessions without `parentSessionId` / `workstreamId` keep working; they just aren't members of any workstream.
- `codeReview:` shim remains worker-scoped; `legacy-code-review` pipeline never fires on workstream events.
- Opt-in: a project starts using workstreams when an orchestrator (or user via `ao spawn --workstream X`) stamps workers. No config change required to disable — just don't use the field.
- Feature flag path: v3's new lifecycle events (`WORKSTREAM_*`, trigger events) are gated behind `AO_PIPELINE_V3=1` during the rollout release; reducer handles unknown events by ignoring, so v3-emitting lifecycle + v0/v1/v2-only reducer is safe (no events fire until flag on).

## Risks

**Risk 1 — Workstream aggregate-state computation cost.** Every poll cycle walks every workstream's members. For projects with many workstreams or many workers per workstream, this is O(workstreams × members) per poll.
*Mitigation:* cache aggregate state in `EngineState.workstreams`; invalidate only when a member's canonical session state changes. Poll cost drops to O(changed members) per cycle.

**Risk 2 — Workstream membership grows without bound.** If an orchestrator agent loops too aggressively, a workstream could end up with hundreds of members before caps kick in.
*Mitigation:* `project.workstreams.maxConcurrent` caps open workstreams per project; `project.workstreams.maxMembers` caps members per workstream (default 10). Enforced at the `ao spawn` CLI validator, not only at pipeline layer — so the CLI-only v3 flow is still protected.

**Risk 4 — `workstream.all_merged` edge-triggered behavior is subtle.** If lifecycle misses a transition (crashed mid-poll, etc.), the aggregate event never fires and `release-gate` stalls.
*Mitigation:* driver hydration on startup re-walks all open workstreams and re-computes aggregate state. Missed events fire on the next recompute cycle. Property test: random crashes during workstream aggregation produce correct final aggregate state.

**Risk 5 — Orchestrator agent and workstream agent confusion.** Users may not distinguish "orchestrator-scoped pipeline" from "workstream-scoped pipeline."
*Mitigation:* Workbench visual distinction (three different scope colors/badges). Docs show the release-v2.5 example walking through when each scope applies. CLI errors disambiguate: `ao pipeline run ao-orchestrator-1 --pipeline release-gate` fails with "`release-gate` is workstream-scoped; use `ao pipeline run release-v2.5 --pipeline release-gate` instead."

**Risk 6 — Worker leaves workstream mid-run.** If an operator kills W_B, the workstream's member set shrinks. `workstream.all_merged` semantics become ambiguous.
*Mitigation:* once a workstream-scoped `RunState` is created, `memberSessionIds` is frozen. Mid-run member removal doesn't affect the in-flight run's aggregate check. New runs (next time a workstream.* event fires) use the updated member set. Operator-killed members are treated as "won't merge" by aggregate predicates unless explicitly forgiven via `ao workstream forgive <workstreamId> <memberId>`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All v0/v1/v2 tests pass unchanged — scope absent defaults to `"worker"`
- [ ] `ao spawn --workstream release-v2.5 --issue 101` creates worker with correct metadata; engine emits `WORKSTREAM_CREATED`
- [ ] Second spawn with same workstreamId emits `WORKSTREAM_MEMBER_ADDED`, not `WORKSTREAM_CREATED`
- [ ] Workstream aggregate events fire edge-triggered: `workstream.all_pr_opened` fires exactly once per transition
- [ ] Workstream-scoped pipeline run has `memberSessionIds` snapshot; mid-run member removal doesn't change it
- [ ] `all_workstream_workers_match` predicate evaluates deterministically (property test)
- [ ] `ao spawn --workstream` rejects exceeding `project.workstreams.maxConcurrent` / `maxMembers`
- [ ] End-to-end integration test for the release-v2.5 scenario (3 workers, all scopes, release-gate completes)
- [ ] Workbench workstream view groups workers under their workstream; workstream state aggregates correctly
- [ ] Scope/trigger validator catches `pr.*` in orchestrator-scoped and `orchestrator.*`/`workstream.*` in worker-scoped
- [ ] `ao pipeline run <sessionId|workstreamId> --pipeline X` works for all three scopes; resolves the kind from the ID type
- [ ] Hydration on restart re-computes workstream aggregate state from member sessions
- [ ] Property test — every workstream event eventually corresponds to a consistent aggregate state change (no missed or duplicate edge-triggered events across 10k random sequences)
- [ ] Docs: `docs/pipelines.md` gains "Workstreams" section with the release-v2.5 walkthrough

## Task checklist

### Session model
- [ ] `SessionMetadata.parentSessionId`, `workstreamId`, `workstreamBaseBranch` fields
- [ ] `SessionSpawnConfig` accepts new fields
- [ ] `SessionManager.spawn` stamps metadata; emits lifecycle event to the pipeline engine

### Config
- [ ] `Pipeline.scope` accepts `"workstream"`
- [ ] `project.workstreams` config block with `defaultBaseBranch`, `maxConcurrent`, `maxMembers`
- [ ] Validator: scope ↔ trigger compatibility for all three scopes
- [ ] Validator: `workstream`-scoped pipelines can reference `workstream.*` triggers

### Engine
- [ ] `EngineState.workstreams` map + `WorkstreamState` type
- [ ] `WORKSTREAM_*` events handled in the reducer
- [ ] Lifecycle manager emits workstream events edge-triggered on aggregate state transitions
- [ ] Reducer creates workstream-scoped `RunState` with frozen `memberSessionIds`
- [ ] Predicate evaluator populates `PredicateCtx.workstream`
- [ ] Hydration on startup re-computes workstream aggregate state

### Executors
- [ ] No new executor kinds. Router + existing builtins unchanged. Pipeline-driven spawn (`spawn-workstream`) explicitly deferred to v3.1.

### New predicates
- [ ] `all_workstream_workers_in_state`
- [ ] `all_workstream_workers_match`
- [ ] `workstream_member_count`

### CLI
- [ ] `ao spawn --workstream <id> --issue <id>` stamps metadata correctly
- [ ] `ao workstream list [project]`
- [ ] `ao workstream show <workstreamId>`
- [ ] `ao workstream forgive <workstreamId> <memberId>` — treats a killed member as "allowed to miss merge"
- [ ] `ao pipeline run <id> --pipeline X` resolves session vs workstream by prefix lookup

### Web (v2 extension)
- [ ] Workbench workstream view (grouping worker cards under workstream cards)
- [ ] Scope filter: workers / orchestrators / workstreams / all
- [ ] Workstream aggregate state displayed (member states, pipeline runs at each scope)
- [ ] Sidebar indicator includes workstreams with open findings

### Tests
- [ ] Unit: workstream state aggregation; event edge-triggering; predicate evaluation
- [ ] Integration: end-to-end release-v2.5 scenario (orchestrator + 3 workers + workstream pipeline)
- [ ] Integration: `workstream.all_merged` fires correctly after real member merges
- [ ] Integration: hydration after crash reconstructs workstream state
- [ ] Property: 9 invariants from v1 + 2 new (workstream events edge-triggered once; member snapshot frozen mid-run)
- [ ] Regression: v0/v1/v2 test suite passes

### Docs
- [ ] `docs/pipelines.md` — new "Workstreams" section with release-v2.5 example
- [ ] Scope table: worker vs orchestrator vs workstream, with trigger and use-case columns
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` update — `parentSessionId` / `workstreamId` in session metadata; workstream scope in pipeline authoring standards
- [ ] Migration note: v3 is additive, opt-in

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** #1346 (v0) and #1349 (v1) — needs reducer, validators, predicates, builtin dispatch infrastructure
- **Enhanced by:** #1350 (v2) — Workbench is where workstream view surfaces; routing to orchestrators/workstreams uses v2's composed-findings path
- v3 can technically ship without v2 but the UX would be CLI-only, which undersells the feature

## References
- Parent spec: #1345
- Foundation: #1346 (v0)
- Multi-stage: #1349 (v1)
- Workbench + chat: #1350 (v2)
- Predecessor: #1275 / PR #1339

title: fix(web): restore terminal cell metrics after xterm v6 upgrade
body:
## Summary

The xterm.js v5 → v6 upgrade (#1276) regressed the in-browser terminal: each character cell renders wider and shorter than the glyph drawn inside it, making horizontal spacing too loose and vertical spacing too tight. This PR restores correct cell metrics.

## What was broken

Four issues compounded in `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx`:

1. **`fontFamily` used `var(--font-jetbrains-mono)`.** xterm's internal character measurement ends up in canvas `ctx.font`, which cannot resolve CSS custom properties. The `var(...)` token poisoned the font string, so measurement fell back to a default font while DOM rows kept rendering in JetBrains Mono — cell width and glyph width drifted apart.
2. **xterm v6 defaults `lineHeight` to `1.0`.** Combined with JetBrains Mono's tall x-height, rows visually collide.
3. **`document.fonts.ready` resolved early.** `next/font` uses `font-display: swap`, so the initial `fit()` can run against the fallback font and xterm never re-measures when the real webfont swaps in.
4. **`p-1.5` padding on the fit-target div** skewed FitAddon's `cols`/`rows` computation.

## What changed

- Dropped `var(...)` from `fontFamily`; use a plain stack `"JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", Menlo, Monaco, "Courier New", monospace`.
- Set `lineHeight: 1.2` on the Terminal options to restore vertical breathing room.
- Added a `document.fonts` `loadingdone` listener that clears the texture atlas and re-fits when the webfont swap actually completes. Unregistered in the effect's cleanup.
- Removed `p-1.5` from the terminal ref div so FitAddon sizes against the real viewport.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck` passes (verified locally)
- [ ] `pnpm dev` and open a session terminal — glyphs fill cells cleanly, no wide horizontal air between characters, no cramped rows
- [ ] Resize the window / toggle fullscreen — cell metrics remain correct
- [ ] Adjust terminal font size via the stepper — grid stays aligned
- [ ] Hard-reload with cache disabled — first paint uses fallback font, swap in to JetBrains Mono triggers a re-fit (verify via logs / visual)
- [ ] Light and dark themes both render correctly

title: fix(web): resolve dashboard issue URLs from tracker
body:
## Summary
- resolve issue links from tracker metadata when sessions only store issue identifiers (for example `42`)
- keep existing absolute URLs unchanged and continue to enrich `issueLabel`/`issueTitle` from the resolved URL
- add regression coverage for identifier-only issue IDs in dashboard metadata enrichment

## Root cause
`sessionToDashboard()` treated `session.issueId` as a URL. For GitHub sessions spawned with an identifier, this produced invalid links like `/42` and broke downstream issue enrichment assumptions.

## What changed
- `sessionToDashboard()` now only initializes `issueUrl` when `issueId` is already an absolute URL.
- `enrichSessionIssue()` now resolves `dashboard.issueUrl` via `tracker.issueUrl()` using the available issue reference (`issueId` or existing `issueUrl`).
- metadata enrichment now runs issue enrichment when either `issueUrl` or `issueId` exists.
- tests updated to verify numeric issue identifiers are converted into valid tracker URLs.

## Why this approach
This keeps backward compatibility for sessions already storing full URLs while fixing identifier-only sessions at the existing enrichment boundary, avoiding schema changes or broader refactors.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- src/lib/__tests__/serialize.test.ts`

Closes #1213.

title: fix(web): treat exited sessions as restorable in detail view
body:
## Summary
- treat `activity: exited` as a terminal condition in `SessionDetail`, even when lifecycle status is still non-terminal
- keep restore eligibility gated by existing `NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES`
- add desktop regression coverage for crashed workers that still report `status: working`

## Root cause
`SessionDetail` only used `TERMINAL_STATUSES` to decide if a session had ended. Sessions that crashed and emitted `activity: exited` before status convergence were rendered as live and had no restore affordance.

## What changed
- include `TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES` in the detail-page terminal-ended predicate
- add a test that verifies ended placeholder + restore button for `status=working` + `activity=exited`

## Why this approach
The rest of the dashboard already uses status-or-activity terminal semantics. Aligning the detail page avoids behavioral drift without changing backend lifecycle logic.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- src/components/__tests__/SessionDetail.desktop.test.tsx`

Closes #1225.

title: fix(core): make opencode worker prompt delivery reliable
body:
## Summary
- deliver OpenCode worker prompts via post-launch runtime messaging with retries
- stop inlining worker prompt payload into the OpenCode launch command path
- add regression coverage proving prompt delivery + metadata state for OpenCode workers

## Root cause
OpenCode worker spawns relied on inline launch-command prompt delivery. If the OpenCode startup flow did not complete cleanly, the prompt could be dropped while AO still marked it as delivered.

## What changed
- in worker `spawn()`, treat OpenCode as a post-launch prompt-delivery flow
- pass `prompt: undefined` to OpenCode launch config so launch only establishes session/runtime
- send the composed prompt through `runtime.sendMessage()` using existing retry logic
- preserve existing behavior for other agent plugins
- add test coverage for OpenCode worker prompt delivery and `promptDelivered` metadata

## Why this approach
This reuses an existing, battle-tested delivery path and keeps the fix tightly scoped to OpenCode worker spawning without changing plugin contracts or broader session lifecycle behavior.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/session-manager/spawn.test.ts`

Closes #1304.

title: fix(core): stop foreign legacy session kind misclassification
body:
## Summary
- derive session kind during metadata reconstruction using project-scoped orchestrator ID rules
- pass explicit `sessionKind` into canonical lifecycle parsing from `sessionFromMetadata`
- add regression assertion that foreign-prefix legacy bare orchestrator records remain `worker` in-memory

## Root cause
When reading metadata, `parseCanonicalLifecycle()` could infer orchestrator kind from `sessionId.endsWith("-orchestrator")` when no role was present. That fallback misclassified foreign-prefix legacy records in-memory even though on-disk repair no longer stamped `role: orchestrator`.

## What changed
- introduced `deriveSessionKindFromMetadata()` in session manager reconstruction flow
- threaded `sessionKind` through `sessionFromMetadata` options into lifecycle parsing
- updated read/get call sites to provide project session prefix context
- extended existing issue #1048 regression test to assert in-memory `lifecycle.session.kind === "worker"`

## Why this approach
This keeps canonical lifecycle parsing deterministic at read time with project context, without changing persisted metadata format or broad lifecycle behavior.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/session-manager/query.test.ts`

Closes #1323.

title: fix(scm-github): avoid conflict misclassification for draft/blocking states
body:
## Summary
- compute `noConflicts` from explicit `mergeable === CONFLICTING` only
- prevent blocked/draft/unknown GitHub merge states from being interpreted as merge conflicts
- add regression assertions for `BLOCKED` and `UNKNOWN` mergeability outcomes

## Root cause
`getMergeability()` set `noConflicts` to true only for `MERGEABLE`. For draft or branch-protection-blocked PRs, GitHub can return non-`MERGEABLE` values without actual conflicts, which caused conflict-based reactions to trigger via `!noConflicts`.

## What changed
- updated conflict derivation to treat only `CONFLICTING` as a conflict signal
- updated tests to assert non-conflicting behavior for `BLOCKED`/`UNKNOWN` states

## Why this approach
It matches GitHub semantics more closely and keeps conflict reactions tied to explicit conflict data, while preserving existing blockers for review/branch-protection/draft conditions.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-github test -- test/index.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts --testNamePattern "merge conflict"`

Closes #1314.

title: fix: ETag Guard mishandles HTTP 304, SSE stream controller-closed spam
body:
## Summary

Three runtime issues observed in the web dashboard (`pnpm dev`) — two are bugs, one is transient/informational.

---

## Issue 1: ETag Guard treats HTTP 304 as failure (P1 — wastes API quota)

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` (lines 336–381, 394–440)

**Symptom:**
```
[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for owner/repo: Command failed: gh api ... gh: HTTP 304
```

**Root cause:** The `gh` CLI exits with a non-zero exit code on HTTP 304 (Not Modified). This causes `execFileAsync` to throw, so the code that correctly handles 304 in stdout (line 357) is **never reached**. Execution jumps to the catch block (line 373), which:
1. Logs a misleading "PR list check failed" warning
2. Returns `true` (assume changed), triggering a redundant GraphQL batch query

**Impact:** The entire 2-Guard ETag caching optimization is defeated — every poll cycle falls through to the expensive GraphQL batch call, wasting GitHub API quota. The caching logic is correct in theory but broken in practice because of how `gh` handles 304.

**Fix:** In both catch blocks (Guard 1 line 373, Guard 2 line 431), detect "HTTP 304" in the error message and return `false` (unchanged) instead of `true`.

---

## Issue 2: SSE stream — unhandled "Controller is already closed" rejections (P2)

**File:** `packages/web/src/app/api/events/route.ts`

**Symptom:**
```
TypeError: Invalid state: Controller is already closed
⨯ unhandledRejection: TypeError: Invalid state: Controller is already closed
```
Repeated many times per client disconnect.

**Root cause:** When an SSE client disconnects, `cancel()` fires and clears the `setInterval` timers. But async polling callbacks (`void (async () => { ... })()` at line 130) that were already in-flight continue to execute and call `controller.enqueue()` on the closed controller. The inner try/catch (line 182) handles some cases, but the race window between `cancel()` and in-flight async callbacks produces unhandled rejections.

**Impact:** Floods the server console with unhandled rejection errors. Not a data-loss bug, but it pollutes logs and could mask real errors.

**Fix:** Track a `closed` boolean flag, set it in `cancel()`, and guard every `controller.enqueue()` call with a check on that flag.

---

## Issue 3: GraphQL batch — TLS handshake timeout (P3 — transient)

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` (lines 547–594)

**Symptom:**
```
[GraphQL Batch Warning] Batch enrichment partially failed: ... Post "https://api.github.com/graphql": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

**Root cause:** Transient network issue — GitHub API latency or local network hiccup during TLS negotiation. The code already handles this gracefully (logs warning, continues to next batch, retries next poll cycle).

**Impact:** Low — affected PRs miss enrichment for one cycle. Fixing Issue 1 would reduce exposure since ETag caching would skip unnecessary batch calls.

**No code change needed** unless this becomes recurring, in which case adding retry-with-backoff for TLS errors specifically would help.

---

## Priority

| Priority | Issue | Reason |
|----------|-------|--------|
| P1 | ETag Guard 304 | Defeats caching, wastes API quota every poll cycle |
| P2 | SSE controller closed | Log noise, unhandled rejections |
| P3 | TLS timeout | Transient, already handled |

title: ao start goes to orchestrator selector instead of last used orchestrator when multiple orchestrators exist
body:
## Problem
When there are multiple orchestrators, running `ao start` takes me to the orchestrator selector page instead of restoring or opening the last used orchestrator automatically.

## Expected behavior
If there is a clearly last-used orchestrator, `ao start` should take me directly to that orchestrator instead of forcing me through the selector page.

## Current behavior
- Multiple orchestrators exist
- Run `ao start`
- It opens the orchestrator selector page
- I have to manually choose the orchestrator I was already using

## Why this matters
- Adds friction to the common resume workflow
- Breaks the expectation that `ao start` resumes the most recent working context
- Makes repeated orchestrator usage slower when several orchestrators exist

## Suggested behavior
- Track the last used orchestrator
- If it still exists and is restorable/usable, have `ao start` open that orchestrator directly
- Fall back to the selector only when there is no unambiguous last-used orchestrator or when the last one cannot be resumed

## Notes
This is specifically about the case where multiple orchestrators are present and the user is trying to continue with the one they used most recently.

title: bug(web): session detail page shows CI as failing when CI is passing (3-way OR + 5-min cache)
body:
## Problem

The session detail page's PR card shows a red **\"CI failing\"** blocker chip when CI on the actual PR is passing (or has no failing checks). The chip sticks around after CI recovers from a transient failure and doesn't clear on navigation.

## Reproduction

1. Open a session whose PR had any transient CI failure (then recovered, re-run green, etc.).
2. Navigate to the session detail page.
3. Observe: \"CI failing\" chip is shown even though `gh pr checks <pr>` reports all checks green.

## Root cause

Three independent sources feed the \"CI failing\" chip via an **OR** — a single stale source keeps the chip up.

### Smoking gun: 3-way OR in `buildBlockerChips`

`packages/web/src/components/SessionDetailPRCard.tsx:39-42`:

```ts
const ciIsFailing =
  pr.ciStatus === CI_STATUS.FAILING ||           // live SCM (cached ≤5min)
  lifecyclePrReason === \"ci_failing\" ||          // lifecycle-derived reason
  lifecycleStatus === \"ci_failed\";               // legacy metadata[\"status\"]
```

If **any one** of these is stale, the chip stays red. Line 50 then reads `pr.ciChecks.filter(c => c.status === \"failed\").length` — which is often 0 when the lifecycle sources are the stale ones — so the chip renders with the generic text \"CI failing\" (no check name), which matches the symptom the user is seeing.

### Stale source #1 — `pr.ciStatus` from 5-min web cache

`packages/web/src/lib/cache.ts`:

- Line 13: `DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000;` — **actual default is 5 minutes**.
- Line 5 (file header): `\"Default TTL: 60 seconds\"` — **docstring lies**.
- Line 108: `/** Global PR enrichment cache (60s TTL) */` — **comment lies**.
- Line 109: `export const prCache = new TTLCache<PREnrichmentData>();` — no TTL override.

`packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:280-296` — when cache hits, we **unconditionally overwrite** `dashboard.pr.ciStatus` from cache and return early, with no freshness signaling. No invalidation hook on CI state changes elsewhere.

→ Once `ciStatus: \"failing\"` lands in the cache, the page shows it for up to 5 min even after CI turns green.

### Stale source #2 — `lifecyclePrReason === \"ci_failing\"`

Derived from `session.lifecycle.pr.reason`. This is updated by the lifecycle poll loop, which in turn reads `getCISummary` / the GraphQL PR-enrichment batch. Two paths can leave it stale:

- `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts:227-241`: Guard 2 (commit-status ETag check) only runs when the cached PR record has a non-null `headSha`. If a PR was first enriched with `headSha: null`, subsequent CI-only changes are invisible until Guard 1 (PR-list ETag) changes — which it won't for CI-only transitions.
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1345-1356`: `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails` clears the fingerprint when exiting `ci_failed`, but the lifecycle **reason** on the PR is computed upstream from enrichment data. Stale enrichment → stuck reason.

### Stale source #3 — `metadata[\"status\"] === \"ci_failed\"`

Session metadata on disk. Written by `updateSessionMetadata(…)` with the result of `deriveLegacyStatus(session.lifecycle, session.status)`. Inherits staleness from source #2 and only gets corrected on a later poll cycle that sees fresh enrichment data.

## Why users feel this bug acutely on session detail

- **Dashboard list view** gets a full poll cycle every 5s via SSE (`useSessionEvents`). Stale cache entries get overwritten quickly.
- **Session detail page** renders from a single API fetch that happily serves the 5-min cached row without a force-refresh path. You land on it and see the 5-min-old state.

## Suggested fix direction (not scope of this issue, just signposting)

1. **Narrow the OR.** The chip should trust exactly one source. Since the lifecycle reason is the policy-layer signal and `pr.ciStatus` is the live SCM signal, pick one and drop the other two from the blocker-chip expression.
2. **Fix the TTL lie.** Either make `DEFAULT_TTL_MS` actually 60s (match docs) or update both comments to 5 min. Current divergence is a trap.
3. **Invalidate on lifecycle CI transition.** When `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails` clears the fingerprint (CI recovered), also invalidate the web `prCache` entry for that PR so the next render fetches fresh.
4. **Fix graphql-batch Guard 2 fallthrough.** If a PR is cached with `headSha: null`, re-check on every poll instead of relying on Guard 1 to eventually notice an unrelated PR-list change.

## Environment

- Seen on `main` (as of 2026-04-20), session detail page.
- Web `prCache` default TTL: 5 min (despite docs).

title: fix: dashboard PR number doesn't update when PR is closed and a new one is opened
body:
## Bug Description

When a session creates a PR, then closes it and opens a new one (e.g., due to branch rebasing or targeting wrong base branch), the dashboard continues showing the old PR number.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Session creates a PR (e.g., PR A)
2. That PR is closed (e.g., wrong base branch)
3. Session creates a new PR (PR B) from the same branch
4. Dashboard still shows PR A for that session

## Expected Behavior

The dashboard should display the latest/active PR number after the old one is closed.

## Actual Behavior

The dashboard continues showing the stale PR number even after it's been closed and a new PR has been created.

## Likely Cause

The session metadata stores the PR number on first creation (`ao report pr-created`) but doesn't update it when a new PR is reported or when the SCM plugin detects the old PR was closed. The lifecycle manager or SCM tracker likely needs to:

1. Listen for PR close events and clear the stored PR reference, OR
2. Allow `pr-created` reports to overwrite the existing PR number, OR
3. Track PR history and always display the most recent open PR

## Environment

- Running via `ao` CLI with GitHub tracker
- Observed on a fork repo (harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator)
- Session branch: `session/aa-43`
- Old PR was closed, new PR was opened, dashboard still shows old one

title: Worker session orchestrator button navigates to lexicographically smallest orchestrator instead of most recent one
body:
## Problem
On a worker session page, the orchestrator button can take me to the wrong orchestrator when multiple orchestrators are alive. It appears to pick the lexicographically smallest session id instead of the most recently used orchestrator.

## Example
I had both `aa-orchestrator-3` and `aa-orchestrator-4` alive. I had used `aa-orchestrator-4` most recently, but clicking the orchestrator button took me to `aa-orchestrator-3`.

## Expected behavior
The worker session page should navigate to the most relevant orchestrator, which in this case should be the most recently used / most recently active orchestrator, not the lexicographically smallest id.

## Current behavior
- Multiple orchestrators are alive
- Worker session page shows an orchestrator button
- Clicking it navigates to the wrong orchestrator
- Selection appears to be based on lexical ordering rather than recency/relevance

## Why this matters
- Sends the user into the wrong context
- Breaks the resume workflow when several orchestrators exist
- Makes orchestrator navigation feel arbitrary and unreliable

## Suggested fix
When multiple orchestrators are available, the button should prefer:
1. the orchestrator most recently used by the user, or
2. the most recently active orchestrator,
with a clear fallback only if recency cannot be determined.

It should not default to the lexicographically smallest orchestrator id.

title: Add  to fully wipe a project's local AO state and reinitialize from scratch
body:
## Problem
There is currently no single command to completely reset an AO project on a machine. Over time, a project can accumulate local AO state such as archives, worker sessions, orchestrator sessions, project config/state, and other persisted metadata.

If I want to make AO treat the project as if it is being seen for the first time on this machine, I should not have to manually hunt through all the AO-managed files and directories.

## Requested behavior
Add an `ao reset`-style command that fully deletes a project's local AO state and returns it to a clean, first-run state on that machine.

## What it should remove
For the targeted project, the reset should remove things like:
- archived AO history/state for the project
- worker sessions
- orchestrator sessions
- project-specific AO config/state
- cached metadata and local persisted session/project records
- any other AO-managed local data that would cause the project to be remembered

In other words, after `ao reset`, AO should behave as though the project has never been configured locally before.

## Expected outcome
After running the reset command for a project:
- there should be no surviving local AO history for that project
- no worker/orchestrator sessions should remain
- no archived session state should remain
- the next AO interaction should require project setup/configuration as if it were the first time

## Why this matters
- makes it easy to recover from local AO state drift or corruption
- gives users a clean way to start over during testing and development
- avoids error-prone manual deletion of hidden AO-managed files/directories
- improves confidence that a reset is complete and not partial

## Possible UX
Something like:

```bash
ao reset
ao reset <project>
ao reset -p <project>
```

Because this is destructive, it should probably:
- show exactly what will be deleted
- require confirmation (unless `--yes` is passed)
- clearly scope the reset to one project unless the user explicitly requests a broader/global reset

## Notes
The important part is that this is not just session cleanup. It should wipe the full local AO footprint for a project so the project is effectively brand new to AO on that machine.

title: Add $schema property support to agent-orchestrator.yaml
body:
## Description

When editing `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, there's no autocomplete or validation support in IDEs. Adding a `` property that points to a JSON Schema would enable:

- **IDE autocomplete** for all config fields
- **Inline validation** — catch typos and invalid values before runtime
- **Hover documentation** for each property

## Proposed Solution

1. Generate (or author) a JSON Schema for the full `agent-orchestrator.yaml` config format.
2. Publish the schema (e.g. on schemaStore or as a raw URL in the repo).
3. Add `: <url>` to the default `agent-orchestrator.yaml` template / docs.

## Example

```yaml
# agent-orchestrator.yaml
$schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/main/schema/config.schema.json
```

This would immediately light up autocomplete in VS Code, JetBrains, and any editor with YAML schema support.

The `ao` CLI has a growing set of subcommands and flags. Shell completion would improve developer experience by enabling quick discovery and reducing typos — especially for less-frequently-used flags.

- add a built-in Jira tracker plugin for AO

- add tests and docs for the new plugin

## Included

- built-in plugin wiring in core/web/CLI config docs
- Jira Cloud config via env and tracker overrides
- `getIssue`, `listIssues`, `createIssue`, `updateIssue`, `isCompleted`, `issueUrl`, `issueLabel`, `branchName`, `generatePrompt`

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-jira typecheck`

title: Lifecycle manager reports CI failure when all GitHub checks are passing
body:
## Problem

The lifecycle manager sends a CI-failing notification/status transition even though all GitHub Actions checks are passing. Observed on PR #1363 — all 10 checks (Lint, Typecheck, Test, Test (Web), Integration Tests, Coverage Report, NPM Audit, Scan for Secrets, Dependency Review, Test Fresh Onboarding) completed successfully, yet the orchestrator still reported a CI failure state.

## Expected behavior

When all CI checks on the PR are green, the lifecycle manager should transition the session to the appropriate passing state (e.g., `ci_passed` / `pr_open`) — not `ci_failed`.

## Possible causes

- Stale CI status cached from a previous commit that was still being polled when the new push landed
- Race condition between the SCM plugin's CI status check and GitHub propagating the final check status
- Mismatch between which checks the lifecycle manager considers "required" vs what GitHub reports

## Steps to reproduce

1. Push a commit that passes all CI checks
2. Observe the lifecycle manager polling the PR's CI status
3. Despite all checks passing on GitHub, the session transitions to or remains in `ci_failed`

## Context

Observed during work on PR #1363 (`feat/1359` branch).

title: bug: spawn prompt message delivered but enter key not pressed
body:
## Description

When spawning a session with `ao spawn --prompt "..."`, the prompt message is delivered to the tmux session but the enter key is not pressed. The text appears in the terminal but is never submitted to the agent, so the agent sits idle without receiving the instruction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ao spawn --prompt "Wait for further instructions."`
2. Session spawns successfully
3. Attach to the session — the prompt text is visible in the terminal but was never submitted (no newline/enter sent)

## Expected Behavior

The prompt message should be fully sent to the agent (including pressing enter) so the agent receives and acts on it.

## Actual Behavior

The message text appears in the terminal buffer but the enter key (`Enter`/`C-m`) is never sent, so the agent never processes the instruction.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- AO version: latest main

title: feat: Add worker-to-orchestrator communication channel
body:
## Problem

Currently, communication between the orchestrator and worker agents is one-directional. The orchestrator can send messages to workers via `ao send`, but there is no mechanism for worker agents to communicate back to the orchestrator.

This means workers cannot:
- Signal that they need human/orchestrator judgment on a decision
- Report blockers that require orchestrator-level coordination
- Request information that only the orchestrator has context for
- Escalate issues that affect other sessions (e.g., dependency conflicts between workers)
- Ask for clarification on ambiguous requirements

## Current Workaround

Workers can only passively signal via `ao report` states like `needs-input` or `waiting`, which the orchestrator must poll for. There is no way to send a structured message or question back upstream.

## Proposed Solution

Add a worker-to-orchestrator communication primitive, such as:

```bash
# From within a worker session
ao signal <message>
ao escalate "I found a breaking change that affects ao-72's work too"
ao ask "Should I use approach A or B for the auth refactor?"
```

### Requirements:
- Workers should be able to send structured messages to the orchestrator
- Messages should appear in `ao status` or trigger a notification
- The orchestrator should be able to respond via `ao send` (existing mechanism)
- Messages should be persisted in session metadata for audit trail
- Support different message types: question, blocker, info, escalation

### Possible Implementation:
- Add an `ao signal` or `ao ask` CLI command available inside worker sessions
- Store messages in session metadata (e.g., `messages.jsonl`)
- Surface unread worker messages in `ao status` output
- Optionally trigger notifiers (desktop/slack/webhook) for urgent escalations
- Dashboard could show a "messages" tab or inline alerts on session cards

## Why This Matters

- Enables true bidirectional orchestration instead of poll-based status checking
- Reduces time workers spend stuck waiting for orchestrator to notice they need help
- Improves coordination for complex multi-agent workflows where sessions have dependencies
- Makes the orchestrator pattern more robust for real-world usage

## Context

In practice, workers often hit decision points or blockers that require orchestrator input. Without a communication channel, the only signal is a state change that the orchestrator must notice during polling, with no context about what the worker actually needs.

title: deploy-vps: run deploy as aoagent instead of root
body:
## Summary

- Change the `appleboy/ssh-action` SSH user in `.github/workflows/deploy-vps.yml` from `root` to `aoagent`, and update the working directory in the same step from `/root/agent-orchestrator` to `/home/aoagent/agent-orchestrator`.

Running the deploy as `aoagent` removes that drift at the source.

- Working-tree path change is cosmetic: `/root/agent-orchestrator` is a symlink to `/home/aoagent/agent-orchestrator`, so we point the deploy at the canonical path.

title: fix: clear stale dashboard PR ownership
body:
## Summary
- clear closed-unmerged PR references from canonical lifecycle metadata so sessions stop carrying a stale PR URL/number
- re-run branch-based PR detection when a tracked PR closes and immediately attach a replacement PR if one already exists
- add regression tests for closed PR cleanup and replacement PR detection, plus a changeset entry

## Root Cause Analysis
The stale dashboard PR number came from a mismatch between raw session metadata and canonical lifecycle state:

1. PR ownership was persisted in two places:
   - legacy/raw metadata via `pr=<url>`
   - canonical lifecycle payload via `statePayload.pr.url` / `statePayload.pr.number`
2. The dashboard read path reconstructed `session.pr` from canonical lifecycle first, then fell back to raw metadata.
3. When lifecycle polling saw a PR become `closed`, it changed only the PR state/reason. It did not clear the stored PR URL/number.
4. Because `session.pr` stayed non-null, the poller never re-entered the `scm.detectPR()` path, so a replacement PR on the same branch was never discovered.
5. Even if a new PR was opened and the `gh pr create` wrapper updated raw metadata, the dashboard still preferred the stale canonical lifecycle PR reference.

That combination left the UI pinned to the first PR number indefinitely.

## Fix
- On `closed` PRs, clear the canonical PR URL/number when no replacement PR exists.
- On `closed` PRs, attempt `scm.detectPR()` for the session branch and attach the new PR immediately when found.
- Preserve merged PR identity; only closed-unmerged PRs are cleared/replaced.

## Validation
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm test`

Fixes ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator#1361.

title: Support custom user instructions on top of worker/orchestrator defaults
body:
## Problem

Currently, worker and orchestrator agents use predefined system prompts/instructions. There is no way for users to inject their own additional instructions on top of what's already defined.

## Use Case

Users may want to:
- Enforce project-specific conventions (e.g., "always use functional components", "follow our error handling pattern")
- Add domain-specific context (e.g., "this is a fintech app, be careful with PII")
- Override or extend default behavior without forking the config

## Proposed Solution

Add a `customInstructions` field (or similar) to the agent config that gets appended to the system prompt for both worker and orchestrator modes. Configurable per-project in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`.

```yaml
# Example
agents:
  worker:
    customInstructions: |
      - Always use TypeScript strict mode
      - Follow the existing test patterns in the repo
  orchestrator:
    customInstructions: |
      - Prefer splitting large tasks into smaller ones
```

## Requirements

- Custom instructions are **appended** to (not replacing) the default prompts
- Works for both worker and orchestrator agent types
- Configurable via `agent-orchestrator.yaml`
- No breaking change to existing configs (field is optional)
