title: feat(plugin): implement kimicode agent plugin
body:
## Summary

Add a new agent plugin for [kimicode](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli) so users can select it as the coding agent in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, matching the same standards as the existing agent plugins (`agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-aider`, `agent-opencode`).

## Motivation

AO's plugin model already supports pluggable AI tools via the `Agent` slot. kimicode is a new coding agent we want to make available alongside the existing four. Dashboard features (PR tracking, cost display, activity/state detection, session resume) should all work the same way for kimicode sessions as they do for the other agents.

## Scope

Create a new plugin package at `packages/plugins/agent-kimicode/` that fully implements the `Agent` interface from `@composio/ao-core`, following the conventions documented in `CLAUDE.md` (§ Plugin Standards / Agent Plugin Implementation Standards).

### Package layout

```
packages/plugins/agent-kimicode/
├── package.json          # @composio/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode
├── tsconfig.json         # extends ../../../tsconfig.base.json
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts          # manifest + create + detect (default export)
│   └── __tests__/        # vitest tests
```

- Package name: `@composio/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode`
- `manifest.name`: `"kimicode"`
- `manifest.slot`: `"agent" as const`

### Required interface methods

All methods from the `Agent` interface must be implemented:

| Method | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| `getLaunchCommand` | Shell command to launch kimicode in the worktree |
| `getEnvironment` | Must set `AO_SESSION_ID`, optional `AO_ISSUE_ID`, and prepend `~/.ao/bin` to `PATH` via `buildAgentPath()` |
| `detectActivity` | Terminal-output classifier; match actual kimicode prompts (test against real output, do not guess) |
| `getActivityState` | Follow the 5-step cascade in CLAUDE.md — process check → actionable states → native signal → **JSONL entry fallback (mandatory)** → null |
| `isProcessRunning` | Support both tmux (TTY + `ps` regex) and process runtime (PID signal-0). Regex must match both the node wrapper and the actual binary name |
| `getSessionInfo` | Extract summary, cost, and native session ID from whatever introspection kimicode exposes; return `null` if unavailable |

### Optional interface methods (implement where applicable)

| Method | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| `getRestoreCommand` | Implement if kimicode supports resuming a prior session; return `null` otherwise |
| `setupWorkspaceHooks` | **Required** for PR tracking. If kimicode has native post-tool hooks, wire them up; otherwise call `setupPathWrapperWorkspace(workspacePath)` |
| `postLaunchSetup` | Re-ensure hooks, resolve binary path, etc. |
| `recordActivity` | Delegate to `recordTerminalActivity(workspacePath, output, (o) => this.detectActivity(o))` unless kimicode emits its own fully-featured JSONL |

### Activity detection pattern

Pick one of the two documented patterns based on what kimicode provides:

1. **Native JSONL** (like Claude Code / Codex) — if kimicode writes a rich JSONL log including tool calls, permission requests, and errors, map entries to activity states.
2. **AO Activity JSONL** (like Aider / OpenCode) — otherwise, implement `recordActivity` via `recordTerminalActivity` and read via `readLastActivityEntry` → `checkActivityLogState` → `getActivityFallbackState`.

All 6 lifecycle states must be reachable: `spawning`, `active`, `ready`, `idle`, `waiting_input`, `blocked`, `exited`.

### Tests

`src/__tests__/index.test.ts` using Vitest. At minimum, cover:

- Manifest values (`name`, `slot`, `version`)
- `create()` return shape
- All public methods happy path
- Error paths (missing binary, invalid config)
- **`getActivityState` required cases (from CLAUDE.md):**
  1. Returns `exited` when process is not running
  2. Returns `waiting_input` from JSONL at a permission prompt
  3. Returns `blocked` from JSONL on error
  4. Returns `active` from native signal when recently active
  5. Returns `active` from JSONL entry fallback when native signal fails (fresh entry)
  6. Returns `idle` from JSONL entry fallback with age decay (old entry)
  7. Returns `null` when both native signal and JSONL are unavailable

Mock external CLIs, file I/O, and HTTP calls. Use `beforeEach` to reset mocks.

### Wiring

- Add the package to the pnpm workspace (inherits from root `pnpm-workspace.yaml`).
- Add `@composio/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode` as a dependency of `packages/cli` so it is bundled into the CLI like the other agent plugins.
- Register it in the plugin registry loading code if registration is explicit (check how `agent-codex` is wired).
- Update default YAML / example config (`agent-orchestrator.yaml` template, onboarding wizard if applicable) so users discover the option.

### Documentation

- Add a section to any agent-comparison docs (e.g. README plugin table) listing kimicode.
- Ensure `detect()` returns `true` only when the kimicode binary is available on `PATH`.

## Constraints

- TypeScript strict mode, no `any` (CLAUDE.md § Code Style).
- Use `shellEscape()` from core for all command arguments — no raw string interpolation into shell commands.
- No hardcoded secrets; use `process.env` and throw with a descriptive message if a required env var is missing.
- Validate plugin config once in `create()`, store via closure — don't re-validate per call.
- File max 800 lines; keep `src/index.ts` lean by extracting helpers into sibling files if it grows.
- Follow existing conventions in `packages/plugins/agent-codex/` as the closest template (PATH-wrapper pattern + native-ish JSONL signal).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/plugins/agent-kimicode/` package created with the layout above
- [ ] Implements every required `Agent` method; optional methods implemented where kimicode supports them
- [ ] All 6 activity states reachable via `getActivityState` over the session lifetime
- [ ] Mandatory `getActivityState` test cases pass
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode test` passes
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and full `pnpm test` all pass
- [ ] `detect()` returns `true` on a machine with kimicode installed, `false` otherwise
- [ ] Selecting `agent: kimicode` in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` spawns a working session; the dashboard shows correct activity states and PR tracking
- [ ] `~/.ao/bin` PATH wrappers (or native hooks) install correctly — PRs created from a kimicode session appear in the dashboard

## References

- Standards: `CLAUDE.md` § Plugin Standards / Agent Plugin Implementation Standards
- Existing plugins for reference: `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code`, `packages/plugins/agent-codex`, `packages/plugins/agent-aider`, `packages/plugins/agent-opencode`
- Core utilities: `@composio/ao-core` exports (see `CLAUDE.md` § Core Utilities Available to Plugins)
- Interface: `Agent` type in `packages/core/src/types.ts`

title: feat(web): make project sidebar resizable with min/max width limits
body:
## Summary

Make the project sidebar in the web dashboard horizontally resizable via a drag handle on its right edge, with a clamped width range and persisted preference.

## Motivation

The sidebar is currently a fixed width. On wide monitors this wastes horizontal space; on narrower screens with long project names it truncates. A user-controlled resize handle is the standard fix and lets each user pick what fits their setup.

## Scope

### UI behavior

- Drag handle on the right edge of the sidebar (`packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx`).
  - Cursor changes to `col-resize` on hover.
  - Grab area should be wide enough to hit easily (6–8px) but render as a 1px visual line.
- Dragging adjusts the sidebar width in real time.
- **Clamped limits:**
  - Min width: `200px` (enough to keep project names + status dots visible; below this, names become unusable).
  - Max width: `480px` (keeps the main content area readable on 1280px laptops).
- Double-clicking the handle resets to the default width.
- While dragging, disable text selection on the document body (add `user-select: none` on the handle's `mousedown`, remove on `mouseup`).

### Persistence

- Store the width in `localStorage` under a stable key (e.g. `ao:sidebar-width`).
- Read it on mount; fall back to the current default if missing or out of range.
- Clamp stored value to the min/max limits on read (protects against future range changes).

### Responsive

- On mobile / narrow viewports where the sidebar is collapsed or hidden, the resize handle should not render. Check the existing mobile breakpoint behavior in `ProjectSidebar.tsx` before adding.

### Styling constraints (from CLAUDE.md)

- Tailwind utility classes only — no inline `style=` attributes for layout, **except** for the dynamic `width` value on the sidebar root (unavoidable for a resizable element). Use a CSS custom property (`--sidebar-width`) set via `style={{ '--sidebar-width': \`\${width}px\` }}` and reference it in a Tailwind arbitrary value class: `w-[var(--sidebar-width)]`. This keeps the exception minimal and contained.
- Dark theme preserved.
- No new UI component libraries — implement the drag handle with plain React + mouse events. Do not pull in `react-resizable-panels`, `re-resizable`, etc.
- No animation libraries.

## Implementation notes

- Use a `useRef` on the sidebar root and a `useState` for the width.
- Attach `mousemove` / `mouseup` listeners on `window` during drag (set on `mousedown`, cleaned up on `mouseup`).
- Throttle to `requestAnimationFrame` so drag stays smooth on re-renders.
- Extract the hook into `packages/web/src/hooks/useResizable.ts` if it grows past ~40 lines — one file per concern.
- Keep `ProjectSidebar.tsx` under the 400-line limit (currently check the file size before refactoring).

## Tests

`packages/web/src/components/__tests__/ProjectSidebar.test.tsx`:

- Default width renders when no `localStorage` value is present.
- Persisted width is applied on mount.
- Out-of-range persisted width is clamped on read.
- `mousedown` on the handle + `mousemove` updates the width; `mouseup` persists it.
- Width below min or above max is clamped during drag.
- Double-click handle resets to default.
- Mobile breakpoint: handle is not rendered when the sidebar is in collapsed/mobile mode.

Use `@testing-library/react` + `userEvent`. Mock `localStorage` via `vi.spyOn(Storage.prototype, ...)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sidebar has a visible, discoverable drag handle on its right edge with `col-resize` cursor.
- [ ] Dragging resizes within `[200, 480]` pixels; values outside the range are clamped.
- [ ] Double-click resets to default.
- [ ] Width persists across page reloads via `localStorage`.
- [ ] No text selection artifacts while dragging.
- [ ] Drag handle hidden on the existing mobile breakpoint.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test` passes with new tests.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web typecheck` and `pnpm lint` pass.
- [ ] Dark theme visually unchanged outside the new handle.
- [ ] `ProjectSidebar.tsx` stays under 400 lines.

## Out of scope

- Collapsible sidebar (separate feature — open a follow-up if desired).
- Resizing other panels (session list, terminal split, etc.).

## References

- Component: `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx`
- Tests dir: `packages/web/src/components/__tests__/`
- Styling conventions: `CLAUDE.md` § Web / Styling, Constraints C-01/C-02/C-05/C-07

title: fix(web): killing session from session page shows error instead of returning to dashboard
body:
## Summary

When a worker session is killed via the Terminate button on the session detail page (`/sessions/[id]`), the dashboard does not navigate away. Instead the now-invalid session URL renders the error boundary (`error.tsx`) because the session no longer exists / is no longer restorable.

Expected: after a successful kill from the session detail page, navigate the user back to the dashboard (or the project view they came from).

## Repro

1. Spawn a worker session: `ao spawn`.
2. Open the session detail page in the browser: `/sessions/<id>`.
3. Click the Terminate button.
4. Observe: the page transitions to an error screen (the App Router `error.tsx` boundary) rather than going back to `/`.

## Root cause (likely)

- Kill handler POSTs to `/api/sessions/[id]/kill` and updates local state.
- The session detail page re-renders. Either:
  - SSE / page data fetch returns 404 / error for the killed session and throws, triggering `error.tsx`, or
  - Server component re-renders with no session data and the page component errors on null access.
- No `router.push('/')` (or equivalent) is fired after a successful kill.

Relevant files:
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` — `killSession` (~L337) already handles navigation from the dashboard context.
- `packages/web/src/components/BottomSheet.tsx` — \`confirm-kill\` flow and \`onRequestKill\` callback.
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — session detail page; needs a post-kill redirect.
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/error.tsx` — currently what the user sees after kill.

## Proposed fix

1. In whatever component hosts the kill button on the session detail page, after the `POST /api/sessions/[id]/kill` call resolves successfully:
   - Use `useRouter()` from `next/navigation` and call `router.push('/')` (or the referring project URL if tracked).
   - Do **not** rely on state updates / SSE to re-render the detail page — navigate explicitly before the next render can fail.
2. If the kill request **fails**, stay on the page and surface an error toast; don't navigate.
3. Confirm the same flow works from both:
   - The session detail page Terminate button.
   - The dashboard BottomSheet confirm-kill path (already works; just verify no regression).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clicking Terminate on `/sessions/[id]` and confirming routes the user to `/` (or the originating project dashboard) after success.
- [ ] The App Router error boundary is not triggered during the kill flow.
- [ ] Kill failures leave the user on the session page with a visible error indication.
- [ ] Test added to `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/__tests__/` (or the component test file) covering post-kill navigation — mock `useRouter` and assert `push('/')` is called on success.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test`, `typecheck`, and `lint` pass.

## Out of scope

- Changing where the session lands after merge / cleanup (separate flow).
- Redesigning the kill confirmation UX — keep existing BottomSheet / confirm dialog.

## References

- Kill API route: `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/[id]/kill/route.ts`
- Dashboard kill handler: `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` (~L337)

title: fix(web): orchestrator terminal session not visible on new dashboard UI
body:
## Summary

After the recent dashboard redesign, the orchestrator's own terminal session is no longer accessible/visible from the web UI. Users can see and attach to worker sessions, but the orchestrator session itself doesn't surface anywhere — so there is no way to watch what the orchestrator is doing or send it a message through the browser.

## Repro

1. Start an orchestrator: `ao start` (spawns `{prefix}-orchestrator` or `{prefix}-orchestrator-N`).
2. Open the dashboard.
3. Observe the session list / kanban / sidebar — worker sessions appear, orchestrator session does not.
4. Try to navigate to the orchestrator detail page. Either the direct URL works but nothing links to it, or the page itself renders without the terminal component.

## Expected

- Orchestrator sessions appear somewhere discoverable — at minimum, a dedicated entry in the `ProjectSidebar` (sidebar already has `isOrchestratorSession` filtering logic at `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:30,163`).
- Clicking the orchestrator entry opens its detail page and renders the terminal with `isOrchestrator` variant.
- The terminal is fully interactive (xterm.js + WebSocket) — same behavior as worker sessions.

## Likely cause

`ProjectSidebar.tsx` line 30 filters **out** orchestrator sessions from the main list (\`!isOrchestratorSession(...)\`). The old UI had a separate surface (header pill / orchestrator selector) that exposed them; the new UI may have dropped that surface without adding a replacement link.

Relevant files:
- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` — filter excludes orchestrators from the worker list; need a separate section or entry for them.
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` — already supports the \`isOrchestrator\` variant (~L35, L342). Rendering path is fine; the problem is navigation to it.
- `packages/web/src/components/OrchestratorSelector.tsx` — may or may not still be wired up in the new layout; verify.
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — verify the detail page passes `isOrchestrator={true}` correctly when the session record indicates an orchestrator role.

## Proposed fix

1. In `ProjectSidebar.tsx`, add a dedicated section at the top (above the worker list) that lists the project's orchestrator session(s) with a link to `/sessions/<id>`. Keep the existing worker filter.
2. Ensure the session detail page correctly passes `isOrchestrator` when the target session's role is orchestrator — check `SessionDetail` wiring from `page.tsx`.
3. Sanity-check that the terminal (`DirectTerminal`) mounts and the WebSocket connects for orchestrator sessions same as worker sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Orchestrator session is visible in the sidebar (dedicated section or clearly distinguishable entry).
- [ ] Clicking the entry opens the orchestrator detail page with a live terminal.
- [ ] Terminal input/output works (can `send` commands, see output).
- [ ] Worker sessions still render correctly and are not double-listed as orchestrators.
- [ ] Dark theme preserved; no inline styles.
- [ ] Test coverage:
  - `ProjectSidebar.test.tsx` — orchestrator section renders when an orchestrator session is present and hides when absent.
  - Session detail page test — `isOrchestrator={true}` passed for orchestrator session records.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test`, `typecheck`, `lint` pass.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning the orchestrator detail page layout.
- Changes to multi-orchestrator selection UX (see existing `OrchestratorSelector.tsx`).

## References

- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/OrchestratorSelector.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`
- Helper: `isOrchestratorSession` from `@composio/ao-core/types`

title: fix(web): kanban board layout breaks on non-13in displays (needs cross-size responsive pass)
body:
## Summary

The kanban board on the dashboard renders well on roughly one viewport size (looks like 13" MacBook — ~1440×900), and looks wonky on most other common displays: ultrawide, 4K, external 27" monitors, and smaller/medium laptops. It needs a proper responsive pass across the range of resolutions users actually have.

## Symptoms (not exhaustive — please enumerate while fixing)

- **Ultrawide / large monitors (≥1920px, ≥27"):** columns stretch to `max-width: 420px` and then leave large empty gutters on each side; or content sits cramped to the left with the rest of the viewport wasted. The board doesn't scale up.
- **4K / HiDPI:** same as above but worse — huge empty space around the board.
- **Medium laptops (~1280px):** columns get clipped or horizontally scroll earlier than expected; column headers wrap awkwardly; count pills overlap titles.
- **Small laptops (~1024–1180px):** horizontal scroll activates but the scroll affordance is not obvious; inner column content (SessionCard) overflows unpredictably.
- **Vertical sizing:** `.kanban-board` uses `height: calc(100vh - 280px)` — the `280px` header allowance is a magic number that breaks on short viewports (e.g. stacked browser toolbars on laptops) and wastes space on tall portrait monitors.

## Root-cause hints

From `packages/web/src/app/globals.css`:

- Line 1839–1846 — `.kanban-board { height: calc(100vh - 280px); ... }` — hardcoded header offset.
- Line 1900–1913 — `.kanban-column { flex: 1 0 260px; min-width: 260px; max-width: 420px; ... }` — fixed pixel min/max with no container-query or viewport-aware scaling.
- Line 1841 — `gap: 8px` — fixed; should likely scale with viewport.
- Breakpoints exist at ~L2112, L2139, L2507, L2515, L2522, L3095, L3099, but only seem to target mobile/tablet — nothing for wide / ultrawide / short-viewport cases.

Relevant code:
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` L635–670 — board markup (`.kanban-board-wrap`, `.kanban-board`).
- `packages/web/src/app/globals.css` — all `.kanban-*` rules.
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` — card sizing should also be checked at narrow column widths.

## Proposed approach

1. **Audit matrix** — test and screenshot each of these at 100% zoom, light + dark theme:
   - 1024×768, 1280×800, 1366×768, 1440×900 (current baseline), 1680×1050, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, 3440×1440 (ultrawide), 3840×2160 (4K).
   - Also short viewports: 1440×720 (laptop with docked toolbars).
   - Attach screenshots to the PR.
2. **Replace magic numbers with flexible sizing:**
   - `height: calc(100vh - var(--header-offset))` driven by a CSS variable computed from the actual header height (or use `flex: 1` on a properly-structured parent column). Do not hardcode `280px`.
   - Column width: consider CSS container queries for the column itself (scoped to the board wrap) rather than viewport media queries, so column sizing is independent of sidebar width.
   - Raise `max-width` ceiling on ultrawide so columns breathe, or add an outer `max-width` on `.kanban-board-wrap` centered in the viewport — pick whichever matches the intended UX.
3. **Explicit breakpoints to add:**
   - `@media (min-width: 1600px)` — cap board content width OR let columns widen gracefully.
   - `@media (min-width: 2000px)` — ultrawide treatment.
   - `@media (max-height: 780px)` — reduce the `--header-offset` so the board isn't a sliver.
4. **Gap scaling:** use `clamp()` for `gap` (e.g. `gap: clamp(6px, 0.6vw, 14px)`).
5. **Ensure horizontal scroll is discoverable** when columns overflow (keep the existing `overflow-x: auto` but verify a visible scrollbar shows up on macOS Safari with ephemeral scrollbars).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit matrix screenshots attached to the PR for all listed resolutions, in light + dark theme.
- [ ] No horizontal overflow at ≥1440px width unless there are genuinely more columns than fit.
- [ ] Columns scale sensibly on ultrawide (either widen, center the board, or both — per design decision).
- [ ] Board vertical height adapts to actual header height; no sliver rendering on short viewports.
- [ ] Column headers / count pills / captions don't overlap or wrap awkwardly on any tested resolution.
- [ ] SessionCard content renders correctly at the narrowest column width (260px) and the widest.
- [ ] Dark theme preserved.
- [ ] No inline styles added to components (per `CLAUDE.md` § Web / Styling).
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test`, `typecheck`, `lint` pass.
- [ ] If possible, add a visual-regression or snapshot test covering the board at two representative widths (laptop + ultrawide); if tooling isn't set up, skip and note it.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning the session card itself.
- Kanban column count/structure changes.
- Mobile kanban layout (already has dedicated mobile handling — leave unless bugs surface during the audit).

## References

- `packages/web/src/app/globals.css` L1839–1946 (kanban rules)
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` L635–670
- `CLAUDE.md` § Web / Styling and Constraints C-01/C-02/C-05

title: refactor(config): split monolithic agent-orchestrator.yaml into per-project configs with a thin global index
body:
## Summary

Today, `agent-orchestrator.yaml` is a single monolithic file that embeds every project's full settings inline under a top-level `projects:` map. As fleets grow to 5, 10, 20+ projects this file becomes a coordination point for unrelated teams, accumulates merge conflicts, and makes it hard to version-control project-specific rules/reactions with the project they describe.

Split the model in two:

1. **Global config** (`agent-orchestrator.yaml`) — thin index. Only global concerns (ports, defaults, installed plugins, shared notifiers, top-level reactions, dashboard) + a **list of project references** (key, name, path, display order).
2. **Per-project config** (`<project>/.ao/config.yaml`, or an external fallback) — everything project-scoped: repo, tracker, scm, agentRules, reactions overrides, agentConfig, symlinks, postCreate, role-specific overrides, session strategies.

## Motivation

- **Project settings travel with the project.** Agent rules, tracker config, and reaction overrides get version-controlled in the repo they describe. A team maintaining `org/backend` owns its AO config without touching a shared file.
- **Fewer merge conflicts on the shared config.** The global file changes only when plugins/ports/notifiers change, not every time someone tweaks a rule in one repo.
- **Natural isolation.** One project's misconfiguration can't silently break another's because their schemas are validated independently.
- **Portable projects.** Moving a project to a different orchestrator is a `git clone` + one line in the global index — no copy/paste across YAML files.
- **Cleaner hash scheme.** The current `sha256(dirname(configPath))` hash couples every project's data directory to the global config's location. Per-project configs let each project own its own hash and data dir, which incidentally removes the hash-collision class of error.

## Current state (summary)

Source: `packages/core/src/config.ts:246-262`

```
OrchestratorConfigSchema {
  port, terminalPort, directTerminalPort,
  readyThresholdMs, power, defaults, plugins, dashboard,
  projects: Record<projectId, ProjectConfigSchema>,  // ← embedded inline
  notifiers, notificationRouting, reactions,
}
```

`ProjectConfigSchema` fields (everything currently inlined per project): `name, repo, path, defaultBranch, sessionPrefix, runtime, agent, workspace, tracker, scm, symlinks, postCreate, agentConfig, orchestrator, worker, reactions, agentRules, agentRulesFile, orchestratorRules, orchestratorSessionStrategy, opencodeIssueSessionStrategy`.

Data directory: `~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/` where `hash = sha256(dirname(configPath)).slice(0, 12)` — shared across every project in the same file (`packages/core/src/paths.ts:20-44`).

## Proposed state

### New global schema

```yaml
# agent-orchestrator.yaml  (global — lives anywhere, e.g. ~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml)
port: 3000
terminalPort: 14800
directTerminalPort: 14801
readyThresholdMs: 300000
power: { preventIdleSleep: true }
dashboard: { attentionZones: simple }

defaults:
  runtime: tmux
  agent: claude-code
  workspace: worktree
  notifiers: [desktop]

plugins: []          # installer-managed external plugins (unchanged)
notifiers: {}        # shared notifier instances (unchanged)
notificationRouting: {}
reactions: {}        # global default reactions (unchanged)

projects:            # now a LIST, not a map — references only
  - key: frontend           # stable id used in URLs, paths, env vars
    name: Frontend           # optional display label (falls back to key)
    path: ~/code/frontend    # resolved to an absolute path
    configPath: .ao/config.yaml   # optional — relative to path; default \".ao/config.yaml\"
    order: 10                # optional — dashboard sort order (ascending)

  - key: backend
    path: ~/code/backend
    order: 20
    # no configPath → resolver looks in <path>/.ao/config.yaml, then external fallback

  - key: legacy-infra
    path: ~/code/legacy-infra
    configPath: ~/.agent-orchestrator/external-configs/legacy-infra.yaml   # external override
    order: 30
```

### New per-project schema

```yaml
# <project>/.ao/config.yaml  (per-project — committed with the repo by default)
repo: org/frontend
defaultBranch: main
sessionPrefix: fe

runtime: tmux           # optional — falls back to defaults.runtime
agent: claude-code      # optional
workspace: worktree     # optional

tracker:
  plugin: github

scm:
  plugin: github

symlinks: [.env]
postCreate:
  - pnpm install

agentConfig:
  permissions: skip
  model: opus

orchestrator:
  agent: claude-code
  agentConfig: { model: claude-sonnet-4-5 }

worker:
  agent: codex

agentRules: |
  Use TypeScript strict mode.
  Always run `pnpm test` before pushing.

agentRulesFile: .agent-rules.md

reactions:
  approved-and-green:
    auto: true

orchestratorRules: |
  Prefer to batch-spawn related issues together.

orchestratorSessionStrategy: reuse
opencodeIssueSessionStrategy: reuse
```

Notably **not** in the per-project file: `port`, `defaults`, `plugins`, `notifiers`, `notificationRouting`, top-level `reactions` defaults, `dashboard`, `power`. Those stay global.

### What moves vs stays

| Field                                   | Global | Per-project |
| --------------------------------------- | :----: | :---------: |
| `port`, `terminalPort`, `directTerminalPort` |   ✓    |             |
| `readyThresholdMs`, `power`, `dashboard`     |   ✓    |             |
| `defaults.*` (runtime/agent/workspace/notifiers/roles) |  ✓   |             |
| `plugins` (installed external plugins)  |   ✓    |             |
| `notifiers` (shared instances)          |   ✓    |             |
| `notificationRouting`                   |   ✓    |             |
| `reactions` (defaults)                  |   ✓    |             |
| `projects` (list of references)         |   ✓    |             |
| `name`, `repo`, `path`, `defaultBranch` |        |     ✓       |
| `sessionPrefix`                         |        |     ✓       |
| `runtime` / `agent` / `workspace` overrides |    |     ✓       |
| `tracker`, `scm`                        |        |     ✓       |
| `symlinks`, `postCreate`                |        |     ✓       |
| `agentConfig`, `orchestrator`, `worker` |        |     ✓       |
| `agentRules`, `agentRulesFile`, `orchestratorRules` | |   ✓       |
| `reactions` (per-project overrides)     |        |     ✓       |
| `orchestratorSessionStrategy`, `opencodeIssueSessionStrategy` | | ✓ |

## Config resolution

```
loadConfig(globalPath):
  1. Parse globalPath as GlobalConfigSchema.
  2. For each entry in projects:
       - Resolve project.path to absolute (expand ~, symlinks).
       - Determine per-project config path:
           a) if entry.configPath is absolute → use it
           b) if entry.configPath is relative → resolve against project.path
           c) if entry.configPath is omitted → try <project.path>/.ao/config.yaml
           d) if still missing → try ~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<key>/config.yaml
           e) otherwise → error with actionable message
       - Parse per-project file as ProjectConfigSchema.
       - Merge with global defaults (runtime/agent/workspace/notifiers).
  3. Return MergedConfig { global, projects: Record<key, ResolvedProjectConfig> }.
```

Resolution is strict — missing per-project files are a hard error, not silent skip. The global index lists projects that must exist.

## Data directory and hash scheme

Currently: `~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/` where `hash` comes from the global config's directory.

Proposed: each project owns its own hash derived from the **project's path** (or its per-project config path if external):

```
~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<hash12>-<key>/
  .origin            # stores resolved project path (collision detection, unchanged pattern)
  sessions/
  worktrees/
  archive/
  feedback-reports/
```

Global-scoped data (dashboard pid, running-state file, etc.) moves to `~/.agent-orchestrator/global/<globalHash12>/`.

**Why project-path hash, not config-path hash:** a project is identified by its repo checkout. Moving the per-project config file (e.g. from in-repo `.ao/config.yaml` to an external fallback) shouldn't re-hash the data dir.

## CLI changes

- `ao start [path]`
  - If `path` is given and has no per-project config, scaffold `<path>/.ao/config.yaml` from detected repo/tracker (same inference as today's `ao start <url>` flow).
  - Add/update the project entry in the global config's `projects:` list (preserving `order`).
  - Existing behavior (starting the dashboard + orchestrator + lifecycle loop) is unchanged.
- `ao project add <path> [--key=..] [--external-config=..]`
  - Explicit, scriptable variant of `ao start <path>` that just registers the project.
- `ao project remove <key>` — removes the entry from the global list. Data dir is left in place; a separate `--purge` flag deletes it.
- `ao project list` — prints the resolved projects with paths, config locations, and status.
- `ao init --project` (new flag) — scaffolds `.ao/config.yaml` inside the current repo without touching the global config.
- `ao config-help` — updated to render both schemas.
- `ao spawn` / `ao batch-spawn` — unchanged surface; `autoDetectProject` already uses `cwd` matching and `AO_PROJECT_ID`, both of which keep working.
- `ao doctor` — extended to warn when a project's per-project config is missing, unreadable, or failing schema validation.

## Migration

- Add `ao migrate --split-projects` that reads an existing monolithic `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, writes `<path>/.ao/config.yaml` for each project, rewrites the global file to the new schema, and creates a backup of the original.
- Run migration automatically the first time `loadConfig` sees an old-format file, behind a prompt in interactive mode and a `--migrate` flag in non-interactive mode.
- Keep a compatibility shim for one minor release: if the global file contains `projects:` as a map (old format), warn loudly and load it as if it had been migrated in-memory. Remove the shim in the release after.

## Plugins and cross-cutting features

- **Plugin contracts are unchanged.** Plugins receive a `ProjectConfig` object at `create()` / method-call time — the source of that object (inline vs per-project file) is invisible to plugins.
- **Notifiers** stay global because they're physical channels (a Slack webhook is one URL). Per-project notifier choice stays under `defaults.notifiers` + optional per-project override list.
- **Reactions** compose: per-project reactions override global reactions for that project's sessions, same semantics as today.
- **Session namespacing:** tmux names become `<globalHash>-<projectHash>-<prefix>-<num>` to keep collisions impossible across both axes. Parser in `packages/core/src/paths.ts:161-174` needs an update.

## Files that will change

Non-exhaustive:

- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — split `OrchestratorConfigSchema` into `GlobalConfigSchema` + `ProjectConfigFileSchema`; add resolver.
- `packages/core/src/paths.ts` — new project-path-based hash fns; extend `parseTmuxName`; add `getGlobalDataDir`.
- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — `OrchestratorConfig` gets a `projectIndex` field; `ProjectConfig` is sourced from the per-project file.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` — write per-project config when scaffolding; update global index.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` — new `--project` flag.
- New: `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts` — `ao project add|remove|list`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts` — `autoDetectProject` / `findProjectForDirectory` read from the new index; no behavior change.
- `packages/cli/src/lib/preflight.ts` — validate per-project config presence in pre-flight.
- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`, `lifecycle-manager.ts` — use resolver instead of direct schema access.
- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts`, Dashboard + ProjectSidebar — consume the new resolved projects list; display `order` for sorting.
- `agent-orchestrator.yaml.example` — rewritten to the new shape.
- `examples/*.yaml` — split into pairs (global + per-project) or a new `examples/projects/*` layout.
- `docs/MULTI_PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md` — rewrite the config sections for the new shape.
- `docs/CLI.md` — document new `ao project` subcommands.
- `SETUP.md` — update config reference.
- Tests across `core/__tests__`, `cli/__tests__` — update fixtures; add resolver tests + migration tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- Loading a new-format global + per-project pair produces the same resolved `OrchestratorConfig` the old monolithic file would have (golden fixture tests).
- `ao start <fresh-path>` creates `.ao/config.yaml` inside the repo and appends to the global index.
- `ao start` with an old-format file migrates it and continues booting without manual intervention (interactive confirmation in a TTY).
- All 8 plugin slots continue to receive the same `ProjectConfig` shape; no plugin code changes required.
- Dashboard sidebar respects `order` from the global index.
- `ao doctor` reports missing/invalid per-project files.
- Existing tests pass; new tests cover: resolver cascade, missing-file errors, migration, project-path hash stability across config moves.

## Open questions

1. **In-repo vs external default:** prefer `<path>/.ao/config.yaml` (in-repo, version-controlled) or `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<key>/config.yaml` (external, doesn't touch the repo)? Proposal: in-repo first, external fallback. Rationale: the main benefit of the split is version-controlling project rules.
2. **Filename:** `.ao/config.yaml`, `.agent-orchestrator.yaml`, or `agent-orchestrator.yaml` at the repo root? `.ao/config.yaml` is shortest and lets us add sibling files (`.ao/rules.md`, `.ao/secrets.env.example`) without polluting the repo root.
3. **Global location:** keep `./agent-orchestrator.yaml` in `cwd` as the discovery root, or move to `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` (XDG-style) and make `cwd`-based discovery a compat shim?
4. **Ordering semantics:** numeric `order` (sparse 10/20/30 for easy reordering) vs. explicit array order (position = order)? Numeric is easier to edit manually; array order is easier to reason about.
5. **Per-project secrets:** should `.ao/config.yaml` support env-var interpolation (`${LINEAR_API_KEY}`) the same way the global file does today? Yes — parity with current behavior.
6. **Monorepo with multiple AO projects:** should one repo be allowed to register N projects (different paths inside the same repo, e.g. `repo/apps/web`, `repo/apps/api`)? Current model doesn't forbid this; keep it permitted.

## Out of scope (for this issue)

- Remote per-project configs (fetched over HTTP) — can follow as a separate RFC.
- Dashboard UI for editing per-project configs — keep editing via YAML for now.
- Config schema versioning (\`apiVersion:\` field) — useful long-term but orthogonal to the split.

## References

- Current schema: `packages/core/src/config.ts:166-262`
- Current hash scheme: `packages/core/src/paths.ts:20-44`
- Project resolver: `packages/cli/src/lib/project-resolution.ts` + `packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts:24-50`
- Related docs: `docs/MULTI_PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md`, `agent-orchestrator.yaml.example`

title: feat(plugin): implement kimicode agent plugin
body:
## Summary

Adds a new agent plugin for [MoonshotAI's Kimi Code CLI](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli) so users can set `agent: kimicode` in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`. Implements the full `Agent` interface from `@aoagents/ao-core`, matching the conventions in CLAUDE.md § Agent Plugin Implementation Standards.

- **Activity detection:** AO activity JSONL (like aider / opencode) with a native-ish signal from `~/.kimi/<session>/` mtimes when a matching `state.json` (by `cwd`) exists. The mandatory JSONL-entry fallback is wired so the dashboard keeps working when the native signal is missing.
- **PATH wrapper hooks:** uses the shared `setupPathWrapperWorkspace` so PRs opened from a kimicode session auto-appear on the dashboard.
- **Prompt delivery:** post-launch via `runtime.sendMessage()` because `kimi -p` implicitly enables `--print` / `--yolo` and exits, which would break supervised sessions.
- **Resume:** `--resume <session_id>` parsed out of the session `state.json`, falling back to `--continue` when no id is recorded.
- **Registration:** wired into `cli/src/lib/plugins.ts`, `detect-agent.ts`, `plugin-registry.json`, CLI `package.json` deps, and the onboarding install list (`start.ts`). Docs and YAML examples updated.

Closes #1384.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode test` — 58 tests green (includes all 7 mandatory `getActivityState` cases, manifest, launch, env, detect activity, process detection, session info, restore command, hooks, detect())
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across the monorepo
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm -r build` — successful
- [x] `pnpm test` — full suite green (502 CLI + integration tests all pass)
- [ ] Manual smoke test: set `agent: kimicode` in a project, install kimi (`uv tool install kimi-cli`), verify a session spawns, the dashboard shows active → ready → idle, `~/.ao/bin` wrappers intercept `gh pr create`, and the PR appears in the UI

title: fix(web): kanban board is broken on mobile viewports (new UI)
body:
## Summary

**This is about the new dashboard UI** (post-redesign — the current `Dashboard.tsx` + kanban layout, not the legacy one).

The kanban board is effectively unusable on mobile. Columns and cards do not adapt properly to small viewports — horizontal scroll feels clumsy, column widths clip content, headers overflow, and interaction (tap targets, swipe) is poor. Needs a proper mobile pass.

## Symptoms (seed list — enumerate more while fixing)

- **Horizontal scroll is the primary interaction but feels wrong:** no visible scroll affordance (e.g. fade on edges or scroll snap), users don't realize they can swipe to see other columns.
- **Column widths:** at `@media (max-width: 640px)`, `.kanban-column` uses `min-width: min(86vw, 320px)` which leaves ~14vw of the next column peeking — intended as an affordance but in practice looks like a layout bug on 360px phones.
- **Session cards clip or overflow:** inside narrow columns, the SessionCard controls (PR badge, kill button, activity pill) wrap unpredictably or get cut off.
- **Header / title row** of each column wraps awkwardly — dot + title + count don't align on small widths.
- **Board height:** `min-height: calc(100vh - 280px)` (L2114) uses the same 280px offset as desktop; mobile header is a different size, so the board doesn't size correctly and has either wasted space or insufficient room.
- **Tap targets on cards** are below the 44×44px accessibility minimum in at least a few places (kill, merge chips). Confirm in audit.
- **No scroll snap** between columns — a phone-native UX would snap one column at a time.
- **Landscape on phones (≤700 height):** board becomes a sliver.

## Root-cause hints

From `packages/web/src/app/globals.css`:

- L2112–2115 — `@media (max-width: 900px)` kanban rules use a desktop-derived `280px` header offset on mobile.
- L2130–2153 — `@media (max-width: 640px)` only adjusts column width and some card min-heights; no scroll snap, no edge affordance, no header restructuring.
- L2507, L2515, L2522 — another breakpoint tier; audit for overlap/conflict with the 640/900 rules.
- L3095, L3099 — column-body / column-title rules at yet another breakpoint.

Component references (new UI):
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` — board markup.
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` — cards may need a compact variant at narrow column widths.
- `packages/web/src/components/__tests__/Dashboard.mobile.test.tsx` — existing mobile tests; extend rather than duplicate.

## Proposed approach

1. **Audit matrix — actual mobile devices / emulations on the new UI:**
   - 320×568 (iPhone SE 1st gen — smallest realistic target)
   - 360×800 (common Android)
   - 390×844 (iPhone 14)
   - 430×932 (iPhone 15 Pro Max)
   - 768×1024 (iPad portrait, tablet cutoff — verify which layout wins)
   - Landscape equivalents (e.g. 844×390) for the short-viewport case
   - Light + dark theme for each
2. **Replace the 280px magic header offset on mobile** — either use a CSS variable computed from the actual mobile header height, or switch to flex-based sizing so the board takes the remaining space naturally.
3. **Add CSS scroll snap** on `.kanban-board` for mobile breakpoints: `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;` with `scroll-snap-align: start;` on `.kanban-column`. Test that swipe feels right and doesn't break desktop overflow scroll.
4. **Edge affordance:** subtle left/right gradient fade on `.kanban-board-wrap` on mobile to signal scrollability. Toggle visibility based on actual scroll position (JS, throttled via rAF) or use CSS-only `linear-gradient` overlays.
5. **Column header compaction** — on widths < 400px, stack dot+title above the count pill, or truncate titles with ellipsis and keep the count right-aligned.
6. **Tap target audit** — ensure kill/merge/send buttons meet 44×44px minimum on mobile (separate compact visual treatment is fine, but hit area must be correct — use `padding` or a transparent hit-area wrapper).
7. **Landscape phones** — for `@media (max-height: 500px) and (orientation: landscape)`, tighten vertical padding and let the board consume more of the viewport.
8. Verify existing mobile drawer / hamburger (`L2156`, `.mobile-menu-toggle`) doesn't interfere with board interactions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit matrix screenshots attached to PR for all listed devices on the **new UI**, both themes, portrait + landscape.
- [ ] Board is swipeable between columns with snap behavior on mobile.
- [ ] Scroll affordance visible (edge fade or similar) so users discover the horizontal swipe.
- [ ] Column headers render cleanly at 320px — no overlap, no awkward wrap.
- [ ] Session cards inside mobile columns don't clip or overflow; all action buttons reachable.
- [ ] All interactive elements on cards meet 44×44px tap target minimum.
- [ ] Board vertical sizing adapts to actual mobile header height, not a hardcoded 280px.
- [ ] Landscape phone viewport renders usable board (not a sliver).
- [ ] Dark theme preserved end-to-end.
- [ ] No inline styles in modified components (per \`CLAUDE.md\` § Web / Styling).
- [ ] Extended \`Dashboard.mobile.test.tsx\` to cover new behavior (snap class applied, edge affordance element present, tap target sizes via rendered styles where possible).
- [ ] \`pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test\`, \`typecheck\`, \`lint\` pass.

## Out of scope

- Desktop / ultrawide kanban issues (tracked in #1388 — do not duplicate).
- Redesigning SessionCard content — only adjust for narrow columns.
- Replacing kanban with a different UI on mobile (e.g. tab-per-column) — evaluate in a follow-up if swipe + snap isn't enough.
- Any changes to the legacy dashboard layout (this issue is scoped to the **new UI** only).

title: feat: add kimi-2-6-code plugin
proposal: prevent bug regressions across agent sessions via tests + agent-lessons.md
body:
## Context

Each AO worker session spawns a fresh agent with no memory of prior bugs. This already bit us on PR #1334 (fixes #895): the first draft of the detailed bugbot-dispatch guidance was missing `--paginate` on step 2, reintroducing the exact pagination failure mode the fix was meant to prevent. It was caught by a reviewer — not by the agent.

As worker sessions scale up, \"reviewer catches it\" is not a durable strategy. We need a mechanism that makes old bugs physically hard to reintroduce, regardless of which model or session is writing the code.

## Why a memory system alone is the wrong answer

Markdown \"lessons\" files get skimmed, drift out of date, are skipped by context-pruned agents, and have no enforcement surface. We should not build one as the primary mechanism.

## Proposal: three-layer defense, priced by cost and effectiveness

### 1. Regression tests are load-bearing (primary, zero infra)

Every `fix:` PR must add at least one test that fails if the bug reappears. PR #1334 demonstrates:

```ts
it(\"paginates every enumerated gh api command (fixes #895)\", () => {
  // asserts all 3 numbered commands carry --paginate
});
```

A future agent that drops `--paginate` gets a red CI without reading any doc.

**Enforcement**: add a rule to `.cursor/BUGBOT.md` (and the new `.github/copilot-instructions.md` if/when we add it):

> On `fix:` PRs, flag any changed test file that does not reference the issue number (`#N`) or include a `fixes #N` comment.

Bot reviewers already read these files every PR. No infra to build.

### 2. `docs/agent-lessons.md` wired via `agentRulesFile` (secondary)

AO's prompt-builder already has a 3-layer prompt (base → config → user rules). Layer 3 reads `agentRulesFile` from `agent-orchestrator.yaml`. That's our \"memory\" hook — worker sessions load it automatically.

Keep it terse and test-linked:

```markdown
# Agent Lessons

One-liner per past incident. Each bullet must link to the regression test that enforces it; if it can't, write a test first.

- #895: detailed bugbot dispatch must include `--paginate` on all three `gh api` calls.
  Enforced by: `format-automated-comments.test.ts:\"paginates every enumerated gh api command\"`.
- #1360: CI-failing chip reads three sources; they must stay in sync on recovery.
  Enforced by: **TODO** — no test yet.
```

Wire in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`:
```yaml
agentRulesFile: docs/agent-lessons.md
```

This file is an **index of tests**, not a behavior policy. Anything that sits in this file without a test-link is a signal to write the test, not to elaborate the prose.

### 3. Review-bot hints (tertiary)

`.cursor/BUGBOT.md` / `.github/copilot-instructions.md` list anti-patterns bots should flag on every diff. Fresh diff analysis triggered by every PR is strictly more effective than any file a future agent might or might not read. This is what caught the `--paginate` miss in #1334.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Convention documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (or similar): every `fix:` commit references its issue in the commit message; every `fix:` PR adds at least one test that references the issue.
- [ ] `.cursor/BUGBOT.md` updated with the \"fix PR must add a regression test referencing the issue\" rule.
- [ ] `docs/agent-lessons.md` created with #895 as the seed entry, strictly formatted as \"bullet → test reference\".
- [ ] `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (example config / template, not the user's personal one) wires `agentRulesFile: docs/agent-lessons.md` so worker sessions inherit it.
- [ ] (Follow-up, not blocking) add a lightweight check — commit-msg hook or CI step — that `fix:` commits reference an issue number.

## Non-goals

- Building a structured memory database / SQLite / vector store. We don't have enough incidents yet, and everything we could store is more durably expressed as a test + a one-line index entry.
- Forcing every `feat:` PR to add a \"lesson\" — only regression-worthy incidents.

## Seed data (for context)

Incidents that would go into the v1 of `docs/agent-lessons.md`:

1. **#895** — review-check logic misses new bugbot comments from the latest push. Test: `format-automated-comments.test.ts`.
2. **#1360** — session detail shows CI failing when CI is passing (3-way OR + 5-min cache). Test: TODO.
3. Whatever incident inspires us to add it next.

## Why this is worth doing now

Between #895, #1334 (nearly-reintroduced #895), and #1360, we already have a pattern: bugs in the PR-feedback and lifecycle paths recur because multiple agents touch similar code without shared history. The fix is structurally cheap (a test + a one-liner) and compounds — every added entry makes the next agent's diff safer.

title: bug: spawned worker agents consistently fail to start working (stuck at idle, zero changes)
body:
## Problem

Spawned worker agents consistently fail to start working. They land in `idle`/`exited` state shortly after spawn with zero code changes, no commits, and no PR created. This has been reproduced 4 consecutive times across different issues.

## Reproduction

1. `ao spawn --prompt "<task description>"` — session spawns successfully
2. Wait 1-5 minutes, check `ao status` — session shows `idle` with no PR, no changes
3. Check worktree — `git status` and `git diff` show zero modifications
4. Session eventually transitions to `exited` or `stuck`

## Evidence

Four consecutive failures today (2026-04-21):

| Session | Issue | Result | Activity |
|---------|-------|--------|----------|
| ao-2 | #1199 | exited (1m) | zero changes |
| ao-3 | #1199 | exited (47s) | zero changes |
| ao-4 | #1199 | idle (3m+, killed manually) | zero changes |
| ao-5 | #1360 | idle (29s, killed manually) | zero changes |

### ao-2 lifecycle metadata (representative)
```
status=stuck
lifecycleEvidence=signal_disagreement runtime=alive process=dead activity_signal=valid via_native activity=exited
reportWatcherActiveTrigger=no_acknowledge
detectingAttempts=38
```

Key signals:
- `no_acknowledge` — agent never acknowledged the prompt
- `signal_disagreement` — runtime reported alive but process was dead
- `detectingAttempts=38` — activity detection ran 38 times without the agent ever starting work

### ao-1 (issue #1073) is the exception
ao-1 is the only session that successfully started working — it has PR #1 open (though CI is failing). This suggests the issue is intermittent but has a very high failure rate (~80% of spawns).

## Environment

- AO version: current `main` (~`64badbd`)
- Platform: macOS (Darwin 25.3.0)
- Agent plugin: claude-code
- Runtime: tmux
- Orchestrator session: ao-orchestrator-1

## Possible causes

1. **Agent process crash on startup** — the claude-code agent process may be crashing before it can read the prompt (consistent with `no_acknowledge`)
2. **Tmux session issue** — the tmux session may not be properly delivering the prompt to the agent
3. **Resource contention** — multiple sessions may compete for resources (tmux sockets, worktree locks)
4. **Prompt delivery failure** — the prompt may not be reaching the agent stdin properly

## Suggested investigation

1. Check tmux pane content for the failed sessions (`tmux capture-pane -t <session>`) to see if the agent binary even started
2. Add logging for prompt delivery confirmation
3. Check if the agent binary path is correct and accessible from the worktree
4. Check system resources (memory, file descriptors) during spawn

title: fix: setup workspace hooks before launching agent to prevent trust prompt
body:
## Summary

- Moved `setupWorkspaceHooks` call before `runtime.create()` in both `spawnSession` and `spawnOrchestrator` flows
- Without this, Claude Code shows an interactive trust prompt in fresh worktrees and the agent never receives its task prompt, causing workers to idle and die

## Root Cause

Claude Code displays "Is this a project you trust?" on first launch in an untrusted directory. The spawn flow was:
1. Launch agent in tmux (triggers trust prompt)
2. Create `.claude/settings.json` via `setupWorkspaceHooks` (too late)

The agent sat at the trust prompt indefinitely, never reaching the task prompt. ~80% of spawns failed (4 out of 5 consecutive attempts).

## Fix

Reorder so `setupWorkspaceHooks` runs **before** `runtime.create()`:
1. Create `.claude/settings.json` (marks workspace as trusted)
2. Launch agent in tmux (skips trust prompt)
3. Deliver task prompt

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 801/801 pass
- [x] `pnpm build` passes

title: Dashboard button in sidebar causes full page reload on every click
body:
## Bug

The small grid icon (4-square) button next to each project name in the sidebar triggers a full page reload on every click instead of a smooth client-side navigation.

## Location

- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` — line 473-483 (the `<Link>` with grid SVG icon)
- `packages/web/src/app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx` — `force-dynamic` SSR page

## Root Cause

The dashboard button uses `<Link href={projectDashboardPath(project.id)}>` which resolves to `/projects/<projectId>`. That page is marked `force-dynamic` (SSR on every request), so every click triggers:

1. Server roundtrip to fetch the RSC payload
2. Full re-render of the page from scratch (`getProjectRouteData` + `getDashboardPageData`)
3. Visible loading delay — the screen blanks and everything reloads

This is noticeably slower than the session links in the same sidebar, which use `router.push()` with `e.preventDefault()` for client-side navigation.

## Fix Options

- **(a)** Add a `loading.tsx` skeleton for the `\/projects/[projectId]` route so the transition is visually smooth
- **(b)** Switch the dashboard button to use `router.push()` with optimistic client-side state (matching the pattern used by session links on lines 315-318)
- **(c)** Both — loading skeleton as fallback + `router.push()` for the sidebar shortcut

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the AO dashboard with at least one project configured
2. Navigate to any session detail page
3. Click the 4-square grid icon next to a project name in the sidebar
4. Observe: the entire page reloads with a visible blank/loading delay

title: Stale reaction dispatch: CI failure and merge conflict messages injected repeatedly despite PR being clean
body:
## Bug

The lifecycle manager repeatedly injects "CI is failing on your PR" and "Your branch has merge conflicts" messages to agent sessions even when the associated PR has passing CI and no merge conflicts. The agent dismisses them as stale noise, but they keep coming.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1481732697225539674/1491735678156013588/1496203865740283987
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** \`59f66f4\` (main)

## Screenshot

See Discord thread — screenshot shows 16+ repeated messages alternating between CI failure and merge conflict dispatches within a single agent session.

## Root Cause

**Status oscillation resets reaction trackers, bypassing retry limits.**

The reaction dispatch chain:

1. **\`checkSession()\`** (\`lifecycle-manager.ts:1634\`) runs \`determineStatus()\` which queries PR state via batch GraphQL enrichment.

2. When \`newStatus !== oldStatus\` (line 1682), the **old status's reaction tracker is cleared** (lines 1712-1718):
   \`\`\`ts
   const oldEventType = statusToEventType(undefined, oldStatus);
   if (oldEventType) {
     const oldReactionKey = eventToReactionKey(oldEventType);
     if (oldReactionKey) {
       clearReactionTracker(session.id, oldReactionKey);
     }
   }
   \`\`\`

3. The **new status's reaction fires** via \`executeReaction()\` (line 1733) — which creates a fresh tracker with \`attempts: 0\`.

4. The \`ci-failed\` reaction has \`retries: 2\`, so it should fire at most 3 times before escalating. But **every oscillation out of \`ci_failed\` clears the tracker, and every oscillation back creates a fresh one** — effectively resetting the retry budget.

**The oscillation trigger:** The \`resolvePREnrichmentDecision()\` path in \`determineStatus()\` (line 739-746) uses batch GraphQL data from \`prEnrichmentCache\`. When the ETag guard (\`shouldRefreshPREnrichment()\` in \`graphql-batch.ts:177\`) says "no changes detected", stale cached data is returned (line 895-916). If the cached data says \`ciStatus: "failing"\` or \`mergeable === "CONFLICTING"\` but the PR has since been fixed, the status incorrectly becomes \`ci_failed\` on every poll cycle — re-firing the reaction.

**Contributing factors:**
- \`statusToEventType()\` (line 139) only considers the **target** status, not the source. So \`working → ci_failed\` and \`pr_open → ci_failed\` both produce \`ci.failing\`.
- \`maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails()\` (line 1291) has fingerprint-based dedup, but the **transition reaction** at line 1733 is NOT fingerprint-gated — it fires the static message "CI is failing on your PR. Run gh pr checks..." every time the status transitions to \`ci_failed\`.
- \`maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()\` (line 1424) uses \`lastMergeConflictDispatched\` metadata for dedup, but stale cached \`hasConflicts: true\` from the ETag guard bypass prevents the "conflicts resolved" path (line 1512-1518) from clearing the flag.

## Fix

**Option A (recommended) — Don't clear reaction tracker for the old status on exit.** The tracker should only be cleared when the condition that triggered the reaction is genuinely resolved (CI goes from failing → passing via live check, conflicts confirmed resolved). Change lines 1712-1718 to only clear trackers for states that were verified as resolved.

**Option B — Add a "recently dispatched" timestamp guard.** Before firing \`executeReaction()\` at line 1733, check if the same reaction was dispatched within the last N seconds and skip if so.

**Option C — Live verification before reaction dispatch.** When the batch cache says CI is failing, make a live \`scm.getCISummary()\` call to confirm before injecting the message.

## Impact

- Agents waste tokens repeatedly dismissing false CI/merge conflict alerts
- Agents may attempt unnecessary fixes (rebase, CI check) on clean PRs
- Creates noise in the agent context window, degrading task performance
- Burns GitHub API rate limit on redundant gh pr checks calls from the agent side
