title: ETag Guard spams warnings on transient network failures
body:
## Bug

When `gh api` can't reach GitHub (network blip, DNS issue, proxy, etc.), the ETag Guard logs a full command + error warning to the terminal every polling cycle.

**Observed:**
```
[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for miniMaddy/gut_microbiome_project: Command failed: /usr/bin/gh api --method GET repos/miniMaddy/gut_microbiome_project/pulls?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=1 -i -H If-None-Match: "4f03d4c95d6e8f22c52f61e076d65acb0a81ca3f36542dfe3664cd23fa222689"
error connecting to api.github.com
check your internet connection or https://githubstatus.com
```

**Location:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` ~L449-461 (catch block in `checkPRListETag()`)

**Current behavior:** All `gh api` failures (304, network errors, rate limits, auth errors) hit the same catch block and log a generic warning.

**Expected behavior:**
- Network connectivity errors should be detected (check for `error connecting to api.github.com` or exit code / stderr patterns) and handled gracefully — log once, then suppress repeated warnings until connectivity is restored.
- The `return true` (assume data changed) is the correct safe default, but the noisy logging is misleading.

**Related but distinct issues:**
- #1482 / #1191 — HTTP 304 treated as error (fixed the 304 case, but the catch-all error handler still doesn't distinguish network vs API failures)

**Reporter:** @Madhav (Discord) — running AO locally with repo `miniMaddy/gut_microbiome_project`

title: ao migrate-storage doesn't relink Codex session storage when worktrees move
body:
## Follow-up to PR #1466

Filing as the **Codex counterpart to PR #1466's commit `ef944356`** (Claude Code session-storage relink). Same root cause, different fix shape — Codex's storage model means the physical-rename trick used for Claude does not apply.

## Background

When `ao migrate-storage` moves a session's worktree from V1 to V2, the workspace cwd changes:

- V1: `~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{project}/worktrees/{sid}`
- V2: `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/{projectId}/worktrees/{sid}`

For Claude Code this orphaned `~/.claude/projects/<old-encoded>/` because the directory name encodes the cwd. Commit `ef944356` fixed this by renaming the dir.

For Codex the failure mode is the same (`getRestoreCommand` returns null, agent launches with no chat history) but the storage layout is different:

- Sessions live at `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`.
- The cwd is recorded **inside** each JSONL's `session_meta` line as a string, not in any directory name.
- `findCodexSessionFile` (`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts`) walks every JSONL and matches by exact string equality on `session_meta.cwd === workspacePath`.

After migration, `session_meta.cwd` in the existing JSONLs still points at the V1 path. `findCodexSessionFile(newWorkspacePath)` returns null. Codex launches fresh, no resume.

## Proposed fix

Two viable approaches; the issue is to pick one and ship it.

### Option A — content rewrite at migration time

For each `(oldWorkspacePath, newWorkspacePath)` pair captured during `migrate-storage`:

1. Walk `~/.codex/sessions/` (date-sharded; bounded depth, the plugin already enforces this).
2. For every JSONL, parse the first N lines (only `session_meta` lives near the top — the plugin already caps this with `SESSION_MATCH_SCAN_LINE_LIMIT`).
3. If `session_meta.cwd === oldWorkspacePath`, rewrite the file replacing only that field with `newWorkspacePath`. Preserve all other content byte-for-byte.

**Risk:** content surgery on potentially-large JSONL files (long conversations grow MBs). One bug here corrupts chat history. Mitigations:
- Atomic write via temp + rename.
- Only rewrite the single line that contains `session_meta`. Other lines are streamed through unchanged.
- Refuse to rewrite if the parsed `session_meta` JSON does not round-trip byte-equivalent under our parser (paranoia gate).
- Dry-run flag must report file count and paths without touching anything.

### Option B — plugin-side path-aliasing

Teach `findCodexSessionFile` to match against a list of candidate cwds, not just the current workspacePath. Source of the alias list:

- A small JSON file written by `migrate-storage` at `~/.agent-orchestrator/codex-cwd-aliases.json` keyed by current workspacePath, mapping to historical paths.
- The plugin reads this file once per call and considers `[currentPath, ...historicalAliases]` as matching keys.

**Pros:** zero risk to existing JSONLs. Reversible by deleting the alias file.
**Cons:** the plugin grows a side-channel dependency on a migration artifact. Performance: every `findCodexSessionFile` call now reads an extra file (cheap but non-zero).

**Recommendation:** Option A. Plugin behavior stays clean; the fix is one-shot at migration time and matches the model used for Claude.

## Where to add it

`packages/core/src/migration/storage-v2.ts`, alongside `relinkClaudeSessionStorage`. The `WorkspacePathMove[]` accumulator is already in place from commit `ef944356` — Codex relink reads the same list.

Add a new helper `relinkCodexSessionStorage(moves, dryRun, log): number` that:
- Returns 0 if `~/.codex/sessions/` does not exist.
- For each pair where `oldWorkspacePath !== newWorkspacePath`, scans JSONLs at bounded depth, rewrites matching `session_meta.cwd` lines, returns the count of files touched.

Add `codexSessionsRewritten: number` to `MigrationResult` and surface it in the migration summary.

Mirror the rollback step in `rollbackStorage` (rewriting cwd back from V2 to V1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Happy path test: seed `~/.codex/sessions/<date>/rollout-uuid.jsonl` whose first line is `{"type":"session_meta","payload":{"cwd":"<v1-path>",...}}`. After `migrateStorage`, the same file's `session_meta.cwd` reads `<v2-path>`. All other lines in the file are byte-identical.
- [ ] Safety test: a JSONL whose `session_meta.cwd` doesn't match any migration pair is left untouched.
- [ ] Atomic write: a simulated mid-write crash leaves either the original file or the new file complete — never a half-written file. Verify with a fault-injection harness or by asserting tmpfile-rename semantics.
- [ ] `--dry-run` prints the file count and paths without modifying anything.
- [ ] `--rollback` reverses the rewrite (V2 cwd → V1 cwd) for the same set of files.
- [ ] No new performance regression for `findCodexSessionFile` in normal (post-migration) operation.

## Out of scope

- Content rewrites for any other JSONL field. Only `session_meta.cwd` is rewritten.
- Codex sessions that pre-date `session_meta` (older Codex versions). If detected, log and skip.
- Cross-version Codex format migration. This issue assumes the current `session_meta` schema.

## Reference

- Claude counterpart: PR #1466, commit ef944356 (`fix(migration): relink Claude Code session storage when worktrees move`).
- Surfaced by Skittle's QA on PR #1466 (Discord).

title: feat: add SQLite-backed activity event logging layer
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an operator-facing activity event log for AO so session and lifecycle behavior can be inspected after the fact.

**Activity event infrastructure**
- Adds a SQLite-backed activity event store with WAL mode, retention cleanup, FTS search, structured filters, and process-local dropped-event accounting.
- Sanitizes event data before storage and search indexing, including token/password-like keys and credential-bearing URLs.
- Exports the event write/query APIs from `@aoagents/ao-core`.

**CLI**
- Adds `ao events list`, `ao events search`, and `ao events stats`.
- Supports project/session/type/since/limit filters and a versioned JSON envelope.
- Parses event `data` into structured JSON for `--json` output.

**Usage precedent**
- Records `session.spawned`, `session.spawn_failed`, and `session.killed` in `session-manager`.
- Records `lifecycle.transition` and `activity.transition` in `lifecycle-manager`.
- Adds tests so these real call sites stay as copyable examples for future contributors.

**Release metadata**
- Adds a patch changeset for `@aoagents/ao-core` and `@aoagents/ao-cli`.

## Test Coverage

All new event infrastructure and call-site examples are covered by focused tests.

Coverage map:

title: Branch naming collision: `session/ao-*` branches from non-AO users pollute other AO dashboards
body:
## Bug

When someone manually pushes a branch named `session/ao-*`, another user's AO instance can actively adopt that branch/PR as one of its own sessions — not just display it as a phantom, but link the PR and track it through the lifecycle.

### Actual Reproduction

1. **Ashish** manually pushed branch `session/ao-153` and opened PR #1528 (without using `ao spawn`)
2. **Maaz** typed a freeform prompt in his AO browser terminal — "spawn, AO will decide later what it will do"
3. Maaz's AO instance ran `reserveNextSessionIdentity()`, which scans remote branches via:
   ```bash
   git ls-remote --heads origin 'session/ao-*'
   ```
   It found Ashish's `session/ao-153` branch.
4. Maaz's dashboard showed **both**:
   - `ao-153` (pending, linked to Ashish's PR) — a session Maaz never spawned
   - `ao-154` (working, his actual spawn)

So the collision is not just cosmetic — AO actively linked another user's PR to a session on Maaz's instance because the branch name matched the `session/ao-*` convention. The `listRemoteSessionNumbers()` scan is meant to *skip* taken numbers, but the session metadata for ao-153 was created anyway and `detectPR` linked Ashish's PR to it.

### Root Cause

AO uses `session/ao-{N}` as the default branch naming convention (`session-manager.ts:1189`). The `listRemoteSessionNumbers()` function (`session-manager.ts:795-816`) scans ALL remote branches matching `session/ao-*` — regardless of who created them or which AO instance they belong to.

The lifecycle manager's `detectPR` flow (`lifecycle-manager.ts:550-590`) then links any PR on a `session/ao-*` branch to a session, and the dashboard surfaces it.

### Code Path

| File | Lines | What it does |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:1189` | Default branch: `session/${sessionId}` |
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:795-816` | `listRemoteSessionNumbers()` — scans remote for `session/ao-*` branches |
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:827-870` | `reserveNextSessionIdentity()` — uses remote scan to skip taken numbers |
| `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:550-590` | `detectPR` — links PRs to sessions by branch name |
| `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts:598-640` | `detectPR()` — `gh pr list --head <branch>` |

### Proposed Fix: Add random suffix to branch names

Change from:
```
session/ao-153
```
To:
```
session/ao-153-k7f2m
```

A 5-char random suffix (base36) makes collisions virtually impossible without requiring any user context or extra API calls.

**Changes needed:**
1. `session-manager.ts:1189` — change `session/${sessionId}` to `session/${sessionId}-${randomSuffix(5)}`
2. `listRemoteSessionNumbers()` — update glob from `session/ao-*` to parse the numeric prefix before the suffix
3. `detectPR()` — already takes branch from session metadata, works as-is
4. `format.ts:humanizeBranch()` — strip the suffix for display

### Alternative Approaches Considered

1. **Username-scoped branches** (`session/{githubUser}/ao-{N}`) — cleaner but requires `gh api user` call at spawn time
2. **Instance/storageKey scoping** (`session/{storageKey}/ao-{N}`) — robust but ugly, leaks internal state
3. **Emdash-style** (`{prefix}/{slug}-{random5}`) — more human-readable but bigger refactor

### References

- PR that triggered this: #1528 (branch `session/ao-153` pushed manually by @ashish921998)
- Emdash uses `Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 7)` for 5-char random suffix
- Conductor avoids this by having the AI agent rename branches descriptively after creation

title: bug(web): removed project reappears on dashboard — missing router.refresh() after DELETE
body:
## Bug Report

**Summary:** Clicking "Remove" on a project in the dashboard sidebar hides it temporarily (optimistic UI), but the project reappears after any state reset (component remount, navigation, SSE cycle).

## Root Cause

The removal flow has a broken data refresh path:

1. **`ProjectSidebar.tsx` (~line 236)** — `handleRemoveProject()` calls `DELETE /api/projects/{id}`, which succeeds on disk (YAML config is updated correctly)
2. **Optimistic hide** — adds project ID to `removedProjectIds` Set (client-side only)
3. **`projects` prop is static SSR data** — computed once in `page.tsx` via `getDashboardPageData()`, never re-fetched after mutation
4. **Cleanup useEffect (~line 163-172)** expects `projects` to eventually update to reflect the deletion, but it never does
5. **Any state reset** (React remount, navigation, SSE refresh) wipes `removedProjectIds` back to empty → project reappears

## The Fix

In `ProjectSidebar.tsx`, after the DELETE response succeeds, add `router.refresh()` to force Next.js to re-fetch server component data:

```typescript
// After successful DELETE
await response.json();
router.refresh();  // Force server component re-render with fresh data
```

## Files Involved

- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` — missing `router.refresh()` call
- `packages/web/src/app/page.tsx` — static SSR prop (no client-side refetch mechanism)
- `packages/web/src/lib/dashboard-page-data.ts` — `getDashboardPageData()` only runs on server render

## Reproduction

1. Start AO dashboard with multiple projects
2. Click "Remove" on any project in the sidebar
3. Project disappears temporarily
4. Navigate away and back, or wait for SSE refresh cycle
5. Project reappears — was never actually removed from the UI state

## Expected Behavior

Project is permanently removed from the sidebar after clicking "Remove" and confirming.

title: fix(core): preserve reaction tracker across status oscillation
body:
Closes #1409

## Summary

The lifecycle manager's reaction system has a retry + escalate mechanism: when CI fails, it sends a message to the agent, and after N retries (`retries: 2` = 3 attempts), escalates to a human. But the retry budget was resetting on every status oscillation, causing infinite message spam and preventing escalation.

**Three root causes fixed:**

1. **Reaction tracker cleared unconditionally on status exit** (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1878-1885`). Every transition away from `ci_failed` deleted the tracker. When CI failed again, a fresh tracker was created with `attempts: 0`. The retry budget never exhausted.

2. **Merge conflict dispatch bypassed `executeReaction` entirely** (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1654-1676`). `maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()` called `sessionManager.send()` directly, so the `escalateAfter: "15m"` config for merge-conflicts was dead code — escalation could never trigger.

3. **Merge conflict tracker cleared on resolve** (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1680`). When conflicts resolved, both the reaction tracker and dedup flag were cleared. When conflicts recurred, the escalation budget started from zero.

## Implementation Plan

### Change 1: Persistent reaction keys

Added `PERSISTENT_REACTION_KEYS = new Set(["ci-failed", "merge-conflicts"])`. These keys represent conditions that can oscillate (CI failing→pending→failing, conflicts resolving→recurring). Their trackers survive status exit so the escalation budget accumulates across oscillations.

At the status-exit clear (line 1883), persistent keys are now excluded:
```typescript
if (oldReactionKey && !PERSISTENT_REACTION_KEYS.has(oldReactionKey)) {
  clearReactionTracker(session.id, oldReactionKey);
}
```

### Change 2: Route merge conflicts through `executeReaction`

Replaced direct `sessionManager.send()` / `notifyHuman()` calls in `maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()` with a call to `executeReaction()`. This enables the existing `escalateAfter: "15m"` config that was previously ignored. Dynamic base branch messages are built before the call via an enriched config.

### Change 3: Preserve merge-conflicts tracker on resolve

When conflicts resolve, only the dedup flag (`lastMergeConflictDispatched`) is cleared — allowing re-notification if conflicts recur. The reaction tracker is preserved so the escalation budget continues counting. Terminal-state clearing (PR closed/merged) remains unchanged.

### Behavior after fix

**CI failure oscillation:**
```
Poll 1: CI failing  → send to agent       (attempts: 1)
Poll 2: CI pending  → tracker PRESERVED
Poll 3: CI failing  → send to agent       (attempts: 2)
Poll 4: CI pending  → tracker PRESERVED
Poll 5: CI failing  → attempts 3 > retries 2 → ESCALATE TO HUMAN
```

**Merge conflict oscillation:**
```
Conflict 1: send to agent (attempts: 1, firstTriggered = T)
Resolved:   dedup flag cleared, tracker preserved
Conflict 2: send to agent (attempts: 2)
Resolved:   dedup flag cleared, tracker preserved
Conflict 3: if T + 15min elapsed → ESCALATE TO HUMAN
```

## Test plan

- [x] **CI failure oscillation test**: Simulates 3 oscillations (ci_failed → pr_open → ci_failed). Verifies agent receives messages on attempts 1-2, then human is notified via escalation on attempt 3.
- [x] **Merge conflict time-based escalation test**: Simulates conflict → resolve → recur with `vi.useFakeTimers()`. Verifies escalation triggers after the `escalateAfter` window.
- [x] **Non-persistent keys test**: Verifies `changes-requested` tracker still clears on status exit (only persistent keys are protected).
- [x] All 917 existing tests pass
- [x] Full typecheck passes across all packages

title: Sub-sessions: multiple agents sharing a common worktree
body:
## Problem

Today, AO cannot have multiple agents working on the same directory/worktree simultaneously. The orchestrator model treats sessions as isolated units — each gets its own worktree. This limits workflows where you want parallel agents collaborating on the same codebase, sharing context and file state.

## Proposal: Sub-sessions

Introduce a **sub-session** concept where:

- Within a parent session, you can spawn **sub-sessions** that all share the same worktree
- Sub-sessions are linked to the parent and can operate concurrently on the same files
- This is NOT the orchestrator-as-master / sessions-as-slaves model — sub-sessions are peers sharing a single worktree
- Parent session coordinates and monitors sub-sessions

## Use-Case

From user 100_gb:

> For anything production-grade involving user interaction, pure vibe coding isn't reasonable. Even with frontier models. I work on plans and keep iterating on plans until the agent and I are satisfied with the fidelity. That's the rationale for features like file tree, git diff, and sub-sessions.

> The goal with sub-sessions is to have multiple AO agents working in the same directory. I can't do that with orchestrator as master and sessions as slaves.

Key workflows enabled:
- Multiple agents working different aspects of the same feature in a shared worktree
- Parallel exploration + implementation within the same codebase
- Coordinated multi-agent work with shared file state and git context

## Open Questions

1. **Conflict resolution** — How do sub-sessions handle concurrent file writes? Locking? Last-write-wins? Git-based merge?
2. **Lifecycle** — What happens when a sub-session fails or completes? Does it affect siblings?
3. **UI representation** — How do sub-sessions appear in the dashboard? Nested under the parent?
4. **Resource limits** — How many sub-sessions per parent? How to prevent resource exhaustion?

## Related

- Part of the broader file-tree / code-awareness initiative (file tree, git diff, local git diff views)
- Tied to the orchestrator page UI redesign moving orchestrator info to the top bar

title: fix(opencode): close stdin to prevent process leak on poll
body:
The lifecycle manager polls `opencode session list --format json` every few seconds via execFileAsync. opencode reads from stdin when piped and hangs forever when it's left open, so each poll orphaned a ~150MB process. Within minutes the box would OOM.

Use a dedicated runOpencode wrapper that closes the child's stdin immediately after spawn. Other execFileAsync callers (tmux, ps) keep the existing promisified path.

Test mock updated to use standard execFile callback semantics (err, stdout, stderr as separate args) and provide a util.promisify.custom implementation for promisified callers.

title: CLI shows stale update prompt for source installs
body:
## Summary

`ao start` can show an update prompt like `Update available: 0.2.5 → 0.3.0 — Run: ao update` even when the user is already on the latest `main` source checkout.

## Impact

This is confusing for source/git installs because the update check compares against the npm latest version, while `ao update` for a source checkout pulls the configured git branch. If npm has a newer published version than `main`, users get a false update warning.

There is also a related npm/global install case where `ao update` can complete but the runnable `ao` binary in PATH may still be the old one, causing users to continue seeing the update prompt.

## Expected behavior

- Source/git installs should compare against the version on the branch that `ao update` would actually pull.
- npm/global installs should verify that the runnable `ao` binary in PATH was updated successfully.
- Cached update-check results should not cross install methods.

## Fix

PR #1536 updates the CLI behavior to:

- detect source/git installs and compare against the git branch version instead of npm latest
- avoid stale `FETCH_HEAD` after failed git fetches
- include install method in the update-check cache key
- verify the runnable `ao` binary after npm updates
- harden version parsing for prefixed `ao --version` output

Related PR: https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1536

title: Orchestrator drops resolved review comments even when PR is CHANGES_REQUESTED
body:
## Summary

When a PR is in `reviewDecision: CHANGES_REQUESTED` state but every inline review thread is `isResolved: true`, the orchestrator's review-comment dispatch path returns nothing — so the agent in the session is never told what to fix. The user has to manually relay the findings as plain text in chat.

Observed on PR #1390 today (2026-04-29). 10 inline comments from `illegalcall` exist on the diff; the orchestrator delivered zero of them to the agent session.

## Root cause

`scm-github`'s `getPendingComments` filters review threads by `isResolved == false`:

```ts
// packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts:843–850
return threads
  .filter((t) => {
    if (t.isResolved) return false; // only pending (unresolved) threads
    const c = t.comments.nodes[0];
    if (!c) return false;
    const author = c.author?.login ?? "";
    return !BOT_AUTHORS.has(author);
  })
  ...
```

This is correct for the common case (a reviewer marks a thread "Resolved" because the agent fixed it). It misses three scenarios where the thread is resolved but the comment is still actionable:

1. **Reviewer approves with prior changes-requested still on the table.** A different reviewer's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review keeps the PR-level decision blocking, but the approver may auto-resolve their own threads on approval. Net: PR is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, no unresolved threads.
2. **Reviewer resolves prematurely** (clicks "Resolve conversation" without verifying the fix landed).
3. **GitHub auto-resolves threads** when subsequent commits touch the same lines and the diff context disappears (`isOutdated: true`). The comment may still describe a real issue that wasn't fixed — it just no longer pins to a visible line.

Lifecycle dispatch in `lifecycle-manager.ts:1158–1234` only fires on the fingerprint of `pendingComments`. With pending = `[]`, fingerprint = empty, no dispatch.

## Reproduction (from PR #1390)

```bash
# All 10 review threads from illegalcall:
gh api graphql -f query='query { repository(owner:"ComposioHQ",name:"agent-orchestrator") { pullRequest(number:1390) { reviewThreads(first:100) { nodes { isResolved comments(first:1) { nodes { author { login } } } } } } } }' \
  --jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes | map({resolved: .isResolved, author: .comments.nodes[0].author.login})'
# → every entry has resolved: true

gh pr view 1390 --json reviewDecision
# → {"reviewDecision":"CHANGES_REQUESTED"}
```

PR-level state says "changes requested." Thread-level state says "all resolved." The agent gets nothing.

## Proposed fix directions (open for discussion)

1. **Use PR-level `reviewDecision` as the gate, not thread `isResolved`.** When `reviewDecision === "CHANGES_REQUESTED"`, fetch all comments (including resolved/outdated) and surface them. Other decisions keep current behaviour.
2. **Surface `isOutdated` threads separately** with a "may no longer apply, please verify" annotation in the dispatch prompt.
3. **Cross-reference resolution timestamp against latest commit:** a thread resolved *before* the most recent push to the PR head is suspect; surface those.
4. **Don't filter on `isResolved` at all**, classify in the prompt instead. Adds noise but never silently drops findings.

(1) is the lowest-risk fix and aligns the dispatch with what the user sees on the PR page.

## Impact

- Agent has to be re-tasked manually with the findings
- Defeats the automated review-handling loop AO is built around
- Silent failure mode: no log line, no notifier, just no dispatch

## Files

- `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` (`getPendingComments`, ~L779–867)
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` (review-backlog dispatch, ~L1118–1234)

title: spawn: chain-spawn prompt delivery has no consume-ack; child sessions silently no-op when keystroke injection partially fails
body:
## Summary

When a parent AO session issues `ao spawn` against a `claude-code` worker (chain-spawn pattern), the spawn prompt is delivered via tmux keystroke injection (per `ao-plugin-runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:111-148` — `C-u` + paste-buffer + 300ms sleep + `Enter`, retried 3× with 3/6/9s backoff, no consume-acknowledgment). On Claude Code v2.1.x there is a class of partial-delivery failures where the buffer paste lands but the `Enter` doesn't trigger a turn, leaving the worker idle with the prompt visible in its input. The parent has no way to detect this — it sees a successful `ao spawn` exit and waits indefinitely.

## Repro

This came up in our chain-spawn review flow (parent implementer session spawns a sibling reviewer session via `ao spawn --agent-type claude-code --prompt "..."`). One specific run (cd-11):

1. Parent issued `ao spawn` with a long heredoc `--prompt` (~50 lines, our reviewer task description).
2. AO created the worktree, launched claude-code in the new tmux pane.
3. The worker fetched the PR diff into its worktree (something landed) — but did not produce a turn or run the review procedure.
4. Manual `tmux send-keys -t <pane> Enter` did not unstick it; only `ao session kill` cleared the session.

Symptom: prompt arrived partially or the `Enter` was eaten by claude-code's UI render. AO's lifecycle metadata showed `signal_disagreement runtime=alive process=alive` for the duration.

Related: #1396 (worker fails to start, same shape, different surface), #1110 (`ao send` heredoc bug), #852 (original report).

## Local workaround we shipped

Filesystem-as-IPC plus an ack file (F2 in our SAS-138 stack):

- Parent writes the full prompt body to `/tmp/ao-spawn-prompts/<key>.md` before spawning.
- `ao spawn` is called with a short pointer prompt: `Read /tmp/ao-spawn-prompts/<key>.md and execute the procedure described inside it.`
- The prompt's first action is `touch /tmp/ao-spawn-prompts/<key>.ack`.
- Parent runs `ao spawn` in the background, polls the ack file with a 30s timeout. Absence of ack within the window is treated as a spawn-prompt-undelivered failure — the parent escalates rather than waiting for the ~300s stuck-detection threshold.

This works around the symptom but doesn't fix the underlying design gap: there is no AO-level mechanism for a parent to confirm the child consumed the spawn prompt.

## Suggested upstream fix

Either:

1. **Consume-acknowledgment in the runtime plugin**: the tmux runtime polls the worker process's stdin/stdout for an ack token after delivering the prompt; spawn returns success only when the token is observed. Bound by a configurable timeout.
2. **`--prompt-file <path>` flag on `ao spawn`**: bypasses tmux keystroke delivery entirely. The plugin's launch command points the worker at the file (e.g., the claude-code plugin passes `--initial-prompt-file` or constructs `cat <file> | claude-code` invocation). Eliminates the delivery channel as a failure mode.

(2) is structurally cleaner because it removes the keystroke channel for prompt-delivery purposes; (1) layers a check on top of the existing channel.

## Why filing this fresh rather than commenting on #1396/#852

Both of those are about agent-not-starting-at-all in single-spawn mode. The chain-spawn variant is distinct because the parent-child relationship adds an observability gap (the parent thinks the spawn succeeded; only the child knows the prompt didn't arrive). Worth tracking separately so the chain-spawn use case doesn't get lost when those single-spawn issues are addressed.

title: lifecycle: ao report completed doesn't terminate the runtime; chain-spawn workers idle until stuck-detection at ~300s
body:
## Summary

`ao report completed` is a state declaration in `session-manager.ts:1444-1485` — it writes `idle/research_complete` to the session's lifecycle and returns. The worker's runtime keeps running; AO's idle-beyond-threshold rule eventually promotes the session to `[stuck]` after ~300s. This is most visible in chain-spawn flows where the worker's "I'm done" signal fires at the application layer (e.g., after `gh pr comment`) but the OS process has no obvious reason to exit on its own.

## Context

PR #1300 (merged 2026-04-18) redesigned the lifecycle state machine, but the redesign focuses on state vocabulary, not on terminal-state process termination. For workers whose work pattern is "do thing, report done, exit," the gap is invisible — but for workers that could plausibly stay alive after reporting (long-running orchestrator-driven flows, chain-spawn reviewers, workers waiting for follow-up prompts), the gap is real and confusing.

## Repro

Our chain-spawn reviewer flow:

1. Parent implementer session spawns a sibling reviewer (`ao spawn --agent-type claude-code`).
2. Reviewer fetches the PR diff, runs `/ce-code-review`, fires a custom subagent on safe-drawer paths, merges output, and posts a `## Review report` PR comment via `gh pr comment`.
3. Reviewer calls `ao report completed`. AO logs the state transition. The `claude-code` process keeps running (it has nothing to do, but no OS-level signal to exit).
4. ~300s later, AO's stuck-detection promotes the session to `[stuck]`. Operator runs `ao session kill cd-N` to clear it.

Test 2b (Day 8 of our internal log) had this happen on cd-9 — `ao report completed` was called explicitly and correctly per the lifecycle vocabulary, and the session still went `[stuck]`.

## Local workaround we shipped

Append `ao session kill $AO_SESSION_ID` to the terminal step of every chain-spawn worker (F3 in our SAS-138 stack):

```
ao report completed && ao session kill $AO_SESSION_ID
```

The report writes the state; the kill terminates the runtime. Both required.

## Suggested upstream fix

One of:

1. **`ao report completed --terminate`**: opt-in flag that combines the state declaration with an OS-level termination signal to the worker process. Lets workers that intentionally stay alive after reporting (rare) keep current behavior; everyone else just adds the flag.
2. **Default `ao report completed` to terminate the runtime**, with `--keep-alive` for the rare opposite case. Aligns the verbal contract ("completed") with the OS contract ("process exits").
3. **Document the current behavior explicitly** and recommend the `&& ao session kill $AO_SESSION_ID` pattern in the docs as the canonical chain-spawn close-out. Lowest-cost fix; doesn't change AO's surface area.

(2) is what most operators expect from "report completed"; (1) is the conservative migration path; (3) is the cheap doc-only option.

Filing fresh because PR #1300 didn't address the runtime-termination dimension, and existing related issues (#1454 inverse case, #1187 zombies, #1503 kill bug) describe different shapes of the same lifecycle-vs-process-exit gap.

title: ao start first-run via autoCreateConfig does not register project in global config
body:
## Summary

`ao start` has multiple entry paths and only some of them write the project to the global registry at `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`. The first-run path (`autoCreateConfig`) writes a flat local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` in the cwd but **never** calls `registerProjectInGlobalConfig`. The dashboard reads only the global config (`packages/web/src/lib/services.ts:loadDashboardConfig`), so a project bootstrapped by first-run is invisible to it until something else registers it later.

This is a leftover gap from the multi-project work in #1343 (`f3ce113c`).

## User-visible symptom

Once a global config exists (because some other project — say project A — was registered via `ao start <path>` while AO was running, or via the `registerFlatConfig` fallback), running `ao start` inside project B with only a local yaml does not add project B to global. **The dashboard keeps showing only project A** even though you just started AO from inside project B and the CLI happily reports the orchestrator/dashboard are up. From the user's POV the dashboard appears broken or stuck on the wrong project; in reality `ao start` silently produced inconsistent state because it took a non-global-registering entry path.

The same inconsistency surfaces as: a second `ao start <other-path>` from outside any repo failing with `ConfigNotFoundError` because the global registry is empty even though the user previously \"registered\" a project via first-run.

## Repro

```bash
# clean slate
rm ~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml
cd /path/to/some-repo-with-no-yaml
ao start              # first run -> autoCreateConfig writes ./agent-orchestrator.yaml
cat ~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml   # ENOENT — global was never created
```

Now open the dashboard at `http://localhost:3000`. The project does not appear because `loadDashboardConfig` falls back to the cwd yaml only when the global is missing, and even then it doesn't persist anything to the global registry.

A second `ao start <other-path>` from a different cwd then fails with `ConfigNotFoundError` (`No agent-orchestrator.yaml found. Run \`ao start\` to create one.`) because the line-1656 branch tries `loadConfig(globalConfigPath)` if exists else `loadConfig()`, and neither resolves.

Multi-project variant (the dashboard-shows-wrong-project case):

```bash
# project A: registered globally via the running+path branch
ao start                       # in project A first time (committed flat yaml -> registerFlatConfig)
# AO running, global has only A

cd /path/to/project-B           # has its own local yaml
ao start                        # uses local yaml, never updates global
# dashboard at :3000 still shows only project A
```

## Expected

Every `ao start` entry path that successfully bootstraps or identifies a project should ensure the project ends up in `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`. The dashboard, `ao start <path>` from elsewhere, and `ao spawn` should all see the project on the next interaction without further manual action.

## Actual

Registration into the global config happens only on these paths:

| Entry | Registers globally? |
|---|---|
| `ao start <path\|url>` while AO is running (`start.ts:1646`) | yes |
| `ao start` (no arg), local yaml exists but fails to validate -> `registerFlatConfig` (`start.ts:2134`) | yes |
| `ao start` (no arg), no yaml anywhere -> `autoCreateConfig` (`start.ts:2127`) | **no** <- bug |
| `ao start <projectId>` against a wrapped multi-project local yaml | no |
| `ao start <path>` while AO is **not** running -> `addProjectToConfig` against a local config (`start.ts:970` else-branch) | no |

## Root cause

`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:797` (`autoCreateConfig`):

\`\`\`ts
const outputPath = resolve(workingDir, \"agent-orchestrator.yaml\");
// ...
writeFileSync(outputPath, yamlContent);
// returns loadConfig(outputPath) — never touches global
\`\`\`

`addProjectToConfig` already shows the right pattern at `start.ts:957`:

\`\`\`ts
if (isCanonicalGlobalConfigPath(config.configPath)) {
  registerProjectInGlobalConfig(projectId, projectId, resolvedPath, {...}, config.configPath);
  ...
}
\`\`\`

`autoCreateConfig` should do the same after the local write.

## Proposed fix

In `autoCreateConfig`, after `writeFileSync(outputPath, yamlContent)`:

1. Ensure the global config exists (create empty if missing — same helper `registerProjectInGlobalConfig` uses).
2. Call `registerProjectInGlobalConfig(projectId, projectId, workingDir, { repo, defaultBranch, sessionPrefix }, getGlobalConfigPath())`.
3. Keep the local flat yaml for behavior config (agent rules, plugin choices) — global only holds identity.

Same approach for the `start.ts:970` else-branch in `addProjectToConfig` and for `ao start <projectId>` against wrapped local — they should also register into global so the dashboard sees them.

## Tests

- `start.test.ts`: first-run with no config anywhere -> assert `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` exists afterward and contains the new project entry.
- Same for `addProjectToConfig` against a non-canonical config path.
- Regression: second `ao start <other-path>` from outside any repo no longer throws `ConfigNotFoundError`.
- Regression: with global already populated by project A, `ao start` inside project B (local-yaml-only) ends with project B present in global config.

## Impact

- **Dashboard shows wrong/stale project set.** Once a global config exists, any project started via the local-yaml path is silently absent from the dashboard — the user sees only the projects that happened to take a global-registering entry path.
- Second `ao start <path>` from outside any repo throws `ConfigNotFoundError` instead of registering and starting (the symptom that prompted this investigation).
- General \"can't make up its mind\" behavior — same UX action produces different registry state depending on which row of the entry-path matrix you hit. Users have no way to predict which.

## Related

- #1343 — original multi-project + global config (the registration paths it wired)
- #1466 — storage redesign (projectId-based paths)
- `packages/web/src/lib/services.ts:loadDashboardConfig` — reads global only, with cwd-yaml fallback that doesn't backfill global

## Out of scope

`ao project add` subcommand exists in `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts` (`registerProject_cmd`) but is not wired into `program.ts` — separate cleanup, file as its own issue.

title: Worktree destroy() fallback uses rmSync without git worktree prune, leaving stale .git/worktrees registration
Dashboard project list shows killed orchestrator as running (stale card)
body:
## Summary

When the only orchestrator session for a project has been terminated (e.g. via `ao session kill <id>`), the project list / dashboard summary still renders an orchestrator card for that project. Clicking through to the session detail correctly shows **Terminal ended — process missing** with reason **Session terminated (manually killed)**. The two views disagree.

## Repro

1. Have multiple projects registered in global config.
2. `ao session kill <orchestrator-session-id>` for projects A and B.
3. `ao start` (restoring only project C's orchestrator, or none).
4. Open dashboard. Projects A and B still show an orchestrator card as if running.
5. Click the card → session detail page shows the session is terminated.

## Root cause

`packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:196–251` — `listDashboardOrchestrators` iterates all sessions from `listCached()`. Selection logic at lines 222–228 prefers a non-terminal session per project, but when *every* candidate for a project is terminal, both branches' `isTerminalSession(...)` are true and the tie falls through (line 239) to picking the lexicographically-latest ID. The terminal session ends up in `bestByProject` and is returned as a `DashboardOrchestratorLink`. There is no final filter at line 244 to drop projects whose winner is terminal.

`ao session kill` itself is correct: `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2142–2157` sets `lifecycle.session.state = "terminated"` and `runtime.state = "missing"` and invalidates the cache. The data on disk is right; the dashboard serializer just doesn't act on it.

The card type carries only `{id, projectId, projectName}` — no lifecycle — so the dashboard renders it as live. The session detail page reads the full record and correctly shows the terminated state. Hence the divergence.

## User-visible impact

- Dashboard misrepresents project state — users think an orchestrator is alive when it's been killed.
- Clicking through is the only way to discover the truth, which erodes trust in the project list.
- Combined with the global-config registration inconsistency (#1561), users see ghost orchestrators they can't directly act on from the project list.

## Proposed fix

In `listDashboardOrchestrators` (`packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:244`), filter the result map before mapping to `DashboardOrchestratorLink`:

```ts
return [...bestByProject.values()]
  .filter((session) => !isTerminalSession(session))
  .map(...);
```

Alternative: surface lifecycle state on `DashboardOrchestratorLink` so the dashboard can render a distinct "killed" treatment. Filtering is simpler and matches user expectation that "killed" means "not running."

## Scope

Cross-platform — exists on macOS, Linux, and Windows main.

title: Restored orchestrator terminal stuck on "Connecting" until manual page refresh
body:
## Summary

After `ao stop` followed by `ao start` (with restore), the orchestrator's terminal pane in the dashboard shows **Connecting** indefinitely. The Claude session content does not appear until the user manually refreshes the page. After refresh, everything works normally.

This is more visible on Windows now that the new pty-host sweep (#TBD-Option-A) makes `ao stop` → `ao start` round-trip cleanly. The same race exists on macOS/Linux where users have likely seen it intermittently.

## Repro

1. Open the dashboard with an orchestrator session running.
2. `ao stop` (parent + pty-hosts shut down cleanly).
3. `ao start` — accept the prompt to restore the orchestrator session.
4. Watch the dashboard tab that was already open. Terminal pane stays at **Connecting**.
5. Refresh the browser → terminal connects and renders correctly.

## Root cause

`packages/web/src/components/MuxProvider.tsx` open-message replay races with the \"exited\" cleanup:

1. Old pty-host exits during `ao stop` → mux server sends `msg.type === \"exited\"` to the browser.
2. `MuxProvider.tsx:147` deletes the sessionId from `openedTerminalsRef`.
3. WS disconnects, then reconnects after pty-host comes back up.
4. `ws.addEventListener(\"open\")` (`MuxProvider.tsx:98–124`) iterates `openedTerminalsRef` to replay open messages — but the entry was already deleted in step 2, so no open is sent for the restored session.
5. `useXtermTerminal.ts:362–369` re-sends *resize* on reconnect but never re-calls `openTerminal`.
6. UI sits at \"Connecting\" forever; manual refresh re-mounts `useXtermTerminal`, which calls `openTerminal` again from scratch.

## Proposed fix

Add an effect in `useXtermTerminal` that re-calls `openTerminal(sessionId, tmuxName)` whenever `muxStatus` transitions to `\"connected\"`. This guarantees the open message is replayed on every reconnect regardless of whether `openedTerminalsRef` still holds the entry, without changing the semantics of `\"exited\"` for legitimate process-died cases.

Alternative: skip the delete in the `\"exited\"` handler so reconnect always replays. Less precise — leaves stale entries in `openedTerminalsRef` for sessions that genuinely ended.

## Scope

Cross-platform. Exists on main for macOS/Linux. Surfaces more reliably on Windows after the pty-host sweep lands because clean `ao stop` → restore is now the common path rather than the orphan/force-kill path.

title: Windows: skeleton console window flashes during ao stop (ConPTY teardown)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `ao stop` paints brief skeleton console windows (empty title bar + client area, ~100ms each) before disappearing. On some Windows builds — observed on a Windows VPS — the windows do not disappear cleanly: a dead terminal with an invisible client area and the visible window chrome persists until manual cleanup.

This is **upstream ConPTY teardown behavior**, not a bug we introduced. Filing for visibility, paper trail, and so we don't re-investigate.

## Repro

1. `ao start <project>` (Windows, ConPTY-backed pty-host runtime).
2. `ao stop` after the orchestrator/sessions are running.
3. Observe one or more skeleton window flashes during the stop sequence.
4. On older Windows builds: at least one window may persist with an empty client area + title bar.

## What is NOT the cause (already verified)

- **Our cleanup path is correct.** Sweep output reads `Swept 1 pty-host(s): 1 graceful, 0 force-killed` — meaning `ptyHostKill()` over the named pipe succeeds, the pty-host's `shutdown()` runs `pty.kill()` (disposes ConPTY), waits 50ms, then `process.exit(0)`. No `taskkill` is invoked in this path.
- **`taskkill` invocations use `windowsHide: true`** (`packages/core/src/platform.ts:138`), so even when force-kill fires they don't paint a window.
- **Removing `detached: true` is not an option.** The pty-host must outlive the parent `ao` process for the session-persistence/restore model to work (mirrors tmux daemon on Linux). Without it, Ctrl+C on the cli would kill every running agent. See `packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/index.ts:103`.

## Root cause (upstream)

When `pty.kill()` disposes the ConPTY pseudo-console inside the pty-host, the entire process group attached to that pseudo-console is torn down: the shell (`pwsh.exe`), node-pty's `conpty_console_list_agent.exe` helper, `conhost.exe` bound to the pseudo-console, and any process the agent itself spawned (claude, codex, git, gh, npm, …). Each of these processes has a console handle that Windows hands back to the desktop on exit. On current Windows builds (< 24H2 / build 26100), Windows briefly paints the console window frame for each one before the process actually exits — the "skeleton" flash.

This is documented across the ecosystem:

- microsoft/terminal#4050 — `ClosePseudoConsole()` leaves lingering `conhost.exe` processes
- microsoft/terminal#1810 — `ClosePseudoConsole` API hanging
- microsoft/terminal#17688 — ConPty hangs when calling `ClosePseudoConsole` (with `PSEUDOCONSOLE_INHERIT_CURSOR`, large buffers)
- microsoft/vscode#86472 — terminal processes (conhost.exe) do not get destroyed/reused
- microsoft/vscode#76548 — closing a conpty terminal can hang the window
- nodejs/node#21825 — `child_process` `windowsHide: true` ignored when `detached: true` (potential secondary cause: one extra spawn-time flash per pty-host)

**Microsoft fixed this for Windows 11 24H2 (build 26100):** `ClosePseudoConsole` now returns immediately without waiting for the PTY to drain. Users on 24H2+ should see materially less of this.

## Why winpty is not an escape hatch

The historical workaround across the ecosystem was switching node-pty's backend via `useConpty: false`. node-pty has **removed winpty support** (microsoft/node-pty#842). The flag is deprecated and gone. Pinning an old node-pty to recover winpty would mean missing security/stability updates and ConPTY-only features — not a viable path.

## Why `start /B` / wrapper approaches don't help

A `cmd.exe /c start /B` wrapper around the shell only changes how the *shell itself* allocates a console. The dominant flash source is the agent's children (gh, git, node helpers) which AO does not control — those launch with whatever flags the agent chooses. The wrapper also adds a `cmd.exe` hop that breaks signal forwarding. Cosmetic gain ≪ correctness loss.

## User impact

- **Cosmetic on modern Windows:** brief skeleton flashes during `ao stop`. Annoying, no functional impact.
- **Worse on older Windows builds (e.g. some VPS images):** dead window may persist with the title bar and an invisible client area. User must close it manually. Underlying cause: `conhost.exe` not exiting after `ClosePseudoConsole` (microsoft/terminal#4050). This is the same family as the WER `0x800700e8` dialog AO previously encountered — both are ConPTY teardown not running cleanly.

## Mitigations we have already shipped

- **Graceful pipe-based shutdown** (`MSG_KILL_REQ`) so `pty.kill()` runs before the host exits. Significantly reduces (but does not eliminate) the WER `0x800700e8` dialog. See `packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/pty-host.ts:321`.
- **50ms `setTimeout` before `process.exit(0)`** so node-pty's native cleanup gets a tick to run before the event loop unwinds. See `packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/pty-host.ts:376`.
- **Sideband pty-host PID registry** (`~/.agent-orchestrator/windows-pty-hosts.json`) so `ao stop` can find and graceful-kill detached pty-hosts even when their session JSON is gone. See `packages/core/src/windows-pty-registry.ts`.
- **Sweep on `ao stop`** that does graceful-then-force kill of every registered pty-host before SIGTERMing the parent. See `sweepWindowsPtyHosts` in `packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/index.ts:498`.

These changes mean every AO-driven stop **does** run the disposal path. The remaining flashes are not from missing cleanup — they are inherent to ConPTY's per-process console teardown on pre-24H2 Windows.

## Possible future work (low priority)

1. **Document as a known Windows behavior** in the README / Windows-specific docs, with a note that 24H2+ is materially better.
2. **Investigate nodejs/node#21825 mitigation.** If `windowsHide: true` is silently ignored for the pty-host spawn (because of `detached: true`), there may be one extra spawn-time flash per session. Workaround would be a `.vbs` or detach-via-job-object spawn helper. Marginal cosmetic gain, non-trivial implementation. Not worth doing speculatively — first verify with a test that observes a spawn-time flash on a single `ao start`.
3. **Bump the minimum supported Windows build to 24H2** in docs as ConPTY usability matures. (Not enforce — just signal.)

## Out of scope

This issue is not blocking the Windows platform adapter merge (`feat/windows-platform-adapter`). The functional path (`ao stop` actually kills sessions, no orphans, no WER dialog blocking the UI) is correct. The flashes are cosmetic on supported Windows and an upstream limitation on older builds.

## Repro environment

- Windows 11 (build varies)
- Observed on developer workstation (multiple flashes during stop) and on a Windows VPS (lingering empty window with title bar)
- node-pty: current version (ConPTY-only)
- AO branch: `feat/windows-platform-adapter` with sideband registry + sweep landed

title: fix(web): refresh session sidebar from local metadata writes
body:
## Summary
- add TanStack Query to the web app provider and use it only for the session-detail sidebar sessions query
- keep the last successful sidebar session list visible when a background refresh fails
- add a sidebar-only `/api/sessions?view=sidebar` path that reads local session metadata via `listLocal()` instead of the live/enriched path
- make `/api/events` and `/api/sessions/patches` local-only with no-store responses so sidebar membership snapshots avoid runtime and agent probes
- watch AO project session metadata directories from the mux WebSocket server and broadcast a fresh sessions snapshot when session JSON files change
- pass the actual sidebar fetch error through to ProjectSidebar for better diagnostics

Closes #1410

## Why
The stale sidebar was not because local JSON reads are inherently slow. The slow path was that the detail-page sidebar and membership signals still depended on APIs that could touch runtime liveness, agent probes, OpenCode discovery, and metadata enrichment. Polling faster helped a little, but it did not make burst-spawn changes arrive when AO writes the local session metadata.

This PR makes the sidebar data path local-only and adds a direct local signal: when AO writes a project session metadata JSON file, the mux server debounces briefly, fetches `/api/sessions/patches`, and pushes that snapshot to connected browsers. The React Query sidebar then overlays known lightweight patch changes and refetches the full local sidebar list when membership changes, which is the piece needed for newly spawned workers to appear quickly.

title: session-manager: kill() races with stale-runtime reconciler — manual kill mislabeled as runtime_lost
body:
## Bug

When a user clicks **Kill** on a session (dashboard kanban or session detail), the resulting metadata records `lifecycle.session.reason = "runtime_lost"` instead of `"manually_killed"`. Same outcome via `ao session kill <id>`. The session correctly transitions to `terminated`, but the *reason* is wrong, which loses the user-vs-environment distinction throughout the system.

**Reproduced on:** `feat/windows-platform-adapter` @ HEAD (cross-platform — observed on Windows, code path is OS-agnostic).

## Reproduction

1. `ao start` in any project, spawn a session
2. Click the **Kill** button on the session detail page (or `ao session kill <id>`)
3. Read `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<projectId>/sessions/<id>.json`

**Observed:**
```json
"lifecycle": {
  "session": { "state": "terminated", "reason": "runtime_lost", ... },
  "runtime": { "state": "exited", "reason": "process_missing", ... }
},
"lifecycleEvidence": "runtime_dead process_dead activity_signal=valid via_native activity=exited at=...",
"status": "killed"
```

**Expected:** `session.reason: "manually_killed"`, `lifecycleEvidence: "manual_kill_requested"` (or similar user-initiated marker).

## Root Cause

`session-manager.ts` `kill()` (around L2055-2160) destroys the runtime *before* writing the terminated lifecycle patch:

```typescript
await runtimePlugin.destroy(handle);     // L2095 — runtime exits here
// ... worktree teardown ...
const terminatedLifecycle = buildUpdatedLifecycle(...);  // L2142
updateMetadata(sessionsDir, sessionId, ...);             // L2151 — patch written
```

In the gap between L2095 and L2151, the lifecycle worker's polling loop calls `sm.list()`, which runs the stale-runtime reconciler. The reconciler sees `runtimeHandle` referencing a dead PID and persists `runtime_lost` to disk. When `kill()`'s patch lands a few ms later, `buildUpdatedLifecycle` reads the just-mutated `raw` and overwrites only the fields it explicitly sets — but `lifecycleEvidence` is set by the reconciler and the timing means we end up with a Frankenstein record.

This is a race between two writers to the same metadata file with no ordering guarantee.

## Why This Matters

- `manually_killed` and `runtime_lost` are not interchangeable in `deriveLegacyStatus` (both currently map to `"killed"` legacy status, but that's coincidental — future state-machine work that distinguishes them will see only `runtime_lost`).
- Telemetry / activity logs lose the user-action signal — unable to distinguish "user killed it" from "tmux daemon crashed."
- The `manually_killed` enum value in canonical lifecycle reasons effectively never gets written in practice. Code paths that branch on it (e.g., recovery actions) are dead.
- Tied to #1503 (kill archives sessions) and #1458 (handle blanked on terminated) — same kill path, different symptoms.

## Suggested Fix

In `session-manager.ts:kill()`:

1. **Write the terminated lifecycle patch FIRST**, before `runtimePlugin.destroy()`. This stamps the user-initiated reason on disk before any reconciler can race.
2. **Make the reconciler in `sm.list()` idempotent on user-initiated reasons.** Add a guard: if `session.lifecycle.session.state === "terminated"` AND `session.lifecycle.session.reason ∈ {manually_killed, pr_merged, auto_cleanup, error_in_process}`, skip the runtime-lost overwrite. The reconciler exists to *detect* dead runtimes, not to relabel sessions that already have a definitive terminal reason.

Either fix alone closes the race; both together is defense-in-depth.

## Test Coverage Gap

`__tests__/session-manager/lifecycle.test.ts` covers transitions but doesn't have a test that holds the reconciler against a concurrent kill. A test that kills a session while a parallel `list()` call runs and asserts `reason === "manually_killed"` would catch this.

## Related

- #1503 — kill() archives sessions (orthogonal symptom of the same kill code path)
- #1458 — runtimeHandle/tmuxName dropped on terminated (different field, same race window)

## Discovered

While exhaustively dashboard-testing on Windows for the `feat/windows-platform-adapter` merge — verified to be a code-path issue, not Windows-specific.

title: bug(web): kanban card stuck in 'stuck · PR not created' after agent opens PR — requires hard reload
body:
## Bug

After an agent successfully opens a PR via the metadata-update hooks, the kanban card stays in the **stuck · PR not created** column on the dashboard kanban view until the user hard-reloads the page (or navigates away and back). Backend metadata is correct: `lifecycle.pr.state = "open"`, `pr.number`, `pr.url` are all written to `<id>.json`. The dashboard's SSE stream is delivering session updates (other fields like activity timestamp tick), but the kanban column placement does not reflect the PR-state flip.

**Reproduced on:** `feat/windows-platform-adapter` @ HEAD; symptom is platform-agnostic — the SSE/serialize layer doesn't differ by OS.

## Reproduction

1. `ao start`, open the project dashboard
2. Spawn a session that will create a PR (e.g., \`ao spawn --prompt "fix typo in README and open a PR"\`)
3. Watch the kanban card status as the agent runs
4. After the agent opens the PR (PR exists on GitHub, `<id>.json` shows `lifecycle.pr.state="open"`):
   - **Expected:** card moves to READY / mergeable / review_pending column within one SSE tick (~5 s)
   - **Observed:** card stays in stuck · "PR not created" column indefinitely
5. Hard-reload the page → card snaps to the correct column immediately

The session detail page (separate route) shows correct PR info the whole time — only the kanban list view is stale.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The kanban serializer (`packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts`) computes the column placement from a hash/diff of session fields delivered via SSE. The hash key for change-detection appears to include `session.state` and `session.reason` but not `lifecycle.pr.state` and `lifecycle.pr.reason` — so when only the PR side flips (and `session.state` stays `working` or `idle`), the client treats it as "no relevant change" and re-renders the card in its old column position.

Sister-bug pattern to #1530 (project deletion not refreshing) and #1564 (terminal stuck on Connecting) — all three are SSR/cache invalidation gaps where backend state is correct but the dashboard misses an update window.

## Affected Files (likely)

- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` — kanban serializer / column-bucket logic
- `packages/web/src/hooks/useSessionEvents.ts` — SSE consumer (may be filtering out PR-only updates)
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` — board memoization

## Suggested Fix

Audit the SSE diff key in `serialize.ts` (or wherever `columnFor(session)` is computed) and ensure it includes:
- `lifecycle.pr.state`
- `lifecycle.pr.reason`
- `lifecycle.legacyStatus` (since column placement keys on it)

Easiest verification: log the inputs to `columnFor()` in dev mode, compare values before vs. after a PR-state flip, confirm the dependency list captures all relevant fields.

## Why This Matters

This is the most-visible kanban bug for users running real agents. The whole point of the dashboard is to see PR progress in real time — when cards lie about PR-creation status, users assume the agent is stuck and intervene unnecessarily, or miss real PRs that need review.

## Discovered

End-to-end Windows dashboard test on `feat/windows-platform-adapter`: real PR (`Priyanchew/ao-test#3` and `#4`) opened by agent, lifecycle metadata flipped to `pr.state=open / merge_ready` within ~10 s, kanban card sat in stuck column for several SSE ticks until manual reload.

## Related

- #1564 — restored terminal stuck on Connecting (sibling SSR-staleness bug)
- #1530 — removed project reappears (missing `router.refresh()` after mutation)

title: bug(cli): ao project command implementation exists but is not registered
body:
## Bug

`ao project` is not available from the real CLI, even though project-management support exists in both the backend and CLI source.

## What exists

Backend routes:
- `packages/web/src/app/api/projects/route.ts`
  - `GET /api/projects`
  - `POST /api/projects`
- `packages/web/src/app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts`
  - `GET`, `PATCH`/`PUT`, `DELETE`, `POST` repair

CLI implementation:
- `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts`
  - `ao project ls`
  - `ao project add <path>`
  - `ao project rm <id>`
  - `ao project set-default <id>`

## Root cause

`packages/cli/src/program.ts` does not import or call `registerProject_cmd(program)`, so the command file is never wired into the actual `ao` command tree.

The existing project command tests instantiate `registerProject_cmd()` directly, so they pass while the real CLI still lacks `ao project`.

## Expected

`ao project --help` should show the project subcommands, and `ao project ls` should work when portfolio mode is enabled.

## Suggested fix

Register the command in `packages/cli/src/program.ts`:

```ts
import { registerProject_cmd } from "./commands/project.js";

// ...
registerProject_cmd(program);
```

Also consider renaming `registerProject_cmd` to `registerProject` for consistency with the rest of the command registration functions.

## Verification

Add or update a program-level test that calls `createProgram()` and asserts the `project` command exists. This catches the exact gap that command-level tests missed.

title: fix(core): deliver enriched review content on changes_requested transition
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the agent never received actual review comment content when a PR transitioned to `changes_requested`. The agent only got a generic message — *"There are review comments on your PR. Details will follow shortly."* — but the detailed review bodies (file paths, line numbers, authors, comment text) never followed.

Closes #1558

## Root Cause

The review dispatch in `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog` has two paths:

| Path | When | What it sends |
|------|------|---------------|
| **Transition reaction** | Status transitions to `changes_requested` | Generic message from config |
| **Backlog dispatch** | Comment fingerprint changes | Enriched content via `formatReviewCommentsMessage()` |

On the first transition, the transition reaction fired (generic message), then the backlog dispatch recorded the fingerprint hash as "already dispatched" — **without ever sending the actual comment content**. The deduplication logic then blocked the enriched dispatch from ever firing for those comments:

1. **Branch B** (lines 1477-1486): recorded `lastPendingReviewDispatchHash` when the transition reaction succeeded, burning the hash without delivering content
2. **Transition guard** (line 1488): `!(oldStatus !== newStatus && newStatus === "changes_requested")` explicitly skipped the enriched dispatch during the transition poll

This is unlike `ci-failed`, which enriches its transition reaction with actual CI check details from the batch cache. `changes-requested` never got the same treatment — review threads are fetched separately in `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`, not in the batch PR enrichment.

## Fix

- **Remove Branch B** — the block that recorded the dispatch hash when the transition reaction succeeded without sending enriched content
- **Remove the transition guard** — so the backlog dispatch fires in the same poll cycle as the transition
- **Update default message** — remove the "Details will follow shortly" promise since details now arrive immediately

After the fix, the enriched review content (file paths, line numbers, authors, comment bodies, thread IDs) is dispatched in the same poll cycle as the transition. The agent receives two messages back-to-back: the generic transition notification followed immediately by the detailed review content. Subsequent polls skip dispatch because the fingerprint hash matches — no duplicates.

## Files Changed

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — removed premature hash recording and transition guard from `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — updated default `changes-requested` message
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts` — updated test to verify enriched content is delivered on transition

## Test plan

- [x] All 1006 core tests pass (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test`)
- [ ] Verify agent receives detailed review comments on first `changes_requested` transition
- [ ] Verify no duplicate dispatch on subsequent polls with unchanged comments
- [ ] Verify new comments arriving while in `changes_requested` trigger a fresh enriched dispatch

title: fix(core): notifier system has 7 bugs — silent by default, dead features, missing context
body:
## Summary

The notifier plugin system has 7 distinct bugs that collectively make it non-functional out of the box and degraded even when explicitly configured. Traced end-to-end from event emission in `lifecycle-manager.ts` through routing in `notifyHuman()` to delivery in each notifier plugin.

---

## Bug 1 (Critical): Zero notifications by default — routing fallback is empty

**Location:** `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1729`

```typescript
const notifierNames = config.notificationRouting[priority] ?? config.defaults.notifiers;
```

`config.defaults.notifiers` defaults to `[]` (empty array) in the schema (`config.ts:273`). `notificationRouting` defaults to `{}` (`config.ts:368`).

With no explicit config, `notifierNames` is always `[]`. The `for` loop never executes. **No notifications are ever sent.**

The desktop notifier is registered and functional out of the box (zero config needed), but nothing routes to it. A user who adds `notifiers.desktop.plugin: desktop` but forgets `notificationRouting` or `defaults.notifiers` gets zero notifications with zero errors — just silence.

**Fix:** Either default `defaults.notifiers` to `["desktop"]`, or emit a startup warning when notifiers are registered but no routing points to them.

---

## Bug 2 (Medium): `includeSummary` is a dead config field — declared but never read

**Location:** `config.ts:728`, `types.ts:1208`

The `all-complete` default reaction declares `includeSummary: true`:

```typescript
"all-complete": {
  auto: true,
  action: "notify",
  priority: "info",
  includeSummary: true,  // declared in schema, never read anywhere
}
```

The field is defined in `ReactionConfig` (`types.ts:1208`) and validated by Zod (`config.ts:159`), but `executeReaction()` in `lifecycle-manager.ts` never reads it. The "all-complete" notification just says:

> "Reaction 'all-complete' triggered notification"

No session summaries, no counts, no useful information.

---

## Bug 3 (Medium): `notifyWithActions()` is never called — actions feature is dead code

**Location:** `types.ts:1081`, every notifier plugin's `notifyWithActions` implementation

The `Notifier` interface defines `notifyWithActions?()`, and Slack, Discord, Desktop, Webhook, and Composio all implement it with rich action button support. But the lifecycle manager has **zero call sites** — `notifyHuman()` only ever calls `notifier.notify()`.

Every notifier's `notifyWithActions` implementation (action buttons in Slack, links in Discord, callback endpoints) is dead code.

---

## Bug 4 (Medium): Status transition events missing PR and CI context

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:2019-2025`

When a status transition fires (e.g., `ci.failing`, `review.changes_requested`), the event is created with:

```typescript
data: { oldStatus, newStatus }
```

But the Slack notifier (`notifier-slack/index.ts:55-78`) tries to render:
- `event.data.prUrl` → always `undefined` for status transition events
- `event.data.ciStatus` → **never set by any code path at all**

PR URL is only included in `pr.closed` events (`lifecycle-manager.ts:2078`). CI status is never included in any event's data.

**Result:** Slack notifications for CI failures, review changes, approvals, etc. never show PR links or CI status badges — the rich formatting the Slack plugin was built for is never triggered.

---

## Bug 5 (Medium): Reaction "notify" action produces generic, unhelpful messages

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:1267-1280`

When a reaction with `action: "notify"` fires, it creates:

```typescript
const event = createEvent("reaction.triggered", {
  message: `Reaction '${reactionKey}' triggered notification`,
  data: { reactionKey },
});
```

This is the notification the user receives for `agent-stuck`, `agent-needs-input`, `agent-exited`, `approved-and-green`, and `all-complete` — all configured with `action: "notify"` by default.

The user gets: *"Reaction 'agent-stuck' triggered notification"* instead of something like *"Session my-session has been idle for 15 minutes on project my-project"*. No session context, no project details, no PR link, no actionable information.

The escalation path has the same problem (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1218-1223`):
```
"Reaction 'ci-failed' escalated after 3 attempts"
```

---

## Bug 6 (Low): Several status transitions emit no events

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:232-261`

`statusToEventType()` returns `null` for these transitions:

| Status | Event emitted | Consequence |
|--------|--------------|-------------|
| `spawning` | none | Session creation is silent |
| `detecting` | none | Status ambiguity is silent |
| `idle` | none | Agent going idle is silent |
| `cleanup` | none | Post-merge cleanup is silent |
| `done` | none | Session completion is silent |
| `terminated` | none | Session termination is silent |

The `idle` gap is notable: when a session transitions to `idle`, no event fires, so no notification is sent. A user expecting "notify me when my agent goes idle" has no way to configure it — `idle` is invisible to the event system.

The `done` gap means individual session completion is always silent. Only the aggregate `all-complete` check fires (and per Bug 2, produces a useless message).

---

## Bug 7 (Low): No validation that routing references resolve to registered notifiers

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:1731-1735`, `notifier-resolution.ts:15-31`

```typescript
for (const name of notifierNames) {
  const target = resolveNotifierTarget(config, name);
  const notifier = registry.get<Notifier>("notifier", target.reference)
    ?? registry.get<Notifier>("notifier", target.pluginName);
  if (notifier) {  // silently skips if null
    await notifier.notify(eventWithPriority);
  }
}
```

If a user has a typo in their routing config (`notificationRouting.urgent: [desktip]`), the registry lookup returns `null`, the `if (notifier)` check silently skips it, and **no notification is sent with no warning**. No startup validation either.

---

## Severity summary

| # | Severity | Issue |
|---|----------|-------|
| 1 | **Critical** | Empty default routing → zero notifications out of the box |
| 2 | Medium | `includeSummary` is dead config — never read |
| 3 | Medium | `notifyWithActions()` is never called — dead code |
| 4 | Medium | Status events missing `prUrl`/`ciStatus` → Slack rich formatting broken |
| 5 | Medium | Reaction "notify" produces generic messages without context |
| 6 | Low | `idle`, `done`, `spawning`, `terminated` transitions invisible to events |
| 7 | Low | Typos in routing config silently produce no notifications |

Bug 1 is the most likely reason it "doesn't work" — even with plugins correctly configured, the routing defaults to empty and nothing fires. Bugs 4 and 5 compound this: even when routing IS configured, the notifications are missing context and rich formatting.

title: bug(scm-github): ETag guards and GraphQL batch spam console with warnings on expected HTTP 304 responses
body: ## Bug The ETag guards and GraphQL batch error handling in `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` use raw `console.warn()`/`console.error()` that fire on every poll cycle. HTTP 304 ("Not Modified") is the **expected** response when the ETag matches — it means nothing changed — but the catch blocks don't distinguish between 304 cache hits and real errors. This floods the orchestrator terminal with noise every poll cycle. ### Screenshot ## All Affected Locations There are **4 raw console statements** in `graphql-batch.ts` that bypass the observer logging pattern: | # | Line | Level | Message | Trigger | |---|------|-------|---------|---------| | 1 | 460 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` | | 2 | 525-527 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 2] Commit status check failed for ${commitKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` | | 3 | 587 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 3] Review comments check failed for ${cacheKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments` | | 4 | 1156 | `console.error` | `[GraphQL Batch Warning] Batch enrichment partially failed: ${errorMsg}` | GraphQL batch query exceptions | Meanwhile, the **other logging in the same file** (lines 1071-1082, 1138) correctly uses `observer?.log("info", ...)` with proper log level management. ## Root Cause All three ETag guard functions (`checkPRListETag`, `checkCommitStatusETag`, `checkReviewCommentsETag`) call `gh api` with an `If-None-Match` header. When the content hasn't changed, GitHub returns 304 and `gh` exits with a non-zero status. The catch blocks fire and log a warning — but they don't check whether the error is a 304 (expected) or an actual failure (network error, auth issue, 5xx). Example from line 460: ```typescript // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- Observability logging for ETag errors console.warn(`[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}`); ``` ## Expected Behavior - HTTP 304 should be handled silently (or at debug level via observer) - Only actual errors (network failures, 4xx other than 304, 5xx) should warn - All logging should use `observer?.log()` instead of raw `console.*` for consistency ## Fix 1. Check for `304` in the error message before warning — skip or downgrade to debug for 304 2. Migrate all 4 instances from raw `console.warn()`/`console.error()` to `observer?.log()` (consistent with the rest of the file) 3. Only log at `"warn"` level for genuine errors, not cache hits ## Impact - **Noise:** Orchestrator terminal becomes unreadable due to warning spam on every poll cycle (3 warnings per cycle × every 5s) - **Misleading:** Operators may think something is broken when the system is working correctly - **No functional impact:** The 304 path works correctly despite the warnings — it just shouldn't log as a failure

title: fix(core): post-launch prompt delivery is unreliable — blind timer, false success, and weak task prompt
body:
## Problem

When a session spawns, the task prompt often never reaches the agent. The agent sits at an empty `❯` prompt with full context in its system prompt but no trigger to start working. This has been reproduced consistently.

### 1. Blind delivery (no readiness check)

The session manager waits a fixed 3 seconds then sends the task prompt via `tmux send-keys`. It doesn't check whether Claude Code has finished starting up. If Claude Code is still loading (banner, hooks, CLAUDE.md), the keystrokes go into the loading screen and are lost.

**Location:** `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:1433-1437`

```typescript
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, baseDelayMs * attempt));
await plugins.runtime.sendMessage(handle, agentLaunchConfig.prompt);
```

### 2. False success (no delivery verification)

The retry logic only catches exceptions from tmux itself. Since tmux successfully accepts the keys — it just pastes them into a loading screen — no exception is thrown. `promptDelivered` is set to `"true"`, the retry loop breaks, and the CLI reports success. The metadata says everything is fine while the agent is idle.

**Location:** `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:1438-1440`

```typescript
promptDelivered = true;
break;
```

### 3. Weak task prompt (causes redundant API calls)

For issue-based spawns, the task prompt is just `"Work on issue: 1580"`. The agent's first instinct is to call `gh issue view 1580` to fetch context — but the full issue details (title, description, labels, code locations) are already in the system prompt. This wastes time and an API call on every spawn.

**Location:** `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts:203-206`

```typescript
taskPrompt: config.userPrompt
  ? config.userPrompt
  : config.issueId
    ? `Work on issue: ${config.issueId}`
    : undefined,
```

## Fix

### Readiness detection before sending

Replace the blind 3s timer with a poll loop that checks for the `❯` prompt via `tmux capture-pane` + `detectActivity()` — the same pattern `ao send` already uses. Only send the task prompt once the agent is confirmed in interactive mode.

### Delivery verification after sending

After sending, poll again to confirm the agent transitioned from idle to active. Only set `promptDelivered = "true"` after confirming the agent is processing. If it stays idle, retry. If all retries fail, set `promptDelivered = "false"` so the CLI warns the user.

### Improved task prompt for issue-based spawns

Change the task prompt from:
```
Work on issue: 1580
```
To:
```
Work on issue #1580. The full issue details are already in your system prompt — you can start implementing without fetching the issue unless you need additional context (e.g. comments, linked issues, or recent updates).
```

## Impact

- Sessions reliably start working on their task without manual intervention
- `promptDelivered` metadata accurately reflects reality
- Agents skip redundant `gh issue view` calls on spawn

title: fix(core): reliable post-launch prompt delivery with readiness polling
