title: fix(cli): sanitize project IDs derived from folder names
body:
This is an independent contribution and is not affiliated with any hackathon or competition.

## Summary

When running `ao start` in a directory whose name contains dots or special characters (e.g. `llama.cpp`), the project ID derived from the folder name fails Zod validation. This change applies the existing `sanitizeProjectId()` helper to auto-generated project IDs before registration.

## Root Cause

The CLI derives the project ID from `basename(projectPath)` without sanitization. If the folder name contains characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` (such as dots), the subsequent Zod schema validation rejects the config with a runtime error.

## Fix

Two call sites now sanitize the derived ID using the already-existing `sanitizeProjectId()` utility from `@aoagents/ao-core`:

1. `registerFlatConfig()` — project ID derived from flat config path
2. `addProjectToConfig()` — project ID derived when adding an existing repo

The helper lowercases the string, replaces invalid characters with hyphens, strips leading/trailing hyphens, and collapses consecutive hyphens. For example, `llama.cpp` becomes `llama-cpp`.

## Testing

- Existing `sanitizeProjectId` test suite covers this transformation (see `config-generator.test.ts`)
- No new logic introduced — just applying an existing, tested utility at the point of ID derivation

title: ui(web): orchestrator session header is noisy, repetitive, and poorly ordered — redesign + strip markdown '#' from auto-title
body:
## Summary

The orchestrator **session detail page** header (`/projects/[id]/sessions/[orchestrator-id]`) is overloaded, repetitive, and poorly ordered. It crams product brand, project name, a role badge, the orchestrator's own activity, the orchestrator's branch, project-wide fleet counts, an auto-generated title, and the session id into a single bar — with the same identity words repeated up to 3×, two different *scopes* (this session vs. the whole fleet) rendered as visual equals, and a raw markdown `#` leaking into the title.

**Source:** dogfooding / live observation | **Reported by:** @i-trytoohard | **Analyzed against:** `a66a087e`
**Confidence:** High (every element traced to source + the redundant title reproduced from live metadata)
**Scope:** the **orchestrator** variant of the header. Worker (non-orchestrator) session headers are largely fine and should keep their title / real branch / PR / Kill affordances.

## Current state

**agent-orchestrator orchestrator page:**
![ao orchestrator header](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-orchestrator-header-redesign/.issue-assets/orchestrator-header-redesign/ao-orchestrator-header.png)

> `Agent Orchestrator` · `orchestrator` · `• Ready` · `orchestrator/ao-orchestr…` · `1 review` `1 working` `2 pending` `27 done` · `# Agent Orchestrator Orchestrator` · `ao-orchestrator`

**mercury orchestrator page:**
![mercury orchestrator header](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-orchestrator-header-redesign/.issue-assets/orchestrator-header-redesign/mercury-orchestrator-header.png)

> `Agent Orchestrator` · `mercury` · `orchestrator` · `• Idle` · `chore/breezy-hr-ci-skip-` · `26 done` · `# mercury Orchestrator` · `mer-orchestrator`

## Element inventory & data sources

Rendered by `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetailHeader.tsx`:

| # | Element | Source | Line |
|---|---------|--------|------|
| 1 | `Agent Orchestrator` brand (product name, hardcoded) | literal string | `~149` |
| 2 | Project label (`mercury`) — hidden when name == "agent orchestrator" | `projects.find(...).name`; `showHeaderProjectLabel` | `~109,155` |
| 3 | `orchestrator` role badge (amber) | `isOrchestrator` | `~163` |
| 4 | `• Ready/Idle` status pill (**this orchestrator's** activity) | `session.activity` | `~168` |
| 5 | Branch pill (`orchestrator/ao-orchestr…`) | `session.branch` | `~180` |
| 6 | Fleet count pills (`OrchestratorZonePills`) (**other sessions'** state) | `orchestratorZones`, computed in `sessions/[id]/page.tsx:~644` by iterating non-orchestrator sessions' `getAttentionLevel()` | `~194` |
| 7 | Auto-title `# <Project> Orchestrator` | `getSessionTitle(session)` → `session.displayName` | `~200` |
| 8 | Session id (dim) | `session.id` | `~203` |

## Problems

### 1. Identity words repeat up to 3×
On the agent-orchestrator page, **"Orchestrator"** appears three times (brand `Agent Orchestrator`, badge `orchestrator`, title `…Orchestrator`) and **"Agent Orchestrator"** appears twice (brand + title). On mercury, **"orchestrator"** appears twice and **"mercury"** twice. The existing `showHeaderProjectLabel` dedupe (hides the project label when it equals "agent orchestrator") is defeated because the auto-title re-adds the same words downstream.

### 2. The auto-title is pure restatement **and** contains a raw markdown `#` (bug)
Live metadata for `ao-orchestrator` has:
```json
"displayName": "# Agent Orchestrator Orchestrator"
```
Root cause: `deriveDisplayName()` in `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:248` takes the first non-empty line of the orchestrator's spawn prompt — which is a markdown `# <Project> Orchestrator` H1 heading — and **does not strip the leading `#`** (contrast `packages/core/src/format-automated-comments.ts:37`, which already does `.replace(/^#{1,6}\s+/, "")`). So the title is:
- a leaked markdown artifact (`# …`), and
- for an orchestrator, **zero new information** — it only restates the project name + the word "Orchestrator," both already shown by elements #2 and #3.

### 3. Two different scopes are rendered as equals
`• Ready` (element #4) is **this orchestrator's own** activity. The count pills (element #6) are **aggregate counts of the other worker sessions** in the project. They sit adjacent with identical visual weight, implying one scope. There is nothing labeling the counts as fleet-wide.

### 4. Low-value / duplicated elements for orchestrators
- **Branch pill** (`orchestrator/ao-orchestr…`): the orchestrator's branch is auto-derived as `orchestrator/<id>`, truncated, and rarely actionable. Tellingly, `humanizeBranch()` already treats `orchestrator/<id>` as noise (returns `""`), yet the raw branch is still shown as a pill.
- **Session id** (`ao-orchestrator`) duplicates what's already inside the branch pill (`orchestrator/ao-orchestrator`).

### 5. Poor reading order
Identity is split across the bar — project + badge on the far left, title + id on the far right — with self-status and fleet-counts wedged between. There's no clean `identity → status → fleet → actions` grouping; the eye ping-pongs.

## Proposed structure

Collapse to **three clearly-scoped zones + actions**, identity-first, one occurrence of each word:

```
[≡]  <Project>  ·  Orchestrator      • Ready          Fleet · 1 review  1 working  2 pending  27 done        [Open board ↗]
     └──── identity (1×) ────┘        └ self ┘         └────────── fleet (scope-labeled) ──────────┘          └ action ┘
```

**Definitely remove:**
- The auto-title for orchestrators (element #7) — pure restatement.
- The duplicate product brand text on session pages (element #1) — the app logo/sidebar already conveys the product; keep one identity unit: `<Project> · Orchestrator`.
- The orchestrator's own branch pill (element #5) — low value, auto-derived.
- Either the standalone session id **or** the branch — not both. Recommendation: drop the branch, keep the id (it's the canonical `ao send <id>` handle), rendered subtly.

**Keep, but improve:**
- `• Ready/Idle` self-status pill — keep.
- Fleet counts — keep (they're arguably the single most useful thing on an orchestrator page), but **scope-label** them (`Fleet` prefix or a labeled divider) and visually separate from the self-status pill so the two scopes aren't conflated. Consider de-emphasizing `done` (least actionable).
- Right side: orchestrators have no PR/Kill, so the right side is mostly empty today — replace with an **Open board / back-to-project** action.

**Independently, fix the `#` bug** in `deriveDisplayName()` (strip leading markdown heading `^#{1,6}\s+`), since the artifact can leak into *any* session whose prompt starts with a heading, not just orchestrators.

## Code touch points
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetailHeader.tsx` — header layout / `isOrchestrator` branch (the redesign).
- `packages/web/src/app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — `orchestratorZones` computation (`~644`) if fleet labeling changes.
- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:248` `deriveDisplayName()` — strip leading markdown `#` (the bug).
- Reuse existing tokens/classes: `.topbar-status-pill`, `.topbar-zone-pill--*`, `.session-detail-mode-badge`, `.dashboard-app-header__*` (no new component library; dark theme preserved).

## Constraints to respect
- Worker (non-orchestrator) headers keep title / real branch / PR / Kill — only the orchestrator branch changes.
- No inline styles; Tailwind + existing `var(--color-*)` tokens only (per DESIGN.md / repo constraints).

## Related
- [#1499](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1499) — sidebar project-row info-density rework (sibling IA polish).
- [#1220](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1220) — session display-name derivation (same `deriveDisplayName` lineage as the `#` bug).

title: bug(cli): ao start silently aborts at 'Restore these sessions?' prompt — promptConfirm process.exit(0) on spurious cancel drops all worker restores
body:
## Bug

On a normal interactive `ao start`, the **`Restore these sessions?`** prompt can auto-cancel without waiting for input, and because `promptConfirm` calls **`process.exit(0)` on cancel**, the rest of `ao start` is silently aborted. The already-spawned dashboard child and the auto-restored orchestrator keep running independently, so it *looks* like startup completed — but worker sessions are never restored and `last-stop.json` is never reconciled.

**Source:** dogfooding / live observation | **Reported by:** @i-trytoohard | **Analyzed against:** `a66a087e`
**Confidence:** High (mechanism traced to exact lines; on-disk state matches exactly). Medium on the precise cancel trigger.

## Reproduction

1. Have active worker sessions (e.g. `ao-180`, `ao-189`, `ao-191`, `ao-200`).
2. `Ctrl+C` the running `ao start` (graceful shutdown writes `last-stop.json` with all sessions).
3. Run `ao start` again, interactively in a terminal.
4. Observe: the orchestrator is auto-restored, the dashboard comes up, then the `Restore these sessions? ● Yes / ○ No` prompt renders **and immediately concludes** (clack `└` close-cap appears right after it) without waiting.
5. `ao start` exits back to the shell. Worker sessions are **not** restored; only the orchestrator is alive.

### Observed state after the abort
- Only `ao-orchestrator` tmux session alive; `ao-180/189/191/200` gone.
- `last-stop.json` **fully intact** (`sessionIds: ["ao-180","ao-189","ao-191","ao-200","ao-orchestrator"]`, plus other-project orchestrators) — never cleared.
- The dashboard child keeps emitting `[direct-terminal] [MuxServer] …` into the shell *after* `ao start` has exited.

## Root cause

`packages/cli/src/lib/prompts.ts:6` — `promptConfirm` exits the process on cancel:

```ts
export async function promptConfirm(message: string, initialValue = true): Promise<boolean> {
  const result = await confirm({ message, initialValue });
  if (isCancel(result)) {
    console.log(chalk.yellow("\nCancelled."));
    process.exit(0);          // ← aborts ALL remaining startup work
  }
  return result;
}
```

The restore offer at `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:1058` calls this:
```ts
const shouldRestore = await promptConfirm("Restore these sessions?", true);
```

When `confirm` returns a **cancel** (which clack does *immediately and non-interactively* when stdin is not a clean TTY), `promptConfirm` runs `process.exit(0)`. That kills `ao start` mid-startup — **before** any of the `clearLastStop()` / restore-loop branches (start.ts:1058–1171) run. This is why `last-stop.json` is left untouched and zero workers are restored. The two booleans paths are ruled out: `true` → a "Restoring N session(s)" spinner would appear (it doesn't); `false` → `clearLastStop()` would empty the file (it didn't). Only the `isCancel → process.exit(0)` path leaves last-stop intact with no spinner, which is what we see.

### Why the prompt cancels spuriously (likely trigger — Medium confidence)
The dashboard child is spawned with **`stdio: "inherit"`** (`start.ts:835`, `:848`) **before** the restore prompt runs. An inherited-stdin child sharing the terminal disrupts the parent's interactive/raw-mode stdin, so clack's `confirm` sees a non-interactive stdin and cancels immediately. (The child surviving the parent's `process.exit(0)` and continuing to spam the shell — visible in the logs — is consistent with this.) This is intermittent: the same prompt has restored successfully on other restarts, pointing to a stdin/TTY race.

## Impact

- **Silent loss of worker-session restoration** on a routine `Ctrl+C` → `ao start`. The orchestrator (restored independently via `ensureOrchestrator`) + the live dashboard mask the abort, so the user believes startup succeeded.
- `last-stop.json` is left stale, so state is inconsistent.
- High impact because it hits the most common restart flow and produces no error.

## Fix

1. **Primary:** an optional prompt must not `process.exit` on cancel. The restore step is non-critical — a cancel should be treated as "skip restore and continue startup" (or the call site should handle `isCancel` itself), never abort the whole process. Consider a variant like `promptConfirm(message, { default, onCancel: "default" | "skip" })` so non-essential prompts degrade gracefully instead of exiting. (`process.exit` on cancel is only appropriate for prompts that genuinely gate the command.)
2. **Trigger fix:** don't let a child grab interactive stdin before an interactive prompt. Either run the restore prompt **before** spawning the dashboard child, or spawn the dashboard with `stdio: ["ignore", "inherit", "inherit"]` (don't inherit stdin). This removes the spurious-cancel race.
3. Either fix alone stops the data loss; doing both is robust.

## Related
- #1743 — `ao stop → ao update → ao start` restore failures (different mechanism: worktree/default-branch recreation; this one is the prompt aborting startup).
- #1924 — "add timeout to 'Restore these sessions?' prompt" (assumes the prompt *blocks*; this bug is the opposite — it auto-cancels and exits. A non-blocking auto-restore default would also fix this case).
- #1951 — quiet down `ao start` output (the `[direct-terminal]` spam around the prompt compounds the UX).

title: dashboard notifications can be written to a store the live dashboard is not watching
body:
## Bug

Dashboard notifications can be written to a different notification store than the one the live dashboard is watching.

AO currently stores dashboard notifications using a path derived from the raw `configPath`:

```ts
getDashboardNotificationStorePath(configPath)
```

In the hybrid config model, AO may use both:

```txt
<project>/agent-orchestrator.yaml
```

and:

```txt
~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml
```

for the same running AO instance. Because the notification store is config-path-scoped, those two config files produce different dashboard notification stores.

**Source:** local operator report/chat on 2026-05-21
**Reported by:** Adil
**Analyzed against:** remote `main` `50dc18ffa1fe1e7944e214a5f854fba87b1afe61`
**Confidence:** High — observed mismatch between `running.json.configPath`, dashboard process env, and the notification store that received the test notification.

## Observed Behavior

The live AO daemon/dashboard was running with:

```txt
running.configPath = /Users/adilshaikh/Desktop/ao/agent-orchestrator.yaml
```

So the dashboard watched:

```txt
~/.agent-orchestrator/1686e4aaaeaa-observability/dashboard-notifications.jsonl
```

But a dashboard notification was delivered using the global config:

```txt
/Users/adilshaikh/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml
```

So it was written to:

```txt
~/.agent-orchestrator/631d47de14e1-observability/dashboard-notifications.jsonl
```

The notification was successfully persisted, but the dashboard did not show it because it was watching a different file.

In plain terms:

> The notification went to mailbox B, while the dashboard was checking mailbox A.

## Reproduction

1. Start AO from a project-local config:

```bash
cd /path/to/project
ao start
```

2. Ensure the dashboard is running and `running.json` points to the project-local config:

```json
{
  "configPath": "/path/to/project/agent-orchestrator.yaml",
  "port": 3000
}
```

3. Trigger a dashboard notification from a path/context that resolves the global config, for example:

```bash
AO_CONFIG_PATH=~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml ao notify test --to dashboard
```

or run a notifier path that loads global config while the dashboard was started from local config.

4. The notification is written to the global-config-derived dashboard store.

5. The live dashboard does not show the notification because it reads the local-config-derived store.

## Root Cause

Dashboard notification persistence is scoped by **raw config file path**, but the dashboard itself is scoped by the **running AO daemon**.

This is no longer equivalent after the global/root YAML split and multi-project dashboard model.

One live AO dashboard may supervise multiple projects, while notification producers may resolve either the global config or a project-local config. If those paths differ, dashboard notifications split across multiple stores.

## Impact

- Dashboard notifications can silently not appear.
- Manual tests such as `ao notify test --to dashboard` may report success while the visible dashboard shows nothing.
- Notifications are persisted on disk but in the wrong store.
- Multi-project setups are especially vulnerable because one dashboard can supervise several projects but config-path-scoped stores can fragment notification streams.
- Users lose trust in dashboard notifications because delivery appears successful but the UI does not update.

## Recommended Fix

Make dashboard notifications **daemon-scoped**, not raw-config-path-scoped.

### Desired model

One running dashboard/daemon should have one notification stream.

Each notification record already includes:

```json
{
  "projectId": "...",
  "sessionId": "...",
  "type": "...",
  "priority": "..."
}
```

So a single daemon-level store can support multiple projects while still allowing the dashboard to filter/group by project.

### Implementation

Add a derived daemon-level dashboard notification store path to `running.json`.

Example shape:

```json
{
  "pid": 1720,
  "configPath": "/path/to/project/agent-orchestrator.yaml",
  "port": 3000,
  "projects": ["project-a", "project-b"],
  "dashboardNotificationStore": "<derived-ao-base-dir>/dashboard-notifications.jsonl"
}
```

Important: the path should **not be hardcoded**. It should be derived through AO path helpers, e.g. a new helper like:

```ts
getDaemonDashboardNotificationStorePath()
```

internally based on AO's base dir.

Then:

- Dashboard `NotificationBroadcaster` reads from `running.dashboardNotificationStore`.
- Dashboard notifier writes to `running.dashboardNotificationStore` when a live daemon exists.
- `ao notify test --to dashboard` uses the live daemon store when a daemon is running.
- If no live daemon exists, fall back to the existing config-scoped store or warn that no live dashboard is available.

## Why this is better

- Matches user expectation: notifications go to the dashboard currently running.
- Avoids split stores between global config and project-local config.
- Works for multi-project dashboards.
- Avoids reading all notification stores and accidentally showing stale/unrelated test notifications.
- Keeps notification records project-aware through existing `projectId`/`sessionId` fields.

## Related

- PR #1736 — added dashboard notifier/manual notification harness.
- PR #1961 — default notifier onboarding changes; related notifier defaults/routing work, but does not address notification store scoping.

title: feat(web): simplify sidebar dot colors to a 5-bucket scheme centered on human action
body:
## Motivation

Today the sidebar dot has 6+ colors (`working`, `pending`, `review`, `respond`, `merge`, `done`) tied to `getDetailedAttentionLevel`. The semantics are muddled: orange-ish covers both *agent crashed* and *CI failed*, even though AO's whole job is to auto-fix CI failures and address review comments. PR-side problems don't need a dedicated color because AO is already on them.

## Proposed scheme

| Color | Meaning | Trigger |
|-------|---------|---------|
| 🟢 Green | Active | Agent is working |
| 🟣 Purple | Merge ready | PR approved + CI green, one click to merge |
| 🟡 Yellow | Idle + PR | PR exists, AO is iterating on it (review_pending / ci_failing / changes_requested) — no human action needed |
| ⚪ Grey | Idle, no PR | Agent finished thinking but hasn't opened a PR yet |
| 🟠 Orange | **Human intervention required** | Only case the user must act on |

## What orange means (exhaustive)

The orange bucket is the only sidebar signal that demands attention. Every other state, AO handles automatically.

| Trigger | Source |
|---------|--------|
| `activity === \"waiting_input\"` | Permission prompt — agent paused, will resume on approval |
| `activity === \"blocked\"` | Agent errored mid-task |
| `activity === \"exited\"` with non-terminal status | Process crashed unexpectedly (the ao-165 shape) |
| `status === \"needs_input\"` | Lifecycle marked agent as needing human |
| `status === \"stuck\"` | Escalated probe failure — auto-recovery gave up |
| `status === \"errored\"` | Unrecoverable error |

## What changes vs today

- `review` level (CI failed, changes_requested, merge conflicts) is removed as a distinct sidebar color. Those cases collapse into **yellow** (idle + PR exists, AO iterating).
- `pending` level collapses into yellow as well.
- `done` continues to be hidden behind the `showDone` / `showKilled` toggles (no change).

## Files to touch

- `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts:480-559` — rewrite `getDetailedAttentionLevel` for the 5-bucket output.
- `packages/web/src/app/globals.css:2299-2331` — update `.sidebar-session-dot[data-level=...]` mappings; retire `review` selector if no longer used.
- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:43` — narrow `SessionDotLevel` type.

Card-level UI (kanban, badges, BottomSheet) calls `getAttentionLevel(session, \"detailed\")` for the full 6-zone result. Decide whether the sidebar should use a separate function (e.g. `getSidebarLevel`) or whether the card kanban also adopts the simpler scheme. Recommendation: introduce a sidebar-specific function so the kanban still has granular zones; the sidebar is the one place where simplicity matters most.

## Related

- #1933 — `stuck` sessions with exited runtime should auto-promote to `terminated`. Lands cleanly with this: post-fix, ao-165-shaped sessions disappear from orange (they go done), leaving orange truly meaning \"the loop is broken right now.\"

title: bug(agent-codex): dashboard enrichment ignores persisted codexThreadId and scans global Codex history
body:
## Bug

Codex dashboard/session enrichment can scan the global `~/.codex/sessions` history even when AO already persisted the native `codexThreadId` for the session. On machines with a large Codex history, opening the dashboard or a session detail page can spend seconds searching/parsing historical JSONL and can push the Next dashboard process toward V8 OOM.

**Source:** local AO dogfooding report in Codex chat; HAR at `~/ao_timeout.har`; crash report `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/node-2026-05-22-010454.ips`.
**Reported by:** @yyovil
**Date:** 2026-05-22
**Analyzed against:** upstream/main `1ed0719770c07081dbcb526419baca996b67c116`; installed AO `0.9.0-nightly-a66a087ef678313bf3a78dfe70aadee9adc25935`; local checkout had dirty Codex-plugin changes so latest was fetched but not pulled.
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.4.0 arm64, Node `v22.22.2`, zsh.
**Confidence:** High — exact request path and plugin lookup behavior traced to source; local data shape reproduces the expensive scan condition.

## Evidence

Local data shape on the reporting machine:

- AO project session metadata files: 67
- Live tmux sessions: only `ao-orchestrator`
- `~/.codex/sessions`: 979 JSONL files, ~2.0 GB total
- Largest Codex JSONL files observed: up to ~92 MB
- Many AO Codex session metadata files already contain `codexThreadId` and `codexModel`

Example: `ao-orchestrator.json` already contains:

```json
"codexThreadId": "019e4b8d-b055-7501-845e-b60da93cb526",
"codexModel": "gpt-5.5"
```

But upstream/main still has `findCodexSessionFileCached(workspacePath)` keyed by workspace path only:

```ts
async function findCodexSessionFileCached(workspacePath: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const cached = sessionFileCache.get(workspacePath);
  if (cached && Date.now() < cached.expiry) return cached.path;
  const result = await findCodexSessionFile(workspacePath);
  sessionFileCache.set(workspacePath, { path: result, expiry: Date.now() + SESSION_FILE_CACHE_TTL_MS });
  return result;
}
```

`findCodexSessionFile(workspacePath)` recursively lists `~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl` and opens prefix chunks to match `session_meta.cwd`. That is unnecessary when `codexThreadId` is already persisted because Codex rollout filenames include the thread id.

## Root Cause

The Codex agent plugin treats workspace path as the primary lookup key on request-time enrichment paths:

- `getActivityState()` calls `findCodexSessionFileCached(session.workspacePath)`.
- `getSessionInfo()` calls `findCodexSessionFileCached(session.workspacePath)`.
- `getRestoreCommand()` only uses persisted `codexThreadId` after it already needs to discover missing metadata; the shared lookup path itself is not keyed by thread id.

For old/restored sessions, workspace path is a poor key: many sessions can share a workspace lineage, and resolving by cwd requires scanning historical Codex JSONL files. Persisted `codexThreadId` is the stable native key and should be the hard fast path.

## Why this compounds the dashboard timeout/OOM bugs

The Next dashboard request path calls session listing/enrichment for dashboard/session pages. With many persisted AO session records and a cold cache, opening the dashboard can trigger many Codex lookups. On this machine, the request path interacts with a 2 GB Codex history corpus and produced a native crash with:

```text
next-server (v15.5.18)
node::OOMErrorHandler
v8::internal::V8::FatalProcessOutOfMemory
Builtins_StringSlowFlatten
Builtins_StringIndexOf
```

That stack is consistent with repeated large string search/flatten/parse work over JSONL data.

## Reproduction

1. Use AO with Codex agents long enough to accumulate many Codex JSONL files under `~/.codex/sessions`.
2. Have AO session metadata records that already contain `codexThreadId`.
3. Run `ao start` and open a session detail page/dashboard with a cold session cache.
4. Observe slow `/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/patches`, or session-detail document requests; on large histories, the Next process can hit V8 OOM.

## Fix

- Change `findCodexSessionFileCached` to accept the full `Session`, not only `workspacePath`.
- If `session.metadata.codexThreadId` exists, search by rollout filename containing that thread id and cache under `thread:<codexThreadId>`.
- Only fall back to cwd-prefix scanning when no thread id exists or the thread-id lookup misses.
- Bound fallback cwd scanning by bytes/lines and make it abortable/cancellable.
- Add tests proving `getActivityState()`, `getSessionInfo()`, and `getRestoreCommand()` use the thread-id path and do not open historical files when `codexThreadId` is present.

## Impact

- Dashboard/session-detail pages can time out or crash for users with large Codex histories.
- A single live orchestrator plus many persisted dead Codex session records is enough to create the expensive cold-cache path.
- This amplifies #1855 and #1935.

## Related

- #1855 — user-visible session-detail timeout family.
- #1935 — Next dashboard V8 OOM on `ao start` / first dashboard load.
- #1976 / #1977 — stream cleanup on aborted Codex reads; necessary but insufficient because this issue is about avoiding the expensive lookup in the first place.
- #1120 — same high-level class for OpenCode: terminal/stale sessions still trigger expensive agent-session discovery on dashboard refresh.

title: bug(core,web): dashboard request paths run expensive agent enrichment for terminated/runtime-lost sessions
body:
## Bug

Dashboard/session request paths synchronously run agent-native enrichment (`getActivityState()` / `getSessionInfo()`) while building session lists, including for persisted sessions whose runtimes are already missing or terminated. This puts expensive observation work on the Next.js request path instead of the lifecycle manager/background observer, and it compounds timeout/OOM failures when many historical session records exist.

**Source:** local AO dogfooding report in Codex chat; HAR at `~/ao_timeout.har`; crash report `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/node-2026-05-22-010454.ips`.
**Reported by:** @yyovil
**Date:** 2026-05-22
**Analyzed against:** upstream/main `1ed0719770c07081dbcb526419baca996b67c116`; installed AO `0.9.0-nightly-a66a087ef678313bf3a78dfe70aadee9adc25935`; local checkout had dirty Codex-plugin changes so latest was fetched but not pulled.
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.4.0 arm64, Node `v22.22.2`, zsh.
**Confidence:** High — current control flow is directly visible in source and local metadata shows only one live tmux session but 67 persisted session records being listed.

## Evidence

The reporting machine currently has only one live tmux session:

```text
ao-orchestrator
```

But the project has 67 persisted AO session metadata files under:

```text
~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/agent-orchestrator_48321dec7a/sessions/*.json
```

Many of those are not alive. Example metadata includes:

```json
"lifecycle": {
  "session": { "state": "terminated", "reason": "runtime_lost" },
  "runtime": { "state": "missing", "reason": "tmux_missing" }
}
```

Despite that, the web/dashboard read path still enumerates those records and can trigger enrichment.

## Root Cause

The request path currently mixes three responsibilities:

1. **Read persisted session rows** from AO metadata.
2. **Probe runtime truth** via runtime/agent plugins.
3. **Extract agent-native details** from external agent state files.

Key source path:

- `packages/web/src/lib/dashboard-page-data.ts` calls `services.sessionManager.listCached()` during dynamic project layout rendering.
- `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts` calls `sessionManager.list()` when `fresh=true`.
- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` `list()` loads every metadata record returned by `loadActiveSessionRecords()` and calls `ensureHandleAndEnrich(...)`.
- `ensureHandleAndEnrich(...)` calls `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState(...)`.
- `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState(...)` can call `plugins.agent.getActivityState(...)` and `plugins.agent.getSessionInfo(...)`.

For dead runtimes, there is a partial guard:

```ts
if (!alive) {
  ...
  if (plugins.agent && canDiscoverSessionInfoAfterRuntimeExit(plugins.agent)) {
    await persistAgentSessionInfo({ skipIfNativeRestoreMetadataPresent: true });
  }
  return;
}
```

But the bigger issue remains: request-time `list()` is still responsible for runtime/agent discovery. For live or indeterminate sessions it can still call native agent disk/probe work, and for terminal rows it still pays enough runtime/probe overhead to reconcile status before deciding what to skip.

The web layer also independently enriches display metadata:

- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` `enrichSessionsMetadataFast(...)` calls `agent.getSessionInfo(...)` for dashboard summaries when `dashboard.summary` is missing.
- `enrichSessionsMetadata(...)` does the same and also fetches issue titles for the full `/api/sessions` route.

So the Next request path can call agent-native session-file reads both through core listing and web serialization.

## Why this is wrong

The lifecycle manager is already the long-running observer that should own expensive polling/probing/enrichment and persist the derived state. HTTP request handlers should mostly deserialize persisted state and perform cheap formatting.

Putting expensive plugin observation on the Next request path creates these failure modes:

- Cold dashboard load fans out across all persisted session records.
- Terminated/runtime-lost historical rows still participate in request-time work.
- Client aborts do not necessarily cancel already-started server-side enrichment work.
- Multiple request surfaces (`/projects` RSC layout, `/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/patches`, mux snapshot fetches) can overlap and duplicate work.
- Large agent-native histories can push the Next process to V8 OOM.

## Reproduction

1. Accumulate many AO session metadata files, including runtime-lost/terminated sessions.
2. Ensure only one or a few sessions are actually alive in tmux.
3. Run `ao start` and open the dashboard/session detail page with a cold cache.
4. Observe request-time session listing/enrichment over many persisted records; with large Codex history, this can produce slow document/API requests and OOM.

## Fix

- Split session read from session observation.
- Add a cheap read-only session list path for dashboard/API routes that deserializes persisted metadata and never calls agent/runtime probes.
- Move expensive `getActivityState()` / `getSessionInfo()` calls into the lifecycle manager or an explicit background observation store.
- For terminated/runtime-lost sessions, skip request-time native agent reads if native restore metadata is already present (`codexThreadId`, `claudeSessionUuid`, `opencodeSessionId`, etc.).
- If summaries/costs are missing, refresh them asynchronously/background rather than blocking the session page.
- Make any remaining request-time enrichment bounded and cancellable via request abort signals.

## Impact

- Dashboard/session detail can time out or crash on projects with many historical session records.
- Users see `Failed to load session` even when the target session exists.
- `ao start` can appear to be the cause because the first dashboard load after startup has cold caches and restored metadata.

## Related

- #1990 — Codex-specific high-cost lookup: persisted `codexThreadId` is not used as the hard fast path.
- #1855 — session-detail timeout family.
- #1935 — Next V8 OOM surface.
- #1120 — OpenCode-specific version of stale/terminal sessions still causing expensive session discovery.
- #1885 — dashboard read path makes per-session `gh` calls.
- #1865 — process probe fanout strategy.

title: ao start can follow local project config while dashboard and supervisor only follow global config
body:
## Bug

AO can start a project from a repo-local `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, but the dashboard and project supervisor still discover projects from the canonical global registry. If the local project is not registered globally, `ao start` can appear successful while the opened dashboard cannot see that project.

**Source:** local triage from `D:\agent-orchestrator`
**Analyzed against:** `ad5ab2dbc68a76a2965a2f97a19856d8b089f29d`
**Confidence:** High - traced current `loadConfig`, dashboard service loading, `ao start` project resolution, dashboard env, and project supervisor loading.

## Reproduction

1. Have a global config with at least one project registered, for example project A in `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`.
2. Have another repo, project B, with a local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` / `.yml` but no corresponding entry in the global config.
3. Run `ao start` from project B.
4. Let the CLI open the dashboard URL.

## Actual

The CLI can resolve/start project B from the local config, but the dashboard project list and project routes are based on the global registry. The dashboard still only sees globally registered projects, for example project A, so project B's dashboard route may not exist or may not show the expected sessions.

The project supervisor has the same mismatch: it loads `loadConfig(getGlobalConfigPath())`, so it will not attach lifecycle polling for project B if project B is local-only.

## Expected

If `ao start` can successfully start or link a project, that project should be visible to the dashboard and supervisor immediately. Before opening a dashboard URL for a selected project, AO should ensure that project is present in the canonical global registry.

Local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` should behave as a project behavior overlay, not as an alternate project registry that the CLI can follow while the dashboard ignores it.

## Root Cause

Different AO surfaces trust different config sources:

| Surface | Current source |
|---|---|
| Generic `loadConfig()` | `AO_CONFIG_PATH`, then cwd-upward local yaml, then canonical global config (`packages/core/src/config.ts`) |
| Dashboard services/project list | canonical global config first, local fallback only when global is missing (`packages/web/src/lib/services.ts`, `packages/web/src/lib/project-name.ts`) |
| Project supervisor / lifecycle polling | canonical global config only (`packages/cli/src/lib/project-supervisor.ts`) |
| `ao start` | can resolve from cwd-local yaml, auto-created yaml, project id, path, URL, or global depending on arg shape and daemon state (`packages/cli/src/lib/resolve-project.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`) |
| Dashboard process env | CLI passes `AO_CONFIG_PATH`, but dashboard discovery still prefers global when global exists (`packages/cli/src/lib/web-dir.ts`) |

This creates a split-brain source-of-truth problem: the CLI may follow the local project config while the dashboard and supervisor follow the global registry.

## Impact

- Dashboard project list can omit the project that `ao start` just started.
- CLI-opened project dashboard links can point to routes that the dashboard cannot resolve.
- Session visibility and project-id resolution in web APIs can be wrong or incomplete.
- Lifecycle polling / project supervisor may not attach for the local-only project.
- Backlog auto-claim and verification-label flows can skip the project because they iterate dashboard/global config.
- Running-state coverage can disagree with the project the user just started.

## Suggested Fix

Define and enforce the invariant that project identity/discovery is global:

1. When `ao start` resolves a local-only project, register it in the canonical global config before launching/opening the dashboard.
2. Treat local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` as behavior-only overlay after registration.
3. If a legacy wrapped local `projects:` config is encountered, either migrate/register it or fail before dashboard launch with an actionable message.
4. Avoid a state where `AO_CONFIG_PATH` lets the CLI and dashboard disagree while global config exists.

## Suggested Tests

1. With global containing project A and project B having only local yaml, `ao start` in project B registers B globally before opening the dashboard.
2. Dashboard `/api/projects` includes project B after startup.
3. `startProjectSupervisor()` attaches/polls project B after startup.
4. `AO_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at B's local config does not let dashboard and supervisor disagree when global exists.
5. Legacy wrapped local `projects:` configs are migrated/registered or rejected before dashboard launch.

## Related

- #1561 covers a first-run/global-registration path. This issue is the broader runtime/dashboard/supervisor source-of-truth mismatch when a local config exists but the project is absent from global.
- #1766 covered a Windows-specific first-run global config creation symptom.
- #1948 covers Codex first-run/defaults and project identity mismatch.

title: refactor(agents): remove transcript token cost enrichment
body:
## Summary
- remove `AgentSessionInfo.cost` / `CostEstimate` and delete live token/cost aggregation from agent session-info paths

This is a follow-up cleanup after #1992 and #1996. It keeps the Codex thread-id lookup/restore behavior needed for legacy sessions while making dashboard/session-list enrichment safe by construction.

Related: #1991, #1935.

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test`

title: bug(web): session enrichment uses project default agent instead of persisted session agent
body:
## Bug

The web dashboard metadata-enrichment path uses the current project/default agent to enrich every session in a project, instead of using the agent persisted on each session record. In mixed-agent projects, a historical `goose` / `gemini` / `grok` / etc. session can be handed to the Codex plugin when the project default is currently Codex.

That causes two bad outcomes:

1. **Performance:** Codex receives a non-Codex session with no `codexThreadId`, falls back to cwd-based discovery, and scans `~/.codex/sessions`.
2. **Correctness:** because cwd is shared, Codex can find an unrelated recent Codex rollout and attribute that Codex model/thread/cost to the non-Codex session.

**Source:** local AO dogfooding / live debugging with `ao_timeout_again.har` and Next OOM logs.
**Reported by:** @yyovil
**Date:** 2026-05-22
**Analyzed against:** upstream/main `d5249228498fc5cb8f14609fcd81baa3630e5076`; installed #1994 worktree commit `63ad054566e706eed989d1d9ce0b696bda58a4b6`; root checkout was dirty/ahead so latest was fetched but not pulled.
**AO version:** `0.8.0`
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.4.0 arm64, Node `v22.22.2`, zsh.
**Confidence:** High — reproduced locally with one concrete session metadata file and traced to exact web serialization code.

## Concrete local example

Problematic session metadata file:

```text
~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/agent-orchestrator_48321dec7a/sessions/ao-22.json
```

Relevant fields:

```json
{
  "agent": "goose",
  "worktree": "/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/agent-orchestrator",
  "createdAt": "2026-05-20T12:48:10.866Z",
  "status": "stuck",
  "lifecycle": {
    "session": {
      "state": "terminated",
      "reason": "runtime_lost"
    }
  }
}
```

This file has no `codexThreadId` because it is not a Codex session.

Current local project state:

```text
project sessions: 69
worker sessions: 68
sessions needing summary and missing codexThreadId: 43
~/.codex/sessions JSONL files: 982
largest JSONL observed: 92 MB
```

The problematic rows are recent, not ancient metadata. They were created between:

```text
2026-05-20T12:48:10Z and 2026-05-21T09:28:37Z
```

## Local reproduction evidence

Direct project listing is not the slow part:

```text
sessionManager.list(project): 243ms, RSS ~79 MB
```

But forcing Codex enrichment on a non-Codex session reproduces the slow and wrong path:

```text
session: ao-22
persisted agent: goose
codexThreadId: undefined
workspacePath: /Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/agent-orchestrator

codex.getSessionInfo(ao-22): 7681ms
```

The result returned unrelated Codex metadata:

```json
{
  "summary": "Codex session (gpt-5.5)",
  "agentSessionId": "019e4b8d-b055-7501-845e-b60da93cb526",
  "metadata": {
    "codexThreadId": "019e4b8d-b055-7501-845e-b60da93cb526",
    "codexModel": "gpt-5.5"
  },
  "cost": {
    "inputTokens": 51287022,
    "outputTokens": 134644,
    "estimatedCostUsd": 129.563995
  }
}
```

That thread id belongs to the current/recent Codex orchestrator, not to `ao-22`'s stored `goose` session. The cwd fallback matched the shared repo path and selected a recent Codex rollout.

## Root Cause

Core session loading preserves enough information to know the session's intended agent. `session-manager.ts` resolves persisted session selection before core enrichment:

```ts
const selection = resolveSelectionForSession(project, sessionId, repaired.raw);
const effectiveAgentName = selection.agentName;
const plugins = resolvePlugins(project, effectiveAgentName);
```

But the web serialization/enrichment layer does not use that persisted session agent. It resolves the project and picks the current project/default agent:

```ts
const agentName = projects[i]?.agent ?? config.defaults.agent;
const agent = registry.get<Agent>("agent", agentName);
return enrichSessionAgentSummary(dashboardSessions[i], core, agent);
```

So if a project default is now `codex`, every session without a summary can be passed to Codex, regardless of whether the session metadata says `agent: goose`, `agent: gemini`, `agent: grok`, etc.

## Why this caused the observed timeout/OOM family

This bug interacts with #1991 and #1855:

- The session-detail page calls fresh session-list endpoints for sidebar/project zone counts.
- `/api/sessions?fresh=true` bypasses `listCached()` and then web enrichment runs over many worker sessions.
- Web enrichment selects Codex for non-Codex rows because the project default is Codex.
- Codex sees no `codexThreadId`, falls back to cwd-based discovery under `~/.codex/sessions`.
- Multiple rows share the same repo cwd, so repeated request-path enrichment can repeatedly scan/parse unrelated Codex history.
- Client aborts/timeouts do not necessarily cancel server-side work already started.

This explains why #1992/#1994 improved real Codex sessions with `codexThreadId`, but did not fully fix the reload timeout/OOM: many rows are not Codex sessions at all, and the web layer is routing them into Codex anyway.

## Reproduction

1. Use a project where the current default/project agent is `codex`.
2. Have existing session metadata files in that project whose persisted `agent` is not `codex`, e.g. `agent: goose`, and which have no persisted summary.
3. Open the session detail page or call the project sessions API path that triggers web metadata enrichment.
4. Observe `enrichSessionsMetadata(...)` choosing the project/default Codex agent and calling `codex.getSessionInfo(...)` for the non-Codex session.
5. On machines with large `~/.codex/sessions`, this can take seconds per fallback and can produce wrong Codex summary/cost metadata for non-Codex sessions.

## Fix

- Preserve/expose the session's persisted agent on the `Session` object, or provide a core helper that resolves the effective agent for a loaded session.
- In `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts`, use the persisted session agent for session-specific summary enrichment before falling back to project/default agent for truly legacy records.
- Do not call Codex `getSessionInfo()` for a session whose persisted agent is known and is not Codex.
- Add regression tests with a mixed-agent project:
  - default/project agent is `codex`
  - stored session metadata has `agent: goose`
  - `enrichSessionsMetadata(...)` must not call Codex `getSessionInfo()` for that row
- Consider skipping agent summary enrichment entirely for terminal/runtime-lost rows unless persisted native metadata is already present.

## Impact

- Dashboard/session-detail can time out or OOM on mixed-agent projects with a large Codex history.
- Non-Codex sessions can display incorrect Codex summaries/costs because cwd fallback may attach the wrong Codex rollout.
- This affects recent sessions too; it is not limited to pre-`codexThreadId` legacy Codex metadata.

## Related

- #1855 — user-visible session-detail timeout family.
- #1935 — Next dashboard OOM surface.
- #1991 — broader bug: request paths run expensive enrichment that should be background/persisted.
- #1990 / #1992 / #1994 — Codex-specific fast paths for real Codex sessions with persisted thread metadata; this bug explains why those fixes were not sufficient for mixed-agent rows.
- #1609 — adjacent but opposite policy question for restore: restore may intentionally use persisted agent; web read/enrichment should also respect persisted session agent for display correctness.
- #1948 — related config/default-agent split-brain class, but this issue is specifically about session-level persisted agent being ignored during web enrichment.

title: fix: use persisted session agent for enrichment
body:
Fixes #1995

## Summary
- Added a shared core `resolveAgentSelectionForSession()` helper for legacy raw metadata repair/backfill boundaries.
- Backfilled missing legacy `agent` metadata on session-manager reads, attached the resolved agent in recovery validation, and preserved it when recovery actions rewrite metadata.
- Tightened normalized `Session` consumers (web enrichment, CLI status/send, lifecycle polling) to use `session.metadata["agent"]` as the session-agent identity instead of inferring from current project/default config.
- Updated new/restored session writes so persisted metadata carries the selected agent.

## Audit findings
- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` was the bug source: it selected the current project/default agent for dashboard summary enrichment. Fixed; web now reads the normalized persisted session agent.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts` had the same root pattern for status-summary introspection. Fixed; it no longer falls back to current project/default config for a loaded `Session`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts` still had a session-specific project/default fallback after `sessionManager.get()`. Fixed to rely on normalized `session.metadata["agent"]`.
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` was a normalized-Session consumer and no longer re-resolves agent identity from project config.
- Recovery scanner/validator reads raw metadata directly, so that is a legacy normalization boundary. It now attaches the resolved agent to the assessment metadata, and recovery actions persist that agent during repair/escalation/cleanup writes.
- Remaining direct project/default agent lookups are not same-root session-loading bugs: spawn paths intentionally use current spawn/project config for new sessions; `doctor` and settings UI are config inspection/editing; plugin config reads are runtime launch config; fallback tmux status has no AO metadata record to resolve from.

## Tests
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/session-manager/query.test.ts src/__tests__/session-manager/communication.test.ts src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts src/__tests__/recovery-validator.test.ts src/__tests__/recovery-actions.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- src/lib/__tests__/serialize.test.ts src/__tests__/api-routes.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- __tests__/commands/status.test.ts __tests__/commands/send.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core build && pnpm --filter './packages/plugins/*' build`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck && pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck && pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck`
- `git diff --check`

## Notes
- Before building core/plugin packages, web typecheck could not resolve workspace package declarations from a fresh install. After building those dependency packages, the package typechecks passed.

title: docs(ao): add npm package README + keywords
body:
## Problem
The published [`@aoagents/ao`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aoagents/ao) package has a **blank README on npmjs.com** — the `packages/ao/` directory never had a `README.md`, so npm rendered nothing. A blank package page hurts trust and discoverability (people are less likely to install).

## Fix
- **Add `packages/ao/README.md`** — a focused, install-first README written specifically for the npm page:
  - **Absolute URLs** for the banner image and all doc links (npm does **not** resolve repo-relative paths, so the root README's `docs/...` links/images would render broken on npm).
  - Install command up top, nightly/stable channels, prerequisites, quick start, how-it-works, the plugin-slot table, and links back to the full docs + Discord.
- **Add `keywords`** to `package.json` (`ai-agents`, `coding-agent`, `orchestrator`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `cli`, …) to improve npm search discoverability.
- **List `README.md` in `files`** explicitly (npm special-cases README so it ships regardless, but this makes intent clear).

Verified with `npm pack --dry-run` — `README.md` (4.6kB) is now included in the tarball.

## Note
npm only renders the README from a **published** version, so this goes live on npmjs.com with the **next publish** (nightly or release) — not on merge alone.

title: Session start hook injection produces malformed settings.json when SessionStart hooks already exist
body:
## Summary

When a project's `.claude/settings.json` already contains a `SessionStart` hook, AO's session-start hook injection (for the activity-updater) appends correctly-formatted entries but does **not** fix or validate the existing entries. If the existing entry uses the old/bare format (`{type, command}` without a `{matcher, hooks}` wrapper), the resulting file fails Claude Code's `/doctor` validation.

Worse: on every **"relaunch (clean)"** from the AO dashboard, the worktree is reset to `main`, restoring the malformed committed version, and AO re-injects its hooks — reproducing the `/doctor` warning every single time.

---

## Before AO injection (committed `settings.json` on `main`)

```json
{
    "permissions": {
        "allow": [
            "Bash(git status*)",
            "Bash(git diff*)",
            "Bash(git log*)",
            "Bash(git add*)",
            "Bash(git commit*)",
            "Bash(git pull*)",
            "Bash(git push*)",
            "Bash(python scripts/*)",
            "Bash(./scripts/sync_notes.sh*)"
        ],
        "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf*)", "Bash(git reset --hard*)", "Bash(git clean -fd*)"]
    },
    "hooks": {
        "SessionStart": [
            {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "python .claude/hooks/session_start_context.py"
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## After AO injects its hooks

```json
{
    "hooks": {
        "SessionStart": [
            {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "python .claude/hooks/session_start_context.py"
            },
            {
                "matcher": "",
                "hooks": [
                    {
                        "type": "command",
                        "command": "node .claude/activity-updater.cjs",
                        "timeout": 2000
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

Note how the **first** `SessionStart` entry (the user's original) is bare `{type, command}` while AO's injected entry correctly uses `{matcher, hooks: [...]}`.

---

## `/doctor` error

```
Settings (.claude/settings.json > hooks.SessionStart.0.hooks): Expected array, but received undefined
```

---

## Reproduction steps

1. Create or use a project whose committed `.claude/settings.json` has a bare `SessionStart` hook entry (`{type, command}` format, no `matcher`/`hooks` wrapper).
2. Start an AO session or do a "relaunch (clean)" from the AO dashboard.
3. AO injects its activity-updater hooks.
4. Run `/doctor` in Claude Code → validation error on `hooks.SessionStart.0.hooks`.
5. "Relaunch (clean)" again → worktree reset to `main` (malformed committed version) → AO re-injects → error reproduces.

The issue is reproducible **on every clean relaunch** because the malformed hook is committed on `main` and AO never normalizes existing entries before appending.

---

## Suggested fix directions

1. **Validate + migrate existing hooks on injection:** When AO injects its activity-updater hooks, also scan existing entries in each hook event array. If any entry uses the bare `{type, command}` format (missing `matcher` / `hooks` wrapper), wrap it automatically: `{ matcher: "", hooks: [entry] }`.

2. **Warn on malformed hooks:** If AO doesn't want to auto-fix, at minimum log a warning when it detects existing hook entries that don't conform to the required schema before injection.

3. **Run `/doctor`-equivalent validation after injection:** After writing the merged `settings.json`, validate the full file against Claude Code's expected hook schema and surface any errors to the user immediately.

---

## Impact

- Every "relaunch (clean)" reproduces the issue, forcing the user or agent to fix it manually each session.
- The user had to manually repair this twice before identifying AO's injection as the root cause.
- Affects any project that added `SessionStart` hooks before AO support existed or using the old bare format.

---

## Environment

- `ao` version: `0.9.0-nightly-a66a087ef678313bf3a78dfe70aadee9adc25935`
- Package: `@aoagents/ao`

title: bug(code-review): review runner hardcodes `codex` CLI, ignores `defaults.agent` config
body:
## Summary

`runCodexCodeReview()` in `code-review-manager.js` hardcodes the `codex` binary regardless of the user's `defaults.agent` setting in `config.yaml`. Users who configure `agent: claude-code` (or any non-Codex agent) still get `codex` invoked for reviews, which fails if Codex isn't installed — and even when Codex *is* installed, fails due to a separate argument-passing bug on Windows (see linked issue).

The error message is also hardcoded: `"Codex review failed: ${details}"` regardless of the configured agent. (Note: Didn't create a separate issue, but the toast error message disappeared before I could read more than two words which is unfortunate, but it was enough to nail down this bug.)

## Environment

- **AO version:** `@aoagents/ao@0.9.0-nightly-a66a087ef678313bf3a78dfe70aadee9adc25935`
- **OS:** Windows 11 Enterprise Evaluation 10.0.26200
- **Node.js:** v24.14.1
- **Codex CLI:** codex-cli 0.125.0 (installed but irrelevant — should be using claude-code)
- **Claude Code:** 2.1.148
- **Config:** `defaults.agent: claude-code`

## Reproduction

1. Set `defaults.agent: claude-code` in `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`
2. Spawn a worker, let it create a PR
3. Click "Review" in the dashboard (or `ao review run <session> --execute`)
4. Review runner invokes `codex exec ...` instead of the configured agent
5. Error toast: `"Codex review failed: ..."` (even though the user never configured Codex)

## Root Cause

`code-review-manager.js` line ~515:

```javascript
async function runCodexCodeReview(context) {
    // ...
    const { stdout, stderr } = await execFileWithClosedStdin("codex", args, {
        //                                                    ^^^^^^
        //                              Hardcoded — should resolve from config
        cwd: context.workspacePath,
        timeout: REVIEW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS,
        maxBuffer: REVIEW_COMMAND_MAX_BUFFER,
        env: process.env,
        shell: isWindows(),
    });
    // ...
    catch (error) {
        // ...
        throw new Error(`Codex review failed: ${details}`, { cause: error });
        //                ^^^^^^
        //        Also hardcoded — should reflect the actual agent
    }
}
```

The function name (`runCodexCodeReview`), binary name (`"codex"`), and error string (`"Codex review failed"`) are all Codex-specific. There is no code path that reads `defaults.agent`, `worker.agent`, or any config to determine which CLI to invoke for reviews.

## Failed Review Run

```json
{
  "id": "review-run-d7addc18-a37a-4c90-93da-ca2acc124a5c",
  "status": "failed",
  "terminationReason": "Codex review failed: error: unexpected argument 'are' found\n\nUsage: codex exec [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]\n       codex exec [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [ARGS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'."
}
```

## Config at time of failure

```yaml
# ~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml
defaults:
  runtime: process
  agent: claude-code    # <-- should be respected
  workspace: worktree
```

No project-level `agent-orchestrator.yaml` override exists.

## Expected Behavior

The review runner should:
1. Resolve the agent CLI from config using the same resolution chain as worker sessions (`session override → project role-specific → project general → global role-specific → global default`)
2. Invoke the resolved CLI (e.g., `claude` for claude-code) with the appropriate arguments for that agent's `exec` interface
3. Use a generic error message (e.g., `"Code review failed: ..."`) or include the resolved agent name

## Suggested Fix

Either:
- Make `runCodexCodeReview` agent-aware by reading from config and dispatching to the correct CLI
- Or implement the `CodeReview` plugin slot architecture from #1275 which already plans for multi-agent review support

## Related Issues

- #1275 — `feat: code-review plugin slot` — acknowledges Codex-first design and lists Claude Code as "a natural follow-up"
- #1948 — `First-run Codex selection leaves global config on claude-code` — related config/agent mismatch
- #139 — Original event-triggered review feature request

bug(web): @aoagents/ao-web bundles agent-grok and runtime-process with /tmp/ao-publish-stable build paths frozen — dashboard 500 on every non-publish host
body:
## Bug

`@aoagents/ao-web@0.9.0` ships Next.js server chunks that **inline two plugin modules with their build-host source paths frozen as `import.meta.url`**. At runtime any code path that touches the bundled module dies with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, and the dashboard root (`/`) returns HTTP 500.

Reproduction: a fresh `npm install -g @aoagents/ao` followed by `ao start` on **any host that is not the publishing build host** triggers this. The publish-time path `/tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/<name>/dist/index.js` is baked into the JS as a string literal and used at runtime to resolve sibling files.

## Symptom

`ao start` succeeds, then the Next server logs (and HTTP 500 on `/`):

```
[next]  ⨯ [Error: Cannot find module '../package.json'
[next] Require stack:
[next] - /tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js] {
[next]   code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
[next]   requireStack: [Array]
[next] }
```

The `requireStack` entry points at a path that **does not exist** on the user's machine — it is the publishing CI's `/tmp` working directory.

## Root cause

Source: `node_modules/@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-grok/dist/index.js` (v0.1.1):

```js
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const packageJson = require("../package.json");   // ← top-level, runs on import
```

When this module is consumed unbundled (e.g. by `ao-core`'s `loadBuiltins()` via dynamic `import()`), `import.meta.url` resolves to the install path and `../package.json` is found correctly.

But `@aoagents/ao-web`'s Next.js build **inlines** the plugin into a server chunk (`.next/server/chunks/9536.js`) and webpack rewrites `createRequire(import.meta.url)` to a literal `createRequire("file:///tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js")`. Verbatim from the published chunk:

```js
let aV = (0, aT.createRequire)(
  "file:///tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js"
)("../package.json"),
```

`../package.json` resolves to `/tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/package.json` — a path that only existed on the publishing machine.

## Scope

`grep -ho "/tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/[a-z0-9-]\+/dist/[a-zA-Z._-]\+" .next/server/chunks/*.js | sort -u` against the published `@aoagents/ao-web@0.9.0` returns **two** affected plugins:

```
/tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js
/tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/runtime-process/dist/index.js
```

- **`agent-grok`** — top-level `require("../package.json")` throws on import. Hard 500.
- **`runtime-process`** — uses `fileURLToPath(...)` against the same frozen path to resolve its sibling `pty-host.js`. Code path:
  ```js
  i = (0, k.resolve)(
    (0, k.dirname)(
      (0, q.fileURLToPath)("file:///tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/runtime-process/dist/index.js")
    ),
    "pty-host.js"
  )
  ```
  Triggered when the dashboard spawns a pty session via the `process` runtime; `pty-host.js` won't be found.

Disabling `agent-grok` in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` does **not** help because the registry never loads it — it is already inlined into the web bundle. `loadFromConfig()` / `loadBuiltins()` (`@aoagents/ao-core/dist/plugin-registry.js`) are only used by the CLI side; the web side has the plugin code embedded.

## Repro

```sh
# Any non-publish host where /tmp/ao-publish-stable does not exist
npm install -g @aoagents/ao
ao start
curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/   # → HTTP 500
# server log shows the Cannot find module '../package.json' stack above
```

Environment in the case I observed:
- `@aoagents/ao` `0.9.0` (manual update channel)
- `@aoagents/ao-web` `0.9.0`
- `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-grok` `0.1.1`
- Node `v25.2.1`
- Linux x86_64
- Next.js `^15.1.0` (per `ao-web` package.json)

## Workaround (user-side, not a fix)

Stage the build-host paths as symlinks before each `ao start`:

```sh
NM=$(npm root -g)/@aoagents
mkdir -p /tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok \
         /tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/runtime-process/dist
ln -sfn "$NM/ao-plugin-agent-grok/package.json" \
        /tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/package.json
ln -sfn "$NM/ao-plugin-runtime-process/dist/pty-host.js" \
        /tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/runtime-process/dist/pty-host.js
ao start
```

`/tmp` is host-local and wiped on reboot, so this needs to be re-run on every fresh boot.

## Fix directions

1. **Don't bundle these plugins into `ao-web`.** The plugin registry is supposed to load them via `import()` from `node_modules` at runtime (`@aoagents/ao-core/dist/plugin-registry.js::loadBuiltins`). Mark them as `serverExternalPackages` (Next 15) or add them to `webpack`'s `externals` so they're required from `node_modules` at runtime instead of inlined. This also matches how the CLI loads them.

2. **Stop using `createRequire(import.meta.url)` to read sibling files in code that gets bundled.** Either:
   - Inline the data at build time (`import pkg from "../package.json" assert { type: "json" }` — Next/webpack will fold it into the chunk and the runtime `require` disappears), or
   - Read the field directly: `const pluginName = "@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-grok"` is a constant — there's no need to read it from `package.json` at runtime.

   The same fix applies to `runtime-process`: replace `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` with a runtime-resolved path (e.g. require.resolve from a non-bundled wrapper, or pass the path in via plugin config).

3. **Add a CI smoke check** that boots `ao start` against the published tarball in a scratch container and `curl`s `/`. This particular regression would have failed that check on the very first boot on any non-build machine.

(1) is the smallest change and the most aligned with the existing plugin-registry architecture. (2) is the durable fix for the underlying mistake. (3) prevents the next variant.

## Related

I didn't find an existing issue for this specific symptom. Closest neighbors:
- #1689 (Dashboard terminal renders blank on connect after upgrading to v0.4.0) — different surface, but `runtime-process`'s frozen `pty-host.js` path could be a contributing factor on affected hosts.
- #1974 (nightly snapshot publish dep resolution) — unrelated; that's a registry-404, this is a runtime-path-404.

title: docs/arch: "one central orchestrator" vs per-project orchestrator agents — unclear design intent
body:
## Summary

The architecture design document describes "one central orchestrator server [that] manages multiple projects," but the implementation creates **one orchestrator agent session per project** (`${sessionPrefix}-orchestrator`). This creates confusion for users with multiple registered projects who see a "Spawn Orchestrator" button for each project and end up with N independent orchestrator agents.

The **daemon process** (`ao start`) does manage all projects centrally, and the **CLI commands** (`ao spawn`, `ao send`, `ao status`) work cross-project. However, the **orchestrator agent sessions** (the actual Claude Code / Codex agents) are project-scoped in their system prompts and context, even though they can technically issue cross-project CLI commands.

## Current Behavior

With 3 registered projects, a user gets:

```
ao status
  volvox-bot:           vb-orchestrator  (independent agent)
  Notes:                not-orchestrator (independent agent)
  Agent Orchestrator:   ao-orchestrator  (independent agent)
```

Each orchestrator agent:
- Has its own worktree
- Has its own context window
- Has a system prompt scoped to one project (session prefix, project ID, repo info)
- **CAN** spawn workers and send messages cross-project via CLI (e.g., `ao spawn ao/2003` from the Notes orchestrator works)
- But has **no awareness** of other projects' context, issues, or workers in its system prompt

So cross-project coordination is technically possible through CLI commands, but the orchestrator agent has no built-in knowledge of other projects — it works because the human operator (or the agent, if instructed) can use `ao spawn <prefix>/<issue>` to target any registered project. This is ad-hoc, not designed.

## What the Docs Say

From `artifacts/architecture-design.md`:
> "one central orchestrator server manages multiple projects"
> "server-centric approach where all agents report to a central server"

This implies a single orchestrator coordinating across projects as a first-class capability.

## What Actually Happens

- `ao start` creates a single daemon process (the "server") — this IS central
- The daemon auto-spawns a separate orchestrator **agent** per project — these are NOT centrally coordinated
- Each orchestrator agent's system prompt only references its own project
- Cross-project CLI commands work (`ao spawn <other-prefix>/<issue>`) but this is incidental, not designed — the orchestrator agent has no multi-project awareness in its instructions
- The "Spawn Orchestrator" button appears per-project on the dashboard, reinforcing per-project scoping

## The Ambiguity

Is the intended end-state:

**A) Per-project orchestrators (current behavior is mostly correct, docs are misleading)**
- The daemon is the "central server," orchestrator agents are intentionally project-scoped
- Cross-project CLI commands are a nice side effect but not a designed workflow
- Docs should clarify: "one central daemon manages multiple projects, each with its own orchestrator agent"

**B) A single cross-project orchestrator agent (current behavior is incomplete)**
- One orchestrator agent should have multi-project awareness in its system prompt
- It should be able to see all projects' status, workers, and issues in its context
- The per-project spawning would be replaced by a single orchestrator with cross-project scope

**C) Hybrid (user's choice)**
- Default to per-project, but allow a user to configure a single orchestrator agent that manages multiple projects
- The orchestrator's system prompt would include all managed projects' context

## Impact

- Users with multiple projects are confused about whether multiple orchestrators are expected
- Cross-project coordination works via CLI but isn't documented or surfaced in the orchestrator's instructions
- The "Spawn Orchestrator" button on each project card implies per-project is expected, but feels redundant to users expecting a central model
- Orchestrator agents can't proactively coordinate across projects (e.g., "this Notes task relates to a Volvox Bot issue") because they lack cross-project context

## Related

- #1279 — `ao start` cross-project state collision (global `running.json` lacks project awareness)
- #1128 — RFC: Multi-base-branch orchestrators (multiple orchestrators within one project)
- PR #870 — Multi-orchestrator isolated worktrees (shipped, enables multiple orchestrators per project)

## Environment

- AO version: `@aoagents/ao@0.9.0-nightly-a66a087ef678313bf3a78dfe70aadee9adc25935`
- 3 registered projects, 3 independent orchestrator sessions spawned
- Cross-project spawn confirmed working: `ao spawn ao/2003` from Notes orchestrator successfully spawned `ao-182` on Agent Orchestrator project

title: fix(code-review, windows): escape args for cmd.exe in review runner
body:
## Summary

- Fix `shell: true` breaking review prompt argument passing on Windows by escaping args for `cmd.exe` in `execFileWithClosedStdin`
- On Windows, `spawn()` with `shell: true` routes through `cmd.exe`, which concatenates args with spaces — splitting the multi-word review prompt into separate CLI tokens. `codex exec` then fails with `unexpected argument 'are' found`
- Add `escapeArgForCmd()` that wraps args containing spaces or `cmd.exe` metacharacters (`"`, `&`, `|`, `<`, `>`, `^`) in double quotes so they survive the `cmd.exe` re-parse, while keeping `shell: true` for `.cmd` shim resolution

Closes #2003

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests for `escapeArgForCmd`: simple passthrough, space wrapping, double-quote escaping, metacharacter handling, empty string, multi-line prompt
- [x] All 6 new tests pass; all 21 pre-existing tests pass (1 pre-existing failure in `prepareGitReviewerWorkspace` is unrelated — Windows HOME path resolution)
- [x] TypeScript typecheck passes
- [ ] Verify on Windows: `codex exec` receives the full review prompt as a single argument

## Summary

When clicking any link in the AO dashboard session chat view, two tabs are opened:
1. First tab opens immediately, positioned directly after the current tab

Every link click produces two identical tabs.
