title: bug(workspace): destroy_fell_back leaves stale git metadata, causing persistent branch_collision on every orchestrator respawn
body:
## Bug

After an orchestrator session is killed, \`destroy()\` sometimes fails to run \`git worktree remove\` and falls back to \`rmSync\`. This deletes the worktree directory but leaves the git-internal metadata intact (the \`.git/worktrees/<id>/\` registration). On every subsequent spawn, \`git worktree add -b orchestrator/<id>\` fails because the branch still exists, triggering the \`branch_collision\` recovery path. That recovery path then fails intermittently because git still considers the branch \"already used by worktree\" at the now-deleted path — causing \`workspace.create failed\` → \`session.spawn_failed\`.

**Source:** local dogfooding session | **Reported by:** @aditi1178 | **Analyzed against:** \`cdd1030d8dbbfa9a8c6cb99c9188eb62af65844e\`
**Confidence:** High — exact event sequence traced to specific code lines

## Reproduction

The \`workspace.destroy_fell_back\` event is the trigger. After it fires:
1. Kill an orchestrator session (produces \`workspace.destroy_fell_back\` warn + \`terminal_pty_lost\`)
2. Spawn the orchestrator again
3. \`workspace.branch_collision\` fires every spawn from here on
4. \~50% of spawn attempts fail with \`workspace.create failed\` / \`session.spawn_failed\`
5. Repeated kill + respawn cycles required until the collision recovery happens to succeed

## Event Timeline (from live session)

```
4:22:44 PM  session.kill_started         ao-orchestrator
4:22:44 PM  ui.terminal_pty_lost         tmux session gone
4:22:44 PM  workspace.destroy_fell_back  destroy fell back to rmSync; git worktree metadata may be stale
4:22:44 PM  session.killed               ao-orchestrator

4:23:03 PM  session.spawned              (first respawn — branch_collision fires, recovery succeeds)
4:23:47 PM  session.spawn_failed         orchestrator spawn failed  ← workspace.create failed
4:23:47 PM  session.spawn_failed         orchestrator spawn failed  ← workspace.create failed
4:24:04 PM  session.spawn_failed         orchestrator spawn failed

4:35:14 PM  session.kill_started
4:35:16 PM  workspace.branch_collision   branch "orchestrator/ao-orchestrator" already exists
4:35:16 PM  session.spawned              (finally stable)
```

The \`branch_collision\` warning also fires on every earlier spawn going back to 11:59 PM the previous night — it's persistent across the session's entire lifetime once \`destroy_fell_back\` fires.

## Root Cause

**File:** \`packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts\`

**\`destroy()\` (lines 471–494):** When \`git worktree remove --force\` fails for any reason, the catch block records \`workspace.destroy_fell_back\` and calls \`removeDirWithRetry()\`. This deletes the directory on disk but git's internal metadata at \`.git/worktrees/<session-id>/\` is never cleaned up — only \`git worktree remove\` or \`git worktree prune\` does that.

**\`create()\` collision recovery (lines 354–403):** When \`git worktree add -b <branch>\` fails with "already exists", the handler tries to re-attach or force-reset the branch (lines 386–391). This fails with **"branch is already checked out / already used by worktree"** when the stale \`.git/worktrees/<session-id>/\` registration still links that branch to the deleted directory. The cleanup on retry failure (line 394) tries \`git worktree remove --force <newPath>\` but \`<newPath>\` doesn't exist yet → silently no-ops → rethrows → \`workspace.create failed\`.

The fix is one line: add \`git worktree prune\` at the top of the collision recovery block (before line 386). \`prune\` removes all \`.git/worktrees/\` registrations whose paths no longer exist on disk — exactly the condition \`destroy_fell_back\` leaves behind. \`restore()\` already does this on line 371 for the same reason.

```typescript
// packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts — inside the branch_collision catch block
// Before: directly attempts re-attach/force-reset (fails on stale metadata)
// After:
try { await git(repoPath, "worktree", "prune"); } catch {}
// then: existing re-attach / force-reset logic unchanged
```

## Impact

- Every orchestrator kill + respawn cycle hits \`branch_collision\` indefinitely once \`destroy_fell_back\` fires
- ~50% of respawn attempts fail outright, requiring multiple kill+respawn cycles
- Affects all platforms (the fallback path is platform-independent, though Windows is more likely to trigger it due to file-handle drain races)
- AO version: **0.8.0** (confirmed); regression likely present since the \`destroy_fell_back\` event was added

## Fix

Add \`git worktree prune\` to the collision recovery block in \`create()\` — mirrors what \`restore()\` already does on line 371. One-line fix.

## Related

- [#1741](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1741) — \`restore()\` similarly missing \`refExists\` branch check (closed; fix was for restore path, not create)
- [#1034](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1034) — orphaned worktrees from interrupted spawn (related but different trigger: interrupted spawn vs failed destroy)
- [#1922](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1922) — project identity split on fresh install triggering \`findManagedWorkspace\` conflict (same subsystem, different root cause)

title: bug(core): restore fails with 409 when runtime=alive but activity=exited (signal_disagreement)
body:
## Bug

**Restore session** returns HTTP 409 \`SessionNotRestorableError\` — "session is not in a terminal state" — for sessions where the tmux runtime is alive but the agent process inside is dead (\`activity=exited\`). The dashboard shows the evidence label \`signal_disagreement runtime=alive process=dead activity_signal=valid via_native activity=exited\` and a **Restore session** button, but clicking it always fails.

**Source:** Chat report | **Reported by:** @aditi1178 | **Analyzed against:** \`cdd1030d\`
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced

## Reproduction

1. Start a session with any agent (claude-code)
2. Kill the agent process inside tmux manually (or let it crash/complete), but leave the tmux session running
3. Wait for dashboard to show \`signal_disagreement\` / Exited state
4. Click **Restore session** — receives 409

Or run:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/sessions/<session-id>/restore
# → {"error":"Session <id> cannot be restored: session is not in a terminal state (status: \"working\", activity: \"exited\")"}
```

## Root Cause

\`isTerminalSession()\` in \`packages/core/src/types.ts:265\` has two branches:

```typescript
export function isTerminalSession(session) {
  if (session.lifecycle) {
    // Only checks lifecycle fields — ignores session.activity entirely
    return (
      session.lifecycle.session.state === "done" ||
      session.lifecycle.session.state === "terminated" ||
      session.lifecycle.pr.state === "merged" ||
      session.lifecycle.runtime.state === "missing" ||
      session.lifecycle.runtime.state === "exited"
    );
  }
  // Non-lifecycle path correctly checks TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES
  return (
    TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(session.status) ||
    (session.activity !== null && TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES.has(session.activity))
  );
}
```

During \`enrichSessionWithRuntimeState\` (session-manager.ts), when there is a signal disagreement:
1. \`plugins.runtime.isAlive()\` returns \`true\` (tmux session alive) → does **not** set \`lifecycle.runtime.state = "missing"\`
2. \`plugins.agent.getActivityState()\` returns \`{ state: "exited" }\` (agent process dead)
3. Line 1168 sets \`session.activity = "exited"\`
4. **Line 1169** sets \`session.lifecycle.runtime.state = "alive"\` ← regardless of whether activity is "exited"

Result: \`lifecycle.runtime.state = "alive"\`, \`lifecycle.session.state = "working"\` (or "detecting"), so the lifecycle branch of \`isTerminalSession\` returns \`false\`. \`isRestorable\` returns \`false\`. Restore throws.

The comment at restore line 3297-3300 in session-manager.ts explicitly notes that enrichment is needed so crashed sessions (\`status=working\`, \`activity=exited\`) are detected as terminal by \`isRestorable\` — but the lifecycle branch bypasses that logic entirely.

## Fix

Add the \`TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES\` check to the lifecycle branch of \`isTerminalSession\` in \`packages/core/src/types.ts\`:

```typescript
if (session.lifecycle) {
  return (
    session.lifecycle.session.state === "done" ||
    session.lifecycle.session.state === "terminated" ||
    session.lifecycle.pr.state === "merged" ||
    session.lifecycle.runtime.state === "missing" ||
    session.lifecycle.runtime.state === "exited" ||
    (session.activity !== null && TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES.has(session.activity))  // ← add
  );
}
```

This makes the lifecycle path consistent with the non-lifecycle path for terminal activity detection.

## Impact

- Any session with signal disagreement (tmux alive, agent process dead) cannot be restored from the UI or API
- Affects claude-code (most common) and any agent running in tmux runtime where the process exits but the tmux container remains
- The **Restore session** button is shown (correctly) but always returns 409

## Related

- [#1245](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1245) — Agent process dies but session remains in \`working\` state
- [#1833](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1833) — restore leaves stale terminatedAt (same restore flow)

title: bug(activity): Claude sessions misreport state — active work shown as "ready", idle_prompt shown as "waiting_input", ready/idle flapping
body:
## Bug

The dashboard activity state for **Claude Code** sessions is frequently wrong. Three concrete, live-reproduced defects, all rooted in the same architectural problem: `getClaudeActivityState` trusts Claude's **noisy native transcript** (read first, aged off **file mtime**, classified by entry *type*) over the **clean, hook-pushed** `.ao/activity.jsonl` event log.

**Source:** live AO session `ao-189` | **Reported by:** @harshitsinghbhandari | **Analyzed against:** `5d0b624f` | **AO:** 0.9.1 | node v22.14.0
**Confidence:** High (reproduced live on a real session; root cause traced to file:line)

This is a focused, evidence-backed sibling of the umbrella redesign #1899. It is **not** fully covered there — #1899 enumerates 15 breakages but does not list the `idle_prompt → waiting_input` mapping defect or the `assistant → ready` shadowing of a freshly-pushed `active`. Related: #1899 (umbrella), #1894 (sticky-state wallclock decay), #1934 (do we need a separate `ready` state). In-flight hook-migration PRs that should converge with the fix: #2030 (opencode), #1950 (codex).

## Reproduction (live `.ao/activity.jsonl` from session ao-189)

**Defect A — active work shown as "Ready".** While actively running tools / generating a response:
```
16:32:53.366  ready    ← Stop hook: previous turn ended
16:32:53.425  active
16:33:01.489  active    ← actively working (running a Bash tool) RIGHT NOW
```
Hook log correctly says `active`. Dashboard showed **Ready**. The pushed `active` was ignored.

**Defect B — normal idle shown as "Waiting for input" for ~15 min.**
```
16:15:46  ready
16:16:47  waiting_input   trigger: "Notification (idle_prompt)"   ← turn finished, awaiting user
16:31:34  active          ← user sent next message 15 min later
```
`idle_prompt` (Claude's "I'm done, waiting for you" nudge) was logged as `waiting_input` and, because actionable states are sticky (never decay), the dashboard showed **"Waiting for input"** for the entire 15-minute wait.

**Defect C — ready/idle flapping** (root cause shared with A): the activity clock is the log file's mtime, which Claude's noise re-snapshot writes (`permission-mode`, `ai-title`, `pr-link`) refresh even while idle → state oscillates ready⇄idle.

## Root Cause

1. **mtime as the activity clock (Defects A & C).** `readLastJsonlEntry` returns `modifiedAt: fileStat.mtime` (`packages/core/src/utils.ts:170`) and `readLastActivityEntry` likewise (`packages/core/src/activity-log.ts:118`). The native transcript's mtime is bumped by noise writes unrelated to real activity, so age-based classification is unstable. The clock should be the embedded per-entry `entry.ts` (which `getActivityFallbackState` already uses correctly — `activity-log.ts:170`).

2. **Native-first cascade + entry-type classification shadows pushed `active` (Defect A).** `getClaudeActivityState` reads the native transcript first and returns before consulting the hook log. It maps `assistant`/`summary` entries to `ready`/`idle` — never `active` (`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/activity-detection.ts:429-431`). While the agent is generating output (newest native entry = `assistant`), it is classified `ready` even though the hook log has a fresh `active` from `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`. The pushed truth loses to the polled noise.

3. **`idle_prompt` conflated with `permission_prompt` (Defect B).** The activity-updater hook maps both notification types to `waiting_input` (`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:451-459`, and the Node/Windows variant ~573-581). Only `permission_prompt` / `PermissionRequest` is a genuine blocked-on-human state; `idle_prompt` is the turn-end "waiting for next instruction" signal and should be `ready` (decaying to `idle`), not a sticky `waiting_input`.

## Fix

Make the **hook-pushed `.ao/activity.jsonl` the source of truth** for activity; demote the native transcript to cost/summary/uuid extraction, `blocked` detection, and a fallback only when hooks are absent. Concretely:

- **A tool_use is unambiguously `working`/`active`.** A fresh pushed `active` event (`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`) must win — never be overridden by an `assistant→ready` read from the native transcript.
- Classify off `entry.ts`, **never** `fileStat.mtime`.
- Remap `idle_prompt → ready` (only `permission_prompt`/`PermissionRequest` → `waiting_input`).
- Add hysteresis so state can't flap within one threshold window.
- Bound sticky actionable staleness so a missed clearing event can't pin `waiting_input` forever.

This is the per-Claude instance of the unified single-clock reducer being designed (intended to be shared across claude-code/codex/opencode after #2030 and #1950 land), and aligns with #1899's inbox-vs-liveness split.

## Impact

- The dashboard's primary signal (is this agent working / done / blocked?) is untrustworthy for Claude sessions: active work reads as idle/ready, and finished-and-waiting reads as blocked.
- Knock-on effects: notifier accuracy, stuck-detection, and any auto-reaction keyed on activity state inherit the wrong state.

title: test: isolated onboarding harness for published @aoagents/ao
body:
## What

A local end-to-end onboarding test for a **published** `@aoagents/ao` npm version — `npm install -g` → `ao start` → dashboard serves → `ao stop` — kept **completely isolated** from any real ao install/runtime on the machine.

### Deliverables
- **`scripts/test-onboarding.sh`** — configurable: `--version latest|nightly|exact`, `--mode fresh|coexist`, `--port` (auto if omitted), `--keep`. Clear pass/fail, non-zero exit on failure.
- **`skills/onboarding-test/SKILL.md`** (+ README entry) — any agent can onboarding-test its own PR/version; documents both modes, isolation guarantees, cleanup.

> The GitHub Actions workflow was dropped at the maintainer's request — this is run locally / on demand. The SKILL documents the one-line CI step for wiring it up later. Per-PR source-build onboarding remains covered by the existing "Test Fresh Onboarding" job.

## Isolation (all enforced by the script)
- Temp npm `--prefix` first on `PATH` — real global modules untouched.
- Sandbox `HOME` → separate `~/.agent-orchestrator`; sandbox `ao stop` only ever sees the sandbox `running.json`.
- Auto-allocated free dashboard + terminal WS ports; refuses reserved `3001`/`14800`/`14801`.
- `runtime: process` (no shared tmux server) — cannot see/kill real tmux sessions.
- Throwaway `git init` repo; non-interactive (`AO_CALLER_TYPE=agent` + `--no-orchestrator`, no LLM key needed).
- One temp root, removed on `trap EXIT` (success/failure/interrupt): graceful sandbox `ao stop --all`, kill recorded daemon pid tree, `pkill -f <unique-temp-root>` safety net, `rm -rf`.

`coexist` mode additionally snapshots the real `running.json` + `tmux ls` + listening ports **before/after** and fails loudly if anything moved.

## Two modes
- **fresh** — canonical clean onboarding (clean CI / new machine).
- **coexist** — machine already runs ao; proves zero change to the real install.

## Validation (run locally, both modes)
- `--version 0.8.0 --mode coexist` → **PASS**: dashboard `/api/sessions` 200, clean stop, and **real ao state IDENTICAL before/after** (running.json, tmux, ports).
- `--version 0.8.0 --mode fresh` → **PASS**.
- `--version nightly --mode fresh` → **PASS**.
- Real daemon (pid 49919, port 3001, 5 tmux sessions) verified **alive and unchanged** after every run; no leftover temp dirs.

### Bug the harness caught 🐛
`--version latest` (**0.9.1**) → **FAIL**: a fresh install returns **HTTP 500** on the dashboard because the bundled `agent-grok` plugin throws `Cannot find module '../package.json'`. This is exactly what `cdd1030d (#2040)` fixes on `main` — but that fix is **not in the published 0.9.1 release**. The harness surfaced a real, ship-blocking onboarding regression in the current published package.

ao update skips rebuild when dist is stale at the current commit
body:
## Summary

`ao update` (git / source installs) only rebuilds when `git fetch` advances the local commit. If the compiled output (`dist/`) is out of sync with `src/` at the **same** commit, the script prints `Already on latest version` and skips the rebuild — so the running binary keeps executing stale compiled code.

## How it happens

The rebuild is gated purely on the SHA advancing:

```sh
if [ "$local_sha" = "$remote_sha" ]; then
  printf 'Already on latest version.\n'   # ← skips pnpm install + build
else
  git pull ... && pnpm install && pnpm build ...
fi
```

So `dist/` can be stale at HEAD via:

- a manual `git pull` **before** `ao update` (HEAD already matches remote → no rebuild)
- a branch switch
- an interrupted previous build (SHA advanced but the build never finished; re-running sees a matching SHA → no rebuild)
- a manual `pnpm clean`

## Impact

Source / `npm link` installs (install method `git`) end up running whatever was last compiled. Seen in practice: a fix that exists in `src/` throws at runtime because `dist/` predates it (e.g. a session-restore change still throwing the pre-fix error). Registry installs (npm / pnpm / bun-global) are unaffected — they ship prebuilt `dist/`.

## Proposed fix

Gate the rebuild on whether `dist/` is in sync with HEAD, not on the SHA advancing:

- record the built commit in a gitignored marker (`node_modules/.ao-build-sha`), written only after a fully successful build + launcher refresh
- rebuild when the marker ≠ HEAD, the build output is missing, or `--force-rebuild` is passed
- add `ao update --force-rebuild` as an explicit escape hatch

Mirror the change in the PowerShell port and wire `--force-rebuild` through `update.ts`.

title: fix(cli): rebuild on stale dist, not just SHA advance, in ao update
body:
## What

`ao update` (git / source installs) only rebuilt when `git fetch` advanced the local SHA. If `dist/` was out of sync with `src/` at the **same** commit, the script printed `Already on latest version` and skipped the rebuild — so the running binary kept executing stale compiled code.

Causes of a stale `dist/` at HEAD:
- a manual `git pull` **before** `ao update` (HEAD already matches remote → no rebuild)
- a branch switch
- an interrupted previous build (SHA advanced but build never finished; re-run sees matching SHA → no rebuild)
- a manual `pnpm clean`

Closes #2057.

## How

Gate the rebuild on whether the compiled output is in sync with HEAD, not on the SHA advancing:

- A gitignored marker `node_modules/.ao-build-sha` records the commit `dist/` was last built from, written **only after a fully successful build + launcher refresh**.
- Rebuild when: the marker ≠ HEAD, the build output is missing (catches a wiped `dist/`), or `--force-rebuild` is passed.
- New flag `ao update --force-rebuild` forces a rebuild on demand.

Mirrored in the PowerShell port (`ao-update.ps1`) and wired through `update.ts` (rejected on non-git installs, like the other build-only flags).

## Tests

- Updated the "already latest" test to require a fresh build (sentinel + marker) before skipping the rebuild.
- Added coverage: rebuild on stale marker at matching SHA, and rebuild on `--force-rebuild` when the build is already fresh.
- Full `ao-cli` update suite green (192 passed, 4 Windows-only skipped); prettier + typecheck clean.

title: ao spawn does not reject closed/cancelled issues — spawns full session on dead work
body:
Bug Description

Running ao spawn <issue-number> on a closed or cancelled issue proceeds through the entire spawn pipeline — session ID reservation, worktree creation, tmux pane, and agent launch — without ever checking whether the issue is still open.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Close an issue in the tracker (e.g. issue #42)
  2. Run ao spawn 42
  3. A session is fully created and the agent starts working on the closed issue

Expected Behavior

ao spawn should reject immediately with an error such as:

Issue #42 is closed. Cannot spawn a session for a closed/cancelled issue.

No session, worktree, or tmux pane should be created.

Root Cause

In packages/core/src/session-manager.ts, the spawn() method fetches the issue via plugins.tracker.getIssue() and stores it as resolvedIssue. It validates:

  • ✅ Issue exists (404 → treat as ad-hoc string)
  • ✅ Auth/network errors (fail fast)
  • ❌ Issue state is never checked

The Issue type already has state: "open" | "in_progress" | "closed" | "cancelled" (defined in types.ts), but after fetching, the code proceeds directly to branch name generation, workspace setup, and agent launch — with no gate on resolvedIssue.state.

Affected Entry Points

Entry Point | Location | Affected? -- | -- | -- CLI (ao spawn ) | → sessionManager.spawn() | ✅ Yes Web API (POST /api/spawn) | packages/web/src/app/api/spawn/route.ts | ✅ Yes Backlog auto-claim | packages/web/src/lib/services.ts:314 | ⚠️ Mostly safe (filters state: "open"), but has a TOCTOU race condition

All of this happens for an issue that was already resolved and won't be worked on — entirely avoidable with a single state check before resource creation begins.

title: feat: implement issue spawn rejection for closed or cancelled states
body: ## Summary This PR prevents AO from spawning new worker sessions for tracker issues that are already `closed` or `cancelled`. Previously, spawn requests could continue even when the linked tracker issue was no longer actionable. The session manager now checks the resolved issue state before creating a workspace or runtime, records a rejection activity event, and throws a typed `IssueNotSpawnableError`. ## Changes - Added `IssueNotSpawnableError` for closed/cancelled issue spawn attempts - Added `isSpawnableIssueState()` helper for spawn-eligible issue states - Updated `SessionManager.spawn()` to reject closed or cancelled tracker issues before workspace/runtime creation - Updated `/api/spawn` to return `409 Conflict` for non-spawnable issues instead of `500` - Added API/activity metadata for rejected spawn attempts - Added session manager tests for: - rejecting `closed` issues - rejecting `cancelled` issues - allowing `in_progress` issues ## Testing - Added coverage in `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/spawn.test.ts`

body:
## Problem

Once an orchestrator finishes a batch of PRs, the review dashboard accumulates entries forever. There is no targeted way to clear them.

In a recent run with 7 worker sessions and 16 review runs, the dashboard ended in this state after every PR was merged and worker sessions were `ao session cleanup`'d:

```
Reviews: 16 runs · 11 active · 0 open findings
  ivt-rev-12 needs_triage → ivt-4 0 open findings
  ivt-rev-16 queued       → ivt-4 0 open findings
  ivt-rev-15 queued       → ivt-4 0 open findings
  ivt-rev-11 needs_triage → ivt-5 0 open findings
  ivt-rev-10 failed       → ivt-5 0 open findings
  ivt-rev-9  running      → ivt-6  (zombie — host was restarted, run never reaped)
  ...
```

11 of these were "active" only because their `linkedSessionId` had been cleaned up but the run JSON was left behind. None had open findings. Statuses included `clean`, `outdated`, `needs_triage`, `queued`, `failed`, and one stuck `running` from a host restart.

The on-disk reality:
- `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<project>/code-reviews/runs/review-run-*.json` — one file per run (kept forever)
- `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<project>/code-reviews/findings/review-finding-*.json` — even resolved findings stay
- `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<project>/code-reviews/workspaces/ivt-rev-N/` — full git worktree per reviewer (10 MB in this run, 12 worktrees)

## What exists today (and why it's insufficient)

- **`ao session cleanup`** — only handles worker sessions, ignores `code-reviews/`.
- **`ao review` subcommands** — `run / execute / send / list`. No `prune`, `delete`, `clear`, or `cancel`.
- **PR #1380 (`ao reset`)** — closest neighbor, but nuclear: deletes the whole project directory, unregisters the project from the global config, kills all live sessions. Way too coarse for "I just want yesterday's review chatter to stop showing up."

## Manual workaround (what I had to do)

```sh
# 1. unregister 12 git worktrees from the upstream repo
cd <repo>
for w in ivt-rev-3 ivt-rev-4 ... ivt-rev-14; do
  git worktree remove --force ".../code-reviews/workspaces/$w"
done
git worktree prune

# 2. delete run + finding JSONs
rm -f .../code-reviews/runs/review-run-*.json
rm -f .../code-reviews/findings/review-finding-*.json
```

Footguns this hits:
- `rm -rf .../workspaces/` would orphan `.git/worktrees/` registrations in the upstream repo (issue #1562 / #2045 territory) — you must go through `git worktree remove` first.
- No CLI signal to AO that the runs are gone, so anything caching review state in memory (e.g. a running `ao start` web server) needs a refresh.
- Easy to delete a run whose linked session is still alive and care about it.

## Proposal

Add `ao review prune` (subcommand of the existing `ao review` group) with these flags:

```
ao review prune [project]
  --status <list>      # comma-separated: clean,outdated,failed,needs_triage,queued,running
                       # default: clean,outdated,failed
  --older-than <dur>   # e.g. 7d, 24h — only prune runs whose updatedAt is older
  --pr-merged          # only prune runs whose linked PR is merged or closed
  --linked-session <s> # only prune runs linked to the given session id (or use `none` for orphaned)
  --dry-run            # print what would be deleted, exit 0
  --yes                # skip confirmation
  --keep-findings      # keep finding JSONs even when their parent run is pruned
```

For each pruned run it should:
1. Run `git worktree remove --force <reviewerWorkspacePath>` against the upstream repo (the path is in the run JSON).
2. `git worktree prune` once at the end.
3. Delete the run JSON and (unless `--keep-findings`) any findings whose `runId` matches.
4. Emit an event so a running `ao start` UI refreshes.

Optionally a sibling `ao review delete <run-id>` for one-off targeted deletion.

## Why now

`ao reset` (#1380) is the only blunt-instrument cleanup, and it's not appropriate when you want to keep the project around. Without `ao review prune`, the dashboard accumulates stale entries indefinitely, including stuck `running` runs from host restarts (no auto-reap on AO startup).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ao review prune --dry-run` lists what it would delete; exit 0
- [ ] Default invocation only touches terminal/dead statuses; never removes a run with open findings unless `--include-findings` (or similar) is passed
- [ ] Reviewer worktrees are unregistered via `git worktree remove`, not just `rm -rf` (avoids #1562/#2045 stale-worktree class of bugs)
- [ ] `ao review list` shows zero entries after `ao review prune --status clean,outdated,failed,needs_triage,queued,running --yes` against a finished project
- [ ] Live UI (web dashboard) reflects the prune without a full reload

## Related

- PR #1380 — `ao reset` (nuclear)
- PR #1871 — code review board (introduced the dashboard with no cleanup story)
- Issue #1562 / #2045 — stale `.git/worktrees/` registration class of bug; `ao review prune` must avoid contributing to it

title: bug(agent-cursor, windows): worker launch fails — POSIX printf + argv-inlined prompt in getLaunchCommand()
body:
## Summary

On Windows, **worker** sessions spawned via `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-cursor` exit within ~1 minute of launch (`agent_process_exited`, no PR, no acknowledge; lifecycle goes `working → detecting → stuck`), while the **orchestrator** session on the same host stays healthy.

Root cause is in how the cursor plugin builds the launch command for the worker path, not in the issue/task content.

`getLaunchCommand()` (`dist/index.js`) branches on whether both a `systemPromptFile` **and** a separate `prompt` are present:

- **Worker** (both present) emits, roughly:
  `agent … -- "$(cat <file>; printf '\n\n'; printf %s '<prompt>')"` → **POSIX sh syntax**.
- **Orchestrator** (only `systemPromptFile`) emits:
  `agent … -- "$(cat <file>)"` → no `printf`.

On Windows, `ao-core` `platform.js` defaults the PTY shell to `powershell.exe -Command` (no `pwsh`). In PowerShell, `cat` (= `Get-Content`) and `$()` (subexpression) are valid, so the **orchestrator** branch survives. But `printf` does not exist in PowerShell, so the **worker** branch dies.

Two distinct signatures observed in the PTY:

- **A:** `printf : The term 'printf' is not recognized` + `error: unknown option '-ne'` — POSIX builtin under PowerShell.
- **B:** `The command line is too long` — the whole prompt is inlined into argv via `$(cat <large-file>)`; for a large body (~24 KB observed) this exceeds the cmd.exe limit (~8191 chars). **Independent of shell** — switching to bash does not help.

This is independent of `"`/JSON in the GitHub Issue body: the prompt is read from a file, so its contents are literal and do not break argv.

## Environment

- AO: `@aoagents/ao@0.9.x`
- OS: Windows 11 (PowerShell 5.1 as PTY shell; no `pwsh`)
- Plugin: `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-cursor`
- Agent launcher: `agent` / `cursor-agent` installed as a Windows `.cmd` shim

## Why AO_SHELL=bash is not a sufficient workaround

`platform.js` exposes `AO_SHELL` as a PTY shell override. Setting `AO_SHELL=C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` removes signature **A** (`printf` resolves), but then:

1. `agent: command not found` — Git Bash does not resolve the Windows `agent.cmd` launcher; and
2. after shimming `agent`, large prompts still hit signature **B** (`command line is too long`).

So `AO_SHELL=bash` does not fix worker launch for non-trivial prompts.

## Proposed durable fix

Deliver the worker prompt via a **file or an explicit agent flag**, instead of inlining it into argv with `$(cat …; printf …)`:

- avoids POSIX `printf` on Windows PowerShell (signature A), and
- avoids the argv length limit for large prompts (signature B).

A cmd.exe-style escape alone (cf. #2003 / #2006 on the code-review path) would not solve signature B, since the prompt would still be inlined into the command line.

## Related

- #2003 — `bug(code-review, windows): shell:true breaks review prompt argument passing` — same *family* (Windows argument passing breaks an AO subprocess invocation), different surface/mechanism (Node `spawn` → cmd.exe word-split on the **review** path vs. PTY shell-string `printf`/argv on the **worker launch** path).
- #2006 — fix PR for #2003 (`escapeArgForCmd`).

title: Windows: worker launch fails — cursor agent plugin uses POSIX printf + inline argv for task prompt
body:
## Summary

On Windows, **worker** Cursor sessions fail to launch because `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-cursor` builds the launch command with the POSIX `printf` builtin and inlines the entire task prompt into `argv`. The agent process exits within ~1 minute of `spawning → working` with no PR, no chat, and the session drifts `working → detecting → stuck` (`agent_process_exited`).

The **orchestrator** session survives on the same machine, which pinpoints the cause exactly (see below).

## Environment

- `@aoagents/ao` 0.9.2, `@aoagents/ao-cli` 0.9.2, `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-cursor` **0.9.1** (current `latest`)
- Windows 11, AO default shell = `powershell.exe -Command` (Windows PowerShell 5.1, no `pwsh`)
- Agent: Cursor (`agent` CLI)

## Root cause (from plugin source)

`dist/index.js`, `getLaunchCommand(config)`. When both a system-prompt file and a task prompt are present (the worker case):

```js
// line ~141 — worker path (system prompt file + task prompt)
parts.push("--", `"$(cat ${shellEscape(config.systemPromptFile)}; printf '\n\n'; printf %s ${shellEscape(config.prompt)})"`);
```

```js
// line ~144 — orchestrator / no-task-prompt path (system prompt file only)
parts.push("--", `"$(cat ${shellEscape(config.systemPromptFile)})"`);
```

The worker line fails on Windows two independent ways:

- **Signature A — `printf` does not exist in PowerShell.** `printf` is a POSIX builtin; Windows PowerShell has no such command (not even for `printf '\n\n'`). The launch line dies with `printf : The term 'printf' is not recognized …`, and the agent CLI then sees a mangled argv (`error: unknown option '-ne'`).
- **Signature B — command line too long.** The full prompt is inlined into `argv` via `printf %s '<prompt>'`. A large prompt (observed ~24 KB issue body) exceeds the Windows command-line length limit: `The command line is too long.` This mode is shell-independent.

**Why the orchestrator survives but workers die:** the orchestrator has only a `systemPromptFile` (no separate `config.prompt`), so it takes the **cat-only** path (line ~144), which works in PowerShell because `cat` is an alias for `Get-Content`. Workers have `systemPromptFile` **and** `config.prompt`, so they take the `printf` path (line ~141) and fail. This is observed, not hypothetical.

## Still present in all current builds

The exact line ~141 is byte-identical in:

- `0.9.1` (`latest`)
- `0.9.3-nightly-96ea22a7…` (current `nightly`, published 2026-05-24)
- `0.10.1-nightly-249c6704…`

`AO_SHELL=bash` is **not** a sufficient workaround: it clears Signature A but then `agent: command not found` (Git Bash does not resolve `agent.cmd` without a shim), and large prompts still hit Signature B.

## Proposed fix

Deliver the **task prompt** the same way the system prompt is already delivered — via a file, `cat`-ed — instead of `printf`-inlining it. On Windows specifically:

```js
// write config.prompt to a temp file, then:
parts.push("--", `"$(cat ${shellEscape(config.systemPromptFile)}; cat ${shellEscape(taskPromptFile)})"`);
```

This mirrors the already-working line ~144, removes the POSIX `printf` dependency (fixes A), and keeps the prompt out of `argv` (fixes B). No new agent CLI flag is required — the positional `$(cat …)` substitution is proven to work on Windows by the orchestrator path. More generally: avoid the POSIX `printf` builtin in the Windows launch template, and prefer file-based prompt delivery over `argv` inlining.

## Repro

1. On Windows (default PowerShell shell), `ao spawn` a worker whose issue/task prompt is non-trivial.
2. Observe the session go `spawning → working → detecting → stuck`, no PR, no Cursor chat.
3. `ao session attach <id>` shows `printf : The term 'printf' is not recognized …` (Signature A) and/or `The command line is too long.` (Signature B).

title: fix: exclude orchestrator sessions from active-session guard in /api/update
body:
The POST /api/update route returns 409 Conflict when any session is active (working/idle/needs_input/stuck). The orchestrator session itself is always idle while the dashboard is running, making the Update button permanently unusable through the web UI.

This fix filters out orchestrator sessions (identified via `isOrchestratorSession()`) from the active session count, so only genuine worker sessions block the update.

title: agent-codex should launch headless workers with codex exec
body:
## Summary

The bundled `agent-codex` plugin launches Codex worker sessions as `codex <prompt>`. With the current Codex CLI, that enters the interactive CLI path rather than the non-interactive worker path. For unattended AO workers, the plugin should launch `codex exec <prompt>`.

## Reproduction

Environment observed locally:

- AO CLI: `0.9.2`
- `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex`: `0.9.1`
- Codex CLI: current npm-installed `@openai/codex`
- Windows process runtime, project configured with `agent: codex`

Steps:

1. Configure a project with `agent: codex`.
2. Start AO: `ao start --no-dashboard --no-restore`.
3. Spawn a prompt worker:
   `ao spawn --agent codex --prompt "create a file and run tests"`
4. Inspect the spawned process command line.

Observed launch command before local patch:

```text
codex -c check_for_update_on_startup=false --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox ... -- '<prompt>'
```

The worker session was created, but Codex did not perform the requested headless work.

## Expected behavior

AO should launch the Codex worker with the non-interactive Codex subcommand:

```text
codex exec -c check_for_update_on_startup=false --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox ... -- '<prompt>'
```

After locally patching the plugin to insert `exec`, the same AO smoke test spawned a Codex worker that created the requested file and ran `npm test` successfully.

## Proposed fix

In `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts`, initialize the launch command parts as:

```ts
const parts: string[] = [shellEscape(binary), "exec"];
```

and update the existing `getLaunchCommand` tests accordingly.

title: fix(agent-codex): launch workers with codex exec
body:
## Summary
- launch Codex worker sessions with `codex exec` so AO-created workers run non-interactively
- keep existing option handling for permissions, model, reasoning effort, config, prompt, and post-launch setup
- add a patch changeset for `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex`

Fixes #2078

## Why
The current `agent-codex` process command starts as `codex ...`, which opens the interactive Codex UI and ignores AO's prompt-driven worker contract. In local AO smoke testing this left spawned workers idle until they were marked `stuck`. The Codex CLI's non-interactive form is `codex exec <prompt>`, which is the expected mode for headless AO worker launches.

## Validation
- `corepack pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core build`
- `corepack pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex test`
- `corepack pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex typecheck`
- `corepack pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex build`

Note: `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` completed, but emitted a local Windows warning about rebuilding `node-pty` because the Visual Studio Spectre-mitigated libraries are not installed. That did not affect the Codex plugin checks above.

title: Question: completed Codex worker later marked stuck during lifecycle detection
body:
## Question
Should a Codex worker session that has already reported `agentReportedState: "completed"` be treated as terminal/success before later process lifecycle probes can mark it `stuck`?

## Context
We are testing AO with the Codex agent plugin on Windows using the local process runtime:

- `@aoagents/ao`: `0.9.2`
- `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex`: `0.9.1`
- Windows PowerShell
- Project agent configured as `codex`
- Worker launched after locally patching `agent-codex` to use `codex exec` for prompt-driven non-interactive work

This is separate from the `agent-codex` launch-command issue in #2078 / #2079.

## Observed behavior
After the local `codex exec` patch, AO spawned session `atp-2` and the Codex worker successfully performed the requested smoke task:

- created `ao-smoke-result.txt` containing `AO_SMOKE_OK`
- ran the project tests successfully
- created branch `feat/ao-smoke-atp-2`

The session JSON contained completion evidence:

```json
{
  "agentReportedState": "completed",
  "agentReportedAt": "2026-06-01T11:23:06.685Z",
  "codexThreadId": "019e82eb-3170-7891-bec0-2291b84ebe5e"
}
```

However, before manual cleanup, `ao session ls --json` later reported the session as `stuck`. The lifecycle evidence looked like:

```text
reason: probe_failure
runtime state: exited
signal_disagreement runtime=alive process=dead activity_signal=valid via_native activity=exited
```

Attempting to report completion externally after that was rejected because the runtime had already exited:

```text
Report rejected: runtime is not alive
```

## Expected / question
For prompt-only local work where the worker has reported `completed`, should AO promote that session to a terminal completed state before runtime exit probes can escalate it to `stuck`?

Or is the current behavior expected because AO requires some other completion path, artifact, PR state, or runtime shutdown protocol in addition to `agentReportedState: "completed"`?

If this is expected behavior, guidance on the intended lifecycle contract for short-lived headless agents would be very helpful.

Updates `ws` from 8.20.0 to 8.20.1
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

Updates `ws` from 8.20.0 to 8.20.1
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

Updates `ws` from 8.20.0 to 8.20.1
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

Updates `ws` from 8.20.0 to 8.20.1
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

Updates `ws` from 8.20.0 to 8.20.1
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

Updates `ws` from 8.20.0 to 8.20.1
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

title: feat(review): per-finding send, programmatic dismiss, and sent-history for legacy ao review (0.9.x)
body:
## Context (orchestrator-pack consumer, AO 0.9.2)

`orchestrator-pack` is building a **finding router** (`forward` | `backlog` | `drop`) after Codex review. Gate 0 spike on **AO 0.9.2** (`@aoagents/ao`) shows legacy `ao review` cannot enact per-finding routes without unsupported state mutation.

Evidence: [orchestrator-pack architecture — Gate 0](https://github.com/chetwerikoff/orchestrator-pack/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#finding-routing-enactment--gate-0-ao-092-2026-06-02). Pack tracking: [chetwerikoff/orchestrator-pack#140](https://github.com/chetwerikoff/orchestrator-pack/issues/140).

## Problem

1. **Bulk send only** — `ao review send <run>` sends **all** `status: open` findings; no per-finding filter (`sendCodeReviewFindingsToAgent` in ao-core 0.9.2).
2. **No CLI terminal transition for non-forward** — Finding statuses: `open` | `dismissed` | `sent_to_agent` | `resolved`. `dismissed` exists but only via **dashboard UI**; no `ao review dismiss`. If a router chooses backlog/drop but finding stays `open`, orchestrator rules (`needs_triage` + `openFindingCount > 0` → send) **re-fire forever**.
3. **No prior_sent at routing point** — `ao review list --json` exposes run aggregates only, not per-finding sent history for duplicate `drop`.

Pack **must not** hand-edit `code-reviews/findings/*.json` (operator runbook).

## Requested API (minimum for legacy `ao review` on 0.9.x)

- [ ] **List findings** for a run (CLI or documented API): id, fingerprint, status, severity.
- [ ] **Selective send**: `ao review send <run> --finding <id>...` (or equivalent) — subset of open findings.
- [ ] **Programmatic dismiss** (or `backlogged` status): transition non-forward findings off `open` so `openFindingCount` decreases without send.
- [ ] **(Desired)** Sent-history in `list --json` per `linkedSessionId` (fingerprints/ids already sent in PR review loop).

## Related (not substitutes on current 0.9.2 CLI)

- Pipeline #1346 / #1350 (`ao artifact dismiss|send`, Workbench) — future; pack on 0.9.2 cannot depend on unreleased pipeline CLI.
- #2070 `ao review prune` — run hygiene, not per-finding routing.

## Acceptance

Orchestrator (or pack wrapper) can forward some findings, dismiss/backlog others, and leave the run quiescent without hand-editing store files.

title: session restore unreachable when agent crashes/hangs but tmux session survives (isAlive treats tmux-session-exists as agent-alive)
body:
## Summary

`session restore` (both the web UI "Restore" link and `ao session restore <name>`) refuses to act on a session whose **agent process has died or hung but whose tmux session still exists**. Such sessions land in a non-terminal `stuck`/`idle` limbo that `isRestorable()` rejects, so there is no in-product way to recover them — you have to manually kill the surviving shell first.

Root cause: for the tmux runtime, `isAlive()` checks **"does the tmux session exist?"**, not **"is the agent process inside the pane alive?"**. When an agent crashes (segfault) or deadlocks, the launch wrapper (`ao-launch-*.sh` / its bash) often survives in the pane, so AO still considers the runtime `alive` → status `stuck` → not terminal → not restorable.

## Environment

- `ao` 0.9.4 (`@aoagents/ao` → `@aoagents/ao-cli`, `@aoagents/ao-core`)
- runtime: `tmux` (tmux 3.2a), agent: `claude-code` (Claude Code 2.1.161)
- workspace: worktree
- Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 22.04)

## What happened

Two sessions died on the same machine:

1. **Orchestrator** — the Claude Code (Bun) process **segfaulted** (`Illegal instruction (core dumped)`), leaving the pane at a bash prompt.
2. **Worker `sen-225`** — the Claude process **deadlocked** (alive but blocked in `futex_wait_queue`, 0 CPU progress, TUI frozen on the same spinner frame for minutes).

In both cases the **tmux session and its wrapper bash were still alive**. The web UI showed:

> process running. The live terminal is gone, but the session context is still available.

Clicking **Restore** did nothing. `ao session restore sen-225` failed identically:

```
Cannot restore: session is not in a terminal state (status: "stuck", activity: "idle")
```

## Root cause (with refs)

The web route `POST /api/sessions/[id]/restore` calls the same `SessionManager.restore()` from `@aoagents/ao-core` that the CLI uses (bundled into the web build), so UI and CLI behave identically.

`restore()` gates on `isRestorable(session)` (`ao-core/dist/session-manager.js` ~L2735; `ao-core/dist/types.js` L61), which requires a **terminal** state:

- `TERMINAL_STATUSES = { killed, terminated, done, cleanup, errored, merged }`
- or `activity === "exited"`
- or `lifecycle.runtime.state ∈ { missing, exited }`

During enrichment (`session-manager.js` ~L779):

```js
const alive = await plugins.runtime.isAlive(session.runtimeHandle);
if (!alive) { /* runtime.state = "missing"; activity = "exited"; ... terminal */ }
// else -> falls through to activity detection -> runtime.state = "alive", status "stuck"/"idle"
```

For the **tmux** runtime, `isAlive()` is true whenever the **tmux session exists** (the failure reason is even labeled `tmux_missing` vs `process_missing` at ~L783). A crashed/hung agent whose wrapper shell survives therefore reports `alive: true` → never terminal → `isRestorable` → false → restore refused.

## Reproduce

1. Spawn a session (tmux runtime).
2. Kill **only the agent** inside the pane, leaving the pane shell alive — e.g. `kill -9 <claude_pid>` (or simulate a crash/hang). The tmux session remains.
3. `ao status` shows the session as `stuck` (or the UI shows "process running / live terminal gone").
4. Click **Restore** (or run `ao session restore <name>`) → rejected: *"session is not in a terminal state"*.

## Workaround

Collapse the tmux session so `isAlive()` returns false, then restore:

```bash
tmux kill-session -t <session>     # or kill the surviving wrapper PID
ao session restore <session>        # now succeeds: runtime "missing" -> terminal -> restorable
```

## Suggested fix

For the tmux runtime, `isAlive()` (and/or enrichment) should distinguish **"tmux session exists"** from **"agent process is alive in the pane."** Options:

- Probe the pane's foreground/child process for the actual agent binary (and/or `pane_dead`) rather than treating session existence as liveness.
- Treat a session whose agent is gone/hung but whose shell survives as a restorable/terminal-ish state (e.g. a `crashed` status), so the existing Restore path can recover it in place instead of requiring a manual `tmux kill-session`.

Bonus: it'd help to have a way to recover a `stuck` (hung-but-alive) session from the UI without dropping to a shell — e.g. a "force restart" that kills the runtime and restores.

title: Lifecycle hook commands use relative paths → `.claude/activity-updater.sh: not found` during sub-agent (Agent/Task) tool calls
body:
## Summary

The Claude Code agent plugin writes its lifecycle hook commands as **relative paths** (`.claude/activity-updater.sh`, `.claude/metadata-updater.sh`) and registers them for every hook event, including `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop`. When a **sub-agent** (the `Agent`/`Task` tool) triggers those hooks, the hook process's working directory is not the worktree root, so the shell can't resolve the relative path:

```
PreToolUse:Agent hook error  ⎿ Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: 1: .claude/activity-updater.sh: not found
PostToolUse:Read hook error  ⎿ Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: 1: .claude/activity-updater.sh: not found
```

The errors are **non-blocking**, but they:
1. spam the agent transcript (one pair per tool call while sub-agents run), and
2. drop the `.ao/activity.jsonl` activity signal during sub-agent work, which can lead to **false `stuck` / `probe_failure`** lifecycle detection on otherwise-healthy sessions.

At the top-level agent cwd (worktree root) the relative path resolves fine — which is why `activity.jsonl` is written normally until the agent dispatches parallel `Explore`/`Task` sub-agents.

## Environment

- `@aoagents/ao` **0.9.4**
- plugin `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code` (manifest version `0.1.0`)
- `claude` **2.1.161**, Linux (bash)

## Root cause

In `ao-plugin-agent-claude-code/dist/index.js`, the hook-setup routine sets:

```js
metadataCommand = ".claude/metadata-updater.sh";
activityCommand = ".claude/activity-updater.sh";
```

and registers `activityCommand` for all of `SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Notification, PermissionRequest, Stop, StopFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, PostCompact`. Relative commands only work when the hook runs from the worktree root; sub-agent tool calls do not guarantee that cwd.

## Suggested fix

Use the `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` variable that Claude Code exports for hook execution, which always points at the project/worktree root:

```js
metadataCommand = "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/metadata-updater.sh";
activityCommand = "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/activity-updater.sh";
```

Apply the same to the Windows `.cjs` branch:

```js
metadataCommand = "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/metadata-updater.cjs";
activityCommand = "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/activity-updater.cjs";
```

The dedup/upsert matching keys off the bare filenames (`activity-updater.sh`, etc.), so prefixing with `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/` is backward-compatible with existing `settings.json` files.

(Note: a bundled copy of the same generator also exists in the `ao-web` server chunks; it would need the same change.)

## Repro

1. Spawn a worker session for any repo.
2. Have the agent dispatch a parallel sub-agent (`Agent`/`Task`, e.g. several `Explore` agents).
3. Observe `PreToolUse:Agent` / `PostToolUse:*` hook errors: `/bin/sh: 1: .claude/activity-updater.sh: not found`.

## Workaround

Edit the worker's `.claude/settings.json` to make the hook `command` absolute (`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/activity-updater.sh`), or patch the plugin's `dist/index.js` accordingly.

title: fix(agent-claude-code): use $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for hook commands (fixes #2090)
body:
## Problem

The Claude Code agent plugin registers its activity/metadata lifecycle hooks with **relative** command paths (`.claude/activity-updater.sh`, `.claude/metadata-updater.sh`) for every hook event, including `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop`.

When a hook fires from a **sub-agent** (`Agent`/`Task` tool) call, the process working directory is not the worktree root, so the shell can't resolve the relative path:

```
PreToolUse:Agent hook error  ⎿ Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: 1: .claude/activity-updater.sh: not found
PostToolUse:Read hook error  ⎿ Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: 1: .claude/activity-updater.sh: not found
```

It's non-blocking, but it (a) spams the agent transcript while sub-agents run and (b) drops the `.ao/activity.jsonl` signal during sub-agent work, which can cause **false `stuck` / `probe_failure`** lifecycle detection on otherwise-healthy sessions. At the top-level agent cwd (worktree root) the relative path resolves fine — which is why it only shows up once the agent dispatches parallel `Explore`/`Task` sub-agents.

## Fix

Prefix the hook commands with `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, which Claude Code exports for hook execution and which always points at the worktree root:

```
$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/activity-updater.sh
node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/activity-updater.cjs   # windows branch
```

This resolves correctly regardless of the hook's cwd, while keeping `settings.json` content **identical across worktrees** (no hardcoded absolute path — preserving the existing "different worktree paths produce identical settings.json" guarantee). The dedup/upsert logic keys off the bare filenames (`activity-updater.sh`, …), so existing settings migrate cleanly.

Applied to both the unix (`.sh`) and windows (`.cjs`) branches.

## Tests

- Updated `index.test.ts` assertions to the new `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` contract (including the "updates an existing absolute hook path" migration test).
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test` → **270 passing**. The one failing test (`activity-updater.integration.test.ts`, a special-character escaping round-trip) **also fails on pristine `main`** in this environment (`/bin/sh` escaping), and is unrelated to this change — it touches neither the hook command paths nor the updater scripts.

Fixes #2090

title: review run fails silently as `failed / 0 findings` when codex isn't installed (spawn codex ENOENT)
body:
## Summary

`ao review run <session> --execute` (without an explicit `--command`) silently fails when the `codex` CLI is not installed. The review run is recorded as **`status: failed`** with **`0 open findings`** and `terminationReason: "Codex review failed: spawn codex ENOENT"`.

This is problematic because:
1. The default reviewer hard-assumes `codex` is on `PATH`; there is no preflight check or actionable error at the CLI ("codex not found — install it or pass `--command`").
2. A `failed` run with `0 findings` is easy to misread as a *clean* review (no findings) rather than *the reviewer never ran*. An orchestrator looping over runs can mistakenly treat it as mergeable.
3. There's no config-level way to set a default reviewer command, so every `ao review run` must pass `--command` to use a non-codex reviewer.

## Environment

- `@aoagents/ao` 0.9.4
- `codex` not installed (`spawn codex ENOENT`)
- Linux

## Repro

1. On a host without `codex` on `PATH`, open a PR from a worker session.
2. `ao review run <session> --execute`
3. `ao review list <project>` → `… failed … 0 open findings …`
4. Inspect the run JSON → `terminationReason: "Codex review failed: spawn codex ENOENT"`.

## Suggestions

- **Preflight**: detect missing `codex` before starting and exit with a clear, actionable message (and a non-zero CLI exit).
- **Distinguish states**: a reviewer that never produced output should not look like `failed + 0 findings`; consider a distinct `errored`/`reviewer_unavailable` status so automation doesn't confuse it with a clean review.
- **Configurable default reviewer**: support a `reviewer.command` (or `defaults.reviewerCommand`) in `config.yaml` so a custom reviewer can be used without passing `--command` on every run.
- Optionally document the expected `--command` stdout contract (`{"findings":[{severity,title,body,filePath,startLine,endLine,confidence}]}`; `{"findings":[]}` = clean) in the help text, since it's currently only discoverable from source.

feat: configurable merge method (ff-only + merge commit fallback)
body:
## Summary

Adds a per-project `mergeMethod` config option so users can preserve full git history instead of always squashing. Default remains `"squash"` (backward compatible). Consumed by the dashboard merge button via `scm.mergePR`.

> **Note:** The `auto-merge` reaction is currently a notify-only stub (`lifecycle-manager.ts`) and does **not** call `scm.mergePR` yet, so it does not consume `mergeMethod`. This option only takes effect from the dashboard merge action today.

New `"ff-only"` strategy (GitHub SCM only):
1. Tries `gh pr merge --ff-only` (clean linear history)
2. Falls back to `--merge` (merge commit) only when the branch has genuinely diverged — other failures (auth, network, not-found) propagate

No squash, no rebase for `ff-only` — git history is preserved. `"ff-only"` is an AO composite strategy, not a native API value; the GitLab SCM throws an explicit error if it's configured there.

### Config Usage

```yaml
projects:
  my-app:
    repo: owner/my-app
    path: ~/my-app
    mergeMethod: ff-only    # try fast-forward, fall back to merge commit
```

Options: `"squash"` (default), `"merge"`, `"rebase"`, `"ff-only"`

## Files Changed

1. `packages/core/src/types.ts` — Add `"ff-only"` to `MergeMethod` (with JSDoc), add `mergeMethod?` to `ProjectConfig`
2. `packages/core/src/config.ts` — Add `mergeMethod` to `ProjectConfigSchema` (default `"squash"`)
3. `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` — `mergePR()` handles `"ff-only"`: try `--ff-only`, fall back to `--merge` only on a non-fast-forward failure
4. `packages/plugins/scm-gitlab/src/index.ts` — `mergePR()` throws for unsupported `"ff-only"` instead of silently ignoring it
5. `packages/web/src/app/api/prs/[id]/merge/route.ts` — Reads `project.mergeMethod` instead of hardcoding `"squash"`

Closes #2095

title: feat(core): make AO-local reviewer backend configurable
body:
## Summary

The AO-local reviewer was hardcoded to shell out to `codex`, so hosts without Codex/OpenAI credentials (e.g. Claude Code-only setups) hit a `401 Unauthorized` on every `ao review run` and had to paste a `--command` wrapper into every call. This makes the reviewer backend configurable, defaulting to the agent the user already runs.

### Resolution precedence

The reviewer backend resolves in the documented order:

1. `--command <shell>` flag (unchanged escape hatch)
2. per-project `projects.<id>.review` (`command` or `agent`)
3. global `review` block (`command` or `agent`)
4. the worker agent (`defaults.agent`) **when it has a known reviewer adapter**
5. `codex` (final fallback — preserves existing behavior)

A `claude-code` worker now reviews with Claude Code by default; `codex` remains the fallback only when the worker agent has no adapter (e.g. `aider`/`opencode`) or already *is* codex.

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/types.ts`** — new `ReviewConfig` (`agent` | `command`, mutually exclusive); `review?` added to `OrchestratorConfig` (global) and `ProjectConfig` (per-project).
- **`packages/core/src/config.ts`** — `ReviewConfigSchema` (strict, mutual-exclusion refinement) wired into both schemas.
- **`packages/core/src/code-review-manager.ts`** — `runClaudeCodeReview` adapter (`claude -p <prompt> --permission-mode bypassPermissions --output-format text`), a `{claude-code, codex}` adapter registry, and `resolveCodeReviewRunner(...)`. Resolution happens up front in `executeCodeReviewRun` so a misconfigured `review.agent` fails fast (clear error naming valid values) before any run state changes. `runReviewer` is kept as an explicit override; the `--command` flag now flows through `reviewCommand`.
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/review.ts`** — `run`/`execute` pass `reviewCommand` instead of constructing the runner; `ao review --help` documents the config keys.
- **Docs/schema** — `schema/config.schema.json`, `README.md`, `agent-orchestrator.yaml.example`, and the `ao config-help` reference all document `review.agent` / `review.command`.

## Tests

New `packages/core/src/__tests__/code-review-backend.test.ts` (13 tests) covers the full precedence ladder, `review.command` → shell runner, fail-fast on unsupported `review.agent` (global & per-project), no regression when the worker agent is already `codex`, `buildClaudeCodeReviewArgs` argv, and `parseReviewerOutput` round-tripping claude-code-style plain + markdown-fenced JSON.

All existing tests pass (core 1353, cli 905); `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm lint` are green.

title: fix(claude-code): anchor workspace hook command paths to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
body:
## Problem

The Claude Code hook installer (`setupHookInWorkspace` in `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts`) wrote the hook `command` strings with **relative** script paths:

- POSIX: `.claude/metadata-updater.sh`, `.claude/activity-updater.sh`
- Windows: `node .claude/metadata-updater.cjs`, `node .claude/activity-updater.cjs`

Claude Code runs hook processes with an arbitrary working directory. As soon as a `Bash` tool command does `cd` into another directory, the hook process inherits that cwd, and the relative path no longer resolves. This surfaces as repeated non-blocking PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook errors:

```
.claude/activity-updater.sh: No such file or directory
.claude/metadata-updater.sh: No such file or directory
```

## Fix

Anchor all four command strings to the `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` environment variable that Claude Code sets for every hook process, quoted so paths containing spaces survive:

- POSIX: `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/metadata-updater.sh`, `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/activity-updater.sh`
- Windows: `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/metadata-updater.cjs`, `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/activity-updater.cjs`

The `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is written as a literal into the command string so the **shell** expands it at hook-run time (not at install time).

Note: the updater scripts themselves **already** resolve the workspace via `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` internally (with a `pwd` fallback). This change therefore only fixes **locating** the script file; it does not change the scripts' behavior.

## Tests

Updated the exact-string assertions in `src/index.test.ts` to the new anchored command strings. Build + full test suite pass (271 tests).

title: feat: configurable merge method with server-side fast-forward
body:
## Summary

Adds a per-project `mergeMethod` config option so users can choose how the dashboard merge action merges PRs. Default remains `"squash"` (backward compatible). Consumed by the dashboard merge route via `scm.mergePR`.

> **Note:** The `auto-merge` reaction is currently a notify-only stub and does not call `scm.mergePR`, so it does not consume `mergeMethod`. This option takes effect from the dashboard merge action.

### Strategies

| Method | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `squash` (default) | GitHub "Squash and merge" |
| `merge` | GitHub "Create a merge commit" |
| `rebase` | GitHub "Rebase and merge" |
| `merge-with-ff` | **AO composite strategy** (see below) |

### `merge-with-ff`

GitHub has **no fast-forward merge button** — `gh pr merge` only offers merge/squash/rebase, and `--merge` always creates a merge commit even when the branch could fast-forward. So `merge-with-ff` can't go through `gh pr merge`; it uses the Git Refs API directly:

1. Compare the PR head against base (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/compare/{base}...{head}`).
2. **If the branch is strictly ahead (no divergence):** fast-forward the base ref server-side — `PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}/git/refs/heads/{base}` with `force=false` (GitHub rejects anything that isn't a true fast-forward), then delete the head branch.
3. **If the branches have diverged:** fall back to a `--merge` commit.

This preserves linear history (no merge commit, no squash, no rebased SHAs) whenever possible.

### Config Usage

```yaml
projects:
  my-app:
    repo: owner/my-app
    path: ~/my-app
    mergeMethod: merge-with-ff   # fast-forward when possible, else merge commit
```

Options: `"squash"` (default), `"merge"`, `"rebase"`, `"merge-with-ff"`

## Files Changed

1. `packages/core/src/types.ts` — Add `"merge-with-ff"` to `MergeMethod` (with JSDoc), add `mergeMethod?` to `ProjectConfig`
2. `packages/core/src/config.ts` — Add `mergeMethod` to `ProjectConfigSchema` (default `"squash"`)
3. `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` — `mergePR()` implements `merge-with-ff` via compare + Git Refs fast-forward, else merge commit
4. `packages/plugins/scm-gitlab/src/index.ts` — `mergePR()` throws for the unsupported `"merge-with-ff"` (no GitLab equivalent) instead of silently ignoring it
5. `packages/web/src/app/api/prs/[id]/merge/route.ts` — Reads `project.mergeMethod` instead of hardcoding `"squash"`

## Tests

- `scm-github`: `merge-with-ff` fast-forwards via Git Refs API when ahead (and never touches `gh pr merge`); falls back to `--merge` when diverged
- `scm-gitlab`: `merge-with-ff` throws and never shells out to `glab`
- web merge route: defaults to `squash`; reads and passes through `project.mergeMethod`

## Caveats

- Branch protection that requires PRs/reviews/status checks before changes to the base branch will reject the server-side ref update (same wall a direct push hits).
- Fast-forwarding the base ref makes the head commits reachable from base; GitHub then marks the PR as merged.

Closes #2095
