title: ao start: show download/install progress (a silent fetch looks like a failure)
body:
## Problem

When `ao start` has to fetch the desktop app (no existing install resolved), it downloads a hundreds-of-MB release asset with zero output until the whole thing is done, then silently runs the install step. On anything but a fast connection this reads as a hang or a failure: the user sees `ao start`, then nothing, and assumes it broke. Encountered this directly while testing the fork `v0.10.4` build on Windows.

Asset sizes today:
- macOS zip ~112 MB
- Windows NSIS installer ~91 MB
- Linux AppImage ~120 MB

## Where

`backend/internal/cli/start.go`:
- `download()` streams `io.Copy(f, resp.Body)` with no progress reporting.
- `fetchAppDarwin` / `fetchAppWindows` / `fetchAppLinux` print nothing before the download, and nothing before the silent post-download step (`ditto` unpack on macOS, NSIS `/S` install on Windows).

So the entire fetch + install is invisible.

## Proposed

- Print a line before the download starts, e.g. `Downloading Agent Orchestrator (<asset>, ~NN MB) from <repo>...`.
- Show download progress during `io.Copy` (percentage when `Content-Length` is present, else bytes transferred). A small counting `io.Writer` / `io.TeeReader` wrapping the copy, writing to stderr. No new dependency.
- TTY-aware: a live progress bar / carriage-return updates on a terminal; degrade to a plain start/done line when stderr is not a TTY (CI, pipes), so logs do not fill with `\r` spam.
- Print a short line before the silent install/unpack step too (`Installing...`), since that is also a multi-second silent gap.

## Notes

- Keep it dependency-light: a hand-rolled progress reader is enough; no need for a progress-bar library.
- Only the fetch path needs this; the resolve-and-launch fast path (existing install) stays quiet.
- Relates to the broader first-run UX of the npm launcher.

## Severity

UX, but high-impact: the very first thing a new user does is `ao start`, and right now a normal slow download looks like a broken tool.

- exposes a **Run / Re-run migration** button hitting the idempotent `POST /api/v1/import` (safe when `completed`/`declined`/`failed`), so a user who chose **Don't Migrate** can redo it.

The choice persists to `~/.ao` and the existing auto-updater consumes it on the next launch / update check.

### #2234 — `ao start` download + install progress
`download()` streamed a hundreds-of-MB asset with zero output, then ran a silent install, so a slow fetch looked like a hang. Now (fetch path only; the resolve-and-launch fast path stays quiet):
- a start line `Downloading Agent Orchestrator (<asset>, ~NN MiB) from <repo>...` (size from `Content-Length` when present),
- a TTY-aware progress reader (`io.TeeReader` + a hand-rolled counting `io.Writer`): live `\r` percentage on a terminal, plain start + `Downloaded NN MiB.` lines off a TTY (CI/pipes, no `\r` spam),

Versioning happens via `frontend-release.yml`, so a changeset would be dead tooling here. Flagging in case the intent was to introduce changesets.

title: publish-feed blocked by scarce macos-13 Intel runner (feed never ships when Intel leg queues)
body:
## Problem

The `publish-feed` job (added in #2226) declares `needs: release`, which waits for **every** leg of the build matrix `[macos-latest, macos-13, windows-latest, ubuntu-latest]`. Because GitHub-hosted **Intel macOS (`macos-13`) runners are scarce and queue for a long time**, a single stuck Intel leg blocks the entire electron-updater feed (`latest*.yml` + `.blockmap` sidecars) from ever being uploaded, even when win/linux/mac-arm all built successfully.

Net effect: the feed (the whole point of auto-update) is hostage to the slowest, scarcest runner.

## Observed

Fork test run for `desktop-v0.10.4` (`harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator`, run 28290189501):
- `release (windows-latest)`, `release (ubuntu-latest)`, `release (macos-latest)` -> success.
- `release (macos-13)` -> **queued for 1h35m+** (no runner assigned).
- `publish-feed` -> never created (its `needs: release` gate is unmet), so **no `latest*.yml` published**.

So a release can have all its installers up and still ship no updater feed for hours, purely due to Intel-runner queueing.

## Where

- `.github/workflows/frontend-release.yml` and `.github/workflows/frontend-nightly.yml`: the `publish-feed` job's `needs: release`.
- `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`: `selectInstallers` already includes only the versioned installers actually present on the release, and `latest-mac.yml` lists whatever mac arch zips exist (the updater filters by the `arm64` url substring). So the feed generator already degrades gracefully to fewer assets; the gating is purely the workflow `needs`.

## Proposed

A few options, roughly in order of preference:

1. **Don't hard-block the feed on the Intel leg.** Let `publish-feed` run once the non-Intel legs finish and generate from whatever versioned assets are on the release. A missing Intel mac zip simply yields an arm64-only `latest-mac.yml` (Intel mac users don't auto-update until the Intel asset lands). Needs a way to re-run/refresh the feed when the Intel leg eventually completes (e.g. `publish-feed` also triggers on the Intel job finishing, or a manual re-dispatch).
2. **Make the Intel leg non-blocking** for the feed: split it into its own job that `publish-feed` does not `need`, or add a guard so `publish-feed` proceeds after the platforms that finished.
3. **Re-evaluate `macos-13` itself** given runner scarcity (#2216 added it for Intel `ao start` coverage) — weigh whether Intel mac is worth gating releases on, or should be best-effort.

## Severity

Important: blocks auto-update feed publication on stable + nightly whenever the Intel runner queues, which is frequent. The installers still publish, so it is not a total release failure, but the updater stays inert until the feed lands.

Related: #2226 (feed publishing), #2216 (added the `macos-13` Intel leg).

title: fix(ci): decouple macos-13 Intel runner from publish-feed (#2237)
body:
## What / why

Closes #2237. The `publish-feed` job declared `needs: release`, which waits for **every** leg of the build matrix including the scarce GitHub `macos-13` (Intel) runner. When that runner queues for hours, the entire electron-updater feed (`latest*.yml` + `.blockmap`) is blocked from publishing even though win/linux/mac-arm built successfully. Observed on the fork `v0.10.4` run: `macos-13` queued 1.5h+, `publish-feed` never started, no feed shipped.

## Change

Both `frontend-release.yml` and `frontend-nightly.yml`:

- **Remove `macos-13` from the `release` matrix** -> `[macos-latest, windows-latest, ubuntu-latest]`.
- **Add a non-blocking `release-intel` job** on `macos-13` that mirrors a macOS build leg (checkout, node 20, go, `macos-signing-setup`, `npm run publish`, the darwin-x64 stable-alias upload). In the nightly workflow it also carries `needs: guard`, `if: should_build`, the nightly version stamp, and `AO_RELEASE_PRERELEASE: "true"`.
- **`publish-feed` stays `needs: release`** (now satisfied by the three fast legs), so the feed publishes as soon as they finish.

The Intel installer + the `darwin-x64` alias still build and upload (for `ao start` and direct download). `feed.mjs` already generates the mac feed from whatever versioned mac zips are present, so `latest-mac.yml` is arm64-first and includes the x64 entry when `release-intel` happens to finish before `publish-feed`.

## Tradeoff

When the Intel runner lags, `latest-mac.yml` ships arm64-only until the next run, so Intel-mac users do not auto-update until the x64 entry lands. That is the accepted tradeoff in #2237 (option 1): the alternative is the entire feed blocked indefinitely on every release. The Intel installer itself is never blocked.

## Note

The macOS build steps are intentionally duplicated between `release` and `release-intel` (GitHub Actions cannot share a leg across a matrix boundary). Keep them in sync.

## Validation

- Both workflows parse (js-yaml load).
- Structural review: `macos-13` is out of both matrices, `release-intel` is a top-level job mirroring the macOS leg, `publish-feed` is unchanged and still `needs: release`. The rest is only verifiable on a real CI run.

title: Electron keeps stale project actions enabled after daemon exit and silently fails with AO daemon is not ready
body:
## Summary

If the Electron-managed daemon exits while the desktop app is still open, the renderer notices enough to stop showing project data, but it leaves project actions such as **New task** and **Spawn Orchestrator** clickable on the stale board route. Clicking **Spawn Orchestrator** produces no visible error or recovery path in the app and logs an unhandled rejection: `AO daemon is not ready`.

This makes daemon crash/restart recovery feel broken: the user is left on an apparently usable screen, but actions silently fail and there is no obvious **Restart daemon** / **Reconnect** affordance even though the Electron preload/main layer already exposes daemon start IPC.

## Reproduced on

- Repo: `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`
- Branch: `main`
- Commit: `77f33c28`
- Platform: macOS / Electron dev app
- Runtime state: isolated local QA state under `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260627-230707`
- Launch env:

```bash
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260627-230707/ao-data \
AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260627-230707/running.json \
AO_PORT=31021 \
AO_TELEMETRY_EVENTS=off \
AO_TELEMETRY_METRICS=off \
AO_TELEMETRY_REMOTE=off \
VITE_AO_POSTHOG_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:9 \
npm --prefix frontend run dev
```

## Repro steps

1. Start the Electron dev app with the isolated env above.
2. Add/open a disposable local git project.
3. Confirm the Electron UI is on a project board route and daemon-backed data is visible.
4. Kill the isolated daemon process listed in `AO_RUN_FILE` while leaving Electron open.
5. Wait for Electron to observe the daemon exit.
6. Click **Spawn Orchestrator** on the still-visible project board.

## Expected behavior

After the daemon exits, the UI should stop offering daemon-dependent actions or show a clear recovery state, for example:

- Disable **New task** / **Spawn Orchestrator** while daemon status is stopped.
- Show a visible **Restart daemon** / **Reconnect** action.
- Catch action failures and render an inline/toast error instead of producing an unhandled rejection.
- Preferably call the already-exposed `daemon.start` IPC when the user chooses recovery.

## Actual behavior

- The sidebar loses project data / shows the stopped state, but the project board route remains mounted.
- **New task** and **Spawn Orchestrator** remain clickable.
- Clicking **Spawn Orchestrator** gives no visible user-facing error.
- Dev logs show an unhandled renderer rejection:

```text
[vite] (client) [Unhandled rejection] Error: AO daemon is not ready.
```

## Screenshots / evidence

Before clicking: stale project board still exposes **New task** and **Spawn Orchestrator** after daemon exit.

![Stale project board still exposes New task and Spawn Orchestrator after daemon exit](https://files.catbox.moe/avbxfb.png)

After clicking **Spawn Orchestrator**: no visible app error; the failure only appears in logs.

![Spawn Orchestrator remains clickable and gives no visible recovery/error UI](https://files.catbox.moe/i918sm.png)

Local evidence files from the repro:

- `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260627-230707/evidence/06-daemon-stopped-project-actions-still-enabled-cropped.png`
- `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260627-230707/evidence/07-daemon-stopped-spawn-click-no-feedback-cropped.png`
- `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260627-230707/logs/electron-dev-tail-after-daemon-stopped-click.log`

Key log excerpt:

```text
[vite] (client) [Unhandled rejection] Error: AO daemon is not ready.
  > spawnOrchestrator src/renderer/lib/spawn-orchestrator.ts:16:8
  > openOrchestrator src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx:107:21
```

## Code pointers

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx`
  - `openOrchestrator` uses `try/finally` but has no `catch`, so daemon/API errors bubble into an unhandled rejection.
  - It also keeps board-level daemon-dependent actions available even after daemon status changes.
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/spawn-orchestrator.ts`
  - Throws the daemon/API error when `/api/v1/orchestrators` cannot run.
- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useDaemonStatus.ts`
  - Applies stopped/ready daemon status and keeps polling, but does not surface a recovery action to the route/action layer.
- `frontend/src/preload.ts`
  - Exposes `daemon.start()` and `daemon.stop()`.
- `frontend/src/main.ts`
  - Registers `ipcMain.handle("daemon:start", () => startDaemon())`, so the recovery primitive already exists.

## Duplicate / overlap check

I checked current open issues and PRs before filing.

Nearby but not the same:

- #2230 is about optionally keeping the daemon alive after the desktop app closes. This issue is about in-app recovery after the daemon dies while Electron remains open.
- #2156 is a broad QA/live-gate tracker for resilience testing, not this specific user-visible failure path.

No exact open issue or PR was found for the stale Electron actions + unhandled `AO daemon is not ready` flow.

## Contribution value

This is a good focused bug because it is:

- User-visible in the real Electron app.
- Reproducible without private credentials or GitHub writes.
- A resilience/onboarding problem that users can hit during local dev, daemon crashes, manual kills, or app/dev-server restarts.
- Likely fixable in one focused PR around daemon status gating, action error handling, and/or exposing a restart CTA using the existing IPC.

title: fix(update): bundle app-update.yml so electron-updater can install (forge omits it)
body:
## What / why

Critical auto-update bug: electron-updater detects a release but crashes during download/install with `ENOENT ... Contents/Resources/app-update.yml`. electron-forge (unlike electron-builder) never generates `app-update.yml`, which electron-updater requires at runtime. The #2221 design assumed `setFeedURL(...)` alone was enough; a real fork build's log disproves it:

```
Checking for update
Found version 0.10.6 (url: Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.10.6.zip)
Downloading update from Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.10.6.zip
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/app-update.yml'
```

This affects every forge build, prod included: updates are found but never install.

## Fix

- **`forge.config.ts`**: a `postPackage` hook writes `app-update.yml` (provider github + owner/repo from the existing `parseReleaseRepo(AO_RELEASE_REPO)` + `updaterCacheDirName`) into each packaged app's resources dir (mac: `<App>.app/Contents/Resources`, win/linux: `resources/`). The repo is baked at build time, so a build auto-updates from whatever repo it was published to.
- **`auto-updater.ts`**: drop the runtime `setFeedURL`/`repo()` override (which read the absent `AO_RELEASE_REPO` env and wrongly defaulted to prod in installed apps). `configureFeed` now only sets channel + `allowDowngrade`; electron-updater loads the bundled `app-update.yml`. This also removes the need for any runtime env to point a fork build at the fork.

## Verification

- typecheck clean; `update-settings` vitest green.
- The packaged-app write is CI-verifiable only (local `npm run package` is a no-op on the build host, pre-existing). Validated by a fresh fork build: confirm `app-update.yml` is in the `.app` and an installed older build updates to completion.

title: fix(import): surface legacy store parse errors instead of swallowing them
body:
Closes #2186.

## Background

`ao import` reported **"No legacy AO projects found"** for a legacy store that actually contained projects but failed to parse, because `HasLegacyData` collapsed every error (including a YAML parse failure) into a bare `false`. A user with a valid store was told there was nothing to import, with no hint of the underlying schema drift.

The issue described two bugs:
1. **`repo:` typed as `string`** while the legacy schema (what `ao project add` writes) stores it as a mapping → `yaml.Unmarshal` fails.
2. **The parse error was swallowed**, surfacing as the misleading "nothing to import".

**Bug 1 already landed** in #2219 (which changed `Repo` to `*yaml.Node` and made `loadLegacyConfig` tolerate type errors), but with **no regression test** and **no reference to this issue**, so #2186 stayed open. This PR adds the missing regression test and fixes the still-open Bug 2.

## Changes

- `HasLegacyData` now returns `(bool, error)`: a missing store is `(false, nil)`; a store that exists but fails to parse returns the parse error so callers can distinguish "nothing to import" from "the store is unreadable".
- `ao import` surfaces that error instead of printing the misleading message.
- The import **service** `Status` keeps its documented "never errors on a missing/unreadable store" contract (the CLI is the diagnostic path).

## Tests
- `TestRun_ObjectFormRepo` — regression guard for the object-form `repo:` mapping (Bug 1).
- `TestHasLegacyData_ParseErrorSurfaced` — covers the new error path (Bug 2).

## Note

## Why
The Desktop release workflow triggers on any `desktop-v*` tag push (or `workflow_dispatch`) and consumes the repo-level macOS signing secrets. There is no tag protection and no environment gate, so **any of the ~10 write-access collaborators can cut a fully signed, notarized production build** to ~7.6k users. Adds `environment: release` to the `release` and `release-intel` jobs so the build that uses the signing secrets cannot run until a **required reviewer approves** the deployment to the `release` environment.

title: Missing tmux makes task spawn return generic Internal Server Error and leave a terminated worker
body:
## Summary

On macOS/Linux, worker/orchestrator sessions depend on `tmux`, but the app does not treat a missing `tmux` binary as a hard prerequisite before spawn. If `tmux` is not installed, starting a worker returns only a generic `Internal server error` to the client and still leaves a terminated worker session behind.

This is confusing in first-run/local-dev onboarding: the real cause is actionable (`tmux` missing), but the UI/API do not surface it, and the board gains a failed terminated task that looks like the agent itself exited.

## Reproduced on

- Repo: `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`
- Branch: `main`
- Commit: `01406edd`
- Platform: macOS / Electron dev app
- Environment condition: `tmux` is not present in `PATH`
- Runtime state: isolated QA state under `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260628-tmux`

Launch env used for the repro:

```bash
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260628-tmux/ao-data \
AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260628-tmux/running.json \
AO_PORT=31031 \
AO_TELEMETRY_EVENTS=off \
AO_TELEMETRY_METRICS=off \
AO_TELEMETRY_REMOTE=off \
VITE_AO_POSTHOG_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:9 \
npm --prefix frontend run dev
```

## Repro steps

1. Use a macOS/Linux machine where `tmux` is not installed or not in `PATH`.
2. Start the Electron dev app with isolated daemon state.
3. Register a disposable local git repo as a project.
4. Spawn a worker task through the New Task flow or directly through `POST /api/v1/sessions`.
5. Inspect the API response, daemon log, and project board.

The worker spawn body used in this repro:

```json
{
  "projectId": "tmux-missing-demo",
  "issueId": "QA missing tmux worker",
  "kind": "worker",
  "harness": "codex",
  "prompt": "Please inspect the README and stop. Do not modify files."
}
```

## Expected behavior

AO should fail before creating a session row, with a clear actionable message such as:

```text
tmux is required to start sessions on macOS/Linux but was not found in PATH.
```

Possible acceptable behavior:

- `ao doctor` should fail, not warn, when the selected runtime requires `tmux`.
- The Electron app should surface the missing prerequisite before task/orchestrator spawn.
- `POST /api/v1/sessions` should return a typed 4xx or structured runtime-prerequisite error instead of a generic 500.
- No terminated worker row should be left behind for a spawn that never reached the runtime.

## Actual behavior

The spawn request returns a generic 500:

```json
{"error":"internal","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal server error","requestId":"Swyams-MacBook-Pro.local/hBuUnvDUiv-000026"}
```

The daemon log contains the real cause:

```text
time=2026-06-28T11:47:50.045+05:30 level=INFO msg="http request" id=Swyams-MacBook-Pro.local/hBuUnvDUiv-000026 method=POST path=/api/v1/sessions status=500 bytes=136 duration=110.67975ms remote=127.0.0.1:57851 error="spawn tmux-missing-demo-1: runtime: tmux runtime: create session tmux-missing-demo-1: exec: \"tmux\": executable file not found in $PATH"
```

The sessions API then shows a terminated worker was created anyway:

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "id": "tmux-missing-demo-1",
      "projectId": "tmux-missing-demo",
      "issueId": "QA missing tmux worker",
      "kind": "worker",
      "harness": "codex",
      "activity": {
        "state": "exited",
        "lastActivityAt": "2026-06-28T06:17:50.04529Z"
      },
      "isTerminated": true,
      "status": "terminated",
      "prs": []
    }
  ]
}
```

## Local evidence files

No screenshots are attached here per request; the useful evidence is in logs/API output:

- `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260628-tmux/logs/api-spawn-worker.json`
- `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260628-tmux/logs/api-sessions-after-spawn-error.json`
- `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260628-tmux/logs/electron-dev-tail-after-spawn-error.log`
- `/tmp/agent-orchestrator-qa-20260628-tmux/logs/api-spawn-worker-request.json`

## Code pointers

- `README.md`
  - Lists `tmux` as optional under prerequisites, even though the selected Unix runtime requires it to start sessions.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/runtimeselect/runtimeselect.go`
  - `New` selects the tmux runtime for every non-Windows platform.
- `backend/internal/cli/doctor.go`
  - `checkTmux` reports missing `tmux` as a warning, not a failure.
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`
  - `Spawn` creates the session row before runtime creation.
  - Runtime creation failure calls `markSpawnFailedTerminated`, leaving a terminated session row.
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope/envelope.go`
  - Non-typed service errors fall back to `INTERNAL_ERROR` / `Internal server error`, hiding the actionable missing-binary cause from the client.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx`
  - The UI renders the generic API message, so the user sees `Internal server error` instead of the missing `tmux` requirement.

## Duplicate / overlap check

Searched open issues/PRs for:

- `missing tmux`
- `tmux missing`
- `tmux runtime`
- `tmux not found`
- `executable file not found in $PATH`

Nearby but not the same:

- #2093 has a similar “internal server” title, but its body is a different old Next.js/file URL error.
- Existing tmux/session lifecycle issues cover runtime probes, restore, reconnect loops, or tmux process behavior after sessions exist. They do not cover the missing-`tmux` first-run prerequisite failure path that returns a generic 500 and leaves a terminated worker row.

## Why this is worth fixing

This is a good focused contribution because it is:

- User-visible in first-run/local-dev flows.
- Reproducible without private credentials or GitHub writes.
- Actionable: the real fix is likely a small combination of prerequisite detection, typed error propagation, and/or avoiding durable session rows before runtime prerequisites are satisfied.
- Cross-platform relevant: macOS/Linux use tmux; Windows uses ConPTY and is not affected the same way.

title: feat: implement collision detection and management for cross-session edits
body:
## What & Why

Closes #2258.

Agent Orchestrator's core premise is running many agents in parallel, each in its own isolated Git worktree. That isolation has a blind spot: two agents can silently modify the **same code** without knowing about each other.

Today, AO only detects this **reactively**—after both agents have opened PRs and GitHub reports a merge conflict. At that point, `lifecycle.ApplyPRObservation` can only nudge an agent to rebase, meaning the duplicate parallel work has already been done.

**Convergence Radar** closes this gap.

It introduces a new observation loop that continuously diffs every active worktree, computes pairwise overlap at both **file** and **hunk-range** granularity, persists those overlaps as durable facts, and proactively nudges colliding agents to coordinate **before** either opens a PR.

Rather than being a bolt-on feature, it follows AO's existing architecture. The convergence observer is a sibling of the SCM observer, reusing `observe.StartPollLoop`, the durable-facts model, and the existing agent nudge pipeline. The result shifts AO from a conflict resolver into a conflict preventer.

## How It Works (OBSERVE → UPDATE → ACT)

### OBSERVE

`ports.WorkspaceDiffer.ChangedRegions` diffs each worktree against the merge-base of `HEAD` and its base branch, including both committed and uncommitted tracked changes. It parses `git diff --unified=0` hunk headers into per-file line ranges.

### UPDATE

The convergence observer groups active sessions by project, compares every pair of worktrees, and classifies shared files as:

* **Hot** — overlapping line ranges intersect, indicating a near-certain merge conflict.
* **Soft** — both sessions modify the same file, but their changed ranges are disjoint.

The observer reconciles durable `session_collision` facts. A content signature ensures stable overlaps are written only once and re-evaluated only when the underlying changes actually differ.

### ACT

`lifecycle.ApplyCollision` sends each affected live session a deduplicated coordination nudge identifying the peer session and the overlapping files.

Current collisions are also exposed via:

`GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/collisions`

## Surface Area

### New

* `internal/observe/convergence`
* `internal/daemon/convergence_wiring.go`
* `domain.SessionCollision`
* Migration `0020_session_collisions`
* SQLC queries and store
* `ports.WorkspaceDiffer`
* `ports.LineRange`

### Extended

* Git worktree adapter (diff capability)
* Lifecycle reactions
* Project service
* `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/collisions` controller
* OpenAPI specification
* Generated TypeScript types

### Architectural Notes

The implementation follows existing AO patterns:

* Durable facts only (status is derived at read time)
* Loopback-only observation
* No manual CDC
* Code-first regeneration via:

  * `npm run sqlc`
  * `npm run api`

## Testing

Validated with:

* `go build ./...`
* `go vet`
* `gofmt` clean across all modified packages
* `go test -race` passing for every touched package, including spec parity/drift tests

New test coverage includes:

* Diff parser
* Overlap classification
* Observer reconciliation
* Deduplication
* Agent nudging
* Lifecycle deduplication
* Store round-trip
* Controller endpoint

## Notes / Follow-ups

* The desktop **⚡ Overlaps** chip is intentionally deferred as a lightweight follow-up built on the new endpoint and derived facts.
* Live user feedback is provided through agent nudges and the read endpoint. V1 intentionally avoids the `change_log` / notifications `CHECK`-constraint table rebuild migrations.
* Existing unrelated failures remain unchanged:

  * tmux integration test (tmux unavailable in the CI sandbox)
  * `TestManager_AddWorkspaceRejectsBareParent` (currently fails on clean `main` with newer Git)

body:
Issue

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4eed2d6-4e3d-4882-9757-e939bf5182dc

 ### Bug Description:

  While trying to scroll down to see the complete list of worker and orchestrator agents in the dropdown, the list would automatically snap back to the top every few seconds, causing a bad user
  experience.

 ### Cause & Fix:

  This issue occurred because the Radix UI  <Select>  component uses an  item-aligned  positioning strategy by default. Whenever the UI received live background updates (like workspace status
  broadcasts), the parent component re-rendered. This caused the dropdown to recalculate its alignment and reset the scroll position to the top.

### After the fix


wrapped the  RequiredAgentField  component with  React.memo . This ensures the dropdown component isolates itself from unrelated parent re-renders caused by background SSE events. The component now only re-renders when the actual agent selection changes, preserving the user's scroll position while maintaining the correct native alignment.

title: ci(nightly): don't gate the nightly feed on the flaky Intel leg
body:
## Problem
Every recent nightly failed, so the nightly update channel 404s (`nightly-mac.yml` not found). Root cause: `publish-feed` was set to `needs: [guard, release, release-intel]`, so **any** Intel-leg hiccup skips the entire nightly feed, for all platforms.

The Intel macOS leg is genuinely flaky:
- transient notary `-1009 "connection offline"` reaching Apple, and
- `osx-sign` keychain races → `Agent Orchestrator.app: code object is not signed at all`.

Both pass on re-run, but a **daily, unattended** nightly shouldn't need a manual re-run to publish anything.

## Fix
Revert nightly's `publish-feed` to `needs: [guard, release]` (its pre-#2244 state):
- arm64 / Windows / Linux nightlies publish **every day regardless of Intel**.
- `feed.mjs` still includes the x64 entry **when the Intel leg finishes in time** (best-effort).

The **stable** release stays gated on Intel , it's manual, re-runnable, and verified, so guaranteeing x64 in the stable feed is worth the gate there. Different reliability needs: stable = correctness, nightly = resilience.

title: fix(update): nightly channel never resolves (missing allowPrerelease)
body:
## Problem
On the **nightly** channel the app 404s:
`Cannot find nightly-mac.yml in the latest release artifacts (.../releases/download/v0.10.0/nightly-mac.yml)`

Nightly builds publish as GitHub **prereleases**, but `configureFeed` set `autoUpdater.channel` and `allowDowngrade` and **never set `allowPrerelease`**. With `allowPrerelease` at its default `false`, electron-updater only inspects the latest **non-prerelease** release (`v0.10.0`) and looks for `nightly-mac.yml` there → 404. So the nightly channel never resolved, even with a valid nightly published.

## Fix
```ts
autoUpdater.allowPrerelease = channel === "nightly";
```
Nightly scans prereleases (finds the `*-nightly-*` feed); stable stays on non-prereleases only.

## Note
Ships in the next desktop release. The currently-installed `v0.10.0` can't self-heal on nightly (that's the bug), users on nightly should switch to Stable once to pick up the build that contains this fix, then nightly works.

title: ci: retry transient macOS sign/notary flakes in the publish step
body:
## Why
Releases fail intermittently on **transient** macOS issues that hit **either** macOS leg, not just Intel:
- Apple notary `-1009 "connection appears to be offline"` , observed on **`macos-latest` (arm64)** in the stable `v0.10.0` run (attempt 1: `release (macos-latest)` failed, `release-intel` succeeded).
- `osx-sign` keychain race → `code object is not signed at all` , observed on **`macos-15-intel`** in the nightly run.

Both pass on a manual re-run. The flakiness is general (Apple/runner), so decoupling only the Intel leg (#2264) doesn't fix it , an arm64 flake still fails `needs: release` and skips the feed.

## Fix
Wrap `npm run publish` in a 3× retry with 30s backoff across all four publish steps (release + release-intel, in both release and nightly workflows). Transient sign/notary failures self-heal in-place. The Intel leg stays coupled, so the x64 feed entry remains guaranteed.

Supersedes #2264.

title: CLI E2E "Fresh-install check (container)" fails on main: ao start now succeeds because v0.10.0 ships a fetchable Linux asset
body:
## Summary
The `container` job of **CLI E2E** ("Fresh-install check") is red on `main` since the `v0.10.0` release went live. `test/cli/install-check.sh` asserts that `ao start` must **fail** on a fresh machine with no installed app, but AgentWrapper's latest release now ships `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage`, so `ao start` on amd64 fetches it and exits 0:

```
FAIL: start unexpectedly succeeded on a fresh machine with no installed app
```

## Evidence
- Passing at commit `ff23e6605` (CI 17:55 UTC), before `v0.10.0` existed.
- Failing at commit `6b56b1c24` (CI 22:07 UTC), after `v0.10.0` was published (~18:13 UTC). Failing run: https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/28337608621
- Only the `container` leg fails; native macOS/Windows/Linux legs pass. The change merged in between (#2265, `auto-updater.ts`) is unrelated.

## Root cause
`test/cli/install-check.sh:31-34` assumes no published asset exists for the platform, so the download 404s and `ao start` exits non-zero. That assumption was only true before the first real AgentWrapper release. Now the `ao start` alias downloads successfully on amd64 and `start` proceeds, exiting 0.

## Suggested fix
Make the check independent of live release state, e.g.:
- Point it at a repo/tag with no assets (`AO_RELEASE_REPO=<empty/nonexistent>`) so the fetch deterministically 404s, or
- Assert the new correct fresh-box behavior (download + launch attempt) instead of "must fail", or
- Stub the network so the fetch path is exercised hermetically.

## Impact
Red CLI E2E on every `main` commit / PR. Not a product/runtime bug, the CLI behaves correctly; the test is stale.

title: fix(ci): Windows publish shell + fresh-install smoke check (#2267)
body:
Two CI fixes.

## 1. Windows publish fails to parse (regression from #2266)

The 3x publish retry added in #2266 is bash (`for i in 1 2 3; do ... done`), but the `release` matrix Publish step had no explicit `shell:`. On `windows-latest` the default shell is PowerShell, so the step failed deterministically:

```
ParserError: Missing opening '(' after keyword 'for'.
```

Every Windows publish (stable and nightly) breaks; this is what failed the v0.10.1 cut. macOS/Ubuntu passed only because their default shell is already bash. Fix: pin `shell: bash` on all four Publish steps (release + release-intel + nightly + nightly-intel). Git Bash ships on `windows-latest`.

Verified green end to end on a fork run of the full Desktop release workflow: all legs including `release (windows-latest)` succeeded and published the Windows `.exe` plus the `latest*.yml` feed.

## 2. Fresh-install smoke check is red on main (#2267)

The container check asserts `ao start` fails cleanly on a fresh box "with no published asset". Now that AgentWrapper publishes a `linux-x64.AppImage`, the unpinned smoke binary downloads it and exits 0, tripping the assertion. Fix: build the smoke binary against a release repo with no assets, so the fetch path deterministically 404s and `start` exits non-zero with a clear error, preserving the test's intent without depending on what the real repo publishes.

Fixes #2267.

title: Auto-updater: don't propagate 'Cannot find latest-mac.yml' 404 to users
body:
## Problem

The Electron auto-updater surfaces a raw `electron-updater` error to users when it can't find `latest-mac.yml` in a release's artifacts. This is a scary, technical 404 that looks like an auth/security failure, but it's really just a missing/incomplete release manifest. It should **not** be propagated to users as an error dialog.

## Observed error

```
Cannot find latest-mac.yml in the latest release artifacts
(https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/releases/download/v0.10.1/latest-mac.yml):
HttpError: 404 "method: GET url: https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/releases/download/v0.10.1/latest-mac.yml

Please double check that your authentication token is correct. Due to security reasons,
actual status maybe not reported, but 404."
    at e.ElectronHttpExecutor.handleResponse (app.asar/.vite/build/main.js)
    at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (app.asar/.vite/build/main.js)
    ...
```

Release: `v0.10.1`. The `latest-mac.yml` update manifest is absent from the release assets, so `electron-updater`'s `checkForUpdates` rejects with a 404 the user never needs to see.

## Impact

- A routine "no update manifest yet" condition is shown to end users as a security/auth error.
- The wording ("double check that your authentication token is correct") is misleading: it's GitHub's generic 404 text, not an actual auth problem.

## Asks

1. **Do not propagate update-check failures to users.** Swallow/log `checkForUpdates` rejections (especially 404 on the `*.yml` manifest) instead of showing an error dialog. Auto-update failing should be silent/log-only; only *successful* update availability or an explicit user-initiated check should produce UI.
2. **Root cause:** ensure releases actually publish `latest-mac.yml` (and the equivalent `latest.yml` / `latest-linux.yml`) so the manifest 404 stops happening in the first place. Investigate why `v0.10.1` shipped without it.

## Notes

- Reported from a packaged build (`/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app`), macOS.

title: Nightly channel should also receive newer stable releases
body:
## Problem

A user on the **nightly** channel should always run the newest build available, whether it came from a nightly or a stable cut. Today they only track the nightly feed, so a newer **stable** release does not reach them and can even surface as a 404.

## Current behavior

`frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts` sets, for the nightly channel:

- `autoUpdater.channel = "nightly"` -> electron-updater reads `nightly-mac.yml` (the channel file)
- `autoUpdater.allowPrerelease = true` -> it picks the newest release across stable + prereleases

`frontend/scripts/feed.mjs` only emits `nightly*.yml` on nightly releases and `latest*.yml` on stable releases. So when the newest release is a **stable** one, a nightly client selects it, then looks for `nightly-mac.yml` in that stable release and 404s (stable publishes only `latest*.yml`).

In normal cadence this is hidden, because nightlies are stamped `X.Y.(Z+1)-nightly.*` and are always ahead of stable. It bites whenever a stable is cut that is newer than the latest nightly, e.g. right after the 0.10.1 stable cut: the newest nightly is `0.10.1-nightly.*` which is now semver-older than stable `0.10.1`, so nightly users 404 until the next `0.10.2-nightly` is built.

## Desired behavior

Nightly channel = max(latest nightly, latest stable). A nightly user gets a newer stable automatically, and never downgrades.

## Proposed approach (one option)

Have **stable** releases also publish the nightly channel feed files (`nightly-mac.yml` / `nightly.yml` / `nightly-linux.yml`) as copies of the `latest*.yml` content. Then a nightly client that selects the newest stable release finds `nightly-mac.yml` there and updates onto stable.

- No downgrade risk: electron-updater's newest-release selection already encodes the max, so the stable file is only chosen when stable >= the user's installed nightly. `allowDowngrade = true` stays only for explicit channel switches.
- Stable users are unaffected: channel `latest` + `allowPrerelease = false` reads only `latest*.yml` from non-prerelease releases and never touches the nightly file.

Mechanically this is small: call `feed.mjs` for both channels on the stable publish-feed step (`.github/workflows/frontend-release.yml`), or add a flag so a stable run emits both `latest*` and `nightly*`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A nightly-channel client with no newer nightly available updates to a newer stable release (no 404).
- A nightly-channel client on a newer nightly than stable stays on the nightly (no downgrade).
- Stable-channel clients never pull a prerelease.
- Verified end to end on the fork release target before shipping.

title: Enrich worker and orchestrator system prompts
body:
## Problem

The Go rewrite currently gives worker and orchestrator sessions only very thin system prompts.

Current behavior:
- Worker prompt is mostly the raw user prompt.
- Worker system prompt only includes orchestrator contact instructions, if an active orchestrator exists, plus multi-PR branch guidance.
- Orchestrator system prompt only includes a small coordinator role block with `ao spawn` and `ao send`.
- `--issue` is passed as `AO_ISSUE_ID`, but the issue title/body/labels/URL are not fetched or injected.
- Project prompt rules from the old AO (`agentRules`, `agentRulesFile`, `orchestratorRules`) are not modeled in `ProjectConfig`.
- Normal spawn passes inline `SystemPrompt` only, so adapters that require `SystemPromptFile` miss the prompt.

We need to restore a richer prompt-enrichment layer for both workers and orchestrators, adapted to the current Go daemon/CLI surface.

## Goal

Add two main generated system prompts:

1. Worker system prompt
2. Orchestrator system prompt

Also add one optional generated task prompt when a worker is spawned with `--issue` but no explicit `--prompt`.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Add a dedicated prompt builder

Create a focused prompt-building module, for example:

- `backend/internal/session_manager/prompts.go`, or
- `backend/internal/prompt/`

The builder should return structured prompt output:

```go
type SpawnTexts struct {
    Prompt           string
    SystemPrompt     string
    SystemPromptFile string
}
```

Keep user task prompt and standing system prompt separate.

### 2. Enrich worker system prompt

Worker prompt should include:

- Worker role and expected behavior.
- Current AO workflow using only commands that exist in the Go rewrite.
- Project context:
  - project id
  - display name
  - repo path
  - repo origin URL
  - default branch
  - session branch namespace guidance
- Orchestrator coordination:
  - include active orchestrator session id if present
  - include exact `ao send --session <id> --message "<message>"` usage
- PR workflow:
  - branch namespace rules
  - multi-PR rules
  - stacked PR rules
  - `ao session claim-pr` / `ao spawn --claim-pr` guidance where relevant
- Issue context, if available:
  - issue id
  - title
  - URL
  - state
  - labels
  - assignees
  - body
- Project-specific worker rules:
  - `agentRules`
  - `agentRulesFile`

Issue body must be clearly marked as untrusted external content. The agent should use it as task context, not as higher-priority instructions.

### 3. Add optional issue fallback task prompt

If worker spawn has `IssueID` but no explicit `Prompt`, generate a small task prompt like:

```txt
Work on issue <issue-id>. Use the issue context in your standing instructions.
```

Do not duplicate the full issue body in the task prompt. Keep full issue details in the system prompt.

### 4. Enrich orchestrator system prompt

Replace the current small orchestrator prompt with a richer template.

It should include:

- Coordinator role:
  - orchestrator coordinates work for the human
  - implementation should usually be delegated to workers
  - only do direct implementation for small coordination fixes or emergencies
- Project context:
  - project id
  - display name
  - repo path
  - repo origin URL
  - default branch
- Worker management:
  - how to spawn workers
  - how to write clear worker prompts
  - how to message workers
  - how to inspect session state
- Current valid AO commands:
  - `ao spawn`
  - `ao send`
  - `ao session ls`
  - `ao session get`
  - `ao session claim-pr`
  - `ao session restore`
  - `ao session kill`
  - `ao orchestrator ls`
  - `ao preview`
- PR/review/CI coordination guidance:
  - track worker PRs
  - avoid duplicate workers on the same PR unless intentionally taking over
  - synthesize results for the user
- Project-specific orchestrator rules:
  - `orchestratorRules`

Do not copy old AO commands that no longer exist, such as old `ao report` workflows.

### 5. Add project config fields

Extend `domain.ProjectConfig` with:

```go
AgentRules        string `json:"agentRules,omitempty"`
AgentRulesFile    string `json:"agentRulesFile,omitempty"`
OrchestratorRules string `json:"orchestratorRules,omitempty"`
```

Then update:

- config validation
- project API DTOs
- OpenAPI spec
- generated frontend schema
- CLI project config mirror types
- legacy importer so these fields are preserved instead of dropped

Run:

```bash
npm run api
```

### 6. Wire issue lookup into spawn prompt enrichment

Use the existing `ports.Tracker` / `domain.Issue` model.

When `SpawnConfig.IssueID` is set:

- resolve it into a `domain.TrackerID`
- fetch issue data through tracker
- include fetched issue context in the worker system prompt
- if lookup fails, do not fail spawn unless the failure is a clear validation/config error
- include a small fallback note saying issue details could not be fetched

This should happen at spawn-time, not dashboard polling time.

### 7. Materialize system prompt files

Do not store generated prompt text in a new DB table.

Generate prompt text at spawn/restore time and write a prompt file under `~/.ao`, for example:

```txt
~/.ao/prompts/<session-id>/system.md
```

Pass both fields to adapters:

```go
SystemPrompt: systemPrompt
SystemPromptFile: systemPromptFile
```

This improves compatibility with adapters that prefer or require files.

### 8. Fix adapter delivery gaps

At minimum:

- Aider should receive the prompt via `SystemPromptFile`.
- Codex/Claude/Amp/etc. should continue working.
- OpenCode needs explicit support, likely through config/instructions file or workspace `AGENTS.md`, because it currently ignores both inline and file system prompts.

For adapters that cannot support system prompt injection, document the limitation clearly.

### 9. Tests

Add/update tests for:

- worker prompt includes project context
- worker prompt includes active orchestrator contact when present
- worker prompt includes issue details when tracker lookup succeeds
- worker spawn with issue and no prompt gets fallback task prompt
- issue body is marked as untrusted content
- orchestrator prompt includes project context and valid command list
- project config accepts `agentRules`, `agentRulesFile`, `orchestratorRules`
- legacy import preserves prompt-rule fields
- `SystemPromptFile` is passed to launch config
- Aider receives prompt file path
- API spec/schema are regenerated

## Acceptance Criteria

- Worker sessions receive enriched system prompts.
- Orchestrator sessions receive enriched system prompts.
- Issue-backed worker sessions include issue title/body/labels/URL when available.
- Project-level worker and orchestrator rules are supported.
- Prompt text is generated at spawn/restore time, not persisted in a DB table.
- Prompt files are written under `~/.ao`.
- Existing prompt confidentiality guard still applies.
- No old/unsupported AO commands are included in generated prompts.

title: fix: deliver generated system prompt files
body:
Fixes #2272
Refs #2371

## Summary
- Materialize generated session system prompts under the AO data dir at `prompts/<session-id>/system.md`, with cleanup on failed spawn, kill, delete, restore failure, and cleanup paths.
- Prefer inline system-prompt delivery when an adapter supports it, while still keeping the prompt file for file-based/fallback paths.
- Pass both `SystemPrompt` and `SystemPromptFile` through fresh launch, native restore, and restore fallback launch configs so supported adapters retain AO standing instructions.
- Re-apply system-prompt flags on native restore for Codex, Cline, Qwen, Droid, Amp, Auggie, Pi, and Goose; document/test explicit exceptions for Aider and Autohand.
- Add worker task prompts for `--issue` spawns, keeping issue details in the task prompt and out of the system prompt.
- Hydrate `IssueContext` in the session service from the daemon-wired GitHub tracker before spawning workers, with graceful fallback when tracker context is unavailable.

## Tests
- focused adapter/session-manager restore tests
- `go test ./internal/service/session ./internal/session_manager ./internal/daemon`
- `cd backend && go test ./...`
- `npm run lint`
- PR CI is green

## Known risks / follow-ups
- Tracker-backed issue context is best-effort and requires `AO_GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`; when unavailable, workers retain the existing issue-only fallback prompt.
- #2371 remains the broader follow-up for an explicit adapter system-prompt capability matrix plus warning/error behavior for adapters that cannot deliver AO system prompts.

title: fix(conpty): avoid integer overflow in payload size validation
body:
## Summary

Fixes a Windows build failure in `EncodeMessage` caused by comparing `len(payload)` with `math.MaxUint32`.

`len()` returns an `int`, and on Windows this comparison can trigger an integer overflow compilation error due to implicit type conversion.

This change replaces the comparison with explicit `uint64` conversions and removes the now-unused `math` import.

## Changes

* Added a typed `maxPayloadSize` constant using `^uint32(0)`
* Replaced the payload size comparison with explicit `uint64` conversion
* Removed the unused `math` import
* Preserved existing protocol behavior and validation logic

## Why this fix

The previous implementation relied on implicit type handling between `int` and `math.MaxUint32`, which caused platform-dependent compilation issues on Windows.

Using explicit `uint64` comparison avoids architecture-specific integer overflow behavior while keeping the original bounds check intact.

## Verification

Tested successfully on:

* Windows 11
* Go 1.25

Build command used:

```bash
go build ./cmd/ao/main.go
```

title: New task dialog ignores the project's default agent and can only spawn 4 of 23 supported agents
body:
### Summary
The **New task** dialog always sends a hardcoded `harness` (defaulting to `codex`) and only exposes 4 of the 23 supported agents. This silently overrides the project's configured **default worker agent**, and makes it impossible to spawn the other 19 agents from the quick-create flow — even though the daemon fully supports them and is explicitly designed to inherit the project default when `harness` is omitted.

### Expected behavior
- The agent selector should default to the project's configured **default worker agent**, not a hardcoded `codex`.
- All supported agents (the 23 in the spawn enum) should be selectable — or, when the user hasn't explicitly chosen one, the request should omit `harness` so the daemon applies the project default.

### Actual behavior
- The dropdown always opens on **Codex**, regardless of the project's configured default worker agent.
- Submitting without changing it spawns **Codex**, ignoring the configured default.
- Only **Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Aider** are selectable. If a project's default is any other agent (Cursor, Amp, Goose, etc.), there is **no way** to launch it from New task, and it silently spawns Codex instead.

### Root cause
The frontend defeats a backend design that already supports project-default inheritance:

1. **`harness` is optional on the API.** `SpawnSessionRequest.Harness` is `json:"harness,omitempty"` with a 23-value enum.
   `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go:146`

2. **The daemon falls back to the project default when `harness` is empty.**
   ```go
   func effectiveHarness(explicit domain.AgentHarness, kind domain.SessionKind, cfg domain.ProjectConfig) domain.AgentHarness {
       if explicit != "" {
           return explicit
       }
       if role := roleOverride(kind, cfg).Harness; role != "" {
           return role // project's worker/orchestrator default agent
       }
       return ""
   }
   ```
   `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:320`

3. **But the dialog hardcodes the agent list to 4 entries:**
   ```ts
   const AGENTS = [
     { value: "codex", label: "Codex" },
     { value: "claude-code", label: "Claude Code" },
     { value: "opencode", label: "OpenCode" },
     { value: "aider", label: "Aider" },
   ];
   ```
   `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx:17`

4. **defaults the selection to `codex` without reading project config:**
   `const [agent, setAgent] = useState<AgentProvider>("codex");` — `NewTaskDialog.tsx:31`

5. **and always sends it explicitly**, so the daemon's fallback never runs:
   ```ts
   body: { projectId, kind: "worker", harness: agent, issueId: cleanTitle, prompt: cleanPrompt, branch: cleanBranch || undefined }
   ```
   `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx:65`

### Steps to reproduce
**A — default agent ignored:**
1. Open **Project Settings**, set **Default worker agent** to e.g. *Claude Code*. Save.
2. Go to the board → **New task**.
3. Note the Agent dropdown shows **Codex**, not Claude Code.
4. Enter a title + brief, click **Start task** without changing the dropdown.
5. Open the spawned session → the running agent is **Codex**, not the configured default.

**B — most agents unreachable:**
1. Set the project default to an agent outside the 4 (e.g. *Cursor*).
2. Open **New task** — Cursor is not in the dropdown; only the 4 hardcoded agents are available.
3. Any task created spawns one of the 4 (Codex by default), never Cursor.

### Affected files
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx` (lines 17–22, 31, 65)
- Backend behavior is correct; no change needed there. References: `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go:146`, `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:320`

title: Activity panel shows derived status instead of agent activity state
body:
## Description

The Session Inspector **Activity** section currently renders derived `session.status` via `workerDisplayStatus(session)` instead of the raw backend `session.activity.state`.

This causes incorrect labels. Example: a Codex session can have:

```text
activity.state = idle
status = review_pending
```

but the Activity section shows:

```text
Input needed
```

because `review_pending -> needs_you -> Input needed` in the frontend display mapping.

## Expected behavior

The Activity section should show only the agent lifecycle activity state:

```text
active        -> Working
idle          -> Idle
waiting_input -> Input needed
exited        -> Exited
```

It should use `session.activity.lastActivityAt` for the timestamp, not `session.updatedAt`.

## Scope

- Preserve `session.activity` in the frontend workspace model.
- Map backend `session.activity` in `useWorkspaceQuery`.
- Update `SessionInspector` Activity section to render raw activity state.
- Do not use PR-derived `session.status` for the Activity section.
- Move or remove synthetic rows like `Opened PR #...` and `Created worktree & branch` if they remain misleading in the Activity section.

## Acceptance criteria

- A session with `activity.state = idle` and `status = review_pending` renders `Idle`, not `Input needed`.
- A session with `activity.state = active` renders `Working`.
- A session with `activity.state = waiting_input` renders `Input needed`.
- Activity timestamp reflects `activity.lastActivityAt`.
- Add or adjust tests covering these cases.

title: Prettier workflow can rewrite generated route and pnpm lockfiles
body:
## Bug

The Prettier workflow runs `prettier --write .` on every non-main branch push, but two generated files are not excluded:

- `frontend/src/renderer/routeTree.gen.ts`
- `frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml`

When either generator produces output that differs from Prettier's rendering, the workflow can push a large formatter commit unrelated to the feature branch. Generated route output and package-manager lockfiles should remain owned by their generators.

Current `main` is already Prettier-clean, so this does not require a repository-wide formatting baseline.

## Proposed fix

Add only those two generated paths to `.prettierignore`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Prettier no longer rewrites the generated route tree or pnpm lockfile.
- Human-authored files remain covered by the workflow.
- The change contains no documentation or source formatting churn.

Ported and narrowed from [the original rewrite issue](https://github.com/aoagents/ReverbCode/issues/417).

title: fix(docs): resolve MDX parsing error in installation tabs
body:
## Description
This PR fixes a critical MDX compilation error (Expected a closing tag for <Tab>) that causes a 500 server error on the Installation documentation page.

## Root Cause:
The bug was inadvertently introduced in commit 598205165. The bash commands inside the "from source" <Tab> component were placed on a single line. This formatting caused the underlying Markdown parser to misinterpret the closing backticks (```), which subsequently swallowed the closing JSX </Tab> tag and broke the page build. Additionally, the bash commands were chained with spaces instead of newlines or && operators, causing terminal execution failures.

## Changes Made:

Reformatted the MDX code blocks across all tabs so that the opening and closing code fences (```) are placed on their own distinct lines, satisfying the strict MDX parser requirements.

Separated the chained bash commands (cd, pnpm install, pnpm build, etc.) in the "from source" tab onto individual lines to ensure they execute sequentially and correctly in the user's terminal.

## Testing:

Verified locally that the docs page now compiles successfully without the Fast Refresh/Webpack serialization errors.

title: Agent Orchestrator New Landing Page UI/UX Audit 1
body:
A practical fix-it sheet to close the gap with superset.sh. Read it top to bottom, fix in order. Nothing here needs a redesign. It is mostly tightening what already exists.

The short version of what is going wrong: Superset breathes, your site holds its breath. They give every section room, one clear idea, and a calm rhythm. Your page is dense, the type fights itself, and things sit wherever they landed. The fixes below are about restraint, spacing, and a proper scale.

---

## Part 1: Issues

These are the things actively hurting the site right now. The first two are the ones you flagged, and they are real bugs, not taste. Fix these first because a broken scroll kills the premium feel faster than any font choice.

**1. The hero scroll break and the navbar stacking are one bug, not three.** This is the important correction. On a fresh page load everything works fine. The break only happens on this exact path: click into a doc from the nav, then click the Agent Orchestrator logo to come back home. After that return trip the hero will not scroll back to the top and the navbar starts sitting on top of the headings. Because it only triggers on the return and never on a cold load, this is a client-side navigation problem, not a styling problem. The hero almost certainly runs a scroll animation (a pinned or scroll-jacked setup, likely GSAP ScrollTrigger, Lenis, Locomotive, or a custom scroll listener). When you navigate to the docs page, that scroll instance is not being destroyed. It lingers with stale measurements, old pin spacers, and listeners bound to a DOM that no longer exists. When you come back home, a fresh hero mounts on top of the dead one, and the two fight. The zombie instance holds the page at a pin point calculated for the old layout, which is why scroll will not return to the top. The navbar offset breaks for the same reason, because the navbar reads its scroll position from the same poisoned state. Fix the teardown and both symptoms go away together.

**2. Snippet interactions feel clunky.** The copy buttons, the tab switches on code blocks, the hover states all feel heavy and slightly off. Superset's snippets feel weightless. Yours have visible jank on switch and no satisfying copy feedback.

**3. The whole page is too dense.** This is the big one. Look at the two sites side by side. Superset uses roughly twice the vertical space between sections. Your sections are stacked tight, so the eye never gets a rest and nothing feels important because everything is competing.

**4. Hierarchy is flat.** On your homepage, the section label, the heading, and the body text are all close in size and weight. The reader cannot tell at a glance what is a heading and what is supporting copy. Superset has a very clear three-step ladder: tiny uppercase label, big bold heading, muted body.

**5. The docs page reads like a wall.** The left nav, the content, and the right "On this page" rail are all the same visual weight and the tables are cramped. It works, but it does not feel like the marketing site. There is no shared design language between the two.

**6. Icon and logo row feels heavy.** Your "One Daemon. 23 Agent Harnesses." logo strip and the trust-logos idea are good, but the icons are inconsistent in size and weight, so the row looks busy rather than reassuring.

**7. Inconsistent card treatment.** The feature cards in the middle of the homepage use different background tones, border weights, and corner radii. Superset keeps every card identical so the content is the star. Yours draw attention to the containers instead.

---

## Part 2: Improvements

Now the fixes. Grouped so you can hand each block to whoever owns it.

### Fix the navigation bug first

Remember this is one bug, not three. The hero scroll lock and the navbar stacking both come from the scroll instance not being destroyed when you leave the homepage. Kill it on the way out and rebuild it clean on the way back, and both symptoms disappear.

- Tear down the scroll setup when the homepage unmounts. If you are on GSAP ScrollTrigger, kill the triggers and pin spacers in the cleanup function, then refresh so measurements recalculate from the clean DOM. If you are on a smooth-scroll library like Lenis or Locomotive, call its destroy method on unmount and create a fresh instance on mount. The old instance must not survive the trip to the docs page.
- On returning to the homepage, force scroll to the top and refresh the scroll library after the new hero has mounted. Many client routers restore the previous scroll position by default, which lands the page at a spot the freshly mounted hero cannot satisfy. Resetting to top on route change clears it.
- Once the teardown is in place, confirm the navbar offset behaves again. It was reading position from the same stale state, so it should fix itself. If any residual overlap remains on the docs page, add `scroll-margin-top` equal to the navbar height plus about 16px on every heading and anchor target.
- Keep the logo a plain link to `/`. This is good practice regardless and keeps browser back and forward behaving correctly.
- Test the exact failing path every time: cold load, click into a doc, click the logo to return, then scroll to the bottom and flick all the way back up. It must land at the very top with the navbar sitting correctly.

### Open up the spacing

This is the highest-leverage change for looking premium. Spacing is what separates the two sites more than any other single thing.

- Use one spacing scale and stick to it. Something like 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128. Every margin and padding should be a value from this list, nothing in between.
- Push section-to-section vertical space up hard. Aim for around 120 to 160px between major sections on desktop. It will feel like too much in the editor and just right in the browser.
- Give the hero more room to breathe above and below the headline. Let the headline be the only thing in the viewport for a beat.
- Add internal padding to your feature cards. Cramped cards read as cheap. Generous padding reads as considered.

### Rebuild the hierarchy

Copy Superset's three-step ladder exactly. It is the reason their sections feel calm.

- **Section label.** Tiny, uppercase, letter-spaced, muted colour. Example: `PARALLEL EXECUTION`. This is the quiet signpost.
- **Heading.** Large, bold, high contrast. This is the one thing the eye should land on.
- **Body.** Mid-grey, comfortable line height, kept to a readable measure of about 60 to 70 characters per line.

Right now your label, heading and body are too close in size. Pull them apart. The heading should be at least 2x the body size, and the label should be clearly smaller than the body with the uppercase treatment doing the work.

### Calm the cards and logos

- Pick one card style. One background tone, one border, one radius, one shadow. Apply it everywhere with zero exceptions.
- Normalise every icon in the logo strip to the same optical size and the same stroke weight. If they come from different sources, redraw or rescale them so they read as a set.
- For the trust and harness logos, set them all to a single muted tone (a soft grey works) so the row reads as a calm wall of names, not a rainbow.

### Make the snippets feel light

- On code-tab switch, swap content instantly with a very short cross-fade, around 120 to 150ms. No layout shift, no height jump. Lock the snippet height so switching tabs does not move the page.
- The copy button should give instant feedback. Icon flips to a tick, label changes to "Copied", reverts after about 1.5 seconds. Keep the button quiet until hover.
- Keep one syntax highlighting theme across the whole site, marketing and docs. Two different code themes is an instant tell that the site was built in pieces.

### Bring the docs in line

- Use the same type scale, the same spacing scale, and the same colours as the marketing site. The docs should feel like the same product, just denser.
- Give the tables more row height and a touch more horizontal cell padding. Right now they are tight enough to feel like a spreadsheet.
- Make the left nav active state and the right rail active state share one accent colour. Pick one accent and use it everywhere, links, active states, primary buttons.

### Add motion, sparingly

Superset's polish is partly its restraint with animation. Match that.

- One pattern only: a gentle fade-and-rise on each section as it enters the viewport. Around 24px of travel, 400 to 500ms, ease-out. Trigger once, do not replay on scroll back.
- Do not animate everything. Animate sections in, and that is mostly it. Buttons and links get quick hover transitions, nothing more.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and switch all of this off for users who ask for it.

---

## Part 3: Typography, Iconography, Spacing and Hierarchy

The reference sheet. Set these as tokens and the rest of the site falls into place.

### Typography

- **Two families maximum.** A clean sans for everything (Inter, Geist, or similar) and one mono for code and the small uppercase labels. Superset uses a mono accent for its labels and hero, and it works well for a developer tool. You can do the same, just be consistent.
- **Set a real scale.** Do not eyeball sizes. Use a fixed set and only these values:
  - Hero headline: 56 to 64px, bold, tight line height around 1.05
  - Section heading: 32 to 40px, bold
  - Subheading: 20 to 24px
  - Body: 16 to 18px, line height around 1.6
  - Small label: 12 to 13px, uppercase, letter-spacing around 0.08em, muted
  - Caption and meta: 13 to 14px
- **Line length.** Cap body paragraphs at roughly 65 characters. Long lines are one of the reasons your page feels like a wall.
- **Weight does the work.** Use weight, not colour, to show importance in headings. Body stays regular, headings go bold. Avoid more than three weights total.
- **Colour for text.** Near-white for headings, a clear mid-grey for body, a dimmer grey for labels and captions. Three text colours, no more.

### Iconography

- **One icon set, one stroke weight.** Pick a single library (Lucide is a safe choice) and never mix in icons from elsewhere. Mixed icon styles are the fastest way to look unpolished.
- **Consistent size.** Inline icons at 16 or 20px, feature icons at 24px. Pick the sizes and stick to them.
- **Optical sizing.** Some logos look bigger than others at the same pixel size. Adjust each one so they look the same size to the eye, not just on paper.
- **Muted by default.** Icons sit in grey and only pick up the accent colour when they are interactive or active.

### Spacing

- **One scale, applied everywhere:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128.
- **Section padding:** 120 to 160px top and bottom on desktop, scaling down to about 64 to 80px on mobile.
- **Card padding:** 24 to 32px inside.
- **Gap between label, heading and body:** label to heading around 12 to 16px, heading to body around 16 to 24px.
- **Content width:** cap your main content column at around 1100 to 1200px and centre it. Full-width text is part of why the page feels unstructured.

### Hierarchy checklist

For every section on the site, it should pass this test at a glance:

1. There is exactly one thing the eye lands on first. That is the heading.
2. The tiny uppercase label sits above it as a quiet signpost.
3. The body sits below in muted grey at a comfortable measure.
4. There is clear empty space around the whole block, so it reads as one unit.
5. Every card, icon and code block on the page matches every other one of its kind.

If a section fails any of these, it is the section that is making the site feel cluttered. Fix it against the checklist and move on.

---

## Where to start

If you only do three things, do these:

1. Fix the navigation bug. Destroy the scroll instance when leaving the homepage and rebuild it clean on return. This one fix clears both the stuck scroll and the navbar stacking, since they share a root cause.
2. Double your section spacing and set the type scale. This alone closes most of the gap.
3. Pick one card style, one icon set, one accent colour, and apply them with zero exceptions.

Everything else is refinement on top of those three.

The daemon panics on startup with a `goose: duplicate version 20 detected` error. Two migration files in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/` both use version number `20`:

- `0020_pr_reviews.sql`

- #2193 — feat: show multi-PR review status

title: fix: resolve duplicate migration version 20 collision
body:
Fixes #2293
Two PRs (#2193, #2200) merged ~2h apart each added a migration file numbered 0020, since each branch only saw one such file at CI time and neither was rebased against the other before merge. Renumbers 0020_pr_reviews.sql to 0021_pr_reviews.sql.

TestMigrationVersionsAreUnique already existed and is correct; it didn't catch this because it only runs against each PR's branch state, not the merged result of both PRs together.

title: Electron app shows default Dock icon instead of AO app icon
feat(icon): apply runtime app icon on macOS
body: ## Description This PR updates the Electron app icon handling so the app uses our AO icon consistently instead of showing the default Electron icon or a hard square icon in the macOS Dock. ## Changes ### Code Updates - **Added macOS runtime Dock icon support in `frontend/src/main.ts`** - Implemented `app.dock.setIcon(...)` to set the Dock icon at runtime - Ensures the correct icon displays in the macOS Dock during development and packaged builds ### Icon Asset Updates - **Reused existing `windowIconPath()` resolution** - Dev mode: loads `frontend/assets/icon.png` - Packaged builds: loads from `process.resourcesPath/icon.png` - Maintains consistency across build modes - **Updated icon assets with rounded corners** - Modified `frontend/assets/icon.png` to have transparent corners - Replaced opaque square background with transparent pixels - Regenerated platform-specific icon assets: - `frontend/assets/icon.ico` (Windows) - `frontend/assets/icon.icns` (macOS, if applicable) ## Why This Change? ### Problem - `BrowserWindow({ icon })` works for Windows/Linux window and taskbar icons - macOS **ignores** `BrowserWindow.icon` for the Dock icon display - Without explicit runtime configuration, the Dock showed: - Electron's default icon - Hard square appearance (opaque background) - Stale/unrounded icon during development ### Solution 1. **macOS Dock requires `app.dock.setIcon(...)`** at runtime - The Dock icon is a separate entity from the window icon on macOS - Must be set after `app.whenReady()` and before window creation 2. **Transparent corners for proper appearance** - PNG corners are now transparent instead of opaque - Provides the rounded, polished look expected on modern macOS 3. **Consistent icon resolution** - Reuses existing `windowIconPath()` logic - Ensures dev and packaged builds both use the correct asset ## Screenshots / Evidence Closes ## Description This PR updates the Electron app icon handling so the app uses our AO icon consistently instead of showing the default Electron icon or a hard square icon in the macOS Dock. ## Changes ### Code Updates - **Added macOS runtime Dock icon support in `frontend/src/main.ts`** - Implemented `app.dock.setIcon(...)` to set the Dock icon at runtime - Ensures the correct icon displays in the macOS Dock during development and packaged builds ### Icon Asset Updates - **Reused existing `windowIconPath()` resolution** - Dev mode: loads `frontend/assets/icon.png` - Packaged builds: loads from `process.resourcesPath/icon.png` - Maintains consistency across build modes - **Updated icon assets with rounded corners** - Modified `frontend/assets/icon.png` to have transparent corners - Replaced opaque square background with transparent pixels ## Why This Change?
