title: feat(spawn): add required --name flag for sidebar display name
body:
Closes #2299

## What

Adds a `--name` flag to `ao spawn` that sets the session's display name shown in the sidebar, capped at 20 characters.

`--name` is **required**: `ao spawn` errors out before touching the network if it is missing or longer than 20 characters. There is no auto-generated default-name fallback for the flag.

## Data flow (end to end)

`ao spawn --name` -> `spawnRequest.displayName` (CLI JSON) -> `SpawnSessionRequest.DisplayName` (POST /api/v1/sessions) -> `ports.SpawnConfig.DisplayName` -> `seedRecord` -> session record (already persisted/read by the store) -> read model. The frontend already renders `session.displayName ?? session.issueId ?? session.id` (`useWorkspaceQuery.ts`), so no renderer logic change was needed; the sidebar picks up the name automatically (the same path the existing rename feature uses).

## 20-character limit

Reject (not truncate), since that is the cleaner rule for a required flag and matches the "error out with a clear message" UX:
- CLI: `--name must be 20 characters or fewer` (counts runes via `utf8.RuneCountInString`, trims surrounding whitespace).
- Daemon: enforces the same cap server-side (`DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`) so a direct API call cannot exceed it.

## Why the daemon keeps `displayName` optional

The required-ness lives at the `ao spawn` CLI surface (the issue's scope). The daemon's `POST /api/v1/sessions` keeps `displayName` **optional** on purpose: the desktop new-task dialog (`NewTaskDialog.tsx`) spawns workers without a name and relies on the read-model id fallback. Making the field server-required would break that flow (and the generated TS type). The daemon still enforces the 20-char cap whenever a name is present.

## Notes

- No changeset file: this Go rewrite has no changeset tooling. Semver is conveyed via the conventional commit (`feat:` = minor).
- Orchestrator sessions spawn through the same `SpawnConfig` with an empty name and fall back to the session id, unchanged.
- The rename endpoint (`PATCH /sessions/{id}`) is left untouched (separate surface, out of scope); a follow-up could share the 20-char cap there for consistency.

## Tests

- `internal/cli`: new `--name` required + overlong guards; existing spawn tests updated to pass `--name`; DTO round-trip asserts `displayName` reaches `SpawnConfig`.
- `internal/httpd/controllers`: spawn round-trip asserts `displayName` flows to the read model; new test asserts the server-side 20-char cap (`DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`).
- OpenAPI spec + `schema.ts` regenerated via `npm run api`.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./...` -> 1650 passed, 80 packages.
- `go vet` on touched packages: clean.
- Manual: `ao spawn --project demo` -> `--name is required`; `--name <21 chars>` -> `--name must be 20 characters or fewer`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix: show latest reviewer verdict after PR updates
body:
Fixes #2300.

## Before
- Review state was selected only by the current PR head SHA.
- If a reviewer completed `changes_requested` on `sha-old` and the worker pushed `sha-new`, the planner found no run for `sha-new`.
- The Reviews tab row became `needs_review`, but had no `latestRun` attached for display.
- The visible row verdict and top badge could fall back to `Not run`, even though the latest actual review verdict was `changes_requested` or `approved`.
- The `Run review` button was available, which was correct.

## After
- The planner still marks the PR as `needs_review` when the head SHA changes, so the button stays available.
- It also attaches the newest review run for that PR as `latestRun`, even if that run was for a previous SHA.
- The Reviews tab now prefers `latestRun.verdict` when choosing the visible label.
- After `changes_requested` on `sha-old` and a push to `sha-new`, the row and top badge still show `Changes requested`.
- The user can still click `Run review` to send the next review request for `sha-new`.

## Reviewer trigger behavior
- No auto-triggering is added.
- Existing trigger flow already sends a message to a live reviewer terminal via `Notify`/`SendMessage`.
- If the reviewer pane is not alive, it spawns a new reviewer with the review prompt in the launch command.

## Tests
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/review ./internal/httpd/...`

title: fix(migrations): resolve duplicate version 20 collision
body:
## Summary

`main` ships **two SQLite migrations at version 20**. Goose panics on every fresh daemon boot before either runs, breaking `ao daemon` and most of the backend test suite.

Renumber the later-merged file (`0020_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql` → `0021_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql`) so versions are unique again.

## Why it's broken

Two PRs added migration version 20 unaware of each other:

- #2193 (`cb456bb2`) → `0020_pr_reviews.sql`
- #2200 (`a31cf1b5`) → `0020_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql`

Goose stable-sorts pending migrations by version on every `Open`, and Go's `sort.Sort` requires a **strict weak ordering**. Two equal versions violate that contract; `Migrations.Less` panics:

```
goose.Migrations.Less
goose.sortAndConnectMigrations
goose.collectMigrationsFS
sqlite.migrate -> sqlite.Open -> daemon.Run
```

## Verified

Repro on isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` with both files present:

```
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-fresh AO_PORT=3098 go run ./cmd/ao daemon
# panic before "daemon listening"
```

With the rename applied:

```
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-fresh-fixed AO_PORT=3097 go run ./cmd/ao daemon
# daemon listening addr=127.0.0.1:3097 pid=...
sqlite3 .../ao.db 'SELECT version_id FROM goose_db_version ORDER BY version_id;'
# 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 — applied in order
```

- `go test ./...` → **zero failures** (was hitting the panic in every sqlite-touching package)
- `go test -race ./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/daemon/...` → green

## Renaming a merged migration

AGENTS.md normally bans renaming merged migrations — the rule protects live DBs whose `goose_db_version` table records the old `version_id`. Here that risk does not apply: **no live DB can have recorded `version_id = 20` for either file**, because goose panics on sort before applying either. The rename is the smallest fix that restores boot.

Body of the renumbered file is unchanged. Its unique-index DDL does not depend on the `pr_reviews` table, so ordering is free.

## Risk

Anyone whose working tree silently lost one of the two files (filesystem case quirks, stale checkout) has been booting on a half-applied state. Their next pull restores the file under version 21; goose applies it on top of the existing DB. Idempotent.

Closes #2305.

title: Daemon panics on fresh boot: duplicate SQLite migration version 20
body:
## Bug

`main` ships two SQLite migrations at version 20:

- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0020_pr_reviews.sql` (from #2193, `cb456bb2`)
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0020_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql` (from #2200, `a31cf1b5`)

Goose stable-sorts pending migrations by version on every `Open`. Go's `sort.Sort` requires a **strict weak ordering**; two entries with equal versions violate that contract and panic `Migrations.Less`. The panic fires inside `sqlite.Open` → so every fresh `ao daemon` boot and every test that opens a SQLite store crashes.

## Repro

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator.git
cd agent-orchestrator/backend
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-repro AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/ao-repro/running.json AO_PORT=3098 \
  go run ./cmd/ao daemon
```

Result: panic before `daemon listening`. Stack trace:

```
panic: runtime error: comparing uncomparable type
goose.Migrations.Less        github.com/pressly/goose/v3@v3.27.1/migrate.go:37
goose.sortAndConnectMigrations                          migrate.go:180
goose.collectMigrationsFS                               migrate.go:170
goose.UpToContext                                       up.go:46
sqlite.migrate                  internal/storage/sqlite/db.go:96
sqlite.Open                     internal/storage/sqlite/db.go:64
daemon.Run                      internal/daemon/daemon.go:58
cli.NewRootCommand.newDaemonCommand.func3   internal/cli/root.go:267
```

`go test ./...` hits the same panic in every package that opens a store (`internal/daemon`, `internal/storage/sqlite/store`, `internal/service/*`, etc.).

## Impact

- Any fresh clone of `main` cannot start the daemon
- `go test ./...` fails for any sqlite-touching package
- Existing developers whose working trees silently lost one of the two files (filesystem case quirks, stale checkouts) keep booting fine until they refresh — then they hit the panic

## Why it slipped through

The two PRs were authored concurrently and neither review surfaced the version collision because goose only fails at the open call, not at `go build` or `go vet`. CI doesn't currently fail on fresh-boot smoke either, so both merged green.

## Fix

PR #2304 renames the later-merged file to `0021_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql`. Renaming a merged migration normally violates AGENTS.md, but the rule's purpose (protect live DBs that recorded the old version) does not apply here: goose panics on sort before applying either file, so no live DB can have `version_id = 20` for either.

Body of the renumbered file is unchanged. Its unique-index DDL does not depend on the `pr_reviews` table, so ordering is free.

## Suggested follow-up

Add a CI guard that fails when two migrations share a version number — a one-line `find` / `sort | uniq -d` check would have caught this at merge time.

[![Compound Engineering](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built_with-Compound_Engineering-6366f1)](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin)
![GPT-5](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPT--5-000000)


## Testing Codex and OpenCode reviewer harnesses end-to-end

Concrete recipe for running a review with each new harness against a live daemon, requested in [this comment](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2306#issuecomment-4846398715).

### Prerequisites

- `codex` and/or `opencode` CLIs installed and on `$PATH` (verify with `codex --version` / `opencode --version`)
- AO daemon running (`ao start` or the desktop app)
- A worker session with at least one open PR — this is the review target

### 1. Set the reviewer harness for a project

Two ways:

**Settings UI** — `Project → Settings → Reviewers → Default reviewer agent`. The Select now lists `codex` and `opencode` alongside `claude-code`.

**CLI** — write the config directly:

```bash
ao project set-config <project-id> --config-json '{
  "worker":       {"agent": "codex"},
  "orchestrator": {"agent": "claude-code"},
  "reviewers":    [{"harness": "codex"}]
}'
# or "harness": "opencode"
```

Verify it persisted:

```bash
ao project get <project-id> --json | jq '.config.reviewers'
# → [{"harness":"codex"}]
```

### 2. Trigger a review on the worker's open PR

```bash
SESSION=<worker-session-id>
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${AO_PORT:-3001}/api/v1/sessions/${SESSION}/reviews/trigger"
```

The daemon resolves the reviewer harness via `ProjectConfig.ResolveReviewerHarness`, picks the matching adapter (`reviewer/codex` or `reviewer/opencode`), and spawns a reviewer pane in the same workspace.

### 3. Verify the reviewer pane launched with the right sandbox

**Codex** — the adapter inserts `--sandbox read-only` and forwards AO location env vars via Codex's `-c shell_environment_policy.set.*`. Inspect the live process:

```bash
ps -axo pid,command | grep '[c]odex' | grep review
# Look for: --sandbox read-only
# Look for: -c shell_environment_policy.set.AO_PORT="3001"
#           -c shell_environment_policy.set.AO_DATA_DIR="/Users/.../.ao"
#           -c shell_environment_policy.set.AO_RUN_FILE="/Users/.../.ao/running.json"
```

Attempt an edit inside the codex pane (e.g. `:!echo x >> README.md`) — Codex refuses because the sandbox is read-only. `git diff`, `gh api`, and `ao review submit` remain available.

**OpenCode** — the adapter injects the permission policy via the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var. Inspect:

```bash
ps -axEo pid,command,env | grep '[o]pencode' | grep -o 'OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT=[^ ]*'
# → JSON: "*":"deny","read":"allow","glob":"allow","grep":"allow",
#         "bash":{"*":"deny","gh api *":"allow","git diff*":"allow",
#                 "git log*":"allow","git show*":"allow","git status*":"allow",
#                 "ao review submit *":"allow"}
```

Inside the OpenCode pane: read/grep/glob and the listed bash commands work; every other tool and bash command is denied.

### 4. Verify the verdict round-trip

The reviewer pane runs `ao review submit --review-id <id> --reviews <json>`. Daemon writes the verdict and emits a notification:

```bash
ao session get "$SESSION" --json | jq '.reviews[-1]'
# → {"id":"...", "verdict":"approved" | "changes_requested", "harness":"codex", ...}
```

### Unit + build coverage already in CI

- `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/codex/codex_test.go`:
  - `TestReviewCommandUsesReadOnlySandbox` — asserts `--sandbox read-only` is inserted before the prompt argument and each AO_* env var becomes a `-c shell_environment_policy.set.*` entry
  - `TestReviewMessageReturnsTaskPrompt` — confirms a follow-up message reuses the same task prompt
- `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/opencode/opencode_test.go`:
  - `TestReviewCommandUsesReadOnlyPermissionPolicy` — asserts the exact policy JSON travels via the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var and the system prompt is folded into the prompt
  - `TestReviewMessageReturnsTaskPrompt`
- `backend/internal/domain/projectconfig_test.go` — `Validate` table rows reject configs that name an unsupported reviewer harness and accept the two new ones
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx` — Reviewer `<Select>` round-trips `codex` and `opencode` through save

Run locally:

```bash
go test ./backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/codex/... \
        ./backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/opencode/... \
        ./backend/internal/domain/... -race -v
cd frontend && npm test -- ProjectSettingsForm
```

## What

Make each worker session's display name editable inline from the sidebar.

body:
Summary
This PR adds a daemon-backed agent catalog, exposes installed/authorized agent state to the frontend, and uses that data in project settings so users can choose worker/orchestrator agents more safely.

It also adds orchestrator replacement handling: when the saved orchestrator agent changes, AO starts the replacement first and only retires the previous orchestrator after the new one is up, so a failed replacement does not cause downtime.

A key caveat is that agent-auth/login flows can interfere with replacement startup. If switching agents triggers the agent’s own bootstrap path, the replacement may come up outside AO’s normal orchestrator initialization path and miss the AO orchestrator system prompt.

What Changed
Backend
Added agent inventory service for:

supported agents
installed agents
authorized agents
counts for each
Added optional AgentAuthChecker capability on adapters.

Added shared CLI auth probing helper for adapters with cheap local auth checks.

Added GET /api/v1/agents.

Extended registry inventory entries to carry adapter manifest metadata for user-facing labels.

Added orchestrator replacement flow in the session service:

spawn replacement first
retire previous orchestrator only after successful replacement
preserve previous orchestrator when replacement startup fails
Added backend tests for agent catalog, controller responses, session replacement behavior, and related project/service wiring.

Frontend
Regenerated API types for the new agents endpoint/DTOs.

Updated ProjectSettingsForm to:

load agent catalog from the daemon
show authorized agent options
handle installed-but-not-authorized states
surface orchestrator replacement pending state
allow retry once replacement is safe to perform
Added/updated tests for the new settings behavior.

title: Project Settings allows switching to unsupported orchestrator agents without preflight install/auth checks
body:
Summary

The orchestrator agent picker currently lets users switch to agents even when AO does not know whether that agent is installed or authenticated. That creates a
broken switch flow:

if the agent is not installed, it should not be selectable as a runnable orchestrator target
if the agent is installed but not authenticated, should not be selectable as a runnable orchestrator target
if switching triggers the agent’s own login/bootstrap flow, that can spawn a fresh session outside AO’s normal orchestrator startup path, so the replacement
session may miss AO’s system prompt / expected initialization
This means the settings UI can present options that are not actually safe to switch to.

Problem

Today the user can pick an orchestrator agent without a reliable preflight check for:

supported by AO
installed locally
authenticated / ready to run
That leads to two bad outcomes:

The agent still appears in the switcher.
The user can save and attempt a restart.
Restart then fails late instead of the UI blocking the choice up front.
The switch is allowed.
The agent may prompt for login during startup.
That login flow can create a new session/process that AO did not initialize the normal way.
The resulting session may not receive AO’s system prompt and expected orchestrator bootstrap.
Expected behavior

The switcher should only present agents in states the user can act on clearly.
Unsupported or unavailable agents should not look like normal selectable options.
If an agent is not installed, the UI should show that state and block switching.
If an agent is not authenticated, the UI should show that state before save/restart, not only after failure.
AO should only cut over to a new orchestrator when the target agent is actually ready to launch through AO’s normal startup path.
Why this matters

This is not just a UX issue. It can produce orchestrator sessions that start outside AO’s intended initialization path, which risks missing the system prompt
and breaking orchestrator behavior in subtle ways.

Acceptance criteria

Agent catalog API exposes per-agent readiness state: supported, installed, authenticated.
Project Settings uses that catalog instead of treating every known agent as equally selectable.
Uninstalled agents are not shown as normal switch targets, or are visibly disabled with an install-required reason.
Installed but unauthenticated agents are clearly marked before switching.
Save/restart is blocked unless the selected orchestrator agent is runnable through AO.
Switching cannot fall into an external login/bootstrap path that bypasses AO’s normal orchestrator initialization.
Tests cover:
uninstalled agent
installed but unauthenticated agent
installed and authenticated agent
restart path preserving AO system-prompt initialization

title: Killed sessions resurrect as alive after Cmd+Q restart (stale session_worktrees restore marker)
body:
## Bug

After Cmd+Q quitting the desktop app and reopening it, sessions the user **killed** reappear as if alive. Killed sessions should stay dead across an app restart (while still being manually restorable on demand).

## Root cause

Category **(c): startup resurrects terminated rows.** `Kill` correctly persists `is_terminated=1`; quit doesn't tear sessions down at all. The fault is the **`session_worktrees` restore-marker lifecycle**: the marker is write-only and never cleared, so the boot-time `RestoreAll` mistakes a user-killed session for a "shutdown-saved" one and relaunches it.

`RestoreAll` gates auto-relaunch solely on whether a `session_worktrees` row exists (`session_manager/manager.go:777-786`):

```go
rows, err := m.store.ListSessionWorktrees(ctx, rec.ID)
if len(rows) == 0 {
    // No marker: this session was killed by the user before shutdown.
    continue
}
// ...otherwise relaunch via m.Restore -> MarkSpawned
```

That comment encodes an invariant ("user-killed sessions have no marker row") that is **false**, because nothing deletes the marker:

- `DeleteSessionWorktrees` exists in the store/gen layer but is **never called in production**.
- `Kill` (`manager.go:430-465`) marks terminated and destroys runtime/worktree but **never touches the marker**.
- `RestoreAll` relaunches a session but **never deletes the marker after consuming it** (`manager.go:768-840`) — the marker is not one-shot.
- The marker is created by `reconcileLive` on boot (`manager.go:683`) and `saveAndTeardownOne` (`manager.go:608`).

On relaunch, `MarkSpawned` (`lifecycle/manager.go:243`) sets `IsTerminated = false` and activity to `idle` — which is why resurrected sessions show up alive.

## Live DB proof (`agent-orchestrator` project)

```
 id    activity_state  is_terminated  markers
 2     exited               1            0     <- killed, NO marker -> stays dead (control)
 7     exited               1            1     <- KILLED but marker present -> will resurrect next launch
 8     exited               1            1     <- same
 9     exited               1            1     <- same
 3,4,5,6,10,11,12  idle    0            1     <- already resurrected once (term cleared), still carry marker
 13,14,15,16  waiting_input 0           0     <- genuinely alive, never saved
```

Session 2 vs 7/8/9 is decisive: all are killed, but only the ones carrying a leftover marker are time-bombs. Sessions 3-6/10-12 are the bug already manifested.

## Repro

1. Spawn session N; let it be alive.
2. Cmd+Q (daemon exits without teardown; runtime dies with it).
3. Reopen -> `Reconcile`/`reconcileLive` writes a marker, marks terminated, then `RestoreAll` relaunches N (`MarkSpawned` clears `is_terminated`). **Marker left in place.**
4. User kills N -> `Kill` sets `is_terminated=1`. **Marker still in place.**
5. Cmd+Q, reopen -> `RestoreAll` finds the stale marker -> relaunches the killed session. **Bug.**

A session spawned and killed without ever surviving a reopen cycle (like session 2) never gets a marker and correctly stays dead, which is why the bug looks intermittent.

## Fix direction

Restore the invariant the `RestoreAll` guard already assumes; two layers:

1. **`Kill` clears the marker** — call `DeleteSessionWorktrees(ctx, id)` in `Kill`. A user kill is explicit terminal intent and must not leave a resurrection marker.
2. **Marker is one-shot** — `RestoreAll` deletes the marker after it successfully relaunches (or leaves terminated), so it never outlives a single restart. A still-live session re-acquires a fresh marker via `reconcileLive` at the next quit.

**Restorability is preserved:** manual restore (`POST /sessions/{id}/restore` -> `manager.Restore`, `manager.go:470`) is marker-independent (only needs `IsTerminated && WorkspacePath && Branch`; re-creates the worktree from the branch). Deleting the marker removes only the *auto-relaunch-on-boot* flag, not the ability to manually restore a killed session later.

One-time cleanup: delete `session_worktrees` rows for sessions where `is_terminated=1` to defuse existing time-bombs.

title: fix(session): keep killed sessions dead across restart (clear stale restore marker)
body:
## What

Killed sessions reappear as alive after a Cmd+Q quit + reopen. This fixes the stale-restore-marker lifecycle so a killed session stays dead across restart, while remaining manually restorable on demand.

Fixes #2319.

## Root cause

The boot-time `RestoreAll` auto-relaunches any terminated session that still has a `session_worktrees` row (the "shutdown-saved" marker). That marker was write-only: nothing ever deleted it. `Kill` left it in place, and `RestoreAll` never consumed it. So a session that survived one reopen cycle (which gave it a marker via `reconcileLive`) and was then killed still carried the marker, and the next boot resurrected it. On relaunch `MarkSpawned` clears `is_terminated`, so it shows up alive.

`DeleteSessionWorktrees` already existed on the store but was never called in production.

## Fix

1. Add `DeleteSessionWorktrees` to the Manager `Store` interface (concrete store already implements it).
2. `Kill` deletes the restore marker after `MarkTerminated` (best-effort, logged on failure). A user kill is explicit terminal intent and must not leave a resurrection marker.
3. `RestoreAll` deletes the marker after consuming it, making it one-shot so it never outlives a single restart. A still-live session re-acquires a fresh marker via `reconcileLive`/`saveAndTeardownOne` at the next quit.

Manual restore (`POST /sessions/{id}/restore`) is untouched and marker-independent, so a killed session stays restorable on demand, just not auto-resurrected on boot.

## Tests

- `TestKill_DeletesRestoreMarker`: after Kill, the marker is gone.
- `TestRestoreAll_DeletesMarkerAfterRelaunch`: marker is one-shot.
- `TestRestoreAll_KilledSessionNotResurrectedOnSecondBoot`: a killed session relaunches at most once and stays terminated on the second boot.

All three failed before the fix for the right reason. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/storage/...` (173 tests) all pass.

## Note for existing installs

Existing DBs may carry `session_worktrees` rows on already-killed sessions (time-bombs). A one-time cleanup `DELETE FROM session_worktrees WHERE session_id IN (SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE is_terminated=1)` defuses them; not included here since it is environment state, not code.

title: Tracker intake: GitHub-only issue-driven session spawning
body:
## Context

The rewrite already supervises agent work after a session exists: project registration, isolated worktrees, worker and orchestrator sessions, PR observation, lifecycle status, notifications, and dashboard visibility.

The missing product loop is issue-driven intake. A human should be able to mark an issue as ready for agent work, and the daemon should start exactly one worker session for it, preserve the issue context on the session, and let the existing PR and lifecycle machinery take over.

This issue narrows #2282 and #2283 to a single GitHub-only slice (backend + dashboard together) so it can ship ahead of multi-provider support. Linear and Jira intake are tracked separately and land as additive follow-ups once this is in.

## Scope

- Daemon-side intake loop for registered projects with issue intake enabled.
- Poll the configured GitHub repo for eligible open issues.
- Define explicit eligibility through a configured label, assignee, or both — no broad/unscoped intake.
- Spawn one worker session per eligible issue, keyed by the canonical `github:<owner>/<repo>#<n>` identifier so restarts cannot double-spawn.
- Build the worker prompt from the issue title, body, URL, and labels/assignees.
- Respect GitHub API rate limits: reuse the existing rate-limit-aware GitHub tracker adapter, back off per-project on a rate-limited or failed poll rather than retrying in a tight loop.
- Carry the configuration through project config, HTTP API types, and CLI (`project set-config --tracker-intake ...`).
- Dashboard: a Tracker Intake section in project settings (enable, repository override, labels, assignee), inline validation, and the canonical issue id surfaced on session cards and the inspector.
- Structure the provider seam (`TrackerResolver` interface) so adding Linear/Jira later is additive: a new adapter package plus a resolver-map entry, no changes to the poll/dedupe/backoff logic.

## Non-goals

- No Linear or Jira adapters in this slice.
- No tracker status transitions or automatic comments — intake stays read-only toward GitHub.
- No webhook receiver.
- No dry-run matching preview, last-poll status, or pause/resume controls beyond the persisted `enabled` flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing projects remain unaffected until they explicitly opt in.
- An eligible GitHub issue creates one worker session with its canonical issue identifier.
- Restarting the daemon does not create duplicate sessions.
- Ineligible issues are ignored; enabling intake without a label or assignee rule is rejected.
- GitHub rate-limit and auth failures back off per-project without blocking daemon startup or other projects' polling.
- Tests cover eligibility, duplicate prevention, prompt construction, failures/backoff, and the dashboard save/validation round-trip.

Supersedes/narrows #2282 and #2283 for the initial GitHub-only release.

title: feat(tracker): GitHub issue intake (backend + dashboard)
body:
## Summary

Registered projects can opt into issue-driven session intake against **GitHub**. The daemon polls each opted-in project's configured repo for eligible open issues and starts one worker session per issue, preserving the canonical `github:<owner>/<repo>#<n>` identifier so restarts cannot create duplicates. Existing projects are unaffected until intake is enabled with an assignee rule; tracker or spawn failures back off per-project without blocking the daemon or other projects.

Closes #2324. Scoped down from the multi-provider design in #2288/#2289 (now parked as draft) to ship GitHub first; Linear and Jira follow as additive slices behind the same seam.

## What this adds

**Backend**
- `TrackerIntakeConfig` on `ProjectConfig` (`enabled`, `provider` — fixed to `github` for now, `repo`, `assignee`), with `Validate()` requiring an assignee when intake is enabled so turning it on cannot drain an entire backlog. **v1 intake is assignee-only** — no label eligibility rule in config/API/CLI.
- `trackerintake.Observer` — a poll loop dispatching through a `TrackerResolver` interface (`SingleTrackerResolver` today). Adding Linear/Jira later is additive: a new adapter implementing `ports.Tracker` plus a resolver-map entry, no changes to poll/eligibility/dedupe/backoff.
- Rate-limit-aware GitHub tracker adapter. Any poll failure — including a GitHub rate limit — puts that project into a 5-minute backoff instead of retrying in a tight loop, and never blocks other projects' polling.
- **Full GitHub pagination.** `List` requests `per_page=100` and follows the `Link` header `rel="next"` until no next link remains, so an assignee with more than one page of open issues is fully swept (single-page listing would let the local `issue_id` dedupe permanently starve later pages). A `maxListPages` guard fails loud on a pathological `Link` cycle; `ListFilter.Limit` is an optional total-result cap.
- **Page-aware ETag conditional caching.** Because intake re-polls the same query every tick, the adapter caches `{ETag, mapped issues, nextPath}` per page path and sends `If-None-Match`. On `304 Not Modified` it returns the cached page and continues to the cached `nextPath` without re-decoding — and a `304` does not consume the primary rate limit — so steady-state polling is nearly free even across multiple pages. The HTTP round-trip was extracted so `Get`/`Preflight` keep identical behavior; the cache is mutex-guarded and bounded by the intake-enabled repo/filter set.
- Daemon wiring constructs the GitHub adapter lazily (only if some project has intake enabled), reusing the existing `AO_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `gh auth token` credential precedence. The observer re-reads each project's config every tick, so a project that enables intake — at creation or later — is picked up on the next poll without a daemon restart.
- CLI: `project set-config --tracker-intake --tracker-repo --tracker-assignee`.
- OpenAPI + generated TS schema regenerated for `TrackerIntakeConfig`.

**Frontend**
- Shared `IntakeFields` component consumed by both the project-settings form and the create-project sheet, so the two surfaces can't drift. A `compact` variant drives the create sheet's leaner presentation.
- **Project settings** Tracker Intake card: a one-line description, the enable toggle, repository auto-detected from the project's git origin and shown as a link (no manual override input for now), and the assignee rule with inline validation (an assignee is required before saving enabled intake).
- **Project creation** the new-project sheet exposes the same intake in a compact form: the enable toggle plus an info (ⓘ) icon whose hover tooltip explains what enabling does, then the assignee input. It drops the descriptive prose, inline validation text, and the repository row (the git origin isn't known there; the daemon derives it server-side). "Create and start" stays disabled until an assignee is set.
- Session cards and the inspector surface the canonical `github:<native>` issue id when a session came from intake.

## Design notes

- Intake is read-only toward GitHub — no comments, no state transitions, no webhook receiver.
- Credentials stay env-var only, daemon-side; the UI never collects or displays tokens.
- The provider field exists end-to-end today but only accepts `github`; the dashboard doesn't render a picker while there's nothing to pick between.
- Intake defaults to off in the create sheet to keep onboarding lean — it's an explicit opt-in.
- v1 eligibility is assignee-only. The generic `domain.ListFilter.Labels` adapter capability is retained for future use; intake config simply doesn't expose labels yet.

## Validation

- `cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/tracker/github/... ./internal/observe/trackerintake/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/cli/...` — green, including the pagination (multi-page accumulation, all-`304` chain continuation, page-count shrink) and `Link`-header parsing cases, and the assignee-required validation. (`go test ./...` still hits the pre-existing duplicate-migration-version-20 panic on `main`, unrelated to this change and already tracked by `fix/migrations-0020-collision`.)
- `npm run api`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `npx vitest run` — 41 files, all green (includes the intake save round-trip, the assignee-required guard, and the create-sheet compact presentation + gating).
- Create-sheet flow driven in the web preview (`dev:web`): the info-icon tooltip surfaces the one-line explanation, enabling reveals the assignee field, submit stays gated until an assignee is set, and a valid submit builds the `trackerIntake` payload into `POST /api/v1/projects`.

## Post-deploy monitoring

For the first project with intake enabled, watch the tracker-intake log lines and confirm one eligible issue creates one worker session carrying the canonical `github:<native>` id. Healthy: no repeated spawn after a second poll or daemon restart, no polling for projects with intake disabled, later pages of a large assignee backlog getting picked up, and steady-state polls returning `304` (served from cache). Rollback trigger: repeated spawn for the same issue, or intake running without an assignee; immediate mitigation is unsetting `trackerIntake.enabled` on the affected project.

title: Add a review-before-send Report a problem diagnostic flow
body:
## Summary

AO should add an explicit, review-before-send **Report a problem** flow that helps users share useful diagnostics without dumping private repo data, prompts, terminal transcripts, or secrets.

This is not a request to make telemetry broader or more automatic. The best first step is a user-controlled support/reporting flow: generate a redacted diagnostic summary, let the user preview it, then let them choose where it goes.

## Why this feels worth doing now

When AO breaks, the useful evidence is scattered across places the average user will not know how to collect:

- Electron renderer errors and PostHog exception breadcrumbs
- daemon status and structured Go logs
- local SQLite telemetry events
- crash dumps under Electron user data
- `ao doctor` output
- current route/surface and daemon readiness state
- project/session context, which must be redacted or hashed carefully

That makes bug reports either too thin ("it broke") or too risky (users paste raw logs with local paths, repo names, prompts, tokens, branch names, issue bodies, etc.). A guided report flow would help maintainers get actionable reports while keeping users in control of what leaves their machine.

## Prior art / research notes

A few mature open-source apps seem to converge on the same pattern:

- **VS Code** separates usage telemetry, error telemetry, and crash reporting behind explicit telemetry levels (`all`, `error`, `crash`, `off`) and documents what each level means: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/telemetry
- **Firefox** explains what crash reports can contain and gives users a case-by-case submission path instead of making every report opaque: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/crash-report
- **Electron** provides `crashReporter`, including local-only collection with `uploadToServer: false`, so desktop apps can gather crash evidence without auto-uploading it: https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/crash-reporter
- **Sentry / PostHog-style tools** are useful for grouping exceptions and breadcrumbs, but they still depend on data scrubbing and user-feedback context to turn an exception into an actionable bug: https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback/ and https://posthog.com/docs/error-tracking/capture
- **GitHub issue forms** work best when the app can generate a structured, pasteable diagnostic block instead of asking users to manually find logs: https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-issue-forms

The common thread: don't ship a scary "send logs" button. Give users a clear preview, safe defaults, and multiple destinations.

## Current AO state

AO already has good pieces to build on:

- Renderer telemetry is documented as automatic PostHog usage/error reporting: `docs/telemetry.md`
- Renderer telemetry already redacts local paths and local URLs before sending: `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts`
- Renderer exceptions are captured through `captureRendererException`: `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts`
- Electron-owned data, including crash dumps, is already pinned under `~/.ao/electron`: `frontend/src/main.ts`
- The daemon has local/remote telemetry sink wiring: `backend/internal/daemon/telemetry_wiring.go`
- Backend 5xx and panic paths already produce structured fingerprints instead of raw payload dumps: `backend/internal/httpd/log.go`, `backend/internal/httpd/recover.go`

The missing piece is a user-facing bridge from "something went wrong" to "here is a safe, useful report I can share".

## Proposed product flow

Add **Report a problem** in a visible place such as:

- Help menu / app menu
- Settings
- error boundary screen after a renderer crash
- daemon error/recovery UI

The dialog could ask:

- What are you reporting?
  - Bug
  - Feature request
  - General feedback
  - Question / setup help
- What happened?
- What did you expect?
- Optional repro steps
- Optional screenshot attachment
- Include diagnostics? default: on
- Include recent logs? default: off or limited preview
- Include crash dump metadata? default: off

Then offer destinations:

- **Copy GitHub issue body**
- **Open GitHub issue** with a prefilled body
- **Copy Discord-ready summary**
- **Copy email-ready report**
- **Export support bundle** as a local `.zip`

That lets the same flow support maintainers, Discord triage, email support, and contributors filing a bug/feature/feedback issue.

## Safe diagnostic bundle: include by default

A first version could include only low-risk structured data:

- AO app version and build mode
- OS / arch
- install source if known
- Electron/Node/runtime versions where easy
- daemon status (`ready`, `stopped`, `starting`, error code/message)
- current UI route surface, not the full local route if it contains IDs
- hashed project/session IDs
- recent telemetry event names, levels, fingerprints, and timestamps
- recent typed API error codes and request IDs
- `ao doctor` summary, redacted
- last N daemon log lines after redaction, with a preview gate
- renderer error name/surface/source, not full user data

## Do not include by default

These should require explicit opt-in or stay excluded entirely:

- repository file contents
- prompts or agent messages
- full terminal transcript
- issue bodies / PR review bodies
- API keys, env vars, tokens, cookies
- raw local paths
- raw project names if they came from local folders
- raw crash minidumps
- full SQLite database
- full daemon log history

## Acceptance criteria for a first useful PR

A narrow first PR could be:

- Add a `Report a problem` entry point in Settings or Help
- Generate a redacted diagnostic object locally
- Show a preview before anything is copied/exported
- Provide buttons for:
  - Copy GitHub issue body
  - Copy Discord summary
  - Export local diagnostic `.json` or `.zip`
- Reuse the existing telemetry sanitization rules where possible
- Add tests for path/token/local URL redaction
- Document exactly what is included and excluded

A later PR can decide whether to add direct upload, direct GitHub issue creation, richer crash dump support, or app-menu integration.

## Why this should not be automatic upload first

AO operates directly around source code, local terminals, worktrees, agents, GitHub/Linear/Jira context, and credentials. Even with good sanitizers, an automatic log uploader would be harder to trust and easier to reject in review.

A preview-first local export flow is safer, easier to merge, and still immediately useful for maintainers.

## Duplicate / overlap check

I checked open and closed issues/PRs for `diagnostic bundle`, `support bundle`, `report problem`, `report issue`, `telemetry feedback`, `crash logs`, and related terms. I did not find a duplicate.

Nearby but different:

- #2210 is about GitHub issue templates. This proposal is about an in-app report/diagnostic bundle flow. They would complement each other: issue templates define the shape, AO fills the useful diagnostic block.

## Suggested implementation areas

Likely frontend/Electron first:

- `frontend/src/main.ts` / preload IPC for diagnostic collection
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts` sanitizers, or a shared redaction helper extracted from it
- Settings/help UI for the report dialog
- optional backend endpoint later if daemon-local telemetry/log summaries should be fetched through the daemon instead of Electron

Likely backend support later:

- expose a safe diagnostic summary endpoint from the daemon
- list recent local telemetry events with payload allowlisting
- expose `ao doctor --json` style diagnostics for the desktop flow

## Priority

P2 / medium enhancement.

This is not blocking core agent workflows, but it would make every future bug report, Discord triage, email support request, and contributor PR much easier to handle safely.

title: Decouple agent-session lifetime from daemon lifetime (survive daemon restart/upgrade)
body:
> **Note (2026-07-02):** original framing corrected after tracing the runtime path. The daemon is already disposable and sessions are already durable in current code; the "build a cross-platform fd-inheriting PTY host" plan is unnecessary. This issue is narrowed to the small remaining gaps. Original problem/solution text preserved at the bottom for history.

## Current reality

The premise the original issue was built on (on Unix the daemon holds the PTY master `*os.File` in-process, so daemon death kills every agent) does not match the code. The runtime is out-of-process on both platforms, the daemon survives its own death, and boot adopts surviving agents.

| Concern | Where | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Unix runtime is tmux, not a daemon-held PTY | `runtimeselect.go:34` (`tmux.New`) | Agent lives in the tmux server, a separate long-lived process. |
| Only daemon-side fd on Unix is an ephemeral attach client | `tmux.go:239` (`ptyexec.Spawn` of `tmux attach-session`) | Daemon death kills the attach client, not the agent. |
| Windows host spawned detached, survives daemon exit | `conpty/spawn_windows.go:54` (`DETACHED_PROCESS \| CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`) | Comment literally: "so the host survives daemon exit." |
| Windows host addr+pid persisted for recovery | `conpty/ptyregistry/registry.go` + `conpty/runtime.go:196` | New daemon re-resolves the session from the registry. |
| Graceful shutdown does NOT tear down sessions | `daemon/daemon.go:174` | "We deliberately do NOT tear down sessions here… next boot's Reconcile adopts them"; teardown-on-shutdown is a compile error. |
| Boot adopts surviving agents | `daemon/daemon.go:151` -> `session_manager/manager.go:658` `reconcileLive`, adopt at `:669` | Alive -> no-op adopt. Dead -> capture work + relaunch. |
| Dead-runtime work preserved | `manager.go:675` `StashUncommitted` | Uncommitted files captured into a preserve ref before relaunch. |

All three original failure modes (daemon crash/restart, graceful shutdown, upgrade to a new binary) already keep agents alive and adopt them on the next boot.

## Remaining work

1. **No per-session crash circuit breaker.** Confirmed absent (only attach backoff exists in `terminal/attachment.go`). A conpty host that crashes on startup could respawn-storm. Add a rolling-window breaker (e.g. 3 crashes / 60s -> stop respawning, surface a typed error, require explicit retry). Low practical exposure today, so it is a guardrail not a fire.

2. **No automated proof durability holds (do first).** No test kills the daemon and asserts the agent survives + is adopted, and no upgrade test. Add: kill-daemon-agent-survives-adopt (Unix, plus Windows `ptyregistry` recovery) and graceful `ao stop && ao start`. If green, the bulk of this issue is closeable as already-done.

3. **Terminal scrollback continuity on re-attach (minor UX).** On restart the `tmux attach` client dies and re-attach redraws the current screen; there is no daemon-side replay ring (`terminal/attachment.go:36`; tmux owns scrollback). Decide whether a bounded ring is worth it or acceptable as-is.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Extracting a cross-platform PTY host / manifest. Unix already has one (tmux); Windows already has one (detached conpty host + `ptyregistry`).
- fd-inheritance handoff (`SCM_RIGHTS` / `ExtraFiles` / ack-before-release). The runtime never lives in the daemon, so upgrade = restart + adopt; there are no live fds to transplant.

Reintroduce either only if a concrete, tested failure shows adoption is insufficient.

---

<details>
<summary>Original issue text (superseded, kept for history)</summary>

## Problem

An agent's life is currently chained to the daemon's life. On Unix (`adapters/runtime/ptyexec/spawn_unix.go`) the daemon holds the PTY master `*os.File` **in-process**, so when the daemon stops for any reason, every running agent dies with it, even though nothing was wrong with the agents.

The daemon is the component that restarts most often, and it's a single point of death for the entire fleet it exists to supervise. Concretely this bites in three ways:

- **Shipping a release is destructive.** A user with N agents mid-task updates AO -> the daemon restarts to load the new binary -> all N agents die.
- **No bulkhead.** A single panic/OOM anywhere in the daemon takes down all agents, including the healthy ones.
- **Long jobs evaporate.** A machine reboot, an Electron-shell bounce, or `ao stop` wipes a 40-minute in-flight task at minute 38.

We already solve half of this on Windows: `adapters/runtime/conpty/host_main.go` runs the PTY in a separate host process. The original proposal was to generalize that pattern with an adopt-don't-respawn supervisor (Phase 2) and fd-inheritance handoff (Phase 3). See the reassessment above: adoption already exists and the fd-host generalization is unnecessary.

</details>

title: fix(desktop): publish nightly feed metadata during stable releases fixes #2271
body:
## Summary

Stable releases currently publish only `latest*.yml` feed metadata. Nightly-channel clients can fail to update to a newer stable release because they request `nightly*.yml`, which is missing from stable releases.

This change makes the stable release workflow generate and upload both:

- `latest*.yml`
- `nightly*.yml`

using the same release metadata.

## Changes

- Generate both latest and nightly feed metadata during stable releases.
- Upload both `latest*.yml` and `nightly*.yml` assets.

## Result

- Nightly clients can update to a newer stable release when no newer nightly exists.
- Stable clients remain unchanged because they continue to use the `latest` channel.

title: bug(send): ao send hangs on multiline — message sits unsubmitted in worker input
body:
## Summary

`ao send` (orchestrator→worker, and back) intermittently leaves the message **unsubmitted** in the
worker's input field. The orchestrator returns HTTP 200 the moment the `tmux send-keys` commands
exit 0, but for a **large multiline** prompt claude-code's TUI never accepts the trailing `Enter`,
so the text sits as an unsubmitted draft until a human presses Enter. `UserPromptSubmit` therefore
never fires, and the orchestrator cannot tell the worker started — it looks identical to an idle
worker, so it polls endlessly. The inverse (worker→orchestrator) has the same symptom.

Related to #2105, but the root shifted: #2105 was the 0.9.2 bracketed-paste path; the Go rewrite
uses `send-keys -l`, yet the same class of failure persists because **paste and Enter fire
back-to-back with no confirmation that the prompt was accepted**.

## Reproduction (live, logged)

Two confirmed cases on the same machine (macOS, tmux, claude-code workers, `~/.ao/daemon.log`):

| time | session | bytes | HTTP | submitted? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10:10:42 | srouter-38 | **3761** (multiline) | 200 | **no** — hung in input |
| 10:20:30 | srouter-37 | **3397** (multiline) | 200 | **no** — hung in input |
| 10:49:27 | srouter-38 | 482 (short) | 200 | yes |
| 10:49:27 | srouter-37 | 357 (short) | 200 | yes |

A manual `tmux send-keys -t <sess> Enter` seconds later submitted the hung text in both cases.

## Root cause

`SendMessage` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:198`) sends `send-keys -l <chunk>`
×N then immediately `send-keys Enter` — **no delay, no retry, no confirmation**:

- For large multiline input the single Enter is absorbed by the paste; claude-code never emits
  `UserPromptSubmit`, so `DeriveActivityState` never flips the session to `active`
  (`claudecode/activity.go:21` — the only producer of `active`).
- A hung message is observationally identical to a finished/idle worker (`status.go:54`: `no_signal`
  clears after the first signal), so the orchestrator can't distinguish "stuck" from "done".

The conpty runtime (Windows) already inserts delays (`conpty/client.go:36-71`: 15ms between chunks,
300ms before Enter); the tmux runtime does not.

## Suggested fix

Make Enter confirmation-based, not fire-and-forget (per #2105's ask: *"retry Enter up to 3× when
the session does not become active/queued"*):

1. After `Enter`, poll the session's `Activity.State` for a short window; if it does not become
   `active`, re-send `Enter` (up to N). This closes the loop for the orchestrator too — `active`
   becomes the observable "the worker started".
2. As a minor guard, port the proven conpty inter-chunk / pre-Enter delays into the tmux adapter so
   the first Enter has a better chance to land.

Same blind-deliver bug also affects review nudges: `lifecycle/reactions.go:536` `sendOnce` stamps the
dedup (`seen[key]=sig`) and `service/review/review.go:235` `MarkReviewRunDelivered` as soon as
`Send` returns nil — a hung nudge is both invisible and dedup-locked, so it is never re-delivered.

## Environment

agent-orchestrator main (post-`c2674206`), macOS arm64, tmux, claude-code workers.

title: fix(status): stop showing open-PR/draft sessions as "Working" in the status pill
body:
Resolves #2345 

## What was wrong

A worker session whose status is `pr_open` or `draft` was shown as a breathing orange **"Working"** pill in the session topbar and inspector — implying the agent is actively working — while the board files the same session under **"In review"** and the sidebar shows a neutral dot. Three surfaces, one contradictory reading: a session that has opened a PR and gone idle awaiting
review was animated as if it were busy coding.

Root cause: two status mappings handled these states differently, and the pill
used the one with no case for them.

- `attentionZone` maps `pr_open`/`draft` → `pending` → board "In review".
- `workerDisplayStatus` had **no case** for `pr_open`/`draft`, so they fell through `default: return "working"` — the one bucket that is orange and breathes (`STATUS_PILL.working = { breathe: true }`).

Both `ShellTopbar` and `SessionInspector` render the pill via `workerDisplayStatus`, so both showed the misleading state.

## What this fixes

Adds a dedicated `in_review` display status covering `pr_open` and `draft`:

- `workerDisplayStatus` now maps `pr_open`/`draft` → `in_review`.
- The pill renders **"In review"**, muted, non-breathing — consistent with the board's "In review" column and the sidebar's neutral dot.
- Reuses the existing `var(--fg-muted)` tone rather than adding a new color, so the "1:1 to accent colors" rule in DESIGN.md still holds.

No new color, no behavior change for any other status.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean — this alone proves every `Record<WorkerDisplayStatus>`
  map (both `STATUS_PILL`s and `workerStatusLabel`) got the new key.
- `npx vitest run src/renderer` (required frontend gate): **255/255 pass**.
- Added `pr_open`/`draft` → `in_review` to the `workerDisplayStatus` mapping
  table and an `in_review` case to the `workerStatusPulses` test.

## Files

- `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.test.ts`

title: Browser tab opens blank for session with stale preview URL instead of falling back to Summary
body:
## Bug
Opening session `agent-orchestrator-19` lands the inspector on an empty Browser tab. The session has useful summary/PR data, so when the saved browser target cannot render the UI should either show live browser content or fall back to the Summary tab.

**Source:** local report in Codex chat
**Reported by:** @chauhan
**Analyzed against:** `c2674206`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** medium - degraded session detail UX; Summary tab is available but hidden behind an empty Browser tab

## Reproduction
1. Open the AO desktop app.
2. Open session `agent-orchestrator-19`.
3. Observe the right inspector rail.

Expected: the right rail renders useful session data, preferably Summary if the preview cannot load.

Actual: the Browser tab is selected and the embedded browser area is empty because the saved preview target does not currently serve content.

## Evidence
- Verified ReverbCode/Go daemon binary built from this checkout: `/tmp/ao status` reports daemon ready on `127.0.0.1:3001`.
- Session state: `/tmp/ao session get agent-orchestrator-19` reports `status: draft`, `activity: idle`, `harness: codex`, `terminated: false`.
- SQLite session row has persisted preview state:
  - `preview_url = http://127.0.0.1:5173/`
  - `preview_revision = 2`
  - `updated_at = 2026-07-01 14:10:24 UTC`
- The saved preview URL is stale/dead now: `curl -I --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:5173/` fails with connection refused.
- The same session has PR data that Summary can render, including open/draft PRs `#2315`, `#2322`, `#2327`, and `#2328`.

## Root Cause
The frontend treats any non-empty `session.previewUrl` as enough reason to select and render Browser, but it does not fall back when the embedded browser has no reachable content.

Relevant code:
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx`: lines 56-85 derive `previewUrl` and switch `inspectorView` to `"browser"` whenever `previewUrl` is non-empty.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx`: lines 223-233 pass the controlled `inspectorView` directly into `SessionInspector`.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`: lines 128-139 render only the selected tab; when `view === "browser"`, Summary is not mounted.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`: lines 649-660 render `BrowserPanelView` whenever `browserView` exists.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/BrowserPanel.tsx`: lines 112-119 only shows the "Enter a dev-server URL" overlay when `navState.url === ""`; a stale non-empty URL can leave the Browser panel blank/failed instead of showing Summary.

## Suggested Fix
Add a guard around Browser tab selection/rendering:
- If `previewUrl` is empty, or the browser nav state has no successfully loaded content/error for a stale preview, keep or restore the inspector tab to `summary`.
- Preserve the existing behavior where a fresh `ao preview` with a reachable URL opens the inspector and selects Browser.
- Add a regression test in `SessionView.test.tsx` for a session with stale preview state / cleared preview returning to Summary rather than showing an empty Browser tab.

## Duplicate Search
No existing issues found for:
- `empty browser summary tab`
- `Browser tab previewUrl`
- `SessionInspector Browser`

title: Add sidebar Feedback report flow
body:
## Summary
Refs #2331

Adds a first, review-before-handoff feedback/reporting flow in the sidebar footer:
- places a dedicated Feedback action directly above Settings in expanded and collapsed sidebar modes
- opens an in-place report dialog with only two user-written fields: `Summary` and `Details`
- shows a preview of the exact draft that will be copied/opened before any handoff
- lets the user choose the reviewed destination from the preview dropdown:
  - `Raise GitHub issue` opens a new issue URL with the title/body prefilled
  - `Report on Discord` opens the official community invite from the README: `https://discord.com/invite/UZv7JjxbwG`
  - `Email support` opens the confirmed AO support mailbox: `support@aoagents.dev`
- copies the reviewed draft to the clipboard before opening the selected destination
- includes safe diagnostics by default: AO version, daemon state, route surface, build mode, platform, and generated timestamp
- redacts local paths, local URLs, JSON/header/assignment secrets, OpenAI keys, GitHub token forms, and common token/key/password values before preview, clipboard copy, or URL generation
- clears the draft fields on close and after successful handoff so sensitive report text is not retained in the dialog

This intentionally does not auto-submit anything, upload anything, or collect raw logs, prompts, terminal transcript, repo contents, issue/PR bodies, env vars, crash dumps, or SQLite data. The user still reviews the draft before sending it anywhere.

## Follow-ups intentionally left out
- direct upload / send flow
- JSON or zip diagnostic export
- raw crash metadata attachment
- daemon-side diagnostic bundle endpoint
- richer destination configuration for maintainers

title: Cut ~3,000 LOC of redundancy in the agent adapter layer
body:
## Summary

The agent adapter layer (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/`, 23 adapters, ~8,000 LOC) has accumulated a large amount of copy-pasted and near-duplicate code. An audit found roughly **~3,000 LOC (~37%) that can be cut** by consolidating shared logic, with no behavioral change and at least one latent correctness fix (missing `fsync`) surfaced along the way.

## Adapter layer map

- **Location:** `backend/internal/adapters/agent/`
- **23 adapters** registered in `registry/registry.go`, each a directory with up to 4 files: `<name>.go` (main), `activity.go` (hook event to activity state), `hooks.go` (install/uninstall/check), plus tests.
- **Shared interface:** `ports.Agent` (`backend/internal/ports/agent.go:20`): `GetConfigSpec`, `GetLaunchCommand`, `GetPromptDeliveryStrategy`, `GetAgentHooks`, `GetRestoreCommand`, `SessionInfo`. Plus `adapters.Adapter` which adds `Manifest()`.

## Findings (ranked by LOC saved)

### 1. Hook install/uninstall/check skeleton duplicated across 10 adapters (~1,500 LOC)
The "matcher-group" adapters (claudecode, droid, goose, qwen, agy, cursor, kiro, autohand, cline, copilot) share the same 3-method skeleton (`GetAgentHooks` / `UninstallHooks` / `AreHooksInstalled`) plus their read/write/parse/marshal helpers. They differ only in a type-name prefix (`claudeMatcherGroup`, `gooseMatcherGroup`, etc.); the group/entry structs are structurally identical (`Matcher *string`, `Hooks []Entry` with `Type/Command/Timeout`).

Refs: `claudecode/hooks.go:77-186`, `goose/hooks.go:70-179`, `agy/hooks.go:53-170`, `droid/hooks.go:76-200`, `cursor/hooks.go:64-170`, `kiro/hooks.go:71-185`, `qwen/hooks.go:83-200`, `autohand/hooks.go:129-230`, `cline/hooks.go:66-170`.

**Fix:** Extract a generic `hooksjson` package (`HookEntry`, `MatcherGroup`, `Read/WriteHooksFile`, `Parse/MarshalHookEvent`, `Install/Uninstall/AreHooksInstalled`). Each adapter reduces to a `ManagedHooks []HookSpec` constant + path derivation.

### 2. Binary resolver boilerplate across all 23 adapters (~650 LOC)
Every adapter has the same shape: `ResolveXxxBinary(ctx)` (LookPath then iterate candidate paths with fileExists) + a cached `p.xxxBinary(ctx)` (mutex + resolvedBinary cache). Only the binary name(s) and well-known install paths vary. Each pair is 30-60 lines.

Refs: `claudecode/claudecode.go:348-415`, `codex/codex.go:153-254`, `goose/goose.go:239-326`, `amp/amp.go:151-224`, and every other `<name>/<name>.go`.

**Fix:** Table-driven shared resolver, e.g. `binaryutil.ResolveBinary(ctx, BinarySpec)` where `BinarySpec` carries `Names/WinNames/ExtraPaths/HomePaths/AppDataPaths`. Per-adapter shrinks to a ~5-10 line `BinarySpec` literal.

### 3. `normalizePermissionMode()` duplicated 17 times (~100 LOC)
Identical 4-case body across most adapters.

Refs: `claudecode/claudecode.go:331`, `codex/codex.go:319`, `goose/goose.go:221`, `cursor/cursor.go:227`, `kiro/kiro.go:256`, `qwen/qwen.go:246`, `kilocode/kilocode.go:227`, `copilot/copilot.go:260`, `autohand/autohand.go:178`, `cline/cline.go:247`, `continueagent/continueagent.go:266`, `grok/grok.go:275`, `devin/devin.go:268`, `aider/aider.go:130`, `opencode/opencode.go:173`, `kimi/kimi.go:172`, `droid/droid.go:337`.

**Fix:** Move `NormalizePermissionMode(mode PermissionMode)` into the `ports` package.

### 4. Identical `DeriveActivityState` bodies in 9 activity.go files (~250 LOC)
Same 4-case switch (session-start/user-prompt-submit -> active, stop -> idle, permission-request -> waiting_input) across autohand, cline, cursor, goose, kiro, kilocode, copilot, qwen (opencode has 3 of 4).

Refs: `cursor/activity.go:17-30`, `cline/activity.go:28-40`, `goose/activity.go:22-35`, `kiro/activity.go:21-34`, etc.

**Fix:** Shared `StandardDeriveActivityState(event string, _ []byte)` helper. **Keep claudecode/droid separate** (they parse JSON payloads for finer-grained state).

### 5. `atomicWriteFile()` re-defined 7 times, some missing fsync (~126 LOC, + correctness)
`hookutil.AtomicWriteFile` already exists and does exactly this, yet 7 hooks files carry a private copy. Some copies **omit the `tmp.Sync()`** the hookutil version includes, silently skipping the fsync.

Refs: `goose/hooks.go:242`, `copilot/hooks.go:250`, `cline/hooks.go:183`, `autohand/hooks.go:305`, `kiro/hooks.go:240`, `kilocode/hooks.go:167`, `qwen/hooks.go:256`.

**Fix:** Delete all 7 copies; call `hookutil.AtomicWriteFile` (already done in claudecode, codex, agy, cursor, droid).

### 6. `SessionInfo` boilerplate across 19 adapters (~100 LOC)
Two shapes: a "read agentSessionID from metadata or return false" body (cline, cursor, copilot, droid, grok, devin, agy, autohand, kiro, continueagent) and a fully-no-op variant (amp, auggie, crush, kimi, pi, vibe, aider).

Refs: `cline/cline.go:130-146`, `cursor/cursor.go:134-146`, `copilot/copilot.go:139-152`, `devin/devin.go:159-171`, `droid/droid.go:159-171`.

**Fix:** `StandardSessionInfo` + `MetadataOnlySessionInfo` helpers. **Keep goose separate** (custom metadata keys, `goose/goose.go:157-158`).

### 7. `GetPromptDeliveryStrategy` identical 5-line body in all 23 adapters (~115 LOC)
Every adapter returns `ports.PromptDeliveryInCommand` after a `ctx.Err()` guard.

**Fix:** Embeddable `BaseAgent` struct defining the method once, or make `PromptDeliveryInCommand` the default and drop it from the required interface surface.

### 8. `GetConfigSpec` no-op repeated ~22 times (~100 LOC)
Every adapter except claudecode returns `ports.ConfigSpec{}, nil` after a `ctx.Err()` guard. Refs: `codex/codex.go:52-57`, `aider/aider.go:55-60`, `amp/amp.go:54-59`, `goose/goose.go:78-83`, +17.

**Fix:** `BaseAgent` embed or shared `NilConfigSpec`.

### 9. Tier-C no-op stubs: `GetAgentHooks` / `GetRestoreCommand` (~80 LOC)
8 hookless adapters (amp, auggie, aider, kimi, pi, vibe, crush, devin) carry identical no-op stubs. Refs: `amp/amp.go:101-103`, `auggie/auggie.go:131-133`, `aider/aider.go:105-107`, `kimi/kimi.go:110-112`, `pi/pi.go:127-129`, `vibe/vibe.go:115-117`, `crush/crush.go:15-20`.

**Fix:** `BaseAgent` embed, or split `ports.Agent` into a required `AgentLauncher` + optional `AgentHooker`/`ConfigProvider` checked via type assertion (already how `PreLaunch` works in claudecode).

### 10. `fileExists()` copied into every adapter, 23 identical copies (~46 LOC)
```go
func fileExists(path string) bool {
    info, err := os.Stat(path)
    return err == nil && !info.IsDir()
}
```
Refs: one per `<name>/<name>.go` (e.g. `claudecode/claudecode.go:506`, `codex/codex.go:331`, ...).

**Fix:** Add `FileExists` to `hookutil` (alongside `AtomicWriteFile`, `EnsureWorkspaceGitignore`).

## Deliberately keep separate (do not over-consolidate)

- **Permission/approval flag mapping** per adapter (Claude `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, Codex `--ask-for-approval on-request`, Goose `GOOSE_MODE=smart_approve`, Aider `--yes-always --no-auto-commits`) is genuine per-agent behavior.
- **Binary candidate lists** differ meaningfully (`~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.claude/local`, `$LOCALAPPDATA/Programs`, codex's `windowsNativeCodexCandidatesForShim`). Share the iteration, not the lists.
- **`readXxxHooks`/`writeXxxHooks` across format families** (Copilot owns its whole file, Cline uses per-file scripts not JSON, Codex delivers config via launch flags). Share only within the matcher-group cohort.
- **claudecode/droid `DeriveActivityState`** parse JSON payloads for fine-grained state.

## Estimated savings

| Finding | Adapters | Est. LOC |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Hook install/uninstall/check skeleton | 10 | ~1,500 |
| 2. Binary resolver boilerplate | 23 | ~650 |
| 3. `normalizePermissionMode` | 17 | ~100 |
| 4. Identical `DeriveActivityState` | 9 | ~250 |
| 5. `atomicWriteFile` re-definitions | 7 | ~126 |
| 6. `SessionInfo` boilerplate | 19 | ~100 |
| 7. `GetPromptDeliveryStrategy` | 23 | ~115 |
| 8. `GetConfigSpec` no-op | 22 | ~100 |
| 9. Tier-C stubs | 8 | ~80 |
| 10. `fileExists` | 23 | ~46 |
| **Total** | | **~3,067** |

## Suggested sequencing

1. **Safe dedup batch** (findings 3, 4, 5, 10) as one low-risk PR. Includes the fsync correctness fix.
2. **Binary resolver** extraction (finding 2).
3. **Interface-shape** cleanup (findings 6-9), via `BaseAgent` embed or interface split.
4. **Generic `hooksjson` package** (finding 1) as its own reviewed change (largest, highest-effort).

title: test(session_manager): prove agent sessions survive daemon restart/upgrade (#2335)
body:
Closes #2335 (the "do first" item).

## Context

After tracing the runtime path end to end, #2335 was narrowed: the daemon is already disposable and agent sessions are already durable across restart/upgrade. The runtime lives out-of-process on both platforms (tmux server on Unix; detached conpty host + `ptyregistry` on Windows), graceful shutdown deliberately does **not** tear sessions down (`daemon/daemon.go`), and boot `Reconcile` adopts survivors. The one thing missing was an automated proof that this holds, which the issue flagged as "do first... if green, the bulk of this issue is closeable as already-done."

## What this PR adds

`TestReconcile_AdoptAcrossDaemonRestart` drives the full boot-time `Reconcile()` pass over the exact mix of session states a daemon restart/upgrade leaves behind, and asserts sessions are decoupled from the daemon's lifetime:

- **Alive orchestrator → adopted in place**: same id, still live, runtime never torn down, and **no new session minted**. This is the id-increment regression guard (the promptless-orchestrator adoption failure that used to mint a fresh id 14→15→16).
- **Alive worker → adopted** as a no-op.
- **Dead worker** (runtime died with the daemon) → work captured into a preserve ref, restore marker written, then **relaunched under its original id** on the same boot; one-shot marker consumed (#2319).
- **Truly-dead, unmarked session → not resurrected** (stays terminated).

Graceful `ao stop` and crash both converge on this same boot-time `Reconcile` path (shutdown does not teardown), so the test covers both.

## Assessed and deferred (per the issue's own framing)

- **Per-session crash circuit breaker (#2335 item 1):** deferred. There is no auto-respawn supervisor in normal operation, relaunch happens once per boot (not a tight loop), and the only existing loop, terminal re-attach, already has its own bounded breaker (`terminal/attachment.go`). A 60s rolling-window breaker would guard a storm surface that does not structurally exist today. Reintroduce if an auto-respawn supervisor lands. Happy to add it in this PR if preferred.
- **Terminal scrollback continuity on re-attach (#2335 item 3):** acceptable as-is. tmux owns scrollback and re-answers the init handshake on every fresh attach; a daemon-side replay ring is not worth the complexity.

## Verification

```
go build ./...   # clean
go vet ./...      # clean
go test ./...     # 1685 passed in 80 packages
```

title: Orchestrator-created agents ignore explicit harness and fall back to project defaults
body:
## Bug
When the orchestrator is asked to create an agent with a specific harness, the spawned agent can still use the harness configured in project settings. An explicit harness request should win over the project's default worker/orchestrator agent.

**Source:** local report in Codex chat
**Reported by:** @chauhan
**Analyzed against:** `e74fb65a853f64bc4c8bfec2720cc078b572a3a5`
**Confidence:** Medium
**Priority:** medium - explicit user intent is ignored, but project defaults still produce a session

## Reproduction
1. Configure a project with a default agent in project settings, for example `worker.agent = claude-code`.
2. Ask the orchestrator/CLI flow to create an agent using a different harness, for example `codex`.
3. Observe the spawned session's harness.

Expected: the new session uses the explicitly requested harness (`codex` in this example).

Actual: the new session uses the project setting default (`claude-code` in this example).

## Root Cause / Why This Looks CLI-Side
The CLI has an explicit harness override for worker sessions, but the orchestrator creation path does not carry a harness field.

Relevant code:
- `backend/internal/cli/spawn.go` accepts `--harness` / `--agent` and sends `SpawnSessionRequest.harness` to `POST /api/v1/sessions`.
- `backend/internal/cli/orchestrator.go` only supports `ao orchestrator ls`; there is no CLI spawn/create command that can pass a harness override for an orchestrator-created session.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` defines `SpawnOrchestratorRequest` with only `projectId` and `clean`.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` decodes `SpawnOrchestratorRequest` and calls `Svc.SpawnOrchestrator(projectID, clean)` without any harness input.
- `backend/internal/service/session/service.go` calls `s.Spawn(ctx, ports.SpawnConfig{ProjectID: projectID, Kind: domain.KindOrchestrator})`, leaving harness resolution to project config/defaults.

Because the explicit requested harness is not represented in the CLI/API request, the daemon cannot distinguish "use project default" from "use this harness for this spawn."

## Probable Fix
Implement the override at the CLI/API boundary:

1. Add a harness/agent option to the orchestrator creation CLI path, likely `ao orchestrator spawn --project <id> --harness <agent>` with `--agent` as an alias matching `ao spawn`.
2. Extend `SpawnOrchestratorRequest` with optional `harness`.
3. Thread the optional harness through `SessionsController.spawnOrchestrator` into the session service.
4. Update `Service.SpawnOrchestrator` or add a sibling method/input struct so it calls `s.Spawn` with `ports.SpawnConfig{ProjectID, Kind: domain.KindOrchestrator, Harness: <explicit>}` when provided.
5. Keep project config as the fallback only when no explicit harness is supplied.
6. Add tests:
   - CLI test asserting `ao orchestrator spawn --project demo --harness codex` sends `{"projectId":"demo","harness":"codex"}`.
   - HTTP/controller test asserting `POST /api/v1/orchestrators` accepts and forwards `harness`.
   - Service test asserting explicit harness overrides the project's role default.
7. Regenerate API artifacts with `npm run api` because the request DTO changes.

## Duplicate Search
No exact duplicate found for:
- `orchestrator harness project settings default`
- `specified harness defaults project settings`

Adjacent but not the same:
- #2276 covered frontend task creation ignoring project defaults; this report is about explicit orchestrator/CLI harness intent being lost and project defaults winning.

title: preview: poller does not clear stale preview_url when workspace entry file is deleted
body:
## Summary

The preview poller detects when a workspace entry file appears and sets `preview_url` in SQLite. But when that file is later deleted, the poller silently skips the session and leaves the stale URL in SQLite indefinitely. The embedded browser then either renders a 404 or keeps showing a cached version of a page that no longer exists on disk.

## Reproduction

1. Start a session in a workspace without an existing `index.html`.

2. Ask the agent to generate a frontend page or scaffold a simple HTML app.

3. Agent creates:

```text
/workspace/index.html
```

4. Preview poller detects the file and sets:

```text
preview_url = .../preview/files/index.html
```

5. Continue prompting the agent to refactor/restructure the project.

6. During refactoring, the agent deletes `index.html` (common when switching frameworks, reorganizing directories, or regenerating frontend structure).

7. Observe:

* `index.html` no longer exists on disk
* `preview_url` remains persisted in SQLite
* Browser panel still auto-opens using the stale URL
* Embedded browser renders either:

  * a 404 page, or
  * a cached/stale version of the deleted page

8. Restarting or opening a new session may still auto-select the Browser tab because the stale `preview_url` remains stored.

## Root Cause

In `backend/internal/preview/poller.go` line 114–115:

```go
entry, ok := DiscoverEntry(sess.Metadata.WorkspacePath)
if !ok {
    continue // stale preview_url is never cleared
}
```

When `DiscoverEntry` returns `ok=false`, the poller moves on without checking whether the session currently has a workspace-type `preview_url` that should now be cleared.

## Evidence

**SQLite state — stale URLs persisted for 4 sessions:**

```text
dummy-14 | http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/dummy-14/preview/files/index.html | revision 2
dummy-12 | http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/dummy-12/preview/files/index.html | revision 3
dummy-10 | http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/dummy-10/preview/files/index.html | revision 6
dummy-13 | http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/dummy-13/preview/files/index.html | revision 3
```

**Disk verification — entry files missing for all 4:**

```text
~/.ao/data/worktrees/dummy-14/index.html → MISSING
~/.ao/data/worktrees/dummy-12/index.html → MISSING
~/.ao/data/worktrees/dummy-10/index.html → MISSING
~/.ao/data/worktrees/dummy-13/index.html → MISSING
```

## User Impact

* Browser panel renders a 404 or stale cached page with no explanation
* Opening a new session from the same project may auto-select the Browser tab due to the persisted non-empty `preview_url`, showing an empty/failed browser instead of the Summary tab
---

This issue is likely the underlying root cause of the broader browser/session-state problem tracked here:

Issue #2347 appears to describe the downstream symptom — stale or incorrect browser state selection caused by persisted `preview_url` values — whereas the bug described here identifies the persistence layer failure that allows those stale preview URLs to survive after the workspace entry file has been deleted.
* User has no recourse except manually running:

```bash
ao preview clear
```

## Suggested Fix

In `poller.go`, after `DiscoverEntry` returns `ok=false`, add a guard:

```go
if !ok {
    // If this session has a stale workspace preview URL, clear it
    if isWorkspacePreviewURL(sess.Metadata.PreviewURL, sess.ID) {
        p.setter.SetPreview(ctx, sess.ID, "")
    }
    continue
}
```

The helper `isWorkspacePreviewURL` already exists in the codebase. This fix only clears URLs the poller itself set — manually set dev server URLs (`http://localhost:5173`) are left untouched.

## Files to Change

* `backend/internal/preview/poller.go` — add clear logic on `ok=false`
* `backend/internal/preview/poller_test.go` — add test case for file deletion scenario

## Duplicate Search

No existing issues found for:

* `preview_url stale`
* `poller clear`
* `preview 404`
