title: feat: enhance Kiro agent integration with custom AO agent prompts
body:
## Summary

This PR updates the Kiro agent integration to run through a workspace-local AO custom agent instead of relying on Kiro headless mode. The custom agent now carries AO's standing system prompt, project-level model configuration, and existing hook setup, so Kiro sessions behave consistently for both worker and orchestrator flows.

## Changes Made

- Updated Kiro launch commands from:
  - `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive ...`
  - to `kiro-cli chat --agent ao ...`
- Added support for a Kiro custom agent file at `.kiro/agents/ao.json`.
- Writes AO-managed custom agent defaults into the Kiro agent file:
  - `name: "ao"`
  - `description`
  - `prompt` from AO system prompt
  - `tools`
  - `mcpServers`
  - `toolAliases`
  - `allowedTools`
  - `resources`
  - `toolsSettings`
  - `includeMcpJson`
  - optional `model`
- Preserves user/custom Kiro agent fields where safe, while overwriting AO-managed fields like:
  - `name`
  - `prompt`
  - configured `model`
- Propagates session kind and agent config through launch, restore, and workspace hook installation.
- Added a new prompt delivery strategy: `custom_agent`.
- Kiro orchestrator sessions without an explicit task prompt now use the custom agent prompt instead of command-line prompt delivery.
- Restore flow now reinstalls hooks/custom agent config after recomputing the system prompt and effective agent config.
- Expanded Kiro adapter tests for:
  - interactive launch command shape
  - orchestrator launch behavior
  - prompt precedence
  - prompt delivery strategy
  - custom Kiro agent file creation
  - system prompt writing
  - model configuration writing and overwrite behavior
  - restore command behavior
- Kiro now uses its normal interactive approval flow instead of forced headless mode.
- Orchestrator standing instructions are delivered through Kiro's custom agent prompt, making Kiro behavior closer to other AO-managed agent integrations.
- Project-level model settings are respected by Kiro sessions through the generated custom agent file.
- Restored Kiro sessions keep the same AO instructions and agent configuration as fresh sessions.
- Existing Kiro hooks remain managed through the same workspace-local file, with custom/non-managed fields preserved where possible.
- This should improve Kiro reliability for orchestrator sessions because AO no longer depends on passing all instructions through a one-shot command prompt.

## Files Changed

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/kiro.go`
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/hooks.go`
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/kiro_test.go`
- `backend/internal/ports/agent.go`
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`

## Testing

Ran focused Kiro adapter tests:

```bash
GOCACHE=/private/tmp/go-build-ao-kiro go test ./internal/adapters/agent/kiro
```

Result:

```
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro
```

## Why We Did Not Use a File-Based Prompt Approach

We considered writing the AO system prompt to a separate file and passing that file into Kiro at launch time, but avoided that approach for a few reasons:

- Kiro already has a first-class custom agent mechanism via `.kiro/agents/*.json`.
- Using the custom agent file keeps AO aligned with Kiro's native configuration model instead of inventing a parallel prompt-loading path.
- A separate prompt file would require extra lifecycle handling during spawn, restore, cleanup, and hook reinstall flows.
- File-based prompt injection would make it easier for the launch command, prompt file, hooks, and project model config to drift out of sync.
- The custom agent approach keeps related Kiro configuration in one place:
  - system prompt
  - model
  - tools
  - MCP settings
  - hooks
- It also lets orchestrator sessions start without a command-line prompt while still receiving standing AO instructions through the Kiro agent configuration.

In short, the custom agent approach is more idiomatic for Kiro, easier to restore consistently, and keeps AO's Kiro integration closer to the daemon-managed workspace configuration model.
closes #2436

title: fix: omit unsupported Amp system prompt flags
body:
---

## What changed
- Removed Amp launch args for `--append-system-prompt` and `--append-system-prompt-file`.
- Updated Amp adapter comments to document that `SystemPrompt` and `SystemPromptFile` are ignored until Amp exposes a supported instruction mechanism.
- Updated Amp adapter tests to assert:
  - inline system prompts are ignored
  - file-based system prompts are ignored
  - unsupported Amp system prompt flags are not emitted

## Why
Amp does not support the Claude-style system prompt flags AO was passing. When Amp is selected as an orchestrator agent, AO launched a command like:

```sh

Amp rejects that immediately with:

error: unknown option '--append-system-prompt'
```

This caused Amp orchestrator sessions to exit on startup. The safest fix is to stop passing unsupported flags and keep Amp launch behavior limited to supported CLI args.

title: Improve prompt delivery strategy and update launch command logic
body:
AO orchestrator sessions are promptless by design, but the Continue adapter always launched fresh sessions with
  cn --print. Continue rejects --print unless a prompt, --prompt, --agent, or resume target is provided, causing
  promptless orchestrator launches to fail immediately with:

  Error: A prompt is required when using the -p/--print flag, unless --prompt, --agent, or --resume is provided.

  The adapter now only uses --print for prompted launches and starts promptless Continue sessions interactively.

  Changes

  - Updated Continue launch command construction:
      - Prompted launch remains:

        cn --print [permission flags] -- <prompt>

      - Promptless launch is now:

        cn [permission flags]

  - Added a Continue-specific prompt delivery strategy:
      - Prompted launches return PromptDeliveryInCommand.
      - Promptless launches return PromptDeliveryAfterStart.

  - Preserved existing permission behavior:
      - default and accept-edits emit no Continue permission flag.
      - auto and bypass-permissions emit --auto.

  - Left restore behavior unchanged:

    cn --print [permission flags] --fork <agentSessionId>
    This remains valid because --fork provides a resume target.

  Why
  Continue’s --print mode is for non-interactive prompt/resume execution. For promptless AO orchestrator sessions,
  there is no prompt to pass, so launching cn --print produces a CLI usage error before the session can start.

  Tests
  Updated backend/internal/adapters/agent/continueagent tests to cover:

  - Promptless launch uses cn without --print.
  - Promptless launch still applies permission flags such as --auto.
  - Prompted launch still uses cn --print -- <prompt>.
  - Prompted launch returns PromptDeliveryInCommand.
  - Promptless launch returns PromptDeliveryAfterStart.
  - Prompt delivery strategy honors canceled context.
  - Restore still uses cn --print --fork <agentSessionId>.
  
  closes #2439

title: feat(preview): agent driven browser previews + Markdown rendering
body:
## Problem

The desktop browser panel could only ever auto-open a file literally named `index.html` (or its `public`/`dist`/`build` variants). Anything else an agent produced — a standalone `report.html`, a chart, a Markdown write-up — could not be surfaced in the panel. Markdown was doubly broken: even when pointed at directly, `.md` files were served by `http.ServeFile` as `text/plain`, so the webview showed raw source instead of a rendered document.

We wanted the agent to decide what to show (similar to how an artifact-aware coding tool opens a preview), while keeping `index.html` auto-opening as a zero-effort fallback.

## What changed

- **Markdown rendering.** The `preview/files` route now converts `.md`/`.markdown` to a styled, self-contained HTML document (goldmark + GitHub-flavored extensions: tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks) and serves it as `text/html`. All other files are served verbatim as before, so the frontend needs no changes — a `.md` URL simply returns rendered HTML.
- **Agent-driven previews.** Worker sessions get a standing system-prompt instruction to run `ao preview <file>` proactively for artifacts a human should see (HTML pages, reports, charts, Markdown docs). This is the mechanism that makes "the agent decides what to open" actually happen; the command doc already documented the CLI usage.
- **Conservative auto-open (poller).** Discovery is split into `DiscoverIndexEntry` (index anchors only) and `DiscoverEntry` (index, then most-recently-modified previewable file). The background poller now uses index-only, so it auto-opens a real app entry but never guesses at loose files. The full most-recent fallback is kept only for a bare, agent-initiated `ao preview`.

## The bug found and fixed along the way

While testing, `ao preview report.html` appeared to do nothing: the panel stayed blank and the session's `previewRevision` kept climbing while `previewUrl` stayed empty. Root cause: after the poller became index-only, any workspace without an `index.html` made it treat the agent's own `/preview/files/...` URL as stale and clear it on every ~250ms cycle — erasing the agent's explicit preview almost immediately. The poller now clears a preview only when it itself opened it for an `index.html` that has since disappeared, and never touches a preview the agent set explicitly.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/preview/... ./internal/httpd/controllers/...` — passes. New/updated tests cover: index precedence and most-recent fallback, the index-only discovery used by the poller, Markdown rendering (HTML document, GFM table, title escaping), the poller ignoring loose non-index files, and the regression fix (`TestPollerPreservesExplicitNonIndexPreview` — the poller must leave an agent-set non-index preview untouched across multiple poll cycles).
- Verified live in the app: `index.html` still auto-opens; `ao preview sample.html` and `ao preview test.md` (relative paths) both persist and render, with Markdown shown as a formatted document rather than raw text.

## Files affected

- `backend/internal/preview/entry.go` — split discovery into `DiscoverIndexEntry` (index-only) and `DiscoverEntry` (index + most-recent fallback); added `IsMarkdownPath`.
- `backend/internal/preview/markdown.go` (new) — goldmark-based `RenderMarkdown` with an embedded light/dark stylesheet.
- `backend/internal/preview/poller.go` — poller uses index-only discovery and only clears previews it opened, never the agent's.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` — `previewFile` renders Markdown to HTML; other files unchanged.
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` — standing worker prompt block instructing proactive `ao preview <file>`.
- `backend/internal/preview/entry_test.go`, `markdown_test.go` (new), `poller_test.go` — coverage for the above.
- `backend/go.mod`, `backend/go.sum` — goldmark dependency (promoted from indirect).

title: feat(frontend): IDE-style file explorer for project files beside the kanban (like Claude Desktop / Cursor agents window)
body:
## Summary

Add an IDE-style **file explorer** to the desktop app that shows the **project's actual files** (the repository the project points at), docked on the right side of the kanban board — the same pattern as Claude Desktop (Cowork) and Cursor's agents window, where a file tree sits alongside the agent view and clicking a file opens it in a read-only viewer.

## Motivation

While orchestrating agents from the kanban, there's currently no way to look at the project's source without leaving the app — you have to open the repo in an external editor or browse GitHub. That context switch is expensive when you just want to:

- Check what a file looks like before writing a task prompt for an agent
- Reference an exact file path or function while reviewing a session
- Skim the project layout to decide how to split work across sessions

A lightweight explorer over the project directory keeps that all in one window, matching what Claude Desktop and Cursor already do for their agent surfaces.

## Proposed UX

- Collapsible **right-side panel on the kanban/dashboard view** showing a file tree of the current project's repository (the project root, not a session worktree)
- Clicking a file opens a read-only preview with syntax highlighting; markdown rendered
- Quick-open by name (⌘P-style fuzzy finder)
- Respects `.gitignore` (hide `node_modules`, build output, etc.)
- Read-only in v1 — editing is out of scope

## Prior art / related work

- #1313 builds a file tree + viewer for the web dashboard, but scoped to a **session's worktree** on the session detail page. This request is different: it's the **project's own repo** browsable from the board. The tree/viewer components and file-serving API shape could still be shared.
- #1321 (reactive sync RFC) mentions file-tree/file-content sync; whatever transport lands there could drive this panel's refresh instead of ad-hoc polling.

## Out of scope (v1)

- In-app file editing
- Full-text search across file contents
- Git operations from the tree

title: fix(cli): wrong exit code on too many args for review submit and preview
body:
Cobra's built-in arg validators (`cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)`, `cobra.NoArgs`) return plain errors, not `usageError`. The root command's `SetFlagErrorFunc` only wraps flag parse errors, so arg-count misuse exits code 1 instead of the documented convention of 2.

Adds an `atMostOneArg` helper (same pattern as the existing `noArgs`) that wraps `cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)` in `usageError`. Uses it for `review submit` and `preview`. Uses the existing `noArgs` for `preview clear`.

Adds three table tests asserting exit code 2 for too-many-args misuse.

Closes #2418

title: feat: feature releases (per-PR installable prerelease builds)
body:
## Feature releases: per-PR shareable prerelease builds, installable in-app

Implements the capability specified in #2366: cut a shareable, installable build of a single **unmerged PR** so it can be dogfooded or demoed in isolation, without dragging in the rest of nightly. Exposed in-app as a third update channel alongside Stable and Nightly.

### What this adds

- **`feature-release.yml`** (`workflow_dispatch`): builds a chosen PR's head as a signed GitHub **prerelease** on an isolated `pr<N>` update channel. Gated behind the same protected `release` environment as stable (required-reviewer approval; the approver must vet the PR head SHA because the build runs unmerged code with signing-secret access). Guard job enforces a 5-build quota and open/non-fork PR checks before the approval; `publish-feed` asserts it never writes `latest*`/`nightly*` manifests (the #2270 `latest-mac.yml` poisoning class).
- **`feature-release-cleanup.yml`**: retires builds on PR close/merge and via a daily 7-day expiry sweep. Only ever touches `pr<N>` prereleases.
- **Main-process engine** (`feature-builds.ts`): lists feature builds from the same repo the app updates from (resolved from `app-update.yml`, so a fork build dogfoods fork releases), filtered to open PRs within the 7-day window and grouped to the newest build per PR. `configureFeed` gains a `pr<N>` branch so the existing electron-updater GitHub provider tracks a pinned PR's newest build natively.
- **Settings UI**: the Updates card gains a "Feature Releases" channel option, a secondary PR-build picker (build id + freshness), and an active-build banner with a "Return to Stable/Nightly" action. The home channel (`latest`/`nightly`) is stored separately and never overwritten by pinning.
- **Version scheme** `v<base>-pr<N>.<ts>`: the slug is display-only and never in the tag, because electron-updater keys the channel off the semver prerelease id (`semver.prerelease(tag)[0]`).

### Isolation, verified

The "no nightly hijack / no stable contamination" guarantee is confirmed against the installed `electron-updater@6.8.9` `GitHubProvider.getLatestVersion()`: prerelease channels are matched by prerelease identifier, so `pr<N>` never collides with `nightly`, and stable resolves only non-prereleases. A regression test (`feature-channel-resolution.test.mjs`) encodes this so a future electron-updater bump that breaks it fails CI.

### Tests / checks

`tsc --noEmit` clean, 79 unit tests pass (feature-build listing/filtering, feed channel isolation, version parse, channel resolution), Prettier clean. The Go daemon is untouched.

### Known follow-ups (not blockers)

- The Update-channel select is disabled while automatic updates are off (pre-existing behavior), and that toggle defaults off, so reaching "Feature Releases" currently requires enabling automatic updates first. Decoupling that is a one-line change left out of this PR pending a product call.
- Env-scoping the signing secrets (they are repo-level today; the `release` environment provides the approval gate) is optional hardening tracked as OQ2 in #2366.

Spec and decision log: #2366.

## Bug: Auto-updater 404 — `gh-attach-assets` release is marked as latest

### Summary
The in-app "Check for updates" fails with a 404 error for every desktop user. A non-prerelease tagged `gh-attach-assets` (title: "gh-attach assets") was created on July 5 and is now GitHub's "latest" release. The electron-updater resolves `latest.yml` against this tag, which has no feed assets → 404.

### Error (from user's machine)
```
Cannot find latest.yml in the latest release artifacts
404 — GET https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/releases/download/gh-attach-assets/latest.yml
```

### Root Cause
```
$ gh release list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --limit 5

v0.10.3-nightly.202607061436   Pre-release
gh-attach-assets               Latest      ← PROBLEM: junk release, not prerelease
v0.10.2                        (stable)
```

The `gh-attach-assets` release is:
- **Not marked as prerelease** → GitHub treats it as the latest stable release
- **Has no `latest.yml`** (or any installer artifacts) → updater gets 404
- Likely created accidentally during release pipeline testing

This hijacks the `releases/latest` URL that electron-updater relies on:
```
https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/releases/latest/download/latest.yml
  → resolves to: .../gh-attach-assets/latest.yml  ← 404
  → should resolve to: .../v0.10.2/latest.yml     ← exists
```

### Impact
**Every desktop user** (Windows + macOS + Linux) hitting "Check for updates" gets this error. Auto-updates are completely broken until fixed.

### Fix
**Immediate (no code change):**
1. Delete the `gh-attach-assets` release:
   ```bash
   gh release delete gh-attach-assets --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --yes
   ```
2. Also delete the tag:
   ```bash
   git push origin :refs/tags/gh-attach-assets
   ```
3. GitHub will re-point "latest" back to `v0.10.2` automatically.

**Preventive (optional, follow-up):**
- Add a CI guard that rejects releases whose tag doesn't match `v<semver>` or `desktop-v*`
- Or: gate release creation behind the `release` environment (already done for the main pipeline, but manual/accidental releases bypass it)

### Environment
- **AO Version:** v0.10.2 (desktop app)
- **Platform:** Windows 11 (confirmed), likely all platforms
- **Repo:** AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator

Reported by: Deepak Modi (@deepakmodidev)

title: [codex] Guard latest desktop release
body:
## What changed

Adds a GitHub Actions guard for the desktop updater's stable release pointer.

The workflow runs when releases are published/edited, on an hourly schedule, and manually. It verifies that GitHub's current `releases/latest` target is a published non-prerelease stable tag matching `vX.Y.Z`, and that the release includes the electron-updater feed assets:

- `latest.yml`
- `latest-mac.yml`
- `latest-linux.yml`

## Why

Issue #2462 shows that an accidental non-prerelease release, `gh-attach-assets`, became GitHub's `latest` release. `electron-updater` then resolved `latest.yml` against that release and hit a 404, breaking in-app update checks for desktop users.

This PR does **not** delete the already-bad release, and it does not by itself clear the current outage. Per the issue, the immediate fix is a maintainer deleting the `gh-attach-assets` release and tag so GitHub points `latest` back to `v0.10.2`. This guard is the issue's *optional preventive follow-up*: it makes the failure visible quickly if the latest pointer is hijacked again or if a stable release is missing feed assets.

## Validation

- `npx prettier --check .github/workflows/release-latest-guard.yml`
- Live `gh release view` currently reports `gh-attach-assets` as latest, which would fail this guard as intended.

title: fix(dev): dev daemon latches onto installed app's daemon, killing it on quit
body:
## Bug

When `npm run dev` is run while the installed AO app is already running, the dev Electron instance connects to the existing daemon instead of spawning its own. Since both share the same port (3001) and run-file (`~/.ao/running.json`), when the dev app exits it tears down the shared daemon — killing the installed app's backend.

The supervisor link is the mechanism: the dev Electron calls `establishSupervisorLink()` against the installed daemon's socket. When the dev process exits, the OS closes the fd and the daemon self-stops after its ~5 s grace period.

## Root cause

`runFilePath()` and `expectedDaemonPort()` in `frontend/src/main.ts` have no dev/prod distinction — both fall back to `~/.ao/running.json` and port 3001 regardless of `app.isPackaged`.

## Fix

In dev mode (`!app.isPackaged`), default to:

- `AO_PORT=3002` — separate port, no collision
- `AO_RUN_FILE=~/.ao/dev/running.json` — isolates `supervise.sock` too (backend derives it as `dir(RunFilePath)/supervise.sock`)
- `AO_DATA_DIR=~/.ao/dev/data` — separate SQLite DB

Explicit env var overrides still win, so contributors can customise via their shell environment.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch the installed AO app (daemon binds port 3001, writes `~/.ao/running.json`)
2. `cd frontend && npm run dev`
3. Quit the dev Electron window
4. Installed app's daemon is now dead

title: fix(dev): isolate dev daemon from installed app on port and state dir
body:
Fixes #2464

## Summary

- `runFilePath()` now returns `~/.ao/dev/running.json` in dev mode — this also moves `supervise.sock` to `~/.ao/dev/supervise.sock` automatically, since the backend derives it as `dir(RunFilePath)/supervise.sock`
- `daemonEnv()` injects `AO_PORT=3002`, `AO_RUN_FILE`, and `AO_DATA_DIR` defaults when `!app.isPackaged` (explicit env vars still win)
- New `resolvedDaemonPort()` helper used by all three port-probe call-sites so they stay consistent with the daemon's actual bind port

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes (verified locally)

title: fix(installer): point Windows NSIS shortcut at the real binary (#2414)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #2414. On Windows the installer created a Start menu shortcut targeting `Agent Orchestrator.exe`, but the packaged binary is `agent-orchestrator.exe`. The shortcut pointed at a file that does not exist, so clicking it **silently did nothing** and the icon fell back to a generic Windows glyph. Affected every Windows user on a fresh install.

## Root cause
electron-builder derives the Windows exe name — and therefore the shortcut's `TargetPath` and `IconLocation` — from `win.executableName`, falling back to `productName` when it is unset. Our custom NSIS maker (`frontend/makers/maker-nsis.ts`) forwarded `productName` (`"Agent Orchestrator"`) but never `executableName`, so electron-builder assumed the binary was `Agent Orchestrator.exe`. Forge's packager, however, names the binary from `packagerConfig.executableName` = `agent-orchestrator` → `agent-orchestrator.exe`. Hence the mismatch.

## Fix
- Forward `win.executableName` through the NSIS maker so electron-builder targets the real binary (this fixes both the broken launch **and** the empty icon, since `IconLocation` defaults to the target exe).
- Hoist the binary name into a single `EXECUTABLE_NAME` constant in `forge.config.ts`, shared by the packager and the NSIS/deb makers, so they can't drift apart again.
- Add a regression test asserting the maker forwards `executableName` to electron-builder.

## Verification
Built the installer on **Windows 11** (`npm run make`), silent-installed it, and read the generated `.lnk` back with `WScript.Shell`:

| Field | Reported bug | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `TargetPath` | `…\Agent Orchestrator\Agent Orchestrator.exe` (missing) | `…\Programs\agent-orchestrator\agent-orchestrator.exe` — exists ✅ |
| `IconLocation` | *(empty)* | `…\agent-orchestrator.exe,0` ✅ |

Then silent-uninstalled to restore the machine. Also: `maker-nsis.test.ts` 3/3 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: Enterprise-grade UX: cohesion, command palette, accessibility, and performance
body:
## Summary

This issue tracks the work to make the renderer **feel enterprise-grade** — an instrument you trust with your work, not just a set of nicely-made screens. Enterprise "feel" is ~80% *consistency + keyboard-first + never-janks + never-dead-ends* and ~20% visual polish. The look is already good (a faithful `DESIGN.md` clone of the agent-orchestrator web app); what's missing is **systemic**: a fragmented control system, no command palette, ad-hoc keyboard shortcuts, no list virtualization, and uneven interaction states.

Everything here is **consolidation and infrastructure, not a restyle**. **Non-goal:** changing the aesthetic — the flat/near-black/hairline direction in `DESIGN.md` (clone agent-orchestrator, no gradients/glow/emoji, lucide icons, system fonts) stays exactly as-is.

Workstream 1 (cohesion) is the first slice to ship; Workstream 2 (command palette) is the single highest-leverage "feels enterprise" jump.

## Guiding principle: shadcn-first, minimize custom components

The single rule this issue enforces, and the one to hold in review going forward:

- **Use shadcn (Radix + `cva`) as much as possible.** It's already configured (`frontend/components.json`: new-york, lucide, `@/components/ui`) and already themed to our CSS-var tokens. `DESIGN.md` already mandates it: *"Build with shadcn primitives where a component fits."*
- **Need a control to look different? Add a `cva` variant/size to the existing primitive — never hand-roll new CSS.** The `dashboard-app-header__*-btn` and `reviewer-card__action*` classes are exactly the anti-pattern being removed: a bespoke stylesheet where a `<Button>` variant belonged.
- **Prefer a shadcn primitive for every control** — buttons, menus, selects, dialogs, tooltips, tabs, inputs, and the command palette (`command`/cmdk) — because Radix also gives us focus management / ARIA / keyboard behaviour for free (directly serving the accessibility goal below).
- **Custom components only where no primitive fits** — the app-shell layout (topbar, split panes), the kanban board, the xterm terminal, and a small token-based `<StatusPill>`/`<Tag>`. Even then: compose from tokens, never one-off values.
- **Net effect:** fewer bespoke components, one visual language, cohesion by construction rather than by discipline.

## Evidence (from the current renderer)

**Controls.** There is no single button. The "primary button" concept alone exists in 3+ forms, none sharing a source of truth:

| Control | Height | Radius | Weight | Hover | `focus-visible` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<Button variant="primary">` (`components/ui/button.tsx`) | 32px | 6px | 400 | opacity-90 | ✅ ring-2 |
| `.dashboard-app-header__primary-btn` | 34px | 7px | 600 | brightness(1.08) | ❌ none |
| `.dashboard-app-header__primary-btn--compact` | 32px | 7px | 600 | brightness | ❌ none |
| `.dashboard-app-header__accent-btn` | 34px | 7px | 600 | bg-swap | ❌ none |
| `.dashboard-app-header__kill-btn` | 30px | 6px | 650 | bg-swap | ❌ none |
| `.reviewer-card__action--primary` | 38px | 7px | 650 | bg-swap | ❌ none |

Across the renderer this compounds into: **51 raw `<button>` vs 23 `<Button>`** (the primitive is bypassed more than used; `ShellTopbar` renders 7 buttons, none via `<Button>`), **6 control heights** (24/28/30/32/34/38), **radii of 4/6/7/8/12/13px** (`7px` isn't a token — the scale is 4/6/8/12), **button weights of 400/600/650/700**, **5 disabled opacities** (0.35/0.45/0.5/0.6), freehand type sizes, and **two sources of truth for session status** (`ShellTopbar.STATUS_PILL` vs `SessionsBoard.sessionBadge()`, already disagreeing: `"Needs input"` vs `"Input needed"`).

**Beyond buttons (the enterprise-feel gaps):**

- **No command palette** — no `cmdk` / command registry anywhere. Keyboard shortcuts are scattered ad-hoc across ~10 components (`_shell.tsx`, `ShellTopbar`, `Sidebar`, `SessionView`, `CenterPane`, `TitlebarNav`, …) with no shared registry — the opposite of the single keybinding/command system that makes VS Code / Linear feel professional.
- **No list virtualization** — no `react-virtual`/`react-window`; the board columns and lists render every row, so they will jank at scale (enterprise = large session counts).
- **Uneven interaction states** — async surfaces lack a consistent loading / empty / error / retry contract, and there is no `:active` press feedback anywhere.

## Proposed target system (controls)

1. **One `<Button>`** that covers the real cases the bespoke CSS was invented for, then delete `.dashboard-app-header__*-btn` / `.reviewer-card__action*` CSS.
   - variants: `primary`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, `danger`, `danger-soft`, `success`
   - sizes: `sm` (28), `default` (32), and one topbar height (kill the 34/38 drift)
   - status tints become variants, not per-component inline `color-mix`.
2. **One `<StatusPill>` + one status registry** — single source for status label + tone, consumed by the topbar and the board.
3. **Locked token scales** — ~6 type sizes, 4 radii, 2–3 icon sizes, one `strokeWidth`; arbitrary Tailwind values discouraged in review.
4. **One state contract on every focusable control**: one hover model, `focus-visible` ring everywhere, one disabled opacity, and an `:active` tactile state.

## Roadmap & checklist

Organized as workstreams; each lands as its own independent, `ao preview`-verified PR.

### Workstream 1 — Cohesion: unify the control system

**P0 — accessibility & correctness (ship first, low-risk)**
- [ ] Add `focus-visible` rings to all currently-unstyled buttons (header, reviewer, done-bar). Fixes a **WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible)** failure that blocks enterprise/VPAT review.
- [ ] Collapse session status to a single registry (dedupe `STATUS_PILL` vs `sessionBadge`).

**P1 — control-system unification**
- [ ] Extend `<Button>` with the missing variants/sizes above.
- [ ] Migrate `ShellTopbar` (most-visible chrome) off bespoke button CSS.
- [ ] Migrate reviewer rail + remaining raw `<button>` controls.
- [ ] Delete the now-dead `dashboard-app-header__*-btn` / `reviewer-card__action*` CSS.
- [ ] Introduce a shared `<StatusPill>` / `<Tag>` primitive; remove inline `color-mix` triplication.

**P2 — token discipline & polish**
- [ ] Define type/space/radius/icon tokens; replace freehand arbitrary values.
- [ ] Standardize icon sizes + `strokeWidth`.
- [ ] Unify disabled opacity and hover model; add `:active` feedback.

### Workstream 2 — Command palette + keybinding registry (flagship)

The biggest "feels enterprise" lever; unifies the board / terminal / git-rail / orchestrator paradigms into one keyboard-driven spine.
- [ ] Add a command registry — every action registered once (id, title, keybinding, `when` context).
- [ ] Build a ⌘K command palette on shadcn's `command` primitive (cmdk).
- [ ] Migrate the ~10 scattered `keydown` handlers to read from the registry (one source of truth for shortcuts).
- [ ] Surface keybindings in menus/tooltips from the same registry.

### Workstream 3 — Accessibility / keyboard operability (VPAT)

Enterprise procurement gates on this.
- [ ] Every action doable without a mouse (the palette covers most of it).
- [ ] ARIA labels + logical tab order across the shell.
- [ ] Screen-reader pass on the board, session view, and dialogs.
- [ ] Visible focus everywhere (shares Workstream 1 · P0).

### Workstream 4 — Performance at scale (virtualization)
- [ ] Virtualize the board columns + long lists with `@tanstack/react-virtual`.
- [ ] Verify no jank at ~200 sessions.

### Workstream 5 — Instrument-grade states & feedback
- [ ] Loading skeletons (not spinners) on async surfaces.
- [ ] Inline errors with retry; no dead-ends.
- [ ] Toasts confirming actions (kill, spawn, PR created).
- [ ] Confirm/undo on destructive actions.

## Non-goals

- No change to the visual language, palette, typography, or layout — `DESIGN.md`'s "clone agent-orchestrator verbatim" direction is preserved.
- No gradients, glassmorphism, or decorative motion — restraint reads more enterprise on a dense control surface.
- No heavy new dependencies beyond the named primitives (cmdk via shadcn, `@tanstack/react-virtual`).
- Each workstream lands as independent, visually-verifiable PRs — nothing merges as one mega-diff.

title: Devin worker sessions fail in non-interactive mode while orchestrator sessions work
body:
## Summary

  Devin works when launched as an AO orchestrator, but Devin worker sessions spawned by an orchestrator are not usable for implementation work. Worker sessions either open to a blank screen or stop with
  a non-interactive permission/write-access message instead of editing files.

  ## Reproduction

  1. Configure/use Devin as an AO agent.
  2. Launch Devin as an orchestrator.
  3. From the orchestrator, spawn a Devin worker for a normal code-editing task.
  4. Ask the worker to make a small file edit.

  Example task:

  ```tsx
  // frontend/src/renderer/components/NotificationCenter.tsx

  // Change:
  <Bell className="h-[15px] w-[15px] fill-current" aria-hidden="true" />

  // To:
  <Bell className="h-[15px] w-[15px] fill-current text-white hover:text-white" aria-hidden="true" />

  ## Expected Behavior

  A Devin worker spawned by AO should be able to perform normal implementation work in its assigned worktree, including editing files and running verification commands.

  ## Actual Behavior

  The Devin orchestrator opens and appears to work correctly.

  But a Devin worker spawned by the orchestrator either:

  - opens to a blank screen, or
  - refuses to edit files and prints a message like:

  To complete this task, I need write access to modify the NotificationCenter.tsx file.

  You can either:
  1. Enable write permissions for this session
  2. Make the change manually
  3. Grant permission for me to use the edit/write tools

  The worker understands the task and can explain the exact change, but cannot apply it.

  ## Suspected Cause

  The Devin adapter appears to launch prompted worker sessions using non-interactive prompt mode:

  devin -p "<task prompt>"

  Orchestrator sessions without an initial prompt appear to launch interactively:

  devin

  This likely causes different behavior by role:

  - orchestrator: interactive Devin session, works normally
  - worker: non-interactive Devin session, cannot request write/edit approvals and may show a blank screen or fail permission checks

  If AO config uses bypass-permissions, the adapter maps that to:

  devin --permission-mode dangerous -p "<task prompt>"

  but the default worker launch path may still be unsuitable for normal Devin implementation work.

  ## Impact

  Devin cannot reliably be used as an AO worker agent, even though it works as an orchestrator. This breaks the expected orchestrator-worker flow for Devin.

  ## Possible Fixes

  - Revisit Devin worker prompt delivery and avoid devin -p if Devin requires interactive mode for implementation tasks.
  - Ensure Devin worker sessions are launched with a permission mode that supports unattended edits when configured in AO.
  - Add adapter tests covering Devin worker launch behavior, role differences, and permission mode mapping.

title: Bug: Qwen worker gets stuck because non-interactive mode lacks `-y`
body:
### Summary

  When spawning a Qwen worker, AO creates the worker session and tmux pane successfully, but the worker terminal appears blank/stuck. After waiting, Qwen prints a warning that tool execution requires
  approval but cannot proceed in non-interactive mode.

  ### Observed behavior

  The Qwen worker session is created and marked working. The terminal initially appears empty. Eventually Qwen shows:

  ```text
  Warning: Tool "agent" requires user approval but cannot execute in non-interactive mode.
  To enable automatic tool execution, use the -y flag (YOLO mode):
  Example: qwen -p 'your prompt' -y

  ### Expected behavior

  Qwen workers spawned by AO should be able to execute tools without getting stuck on an approval prompt that cannot be answered.

  ### Likely cause

  The Qwen adapter launches workers with -p/--prompt, which is non-interactive mode:

  qwen --append-system-prompt ... -p "<task prompt>"

  But it does not always pass Qwen’s auto-approval flag:

  -y

  or equivalent YOLO mode.

  Current behavior appears incompatible with Qwen Code 0.19.2, which explicitly says non-interactive tool execution needs -y.

  ### Proposed fix

  Update the Qwen adapter so AO-managed non-interactive worker launches pass -y/--yolo when appropriate, especially for the default headless worker mode or bypass-permissions.

  Relevant file:

  backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/qwen.go

  Potentially update tests in:

  backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/qwen_test.go

  ### Environment

  - Agent: Qwen Code
  - Qwen version: 0.19.2
  - Runtime: tmux
  - AO launches Qwen worker through the Qwen adapter

title: Bug: Continue workers with prompts are launched in non-interactive mode
body:
### Summary

  AO launches Continue worker sessions with prompts using Continue’s headless/non-interactive mode:

  ```bash
  cn --print -- "<task prompt>"

  This is risky for AO workers because they are expected to perform implementation tasks, use tools, edit files, and possibly ask for/handle approvals. In --print mode, Continue is intended to print a
  response and exit, not run as an interactive long-lived worker.

  ### Observed behavior

  Continue prompted workers are launched through the adapter with:

  cn --print -- "<prompt>"

  For default permissions, AO does not pass --auto, so if Continue needs tool approval, the worker may block, fail, or exit instead of continuing the task.

  ### Expected behavior

  Continue workers spawned by AO should run in a mode suitable for autonomous worker sessions. A prompted worker should be able to receive the task, execute tools, and continue working without getting
  stuck because the CLI is in non-interactive print mode.

  ### Likely cause

  The Continue adapter treats prompted launches as headless:

  backend/internal/adapters/agent/continueagent/continueagent.go

  Current behavior:

  cn --print -- "<prompt>"

  Potentially better behavior may be one of:

  cn --auto -- "<prompt>"

  or another Continue-supported interactive/task mode that accepts an initial prompt without forcing --print.

  ### Proposed fix

  Update the Continue adapter so AO worker sessions with prompts are not launched in --print mode unless that mode is explicitly intended.

  At minimum, prompted headless launches should pass a non-blocking permission mode such as:

  --auto

  But preferably AO should launch Continue workers in an interactive/session mode with the prompt supplied as the initial message, so the terminal remains useful and the worker can continue operating.

  ### Relevant files

  backend/internal/adapters/agent/continueagent/continueagent.go
  backend/internal/adapters/agent/continueagent/continueagent_test.go

  ### Why this matters

  AO workers are long-running agent sessions, not one-shot print commands. Launching Continue workers with --print can make them behave like one-shot non-interactive jobs and can prevent tool approval
  flows from working correctly.

title: Bug: Kimi worker does not open TUI for prompted AO tasks
body:
### Summary

  AO launches Kimi workers with prompts in non-interactive mode using:

  ```bash
  kimi -p "<task prompt>"

  This streams plain assistant output to stdout and does not open the Kimi TUI. As a result, the dashboard terminal shows text transcript output instead of the expected interactive Kimi interface.

  ### Observed behavior

  When spawning a Kimi worker, the terminal shows plain streamed text such as planning steps and status messages, but no interactive TUI appears.

  Example:

  1. I need to change the notification icon color...
  2. I need to locate the notification bell/icon component...
  ...
  Let me start by exploring the frontend structure...

  ### Expected behavior

  Kimi workers shown in the AO dashboard terminal should use an interactive/TUI mode when possible, or AO should clearly treat Kimi as a headless transcript-style worker and render the output
  accordingly.

  ### Likely cause

  The Kimi adapter intentionally uses non-interactive prompt mode for new prompted tasks:

  backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/kimi.go

  Current launch behavior:

  kimi -p "<prompt>"

  The adapter comments state that this runs without opening the TUI.

  ### Proposed fix

  Investigate whether Kimi supports starting an interactive TUI with an initial prompt. If yes, update the adapter to use that mode for AO worker sessions.

  If Kimi does not support interactive prompted launches, then AO should document/render Kimi as a headless transcript-style agent rather than expecting a TUI.

  ### Impact

  Kimi workers may be running correctly, but the dashboard terminal UX is confusing because users expect a TUI and instead see plain streamed output.

title: Bug: Cline worker terminal shows raw NDJSON outpu
body:
## Summary

AO launches prompted Cline workers in headless JSON mode using `--json`. As a result, the dashboard terminal shows raw NDJSON event lines instead of a readable agent terminal UI.

## Observed Behavior

When spawning a Cline worker, the terminal displays raw JSON events like:

```json
{"type":"agent_event","event":{"type":"content_start",...}}
{"type":"hook_event","hookEventName":"tool_call",...}
{"type":"agent_event","event":{"type":"iteration_end",...}}
```

The worker appears to be running, but the terminal is hard to use because it is showing machine-readable event output directly.

## Expected Behavior

The dashboard terminal should show a human-readable Cline session, or AO should parse/filter the NDJSON stream and render useful status/output instead of raw JSON.

## Likely Cause

The Cline adapter launches prompted workers with `--json`.

**Relevant file:**

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/cline.go`

## Possible Approaches

Choose one of these approaches:

1. Launch prompted Cline workers in interactive/readable mode when displayed in the dashboard terminal.
2. Keep `--json`, but parse/filter NDJSON before rendering terminal output.

## Impact

Cline workers are spawned and running, but the terminal UX is poor because users see raw event JSON instead of a readable agent interface.

title: Persist immutable repo metadata on session_worktrees
body:
## Problem

Workspace session lifecycle code currently resolves historical `session_worktrees` rows through the current workspace registry. A child row stores `repo_name` and `worktree_path`, but not immutable repo metadata such as the source `repo_path` or registered `relative_path`.

After workspace registry drift, for example remove/re-add of the same workspace path/id with a changed child set, older dirty or preserved child rows may no longer resolve. Recent lifecycle changes fail closed to avoid data loss, but that still means AO cannot operate on those historical child worktrees until the registry is repaired.

## Proposed follow-up

Persist enough immutable repo information on each `session_worktrees` row when the row is written, likely including:

- `repo_path` for the source repository path at session creation/save time
- `relative_path` for the child path within the workspace
- optionally origin/default-branch metadata if needed by restore/cleanup flows

Then update workspace-project row reconstruction to prefer persisted row metadata and only use the current workspace registry as a legacy fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add SQLite migration and sqlc updates for the new columns.
- Populate the new fields for root and child rows in spawn/save/restore active inventory paths.
- Update kill/restore/save/replacement cleanup to operate on historical rows even when the current workspace registry has drifted.
- Keep compatibility for legacy rows missing the new metadata.
- Add a regression test where a dirty/preserved child row is still cleaned/restored after the child is removed from the current registry.

## Context

Follow-up from PR #2460. The current PR intentionally fails closed on unresolved historical rows to prevent data loss; this issue tracks making those rows independently operable.

title: Pi Adapter — Non-Interactive Launch Issue
body:
## Problem

The `pi` adapter currently launches sessions with `--print`, which runs Pi in non-interactive/headless mode:

```go
cmd = []string{binary, "--print"}
```

This is not a good fit for AO sessions. Both worker and orchestrator sessions should be long-lived interactive agent sessions inside the terminal pane.

Current behavior affects both roles:

- **Worker sessions** run as one-shot/headless Pi commands instead of interactive sessions.
- **Orchestrator sessions** also run with `--print`, even though orchestrators are meant to stay alive and coordinate work over time.
- Pi does receive the AO system prompt via `--append-system-prompt`, but the non-interactive launch mode makes it unsuitable for long-lived orchestration.

**Relevant files:**

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/pi/pi.go`
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/pi/pi_test.go`

## Expected Behavior

Pi should launch interactive sessions for both workers and orchestrators.

Expected launch shape should be closer to:

```
pi [--append-system-prompt <system prompt>] [prompt]
```

instead of:

```
pi --print [--append-system-prompt <system prompt>] [prompt]
```

For orchestrators, AO should still pass the generated orchestrator system prompt so Pi knows to coordinate work, spawn/message workers, and avoid implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `GetLaunchCommand` no longer uses `--print` for normal AO worker or orchestrator sessions.
- [ ] Worker sessions launch interactively.
- [ ] Orchestrator sessions launch interactively.
- [ ] AO system prompt injection remains supported through `--append-system-prompt`.
- [ ] Restore behavior is reviewed and adjusted if `--print --session <id>` is also non-interactive.
- [ ] Tests in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/pi/pi_test.go` are updated to assert interactive launch behavior.
- [ ] Add or update tests covering:
  - Worker launch with prompt
  - Orchestrator launch with system prompt
  - Restore command behavior
  - Prompt delivery strategy if it changes

title: claim-pr cannot claim upstream PRs from fork-registered projects
body:
## Summary

`ao spawn --claim-pr` / `ao session claim-pr` cannot manually claim an upstream PR when the AO project is registered to a fork, even when the local checkout has an `upstream` remote configured.

## Why this matters

This blocks AO from attaching lifecycle/nudge behavior to normal fork-based contribution PRs. A user can still push fixes to the fork branch manually, but AO does not own the upstream PR and therefore cannot surface review comments, CI state, or other PR nudges to the worker session.

## Reproduction

Project registration:

- AO project repo/origin: `https://github.com/VenkataSakethDakuri/agent-orchestrator`
- Local git remotes include:
  - `origin` -> `https://github.com/VenkataSakethDakuri/agent-orchestrator`
  - `upstream` -> `https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator.git`

Upstream PR:

- `https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2458`
- PR head branch lives in the fork: `VenkataSakethDakuri/agent-orchestrator:fix/scm-pr-reaction-control-flow`

Command:

```bash
ao spawn --project agent-orchestrator --name fix-pr-2458 --claim-pr 2458 --agent codex
```

Observed result:

```text
failed to claim PR 2458: Unknown PR (PR_NOT_FOUND)
```

## Root cause observed

The manual claim path normalizes numeric PR refs against the registered project repo/origin. In this setup, `2458` is interpreted as:

`VenkataSakethDakuri/agent-orchestrator#2458`

That PR does not exist. The actual PR is:

`AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator#2458`

The claim service also enforces that the PR URL matches the project origin repo, so passing the full upstream PR URL is not a clean workaround for a fork-registered project.

## Related code paths

- CLI numeric PR ref resolution uses the project repo: `backend/internal/cli/pr_ref.go`
- Claim service normalizes and enforces same-repo matching: `backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go`
- Background SCM observer already has upstream remote scan support for cross-fork PR discovery: `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`

## Expected behavior

Manual `claim-pr` should support the same fork-to-upstream workflow that the SCM observer can discover:

- If the project origin is a fork and the local checkout has an upstream GitHub remote, AO should be able to claim a PR from that upstream repo when the PR head repo matches the project origin/fork.
- Numeric PR refs may remain project-origin scoped, but full upstream PR URLs should be claimable when the PR head repo belongs to the project origin.
- Alternatively, numeric refs could resolve against eligible scanned remotes when unambiguous.

## Notes

This is separate from review-thread refresh behavior. The immediate blocker is that manual claim never attaches the upstream PR to a live AO session, so lifecycle nudges have no PR owner/target.

title: feat(pi): update Pi agent to support interactive sessions and adjust …
body:
## Summary

  This updates the Pi adapter so AO launches Pi as a long-lived interactive terminal session instead of using Pi's headless `--print` mode.

  Previously, Pi sessions were launched as:

 
  pi --print [--append-system-prompt <system prompt>] [prompt]

  That made both worker and orchestrator sessions behave like one-shot/headless commands, which does not match AO's terminal-pane session model.

  After this change, Pi launches as:

  pi [--append-system-prompt <system prompt>] [prompt]

  Restore commands also drop --print and now resume interactively:

  pi --session <agentSessionId>

  When a restore includes standing system instructions, AO re-applies them:

  pi --append-system-prompt <system prompt> --session <agentSessionId>

  ## What Changed

  - Removed --print from GetLaunchCommand.
  - Removed --print from GetRestoreCommand.
  - Kept inline AO system prompt injection through --append-system-prompt.
  - Preserved in-command prompt delivery for the initial task prompt.
  - Re-applied SystemPrompt during restore when provided, so orchestrator sessions retain their coordination instructions.
  - Updated adapter comments to describe Pi as interactive instead of headless.
  - Updated Pi adapter tests to assert the new interactive command shape.

  ## Why

  AO sessions are meant to be long-lived agent sessions inside a terminal pane.

  Using --print starts Pi in non-interactive/headless mode, which is a poor fit for both AO workers and orchestrators:

  - Workers should remain usable as terminal-backed agent sessions.
  - Orchestrators need to stay alive over time to coordinate workers.
  - The orchestrator system prompt was already being passed, but --print caused the session mode to be wrong.

  ## Test Coverage

  Updated backend/internal/adapters/agent/pi/pi_test.go to cover:

  - Worker launch with prompt:
      - pi "add a health check"

  - Orchestrator launch with system prompt:
      - pi --append-system-prompt <prompt> <task>

  - System prompt file inlining still works.
  - Permission modes still emit no Pi-specific permission flag.
  - Restore command no longer uses --print.
  - Restore command re-applies system prompt when provided.
  - Prompt delivery strategy remains PromptDeliveryInCommand.


closes #2478

title: E2E test platform pilot: master test case catalog for the nightly gate
body:
## Context

We are piloting an e2e test platform (cloud-agnostic, pod-per-run Kubernetes Jobs) with the **Linux nightly build as the first gated workload**: after `frontend-nightly.yml` publishes, a pod installs the packaged artifact, drives the full app with Playwright, and posts an `ao-nightly-gate` commit status plus artifacts. Design doc: https://pritom14.github.io/ao-e2e-platform/

This issue is the **master test case catalog**: every smoke/e2e case we intend to automate, from install to teardown. It is the source of truth for suite manifests; tests will live in-repo and reference these IDs.

## Legend

**Tier**
- `T0` smoke: runs on every trigger (~15 cases, target < 5 min)
- `T1` core: full nightly run
- `T2` extended: nightly/weekly, lower priority to automate

**Runs** (execution environment classification)
- `POD` pure pod-runnable (packaged app + Playwright + fixtures, no external deps)
- `FAKE` needs the scripted fake-agent harness (deterministic agent plugin, no LLM calls)
- `EXT` needs the external GitHub sandbox repo (`Pritom14/Agreemint`) + bot token

## Prerequisites (tracked separately, blockers for automation)

1. `data-testid` instrumentation across renderer components (selector policy)
2. **Fake agent plugin**: scripted Agent implementation emitting canned JSONL/terminal output on a timeline (spawning, active, waiting_input, blocked, done, PR push against sandbox repo). No tokens, deterministic, instant
3. GitHub sandbox: throwaway repo + bot token, wiped between runs
4. Clock control: activity thresholds (30s active window, 5min idle) configurable via env so pods do not sleep real minutes

title: bug(terminal): tmux pane shows garbled ASCII/underscores, and Ctrl+Arrow/Ctrl+Backspace/Ctrl+V double-fire (AO-only, not reproducible in a bare tmux)
body:
## Bug

Using the embedded terminal (xterm.js attached to a tmux-backed session via `tmux attach-session`), two related but distinct symptoms show up that do **not** reproduce when attaching to the same tmux session directly from a regular terminal:

1. **Garbled rendering**: a lot of the pane's box-drawing / line output renders as underscores and other ASCII substitutes instead of proper glyphs.
2. **Doubled input**: holding Ctrl and pressing Arrow keys or Backspace (word-nav/word-delete) performs the action twice. Ctrl+V paste also pastes twice.

Both go away when attaching to the same tmux session from a plain terminal outside AO, so the corruption/duplication is introduced somewhere between AO's PTY attach and/or the xterm.js render path — not in tmux itself.

## Investigation so far

- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go` (`attachEnv`, ~line 252) unconditionally overwrites `TERM=xterm-256color` on every `tmux attach-session` process, and forwards no locale (`LANG`/`LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`) at all — the daemon may not have one to forward if launched without an interactive shell profile.
- Hypothesis tested: tmux falls back to ASCII line-drawing when it can't confirm the attached client is UTF-8-capable via locale. **This did not hold up under test**: reproduced a real tmux 3.4 session (with a split pane, so a real border byte exists) and attached via a real pty twice — once with the environment completely stripped of all locale vars, once with `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` added. Both attaches sent identical bytes for the border (`e2 94 82`, correct UTF-8 for `│`). So locale had no effect on this tmux version's border rendering, and the ASCII-fallback theory as stated is **disproven**, at least for tmux 3.4.
- This means the underscore corruption is more likely introduced **downstream of tmux** — most likely in `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx`'s WebGL/Canvas glyph rendering (`loadRenderer`), or in how the attach PTY's bytes reach xterm.js — rather than in the tmux runtime adapter.
- For the doubled Ctrl+Arrow/Ctrl+Backspace/Ctrl+V: traced `XtermTerminal.tsx`'s `attachCustomKeyEventHandler`/`normalizedTerminalShortcut`/`isTerminalPasteShortcut` — these call `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation` and return `false` to suppress xterm's default handling, and no second keydown/paste listener elsewhere in the frontend was found that would explain a second emission. Root cause not yet found.

## Repro

1. Open a session's terminal in AO (tmux runtime).
2. Hold Ctrl and press Left/Right/Backspace repeatedly, or Ctrl+V paste something — the action applies twice.
3. Observe pane text/borders for stray underscores in place of expected characters, especially in agent CLI TUI chrome.
4. Compare against attaching to the same tmux session (`tmux attach -t <session>`) from an unrelated terminal — neither symptom reproduces there.

## Next steps

title: feat: bundle static tmux in macOS/Linux installers as a private fallback
body:
Closes #2443.

On macOS/Linux, session spawn is tmux-only, but the packaged app ships no tmux — a clean machine fails pre-spawn with `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` (#2256/#2259 made that failure clear; this makes it go away). Implements the private bundled fallback discussed in the issue: never a system install, never mutating the user's machine.

## Resolution order (re-evaluated on every command)

1. `AO_TMUX_BIN` — explicit override; a set-but-broken value fails loudly instead of falling through
2. **System tmux from `PATH` — always wins when present.** Existing users see zero behavior change, and installing tmux later takes effect on the next spawn
3. App-bundled binary at `Resources/tmux-dist/tmux` (stamped into the daemon env as `AO_BUNDLED_TMUX` by the Electron supervisor; accepted only if an executable regular file)
4. The existing clear `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` error (wire code unchanged, no API contract regen)

## What's in here

- **Backend**: new `tmux.ResolveBinary`/`NewResolver` shared by all consumers — the tmux runtime adapter (per-command resolution), the spawn prerequisite gate (`validateRuntimePrerequisites`), and `ao doctor` (PASS output now shows provenance: `via PATH | bundled | AO_TMUX_BIN`) — so they can never disagree on which binary is used. `AO_TMUX_BIN`/`AO_BUNDLED_TMUX` are read centrally in `config.Load()`.
- **Artifact pipeline**: manual-dispatch `.github/workflows/tmux-artifacts.yml` builds tmux 3.5a + libevent 2.1.12 + ncurses 6.5 from sha256-verified source tarballs, natively per target (macOS arm64/x64: static deps, dynamic only against libSystem; Linux x64: musl fully-static on alpine with compiled-in terminfo fallbacks), and publishes a `tmux-artifacts-v<ver>-<rev>` release with `checksums.txt` + provenance/license notes (tmux ISC, libevent BSD-3, ncurses MIT-X11).
- **Packaging**: `fetch-tmux.mjs` runs in `prepackage`/`premake`/`publish` (before signing, so the binary is sealed into the macOS signature), verifies the download against the release `checksums.txt` with optional in-repo pins as a cross-check, and ships `tmux-dist` as an `extraResource`. `AO_SKIP_TMUX_FETCH=1` escape hatch for offline dev packaging. deb/rpm additionally declare a system tmux dependency as a cheap complement.
- **Docs**: provenance + rollover procedure in `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md`; landing docs updated so "install tmux" is CLI-only guidance.

## Testing

- Backend: full `go test ./...` green — new table-driven resolver tests (override wins / system beats bundled / bundled accepted when PATH empty / non-executable rejected / sentinel errors), per-command re-resolution tests in the tmux adapter, spawn-gate tests (bundled accepted, resolver failure creates no session row), doctor provenance tests.
- Frontend: 460 vitest tests green, incl. `bundledTmuxPath` and checksum-parsing/pin-resolution suites.
- Live smoke with the compiled `ao` binary across all four states:
  WARN tmux: not found in PATH (the desktop app falls back to its bundled tmux; …)
  PASS tmux: …/faketmux/tmux (tmux 3.5a, via bundled)
  PASS tmux: /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux (tmux 3.7b, via PATH)
  PASS tmux: …/faketmux/tmux (tmux 3.5a, via AO_TMUX_BIN)

## Follow-ups before release

- Dispatch the `tmux-artifacts` workflow once to cut `tmux-artifacts-v3.5a-1`, then (optionally) copy the per-asset sha256 pins into `fetch-tmux.mjs`.
- Prove macOS notarization of the bundled Mach-O on a test release; if osx-sign misses it under `Resources/`, the fallback is an explicit `binaries` list in `osxSign`.
- Packaged smoke on a tmux-less machine per the checklist in `desktop-release.md`.

title: fix(desktop): wheel-scroll codex (and plain-shell) transcripts
body:
## What

Mouse wheel (and PageUp/PageDown) did nothing when scrolling a **codex** pane on Windows. This makes the wheel scroll codex's transcript, the same way it already works in a raw terminal — without regressing the opencode scroll fix.

## Root cause

The terminal was built on the assumption that every pane is a full-screen **alt-buffer** app under **tmux** (macOS/Linux): it set `scrollback: 0` and synthesized SGR mouse reports so tmux copy-mode does the scrolling. The recent opencode fix layered on a blanket `isWindowsPlatform()` rule that force-fed PageUp/PageDown to *every* Windows pane.

Codex breaks all of those assumptions. Probing `term.buffer`/`term.modes` while wheel-scrolling a live codex session showed:

- `buf=normal` — codex is a **normal-buffer** app, not alt-screen
- `mode=none` — it does **not** track the mouse (SGR reports are ignored)
- it ignores PageUp/PageDown (confirmed by hand)
- `len == rows`, `baseY ≈ 0` even after a long chat

Codex just **prints its transcript and relies on the terminal's own scrollback** (exactly what you see in raw PowerShell). But `scrollback: 0` discarded every line that scrolled off, so there was nothing to scroll — and the Windows rule sent codex page keys it ignores.

## Fix

- `scrollback: 0 → 5000` so normal-buffer panes retain history. Alt-buffer panes (tmux, mouse-tracking TUIs) never feed this buffer, so they're unaffected.
- Wheel handler now branches on buffer + mouse-tracking, in order: (1) `paneScrollsByKeyboard` → PageUp/PageDown (**opencode — unchanged, kept first**); (2) mouse-off + **normal buffer** → `term.scrollLines()` native scroll (**codex, new**); (3) mouse tracking on → SGR reports (tmux/zellij copy-mode); (4) alt-buffer fallback → page keys.
- Removed the blanket `isWindowsPlatform()` branch; opencode is already covered by rule 1 on every platform.
- Hid the `.xterm-viewport` scrollbar so the new scrollback doesn't reserve width and shift the grid; dropped the now-dead scrollbar-thumb CSS.

## Testing

- Manually verified on Windows: codex now wheel-scrolls its transcript; opencode scroll unchanged.
- Updated `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` — added codex native-scroll and alt-buffer fallback cases; 31/31 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: feat(ui): list all supported agents in the session switch dropdown
body:
## What & why

Follow-up to #2412 (mid-session agent switch). The Agent-row switch dropdown in the session inspector listed **only authorized** agents, hiding everything else — so on a machine with a few CLIs installed you'd see a short list with no indication of what other agents exist or why they're unavailable.

This lists **every supported agent**, mirroring the onboarding / spawn picker (`RequiredAgentField`) so the two surfaces behave identically.

## Behaviour

Sorted selectable-first, each agent labeled by status:

| Status | Label | Selectable? |
|---|---|---|
| Authorized | — | ✅ |
| Auth unknown | ⚠ `Auth unknown` | ✅ |
| Needs auth (installed, signed out) | `Needs auth` | ❌ disabled |
| Needs install (no CLI on PATH) | `Needs install` | ❌ disabled |

The daemon remains the authoritative auth check at spawn; the disabled states just keep un-runnable agents visible-with-a-reason instead of hidden.

## Notes
- Frontend-only; reuses the existing `/api/v1/agents` catalog (`supported`/`installed`/`authorized`) and the `dropdown-menu` primitive.
- Status/label logic matches `RequiredAgentField` exactly for consistency.
- `tsc` and the SessionInspector unit tests pass.

title: Offer to relaunch sessions when the project's default permission mode changes
body:
When a user changes the default permission mode in Project Settings (e.g. from Bypass Permissions to something else), running sessions keep their old mode. We should offer an option to relaunch the affected sessions, i.e. kill and restart them with the new permission mode applied.

- Trigger: on saving a changed default permission mode in Project Settings.
- Action: prompt the user (something like 'Relaunch N running sessions with the new permission mode?'), and on confirm, restart those sessions.
- Most of the plumbing already exists (session kill + restore/relaunch), so this should mostly be wiring the settings-change event to a confirm + relaunch flow. Don't relaunch silently; make it opt-in.

title: macOS app menu shows Electron instead of AO / Agent Orchestrator
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the running Electron app still shows `Electron` as the application menu label in the system menu bar instead of AO / Agent Orchestrator.

This is visible while the app window itself is open and titled `agent-orchestrator`, so the top-level macOS menu looks like a generic Electron app rather than the AO desktop app.

## Repro

1. On macOS, run the desktop app locally:

   ```bash
   npm --prefix frontend run dev
   ```

2. Wait for the Electron window to open.
3. Look at the macOS menu bar at the top of the screen.

## Expected

The first application menu should use the product/app name, for example:

```text
Agent Orchestrator
```

or the shorter AO branding if that is the intended user-facing name.

## Actual

The macOS menu bar shows:

```text
Electron  File  Edit  View  Window  Help
```

## Evidence

Local screenshot from Electron smoke test:

```text
/Users/cruzer/Documents/CleanShot 2026-07-08 at 11.45.27@2x.png
```

The screenshot shows the app window open with the title `agent-orchestrator`, while the macOS app menu still reads `Electron`.

## Code references

The app already appears to intend custom branding:

- `frontend/package.json` sets `productName` to `Agent Orchestrator`.
- `frontend/forge.config.ts` sets `packagerConfig.name` to `Agent Orchestrator`.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` calls `app.setName("Agent Orchestrator")` before app ready.

So this looks like the current name/config path is not enough for the macOS app menu in the dev/runtime flow, or the app needs an explicit application menu/template override.

## Impact

This is not a functional blocker, but it is user-visible desktop polish:

- first-run macOS users see generic `Electron` branding
- screenshots/demos look unfinished
- the app menu does not match the AO / Agent Orchestrator identity used elsewhere

## Suggested fix shape

- Ensure the macOS application menu label uses the AO/Agent Orchestrator name in dev and packaged builds.
- If needed, install an explicit Electron `Menu` template after app initialization with the first app menu labelled from the product name.
- Verify on macOS by launching the app and checking the system menu bar.

## Duplicate check

I checked current open issues/PRs for nearby terms like `Electron menu`, `macOS menu`, `app name`, and `application menu`. I did not find an open issue specifically tracking the macOS menu bar still showing `Electron`.

title: Brand native Electron menu as Agent Orchestrator
body:
## Summary

Closes #2507.

This replaces Electron's default native menu with an app-owned `Agent Orchestrator` menu template and preserves the standard native menu roles/shortcuts.

The macOS dev path needed one extra piece beyond the menu template: `electron-forge start` launches the stock `Electron.app` binary directly, so macOS still labels the first menu item from the executable path. This PR adds a tiny Forge start plugin that, on macOS dev runs only, creates/uses a branded executable alias inside the local Electron dev bundle so the system menu bar shows `Agent Orchestrator` during `npm run dev` too. Packaged builds continue to use the existing Forge packager config.

## What changed

- Added a testable main-process app menu helper:

- Installed the native menu inside `app.whenReady()` before `createWindow()`.
- Added a macOS dev-only Forge executable alias helper so `electron-forge start` no longer leaves the native app menu branded as `Electron`.
- Added focused unit coverage for both the menu template and dev executable branding path.

title: SCM observer reloads tracked PR repos without owner/name, causing check-runs 404s
body:
## Bug
Tracked PR status polling can get stuck after AO reloads an existing PR row from SQLite. The observer logs repeated check-runs guard failures and the PR row stays with stale/partial facts such as `ci_state=unknown`, `mergeability=unknown`, and empty `observed_at`/`ci_observed_at`.

**Source:** AO session chat report from @chauhan, with live logs for `agent-orchestrator-37`
**Reported by:** @chauhan
**Analyzed against:** local checkout `a54003e7`; current `origin/main` `35012bd9` still has the same code path
**AO version:** `dev`
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 24.6.0 arm64, zsh, Go `go1.26.3 darwin/arm64`
**Verified binary:** locally built `/tmp/ao`; `/tmp/ao status` reports port `3001`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** high: PR/CI status refresh is a core feedback loop and affected sessions never receive the failing CI state.

## Reproduction
1. Run the Go rewrite daemon on port `3001`.
2. Have AO track an existing PR row whose persisted `pr` facts include `provider`, `host`, and `repo`, for example:
   - session: `agent-orchestrator-37`
   - PR: `https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2506`
   - repo: `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`
   - head SHA: `6f52e45c471476e2b1ad1b837ff5f82911f913cd`
3. Let the SCM observer poll.
4. Observe daemon logs like:

```text
time=2026-07-08T14:35:20.208+05:30 level=ERROR msg="scm observer: commit check-runs guard failed" pr=https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2506 sha=6f52e45c471476e2b1ad1b837ff5f82911f913cd err="scm: not found: Not Found"
```

5. Inspect SQLite: the PR row remains stale/partial:
   - `ci_state=unknown`
   - `mergeability=unknown`
   - `observed_at` empty
   - `ci_observed_at` empty
6. Verify GitHub has status checks for the same SHA:

```bash
gh pr view 2506 --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --json statusCheckRollup,mergeable,reviewDecision,headRefOid
```

For the live report, GitHub returned `mergeable=MERGEABLE`, `reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED`, and check runs `format` failure plus `test`/`scan` success.

## Root Cause
`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go` rebuilds the provider repo for a stored PR in `repoForTrackedPR`. When the row has `Provider`, `Host`, and `Repo`, it returns:

```go
ports.SCMRepo{Provider: pr.Provider, Host: pr.Host, Repo: pr.Repo}
```

That leaves `Owner` and `Name` empty. The GitHub observer provider builds REST paths from `repo.Owner` and `repo.Name` in `backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go` (`CommitChecksGuard` calls `repoPath(repo.Owner, repo.Name, "commits", headSHA, "check-runs")`). With empty owner/name, AO calls an invalid repo path and GitHub returns 404.

Manual verification rules out GitHub missing the resource: this succeeds with the same account/token:

```bash
gh api repos/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/commits/6f52e45c471476e2b1ad1b837ff5f82911f913cd/check-runs --jq '{total_count, names:[.check_runs[].name]}'
# {"names":["scan","format","test"],"total_count":3}
```

## Fix
When `repoForTrackedPR` trusts the persisted provider/host/repo tuple, rehydrate `Owner` and `Name` by splitting the persisted `Repo` value (`owner/name`) before returning the `ports.SCMRepo`. Add a focused observer test that asserts `TestRepoForTrackedPRUsesPersistedRepoWhenCurrentScanDropsUpstream` returns `Owner="upstream"` and `Name="api"` for `Repo="upstream/api"`.

## Related
- [PR #2492](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2492): recently enriched PR observation context but did not change this tracked-PR repo reconstruction path.
- [PR #2368](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2368): related cross-fork/upstream SCM discovery work; this bug affects the later refresh of already tracked persisted PR rows.

## Impact
- Existing tracked PRs can stop refreshing CI and mergeability after reload.
- Sessions such as `agent-orchestrator-37` remain in stale states like `review_pending` with `ci_state=unknown` despite failing checks.
- Agent CI feedback nudges may not fire because lifecycle never receives the updated SCM observation.

title: Frontend shows 'No session selected' while a new worker is still spinning up
body:
## Bug

When a worker agent takes time to spawn, the Electron terminal pane can show:

```text
No session selected. Pick a worker to attach its terminal.
```

That is misleading when the user has just started a worker. The UI should show that the worker/session is spinning up, and ideally expose which phase is taking time, rather than implying the user failed to select a session.

**Source:** human report in AO session chat on 2026-07-08  
**Reported by:** @chauhan  
**Analyzed against:** `992e3d01127873eb2ed97b5bd5513f48a4114b23`  
**Verified binary:** built from this checkout as `/tmp/ao`; `/tmp/ao status` reported daemon ready on port `3001`  
**Area:** Electron frontend + daemon session spawn path  
**Confidence:** High for the UI placeholder cause; Medium for the exact slow phase without per-spawn timing instrumentation.  
**Priority:** medium — user-visible confusing state during a common workflow; spawn still eventually succeeds.

## Reproduction

1. Open the Electron supervisor for a project.
2. Start a new worker from the UI, e.g. the New task dialog.
3. Use a project/agent where spawn takes noticeable time, such as a worktree-heavy repo or one with provisioning/post-create hooks.
4. Observe the center terminal area while the spawn is still in progress or while the session row exists before its terminal handle has been populated.

## Expected

The terminal area should make the pending state explicit, for example:

```text
Starting worker session...
Preparing worktree and terminal.
```

The UI should not say `No session selected` when the app knows a spawn is in progress or has a selected session record that is not attachable yet.

## Actual

The terminal empty state is keyed only on a missing terminal handle:

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx` derives `handleId` from `attachSession?.terminalHandleId`.
- If `!handleId`, it renders the generic empty state: `No session selected. Pick a worker to attach its terminal.`

That message is correct when there is no selected session, but not correct when a session is selected or a just-started spawn is pending and the terminal handle is not ready yet.

## Code Path / Root Cause

The frontend submit path waits on the spawn API before it can navigate to the created worker:

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx` posts to `POST /api/v1/sessions` and only calls `onCreated(data.session.id)` after the response returns.

The backend spawn path is synchronous and does a lot before returning an attachable session:

- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` creates the durable seed row.
- It creates/materializes the workspace/worktree.
- It runs per-project workspace provisioning hooks.
- It prepares agent-specific workspace files/settings.
- It resolves prompt delivery and launch command.
- It validates the agent binary.
- It creates the runtime terminal/session.
- It calls lifecycle `MarkSpawned`, which writes the runtime handle metadata.
- For after-start delivery agents, it may also send the prompt before returning.

So spawn can legitimately take time because AO is doing worktree/provisioning/agent/runtime setup inline before the API returns. During that gap, current UI state has no explicit "pending spawn" object to display. If the UI does render a selected session before `terminalHandleId` is available, `TerminalPane` treats it exactly like no selected session.

## Fix Shape

Small frontend fix:

- Split the terminal empty state into two states:
  - no `session`: keep `No session selected`.
  - `session` exists but no `terminalHandleId`: show a worker/orchestrator startup message.
- For New task and orchestrator spawn call sites, consider a route/global pending-spawn state so users see "Starting worker..." immediately while the POST is still in flight, before the new session id is known.

Backend observability follow-up:

- Add or surface phase timings around spawn steps (workspace, provision, agent prepare, runtime create, prompt delivery) so the UI or logs can explain why a spawn is slow instead of treating all delay as one opaque POST.

## Diagnostics Gathered

```text
/tmp/ao version -> dev
/tmp/ao status -> ready, port 3001, run file ~/.ao/running.json
/tmp/ao session ls -> live agent-orchestrator sessions listed; daemon is current Go rewrite path, not a stale :3000 install
```

Duplicate search performed in `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` with these terms:

```text
No session selected spawn
spinning up session selected
New task creates a worker leaves UI previous session
terminal pending spawn
terminalHandleId No session selected
worker spinning up
```

No exact duplicate found. Nearby issues include terminal focus/blank terminal and generic spawn failures, but they do not cover this misleading pending-spawn placeholder.
