title: Electron briefly shows onboarding before existing projects load
body:
## Bug

On Electron app open, the UI briefly shows the first-run onboarding/welcome page, then switches to the existing project list. The onboarding page should only appear when there are actually no registered projects, not while daemon/API discovery is still settling.

**Source:** human report in AO session chat on 2026-07-08  
**Reported by:** @chauhan  
**Analyzed against:** `f9a25a7467aaba3f17fbb4699d80e8a618ba3da6` in `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`  
**Verified binary:** `/tmp/ao` built from this checkout; `/tmp/ao status` reported ready on port `3001`  
**Local state:** `/tmp/ao project ls` showed existing projects (`agent-orchestrator`, `punereads`)  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** medium — visible startup flicker/confusing first-run state; no data loss.

## Reproduction

1. Have at least one project registered in AO.
2. Open the Electron app fresh.
3. Watch the initial board content before the projects/sidebar list appears.

## Expected

The onboarding/welcome page appears only when the authoritative project query has completed against the daemon and returned zero projects.

When projects exist, startup should show a loading/shell state until the real project list is known, then render the project list/board directly.

## Actual

The app can briefly render the first-run onboarding page, then replace it with the project list once daemon discovery/API state catches up.

## Root Cause

`fetchWorkspaces()` returns an empty array before the renderer has a trusted daemon API base URL:

- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useWorkspaceQuery.ts`: if `!hasTrustedApiBaseUrl()`, it returns `[]`.

React Query treats that `[]` as a successful workspace query result. The board then interprets `isSuccess && all.length === 0` as a true first-run state:

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx`: `showWelcome = !projectId && isLoaded && all.length === 0`.

Later, when daemon status becomes ready, `_shell` invalidates the workspace query and the real `/api/v1/projects` + `/api/v1/sessions` result replaces the empty list:

- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx`: the daemon-ready effect invalidates `workspaceQueryKey`.

That makes the onboarding page a transient daemon-discovery placeholder rather than an authoritative no-projects state.

## Fix Shape

Do not represent "API base not trusted yet" as an authoritative empty project list. Possible approaches:

- Make `fetchWorkspaces()` stay pending or throw a typed not-ready state until the daemon API base is trusted.
- Gate `showWelcome` on a query result that definitely came from `/api/v1/projects`, not the pre-daemon fallback `[]`.
- Add a test that simulates `hasTrustedApiBaseUrl() === false` followed by daemon-ready invalidation and asserts the welcome page does not flash when projects later exist.

## Duplicate Search

Searched `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` issues with:

```text
onboarding page project list
Welcome to Agent Orchestrator projects
onboarding flash
hasTrustedApiBaseUrl
first launch welcome projects
```

No exact duplicate found.

title: Vibe worker spawns into blank terminal with no TUI or visible output
body:
When spawning a worker with the vibe harness, the session terminal appears blank. There is no Vibe TUI, no startup text, no
  progress output, and no obvious error message.

  Expected behavior:

  - Either Vibe should open an interactive TUI like other terminal agents, or
  - AO should clearly show that Vibe is running in headless/programmatic mode and stream/print useful output or failures.

  Actual behavior:

  - The terminal stays blank after spawning the worker.
  - It is not clear whether Vibe is running, waiting, crashed, or exited.
  - The pane remains open because AO keeps the tmux session alive after the agent exits.

  Relevant code:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/vibe/vibe.go
  - The adapter launches Vibe with:

  vibe --trust --output text --workdir <workspace> ... -p <prompt>

  This uses Vibe programmatic mode, not the interactive TUI. With --output text, Vibe may only print the final response and may
  not stream progress.

  Possible causes:

  - --output text hides progress until completion.
  - Vibe exits quickly and AO leaves a blank keep-alive shell.
  - Vibe crashes before output, but the error is not visible enough in the terminal.
  - Empty/missing prompt may launch a mode that does not behave as AO expects.

  Suggested fixes:

  - Use --output streaming for Vibe workers so output appears while the task runs.
  - Or support an interactive/TUI launch mode for Vibe.
  - Surface Vibe startup/crash errors clearly before entering the keep-alive shell.
  - Add a guard/error for empty prompts if Vibe requires -p <prompt> for AO-managed workers.

  Local observation:
  Running vibe --help showed that -p/--prompt is programmatic mode, and --output text is for final human-readable output. This
  matches the blank/no-TUI behavior.

title: grok worker launches in single-turn mode and exits without editing
body:
## Problem

  When spawning a `grok` worker, AO launches Grok with `-p <prompt>`. On Grok `0.2.64`, `-p` / `--single` means single-turn
  mode: Grok prints a response to stdout and exits.

  As a result, AO workers using Grok do not stay in an interactive coding session and may make no file changes.

  ## Example

  Session: `renz-ui-51`
  Task: `add good morning message in hero section`
  Harness: `grok`

  The tmux pane showed only:

  ```text
  I'll find the hero section in the codebase and see how it's structured so we can add a good morning message.
  The hero already has a static greeting — I'll check other landing files and styles to see if we should make it time-based or
  more prominent.

  Then Grok returned to the shell prompt. git status was clean.

  ## Root Cause

  AO currently builds the Grok launch command as:

  grok --no-auto-update -p "<task>"

  But grok -h documents:

  -p, --single <PROMPT>
    Single-turn prompt. Prints the response to stdout and exits

  ## Expected Behavior

  A Grok worker should start an interactive coding session and continue running so it can inspect files, edit code, run checks,
  and respond to follow-up messages.

  ## Suggested Fix

  Change the Grok adapter to pass the initial task as the positional prompt instead of using -p:

  grok --no-auto-update "<task>"

  Keep -p only for an explicit one-shot/headless mode, if AO supports that separately.

  ## Impact

  Grok workers can appear idle/alive in AO because the tmux shell remains open, but the Grok process has already exited and no
  work is being performed.

title: After-start prompt delivery can be lost for interactive TUI agents
body:
## Summary

  Workers using after-start prompt delivery can spawn into an idle TUI without receiving the initial task prompt.

  I observed this with `cline` and `kimi`: AO created the sessions and stored the prompt, but the agent panes remained at their
  empty input screens and no prompt activity signal was recorded.

  ## Evidence

  Recent sessions had the prompt persisted in SQLite:

  - `renz-ui-48` / `cline` / prompt: `add good morning message in hero section`
  - `renz-ui-49` / `kimi` / prompt: `add good morning message in hero section`

  But both panes were idle at the TUI input prompt, and `first_signal_at` was empty for both sessions.

  Kiro behaved differently: `renz-ui-50` launched with the prompt in argv:

  ```sh
  kiro-cli chat --agent ao -- "add good morning message in hero section"

  and had first_signal_at populated, so this appears specific to PromptDeliveryAfterStart.

  ## Likely Cause

  For agents returning PromptDeliveryAfterStart, the session manager creates the runtime and immediately calls
  m.messenger.Send(...):

  - backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go
  - after-start handling around prompt stripping and post-spawn send

  Cline and Kimi both rely on this path:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/cline.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/kimi.go

  The prompt is probably sent before the interactive TUI is ready to accept input, so the keystrokes are lost or ignored.

  ## Expected Behavior

  When a worker is spawned with a prompt, the agent should reliably receive and submit that prompt, or AO should fail the spawn
  instead of leaving an idle worker.

  ## Actual Behavior

  The worker appears live, but it is just sitting at the agent TUI with no task running.

  ## Suggested Fix

  Add reliable readiness handling for PromptDeliveryAfterStart, such as:

  - wait until the pane output matches an agent-specific ready/input state before sending
  - retry delivery if no first signal/activity is observed shortly after send
  - add adapter-specific delivery implementations where generic tmux keystrokes are unreliable
  - surface a spawn warning/error if prompt delivery cannot be confirmed

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

title: fix(agent-claude-code): stop conflating idle_prompt with permission_prompt
body:
Fixes #2525

## Summary
`notificationState()` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/activity.go` previously mapped both `idle_prompt` (routine end-of-turn idling, not a real blocker) and `permission_prompt` (genuine tool-permission block) to the same `domain.ActivityWaitingInput` state, causing sessions to show `needs_input` — and mask their real PR-derived status — whenever they were simply idle between turns rather than actually blocked.

This narrows the mapping so only `permission_prompt` sets `ActivityWaitingInput`; `idle_prompt` now sets `ActivityIdle` instead. Doc comments in `claudecode/activity.go` and `domain/activity.go` were updated to describe the corrected, narrower semantics, and the one test that encoded the old conflated behavior was updated.

This is a deliberately narrow fix — it does not change `deriveStatus()`'s precedence (confirmed intentional, documented in `docs/architecture.md`), the reaper's staleness handling (tracked separately in #2501), or any frontend code.

## Test plan
- `cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./...`

title: Add prompt readiness hints for interactive agents
body:
## Summary

  Adds prompt-readiness handling for interactive agent adapters that receive their initial worker task after the CLI starts.

  ## Why

  Some terminal-based agents are not ready to accept input immediately after process launch. AO could send the worker prompt
  too early, causing it to be ignored, misparsed, or injected before the interactive prompt was active.

  ## Changes

  - Added optional `AgentPromptReadinessProvider` support for adapters.
  - Added `PromptReadinessHints` with delay, polling, output patterns, timeout, and line count.
  - Updated the session manager to wait for readiness before sending `PromptDeliveryAfterStart` prompts.
  - Falls back to sending the prompt after timeout so startup does not block indefinitely.
  - Added readiness hints for Cline, Kimi, Kiro, and Crush.
  - Adjusted Kiro and Crush worker launches so prompted workers stay interactive and receive prompts after startup.
  - Added tests for readiness waits, timeout fallback, and adapter hint coverage.

  ## Verification

  ```bash
  GOCACHE=/private/tmp/go-build-ao-agent-readiness go test ./internal/adapters/agent/cline ./internal/adapters/agent/kimi ./
  internal/adapters/agent/kiro ./internal/adapters/agent/crush ./internal/session_manager

title: feat(mobile): Connect Mobile: password-authenticated LAN bridge
body:
Adds an opt-in LAN bridge so the mobile app can reach the daemon over the local network. 

A second, on-demand HTTP listener runs inside the daemon (loopback listener unchanged);

it serves the app API behind a bearer-password auth middleware with a per-source lockout, and 404-blocks the loopback-only control routes. 

Desktop gets a Connect Mobile toggle in the Settings menu (QR + password); mobile scans to connect.


instructions while running : 
when running the mobile server run : npx expo run:ios --device 
and also have a physical device attached via cord for installing the dev client. as we have a native camera dependency for scan so expo go does not work for that feature.

title: feat(notifications): dock bounce, taskbar flash, and unread badge count
body:
## Summary

- **macOS**: dock icon bounces once (`informational`) when a `needs_input` or `ready_to_merge` notification arrives and the app is not focused
- **Windows**: taskbar flashes until the user focuses the window; rapid arrivals are deduped so multiple notifications do not stack focus listeners
- **Linux**: `flashFrame` for taskbar attention + `app.setBadgeCount` for Unity/KDE numeric badge
- **Badge count**: unread notification count kept in sync on all platforms — macOS `dock.setBadge`, Windows overlay icon red dot, Linux `setBadgeCount`
- **Notification panel**: `needs_input` uses a minimal amber dot indicator; `ready_to_merge` keeps the `GitPullRequest` icon; sticky error state clears on dropdown reopen; panel width tightened to 320px

## How it works

Real notifications arrive via SSE (`notification_created` event) and are merged into the React Query cache. The existing `NotificationCenter` component syncs badge count via a `useEffect` on `unreadCount`. The main process handlers (`notifications:show`, `notifications:setBadge`) are platform-branched with guards for null window, NaN/negative counts, and rapid-call dedup.

## Testing in dev

```js
// DevTools console — injects a fake notification and bounces the dock after 3s
__testNotif("needs_input")
__testNotif("ready_to_merge")
```

## Test plan

- [ ] macOS: `__testNotif("needs_input")` — dock bounces once, bell shows count
- [ ] macOS: dock badge count (System Settings > Notifications > Electron > Badge app icon must be enabled)
- [ ] Windows: taskbar flashes on notification, stops on window focus
- [ ] Linux: `flashFrame` fires; `app.setBadgeCount` called
- [ ] Multiple rapid notifications only flash once (dedup guard)
- [ ] All unit tests pass: `npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/notifications.test.ts`

title: feat(mobile): real web terminal + LAN proxy Origin/CORS rewrite
body:
## Summary
- Adds a real xterm.js terminal to the mobile app's web target (`packages/mobile/lib/WebTerminal.web.tsx`), a faithful port of the Electron renderer's hardened `XtermTerminal.tsx`, wired into the session screen in place of the previous "Terminal is phone-only" placeholder.
- Rewrites `ao-phone-proxy.js` into an HTTP-aware reverse proxy that rewrites Origin/CORS so a browser on another machine can reach the daemon through it (test-first, `ao-phone-proxy.test.js`).
- Two real bugs found and fixed during end-to-end verification against a live daemon:
  - `lib/mux.ts`: the React-Native-only WebSocket 3-arg header workaround broke every browser's handshake outright (`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` error) — browsers silently failed to connect at all.
  - `app/session/[id].tsx`: the web terminal's ready callback always fired before the async mux connection finished (a guaranteed effect-ordering race, not a rare one), so the PTY attach silently never happened even though status showed "live" with correct dims.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (packages/mobile) — exit 0
- [x] `node scripts/ao-phone-proxy.test.js` — Origin/CORS rewrite self-check passes
- [x] Native bundle purity: `npx expo export --platform ios` contains no `xterm-helper-textarea` string
- [x] Live verification against a running daemon: connect → live status + real dims, TUI output renders correctly (colors, formatting), keyboard input round-trips to the PTY, window resize reflows the grid, zoom changes font in place without re-attaching, kill → dead overlay → Restore brings the terminal back live, compose sends via REST and the agent responds
- [ ] Wheel-scroll → tmux copy-mode: SGR report generation confirmed (event correctly intercepted, preventDefault fires) but couldn't visually confirm tmux copy-mode entry against the specific test session used (its own CLI likely captures mouse tracking first)
- [ ] Copy-on-select / paste, click-to-open-link: not independently exercised this pass (code is a byte-for-byte match against the design spec's reference implementation)
- [ ] Daemon-restart reconnect: skipped — daemon is shared with other live sessions, too risky to restart for this verification pass

**Known gap before merge:** this branch was cut from an older `main` and has not been reconciled with everything since merged to `origin/main` — in particular unrelated frontend refactors in `SessionView.tsx` (CenterPane extraction) produce a real merge conflict that needs someone with context on that work to resolve before this can land cleanly.

title: Sync session topbar status to agent activity
body:
## Problem

On the session detail page, the topbar status pill and the Summary sidebar Activity row can show conflicting agent states.

Example from the attached screenshot:

![Session topbar shows Working while Activity shows Idle](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/whoisasx/7ab262b0a25a96b67d9694d382556aa6/raw/d0a8b9932fee39f02bec66849f646f1847e64bd3/session-topbar-activity-mismatch.svg)

In the screenshot, the topbar shows `Working`, while Summary > Activity shows `Idle`.

This happens because the two surfaces currently render different session fields:

- The topbar uses the coarse worker display bucket derived from `session.status` via `workerDisplayStatus(session)`.
- The Summary > Activity row uses raw agent activity from `session.activity.state`, and then adds SCM/session context badges separately.

The topbar reads like it is showing the current agent state, so it is confusing when it says `Working` while the agent activity state is actually `Idle`.

## Desired Behavior

Sync the session topbar pill to the raw agent activity state.

The Summary > Activity section should continue showing the combined current-state row:

- Agent activity state: `Working`, `Idle`, `Input Needed`, `Exited`, or unavailable.
- SCM/session context badges: `CI Failed`, `Changes Requested`, `Conflict`, `No Signal`, etc.

The topbar should only show the agent activity state. It should not show PR/SCM-derived states.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files:

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts`
- `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.test.ts`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.test.tsx`

Current source split:

- `ShellTopbar.tsx` renders `SessionStatusPill` using `workerDisplayStatus(session)`.
- `SessionInspector.tsx` renders `InspectorActivityPill` using `session.activity?.state ?? "unknown"`.
- `workerDisplayStatus` currently maps `idle` into the `working` bucket, which is correct for broad board grouping but wrong for the topbar's current-agent-state affordance.

Consider extracting a shared agent activity pill mapper so the topbar and inspector use the same labels/tone for agent activity:

- `active` -> `Working`
- `idle` -> `Idle`
- `waiting_input` -> `Input Needed`
- `exited` -> `Exited`
- missing/unknown -> `Activity Unavailable` or an equivalent compact topbar label

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `session.activity.state === "idle"`, the topbar shows `Idle`.
- When `session.activity.state === "active"`, the topbar shows `Working`.
- When `session.activity.state === "waiting_input"`, the topbar shows `Input Needed`.
- When `session.activity.state === "exited"`, the topbar shows `Exited`.
- The topbar does not show PR/SCM-derived states like `CI Failed`, `Changes Requested`, `Ready`, or `Done`.
- The Summary > Activity row still shows agent activity plus SCM/context badges as it does today.
- Tests cover the topbar rendering from raw agent activity, including the `Idle` case.

title: fix: refine renderer scrollbars
Kilo Code terminal does not scroll in AO UI
body:
Description
  Kilo Code sessions cannot be scrolled in the embedded AO terminal. Mouse wheel / trackpad scrolling has no visible effect, while similar full-screen TUI
  agents need wheel input translated into PageUp / PageDown.

  Likely Cause
  The frontend only treats opencode as a keyboard-scrolling pane app:

  const KEYBOARD_SCROLL_PROVIDERS = new Set(["opencode"]);

  This is used to set paneScrollsByKeyboard on XtermTerminal.

  Kilo Code is an opencode fork and appears to share the same TUI scrolling behavior, but kilocode is not included in that set. As a result, AO sends SGR
  wheel reports into tmux instead of sending PageUp / PageDown, and Kilo ignores them.

  Relevant Files

  - frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx
  - frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/kilocode/kilocode.go

  Expected Behavior
  Scrolling in a Kilo Code terminal session should move through the Kilo transcript/history.

  Actual Behavior
  Mouse wheel / trackpad scrolling does nothing in Kilo Code sessions.

  Suggested Fix
  Add kilocode to KEYBOARD_SCROLL_PROVIDERS:

  const KEYBOARD_SCROLL_PROVIDERS = new Set(["opencode", "kilocode"]);

  Add or update a focused frontend test to verify that Kilo Code receives paneScrollsByKeyboard={true} and wheel input is translated to PageUp / PageDown.

title: Orchestrator restart fails with INTERNAL_ERROR when live orchestrator points to stale/non-git worktree
body:
Description
  After saving project settings, AO attempts to restart/replace the project orchestrator. The settings save succeeds, but the restart can fail with:

  Orchestrator restart failed: Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR)

  In the observed case, the active orchestrator row pointed at a canonical worktree path that existed on disk but was no longer a valid Git worktree.

  Example state:

  session: agent-orchestrator-142
  kind: orchestrator
  is_terminated: false
  workspace_path: ~/.ao/data/worktrees/agent-orchestrator/orchestrator/agent-orches-orchestrator
  branch: ao/agent-orches-orchestrator

  But the workspace directory contained only agent config files, such as .claude, and no .git or source checkout. During clean replacement, AO tries to
  retire the old orchestrator and preserve/stash uncommitted work before freeing the canonical branch. Since the recorded workspace path is stale/non-git,
  retire fails and the API returns a generic 500.

  Expected Behavior
  AO should handle stale/broken orchestrator worktree state during clean replacement.

  If the recorded path is not a valid Git worktree, AO should:

  - destroy the old runtime if present,
  - mark the stale orchestrator session terminated,
  - preserve/move aside any stray directory contents,
  - recreate the canonical orchestrator worktree,
  - start the replacement orchestrator.

  Actual Behavior
  The settings save succeeds, but orchestrator restart fails with a generic internal error. The project can be left with a live orchestrator row pointing at
  an unusable workspace path.

  Why This Matters
  This makes settings changes feel partially applied and leaves users unable to restart the project orchestrator from the UI. The error also hides the real
  cause, making recovery difficult.

  Suggested Fix

  - Add a typed backend error for stale/unavailable worktree paths, distinct from dirty worktrees.
  - During SpawnOrchestrator(clean=true) / RetireForReplacement, treat stale non-git worktree paths as recoverable:
      - do not force-delete valid dirty worktrees,
      - but allow stale/non-git paths to be moved aside and the row marked terminated.

  - For replacement spawns, allow AO to move aside a non-empty unregistered canonical path before creating the new Git worktree.
  - Improve the UI message so it says something like:

  Saved, but orchestrator restart failed: stale worktree could not be retired

  instead of only:

  Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR)

  Relevant Areas

  - backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go
  - backend/internal/service/session/service.go
  - frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx

title: Amp worker launches with -x execute mode instead of interactive TUI
body:
## Problem

  Amp workers spawned by AO do not open the interactive TUI when the worker has an initial prompt.

  The Amp adapter currently builds prompted launch commands as:

  ```bash
  amp -x "<prompt>"

  ```
  See:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp_test.go

  -x appears to be Amp execute mode, so AO gets a non-interactive execution path instead of the normal terminal UI. This makes
  Amp behave differently from TUI-first adapters like Kimi and Cline.

  ## Expected Behavior

  AO should launch Amp workers interactively:

  amp

  Then AO should deliver the initial worker prompt after startup through the runtime pane/tmux, same as other TUI-first
  adapters.

  ## Actual Behavior

  AO launches prompted Amp workers as:
 ```
  amp -x "<prompt>"
  ```

  This prevents the Amp TUI from opening reliably and can result in the process streaming output or exiting instead of staying
  attached as an interactive worker.

  ## Likely Fix

  Update the Amp adapter to:

  1. Launch amp without -x, even when LaunchConfig.Prompt is present.
  2. Override GetPromptDeliveryStrategy to return ports.PromptDeliveryAfterStart.
  3. Update Amp adapter tests to expect the prompt to be delivered after startup.
  4. Keep system prompt and permission behavior unchanged unless Amp exposes documented interactive flags for them.

  Relevant reference patterns:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/kimi.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/cline.go

  ## Notes

  This looks like an adapter behavior issue, not a tmux/browser terminal issue. The tmux runtime is already capable of launching
  interactive TUIs; the Amp adapter is selecting the non-interactive command path.

title: Amp adapter passes unsupported --permission-mode flags
body:
## Description

  The Amp adapter maps AO permission modes to Claude-style `--permission-mode` CLI flags:

  ```go
  func appendPermissionFlags(cmd *[]string, mode ports.PermissionMode) {
        switch mode {
        case ports.PermissionModeAcceptEdits:
                *cmd = append(*cmd, "--permission-mode", "acceptEdits")
        case ports.PermissionModeAuto:
                *cmd = append(*cmd, "--permission-mode", "auto")
        case ports.PermissionModeBypassPermissions:
                *cmd = append(*cmd, "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions")
        }
  }

  Relevant files:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp_test.go

  Amp’s documented permissions model does not appear to expose a --permission-mode CLI flag. The Amp manual describes permissions through
  settings/plugin behavior instead:

  - amp.permissions
  - amp.guardedFiles.allowlist
  - amp.dangerouslyAllowAll

  Amp also states that it does not ask for approval before running tools by default.

  ## Problem

  When AO launches Amp with a non-default permission mode, it can build commands like:

  amp --permission-mode acceptEdits
  amp --permission-mode auto
  amp --permission-mode bypassPermissions

  If Amp does not support these flags, the CLI may fail on startup or exit before opening the TUI.

  This is separate from the prompt delivery issue. Even after Amp launches interactively without -x / prompt argv, permission modes can still
  make the launch command invalid.

  ## Expected Behavior

  AO should only pass documented Amp CLI flags.

  If Amp does not support CLI permission flags, the Amp adapter should either:

  - omit AO permission-mode flags for Amp, or
  - translate them into Amp-supported settings/plugin configuration if available.

  ## Actual Behavior

  AO currently appends --permission-mode <mode> for Amp when project/session permissions are configured.

  ## Why This Matters

  Projects that configure worker permissions globally can make Amp workers fail to start, even though plain amp works.

  This can be confusing because the failure depends on AO permission configuration, not on Amp installation or auth.

  ## Suggested Fix

  - Remove --permission-mode mapping from the Amp adapter unless Amp documents support for it.
  - Keep default Amp launch as:

  amp

  - Add/update tests so Amp permission modes do not emit unsupported CLI flags.
  - If AO wants to support Amp-specific permissions later, implement it through documented Amp settings/plugin behavior.

title: fix: omit unsupported amp permission flags
body:
## Summary

  Removes Amp’s AO permission-mode CLI mapping because Amp does not document support for `--permission-mode`.

  Previously, AO could launch Amp with commands like:

  ```sh
  amp --permission-mode acceptEdits
  amp --permission-mode auto
  amp --permission-mode bypassPermissions

  Those flags appear to be Claude-style permission flags, not Amp CLI flags. When a project or session config sets a non-default permission mode,

title: fix(mobile): shared-terminal co-view, phone zoom/pan, width & Android fixes, authenticated LAN preview
body:
## What

Brings the shared-terminal co-view work (originally proposed in a downstream PR) on top of `main`, plus a set of mobile-app fixes uncovered while testing it on physical devices. and added menu picker for spawing new agents which are auth harnesses.

## Commits

**Terminal (backend) — one authoritative grid for co-viewers**
- `fix(terminal): size the shared PTY to the largest attached client`
- `fix(terminal): size the shared PTY to one authoritative grid so co-viewers (desktop + phone) don't mis-render`

The PTY is now sized to a single authoritative grid so a desktop and a phone viewing the same terminal no longer fight over dimensions and mis-render.

**Mobile — terminal rendering & interaction**
- `fix(mobile): let the phone zoom and pan the shared terminal grid instead of only shrinking it to an unreadable overview` — pinch-zoom between fit and 1:1, one-finger pan while zoomed, double-tap to toggle, cursor auto-follow.
- `fix(mobile): make the terminal fill the screen width on iOS and Android` — zero xterm's phantom mobile scrollbar (overlay scrollbars measure 0px, so its `|| 15` fallback reserved 15px it never used) before measuring, and re-measure a few times as Android layout/fonts settle so the grid reaches full width without needing a keyboard toggle.
- `fix(mobile): stop the Android terminal from crashing to black, and reserve keyboard space on both platforms` — drop `androidLayerType:"hardware"` (a hardware layer composites the xterm `<canvas>` blank on many devices), surface a render-process crash instead of a silent black screen, and reserve keyboard height on both platforms (Android edge-to-edge defeats `adjustResize`).

**Mobile — authenticated previews over the LAN bridge**
- `feat(mobile): serve authenticated previews over the LAN bridge` — the LAN listener gates the preview route behind the connection-password. A preview page's WebView subresource requests (images/CSS/JS) can't carry our `Authorization` header, so the backend now drops a path-scoped, HttpOnly auth cookie scoped to that session's `/preview/files/` path only (it can never authenticate `/kill`, `/send`, or another session). Runs on the LAN listener only; the loopback/desktop path is unchanged. Mobile sends the Bearer header on the top-level preview load.

**Tooling**
- `chore(mobile): patch @fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview via patch-package`

## Verification

Ran the checks CI performs for this diff:

- `gofmt -l`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` — clean
- **golangci-lint v2.12.2** — 0 issues
- `go test -race` on all changed backend packages (httpd, terminal, conpty, tmux) — pass
- `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...` — pass
- **prettier@3 `--check`** on changed files — clean
- Mobile `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- Manually tested on physical iOS and Android devices: terminal fills width, zoom/pan gestures, Android renderer stability, authenticated preview.

## Notes

title: Windows Codex auth probe reports Needs auth when WindowsApps codex.exe shadows npm codex.cmd
body:
## Bug

On Windows, Agent Orchestrator shows Codex as `Needs auth` in the Project agents picker even though the user's installed npm Codex CLI is logged in.

**Source:** local Codex desktop chat report + screenshot  
**Reported by:** @somewherelostt  
**Analyzed against:** `1a056aa1ad93fe7146900629d005f8de0f72e1e9` (`origin/main`, 2026-07-10)  
**AO version:** `dev`  
**Daemon under test:** rewrite daemon, `go run ./cmd/ao status --json` reported `state=ready`, `port=3002`, `dataDir=C:\Users\abuma\.ao\data`  
**OS:** Windows NT `10.0.26200.0`, PowerShell `7.6.3`, Go `go1.24.4 windows/amd64`  
**Priority:** high - Codex is a core agent option and becomes unavailable in the UI on affected Windows installs.  
**Confidence:** High - reproduced locally, traced exact resolver order and failing executable.

![Project agents picker showing Codex Needs auth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-windowsapps-auth/.issue-assets/codex-windowsapps-auth/needs-auth-picker.png)

## Reproduction

1. On Windows, install/use Codex such that both of these exist:
   - WindowsApps packaged Codex executable under `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_*\app\resources\codex.exe`
   - npm Codex shim under `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd`
2. Log into the npm Codex CLI.
3. Start AO from latest `main`.
4. Open a project's **Project agents** picker.
5. Observe `Codex` is disabled and marked `Needs auth`.

## Observed

AO's agent probe reports Codex as unauthorized:

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "id": "codex",
    "label": "Codex",
    "authStatus": "unauthorized"
  },
  "supported": true,
  "installed": true
}
```

The UI renders `Codex — Needs auth`.

## Expected

If the user's Codex CLI reports logged in, AO should mark Codex as authorized and allow Codex to be selected.

## Local Verification

The npm shim is authenticated:

```powershell
& "$env:APPDATA\npm\codex.cmd" login status
# Logged in using ChatGPT
# exit=0
```

Windows command resolution returns the WindowsApps packaged executable first for `codex.exe`:

```powershell
where.exe codex.exe
# C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_26.707.3563.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\app\resources\codex.exe

where.exe codex.cmd
# C:\Users\abuma\AppData\Roaming\npm\codex.cmd
```

Trying to run the WindowsApps executable directly fails:

```text
Program 'codex.exe' failed to run: ... Access is denied.
```

## Root Cause

The Windows branch of `ResolveCodexBinary` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go` checks broad PATH lookup for `codex.exe` before known user-install locations:

```go
for _, name := range []string{"codex.exe", "codex.cmd", "codex"} {
    path, err := exec.LookPath(name)
    if err == nil && path != "" {
        return resolveNativeWindowsCodex(path), nil
    }
}
```

Because `codex.exe` is checked first, `exec.LookPath` can return the WindowsApps package resource before AO checks `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd` or the npm package's bundled native executable.

The auth probe then runs:

```go
exec.CommandContext(probeCtx, binary, "login", "status")
```

That direct child process fails with Access denied before producing `logged in`, so AO falls through to `unauthorized` and the UI incorrectly asks the user to authenticate.

Relevant code path:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`: `AuthStatus`
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`: `ResolveCodexBinary`
- `backend/internal/service/agent/service.go`: catalog/probe maps auth status into agent inventory
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx`: displays unauthorized agents as `Needs auth`

## Fix Direction

Prefer known user-install paths on Windows before broad `codex.exe` lookup, especially:

- `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\@openai\codex\...\codex.exe`
- `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd`
- `%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin\codex.exe`

Also consider skipping `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_*\app\resources\codex(.exe)` for direct daemon execution, or treating direct-launch `Access is denied` as `unknown` rather than `unauthorized` so the UI does not incorrectly say the user needs to log in.

## Impact

- Codex appears unavailable in AO on affected Windows machines.
- Users who are already logged in through npm Codex are told they need auth.
- Worker/orchestrator agent selection is misleading and blocks Codex selection from the UI.

## Duplicate Search

No matching existing issue or PR found on 2026-07-10 using:

```bash
gh issue list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex WindowsApps auth"
gh issue list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex auth unauthorized Windows"
gh issue list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "Needs auth Codex"
gh pr list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex WindowsApps auth"
gh pr list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex.exe codex.cmd"
```

The only `Needs auth Codex` issue-search hit was unrelated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On Windows with both WindowsApps Codex and npm Codex installed, AO resolves the npm/bundled Codex CLI for auth probing.
- `codex.cmd login status` returning logged in results in AO `authStatus: authorized`.
- Add a regression test covering WindowsApps `codex.exe` shadowing `codex.cmd`.
- UI no longer shows `Codex — Needs auth` for an authenticated npm Codex CLI.

title: fix(frontend): surface daemon failure reason instead of generic "not ready" error
body:
## Bug

When a second checkout's Electron instance cannot attach to the daemon (checkout identity mismatch — but also spawn failure or unexpected exit), the main process computes a specific, actionable diagnostic and sends it over the `daemon:status` IPC. The renderer drops it: every API call surfaces only the generic `"AO daemon is not ready."` error, so the user never learns another checkout owns the daemon or how to fix it.

## Root cause

- `applyDaemonStatus()` (`renderer/lib/daemon-status.ts`) quarantines the base URL for non-ready statuses but discards `status.message`.
- `runtimeFetch()`'s 503 short-circuit (`renderer/lib/api-client.ts`) hardcodes the generic body, so `apiErrorMessage()` can only ever surface the fallback.

The diagnostic is computed in `main.ts` (`daemonIdentityError()`), shipped over IPC, and then dead on arrival.

## Fix

Keep the status message alongside the quarantined base URL (`setDaemonUnavailableMessage`), and let the 503 short-circuit prefer it over the generic fallback — the same `status.message || "AO daemon is not ready."` pattern `_shell.tsx` already uses for project creation. This benefits every `daemonStatus` failure path (identity mismatch, spawn failure, daemon exit), not just the issue's trigger, and complements #2253 (which disables actions and adds a Restart button but does not fix the message masking).

## Testing

- New `renderer/lib/daemon-status.test.ts` regression test: fails before the fix (generic message masks the identity diagnostic), passes after. Also covers the no-message fallback and that a stale reason is cleared once the daemon is ready again.
- `useDaemonStatus.test.tsx`: completed the partial `api-client` mock with the new export.
- Full frontend vitest suite, `tsc --noEmit`, and `prettier --check` on the changed files all pass.

Fixes #2481

## Summary

Improve the **contributor experience** without turning `CONTRIBUTING.md` into a second setup handbook.

`AGENTS.md` already owns layout, commands, hard rules, and PR hygiene. `CONTRIBUTING.md` should stay the human front door (Discord, claiming work, manners) and point at the deep docs.

Design draft: https://app.notion.com/p/batmnnn/Enhanced-CONTRIBUTING-md-Draft-399b156bc37081ba85d7d3d7256cd854
## Motivation

Current `CONTRIBUTING.md` is Discord-first and short (good), but thin on:

- Non-code contribution paths
- Issue claiming (avoid duplicate work)
- Clear handoff to bug/feature/PR structure

There are also **no** GitHub issue/PR templates under `.github/`, so the guidance we keep out of CONTRIBUTING has nowhere to land in the UI.

## Scope

**In**
- Enrich `CONTRIBUTING.md` (ways to contribute, claim step, Discord vs GitHub, pointers to `AGENTS.md` / README / `docs/architecture.md`, CoC one-liner)
- Add `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` (bug + feature forms + `config.yml` contact links)
- Add `.github/pull_request_template.md` (What / Why / How / Testing + checklist)

**Out**
- No setup/command dump in CONTRIBUTING (stays in README / `AGENTS.md` / `docs/`)
- No rewrite of `AGENTS.md`
- No new `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` / `CONTRIBUTORS.md` files in this change (optional follow-up)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` stays short and CX-focused; still links `AGENTS.md`
- [ ] “New issue” offers Bug report and Feature request forms
- [ ] New PRs prefill from the PR template
- [ ] Issue template config links Discord + CONTRIBUTING

## Notes

Precedents for the shape: Vite (skimmable contributor guide), GitHub Docs (contribution types + templates).

title: Dev daemon state split makes project imports and registry look inconsistent
body:
## Bug

After PR #2465, dev Electron runs its own daemon on port 3002 with state under `~/.ao/dev/data`, while normal/packaged AO and the verified CLI default to port 3001 with state under `~/.ao/data`. This prevents daemon collisions, but it also forks the project registry and import state. A project can appear to already exist in one mode while the other mode shows a different or empty registry, forcing manual reconciliation of local daemon state.

**Source:** User report in local Codex chat on 2026-07-11
**Reported by:** @nikhilachale
**Analyzed against:** `5b0c4f5289c654b51ede4a4a927cced0013808de` / upstream main `5b0c4f52`
**AO version:** `dev` from repo-built `/tmp/ao`
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, zsh, Go 1.26.4
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Have normal AO state in `~/.ao/data/ao.db` with registered projects.
2. Run Electron in dev mode, which starts/uses a dev daemon on port 3002.
3. Observe dev mode reads `~/.ao/dev/data/ao.db` instead of `~/.ao/data/ao.db`.
4. Try to import/register projects and compare what the dev UI shows vs what normal mode/CLI sees.

Observed locally:

- `~/.ao/running.json` pointed at port 3001 and `~/.ao/data`, but was stale/dead.
- `~/.ao/dev/running.json` pointed at live port 3002.
- Direct `curl http://127.0.0.1:3002/readyz` returned ready for the dev daemon.
- `~/.ao/data/ao.db` had active projects including `agent-orchestrator`, `mj-scaffold`, `renz-ui`, and `reverbcode`.
- `~/.ao/dev/data/ao.db` initially had only the dev-mode project row, so the dev UI showed different data from normal mode.

## Root Cause

PR #2465 fixed #2464 by intentionally isolating dev mode from the installed app. The current code in `frontend/src/main.ts` does this unconditionally when `!app.isPackaged`:

- lines 136-141 define `DEV_DAEMON_PORT = 3002` and `DEV_STATE_SUBDIR = "dev"`.
- lines 300-303 make dev read `~/.ao/dev/running.json`.
- lines 390-393 inject `AO_PORT=3002`, `AO_RUN_FILE=~/.ao/dev/running.json`, and `AO_DATA_DIR=~/.ao/dev/data`.
- lines 567-571 make port probes prefer 3002 in dev.

The backend default remains canonical `~/.ao/data` when `AO_DATA_DIR` is unset (`backend/internal/config/config.go` lines 282-293). Import idempotency checks project IDs in whichever store is open (`backend/internal/legacyimport/importer.go` lines 130-136), and project add rejects active path/id conflicts in the current store (`backend/internal/service/project/service.go` lines 181-196). With two stores, those checks are internally correct but user-visible state diverges across dev and normal modes.

## Related

- #2464: original bug where dev latched onto the installed daemon and killed it on quit.
- #2465: merged fix that introduced isolated port/run-file/data-dir defaults.

## Fix

Do not blindly revert #2465; it fixed a real supervisor collision. Possible fixes:

1. Keep separate ports/run-files/supervisor sockets for dev, but make project registry/import state shared or explicitly synchronized.
2. Make isolated dev data opt-in, while default dev mode attaches to canonical state without linking in a way that can kill the installed daemon.
3. Add an explicit dev-state import/sync path and UI/CLI messaging so users know dev mode is using a separate registry and can reconcile it without direct SQLite/manual API calls.

The safest implementation should preserve the #2464 guarantee: quitting dev Electron must not kill the installed app daemon.

## Impact

- Developers running `npm run dev` see a different project list than the installed app/normal daemon.
- Legacy project import can report rows as already present in one store while the active dev UI is pointed at another store.
- Users have to manually reconcile `~/.ao/data` and `~/.ao/dev/data`, which is brittle and confusing.

title: fix(workspace): recover stale orchestrator worktrees during replacement
body:
## Summary

  This fixes clean orchestrator replacement when AO has an active old orchestrator row whose recorded workspace path is stale.

  Previously, `RetireForReplacement` always called `StashUncommitted` before removing the old orchestrator worktree. If the stored path still existed
  but was no longer a valid git worktree, `git status` failed with `not a git repository`, which bubbled up as an error and blocked replacement. The
  user saw a failed restart even though the stale path was AO-managed state that could be safely recovered.

  ## What Changed

  - Added `ports.ErrWorkspaceStale` to represent AO-managed workspace paths that no longer point to a valid registered git worktree.
  - Updated `gitworktree.StashUncommitted` to return `ErrWorkspaceStale` only after path safety checks, for:
    - missing managed workspace paths
    - existing paths not present in `git worktree list`
    - paths where `git status` reports `not a git repository`
  - Updated `RetireForReplacement` to handle only `ErrWorkspaceStale` as recoverable:
    - skip stash/preserve for the stale workspace
    - clear `session_worktrees` restore markers
    - destroy runtime if present
    - best-effort remove the stale AO-managed folder
    - mark the old orchestrator session terminated
    - continue spawning the fresh orchestrator
  - Kept all other stash/preserve errors fatal, so AO does not delete a real workspace when it cannot preserve work.
  - Added tests for stale classification, unsafe-path behavior, stale replacement recovery, and non-stale preserve failure behavior.

  ## Behavior Covered

  - Valid dirty git worktree: preserve changes, remove old worktree, mark old orchestrator terminated, spawn fresh orchestrator.
  - Valid clean git worktree: remove old worktree, mark old orchestrator terminated, spawn fresh orchestrator.
  - Missing / unregistered / non-git AO-managed path: treat as stale AO-owned state and recover.
  - Real git worktree with preserve failure: fail replacement and leave session/worktree state intact.
  - Path outside AO’s managed workspace root: fail safely and do not touch it.

  ## Data Model

  This does not delete the old orchestrator session row. The old row remains as durable history/debug context. The fix only clears restore/worktree
  markers that could cause incorrect restore behavior, then marks the old orchestrator terminated.
  
  closes #2551

title: feat(cli): add dev command for importing projects from data directory
body:
## Summary

Adds a manual dev-only project registry import command:

```bash
ao dev import-projects
```

This lets a dev AO daemon copy project registry metadata from the normal AO data dir into the current dev AO data dir without sharing SQLite state or copying runtime/session data.

Also namespaces generated branches for the default dev data dir so dev AO worktrees do not collide with normal AO worktrees in the same source repository.

## What changed

### Dev project import

Added:

```bash
ao dev import-projects
```

Flags:

- `--from-data-dir <path>`
- `--dry-run`
- `--json`

Default behavior:

- Source data dir defaults to `~/.ao/data`
- Target data dir is the current `AO_DATA_DIR`
- Typical dev target is `~/.ao/dev/data`

The command copies only active project registry data:

- project ID
- project path
- display name
- repo origin
- project kind
- registration timestamp
- project config
- workspace child repo registry

It does not copy:

- sessions
- worktrees
- runtime or terminal handles
- PR/review/check facts
- notifications
- telemetry
- hooks
- runtime files
- repository folders

### Safety checks

Before writing, the command refuses when:

- the target daemon is live according to the current `AO_RUN_FILE`
- source and target data dirs resolve to the same path

### Conflict behavior

- same ID + same path: update target metadata/config
- missing ID/path: insert into target
- same path with different active ID: skip and report conflict
- same ID with different active path: skip and report conflict
- never archives or deletes target projects

Dry-run uses the same planning path as real writes, including planned insert conflict detection.

### Dev branch namespace

When the daemon uses the default dev data dir:

```
~/.ao/dev/data
```

generated AO branches now use the `ao/dev/...` namespace.

Examples:

```
ao/dev/reverbcode-orchestrator
ao/dev/reverbcode-1/root
```

Normal AO keeps existing branch names:

```
ao/reverbcode-orchestrator
ao/reverbcode-1/root
```

Explicit user-provided `--branch` values are unchanged.

This prevents dev AO from failing with `BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE` when normal AO already has the canonical orchestrator branch checked out in another worktree.

## Why

The dev daemon is isolated by port, run file, and data dir, but Git branch checkout locks live in the underlying source repository. After importing project registry metadata into dev AO, both normal AO and dev AO may point at the same repo path. Without a dev branch namespace, dev AO can try to create a worktree for a branch already checked out by normal AO.

The import command keeps state sharing explicit and narrow, while the branch namespace keeps dev and normal worktrees from colliding.

## Verification

Ran:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/devimport/... ./internal/session_manager ./internal/service/session
go test ./internal/cli/... ./internal/service/... ./internal/devimport/...
go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/...
```

All passed.

Working tree is clean and branch is tracking `origin/fix/dev-import-projects`.

closes #2597

title: fix(terminal): force UTF-8 client mode on tmux attach
body: ## Summary Fixes #2603. - Root-causes and fixes the garbled box-drawing/underscore rendering symptom. - `tmux attach-session` infers UTF-8 client capability from `LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`/`LANG` in the attaching process's environment. AO's daemon typically runs without an interactive shell's locale, so tmux silently treats the attach client as non-UTF-8. - A non-UTF-8 client makes tmux's `tty_check_codeset` (tty.c) replace any character it can't map through its legacy ACS table with underscores matching the glyph's display width. Common box-drawing glyphs (│ ─ etc.) are in that ACS table, so they still rendered correctly — which is why an earlier investigation attempt, testing only a box-drawing border character, concluded locale had no effect and marked the theory disproven. Agent CLI status icons outside the ACS table (e.g. Claude Code's spinner `✻` U+273B, its `⎿` U+23BF continuation marker) are not covered and were silently rewritten to `_`. - Passing `-u` to `tmux attach-session` forces `CLIENT_UTF8` on regardless of the daemon's environment, matching how a bare `tmux attach` from an interactive shell (which does have a UTF-8 locale) already behaves — which is why the bug only reproduced through AO, never through a bare terminal attach to the same session. Confirmed with a byte-level repro outside AO/Electron entirely: spawning `tmux attach-session` via a pty with a stripped, locale-less env reproduces `_ _ _` for `✻ ⎿ ←` while `│` still renders correctly; adding `-u` fixes the icons with no change to the box-drawing case. ## Screenshots **Before** (`-u` not passed) — agent status icons (spinner, continuation marker) render as `_`: **After** (`-u` passed) — icons render correctly; box-drawing glyphs unaffected either way: ## Test plan - [x] `go build ./...` (backend) - [x] `go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/...` — updated `TestAttachCommandReturnsExpectedArgv` for the new `-u` flag, both attach-command tests pass - [x] `go test ./...` (backend) — no new failures (4 pre-existing, unrelated `internal/cli` failures confirmed present on a clean checkout too) - [x] Manual byte-level repro: pty-attached to a live tmux session with a stripped env, with and without `-u`, confirmed the underscore substitution and the fix directly against tmux 3.4's actual output bytes 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(terminal): agent CLI status icons render as underscores over tmux attach (AO-only)
body: ## Bug Box-drawing/agent-status Unicode characters in AO's embedded terminal (xterm.js attached to a tmux session) sometimes render as underscores instead of their proper glyphs — e.g. Claude Code's spinner `✻` (U+273B) and its `⎿` (U+23BF) continuation marker both showed up as `_`. Common box-drawing glyphs (`│ ─` etc.) were unaffected. This does not reproduce when attaching to the same tmux session from a bare terminal outside AO. This is a split-off of the garbled-rendering half of issue 2484 (that issue also covered a Ctrl+Arrow/Ctrl+Backspace/Ctrl+V double-fire bug, fixed separately in #2586; the rendering half was left open with only an unconfirmed hypothesis). ## Root cause `tmux attach-session` infers UTF-8 client capability from `LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`/`LANG` in the attaching process's environment, unless `-u` is passed explicitly. AO's daemon typically runs without an interactive shell's locale, so tmux silently treats every attach client as non-UTF-8. A non-UTF-8 client makes tmux's `tty_check_codeset` (`tty.c`) replace any character it can't map through its legacy ACS table with underscores matching the glyph's display width. Common box-drawing glyphs are in that ACS table, so they still rendered correctly — which is why an earlier investigation attempt, testing only a box-drawing border character, concluded locale had no effect. Agent CLI status icons outside the ACS table (Claude Code's spinner, its continuation marker, etc.) are not covered and were silently rewritten to `_`. Confirmed with a byte-level repro outside AO/Electron entirely: spawning `tmux attach-session` via a pty with a stripped, locale-less env reproduces `_ _ _` for `✻ ⎿ ←` while `│` still renders correctly. ## Fix Pass `-u` to `tmux attach-session` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go`) to force `CLIENT_UTF8` on regardless of the daemon's environment — matching how a bare `tmux attach` from an interactive shell (which does have a UTF-8 locale) already behaves. ## Screenshots **Before** (no `-u`, glyphs corrupted): **After** (`-u` passed, glyphs correct):

title: feat(config): per-role worker environment profile — MCP, plugins, system prompt, env (claude-code)
body:
## What

Closes #2195. Widens the per-role `RoleOverride` beyond `{agent, model, permissions}` into a full worker environment profile: **system prompt, env, MCP servers, plugins** — scoped per role (worker/orchestrator), defaulting to today's inherit-everything behavior so nothing breaks.

## Why

Today every worker inherits the orchestrator's whole environment from the global `~/.claude`: full MCP set, every plugin, no per-role standing instructions. A code-change worker carries tools and power it does not need — slower, noisier, broader than the task. The per-role mechanism already exists and is proven for `agent`/`model`/`permissions`; this widens the same `RoleOverride` to the rest of the environment.

claude-code already ships a CLI flag for **each** aspect (verified against `claude --help`):

| Aspect | claude-code flag |
|---|---|
| System prompt | `--append-system-prompt` (already mapped) |
| Env | process environment (AO already forwards `project.Env`) |
| MCP | `--mcp-config <json-or-path>` (repeatable) |
| MCP isolation | `--strict-mcp-config` — ignore all other MCP sources ("workers default to none") |
| Plugins | `--plugin-dir <path>` / `--plugin-url <url>` (repeatable) |

## Changes

- **domain** (`backend/internal/domain/agentconfig.go`): `AgentConfig` gains `SystemPrompt`, `Env`, `MCP (*MCPConfig)`, `PluginDirs`. `MCPConfig{Configs, Strict}` — Strict alone (empty configs) is valid and means isolation. `IsZero` → `reflect.DeepEqual`; `Validate` checks the new fields.
- **session manager**: `effectiveAgentConfig` merges the new fields (Env per-key with role winning — deep-copied via the existing `mergeEnv` helper so it never mutates the project config); `buildSystemPrompt` appends the per-role `SystemPrompt` inside the guarded region; role `Env` is layered onto `project.Env` at the `runtimeEnv` call sites (spawn + restore).
- **adapter claudecode**: `appendMCPFlags` / `appendPluginFlags` emit the flags in both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` (resume rebuilds from flags, like `--append-system-prompt`). nil/empty → nothing emitted (inherit global, unchanged).
- **CLI** (`backend/internal/cli/project.go`): mirror structs gain the fields; `--worker-mcp-config` (repeatable), `--worker-strict-mcp`, `--worker-plugin-dir` (repeatable); full surface also via `--config-json`.
- **Regen**: `openapi.yaml` + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.

## Scope

**claude-code only this pass.** codex/other adapters inherit as today (they do not map these flags yet) — follow-up. UI (`ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`) deferred to a separate pass; config is settable via CLI now.

## Verification

- `gofmt` clean, `golangci-lint v2` 0 issues, full affected Go suite passes.
- New unit tests: `agentconfig_test.go` (Validate/IsZero for MCP strict+empty, plugin-dirs), `projectconfig_test.go` per-role cases, `manager_test.go` (`effectiveAgentConfig` merge incl. a non-mutation regression test for Env aliasing, `buildSystemPrompt` appends role prompt, `mergeEnv`), `claudecode` launch/restore emit `--mcp-config`/`--strict-mcp-config`/`--plugin-dir[-url]` in correct positions.
- End-to-end on a live daemon: `ao project set-config <id> --config-json '{...mcp.strict...}'` round-trips all 4 fields; `ao spawn` with a **wrong-shaped** mcp value made claude-code error on validation (= flag reached the CLI); with a correct `{"mcpServers":{...}}` value it started clean; with no `mcp` field it inherited the global MCP set as before.

## Note on MCP config shape

claude-code requires `--mcp-config` values in the `{"mcpServers": {...}}` shape (not a bare server JSON). This is a user-config detail, not a code issue — worth documenting in the per-role guide if/when UI lands.

title: fix(browser): keep preview live and under modal dialogs
body:
Fixes #2615

## Problem

With the Browser tab active, any modal dialog opens underneath the browser preview. The preview is a native WebContentsView that Electron composites above the renderer DOM, so no z-index can place a dialog over it. The dialog close button is unreachable until the dialog is dismissed by clicking outside.

## Solution

While a dialog is open, the native view is parked offscreen at full size, still visible, so video and animation playback never pauses. The panel mirrors the view into the DOM under the dialog, using a live display-media stream of the view frame with a capturePage polling fallback. Closing the dialog restores the view and drops the mirror. Mirror grants are one-shot, expire in 5 seconds, and capture and mirror requests are denied for views the renderer does not own.

## Testing

- npx vitest run: 545 passed
- npm run typecheck: clean
- prettier check on changed files: clean
- Verified in the desktop app: dialog stacks above the preview, close button clickable, page animations keep playing while the dialog is open

Closes #2230. Closes #2195.

---

## Part 1 — `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` (desktop keep-alive) — closes #2230

Opt-in env var: when set, the desktop app spawns its daemon **without** the OS-native supervisor link and skips the orphan-cleanup kill on exit, so the daemon persists across app quit and stops only on an explicit `ao stop`. Default (unset) is byte-for-byte unchanged — the daemon self-stops shortly after the app quits.

Beyond \"power users with long sessions,\" the persistent-daemon mode is a prerequisite for a **detached / remote** topology (a headless daemon in a container, attached from the desktop over an SSH tunnel): without it, closing the desktop window arms-then-fires the supervisor watchdog and kills every running agent session in the container.

Both maintainer (illegalcall) review comments are addressed in the included commits:

- **Cross-launch regression (persist the keep decision with the daemon):** the keep decision is read from the daemon's durable `running.json` owner record (`\"persistent\"` vs `\"app\"`), never the current Electron process env. A daemon spawned keep-alive stays persistent even when the app is later reopened **without** `AO_KEEP_DAEMON`. `shouldLinkOnAttach(\"persistent\") === false` is encoded as a regression test.
- **fd leak:** the parent's `keepDaemonLogFd` is closed immediately after `spawn()` (the child holds its own inherited copy via stdio) and on the spawn-throw path, so each keep-alive start/stop cycle no longer accumulates descriptors.
- **stdio lifetime:** under the flag the daemon's stdio is redirected to `~/.ao/daemon.log` (stdin ignored) and the child is `unref()`'d, so Electron-owned pipes no longer kill the kept-alive daemon on the next stderr log write.
- **truthy parsing:** `keepDaemonAlive` uses an explicit allowlist (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`); `off`/`no` and any unrecognized string keep the default self-stop behavior.

Files: `frontend/src/main.ts`, `frontend/src/main/daemon-owner.ts(.test.ts)`, `frontend/src/shared/daemon-discovery.ts`, `backend/internal/runfile/runfile.go`, `docs/cli/README.md`.

## Part 2 — per-role worker environment profile (claude-code) — closes #2195

Widens the per-role `RoleOverride` beyond `{agent, model, permissions}` into a full worker environment profile: **system prompt, env, MCP servers, plugins** — scoped per role (worker/orchestrator), defaulting to inherit-everything so nothing breaks. claude-code ships a CLI flag for each aspect (`--append-system-prompt`, `--mcp-config`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--plugin-dir`/`--plugin-url`).

- **domain** (`agentconfig.go`): `AgentConfig` gains `SystemPrompt`, `Env`, `MCP *MCPConfig`, `PluginDirs`; `MCPConfig{Configs, Strict}` (Strict alone = isolation, valid).
- **session manager**: `effectiveAgentConfig` merges the new fields — Env per-key via deep-copying `mergeEnv` (a regression test pins that it never mutates the project config), and the MCP pointer / PluginDirs slice are copied rather than aliased (same defense-in-depth). `buildSystemPrompt` appends the per-role prompt; role `Env` layers onto `project.Env` at spawn + restore.
- **adapter claudecode**: `appendMCPFlags` / `appendPluginFlags` emit in **both** `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` (resume rebuilds from flags); both paths call `cfg.Config.Validate()` for symmetry. nil/empty → inherit global, unchanged.
- **CLI**: `--worker-mcp-config` (repeatable), `--worker-strict-mcp`, `--worker-plugin-dir` (repeatable); full surface also via `--config-json`. UI deferred to a follow-up.
- Regen: `openapi.yaml` + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.

**Scope of Part 2:** claude-code only this pass. codex/other adapters inherit as today (follow-up).

## Verification

- `gofmt` + `go vet` clean; affected Go suites pass (`session_manager`, `claudecode`, `domain`, `cli`, `runfile`).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; 26 `daemon-owner` tests pass (incl. the cross-launch and allowlist cases).
- Local review (Claude subagent + Codex adversarial, both approve) on each part independently: no critical issues, all high-risk areas pass (env-merge mutation leak fixed; restore re-applies MCP/plugin flags; nil/empty preserves default behavior; cross-launch keep decision persisted on the daemon record).

## Note

claude-code requires `--mcp-config` values in the `{\"mcpServers\": {...}}` shape (not a bare server JSON) — a user-config detail worth documenting when the UI lands.

title: fix: attribute cross-fork PRs pushed to a non-origin remote
body:
## Summary
- `discoverSubjects` hardcoded `headRepo` to the project's registered origin for every scanned remote, so a PR whose head branch actually lives in a different checkout remote (e.g. a personal `fork` remote used to push branches — the standard OSS contribution pattern) never matched in `candidatesForHeadRepo` and was silently dropped, leaving "no PR yet" forever even though the PR was real and open.
- Fix: pair each scanned repo against every remote in the checkout (including itself) as a `headRepo` candidate, instead of always using origin. `candidatesForHeadRepo` still strictly matches against the PR's actual GitHub head repo, and `matchSession` still requires a branch-prefix match, so over-generating candidates cannot misattribute a stranger's PR — it only allows a genuine cross-fork PR to be attributed correctly instead of dropped.

Fixes #2609

## Test plan
- [x] `cd backend && go build ./...`
- [x] `cd backend && go test ./...` (all pass except 4 pre-existing, unrelated `internal/cli` spawn-command failures that also fail on `main` without this change)
- [x] Added `TestPoll_DiscoversCrossForkPRPushedToForkRemote` covering the exact scenario from the issue: project origin is the upstream base, session pushes to a separate `fork` remote, and the PR opened against origin has its head in the fork — verified this test fails without the fix and passes with it.

title: fix(amp): remove unsupported --permission-mode CLI flags
body:
## What

Removes `appendPermissionFlags` from the Amp adapter. Amp does not support `--permission-mode` CLI flags - its permission model is configured through settings/plugins (`amp.permissions`, `amp.guardedFiles.allowlist`, `amp.dangerouslyAllowAll`), not CLI arguments.

## Why

When AO launches Amp with a non-default permission mode, it builds commands like `amp --permission-mode acceptEdits` which can fail on startup or exit before opening the TUI. Projects that configure worker permissions globally make Amp workers fail to start even though plain `amp` works fine.

Closes #2561

## Changes

- Removed `appendPermissionFlags` function from `amp.go`
- Removed the call to `appendPermissionFlags` in `GetLaunchCommand`
- Removed the call to `appendPermissionFlags` in `GetRestoreCommand`
- Updated comment on `GetLaunchCommand` to reflect `amp` (no flags)
- Updated tests: all permission modes now produce just `{"amp"}` with no `--permission-mode` flags
- Updated restore command test to expect `{"amp", "--resume", "T-abc123"}` without permission flags

## Testing

All existing tests pass with the updated expectations. The test table in `TestGetLaunchCommandMapsPermissionModes` now verifies that every permission mode (default, acceptEdits, auto, bypass) omits `--permission-mode` from the command.

title: fix: make dev:web work on Windows with cross-env
body:
## What

Fixes `npm run dev:web` on Windows by replacing POSIX-style inline env vars with `cross-env`.

## Problem

The current script `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts` fails on Windows because `cmd.exe` and PowerShell don't support inline environment variable assignment. Contributors on Windows see:

```
'VITE_NO_ELECTRON' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.
```

## Fix

- Added `cross-env` as a devDependency
- Changed script to `cross-env VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts`

`cross-env` is the standard solution for this - it sets environment variables in a cross-platform way without changing the command behavior on Unix.

Closes #2589

## Testing

- On Unix: behavior is identical (cross-env just passes the env var through)
- On Windows: `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` is now properly set before vite runs

title: fix: make project deletion tolerant of stale session state
body:
## What

Makes project deletion (`DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}`) robust to stale, legacy, or inconsistent session state by making session teardown errors non-fatal during project removal.

## Why

When a project has stale sessions (locked worktrees, archived project refs, missing runtime handles, etc.), `TeardownProject` returns an error and the entire `Remove` call fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The project stays registered and the user has no recovery path from the UI.

The issue (#2598) explicitly says: "local project removal must be robust to stale, legacy, partially missing, or otherwise inconsistent AO-managed state. If the user asks to remove a local project registration, AO should work around bad session/worktree/runtime records and complete the unregister flow wherever it can do so without deleting unpurged session state."

Closes #2598

## How

Changed `Service.Remove` in `backend/internal/service/project/service.go` to ignore the error from `m.sessions.TeardownProject(ctx, id)` instead of propagating it. The project is still archived (soft-deleted) regardless of whether session teardown succeeded.

This means:
- Sessions that can be torn down, will be
- Sessions that cannot (stale, locked, missing) are left for later cleanup
- The project is always archived, so the user can re-add it without a blocked delete

## Testing

Updated `TestManager_RemoveDoesNotArchiveWhenTeardownFails` to `TestManager_RemoveToleratesTeardownFailure`. The test now verifies that:
- Remove succeeds (no error) even when teardown fails
- The project is archived (no longer active) after Remove returns

Run: `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/project/...`

title: fix(codex): prefer npm/cargo paths over WindowsApps on Windows
body:
## What

On Windows, `ResolveCodexBinary` now checks known user-install paths (npm `codex.cmd`/`codex.exe`, cargo `codex.exe`) before falling back to `exec.LookPath`. When `exec.LookPath` is used as a last resort, paths under `WindowsApps` are skipped.

## Why

On Windows machines with both the WindowsApps packaged Codex and an npm-installed Codex CLI, `exec.LookPath("codex.exe")` resolves to the WindowsApps executable first. That binary cannot be launched directly by AO (Access denied), so the auth probe fails and the UI incorrectly shows `Codex - Needs auth` even though the npm Codex CLI is logged in.

Closes #2582

## How

1. Reorder the Windows resolution: check known npm/cargo candidate paths first, then fall back to `exec.LookPath` only if none exist.
2. Add `isWindowsAppsPath` filter to skip WindowsApps results from `exec.LookPath`, since those binaries cannot be spawned directly by the daemon.
3. Add `TestIsWindowsAppsPath` covering forward/back slashes, case sensitivity, and non-WindowsApps paths.

## Testing

- `TestIsWindowsAppsPath` passes on all platforms (pure string matching, no Windows required).
- Existing `TestResolveCodexBinaryFindsNVMInstallWhenPathIsSparse` still passes (Unix path resolution unchanged).
- The reorder only affects the Windows branch; non-Windows code paths are untouched.

title: feat: split design tokens into TS modules with generated CSS
body: ## Summary This PR replaces the monolithic hand-maintained `tokens.css` with a **typed TypeScript token pipeline** that generates a single committed CSS bundle. Visual output is unchanged, this is a **maintainability and safety** refactor, not a redesign. Follows up on #2535 (token-based design system) by making tokens the real source of truth: editable in TS, validated by tests, and enforced in CI. --- ## Problem Before this change: - Design tokens lived in **`frontend/src/styles/tokens.css`**, with a large amount of theme/bridge/utility CSS inlined in **`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`** - No compile-time types, no generator, no drift detection - Hard to know where to edit (CSS vs TS vs components) - `frontend/src/renderer/lib/design-tokens.ts` was a thin re-export shim That worked for the initial migration but didn’t scale for ongoing UI work or revamps. --- ## Solution ### New file layout (`frontend/src/styles/`) | File | Role | |------|------| | **`primitives.ts`** | Source of truth for values: colors, typography, space, radius, layout sizes, motion, terminal palette, theme metadata | | **`tailwind-bridge.ts`** | Maps Tailwind v4 `@theme` keys → semantic CSS vars (bridge aliases, font aliases, spacing/icon theme vars) | | **`utilities.ts`** | Token-derived `@utility` rules (dialog widths, purple/surface tints, timeline shadows, etc.) | | **`css-utils.ts`** | Naming conventions: `kebab()`, `layoutCssVarName()`, `parsePx()`, `isLayoutIconKey()` | | **`build-tokens-css.ts`** | Generator script — assembles all sections into one CSS string | | **`design-system.generated.css`** | **Committed generated output** (~631 lines) — do not hand-edit | | **`tokens.ts`** | Public barrel export for app code (`import from "../../styles/tokens"`) | | **`tokens.test.ts`** / **`css-utils.test.ts`** | Parity + convention tests | ## No UI / Visual changes ##Before ## After

title: feat: offer to relaunch sessions when the project default permission mode changes (#2504)
body:
Closes #2504.

When a project's default permission mode changes in Project Settings, running sessions keep their old mode. This adds an opt-in offer to relaunch (kill + restore) the affected sessions with the new mode. Restore already re-reads the project's current default, so a kill+restore picks up the new mode automatically; this PR wires the settings-change to a confirm + batch-relaunch flow.

## Backend
- Persist the launched permission mode on the session (`SessionMetadata.Permissions`, migration-free JSON field), set at spawn and restore, so we can tell which running sessions diverge from a new default.
- `Manager.AffectedByPermissionChange` / `RelaunchForPermissionChange` (`session_manager/permission_relaunch.go`): the affected set excludes terminated sessions, the orchestrator, and non-restorable sessions, and includes only those whose normalized stored mode differs from the project's current effective mode (role-override-masked changes are correctly treated as no-ops). Relaunch does a sequential kill+restore per session, records a per-session outcome, and never aborts the whole batch on one failure.
- Endpoints: `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/permission-relaunch/affected` and `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/permission-relaunch`, plus service wrappers, DTOs, and OpenAPI spec entries (regenerated).

## Frontend
- `RelaunchSessionsDialog`: fires from the settings save flow only when the mode actually changed and there is at least one affected session (auto-dismisses on zero). Lists affected sessions with `from -> to` modes, Cancel is the default (opt-in), reports "Relaunched X, failed Y", and invalidates the workspace query.

## Edge cases
- Orchestrator is never killed.
- Uncommitted work is preserved (kill keeps a dirty worktree, restore restores the branch and resumes the conversation); the dialog warns that an in-progress agent turn is interrupted.
- Sessions already on the new mode (including role-override-masked) are excluded from the count.
- Partial batch failure is reported per session and does not abort the batch; a session left terminated can be restored from the existing session UI.

## Testing
- Backend: `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean; new predicate tests (8 cases) and endpoint tests pass; full suite green apart from 4 pre-existing environment-only `cli/spawn_test.go` failures.
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean; dialog and settings-form tests pass.
