title: Agents can open OS browser instead of AO in-app preview for local pages
body:
## Bug report

**Reported by:** user in AO worker chat
**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Checkout analyzed:** `80a95462d9df4c4b492a45c1605e99345332bb47`
**AO daemon:** `ao status` reports ready on port `3001` with data dir `~/.ao/data`

## What happened

During local landing-page verification for [PR #2807](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2807), the agent opened `http://localhost:3002/landing` with the host OS browser via macOS `open` even though repo guidance says frontend demos should use `ao preview [url]` so the page renders in the AO desktop app inspector rail Browser tab.

The agent later corrected this by running:

```bash
ao preview http://localhost:3002/landing
```

But the mistake is easy for future agents to repeat because local-web-preview requests often trigger generic browser habits (`open`, Playwright, or external browser tooling) instead of the AO-specific preview workflow.

## Why this matters

- The user explicitly expected the in-app browser, not a separate OS browser window.
- It weakens validation for AO UI/browser-preview work because the wrong browser surface may have different session state and behavior.
- It creates user confusion when the desktop Browser tab does not reflect what the agent claims to have opened.

## Reproduction

1. In an AO worker session, run a local app, for example:

```bash
cd frontend/src/landing
npm run dev
```

2. Ask the agent to "open the landing page in the browser".
3. The agent may choose `open http://localhost:3002/landing` or another generic browser method instead of `ao preview http://localhost:3002/landing`.

## Expected behavior

For local URLs or frontend demos inside this repo, agents should use AO preview first:

```bash
ao preview http://localhost:3002/landing
```

Only fall back to the OS browser if the user explicitly asks for it or if `ao preview` fails and the agent reports the fallback clearly.

## Existing guidance

`AGENTS.md` already says:

> When showing or demoing frontend changes, run `ao preview [url]` from inside the session so the change renders in the desktop browser panel (the inspector rail's Browser tab); do not just describe it.

This issue is to make that harder to miss in future sessions.

## Possible fixes

- Strengthen `AGENTS.md` with an explicit "do not use macOS `open` / OS browser for local previews unless requested" rule.
- Add a checklist item to the project or bug-triage guidance for frontend validation: "local page opened with `ao preview`, not system browser."
- Consider adding a lightweight warning/lint or agent-facing docs snippet for common local preview commands.

## Duplicate search performed

Searched open/closed issues for:

- `ao preview in-app browser open local browser agent`
- `in-app browser preview local browser`
- `agent opens system browser instead of ao preview`
- `browser preview agent instructions`

Related but not duplicate: [#2779](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2779) tracks proxied preview asset resolution, not agents choosing the wrong browser surface.

## Root cause confidence

Medium. This is primarily an agent/process/documentation guardrail gap, not a daemon/runtime defect. The product command `ao preview` works when used.

title: Telemetry leak: ao.cli.usage_errors.command ships raw positional args (URLs, paths, free text) to PostHog verbatim
body:
## Bug

The `ao.cli.usage_errors` telemetry event records `command` and `command_path` as the **raw positional argument tokens** from the failed invocation, not the resolved command name/shape. Because argument parsing has already failed by the time this event fires, whatever the user typed in the command slot is forwarded verbatim — including URLs, absolute file paths, multi-paragraph instructions, and non-English free text. The remote telemetry allowlist was intended to permit only a short command name through, but it gates only the **keys**, not the **values**, so unbounded free text reaches PostHog.

**Source:** reported by @Tom24 in #bug-triage (Discord)
**Analyzed against:** `a2d4ab6b` (`fix: update landing demo video (#2807)`)
**Confidence:** High — traced exact code path end-to-end (CLI client → daemon route → PostHog sink)

## Reproduction

1. Daemon running on `:3001`, telemetry enabled.
2. Run any command whose first positional arg is free text, so Cobra fails to resolve a subcommand:
   ```
   ao "https://gitlab.com/myorg/repo/-/merge_requests/123"
   ao /Users/fora/Sites/internal-tool
   ao "Review this PR and merge if CI is green; if the diff touches auth, ping @security before..."
   ```
3. Parse fails → `usageError` → CLI emits usage-error telemetry.
4. Inspect the outgoing PostHog `/capture/` request body (or the sampled events): the `command` and `command_path` properties contain the verbatim free text.

Sampled events from the reporter include GitLab MR URLs, absolute local paths (`/Users/fora/Sites/…`, `/tmp/claude-1000/…`), full internal PR-review instructions, multi-paragraph orchestration directives, and non-English commands (34+ events).

## Root Cause

Two layers fail to bound the value; together they leak:

**1. CLI client populates `command`/`command_path` from raw args — `backend/internal/cli/root.go:238-252`:**
```go
func usageErrorCommand(args []string) (string, string) {
    tokens := []string{"ao"}
    for _, arg := range args {
        if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") {
            break
        }
        tokens = append(tokens, arg)   // raw positional, no shape check
    }
    commandPath := strings.Join(tokens, " ")
    command := "ao"
    if len(tokens) > 1 {
        command = tokens[len(tokens)-1]  // last raw token, verbatim
    }
    return command, commandPath
}
```
Any non-flag positional arg is jammed into `command`/`command_path` unchanged. A URL, file path, or instruction string becomes the "command name."

Contrast with the **non-error** path `emitCLIInvoked` (`root.go:218-225`), which uses `cmd.Name()` / `cmd.CommandPath()` from the *successfully parsed* Cobra tree — those are safe short names. The error path can't use them because parsing failed, so it falls back to raw `args` with no validation.

**2. PostHog sink only allowlists keys, not values — `backend/internal/adapters/telemetry/posthog.go:236-294`:**
- `remotePayloadAllowlist["ao.cli.usage_errors"]` (lines 37-44) permits the `command` and `command_path` keys.
- `sanitizeRemoteValue` (lines 254-294) for the `string` case does only `strings.TrimSpace` + non-empty check. **No length cap, no shape/charset validation, no redaction.**
- So a 2 KB URL or multi-paragraph blob passes the "sanitizer" unchanged and is shipped to PostHog.

Net effect: the allowlist provides a false guarantee — it looks like a privacy boundary but does not bound content.

## Fix

Primary (client) + defense-in-depth (sink):

**Primary — bound the value at the source, `backend/internal/cli/root.go` `usageErrorCommand`:**
Only accept a token as the command name if it matches a registered command shape (e.g. `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,31}$`), or — better — validate it against the live Cobra command tree (`root.Commands()`) passed in via the caller. If the first positional token is not a known command name, emit `command = "<unknown>"` (or a short hash of the token) and `command_path = "ao <unknown>"`. This mirrors what the non-error path already produces (a real command name) and never leaks the raw positional.

Sketch:
```go
func usageErrorCommand(known map[string]bool, args []string) (string, string) {
    commandPath := "ao"
    command := "ao"
    for _, arg := range args {
        if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") {
            break
        }
        if known[arg] {
            command = arg
            commandPath = commandPath + " " + arg
            continue
        }
        // free text / URL / path — do NOT propagate
        command = "<unknown>"
        commandPath = "ao <unknown>"
        break
    }
    return command, commandPath
}
```
(Thread the registered command names from `NewRootCommand` into `emitCLIUsageError`; the call site at `root.go:33` already has the dep context.)

**Defense-in-depth — bound values at the sink, `backend/internal/adapters/telemetry/posthog.go` `sanitizeRemoteValue`:**
For the `string` case, cap length (e.g. 64 chars) and, for keys documented as holding a command name / path, reject values that don't match the expected shape (replace with a sentinel or `sha256(value)[:16]`). This catches any future emitter that re-introduces the leak. The fingerprint-style hashing pattern is already in the file (`sha256String`, line 312).

**Test coverage to add:**
- `usageErrorCommand` with a URL, an absolute path, and a multi-paragraph string → assert `command == "<unknown>"`, `command_path == "ao <unknown>"`, raw text never appears in output.
- `telemetry_test.go` already asserts `error` text is dropped (lines 92-94) — extend it to assert `command`/`command_path` are bounded sentinels when fed free text via the route.

## Impact

- **Privacy / data hygiene:** internal URLs (GitLab MRs), absolute local file paths, and free-text instructions leave the user's machine and land in a third-party analytics service. This is exactly the class of leakage the telemetry allowlist exists to prevent.
- **Severity framing:** bounded leak (only usage-error events, only what users type as positional args before a flag), no auth bypass, no RCE, no local data loss. But it is unsanitized internal/sensitive text leaving the machine — high, not critical.
- **Trust:** the allowlist currently reads as a privacy guarantee but does not bound content; maintainers cannot rely on it as a leakage boundary without this fix.

## Related

- #2331 — review-before-send diagnostic flow (overlapping telemetry-trust theme, different feature)
- #2362 — telemetry blind spots (opposite direction: missing instrumentation, not leakage)

## Notes

- I have the full fix traced and can open a PR (client-side primary change + sink-side bound + tests) if a maintainer wants it. Holding off pending triage since this is a privacy-sensitive telemetry path.

title: fix(daemon): repair PATH with a tool floor at startup so headless daemons find tmux (#2812)
body:
## What
Fixes #2812. A daemon started outside the Electron launcher (headless `ao start`, systemd, cron, container, automation) inherits a minimal `$PATH` and can't see `tmux` under `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `/usr/local/bin`, so **every spawn** fails the prereq gate with `tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH` — even though tmux is installed.

## Root cause
`session_manager.validateRuntimePrerequisites` gates each spawn on `exec.LookPath("tmux")` against the daemon's own inherited PATH (`manager.go:2488` / prod wiring `manager.go:228`). The PATH floor + login-shell probe that fixes this exists **only in the Electron launcher** (`frontend/src/shared/shell-env.ts`), so it never reaches a non-Electron daemon.

## Fix
- New `internal/runtimeenv` package ports the static PATH floor (`FALLBACK_PATH_DIRS`) from `shell-env.ts` to Go.
- `daemon.Run()` calls `runtimeenv.EnsureFallbackPath()` once at startup, **before any `exec.LookPath`**, so the tmux prereq gate *and* the agent-binary preflight both see the floor.
- Existing PATH entries keep precedence (only appended, de-duped). No-op on Windows (the tmux gate is Windows-exempt; floor dirs are POSIX).

## Scope
This is the **core fix** (#1 in the issue). The two complementary items — enriching `ao doctor`'s tmux check to stat floor dirs, and making the spawn error actionable — are intentionally left as separate follow-up PRs so this stays focused and low-risk.

## Tests
`internal/runtimeenv/pathfloor_test.go`: appends missing floor dirs, preserves existing order/precedence, de-dupes, empty-PATH → floor only, drops empty segments. `go build` / `go vet` / `go test ./internal/runtimeenv/` all pass; gofmt clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(telemetry): stop shipping raw CLI args in ao.cli.usage_errors (#2813)
body:
## What
Fixes #2813. `ao.cli.usage_errors` recorded `command`/`command_path` as the **raw positional args** of the failed invocation. Because parsing already failed, whatever the user typed went verbatim to PostHog — URLs, absolute file paths, multi-paragraph instructions, non-English text — and the remote allowlist gates only **keys**, not **values**.

## Fix (primary + defense-in-depth)
**Client — `cli.usageErrorCommand` (`root.go`):** only propagate tokens that are **registered command names** (collected from the Cobra tree). The first non-flag token that isn't a known command becomes the sentinel `<unknown>` and the scan stops, so raw positional text never leaves the machine. A known command followed by a bad arg keeps the command name and records `<unknown>` for the arg (e.g. `ao list some-project` → `command=list`, `command_path=ao list <unknown>`).

**Sink — `telemetry.sanitizeRemoteValue` (`posthog.go`):** command-shaped keys (`command`/`command_path`) whose value isn't command-shaped are replaced with a stable, non-reversible `sha256:<16>` token; all allowlisted strings get a length backstop. Catches any future emitter that reintroduces the leak.

## Tests
- `usageErrorCommand`: URLs, absolute paths, prose, non-ASCII → `<unknown>`; known-command-then-free-text keeps the command and redacts the arg; asserts **no raw token ever appears** in output.
- `sanitizeRemoteValue`: non-command-shaped command values → `sha256:` token (raw text never present); real commands + the `<unknown>` sentinel pass through; length backstop applied.
- `go test ./internal/cli/ ./internal/adapters/telemetry/`, `go vet`, `gofmt` all clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Resolve root relative assets in static previews
body: ## Issue AO serves workspace previews beneath `/api/v1/sessions//preview/files/...`. Root-relative references such as `/assets/app.css`, `/images/logo.svg`, ES modules, and `fetch("/data.json")` therefore escaped the preview namespace and resolved against the daemon API root. Imported projects and production builds using root-relative assets could render without styling or fail to load runtime resources. ## Fix Serve each static workspace preview from a session-specific `*.localhost` origin on the existing daemon port. The selected entry directory is mounted as the origin root, so: - `dist/index.html` serves `/assets/app.css` from `dist/assets/app.css`. - Relative asset paths continue to work. - CSS images and fonts, ES modules, and runtime root-relative requests resolve naturally. - Concurrent session previews use isolated origins and cannot mix assets. - Explicit dev-server and `file://` preview targets remain unchanged. The existing `/preview/files/...` route remains available for compatibility, and the preview poller migrates stored legacy workspace-preview URLs to the new origin. CORS now recognizes the RFC-reserved `*.localhost` subtree so browser module requests are accepted without allowing localhost lookalike domains. ## Files affected - `backend/internal/preview/entry.go` - Generates DNS-safe, session-specific localhost origins. - Handles long and Unicode session IDs. - Avoids double-escaping filenames containing spaces or special characters. - `backend/internal/preview/poller.go` - Recognizes both legacy preview routes and isolated preview origins. - Migrates legacy workspace-preview URLs automatically. - `backend/internal/httpd/router.go` - Routes isolated preview hosts through the workspace preview handler. - `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` - Mounts the selected entry directory at the preview origin root. - Preserves confinement to the session workspace and existing Markdown behavior. - `backend/internal/httpd/cors.go` - Allows valid `localhost` subdomain origins while rejecting suffix lookalikes. - Preview, controller, poller, and CORS tests - Cover root-relative assets, nested entry directories, concurrent sessions, router restart, legacy migration, URL encoding, and CORS boundaries. ## Validation - Passed: `go test ./internal/preview ./internal/httpd/controllers` - Passed: `go test ./internal/httpd -run 'TestCORS'` - Passed: `go vet ./internal/preview ./internal/httpd/controllers ./internal/httpd` - Passed: `npm run frontend:typecheck` - Passed manual Chromium smoke test covering: - Root-relative stylesheet loading - CSS-referenced images - Root-relative `` assets - ES module execution - `fetch("/data/message.json")` - No browser console warnings or errors The repository-wide `go test ./...` remains blocked by unrelated existing Windows/environment failures involving agent-auth fixtures, executable-bit assertions, CRLF expectations, missing `sh`, port-conflict handling, and stale generated OpenAPI output. ## Risks and scope - The isolated-origin behavior applies only to AO-served workspace files. Explicit HTTP(S) development servers and `file://` targets are not rewritten. - The implementation relies on the standards-reserved `*.localhost` namespace; this was manually verified in AO’s Chromium browser on Windows.

title: fix(sessions): reclaim the worktree on merge-triggered termination (#2811)
body:
Fixes #2811.

When a PR is merged (or closed, or a tracker issue reaches a terminal state), the lifecycle reaction terminates the session with `MarkTerminated` — which only sets `is_terminated` and tears down no external resources. The full teardown (runtime + worktree) lives on the Kill path (`POST /sessions/{id}/kill`), and that button is hidden the moment a session is terminated. So every merged-PR session leaves an orphaned worktree on disk that you can't reclaim from the UI. On an active project this piles up fast. The only recovery today is the project-scoped `ao session cleanup`, which isn't discoverable once the session drops out of the sidebar.

There's no automatic reclaim anywhere either: the reaper skips terminated sessions, and the boot-time Reconcile reap only kills a leaked runtime, never the worktree.

## What this does

Bridges the fact-driven termination to the teardown the session manager already owns, without dragging runtime/workspace deps into the lifecycle layer:

- `session_manager`: pull the per-session teardown out of `Cleanup`'s loop into `reclaimTerminatedWorktree` (no behavior change), and add `ReclaimOnTerminate(id)` — best-effort, skips dirty worktrees (never force-removed), no-ops for an unknown or still-live session. It runs the teardown under `context.WithoutCancel` so a daemon shutdown can't interrupt `git worktree remove` half-way (same reasoning as #2731).
- `lifecycle`: a narrow optional `terminationReclaimer` seam satisfied by the session manager, wired after construction via `SetTerminationReclaimer` (the lcm and session manager are built over each other, so it can't be a constructor option). `MarkTerminated` is split so the reclaim fires only on the actual termination transition — repeat observations on an already-terminal PR or issue stay no-ops. The merge/close and tracker-terminal reaction sites now reclaim; Kill's own `MarkTerminated` is untouched, so nothing double-tears-down.
- `daemon`: one line in `startSession` to wire it up.

The reclaim is best-effort throughout: a dirty worktree is preserved and a teardown error is logged, never surfaced, so a filesystem hiccup can't wedge the observation pipeline or leave the row un-terminated.

Backend-only, no API or SQLite regeneration.

## Tests

- lifecycle unit: merge and tracker-terminal reclaim; a merged PR with an open sibling does not reclaim; idempotent repeats don't re-tear-down; a reclaim error is swallowed; merge without a reclaimer wired still terminates.
- session_manager unit: `ReclaimOnTerminate` reclaims runtime + worktree, preserves a dirty worktree, and no-ops for a live or unknown session.
- integration (`internal/integration/reclaim_worktree_test.go`): over a real SQLite store and a real git-worktree adapter, a merged-PR observation driven through the real PR service physically removes the worktree directory from disk, and a dirty worktree is preserved.
- Existing `Cleanup` tests still pass over the extracted helper.

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race`, and golangci-lint all pass.

## Known boundary

A session already terminated by another path before its PR merges (e.g. the reaper marking it terminated on runtime death) hits the no-transition path and isn't reclaimed by the later merge; reaper-death sessions are also left alone since they may hold uncommitted work. Reclaiming those uniformly needs a boot-time or periodic reconcile pass, which I've left out to keep this change scoped to the merge path.

title: bug(workers): orchestrator doesn't proactively report when a spawned worker goes idle / finishes
body: ### Description When I ask the orchestrator to spawn a worker and work on a task, the orchestrator does **not** tell me when that worker finishes. The worker sits idle after completing its work, and I only find out it's done when I *manually* ask the orchestrator to check in on it. In the attached session, I spawned worker `miru-8` on a task and waited a long while, assuming it would let me know when it was done. It never did. Only after I explicitly asked it to "check pls?" did it report that the worker was **idle and had already committed** its work. ### Expected behavior The orchestrator should notify me the moment a spawned worker goes idle / completes its task, rather than leaving it sitting silently in the working area until I ask. ### Actual behavior The orchestrator stays silent after a worker finishes. When questioned, the model explained the root cause itself: > `ao spawn` workers run **outside** this harness, so it doesn't get an automatic "done" signal when one finishes — it only learns a worker's state when it actively polls `ao session get`. Last time it checked, the worker was mid-edit, so it said it would relay "once it reports done" — but nothing actually reports back to it, so it has to poll again on its own. It never re-polled, so it waited instead of informing me. So the underlying problem is: **spawned workers have no completion callback into the orchestrator, and the orchestrator does not poll on a schedule** — it only checks state on demand. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Give the orchestrator a task and have it spawn a worker to do it (`ao spawn`). 2. Wait for the worker to finish its work. 3. Observe that the orchestrator never proactively informs you that the worker has gone idle / completed. 4. Manually ask the orchestrator to check — only then does it report the worker as idle and committed. ### Suggested fix For any spawned worker, the orchestrator should poll `ao session get` at a sensible interval and ping the user the moment the worker transitions to idle, instead of waiting to be asked. (The model itself offered to do this via a scheduled check.) ### Environment - **AO version:** dev - **OS:** macOS Tahoe 26.2 - **Model:** Opus 4.8 (1M context) ### Attachments

title: Worker spawn silently compresses/truncates a too-long task prompt instead of failing fast — pre-flight size check?
body:
## Summary

When the orchestrator spawns a worker with a task prompt that exceeds the receiving agent's input limit (observed ~4.8 KB), the spawn fails / the prompt gets silently compressed or truncated instead of AO telling the user up front that the prompt is too large. The worker then runs on a lossy/shortened prompt and the human only finds out from a message like:

> Again at the AO limit of 4.8KB. I'll compress to ~3.5KB — the issue is detailed, the worker (Codex GPT-5.6 xhigh) will read it and figure it out.

i.e. the orchestrator **itself** decides to compress the prompt to fit, rather than AO rejecting the spawn (or warning) before it ever reaches the agent. This is fragile — the compression is lossy and the worker may miss context the human intended.

## What I'd expect

AO should know — before spawning — whether the assembled task prompt fits the target agent's accepted input, and either:

1. **Reject the spawn with a clear error** ("prompt is N bytes, agent X accepts ~M — shorten it, or move the bulk into a file the worker reads"), or
2. **Warn and offer a mitigation** (write the long context to a temp file in the workspace and pass a short pointer prompt), or
3. At minimum **log/notify** that the prompt was compressed/truncated and by how much — so the human can decide whether the lossy version is acceptable instead of discovering it from the worker's behavior.

Today it's silent (or only surfaced by the worker itself mid-run), which is the worst case: the spawn "succeeds" but on the wrong input.

## Where the limit seems to live today

- `backend/internal/observe/trackerintake/observer.go:28` — `maxIntakePromptLen = 4096` for issue-context intake, with a `"[Issue content truncated to fit the session prompt limit…]"` notice. So AO already truncates one prompt source (issue context) rather than rejecting.
- The task prompt itself is passed to the agent as a **positional argv** (e.g. claude-code: `claude … -- <prompt>` at `claudecode.go:134-145`), so the effective ceiling is a mix of the OS argv limit and what the receiving CLI (Claude Code / Codex) accepts on its input — and it varies per agent. AO doesn't appear to model "max prompt bytes for agent X" anywhere.

## Question

How are people supposed to handle this today? The options I can think of:

- Hand-compress every prompt before `ao spawn` (what I do now — tedious, lossy, and easy to get wrong).
- Move the long content into a workspace file and tell the worker to read it (works, but it's a manual workaround the human has to remember every time, and AO gives no hint that it's needed).

## Suggestion: pre-flight prompt-size check (Claude-Code-style hooks as a model)

Claude Code has a **hooks** system (PreToolUse / PostToolUse) that runs before/after tool calls and can block or modify them. The analogous idea here: a **pre-spawn gate** that measures the assembled task prompt against the target agent's known limit **before** the spawn is dispatched, and either blocks with a clear message or routes the overflow into a workspace file + short pointer.

Concretely, something like:

- AO knows (or is configured with) a per-agent `maxPromptBytes`.
- On `ao spawn --prompt …` (and on issue-context intake), AO computes `len(assembledPrompt)`.
- If over the limit: fail fast with `prompt is 5.2 KB, claude-code accepts ~4.8 KB — shorten, or pass --prompt-file <path> and the worker will read it`, instead of silently compressing.
- Optionally: an opt-in `--prompt-file` / auto-spill flag that writes the long prompt to `<workspace>/.ao/task-prompt.md` and passes a short pointer, so a genuinely long task still runs intact.

Even just **surfacing the limit and the truncation** (a one-line warning at spawn time: "prompt truncated from 5.2 KB to 4.0 KB to fit agent limit") would be a big improvement over the current silent lossy behavior.

## Environment

- Self-built `ao` from `fork/main` (recent), claude-code + codex workers
- Observed on orchestrator→worker spawns where the task prompt + issue context together exceed ~4.8 KB

Happy to help scope a pre-flight check if there's interest — wanted to open this as a question first, since I'm not sure if there's an existing recommended pattern I'm missing.

title: fix(lifecycle): wake orchestrator when a spawned worker goes idle
body:
## Summary

Wakes the orchestrator when a spawned worker becomes idle, instead of leaving it silent until the user explicitly asks it to check.

**Closes:** AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator#2820

## Problem

The orchestrator only discovered that a worker had finished after the user prompted it to poll. Since nothing reacted to a worker transitioning from **active → idle**, the orchestrator remained silent even after the worker completed its task, forcing the user to manually ask it to check for updates.

## Solution

Added a lifecycle hook in `ApplyActivitySignal` that detects when a live worker transitions from **active → idle**. When this occurs, it:

- Resolves the project's active orchestrator.
- Wakes it through the existing `sessionguard` mechanism.
- Prompts it to inspect the completed worker and report the results to the user.

The wake-up is **best-effort** and **non-blocking**:

- Failure to locate an orchestrator does not affect the activity update.
- If the orchestrator is blocked or waiting for user input, no wake-up occurs.
- Only an idle orchestrator is nudged, ensuring active user interactions are never interrupted.

To avoid unnecessary wake-ups, the trigger is gated on a true **active → idle** transition. This skips:

- The initial idle state assigned when a worker is spawned.
- `waiting_input → idle` transitions.

As a result, the orchestrator is notified only when a worker has genuinely completed its execution.

## Scope

- Applies to any worker within a project that has an active orchestrator.
- Uses the existing per-project orchestrator link already available in the worker's system prompt.
- Intentionally includes workers created through **"New Task"**, not just orchestrator-spawned workers. Restricting this behavior would require introducing a new `spawned_by` column and a database migration.
- Changes are confined to the lifecycle package.
- No API, DTO, or schema changes.

## Tests

Added test coverage for:

- Waking the orchestrator when a worker becomes idle.
- No-op behavior when no orchestrator exists.
- Preventing the orchestrator from waking itself on its own idle transition.
- Ignoring `waiting_input → idle` transitions.
- Leaving blocked orchestrators untouched.

title: fix(mobile): request iOS local network access
body:
## Summary

- add `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` to the Expo iOS configuration
- explain that AO uses local-network access to connect to the desktop daemon

## Root cause

The generated iOS app included the ATS local-network transport setting but omitted the local-network privacy usage description. iOS therefore blocked direct requests to the AO LAN listener before they reached the daemon, and React Native surfaced only `Network request failed`.

## User impact

Fresh iOS builds now display the system Local Network permission prompt. After the user allows access, AO can connect to the authenticated Connect Mobile listener on the same LAN. Existing installed binaries need to be rebuilt or updated to include the new native metadata.

## Validation

- `cd packages/mobile && npm run typecheck`
- verified the resolved Expo configuration emits the expected `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`
- built, signed, and installed a Release build on a physical iPhone; connection succeeded after granting Local Network access

title: feat(landing): conversion-focused redesign of the aoagents.dev landing page
body:
## Summary

Conversion-focused redesign of the public landing page (`frontend/src/landing`, deployed at aoagents.dev). Every change is aimed at one metric: more visitors starring the repo and trying AO. The stack is unchanged (Next.js + Tailwind + GSAP), and every claim on the page is real and verifiable (8.4k stars, Apache-2.0, nightly releases, the public `agentwrapper/tap` Homebrew cask).

## Before / after

**Hero — desktop.** Before: headline + two CTAs, nothing that says what AO *is*; the primary CTA on macOS was a dropdown ("Desktop downloads") instead of a button.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![hero before](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/hero-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![hero after](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/hero-after.jpg?raw=true) |

**Hero — mobile (real iPhone UA).** Before: oversized headline and a desktop-download dropdown that is useless on a phone. After: readable scale, subhead, repo-first primary CTA.

| Before | After |

| ![hero mobile before](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/hero-mobile-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![hero mobile after](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/hero-mobile-after.jpg?raw=true) |

**Social proof.** Before: each tweet wrapped in editorializing chrome ("Most important outside validation.") that tells the visitor what to think. After: the real posts speak for themselves; the self-congratulatory official tweet was removed.

| Before | After |

| ![social before](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/social-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![social after](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/social-after.jpg?raw=true) |

**New sections.** A three-step quickstart that removes the "setup looks heavy" objection, a video facade (Mux iframe no longer blocks first paint), and a closing CTA that repeats the conversion ask with proof.

| Quickstart (new) | Final CTA (new) | Video facade |
|---|---|---|
| ![install](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/install-after.jpg?raw=true) | ![cta](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/cta-after.jpg?raw=true) | ![video](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-26/landing-conversion/docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/video-after.jpg?raw=true) |

## Conversion decisions

1. **Subhead under the headline.** The old hero jumped from slogan to buttons; a new visitor had to parse the mockup to learn what AO is. New subhead answers it in ~40 words: "Mission control for a fleet of coding agents. AO runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor — 23 harnesses — in isolated git worktrees, watches every PR, and routes CI and review feedback back to the agent that owns the branch."
2. **Direct download CTA on every desktop platform.** `getDownloadTarget()` returned `null` for macOS, so the majority of devs got a dropdown while Windows/Linux got a one-click button. macOS now gets `Download for macOS` (Apple silicon build; Intel remains one click away via "All platforms"). Portable devices get a repo-first CTA ("Get Agent Orchestrator") since a zip is useless on a phone — the achievable conversion there is a star.
3. **Copy-paste install command in the hero.** The public `agentwrapper/tap` Homebrew cask is real (`brew install --cask agentwrapper/tap/agent-orchestrator`, verified this session), so macOS visitors get a Warp-style copyable command block with clipboard feedback. Shown again in the quickstart and final CTA.
4. **Live credibility markers.** Release pill above the headline (latest stable tag + "nightly builds ship every day" — verifiable in Releases), live star count in the nav (Warp pattern), persistent Download button in the nav, and trust microcopy (Apache 2.0, runs 100% locally).
5. **Quickstart section.** Three cards — install (brew + platform buttons), connect (`gh auth login`, agent CLIs you already have), spawn (`ao spawn --prompt …`) — directly attacking the "orchestration = complicated" objection.
6. **Final CTA section.** The page previously ended with tweets → footer. It now closes with "Your agents are waiting. Put them to work." plus the same download/star/brew trio.
7. **Honest social proof.** Removed the editorial `label`/`note` layer and the official self-tweet. Five real third-party posts, names/verified badges/dates/likes intact, each linking to the original.
8. **Sharper metadata.** Title is now "Agent Orchestrator - Mission control for coding agents", description mirrors the subhead, and `metadataBase` makes `og:image` absolute (it previously resolved relative to the host and would break in scrapers). `/` now carries full OG/Twitter tags, not just `/landing`.

## Accessibility & performance

- `--fg-dim` (#79796f → #8a8a82) lifts small-label contrast from ~4.3:1 to ~5.4:1 (WCAG AA on the dark background).
- Global `:focus-visible` accent ring for all interactive elements in the landing tree (verified by tabbing through the page).
- Autonomous GSAP intros (hero, tweets) now respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; CSS reveals already did.
- Copy blocks are real `<button>`s with aria-labels that flip to "Copied to clipboard".
- Video facade: the Mux iframe (and its JS) now loads on click instead of at page load.
- GitHub API usage: the old code fetched stars per component on a 5-minute poll; hero + nav + CTA would have tripled that. New shared store (`useSyncExternalStore`) issues **one** fetch per page load — matters because unauthenticated GitHub API is capped at 60 req/hr/IP and visitors share NAT egress. When the API is unavailable, the star count simply hides instead of showing a stuck "…".
- First load: ~170 KB JS (build output), system serif for the headline (zero webfont cost).

## Verification

- `npx next build` passes (63/63 pages); `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (only the two pre-existing `desktop-downloads.test.ts` vitest-typing errors that exist on main).
- Prettier check passes on all touched files.
- Download-target logic exercised for Windows/Linux/macOS/iPhone/Android/iPad (see `desktop-downloads.test.ts` update).
- Click-tested in a real browser: copy button writes the full command to the clipboard and flips to "Copied"; video facade mounts the Mux iframe with autoplay; mobile menu, nav collapse, and social links verified.
- Screenshot-audited at 1440px and 390px (real iPhone UA) against the production build, including docs pages (unchanged).

## Risks / follow-ups

- macOS download defaults to Apple silicon (UA can't distinguish arch); Intel Mac users use "All platforms" → install docs. Same trade-off Cursor makes.
- PR screenshots are committed under `docs/screenshots/landing-refresh/` so they render permanently; happy to drop them from the branch if you'd rather keep the repo lean.
- Star count/release tag are client-fetched, so they can lag a release by one page load; acceptable trade for a fully static page.

title: feat: standalone terminal pane (free shell, not tied to an agent session) — like VS Code's Ctrl+`
body:
## What

Add the ability to open a **standalone terminal pane** — a shell not bound to any agent session — like the `Ctrl+`\`` shortcut in VS Code / the "New Terminal" action in other IDEs.

**Reported by:** keshav (Discord, #bug-triage)

> "I am unable to open a new terminal manually (like we do in other IDE's (ctrl +`), it is just showing the running agent's terminal. Is there any way to do so or we don't have the feature at this moment?"

## Current behavior

Every terminal pane in the desktop app is bound 1:1 to an agent session's runtime PTY. There is no way to get a shell inside the app that is independent of a session.

### Why — evidence from the codebase

**Frontend** — `useTerminalSession` only ever attaches to a session handle:

```ts
// frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts:293
const handle = sessionRef.current?.terminalHandleId ?? null;
```

The mux client's `open(id, cols, rows)` takes a runtime handle id; there is no path to open a pane without a session behind it.

**Backend** — the `Source` interface only knows how to *attach* to a session PTY, never spawn an arbitrary one:

```go
// backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go:18,137
type Source interface { ... }
p, err := a.src.Attach(ctx, a.handle, rows, cols)  // handle = ports.RuntimeHandle (a session)
```

`backend/internal/terminal/doc.go` spells out the design intent: *"Per-client attach (no shared PTY)… the runtime owns the session."* No `Spawn`-style API exists.

**Shortcuts** — `frontend/src/shared/shortcuts.ts` defines five app shortcuts (`new-session`, `keyboard-shortcuts`, `toggle-sidebar`, `open-project`, `toggle-inspector`). There is no `new-terminal` binding. `new-session` (`⌘N`/`Ctrl+Shift+N`) opens the **New Task** flow (spawns a full agent + runtime + worktree), not a shell.

The old TypeScript implementation had no standalone-terminal feature either (0 matches in `ao-pr1483/`), so this is a genuine product gap — not a regression from the TS→Go rewrite.

## Proposed

A free-standing terminal pane that opens in the desktop app, scoped to a project's workspace root (or the daemon's cwd), with the usual shell:

- **Keyboard shortcut:** `Ctrl+`\`` (matches VS Code / IntelliJ / most IDEs). On macOS, the conventional binding is `⌃`\`` (Ctrl, not ⌘) — but verify against `matchesNewSessionShortcut` conventions in `shortcuts.ts`.
- **UI:** a "+ Terminal" action in the session inspector / topbar, or a slot in the sidebar.
- **Scope:** shell starts in the project root (or `~/.ao` if no project context).

## Scope of the change (for whoever picks this up)

This is non-trivial because the entire terminal mux is session-coupled end-to-end:

1. **Backend** (`backend/internal/terminal/`): the `Source` interface (`attachment.go`) needs a session-less attach path — either a new `Source.Spawn(rows, cols)` for ephemeral shells, or a dedicated "shell terminal" kind that bypasses `ports.RuntimeHandle`. The `sharedTerm` bookkeeping in `manager.go` keys on terminal id without checking session-ness; revisit that. The mux wire protocol (`protocol.go`) already tags frames by opaque `id`, so the framing itself is fine — only the `Source`/handle contract needs to widen.

2. **Frontend** (`frontend/src/renderer/`): `useTerminalSession` needs to accept either a session `terminalHandleId` *or* an ephemeral id returned from a new "open shell" API call. A "+ Terminal" control in the inspector or topbar (`ShellTopbar.tsx`). New shortcut + entry in `APP_SHORTCUTS` (`shortcuts.ts`) so it shows up in the keyboard-shortcuts dialog.

3. **Lifecycle:** ephemeral terminals should not appear in the kanban / session board, and should be cleaned up on close or daemon exit (they have no durable state to persist).

## Workaround

None in-app. Use an external terminal, or open an agent session and use its pane.

## Related

- #1422 — fate of the `Terminal` plugin slot (orthogonal: plugin API, not user-facing standalone terminal)
- #2687 — added `⌘N`/`Ctrl+Shift+N` for spawning *agent sessions* via shortcut (closest cousin; different purpose — full agent + runtime, not a shell)
- #2435, #1283, #1704, #2643 — existing bugs against the session-bound terminal pane

title: fix(telemetry): cap CLI event volume and switch PostHog to anonymous …
body:
CLI telemetry counted every invocation uncapped, and a few other events
(http errors, panics, generic renderer events) had no ceiling either.

This caps everything at the point it leaves the machine: CLI commands
report at most once per command per day (so polling loops become "used
today" instead of one event per call), events that need an actual count
(errors, crashes), and events bill as anonymous instead of identified since
our distinct id is just a random install id, not a person. Apart from that events like errors etc. are aggregated and have generous rate limits.

title: Fix/tmux isalive agent exited 2802
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2802 by ensuring `tmux.IsAlive()` correctly detects when an agent has exited, even if the tmux pane remains open.

Previously, liveness checks only verified that the tmux session existed. Since the keep-alive shell leaves the pane running after the agent exits, completed agents were incorrectly reported as still alive.

With this change, the runtime sets a pane-scoped `@ao_agent_exited` option when the agent exits. `IsAlive()` now checks this marker after `has-session` and reports the correct agent state while remaining backward compatible if the option is unavailable.

## Implementation

* Added a helper to build the `show-options` command for `@ao_agent_exited`.
* Updated the launch command to set `@ao_agent_exited=1` before starting the keep-alive shell.
* Updated `IsAlive()` to check the exit marker after `has-session`.
* Preserved backward compatibility by treating missing or unsupported options as alive.

## Testing

Added and updated tests covering:

* `show-options` command generation.
* Launch command includes the exit marker.
* `IsAlive()` reports exited agents correctly.
* Fallback behavior when `show-options` fails.

Verified with:

* `go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/...`
* `go vet ./...`

title: fix(adapters): npm/nvm binary detection gap across agent adapters (grok, droid, kimi, kiro, devin + systemic nvm blind spot)
body:
## Summary

Several npm-distributed agent adapters omit npm global bin search paths on Unix, causing "Needs install" false negatives in the agent selector even after clicking "Refresh agents." This is a systemic gap with a clean fix.

**Trigger:** the daemon runs inside the Electron process and inherits a minimal PATH from the GUI launcher — it does **not** source shell rc files. So `exec.LookPath("kimi")` fails for any binary whose only presence on PATH comes from an nvm/volta/fnm shell init. The hardcoded candidate paths are the backstop, and several adapters have incomplete backstops.

## Root cause evidence (user report)

User on nvm installed `@moonshot-ai/kimi-code` via `npm i -g`. Agent selector showed "Needs install" after refresh. Diagnostic output from a second user where detection *did* work:

```
which kimi              → /opt/homebrew/bin/kimi          ← adapter searches this ✅
npm config get prefix   → ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1   ← fresh npm installs land here ❌
node -v                 → v22.23.1 (nvm)
```

The `/opt/homebrew/bin/kimi` was a leftover masking the bug. A fresh reinstall would land in `~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1/bin/kimi`, which no adapter searches — detection would break for that user too.

## Audit results (all 23 adapters)

### 🚩 Confirmed Kimi-class bugs (npm-distributed, zero Unix npm paths)

Windows `WinPaths` already declare `npm/X.cmd`, proving devs knew these are npm tools — the Unix side was forgotten:

| Adapter | Binary | File | Searches today | Upstream |
|---------|--------|------|----------------|----------|
| **kimi** | `kimi` | `kimi.go:155` | `~/.local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin` | `@moonshot-ai/kimi-code` (npm) |
| **grok** | `grok` | `grok.go:33` | `~/.grok/bin`, `~/.local/bin` | xAI Grok (npm) |
| **droid** | `droid` | `droid.go:226` | `~/.local/bin`, `~/.factory/bin` | Factory Droid (npm) |

### ⚠️ Probable (need maintainer confirm)

| Adapter | Binary | File | Note |
|---------|--------|------|------|
| **kiro** | `kiro-cli` | `kiro.go:160` | Native installer primary, npm fallback on Windows only |
| **devin** | `devin` | `devin.go:38` | npm-distributed (`@cognition-ai/devin`) but no npm paths on either platform |

### ⚠️ Systemic gap — nvm glob missing everywhere except codex

**No `binaryutil.BinarySpec` adapter includes the nvm glob** (`~/.nvm/versions/node/v*/bin/X`). Only `codex` handles it, via a custom `nvmNodeBinCandidates()` resolver (`codex.go:229`). Every `BinarySpec` adapter will miss users whose only Node is nvm-managed.

### Minor asymmetries (npm-distributed, partial coverage)

| Adapters | Have | Missing |
|----------|------|---------|
| claude, amp, crush, goose, copilot, opencode, autohand, agy | `~/.npm/bin/X` | `~/.npm-global/bin/X` |
| pi | `~/.npm-global/bin/X` | `~/.npm/bin/X` |

### ✅ Best-in-class (reference pattern)

| Adapter | npm-global | npm-bin | nvm-glob |
|---------|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| auggie | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| cline | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| qwen | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| kilocode | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| continueagent | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| codex (custom) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |

### ✅ Not npm (no gap)
`vibe` (uv/pipx), `aider` (pipx), `cursor` (native installer)

## Proposed fix

The clean move is a **two-part change**:

**1. Add nvm glob support to `binaryutil` itself** so every `BinarySpec` adapter gets nvm coverage for free. Port codex's `nvmNodeBinCandidates()` pattern (`codex.go:229-236`) into `binaryutil.ResolveBinary`, applied when `spec.UnixHomePaths` is walked.

**2. Normalize `UnixHomePaths` across all npm-distributed adapters** to the canonical set:
```go
UnixHomePaths: [][]string{
    {".npm-global", "bin", "<bin>"},
    {".npm", "bin", "<bin>"},
    {".local", "bin", "<bin>"},
    // adapter-specific paths (e.g. .cargo/bin, .factory/bin, .grok/bin)
},
```

This fixes grok/droid/kimi/kiro/devin + the systemic nvm gap + the minor asymmetries (pi, claude, amp, etc.) in one coherent change rather than patching 15 adapters ad hoc.

### Minimal alternative (if the above is too broad)

Just patch the three confirmed bugs to match the cline/qwen pattern:
- `kimi/kimi.go:155`
- `grok/grok.go:33`
- `droid/droid.go:226`

Add `~/.npm-global/bin/<bin>` and `~/.npm/bin/<bin>` to each. This leaves the systemic nvm gap and minor asymmetries unfixed but unblocks affected users immediately.

## Workaround (for affected users now)

```bash
# Symlink to a searched location (fastest)
sudo ln -sf "$(which <bin>)" /usr/local/bin/<bin>
# Then click "Refresh agents"
```

Or launch AO from a terminal where the shell has sourced nvm (inherits full PATH).

## Context

- Reported by @prateek in Discord (#🪲-report-bugs)
- Triaged and confirmed with diagnostics from @NikhilAchale

title: fix: merged PR sessions disappear from sidebar AND leak runtime RAM (not torn down)
body:
## Summary

When a session's PR is merged, the session silently disappears from the sidebar and gets buried in the collapsed "Done / Terminated" bar on the kanban board — with **zero user feedback** explaining what happened. Worse, the underlying runtime process (tmux/conpty + agent + worktree) is **never torn down**, so it keeps consuming RAM until the daemon is restarted.

This combines a UX problem (no transition feedback) with a real resource leak (merged sessions are marked dead in the DB but their processes stay alive).

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a worker session that opens a PR
2. Merge the PR (from the dashboard, GitHub UI, or `gh pr merge`)
3. Observe:
   - ❌ The session **vanishes from the sidebar** with no toast/notification
   - ❌ The session **drops into the collapsed "Done / Terminated" bar** on the kanban board (collapsed by default — invisible)
   - ❌ The tmux/agent process is **still alive** and holding RAM (verified by checking `tmux ls` or process list)

## Two Distinct Bugs

### Bug A — RAM leak (the real issue, `priority:high`)

When a PR merges, the SCM observer fires `ApplyPRObservation` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:132-141`), which calls `MarkTerminated`:

```go
// reactions.go:138
if done {
    return m.MarkTerminated(ctx, id)
}
```

But `MarkTerminated` **explicitly does NOT tear down external resources**:

```go
// backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:254
// MarkTerminated marks a session terminated without tearing down external resources.
func (m *Manager) MarkTerminated(ctx context.Context, id domain.SessionID) error {
    // ... only sets is_terminated=true, activity_state=exited
}
```

It only flips two DB flags. The tmux/conpty process, the agent process, and the git worktree all stay alive indefinitely.

Compare with `Kill()` (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:439-477`), which does the **full teardown**:

| | Merge path (`MarkTerminated`) | Manual kill (`Kill`) |
|---|---|---|
| Flags set in DB | ✅ | ✅ |
| tmux/conpty process killed | ❌ | ✅ |
| Worktree removed | ❌ | ✅ |
| RAM freed | ❌ | ✅ |

The reaper (`backend/internal/observe/reaper/`) doesn't help — it **skips terminated sessions** (`reaper_test.go:88`: "terminated sessions must not be probed"). The `reconcileReap` pass only runs at **boot time** (`manager.go:810-817`). `Cleanup()` does tear down terminated runtimes, but it's only triggered manually (CLI/project removal), never automatically on merge.

**Result:** every merged session leaks its process until the daemon restarts. Over a workday of merges, this adds up fast.

### Bug B — Silent disappearance (UX)

The frontend filters merged sessions out without any visible transition:

- **Sidebar** (`frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:433`): `workerSessions(workspace.sessions).filter(sessionIsActive)` strips them out — `sessionIsActive()` returns `false` for `status === "merged"` (`frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:275-277`)
- **Kanban** (`frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:327-329`): `attentionZone()` maps `merged` → `"done"` zone → session falls into the collapsed "Done / Terminated" bar at the bottom (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx:214-256`), which is collapsed by default

The lifecycle does fire a `NotificationPRMerged` notification (`reactions.go:320-321`), so the notification *exists* — but it doesn't tell the user *where the session went*. A user who merges from GitHub sees their session vanish with no breadcrumb.

## Suggested Fixes

**For Bug A (RAM leak):** The merge-completion path in `reactions.go:132-141` should trigger actual runtime teardown, not just a flag flip. The lifecycle layer is intentionally a fact-reducer that doesn't own resource teardown — but the merge-completion path crosses that boundary and nothing picks up the teardown. Options:

1. Have the SCM observer's completion signal call through the session manager (which owns `Kill`) instead of stopping at the LCM.
2. Add an automatic post-merge teardown in the reaper for sessions marked terminated-but-not-reaped.
3. Have the merge path call `Kill` directly.

The architectural seam to resolve: `MarkTerminated` lives in the LCM (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go`), `Kill` lives in the session manager (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`). The merge path stops at the LCM.

**For Bug B (UX):** Add a visible transition when a session moves to the "Done" zone — e.g., a toast/banner, or don't auto-collapse the Done bar so the user sees where their session went.

## Severity

`priority:high` — Bug A is a core feature broken (merged sessions leak resources) with no workaround for users. Bug B is UX friction.

Reported by @prateek. Triage by @i-trytoohard.

title: Activity timeline: PR number not clickable + missing "Opened PR" timestamp
body: ## Bug: Activity timeline — PR number not clickable, and no "Opened PR" timestamp In the **Activity** section of the session **Summary** pane (right-hand inspector), the PR timeline events render incompletely: 1. **PR number is plain text, not a clickable link.** `Opened PR #2807` should link to the PR on GitHub but renders as inert bold text. 2. **PR events have no timestamp.** "Created worktree & branch" shows `5d ago` and the current status row shows `just now`, but the middle "Opened PR #2807" row shows nothing. ### Screenshot See attached image below. ### Root cause Both issues live in the `ActivityTimeline` component in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`. **1. PR number not clickable — frontend-only, trivial.** The PR number is rendered as plain bold text at three sites: - `SessionInspector.tsx:277` — `Draft PR #{pr.number}` - `SessionInspector.tsx:289` — `Opened PR #{pr.number}` - `SessionInspector.tsx:323` — `Merged PR #{pr.number}` But the `pr` object already carries `url` (`PullRequestFacts.url`, `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:105`). It's just never rendered as a link. Fix: wrap `#{pr.number}` in ``. ~3 lines, pure frontend, no API change. **2. No "Opened PR" timestamp — needs a backend wire change to be correct.** All three PR events hardcode `ts: null` (lines 280, 292, 326). This is not just a frontend omission — the creation timestamp is genuinely missing from the wire. Tracing the data path: | Layer | PR creation time present? | |---|---| | DB `pr` table → `created_at_provider` column | ✅ yes | | `GetPR` query / domain `PullRequest` (`backend/internal/domain/pr.go:59` `CreatedAtProvider`) | ✅ yes | | domain `PRFacts` (slim read model, `pr.go:9`) | ❌ dropped — only `UpdatedAt` | | `GetDisplayPRFactsBySession` query (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/gen/pr.sql.go:50`) | ❌ does not SELECT it | | DTO `SessionPRFacts` (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go:244`) | ❌ only `updatedAt` | | Frontend `PullRequestFacts` (`frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:104`) | ❌ only `updatedAt` | So the provider's creation timestamp exists at the source but is stripped at the `PRFacts` / DTO boundary. To show a correct "opened at" time, `created_at_provider` must be threaded through: the query → `domain.PRFacts` → `SessionPRFacts` DTO → `npm run api` (regen OpenAPI + TS types) → frontend type + `toPullRequestFacts` (`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useWorkspaceQuery.ts:14`) → `ActivityTimeline`. > ⚠️ Avoid a frontend-only stopgap of reusing the existing `pr.updatedAt` — that shows *last updated*, not *opened*, which is misleading for older PRs. ### Suggested fix split - **PR A (quick, frontend-only):** clickable PR links using the already-available `pr.url`. Ships standalone. - **PR B (backend wire change):** add `createdAt` (sourced from `created_at_provider`) to the `SessionPRFacts` wire shape, regenerate API types, then wire it into the timeline for the open/draft/merged rows. ### Severity **Minor** — cosmetic/UX polish, no functional break. But the dead `ts: null` is clearly an unfinished placeholder, so worth closing. ### Environment Observed on the desktop app session inspector (Summary → Activity). --- _Triage by @i-trytoohard._

title: fix(lifecycle): durably deliver worker-idle completions to the orchestrator
body:
# Wake the orchestrator when a worker finishes — durably, exactly-once, without interrupting it

Closes AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator#2820

Supersedes my earlier PR (#2823 ).

## Problem

When the orchestrator spawns a worker, it was never told when that worker finished. Nothing reacted to a worker's active → idle transition, so a completed worker sat silent until the human manually asked the orchestrator to poll (#2820).

## Approach

active → idle is the completion signal, and waking the project orchestrator is preferable to polling every worker. The key design point from review: recording that a worker finished and delivering that fact to the orchestrator are two separate responsibilities. They are now decoupled behind a durable, at-least-once outbox.

**Invariant:** once AO accepts a worker-completion signal, it stays pending until AO successfully attempts delivery to a safe orchestrator. Duplicates after a crash are acceptable; silent loss is not.

## What changed

- **worker_idle_events outbox (migration 0024):** project, worker, transition time, delivery state. A partial unique index on `worker_id WHERE pending` coalesces repeated completions to one pending row.
- **Atomic persistence (RecordWorkerIdle):** the worker's active → idle transition and its outbox event are written in one transaction, so a crash cannot save the worker idle while losing the delivery work.
- **Dispatcher (DispatchProject / DispatchAllPending):** resolves the current orchestrator at delivery time (never bound to one that may be replaced), routes through `sessionguard.Nudge`, and marks an event delivered only when the guard reports a pane write was attempted — suppressed outcomes stay pending.
- **Grounded nudge:** the message tells the orchestrator to run `ao session get <worker>`, embedding no status snapshot that could be stale by delivery time.

## Explicit delivery contract

This reconciles the two review threads (one asked for "idle only"; the other correctly noted that active delivery is safe for harnesses like Codex where Enter steers the current turn, and that "idle only without retention" would itself create a lost-notification path):

| Orchestrator state | Action |
|--------------------|--------|
| Idle | Deliver now |
| Active and harness steers active turns | Deliver now |
| Active without safe steering | Defer |
| Blocked / waiting-input | Defer |
| Missing / terminated | Defer until an orchestrator is available |

Active-turn steering is an explicit harness capability (`HarnessSteersActiveTurn`), defaulting conservatively to `false` for any unknown harness.

## Addressing Reviewer @Vaibhaav-Tiwari  (active-orchestrator behavior)

The contract above makes the description and implementation agree: an active orchestrator is only nudged when its harness can safely steer; otherwise the completion is retained, not dropped.

Added a test: a worker goes active → idle while the orchestrator is active (non-steering) and no nudge is sent — the event is retained and delivered later.

## Addressing Reviewer @illegalcall  (durable at-least-once delivery)

- Typed, project-scoped `worker_idle` event — ✅
- Durable internal outbox (not human-facing dashboard notifications) with project/worker/kind/transition/delivery state — ✅
- Activity transition + outbox event persisted atomically — ✅
- Coalesce repeated completions per worker — ✅ (partial unique index)
- Delivery resolves the current orchestrator at delivery time — ✅
- Route through `sessionguard.Nudge`; mark delivered only on an attempted pane write; suppressed stays pending — ✅
- Retry on: event creation, orchestrator entering a safe state, orchestrator spawn/restore, daemon start, and a low-frequency recovery sweep — ✅
- Active-turn steering as an explicit harness capability, conservative default — ✅
- Grounded nudge (`ao session get <worker>`, no stale snapshot) — ✅
- Test matrix — ✅ (below)

## Tests

- **Lifecycle:** idle orchestrator delivers; steerable-active delivers; unsafe-active / blocked / waiting / missing orchestrator retain; deferred delivery fires when the orchestrator becomes safe; repeated completions coalesce to a single delivery; destination is the orchestrator session id (not merely "a message was sent"); `DispatchAllPending` delivers then does not re-deliver.
- **Store:** atomic record, coalesce, mark-delivered, and pending persistence.
- **Session manager:** an orchestrator spawn triggers dispatch; a worker spawn does not.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and all touched-package tests pass locally.

I could not run `golangci-lint` or `go test -race` in my environment (toolchain limitation), so CI is the first full lint/race pass — happy to fix anything it surfaces.

---
cc @Vaibhaav-Tiwari @illegalcall

title: Fix detection of npm agent binaries from GUI path
body:
## Summary

Fix agent binary detection for npm-distributed adapters when AO is launched from Electron/GUI with a minimal `PATH`.

The daemon currently relies on `exec.LookPath` first, but GUI-launched Electron does not source shell rc files, so nvm/volta/fnm-managed npm global bins are often absent from `PATH`. This caused false "Needs install" results after refreshing agents, especially for adapters like Kimi, Grok, and Droid.

## Changes

- Add shared nvm fallback support in `binaryutil.ResolveBinary`
  - Probes `~/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin/<binary>` on Unix.
  - Keeps existing precedence: `PATH` first, configured absolute/home candidates next, nvm candidates last.
  - Sorts nvm matches in reverse lexicographic order for deterministic newest-looking selection.
- Normalize Unix npm fallback paths for npm-distributed `BinarySpec` adapters:
  - `~/.npm-global/bin/<binary>`
  - `~/.npm/bin/<binary>`
  - `~/.local/bin/<binary>`
  - adapter-specific fallback paths afterward.
- Patch custom npm-style resolvers:
  - `codex`: uses the shared nvm helper and now includes npm-global/local fallbacks.
  - `opencode`: adds npm-global, local, and nvm fallbacks.
  - `copilot`: adds npm-global and nvm fallbacks while preserving native-loader resolution.

## Why

Users installing agents globally through nvm-managed npm can end up with binaries only under paths like:

```bash
~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1/bin/kimi
```

Those paths are usually available in an interactive shell, but not in the Electron daemon process. The selector then reports "Needs install" even though the agent is installed.

So if a user launched AO from the terminal, it might work because shell init added nvm to `PATH`. But if a user launched AO as the desktop app, it might fail because the Electron-launched daemon never saw the shell's nvm `PATH`.

What we changed:
- Keep `PATH` lookup first.
- Add shared fallback detection for nvm npm global binaries.
- Normalize npm fallback paths across npm-distributed adapters.
- This makes "Refresh agents" work even when AO is launched from the desktop app with a minimal environment.

## Testing

Ran:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/binaryutil ./internal/adapters/agent/copilot ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/...
go test ./internal/service/agent/...
go test ./...
```

```bash

```

Fixes #2832

title: Dev daemon isolation from #2465 regressed pnpm dev: revert to shared port/rundir, gate isolation behind ISOLATE_DEV
body:
## What happened

#2465 moved the dev daemon (`app.isPackaged === false`) onto its own port and state dir: `AO_PORT=3002`, `AO_RUN_FILE=~/.ao/dev/running.json`, `AO_DATA_DIR=~/.ao/dev/data`. Two problems:

1. **Proxied renderer paths have been broken in dev since it merged.** `vite.renderer.config.ts` still defaults its `/api` and `/mux` proxy targets to `http://127.0.0.1:3001`, so anything going through the Vite proxy (notifications stream, `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` browser preview) gets ECONNREFUSED while the daemon sits healthy on 3002. Symptom: UI loads but data-driven surfaces are empty or stale, with `http proxy error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3001` in the dev console.
2. **Dev silently forks app state.** The fresh `~/.ao/dev/data` DB means projects, sessions, and persisted settings (e.g. `pipelines.enabled`) from the installed app vanish in dev with no indication why.

## Decision

The separate port and rundir are the regression, not the lifecycle coupling. The supervisor stopping the daemon on quit is by design: the daemon's lifecycle belongs to whichever app supervises it.

Rework:
- Dev uses the **same port and rundir as the installed app by default** (3001, `~/.ao`).
- The isolation from #2465 moves behind an explicit **`ISOLATE_DEV=true`** opt-in for anyone who wants a sandboxed dev daemon.
- The Vite proxy default must follow the same switch as the daemon port, or both should derive from one shared constant, so the two can't desync again. Hardcoding the port in two files (`main.ts` DEV_DAEMON_PORT vs `vite.renderer.config.ts`) is what let this ship.

## Repro

With an installed AO app present (or a stale `~/.ao/running.json` holding 3001): `pnpm dev` in `frontend/`, open the notifications stream or any proxied path. Observe ECONNREFUSED against 3001 while the dev daemon listens on 3002.

title: feat(desktop): AO_KEEP_DAEMON to keep the daemon alive after the app closes (#2230)
body:
## Summary

Opt-in `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` env var: when set, the desktop app spawns its daemon **without** the OS-native supervisor link and skips the orphan-cleanup kill on exit, so the daemon persists across app quit and stops only on an explicit `ao stop`. Default (unset) is byte-for-byte unchanged — the daemon self-stops shortly after the app quits.

Beyond "power users with long sessions," the persistent-daemon mode is a prerequisite for a **detached / remote** topology (a headless daemon in a container, attached from the desktop over an SSH tunnel): without it, closing the desktop window arms-then-fires the supervisor watchdog and kills every running agent session in the container.

Closes #2230.

## History / why a new PR

This supersedes the combined #2621 for the #2230 part, splitting it per the one-issue-per-PR review feedback. It also continues the **#2231** review thread (closed when its head branch was accidentally removed during a fork cleanup, not for any code reason). All four @illegalcall review points from July 11 on #2231 are addressed in this branch:

- **Cross-launch regression (persist the keep decision with the daemon):** the keep decision is read from the daemon's durable `running.json` owner record (`"persistent"` vs `"app"`), never the current Electron process env. A daemon spawned keep-alive stays persistent even when the app is later reopened **without** `AO_KEEP_DAEMON`. `shouldLinkOnAttach("persistent") === false` is encoded as a regression test.
- **fd leak:** the parent's `keepDaemonLogFd` is closed on the spawn-throw path and after a successful spawn (the child holds its own inherited copy via stdio), so each keep-alive start/stop cycle no longer accumulates descriptors.
- **stdio lifetime:** under the flag the daemon's stdio is redirected to `~/.ao/daemon.log` (stdin ignored) and the child is `unref()`'d, so Electron-owned pipes no longer kill the kept-alive daemon on the next stderr log write.
- **truthy parsing:** `keepDaemonAlive` uses an explicit allowlist (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`); `off`/`no` and any unrecognized string keep the default self-stop behavior.

Rebased clean onto current `main` (`5532fa1b`); the keyboard-shortcut refactor (PR #2795) that landed in the meantime is left untouched.

## Mechanism

- `daemonEnv()` stamps `AO_OWNER="persistent"` under `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` (else `"app"`). The daemon writes `AO_OWNER` verbatim into `running.json` (`server.go`); the attach path reads that durable record (not this Electron process's env, which differs across launches) and skips the supervisor re-link for `"persistent"`.
- Under the flag the daemon's stdio is redirected to `~/.ao/daemon.log` and the child is `unref()`'d; the port-bound supervisor link and the stdio port-scanners are skipped (port discovery falls back to the `running.json` handshake).
- The `process.on("exit")` orphan-cleanup kill is skipped under the flag.

Files: `frontend/src/main.ts`, `frontend/src/main/daemon-owner.ts(.test.ts)`, `frontend/src/shared/daemon-discovery.ts`, `backend/internal/runfile/runfile.go`, `docs/cli/README.md`.

## Verification

- `gofmt` clean; `go build ./...` ok; `runfile` Go suite passes.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean (one pre-existing upstream `semver` types error in `escalation-evaluator.ts`, unrelated to this PR).
- 26 `daemon-owner` tests pass, incl. the cross-launch and allowlist cases.

title: feat(mobile): push notifications for iOS and Android
body:
## Mobile push notifications (iOS + Android)

Adds real OS push notifications to the mobile app so a user is alerted — when the app is backgrounded or killed — the moment one of their agents needs attention (needs input, PR ready to merge, PR merged, PR closed unmerged). Tapping a notification deep-links into the relevant screen.

### The design constraint

The "server" is the user's **own daemon** running on their laptop (reached over LAN/Tailscale), not a cloud service. So **the daemon is the push sender**: on each notification it makes an outbound call to the Expo Push Service, which relays to APNs/FCM. This is purely additive to the existing notification pipeline (`lifecycle → notify.Manager → notify.Hub`, which already backs the web dashboard's SSE).

### What's included

**Backend (Go daemon)**
- `internal/mobilebridge/pushdevices.go` — persistent push-device registry at `~/.ao/<data>/mobile/push-devices.json` (Expo token as primary key, idempotent upsert, atomic 0600 writes), co-located with the existing Connect Mobile state.
- `internal/httpd/controllers/push.go` — `POST`/`DELETE /api/v1/push/devices` behind the existing Bearer-password auth, with token validation and OpenAPI operations (route↔spec parity + regenerated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`).
- `internal/push/` — an Expo client (batching, optional `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN`) and an additive `notify.Hub` subscriber (the "dispatcher") that sends to all registered devices and prunes tokens Expo reports as `DeviceNotRegistered`.
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — loads the registry on boot (degrades to no-push on failure) and runs the dispatcher for the process lifetime.

**Client (Expo / React Native)**
- `lib/push.ts` — permission-after-pairing, Expo token acquisition + registration, resilient to unprovisioned builds (no crash on a build lacking push entitlement).
- `lib/PushManager.tsx` — headless coordinator: registers on connect, refreshes on foreground, unregisters when switching daemons, and routes taps (needs_input → session screen; PR events → PRs tab) including cold-start via `getLastNotificationResponseAsync`; marks the record read on tap.
- Settings **Notifications** section — shows push status and the single next action (Enable / Register / Open settings), closing the "denied on first try, no way back" gap.
- Supporting: `lib/api.ts` (register/unregister/mark-read), `app/_layout.tsx` (mount), `expo-notifications` plugin + deps, `eas.json` build profiles.

### Testing

- Backend: `go build`, `go vet`, `go test -race`, golangci-lint, and the OpenAPI route↔spec parity test all pass.
- Verified **end-to-end on physical devices**: a real daemon-generated `needs_input` was delivered and correctly deep-linked on **both** a physical Android phone (FCM) and a physical iPhone (APNs).

### Deliberate scope (v1)

- OS-tray push only — no in-app notification center, no app-icon badge, no per-type toggles.
- Immediate `DeviceNotRegistered` token pruning; Expo's delayed-receipt polling is deferred.
- Global device scope (records carry `projectId` for future per-project filtering).
- Hub buffer-drop is accepted (huge relative to human-paced events; the phone catches up via the existing REST poll).

### Notes for maintainers

- `google-services.json` (Firebase Android config) is **gitignored** and re-included for EAS builds via `.easignore` — anyone building the Android app provides their own Firebase config. Push requires an EAS project + FCM V1 (Android) / APNs (iOS) credentials.

title: fix(dev): gate daemon isolation behind opt-in
body:
## What

Restore the shared daemon port and state directory for development builds by default.

- Development now uses port `3001` and the standard `~/.ao` state directory.

## Why

The previous development isolation behavior caused Electron and Vite to use different daemon ports. It also silently separated development data from the installed application's data.

Fixes #2845.

The shared resolver:

- Uses port `3002` only when `ISOLATE_DEV=true`.
- Gives an explicit `AO_PORT` precedence in either mode.

Electron only switches the run file and data directory to `~/.ao/dev` when isolation is explicitly enabled.

Regression tests cover the default port, isolated port, and explicit port overrides.

title: feat(storage): add session cleanup-facts table and cleanup_generation (#2811)
body:
Part of #2811 (terminated sessions leaking runtime + workspace resources).

This PR is storage-only and **has no behavior change** — it lays the durable
foundation for reconciling a terminated session's runtime and workspace teardown.

### What's here
- **Migration 0024** — `session_cleanup_facts` (PK `session_id`, FK
  `ON DELETE CASCADE`): the durable disposition of a terminated session's runtime
  + workspace teardown (`workspace_disposition` rollup, `runtime_released_at`,
  capped-backoff retry bookkeeping, `failure_code`). Plus an additive
  `sessions.cleanup_generation` counter. No stored display status (status stays
  derived from durable facts).
- **CDC** — facts-table triggers emit the **existing** `session_updated` event
  (no `change_log` rebuild, no new event_type). Payload is `{id}`-only; the UPDATE
  `WHEN` guard fires only on disposition / runtime-release changes and excludes the
  retry-bookkeeping columns so retry-scheduling writes don't flood CDC.
- **Store / domain** — `cleanup_generation` query fan-out (mirrors
  `preview_revision`), `domain.SessionCleanupRecord`, and a cleanup store with
  upsert/get plus the coarse `sessions LEFT JOIN facts` candidate scan (raw SQL —
  sqlc 1.31's SQLite parser truncates trailing clauses after a `?` placeholder).
- **Tests** — store round-trip, facts-trigger emits `session_updated` with the
  WHEN-guard suppression, and the three candidate-scan branches (no facts row /
  stale generation / pending-and-due).

### Validation
`go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`,
golangci-lint, and `npm run sqlc` all pass. Goose `Down` manually verified via an
Up→Down→Up round-trip (drops triggers, table, and the column cleanly).

title: fix(review): destroy the reviewer pane on cancel instead of only interrupting
body:
The AO reviewer runs as a stable pane (`"review-"+workerID`) reused across
review passes. `Cancel` only *interrupted* that pane, so a cancelled reviewer
left a live pane + agent process running — a standing leak.

This adds a real teardown:
- `Launcher.Teardown(handleID)` destroys the pane via the runtime's `Destroy`
  (idempotent — empty / already-gone handle is a no-op).
- `Engine.TeardownReviewer(workerID)` destroys the deterministic
  `"review-"+workerID` pane under `lockWorker`, so it can't race a concurrent
  (re)spawn; idempotent.
- `Cancel` now calls it, so a cancelled reviewer's pane is destroyed rather
  than left interrupted-but-alive.

### Depends on
Stacked on #2800, which introduces the `reviewerRuntime.Destroy` seam this
reuses. Until #2800 merges this PR's diff also shows that commit — review the
`reviewer-teardown` commit.

### Tests
- launcher `Teardown` destroys the pane + no-ops on an empty handle
- `TeardownReviewer` tears down the deterministic handle, is idempotent, and
  rejects an empty worker id
- `Cancel` now tears the pane down (regression pin for the leak)

### Validation
`go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./internal/review/...`,
`go vet ./...`, golangci-lint — all green.

Fix Goose session restoration so AO resumes the original interactive Goose conversation using its persisted native session ID.

Goose automatically persists interactive sessions in its local SQLite database. AO already captures the native Goose session ID through lifecycle hooks and stores it as `agentSessionId`.

Using that ID allows a terminated AO session to resume the same Goose transcript instead of starting a new conversation or accidentally restoring the most recent unrelated Goose session.

## Restore flow

1. Goose emits a `SessionStart` hook containing its native session ID.
2. AO records that value in the session’s `agentSessionId` metadata.
3. When the AO session is restored, the Goose adapter runs:

   ```bash
   goose session --resume --session-id <agentSessionId>

title: feat(vibe): restore native sessions
