## Summary

Add native session restore support for Mistral Vibe.

AO already generated `vibe --resume <session-id>` when a native session ID was available, but the Vibe adapter did not capture that ID. This change installs workspace-local Vibe hooks and persists the `session_id` through AO's existing activity and lifecycle pipeline.

## Changes

- Install managed Vibe hooks in `.vibe/hooks.toml`:
  - `pre_tool`
  - `post_tool`
  - `post_agent`
- Capture Vibe's native `session_id` from hook payloads.
- Persist the native ID as `agentSessionId`.
- Enable `log_interactions` in the workspace-local Vibe configuration, as required by Vibe session resume.
- Register Vibe with the activity dispatch pipeline.
- Map Vibe activity conservatively:
  - `pre-tool` and `post-tool` → `active`
  - `post-agent` → `idle`
- Surface captured metadata through `SessionInfo`.
- Preserve existing user hooks and unrelated TOML configuration.
- Add hook installation, activity mapping, metadata capture, and restore tests.

## Restore flow

1. AO launches Vibe in the managed worktree.
2. A Vibe hook reports the native `session_id`.
3. AO stores it in the existing session metadata.
4. `ao session restore <id>` relaunches Vibe with:

   ```text
   vibe --resume <native-session-id>

title: bug(preview): new session's in-app browser opens non-empty — poller auto-previews a workspace file on first scan
body:
## Bug

When a new worker session is created, its in-app browser panel opens **non-empty**, navigated to a daemon preview-files URL for some Markdown/HTML file in the session's worktree, instead of starting empty.

Observed URLs (reporter created "simple new sessions"):
- `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/safesplit-10/preview/files/website-setUp-for-links.md`
- `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-28/preview/files/test/cli/README.md`

**Source:** Discord `#🧑‍🔧-bug-triage` | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `470a0fb9` (local main, 2026-07-19)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced and reproduced at the unit level (see Reproduction).

![reporter screenshot — new session's browser opened non-empty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-new-session-browser-autopreview/.issue-assets/new-session-browser-autopreview/new-session-browser.png)

## Reproduction

A focused test that mirrors the report — a brand-new worker session whose worktree has **no `index.html`**, only Markdown (like essentially every repo):

```go
workspace := t.TempDir()
writeFile(t, filepath.Join(workspace, "README.md"), "# project")
writeFile(t, filepath.Join(workspace, "docs/website-setUp-for-links.md"), "# setup")
svc := &fakePreviewSessions{sessions: []domain.SessionRecord{workerSession("safesplit-10", workspace, "")}}
poller := NewPoller(svc, svc, "http://127.0.0.1:3001", PollerConfig{Logger: discardLogger()})
poller.Poll(context.Background())
```

Result (single `Poll()`):
```
REPRO: new session safesplit-10 auto-previewed to -> http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/safesplit-10/preview/files/README.md
```

That is the exact URL shape the reporter saw — produced on the poller's **first scan** for a session that was never explicitly previewed.

End-to-end repro in the app:
1. Create a new worker session in any project whose worktree contains a `.md`/`.html` file and no `index.html`.
2. Within ~250 ms the in-app browser opens to that file (and the inspector's Browser tab auto-reveals).

## Root Cause

The **preview poller** (`backend/internal/preview/poller.go`), started in `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:136`:

```go
previewDone := preview.NewPoller(store, sessionSvc, "http://"+cfg.Addr(), preview.PollerConfig{Logger: log}).Start(ctx)
```

scans every active worker session every 250 ms (`DefaultPollInterval`). For each one it calls `DiscoverEntry(workspacePath)`:

- `backend/internal/preview/entry.go:43` — if none of `index.html`, `public/index.html`, `dist/index.html`, `build/index.html` exist, it falls back to `mostRecentPreviewable` (`entry.go:57`), which walks the whole workspace and returns the **most-recently-modified** `.html/.htm/.md/.markdown` file. Most repos have several, so this fallback almost always matches.

Then `shouldRefresh` decides whether to write the URL. For a **brand-new** session it returns true:

```go
// backend/internal/preview/poller.go:151
func (p *Poller) shouldRefresh(sess domain.SessionRecord, target string, seenBefore bool) bool {
    current := strings.TrimSpace(sess.Metadata.PreviewURL) // "" for a new session
    if current == "" {
        if !seenBefore {                                    // true: poller's first time seeing it
            return sess.Metadata.PreviewRevision == 0       // 0 == 0 -> TRUE -> auto-set
        }
        ...
```

So the poller immediately calls `SetPreview(id, FileURL(...))` (`poller.go:138`), which writes `preview_url` and bumps `preview_revision` (`SetSessionPreviewURL`, `queries/sessions.sql:42`). The CDC trigger (`migrations/0017/0019`) fans the change out; the renderer invalidates its workspaces query (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/event-transport.ts:53`) and refetches; `SessionView` reads `session.previewUrl` and auto-navigates the browser (`useBrowserView.ts:456`) plus auto-opens the inspector Browser tab (`SessionView.tsx:110`).

This is **intended behavior over-applied**: the poller was designed to auto-surface "a freshly generated report or document" (`entry.go:42`) and static frontends. But the `.md` fallback, combined with firing on the very first poll when `PreviewRevision == 0`, means **every new session in a Markdown-rich repo auto-opens its browser to a repo doc** — directly contradicting the expectation that a new session's browser starts empty.

## Fix

Make auto-preview **opt-in**: a session should only get an auto-discovered preview *after* the user/agent has explicitly run `ao preview` at least once (`PreviewRevision > 0`). New sessions (`PreviewRevision == 0`) stay empty.

Primary fix — one line in `shouldRefresh` (`poller.go:155`):

```go
if current == "" {
    if !seenBefore {
        return false // do not auto-preview a brand-new, never-previewed session
    }
    previous := p.seen[sess.ID]
    return previous.cleared
}
```

After an explicit `ao preview <file>` opts the session in, the `current != ""` branch keeps the preview fresh as the file changes, and `ao preview clear` continues to stop re-discovery. The behavioral cost is that a "freshly generated report" no longer auto-surfaces in a session the user never previewed — which is exactly the behavior this report is asking to remove.

Alternative (more surgical, preserves built-frontend auto-preview): restrict the poller's auto-discovery to real web entry points (`index.html` variants in `entryCandidates`) and do **not** apply the `.md`/`.html` `mostRecentPreviewable` fallback for auto-set. This keeps "auto-surface a built static frontend" while killing the "auto-surface README.md" noise.

The existing poller tests would need updating either way (`TestPollerSetsPreviewWhenActiveWorkerEntryAppears` etc. assert the current auto-set-on-first-poll behavior).

## Impact

- Every new worker session in a normal repo (one with Markdown docs) opens its browser to a seemingly-random repo file — confusing and looks like a state leak. It's the #1 thing a user sees on session creation.
- Workaround: close the Browser tab / run `ao preview clear`. Not data loss.
- **Priority: medium** — UX/confusion, no data loss, workaround exists. (No `preview`/`frontend` labels exist on this repo; applied `bug`.)

## Related observations (found during triage — separate issues, not the cause here)

1. **`NextSessionNum` is non-monotonic** (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/sessions.sql:2`): `SELECT COALESCE(MAX(num),0)+1 ...`. It's `MAX` over *surviving* rows, so it recycles a number whenever the highest session row is removed. Session IDs are used as durable keys (browser views, terminal handles, restore markers, CDC cache) and should be unique forever; this is a latent collision risk worth its own ticket. (Today `DeleteSession` only removes seed-state rows, which limits reachability, but the invariant is wrong.)
2. **Native browser views are never destroyed on session close/navigation.** `useBrowserView`'s `ensure`-effect cleanup only hides (`sendHiddenBounds`); the hook's `destroy` (`useBrowserView.ts:482`) has zero call sites in the renderer. So the main-process `entries` map retains a `WebContentsView` per session for the window's lifetime. On its own this is a memory/leak issue, but combined with (1) it would let a recycled session ID adopt a stale view + URL. Worth its own ticket.

## Related

- [#2352](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2352) — preview poller not clearing stale `preview_url` when the workspace entry file is deleted (same subsystem, different symptom).

title: fix(preview): don't auto-preview Markdown docs for brand-new sessions
body:
Fixes #2859

## Summary

A new worker session's in-app browser was opening non-empty — navigated to an arbitrary repo Markdown/HTML file (e.g. `README.md`) instead of starting empty. Reported by @prateek: new sessions showed URLs like `…/sessions/safesplit-10/preview/files/website-setUp-for-links.md`.

**Root cause:** the preview poller (`backend/internal/preview/poller.go`) auto-discovers a workspace file on its very first 250 ms scan and sets `preview_url` for every active worker session. `DiscoverEntry`'s `mostRecentPreviewable` fallback (`entry.go`) returns the most-recently-modified `.md`/`.html` file anywhere in the workspace, so nearly every new session in a Markdown-rich repo matched and got auto-previewed — directly contradicting the expectation that a new session's browser starts empty.

## The fix

Restrict the **never-previewed** (`workspaceOwned == false`) auto-discovery path to real static-frontend entrypoints (`index.html` and its `public/`/`dist/`/`build/` variants). Drop the `.md`/`.html` `mostRecentPreviewable` fallback for that path only.

- New `DiscoverWebEntrypoint(workspacePath)` (`entry.go`) — entrypoint candidates only, no document fallback.
- `DiscoverEntry` is refactored to delegate to `DiscoverWebEntrypoint` first, then `mostRecentPreviewable` — **behavior-preserving** for its other callers (the explicit `ao preview` HTTP path at `sessions.go:733`, and the `entry_test.go` suite).
- In the poller, the fallback after `EntryAtPath` fails now branches on `workspaceOwned`: already-previewed sessions keep full `DiscoverEntry` (so their preview stays fresh as files change, including `.md`), while never-previewed sessions use `DiscoverWebEntrypoint`.

**Behavior after the fix:**
| Session state | Workspace has | Browser on creation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New (never previewed) | only `.md` docs | **empty** (fixed) |
| New (never previewed) | `dist/index.html` | auto-previews the frontend (preserved) |
| Explicitly previewed (`ao preview X`) | `X` changed | refreshed (unchanged) |
| Explicitly previewed, file deleted | other `.md` | full re-discovery (unchanged) |

This is the "surgical alternative" noted in the issue rather than a blanket opt-in: it fixes both reported cases (`.md` repo docs) while preserving the poller's primary purpose of auto-surfacing built static frontends.

## Test

Two new tests in `poller_test.go`:
- `TestPollerDoesNotAutoPreviewMarkdownOnlyNewSession` — a brand-new session with only `README.md` + `docs/setup.md` gets **zero** preview sets (the bug).
- `TestPollerKeepsMarkdownPreviewFreshOnceExplicitlySet` — a session explicitly previewed against `docs/report.md` still gets its preview normalized/maintained (the restriction only affects never-previewed sessions).

All 17 existing poller/entry tests pass unchanged (the entrypoint-selection tests use real `index.html`/`dist`/`public`, which `DiscoverWebEntrypoint` still finds).

```
cd backend
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./internal/preview/...     # 19/19 pass
go test ./...                      # full backend suite green
```

title: feat: standalone shell terminal, not bound to any agent session (#2828)
body: Closes #2828. Adds a shell you can open by hand — from a terminal button in the topbar or ``Ctrl+` `` — with no agent session behind it. Until now every terminal pane in the app was bound 1:1 to a session's runtime PTY, so there was no way to get a plain shell inside AO. ## Screenshots **1. The new terminal button** — sits beside the notification bell, on every route. **2. The terminal itself** — standalone shells render as tabs beside the session's own pane, each with its own close control. ## Approach The issue scoped this as a large change, proposing a new `Source.Spawn` on the terminal mux and describing it as "session-coupled end-to-end." **That turned out not to be the case, and `internal/terminal` is unchanged by this PR.** At `manager.go:353` the daemon already passes the client-supplied terminal id straight through as the runtime handle, with no session lookup anywhere in the package: ```go a = newAttachment(id, ports.RuntimeHandle{ID: id}, c.mgr.src, ...) ``` So the mux was never session-aware — it attaches to whatever handle it's given. And `ports.Runtime.Create` already accepts arbitrary `Argv`. The only missing capability was a way to *create* a session-less PTY. That reframing is what kept this small: no protocol change, no `Source` change, no `sharedTerm` rework. ### Backend New `internal/service/shellterm`, parallel to the session service rather than inside it — a shell terminal has no agent, no worktree, and no lifecycle state machine, and shares exactly one mechanism with sessions (the runtime adapter). - Own id namespace (`shellterm-`), constrained to what both runtime adapters accept (conpty enforces `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`; tmux uses the id as a session name) - Own table (`shell_terminals`, migration `0024`) with no FK to `sessions` and no CDC, so shells can never surface on the board - `GET`/`POST /api/v1/shell-terminals`, `DELETE /api/v1/shell-terminals/{handleId}` ### Lifetime: survives a daemon restart, dies with the app The PTY lives in tmux / a conpty pty-host, both of which outlive the daemon, so surviving a restart is mostly a matter of persisting enough to re-attach. Dying with the app is the harder half, and needs two mechanisms because the clean path isn't enough: 1. **Clean quit** — the supervisor closes shells on exit. 2. **Crash / force-kill** — nothing gets to run, so shells would leak forever. Each row is stamped with an **app-run id** (`AO_APP_RUN_ID`), minted once per app launch and held constant across daemon restarts the supervisor performs. At boot the daemon destroys any shell stamped with a *different* run id. A bare `ao daemon` mints its own id per boot, so its shells correctly do not outlive it. ### Frontend `useTerminalSession` gained exactly one option, `shellTerminalHandleId`. The mux draws no distinction between a shell handle and a session handle, so all the attach/reattach/backoff/resize machinery is shared verbatim — only the handle's source and the session-specific side effects branch. (A shell exit no longer invalidates the workspaces query; it carries no news for the session board.) Shell tabs live in two places: beside the session pane when a session is on screen, and in a standalone `/terminals` view otherwise. Both read the active handle from the store, so they never disagree. ### ``Ctrl+` `` Verified unused — no accelerator, no matcher, nothing in the Electron menu. Same binding on both platforms, matching VS Code (``⌘` `` is taken by macOS for window cycling). **One deliberate tradeoff:** like the other app shortcuts, it's handled in the main process so it fires with focus inside xterm. That means no shell or TUI running in a pane can receive ``Ctrl+` `` while AO owns it. Almost nothing binds that chord and VS Code makes the same trade, but it's a permanent decision worth a reviewer's eye. ## Testing **Verified against a live daemon on Windows (real conpty PTYs), not just fakes:** | Check | Result | |---|---| | `POST /shell-terminals` | `201`, real PTY spawned | | `GET` (runs a liveness probe) | listed | | Daemon restart, **same** `AO_APP_RUN_ID` | survived | | Daemon restart, **new** `AO_APP_RUN_ID` | reaped — `reaped shell terminals from previous app runs count=1` | | `DELETE` | `204`, then `404` on repeat | **Automated:** - 12 service tests, incl. rollback when persistence fails, pruning dead shells, and *not* deleting a shell when a liveness probe errors (an error is not proof of death — same rule `internal/terminal` applies on attach) - 5 store tests against real SQLite - 7 controller tests, incl. the 501 path when the service is absent - 3 e2e tests - OpenAPI route/spec parity passes; `openapi.yaml` + `schema.ts` regenerated and committed ## Bugs found by running the app Two things the test suite passed but the running app did not: 1. **The button and shortcut did nothing outside a session.** The open request was consumed by `SessionView`, which only mounts on session routes — so on the board, or in a project with no sessions yet (exactly when a plain terminal is most useful), the signal was raised and nothing was listening. Fixed by moving ownership to the shell layout, which is mounted everywhere, plus the standalone `/terminals` view. There's an e2e regression test for this case. 2. **The browser-preview build misrepresented the feature** — a selected shell tab still rendered the session's agent transcript, and the mock list couldn't shrink so the close X did nothing visible. Desktop was unaffected, but it made the feature untestable without a daemon. ## Notes for reviewers - **Pre-existing failures, unrelated to this branch** (all confirmed failing on clean `main`): `supervisor-link` (4 tests), `TestNewFallsBackOnPortConflict`, and the `aider`/`grok`/`ptyregistry`/`gitworktree` suites — all Windows environment issues. The existing e2e specs also target `refactor-mux`, a session no longer present in the mock data. - **Not addressed, happy to follow up:** multiple shells in one project share a tab title (`ao-demo`, `ao-demo`) with no `(2)` disambiguation; and shells opened from `/terminals` have no project context, so they start in the daemon data dir rather than the project you came from. - The mux attaches to any client-supplied handle id with no authorization check. Pre-existing and out of scope here, but this PR adds a documented endpoint that mints handles running the user's login shell, which makes that surface slightly more interesting. ## Commits | | | |---|---| | `d6b692e6` | backend: service, storage, REST, daemon wiring | | `a9fada60` | frontend: tabs, topbar button, ``Ctrl+` ``, `AO_APP_RUN_ID` | | `9b3babd3` | preview-build support + e2e | | `a3469456` | fix: open terminals from any route | Happy to squash `9b3babd3` into `a9fada60` — it only exists because the preview path I shipped didn't represent the feature.

title: Add dispatchable unsigned-artifact desktop build workflow (conductor handoff)
body:
## Summary

Add a new `workflow_dispatch`-triggered workflow (`build-artifacts.yml`) that builds the desktop app for all four platform targets and hands the outputs off as run artifacts, so an external release conductor can pin a ref, verify digests, and sign/publish separately. This is additive: the existing `frontend-release.yml` / `frontend-nightly.yml` signed-release paths stay untouched.

## Requirements

- Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` with two inputs: `ref` (git ref/SHA to build) and `version` (version string to stamp).
- Build at the pinned `ref`; stamp `package.json` version = `version` before packaging (reuse the existing nightly version-stamping approach).
- Platform matrix: mac arm64 (`macos-latest`), mac x64 (`macos-15-intel`), windows (`windows-latest`), linux (`ubuntu-latest`).
- macOS output is **unsigned** in this workflow (no `osxSign`/`osxNotarize`, no signing secrets referenced).
- `actions/upload-artifact` each platform output with **1-day retention**.
- Emit each artifact's SHA256 as a run output (per-platform), so a downstream consumer can verify integrity.
- Creates **no** GitHub Release and references **no** secrets. Uses only the native `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Out of scope

Removing or changing the existing signed-release workflows, signing, feed generation, or release creation. Those are handled separately once the conductor is live.

title: feat(pipelines): agent pipelines v2, behind AO_PIPELINES
body:
Agent pipelines behind the `AO_PIPELINES` flag (default off, toggled from Settings). When the flag is off no engine, supervisor or trigger bridge starts and every `/api/v1/pipelines/*` route answers 501, so the feature costs nothing until it is switched on.

**This PR now carries pipelines v2.** An earlier revision of this branch shipped v1 (predicate DSL, loop semantics, a findings subsystem with lifecycle states). That design was rebuilt in place: v1's expression language, loop rounds and findings machinery are deleted, and the net diff is v2 only.

## The model

A pipeline is a set of stages connected by `on_success` and `on_failure` edges, triggered by PR events, session events, or manually. A run freezes its definition at trigger time and never re-reads it.

- **Two executor kinds.** `command` stages: exit status is the outcome, full output streams to the run folder. `agent` stages: a real agent session that settles itself with `ao pipeline done` or `ao pipeline fail --reason "..."`.
- **An outcome taxonomy, not pass/fail.** `succeeded`, `succeeded_unverified`, `failed`, `no_output`, `no_signal`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `skipped`. The distinctions are the point: an agent that claimed success without writing its declared artifact (`no_output`) is not the same failure as one that never signalled (`no_signal`).
- **One nudge.** An agent that signals done without producing its declared artifact gets exactly one message asking it to fix that, then settles.
- **A run folder** per run under `~/.ao/pipelines/<project>/<run>/`: the frozen `definition.yaml`, `run.json`, `Context.md`, `agent-outputs/`, `stage-logs/`.
- **Workspaces resolved from the subject**: `session`, `run`, `stage`, `checkout`, `inherit`. Owned trees are destroyed when a run succeeds and kept when it fails, so a failure is still there to look at.
- **Concurrency groups** with `cancel-in-progress` and a queue depth of one.
- **Credentials held by the engine**, injected into command stages only, never into agent stages, and never echoed back by any read path.

## Surface

Visual canvas editor with success and failure edges, stage inspector, settings modal, three starter templates, a Kanban run board, run detail with logs and artifacts, and `ao pipeline list|runs|show|run|cancel|done|fail|credential`.

## Verification

Unit and integration tests throughout, plus live dogfooding against a real daemon: a real agent stage completing under its own power, failure routing with skip cascade, the nudge path, `timed_out` with the session preserved, a PR-subject run through the CDC bridge, cancel-in-progress superseding an older run, restart reconciliation settling lost stages, and workspace teardown checked on the filesystem.

Two bugs that only live dogfooding could find were fixed here: a spawned session's row is seeded `idle` before the harness's first hook lands, which the agent executor read as real idleness (no agent stage could ever have succeeded); and `kill-on` matched outcomes literally, so a stage with no `produces` leaked its session.

## Known gaps

`docs/plans/2026-07-26-pipelines-v2-followups.md` lists every deferred item, every divergence from the design spec, and six findings the drills surfaced that are not fixed. The notable ones: a restart settles a lost stage but leaks its process, run folders are never garbage collected, and `docs/pipelines.md` still documents the v1 vocabulary.

title: feat(ci): add dispatchable unsigned desktop build-artifacts workflow
body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml`, a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow that lets an external release conductor drive a desktop build and consume the outputs as run artifacts:

- Inputs: `ref` (git ref/SHA to build, checked out via `actions/checkout` `ref:`) and `version` (stamped into `frontend/package.json` using the exact nightly stamping mechanism from `frontend-nightly.yml`).
- Platform matrix matching the existing release workflows: mac arm64 (`macos-latest`), mac x64 (`macos-15-intel`), windows (`windows-latest`), linux (`ubuntu-latest`).
- macOS builds are intentionally UNSIGNED: the workflow never invokes `macos-signing-setup` and sets no Apple env vars, and `forge.config.ts` only activates `osxSign`/`osxNotarize` when those vars are present. The conductor signs downstream.
- Pinned artifact contract (per the release conductor): upload-artifact names `mac-arm64`, `mac-x64`, `win`, `linux`, each containing the existing stable alias filename (`agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.zip`, `agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.zip`, `agent-orchestrator-win32-x64.exe`, `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage`), uploaded with `retention-days: 1`.
- A `digests` artifact contains `digests.json`, a flat JSON object mapping each of those four filenames to its sha256 hex string; the conductor reads it to verify hashes before signing. Digests are also echoed to the step summary.
- Creates no release and references no secrets; `permissions: contents: read` only.

Strictly additive: no existing workflow, signing, or release path is touched.

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean, `prettier --check` clean.
- Real `workflow_dispatch` verification run of the final contract (all four platforms green, artifacts `mac-arm64`/`mac-x64`/`win`/`linux` uploaded, flat `digests.json` emitted): https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/29832852780 (earlier pre-contract run: https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/29775090632)
- Note on branch history: GitHub does not register a dispatch-only workflow until it reaches the default branch, so two temp commits add and then remove a branch-scoped push trigger purely to register the workflow for the verification dispatch. The final tree is dispatch-only; happy to squash-merge.

Closes #2862

title: fix(feature-builds): strip doubled title prefix, add GitHub fetch timeout
body:
Two small fixes in the feature-releases code from #2459, both surfaced by an automated review pipeline run (the pipelines feature proposed in #2863 reviewing its own repo):

1. **Doubled title prefix.** The workflow titles releases `[feature] PR #<N>: <title>` and `listFeatureBuilds` passed `rel.name` through raw, so UI labels composing their own `PR #<N>: <title>` rendered the prefix twice (e.g. the pin-confirmation dialog). Now stripped at the parse layer so every consumer gets the bare PR title; titles without the authored prefix pass through unchanged.
2. **No fetch timeout.** `fetchJson` had no deadline, so a wedged connection could hang the updates flow indefinitely for a user pinned to a feature build. Every GitHub API call is now bounded with `AbortSignal.timeout(10s)`.

Tests: two new cases for the title stripping (authored prefix stripped, plain titles untouched); full feature-builds suite 27/27, tsc and prettier clean.

title: fix: stabilize daemon spawn working directories
body:
## Summary

- launch packaged desktop daemons from a stable `~/.ao` cwd instead of the versioned app resources directory
- chdir the daemon to its configured data dir before runtimes can start long-lived helpers
- guard tmux launch commands with `cd <workspace> || exit`, verify the pane cwd after spawn, and fail with a clear mismatch instead of silently starting in a poisoned cwd

title: fix(kimi): report mid-turn tool activity so working sessions are not shown Idle
body:
Fixes #2814.

## Problem

The activity pill showed **Idle** while a Kimi session was actively working. The Kimi adapter installed only `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`PermissionRequest`/`Stop` hooks — no mid-turn tool-use hooks — and AO's activity state is purely event-driven, so the first `Stop` parked the state on idle for the rest of the turn even while the agent kept executing tools.

## Fix

Mirrors the Claude Code adapter's tool-use trio, per the issue's suggested approach:

- **`kimi/hooks.go`** — `kimiHooksConfigBlock()` now also installs `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` / `PostToolUseFailure` → `ao hooks kimi pre-tool-use|post-tool-use|post-tool-use-failure`.
- **`activitystate/activitystate.go`** — `StandardDeriveActivityState` maps the trio to `active` (the issue's "extend the standard deriver" option: the events are generic, and other standard-deriver adapters are unaffected because they don't install these callbacks).
- `permission-request` deliberately stays `waiting_input`, not `blocked`: Kimi identifies tool calls as `tool_call_id` (not claude-code's `tool_use_id`, which is what `ao hooks` lifts onto the wire and what lifecycle's correlated blocked-clear keys on), so `blocked` could only fail closed until the turn boundary. `waiting_input` is already sticky against tool-use traffic in lifecycle, so the new trio cannot demote a pending approval.

## Verification of the issue's stated assumption

The issue flagged *"Assumption to verify: the Kimi CLI emits PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook events."* Verified against the locally installed Kimi Code **0.27.0** binary, two ways:

1. **Static**: the binary's `HOOK_EVENT_TYPES` (packages/agent-core*/…/hooks/types.ts in the embedded bundle) includes `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, with live `triggerBlock("PreToolUse", …)` / `fireAndForget("PostToolUse"|"PostToolUseFailure", …)` call sites. External hook stdin payloads are snake_cased and carry `tool_name` + `tool_call_id`.
2. **End-to-end**: installed the exact AO-managed hook block via the adapter's own `GetAgentHooks` code path into an isolated scratch `KIMI_CODE_HOME`, shimmed `ao` with a logger, and ran a one-shot `kimi -p` that reads a file. The shim recorded, in order:
   ```
   hooks kimi session-start      | {"hook_event_name":"SessionStart", ...}
   hooks kimi user-prompt-submit | {"hook_event_name":"UserPromptSubmit", ...}
   hooks kimi pre-tool-use       | {"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Read","tool_call_id":"tool_…", ...}
   hooks kimi post-tool-use      | {"hook_event_name":"PostToolUse","tool_name":"Read","tool_call_id":"tool_…", ...}
   hooks kimi stop               | {"hook_event_name":"Stop", ...}
   ```
   so the exact TOML AO writes is accepted by kimi 0.27.0 and the trio fires mid-turn with payloads the deriver maps to `active`. (This session cannot spawn AO sessions; the live kimi sessions on this machine were observed read-only via `tmux capture-pane` for context — they predate hook installation, consistent with the reported symptom.)

## Tests

- `activitystate_test.go`: trio → `active` cases added.
- `dispatch_test.go`: new `TestKimiDerivesMidTurnToolActivity` covering the `kimi` token end-to-end through `Derive` (the exact #2814 regression: mid-turn tool events must derive `active`, `stop` → idle, `permission-request` → waiting_input).
- `kimi_test.go`: asserts the three new hook entries are installed.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/... ./internal/lifecycle/...` passes; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean. (Pre-existing, unrelated `internal/cli` spawn-test failures reproduce on the base commit on this machine.)

## Known limitation / follow-up

After a permission approval, the pill reads "Input Needed" until the next turn boundary (`waiting_input` is sticky against tool traffic). Matching claude-code's correlated clear would need `ao hooks` to also lift `tool_call_id` as the tool-use id and a look at kimi's PermissionRequest/PreToolUse ordering — left out of scope here; AO spawns kimi in yolo mode so permission prompts are rare. The issue's note about the kilocode/opencode `session.status(busy)` variant is also untouched (separate adapter path).

title: feat(web): right-click context menu in terminal pane (Copy / Paste / Select All / Clear)
body:
## Summary

Right-clicking inside an orchestrator/agent terminal pane does nothing. There is no context menu, so users cannot Copy, Paste, Select All, Clear, or Search with the mouse. The only way to interact is via keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V), which is not discoverable and impossible on touch/mobile.

## Current behavior

- Right-click in any terminal pane → nothing happens (no native browser menu either, since xterm.js captures the event).
- Copy/paste only works via keyboard shortcuts.
- No way to Clear or Search the terminal buffer via mouse.

## Expected behavior

A context menu appears on right-click offering at minimum:

- **Copy** — copy current selection (if any) to clipboard
- **Paste** — paste from clipboard at cursor
- **Select All** — select entire scrollback buffer
- **Clear** — clear the terminal (`term.clear()`)
- **Search** (optional / nice-to-have) — search the scrollback buffer

Menu should respect theme (dark/light), position at cursor, and dismiss on outside click / Escape.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx` and `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx` register **no `contextmenu` event listener**. A repo-wide grep for `contextmenu`, `context-menu`, `rightclick`, `right-click`, and `oncontextmenu` under `frontend/src/` returns **zero hits**. xterm.js does not ship a built-in context menu, so nothing renders on right-click.

The handle object exposed outward (`AttachableTerminal` in `useTerminalSession.ts`) exposes `cols`, `rows`, `write`, `writeln`, `clear`, `onUserInput`, `onResize` — no `focus` or selection/clipboard helpers, so even the building blocks for a context menu are not fully exposed yet.

## Proposed implementation

1. Add a `contextmenu` handler on the xterm.js container element in `XtermTerminal.tsx` (or `TerminalPane.tsx`).
2. Render a themed floating menu (existing UI components/menus in the frontend can be reused).
3. Wire menu items to:
   - Copy → read `term.getSelection()` → `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`
   - Paste → `navigator.clipboard.readText()` → write to pty / `term.paste(...)` (xterm `@xterm/addon-clipboard` or manual)
   - Select All → `term.selectAll()`
   - Clear → `term.clear()`
4. Expose any missing primitives (selection, clipboard write) through `AttachableTerminal` if needed.
5. Prevent default browser context menu inside the terminal container.

## Related issues

- #1295 — [ENH] Copy text from terminal on dashboard (a context menu would address part of this)
- #1248 — Terminal selection vanishes on session update (~5s)
- #1221 — Terminal text selection offset (overlay scrollbar)
- #2434 — Terminal does not get keyboard focus on open
- #2537 — Drag file onto terminal does not insert path
- #237 — fix(terminal): OSC 52 clipboard, resize frame cap, hardcoded height (clipboard plumbing)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Right-click inside a terminal pane opens a themed context menu.
- [ ] Copy copies the current selection to the system clipboard; disabled/hidden when nothing is selected.
- [ ] Paste inserts clipboard contents at the terminal cursor.
- [ ] Select All selects the full scrollback buffer.
- [ ] Clear runs `term.clear()`.
- [ ] Menu dismisses on outside click, Escape, and after an action.
- [ ] Menu follows the active app theme (dark/light).
- [ ] No regressions to existing keyboard shortcut behavior (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V).
- [ ] Works across orchestrator and worker session terminals.

title: fix(frontend): deep-link PR notifications to sessions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2726 (AO-09, P1). PR-type notifications only opened the external GitHub PR link and never navigated into the owning AO session — the in-app navigation path was unreachable because the PR branch returned early.

This removes the early `return` after `window.open(...)` in `NotificationCenter`, so clicking a PR notification now:
- opens the external GitHub PR link (unchanged), **and**
- also navigates to the owning AO session when a session id is present.

Backend already carries session context for PR notifications (`service/notification/service.go`, `httpd/controllers/notifications.go` set `Kind: "pr"` with `SessionID`), so no backend change is required.

Ports the fix merged on the fork PR xuelongmu/agent-orchestrator#196.

## Changes
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NotificationCenter.tsx` — drop the early return in the PR-target branch.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NotificationCenter.test.tsx` — regression tests:
  - project-scoped PR → navigates to scoped session route
  - unscoped PR → navigates to unscoped session route
  - session-kind notifications unchanged
  - PR without session id → opens PR link, no in-app nav

## Notes / follow-ups
- `ao.renderer.notification_opened` now emits twice for a PR click (`target: "pr"` then `target: "session"`). Flagging in case dashboards assume one event per click — can adjust telemetry in a follow-up if intended.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

... (truncated)

title: feat(mobile): terminal scroll-to-top, tab scroll-to-top, and open new session on spawn
body:
Three small mobile UX changes, one per commit.

## Scroll-to-top button in the session terminal

A floating button at the bottom-right of the terminal scrolls back to the oldest output.

It lives in the terminal DOM rather than in React Native, because `@fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview` exposes only a narrow handle (`write / clear / focus / resize / fit`) and keeps its WebView ref private — there is no way to inject JS from RN. So the button is created inside the existing `TERMINAL_ENHANCE_JS`.

It follows the same split the drag handler already uses (`appDrivesScroll()`):

- **Normal buffer** — xterm owns the scrollback, so `scrollToTop()` is a true jump, and `viewportY` tells us when to hide the button at the top.
- **Alt buffer / mouse-tracking** (Claude Code, Codex, aider, vim, less) — the *app* owns its scrollback, so `scrollToTop()` cannot reach it. Instead we send the same wheel notches a drag produces, through the existing `wheelTick()`. This keeps the behavior harness-agnostic rather than encoding scroll bytes per harness. The burst is chunked across animation frames so it doesn't block the renderer, and the button is always visible here since there is no way to query the app's scroll position.

The document-level touch listeners run in the capture phase, so they now ignore touches that originate on the button — otherwise a tap would be consumed as a terminal tap or long-press.

## Tap the active tab to scroll it to top

Tapping the already-focused tab scrolls its list to the top (the standard iOS tab-bar gesture). Pressing a *different* tab still just switches.

This wraps React Navigation's `useScrollToTop` in a small shared hook so each screen needs one line plus the ref binding. The hook is also the single place we import `@react-navigation/native` — it reaches us transitively through `expo-router` rather than as a declared dependency, so keeping that coupling in one file makes it cheap to change later.

Applies to all four tabs: Kanban, PRs, Orchestrator, Settings.

## Open the new worker session after spawning

Spawning from the modal previously left you on the list, having to hunt for the session you just created. Now the modal dismisses and navigates to the new session's terminal.

`spawn()` returns the created session so the caller knows where to go. The navigation waits on `runAfterInteractions` — firing both in the same tick overlaps the animations, with the modal retracting while the session is already sliding in.

## Testing

`npm run typecheck` passes in `packages/mobile`.

The terminal button was verified by hand on device against a live Claude Code session. The tab gesture and the spawn redirect have not been exercised on device yet.

title: Audit and tighten excess padding in AO UI surfaces
body:
Several AO UI surfaces have padding that does not carry useful information and makes compact workflows feel sparse. This issue tracks a pass over the repeated spacing patterns rather than treating each screenshot as a one-off.

Examples from current UI:

- Board/session cards: cards like the `Needs You` example leave a lot of vertical space around the status, title, path, and PR row. The content is small, but the card height is relatively tall.
- Compact header controls: controls like `Summary` / `Review` use pill-style padding that feels large for a dense inspector/header area.
- Review/diff panel: the review header, `Collapse all` button area, file row, and diff container have stacked padding that reduces visible diff content, especially in narrow panes.

Expected direction:

- Make repeated AO work surfaces denser and more utilitarian while preserving click targets and readability.
- Prefer consistent spacing tokens for compact panels, cards, tab bars, file rows, and inspector headers.
- Review the app broadly for similar excessive padding instead of only fixing the attached examples.
- Validate at narrow desktop widths so content does not feel cramped or overlap after tightening.

This is not a request for a redesign; it is a spacing/density cleanup pass across existing UI patterns.

title: Cursor ignores role-specific model config on launch
body:
## Context (shared across all harnesses)

AO stores a per-role model in `agentConfig.model` (`backend/internal/domain/agentconfig.go:27`). `session_manager.effectiveAgentConfig` merges the project base config with the role override and `Spawn`/`Restore` forward the resolved value into every adapter as `cfg.Config.Model` (`backend/internal/ports/agent.go`). **Each adapter must opt in to forwarding that value to its CLI.** Today only the Claude (`claudecode/claudecode.go:172`), Codex (#2869), and Kiro (config-file `model` key) adapters do. Every other adapter silently drops it, so a configured worker/orchestrator falls back to the CLI's global default model.

- Original report: #2769
- Reference fix (the pattern to copy): #2869 (Codex) — adds an `appendModelFlag` helper called in both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`, plus a `GetConfigSpec` `model` field and regression tests.

## Problem

The **Cursor** adapter (`cursor`, binary `cursor-agent`) never forwards `cfg.Config.Model` to the `cursor-agent` CLI. A Cursor worker/orchestrator configured with a specific model therefore silently uses `cursor-agent`'s global default instead.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a project with a `cursor` role and a specific model:
   ```json
   { "worker": { "agent": "cursor", "agentConfig": { "model": "gpt-5" } } }
   ```
2. `ao spawn --project <project> --name model-check`
3. Open the worker session and inspect the active model.

## Actual result

The worker starts on `cursor-agent`'s global default model.

## Expected result

The worker starts on the configured `gpt-5`.

## Suspected cause

`GetLaunchCommand` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/cursor.go:83-99`) and `GetRestoreCommand` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/cursor.go:109-128`) build argv without reading `cfg.Config.Model`. The adapter also inherits the empty `agentbase.Base.GetConfigSpec` (`agentbase/agentbase.go:20-21`), so it never advertises a `model` field.

## CLI mechanism

`cursor-agent` supports a launch-time model override via `--model`.
Source: Cursor CLI docs — https://cursor.com/docs/cli/overview (`agent -p "..." --model "gpt-5"`)

## Suggested fix (mirror #2869)

- Add an `appendModelFlag`-style helper that appends `--model <trimmed model>` when `strings.TrimSpace(cfg.Config.Model) != ""`, and call it in both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`.
- Override `GetConfigSpec` to advertise the `model` field (`ports.ConfigFieldString`), matching `codex/codex.go` and `claudecode/claudecode.go:172`.
- Add command-construction regression tests: trimmed value present, blank omitted, restore path.

## References

- Reference fix: #2869 (Codex) · Original context: #2769
- Relevant file: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/cursor.go`
- Launch: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/cursor.go:83-99`
- Restore: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/cursor.go:109-128`

AO already injects a per-agent config via the `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var and selects it with `--agent`, but that config only carries `permission` + `agent.prompt` — never a model — so a configured worker model is silently dropped.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a project with a `kilocode` role and a model:
   ```json
   { "worker": { "agent": "kilocode", "agentConfig": { "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-20250514" } } }
   ```
2. `ao spawn --project <project> --name model-check`
3. Inspect the worker's active model.

## Actual result

Worker uses Kilo Code's global/default model.

## Expected result

Worker uses `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-20250514`.

## Suspected cause

`GetLaunchCommand` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/kilocode/kilocode.go:83-102`) and `GetRestoreCommand` (`:110-135`) build the env-injected config via `kilocodeConfigEnvPrefix` (`:200-224`) and the structs `kilocodeInlineConfig`/`kilocodeAgentSettings` (`:181-188`), none of which carry a model. Inherits empty `GetConfigSpec`.

## CLI mechanism

Kilo Code sets a **per-agent** model in its config under `agent.<name>.model` (e.g. `"anthropic/claude-haiku-4-20250514"`), precedence "session override > per-agent config > global > auto". A `--model` flag exists only on the non-interactive `kilo run`, so it is **not reliable for the TUI launch AO uses** — the config route is correct here.
Source: https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli , https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/agents/model-selection

- Add regression tests asserting the model lands in `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` (and is omitted when blank).
- Model format is `provider/model-id`.

- Reference fix: #2869 (Codex) · Original context: #2769
- Relevant file: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kilocode/kilocode.go`

title: Droid: decide whether to honor role-specific model config on launch
body:
## Context (shared across all harnesses)

AO stores a per-role model in `agentConfig.model` (`backend/internal/domain/agentconfig.go:27`). `session_manager.effectiveAgentConfig` merges the project base config with the role override and `Spawn`/`Restore` forward the resolved value into every adapter as `cfg.Config.Model` (`backend/internal/ports/agent.go`). **Each adapter must opt in to forwarding that value to its CLI.** Today only the Claude (`claudecode/claudecode.go:172`), Codex (#2869), and Kiro (config-file `model` key) adapters do. Every other adapter silently drops it, so a configured worker/orchestrator falls back to the CLI's global default model.

- Original report: #2769
- Reference fix (the pattern to copy): #2869 (Codex) — adds an `appendModelFlag` helper called in both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`, plus a `GetConfigSpec` `model` field and regression tests.

## Decision needed

The **Droid** (Factory) adapter (`droid`, binary `droid`) does **not** forward `cfg.Config.Model`, and this is currently **by design** — the package comment states *"Droid resolves its model and other defaults from the user's own settings; only the autonomy level is overridden"* (`droid/droid.go:70-74`, `:149-169`). We need a product/architecture decision on whether AO should override the model for Droid roles.

## Findings

- **No interactive `--model` flag.** `-m, --model <id>` exists only on `droid exec`; the interactive `droid [prompt]` mode AO launches changes model via `/model` or `Ctrl+N` mid-session (Factory CLI reference — https://docs.factory.ai/reference/cli-reference).
- **Model *is* settable via the settings file** AO already writes and passes: top-level `"model": "<id>"` in the JSON blob emitted by `permissionSettingsArgs` (`droid/droid.go:180-198`) and passed with `--settings <path>`. Currently that file is written **only for non-default permission modes** and carries only `autonomyLevel` (Factory settings docs — https://docs.factory.ai/cli/configuration/settings).
- **Upstream risk:** open Factory issues show model-config precedence flakiness (Factory-AI/factory #660, #787), and the docs don't explicitly confirm the top-level `model` in a `--settings` file overrides the session.

## Options

1. **Honor it:** add top-level `"model": strings.TrimSpace(cfg.Config.Model)` to the settings blob and emit `--settings` whenever autonomy **or** model is set. Requires verifying against a live `droid` that `--settings` model actually re-pins the session model.
2. **Keep deferring** to the user's `~/.factory/settings.json` and document that `agentConfig.model` is intentionally a no-op for Droid.

## Suggested fix (only if option 1 chosen)

Extend the settings builder (`permissionSettingsArgs`) with the top-level `model` key; always write the settings file when a model is set; add a `GetConfigSpec` `model` field; add regression tests. **Do not** add a `--model` argv flag — the interactive binary rejects it.

## References

- Reference fix: #2869 (Codex) · Original context: #2769
- Relevant file: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/droid/droid.go`

This issue tracks **Kiro** for completeness of the harness-model-config audit (sibling issues: #2883–#2901).

## Situation — Kiro honors the model but does NOT advertise it

Good news first: **Kiro already forwards the configured model.** `setKiroAgentDefaults` writes `model` into Kiro's agent-config file when `agentConfig.Model` is non-blank (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/hooks.go:268-272`), and this is covered by tests (`kiro/kiro_test.go:520 TestGetAgentHooksWritesConfiguredModel`, plus a project-model preservation assertion at `:167-208`). So Kiro is **not** affected by the launch bug the sibling issues describe.

The gap: **Kiro has no `GetConfigSpec` override** (it inherits the empty `agentbase.Base.GetConfigSpec`, `agentbase/agentbase.go:20-21`). So while Kiro consumes `agentConfig.model`, it never *declares* that it supports the `model` field — inconsistent with Claude and Codex, and it means the field isn't discoverable/validated through the config-spec surface for Kiro.

## Expected

Kiro should advertise the `model` config field it already honors, matching the Claude/Codex contract.

## Suggested fix (small)

- Override `GetConfigSpec` in the Kiro adapter to report a `model` field (`ports.ConfigFieldString`), mirroring `claudecode/claudecode.go:104-106` and `codex/codex.go`.
- Add/extend a `GetConfigSpec` test asserting the `model` field is reported (see the codex/claude spec tests for the pattern).

## Notes

Low priority / consistency polish — Kiro's runtime behavior is already correct; this only aligns its declared config spec with the other model-aware adapters.

## References

- Sibling audit issues: #2883–#2901 · Original context: #2769 · Reference pattern: #2869
- Relevant files: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/kiro.go`, `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/hooks.go:268-272`

title: bug(ui): synchronize BrowserView theme with application theme
body:
## Summary

When switching the application theme (Light ↔ Dark), the embedded Orchestrator/Agent preview does not stay synchronized with the rest of the application. The main UI updates immediately, while the BrowserView continues rendering with its previous theme, resulting in a noticeable visual mismatch until a later repaint or navigation occurs.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the application.
2. Open any Orchestrator/Agent so the preview panel is visible.
3. Toggle the application theme (Light ↔ Dark).
4. Observe the main application UI and the embedded preview.

## Expected Behavior

The Orchestrator/Agent preview should update its theme at the same time as the rest of the application, with no visible desynchronization.

## Actual Behavior

The application UI switches themes immediately, but the embedded BrowserView remains on the previous theme for a short period (or until a later repaint/navigation), causing a temporary visual mismatch.

## Root Cause

The application currently has two independent theme surfaces:

- **React application UI** uses the Zustand theme store. On theme changes, `applyDocumentTheme()` immediately updates `data-theme` and `colorScheme`, keeping the shell synchronized.
- **Embedded BrowserView (Orchestrator/Agent preview)** is created in `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts` but is not connected to the application's theme system.

The BrowserView currently:

- Receives no theme updates from the application.
- Has no IPC/API for propagating theme changes.
- Does not reference Electron's `nativeTheme`.
- Falls back to the operating system's `prefers-color-scheme`.

As a result, changing the application theme only updates the React shell, while the embedded BrowserView continues using its previous appearance until Chromium eventually repaints or reloads.

## Possible Fix

Synchronize the BrowserView with the application's theme when the user changes themes.

Possible approaches:

- Update Electron's `nativeTheme.themeSource` whenever the application theme changes so BrowserView content follows the selected theme.
- Alternatively, introduce a dedicated `browser:setTheme` IPC that updates the BrowserView's background and propagates the selected theme into the embedded document.

## Related Issues

This appears to be the same underlying class of issue as the existing terminal theme synchronization bug:

- #1283 — Live terminal ignores light theme

However, this issue affects the embedded BrowserView used for the Orchestrator/Agent preview rather than the terminal.

title: feat(web): image paste/drop/attach in the New Task brief (#2722)
body:
## What

Adds image attachment support to the **New Task "Brief"** composer, addressing the P1 finding in #2722 (part of the UX-audit epic #2728). Previously the Brief was a plain `<textarea>` with no way to paste, drop, or attach an image.

## Screenshots

Empty composer — note the **Add image** affordance and the paste/drop hint:

![New Task composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/ao/ao-5/pr-assets/docs/pr-2907/composer-empty.png)

Pasted/attached images render as a tidy, aligned grid of numbered **Image N** chips with thumbnails and per-item remove:

![Composer with image chips](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/ao/ao-5/pr-assets/docs/pr-2907/composer-grid.png)

The chip area is **height-capped and scrolls**, so many attachments never stretch the dialog past the viewport:

![Many images, scrollable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/ao/ao-5/pr-assets/docs/pr-2907/composer-scroll.png)

## Changes

**Frontend**
- New reusable `useImageAttachments` hook (paste / drop / file-picker → staged base64 payloads).
- `NewTaskDialog`: **Cmd+V paste**, drag-and-drop, and an **"Add image"** picker on the Brief. Attachments render as numbered **"Image 1", "Image 2"** chips (uniform grid, thumbnails, per-item remove); state clears when the dialog closes. The chip list is capped and scrollable.

**Backend**
- `SpawnSessionRequest` accepts optional inline base64 image attachments, validated for count (≤8), per-image size (≤10 MiB), total size (≤25 MiB), and image MIME type.
- On spawn, images are written into the session worktree under `.ao/attachments/` (added to the worktree's git excludes so they don't dirty the tree) and their paths appended to the prompt — CLI agents receive the prompt as text and can then read the files for visual context.
- Regenerated `openapi.yaml` + TS `schema.ts`.

## How to test

- `pnpm --prefix frontend test` (or `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.test.tsx`) — covers paste → numbered chip → spawn body, removal/renumber, non-image paste ignored.
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers/ ./internal/session_manager/` — covers attachment decode/validation, worktree writing, and prompt augmentation.
- Manually: open New Task, Cmd+V a screenshot into the Brief → "Image 1" chip appears; start the task → the agent's worktree contains `.ao/attachments/image-1.png` and the prompt references it.

## Notes / follow-ups
- **Orchestrator brief:** the "new orchestrator" flow is a one-click spawn with **no brief input** today (orchestrators are promptless by design), so there is nothing to paste into there yet. The `useImageAttachments` hook was built to be reusable if we add an orchestrator brief later.
- Screenshots were captured by driving the real Electron app via Playwright; they are hosted on the `ao/ao-5/pr-assets` branch and are **not** part of this PR's diff.

Refs #2722

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

... (truncated)

title: fix(desktop): sync embedded preview BrowserView with app theme
body:
Closes (#2906)

## Summary

Toggling the app theme (Light ↔ Dark) left the embedded Orchestrator/Agent preview on its previous appearance. The React shell repainted immediately, but the preview `WebContentsView` stayed on the old theme until a later Chromium repaint or navigation, creating a visible desync.

The preview was never connected to the app's theme system. It received no theme updates, referenced no `nativeTheme`, and only fell back to the OS `prefers-color-scheme`.

This change drives Electron's `nativeTheme.themeSource` from the shell's theme preference so the preview updates at the same time as the rest of the UI.

## Approach

The preview renders arbitrary web content (AO preview targets), so `nativeTheme.themeSource` is the correct integration point. Since it changes what `prefers-color-scheme` reports to every `WebContents` in the app, any target that respects `prefers-color-scheme` switches themes immediately, with no reload or per-page injection.

The renderer sends the **theme preference** (`light` / `dark` / `system`), not the resolved theme, because these values map 1:1 to `themeSource`.

This distinction is important for `system`: forcing `themeSource` to `light` or `dark` while the app is set to System would freeze the shell's own `matchMedia`, breaking the existing follow-OS behavior. Sending `system` preserves OS-driven updates for both the preview and the shell.

This is the same class of issue as the terminal theme sync bug (#1283), but for the preview `BrowserView`.

## Changes

- `preload.ts` — expose `theme.set(preference)` on the bridge → `theme:set` IPC.
- `main.ts` — `theme:set` handler sets `nativeTheme.themeSource` (validated to `light` / `dark` / `system`).
- `_shell.tsx` — effect keyed on `themePreference` calls `aoBridge.theme.set(...)` alongside the existing `applyDocumentTheme`.
- `bridge.ts` / `test/setup.ts` — add a no-op `theme.set` for browser-preview and test modes.

**32 insertions, 0 deletions.** No UI, markup, or style changes.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` passes cleanly.
- Packaged the app and launched a real Electron build under Playwright.
- Drove the actual **Settings → Theme** control.
- Verified that a single store update per selection kept both the shell and preview synchronized.

| Pick | Shell `data-theme` | `nativeTheme.themeSource` |
|------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| Light | `light` | `light` |
| Dark | `dark` | `dark` |
| System | `light` (OS) | `system` |
| Light | `light` | `light` |

## Notes

If a preview target ignores `prefers-color-scheme` and implements its own theme toggle, this approach (like any `nativeTheme`-based solution) will not override it. That behavior is outside the scope of the reported OS-fallback issue.

---

cc @Vaibhaav-Tiwari

title: feat(landing): add privacy policy page
body:
## What

Adds a `/privacy` page to the landing site and links it from the footer.

## Why

A publicly hosted privacy policy URL is a hard requirement for App Store and Play Store submission, and for external TestFlight distribution of AO Mobile. There was no such page on aoagents.dev.

An earlier draft existed as an unpublished `docs/privacy-policy.html`, but it covered the mobile app only and was never served anywhere.

## Details

The content is written from what the code actually does, not boilerplate:

- **AO Mobile** — server host/port in local storage and the connection password in the platform keychain (`expo-secure-store`), camera used solely to decode the pairing QR (`expo-camera`), push token registered with the user's *own* server and relayed via Expo → APNs/FCM (`expo-notifications`). States plainly that there are no analytics or tracking SDKs, which matches the dependency list.
- **Desktop app and CLI** — discloses the anonymous PostHog telemetry from `docs/telemetry.md`: the event categories, path/URL redaction, SHA-256 hashed project IDs, the install ID at `~/.ao/data/telemetry_install_id`, 30-day local SQLite retention, session recording of AO's own UI, and how to turn it off.
- **This website** — no cookies or analytics, but honest about the two real third-party requests: the GitHub API call for star count/latest release, and the embedded Mux player.
- Plus what is never collected, third-party services, storage/security, retention, rights, children, changes, and contact.

Contact routes to GitHub issues and Discord rather than a personal email address.

Ordering puts the mobile section first, since that is the App Store–facing part a reviewer needs to find.

## Notes

- Built from `components/ui` conventions already used on the landing site — reuses `LandingNav`, `LandingFooter`, `ScrollRevealProvider`, and the existing CSS tokens, so it inherits the site's dark theme with no new styles.
- `deploy-landing.yml` already matches `frontend/src/landing/**`, so this deploys automatically on merge to `main`.
- Also adds a Privacy link to the footer's Community column and the footer bottom bar.

## Testing

- `npm run build` in `frontend/src/landing` succeeds; `/privacy` is emitted as a static route in the export.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npx prettier@3 --check` clean on both files.
- Rendered and visually verified against the local static export at `/privacy/`; nav, content, and footer render correctly in the site's dark theme.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `docs/privacy-policy.html` is now redundant and could be deleted or made to point here.
- The footer's `Features` / `Agents` links are bare `#features` / `#agents` anchors, so they are dead links on any non-home page including this one. Fixing them to `/#features` changes behavior on the landing page itself, so it is left alone here.

title: Trim public build workflows: signing and publishing move to external release conductor
body:
## Summary

Once the external release conductor is live, the public repo should build only unsigned artifacts on dispatch and hold no release secrets. This issue tracks the trim. **Do not merge until the conductor has produced at least one real signed release**, otherwise shipping breaks.

## Changes

- Remove in-build signing: drop `osxSign`/`osxNotarize` activation and the `macos-signing-setup` invocations from `frontend-release.yml` and `frontend-nightly.yml`.
- Remove `publisher-github` release creation and the alias `gh release upload` steps from those workflows (the conductor creates releases now).
- Remove the `publish-feed` job (feed generation moves to the conductor).
- Delete the nightly `schedule:` cron from `frontend-nightly.yml` (the conductor's cron drives nightly).
- Retire `feature-release.yml` (PR previews move to the conductor).

## Depends on

The conductor (AgentWrapper/ao-releases) being live and proven. Neutral capability workflow added in #2862.

title: ci: trim public repo to unsigned builds and retire the desktop-v* release trigger
body:
Closes #2914

Last step of the release migration. Signing, notarization, feed generation and
publishing now live in the access-restricted release conductor
(`AgentWrapper/ao-releases`); this PR removes the machinery they replaced from
the public repo. The stable v0.11.0 cut through the conductor today confirms
everything removed here is unused.

## What this does

**The public repo builds unsigned artifacts and nothing else.**
`build-artifacts.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` only) builds all four platform
targets, uploads them as run artifacts plus a `digests.json`, references no
secrets and creates no release. The conductor pins a commit, verifies those
digests, signs and notarizes macOS, generates the electron-updater feeds, and
publishes the GitHub Release.

Removed:

- `.github/actions/macos-signing-setup/` and every reference to the six Apple
  signing secrets.
- `frontend-release.yml` (see below).
- `feature-release.yml` (PR previews move to the conductor).
  `feature-release-cleanup.yml` stays so already-published feature prereleases
  still get retired.
- The `publish-feed` and `e2e-gate` jobs. The gate harness
  (`scripts/ao-e2e-pod-gate.mjs`, its tests, `test/e2e-pod/*`) and
  `e2e-gate-tests.yml` stay here: the conductor checks them out at runtime and
  the unit tests still belong in this repo.

`frontend-nightly.yml` hunks from the original version of this PR were dropped
during the rebase: #3070 deleted that file on `main`, and it is not resurrected
here.

## Closing the `desktop-v*` tag hole

`frontend-release.yml` triggered on `push: tags: desktop-v*`. Creating the
`desktop-v0.11.0` tag today fired the entire legacy release pipeline against the
freshly published v0.11.0 release (run 30338459688). It was caught in the
`environment: release` wait state and cancelled before it could clobber
anything, but that was luck, not design.

The conductor still **needs** `desktop-v*` tags to exist, because `ao-releases`
`nightly.yml` computes the next nightly version from them. So the trigger had to
go, not the tags. Once the trigger is gone the workflow is a pure duplicate of
the build legs already in `build-artifacts.yml`, `desktop-testing.yml` and
`testing-build.yml`, so it is retired outright rather than left dispatch-only.

`desktop-v*` tag pushes are now inert in this repo: no workflow triggers on
them.

Dangling references to the retired workflow were cleaned up in the same pass:
the `e2e-gate-tests.yml` path filter, the `scripts/` pod-gate header comment and
package description, and a stale `frontend-nightly.yml` comment in
`build-artifacts.yml`.

## Docs

No release documentation remains in this repository.

- `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md` is reduced to a stub: releases are not cut
  here, open PRs against `main`, builds here are unsigned. The architecture,
  channel names, asset/feed filenames and `desktop-v*` tag semantics are gone.
- `docs/ao-start-bootstrapper-and-npm-deprecation.md` is deleted. The `ao start`
  bootstrapper work it specced has shipped, and its sections 1.2/1.4 were a
  stale description of the retired pipeline and its signing secrets. Nothing in
  the repo referenced it.
- The auto-update comment in `frontend/src/main.ts` no longer points at the
  release doc.

A grep for `notariz`, `CSC_LINK`, `APPLE_API`, `desktop-v`, `electron-updater`,
`publish-feed`, `cut a release`, `release process` and `nightly channel` across
every `.md`/`.mdx` in the repo now returns zero hits. The README download table,
`AGENTS.md`, the `using-ao` skill and the landing docs are untouched: those
describe *installing* the app, not producing a release.

## Follow-up for a repo owner (not done here)

The six Apple secrets (`CSC_LINK`, `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_API_KEY_BASE64`,
`APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`) are now unused
by any workflow in this repo and should be deleted from repo Actions secrets.
That is a repo-owner action for Prateek after this merges; this PR deletes no
secrets. Note that the material in `ao-releases` is a re-export of the same
cert and key, so deleting them here does not by itself close the exposure; only
reissuing them in the Apple Developer portal does.

The repo's `release` environment (and its required-reviewer list) is also
referenced by no workflow after this PR and can be removed at the same time.
`deploy-landing.yml` uses `github-pages`, which is unaffected.

`frontend/forge.config.ts` is intentionally untouched. Its `osxSign`/
`osxNotarize` blocks and the `publisher-github` entry are env-gated and inert
without those env vars; the conductor reuses this same config to produce the
signed build.

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean across all workflows.
- `node --test scripts/ao-e2e-pod-gate.test.mjs`: 17/17 pass.
- `grep` over the repo returns zero references to `macos-signing-setup`,
  `publish-feed`, `frontend-release.yml` or `frontend-nightly.yml` outside the
  dated spec doc noted above.

title: fix(opencode): forward role-specific model config on launch and restore
body:
## What

Forward the configured role model to the `opencode` CLI on both launch and restore, and advertise the `model` config field.

## Why

Fixes #2891.

`GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` built their argv without reading `cfg.Config.Model`, so a worker or orchestrator configured with a specific model silently started on opencode's global default. The adapter also inherited the empty `agentbase.Base.GetConfigSpec`, so it never advertised a `model` field.

## How

Mirrors the Codex fix in #2869:

- `appendModelFlag` appends `--model <trimmed model>` when `strings.TrimSpace(cfg.Config.Model) != ""`, called from both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`.
- `GetConfigSpec` override advertising `model` as `ports.ConfigFieldString`.

The flag is appended right after the permission flags so it sits with the other `append*Flags` output, ahead of `--agent` and the trailing `--prompt` / `--session` argument pairs. opencode gives the CLI flag the highest precedence, above the config file, so this wins over a user's `model` config value as intended.

Model values stay in opencode's `provider/model` form; the adapter passes the string through untouched apart from trimming.

## Testing

```
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/    ok
gofmt -l / go vet                              clean
go build ./...                                 clean
```

Three new tests, proven to fail on `main` before the fix:

```
--- FAIL: TestGetConfigSpecReportsModelField
         got: []ports.ConfigField(nil)
--- FAIL: TestGetLaunchCommandAppendsConfiguredModel
        want: []string{"opencode", "--model", "anthropic/claude-4.5-sonnet"}
         got: []string{"opencode"}
--- FAIL: TestGetRestoreCommandAppendsConfiguredModel
        want: []string{"opencode", "--model", "anthropic/claude-4.5-sonnet", "--session", "ses_abc123"}
         got: []string{"opencode", "--session", "ses_abc123"}
```

`TestGetLaunchCommandOmitsBlankConfiguredModel` passes both before and after, so it pins the blank/whitespace case rather than restating the fix.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

title: feat(settings): add app links and LAN/Tailscale setup steps to Connect Mobile
body:
## Problem

The Connect Mobile modal shows a pairing QR, but:

1. **It never says where to get the app.** The QR is meaningless until Agent Orchestrator is installed on the phone.
2. **Tailscale is invisible.** The LAN listener binds all interfaces, so Tailscale already works — but only if the user types the `100.x` host into the mobile app's Settings by hand (`packages/mobile/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx:151`). The pairing QR structurally cannot carry it: `mobilebridge.AutopickLANIP()` skips `utun*` interfaces and accepts only RFC1918 addresses, and Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` is CGNAT, not private (`backend/internal/mobilebridge/netiface.go:12,48`). Nothing in the desktop UI said so.

## Changes

Frontend only — no backend, API-schema, or dependency changes.

- **`ConnectMobileGetApp`** — a "Get the app" card above the Enable toggle, outside the enable-collapse since installing the app is independent of whether the bridge runs. iOS row links to the TestFlight beta via `aoBridge.app.openExternal` (no `<a href>`), with a collapsible QR of the join URL so you can install from the phone without typing. Android row is an informational "coming soon" chip.
- **`ConnectMobileSetup`** — `LAN` / `Tailscale` tabs with per-transport steps, placed above the pairing QR so the choice is visible without scrolling. Tailscale steps are manual-entry on purpose, for the reason above.
- **Modal** — widened 336px → 500px, body scrolls past `80vh` with the scrollbar hidden via a new `.scrollbar-none` utility (following the existing `.xterm-viewport` pattern).

Both new components are pure and presentational; `ConnectMobileModal` keeps sole ownership of bridge state.

## Testing

- 6 new unit tests across the two components; 574 renderer tests pass.
- Verified in the Electron app and via Playwright screenshots in dark mode, in both tabs and with the QR expanded/collapsed.

## Notes

- The width bump is a deliberate deviation from the agent-orchestrator dialog width DESIGN.md pins — happy to revert it if you'd rather keep them uniform.
