title: refactor(lifecycle): remove the worker-idle orchestrator nudge
body:
Closes #3038.

## What

Drops the `[AO] Worker <id> has gone idle and may be done. Inspect it with ...` message the daemon auto-sent to the orchestrator session whenever a worker went idle.

Per the issue, the nudge added no signal and cost turns:

- It re-fired repeatedly for the same worker (each idle re-nudged, including ones already inspected).
- Idle does not mean done: read-only/research workers idle immediately after reporting.
- The human already sees idle state in the sidebar, and the orchestrator inspects workers on demand.

## How

The nudge was the sole consumer of the `worker_idle` outbox, so the whole pipeline that existed only to carry it is removed:

- `domain.WorkerIdleEvent`, the store methods (`RecordWorkerIdle`, `ListPendingWorkerIdleEvents*`, `MarkWorkerIdleEventDelivered`), and the sqlc query/model.
- Lifecycle dispatch plumbing: `DispatchPendingWorkerIdleEvents`, `DispatchAllPendingWorkerIdleEvents`, `workerIdleNudgeMessage`, `crossedToIdle`, `orchestratorDispatchTrigger`, `safeToDeliver`, `liveOrchestrator`, and the per-project dispatch locks.
- Daemon wiring: the boot-time redelivery goroutine and the 2-minute recovery sweep.
- Migration `0037` drops the now-unused `worker_idle_events` table.

Idle **detection** on the session row is untouched (the UI still shows idle state); only the orchestrator-directed message goes away. Net: +35 / -1330 lines.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt` clean.
- `go test ./internal/lifecycle/ ./internal/adapters/agent/fake/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/...` pass (the sqlite suite applies migration 0037).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failures confirmed identical on pristine `upstream/main`: macOS `/private/var` symlink path tests (`workspace/scratch`, `daemon` wiring) and the `internal/cli` spawn 404 integration tests.

## Rebase onto main (2026-07-28)

Rebased onto `upstream/main` (a10c98c80) to clear the conflict. Resolutions:

- `daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go`: kept mains new `runtimeReaper` / `activityDone` fields, the activity poller wiring, and `ReconcileRuntime`; dropped only `sweepDone` and the `startWorkerIdleSweep` start/drain.
- Migration renumbered `0031` -> `0037`: main took 0031-0036 in the meantime, and `TestMigrationVersionsAreUnique` rejects a duplicate version.
- `lifecycle/manager_test.go` and `observe/activity/observer_integration_test.go`: main added assertions on the `worker_idle` outbox as a proxy for the idle transition landing. Dropped those assertions; the `Activity.State` assertions next to them already cover the same behaviour, and idle detection itself is unchanged.

title: fix(orchestrator): open most recently active session, not newest-created
body:
## Problem

Clicking **Orchestrator** (sidebar / topbar / board / command palette) sometimes opened an **empty conversation** as if history had been wiped. History was still on another live orchestrator session; the UI/daemon had attached to a different, newer empty one.

## Root cause

When more than one non-terminated orchestrator existed for a project (overlap during replacement, accidental duplicates, etc.), both the frontend picker (`newestActiveOrchestrator`) and the daemon ensure path (`SpawnOrchestrator` clean=false → `newestSession`) ranked by **createdAt first**.

That preferred a brand-new empty spawn over an older still-active orchestrator that held the real conversation — matching the “wrong session / empty history on open” report and the recency intent of #1362 (most recently **used/active**, not lex-smallest or newest-created).

## Fix

Rank live orchestrators by:

1. `activity.lastActivityAt` (most recently used)
2. `updatedAt`
3. `createdAt`
4. session id

Applied in both:

- `frontend/.../workspace.ts` (`newestActiveOrchestrator` — all open entry points already use this)
- `backend/.../service/session/service.go` (`sessionNewer` — ensure/reuse when clean=false)

## What was deliberately not changed

| Path | Behavior preserved |
|------|-------------------|
| `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=false)` with **one** active orchestrator | Still returns that session; no spawn |
| `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=true)` / restart / settings / restore-dialog | Still retires then spawns |
| Kill / terminate / multi-project isolation / worker spawn / review | Untouched |
| #3032 sidebar pinned Orchestrator row | **Not** duplicated; that remains a separate UX PR |
| #2501 false terminate + silent replace | **Not** fixed here (lifecycle); residual risk noted below |

## Tests

- Frontend: `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/types/workspace.test.ts` — prefers recently-active over newer empty spawn
- Backend: `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/session/ -count=1` — ensure returns most recently active among duplicates; existing clean=false/true tests still pass

## Residual risks / follow-ups

- **#2501**: if the reaper falsely marks the live orchestrator terminated, ensure still spawns a cold session. Consecutive-probe work is in #2587; unlinked respawn notification is still open.
- Parent-orchestrator linkage (#1211) is still absent in the Go domain; when multiple lives exist we pick by activity recency, not worker parent.

Closes nothing automatically; addresses the open-path half of the “click Orchestrator clears history” report and improves #1362 targeting.

title: fix(renderer): refetch once before spawning orchestrator on open
body:
## Problem

Clicking Orchestrator sometimes opened an empty conversation. History still lived on the live orchestrator; the UI had treated a **stale empty workspace cache** as “no orchestrator” and spawned a blank new one.

## Fix

Shared `openOrEnsureOrchestrator` helper used by **ShellTopbar**, **Sidebar**, and **CommandPalette**:

1. Prefer `newestActiveOrchestrator` / `findProjectOrchestrator` from the current cache
2. If none → **refetch workspaces once**, recompute
3. If still none → `spawnOrchestrator(..., clean=false)` only
4. Never passes `clean=true`

## Preserved

- Restart / settings / restore_dialog `clean=true` paths
- Kill / terminate / multi-project isolation / worker spawn
- Backend ensure semantics (unchanged)

## Residual risk

- **#2501 / #2587**: false-terminated live orchestrator on the daemon still causes ensure to mint a new empty session. Not addressed here (lifecycle probe race).

## Tests

```bash
cd frontend && npm test -- --run \
  src/renderer/lib/open-orchestrator.test.ts \
  src/renderer/lib/spawn-orchestrator.test.ts \
  src/renderer/components/CommandPalette.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.test.tsx
```

title: fix(kilocode): forward role-specific model config on launch
body:
Closes #2896.

## Problem
AO forwards a per-role model (`agentConfig.model`) into every adapter as `cfg.Config.Model`, but each adapter must opt in to passing it to its CLI. The Kilo Code adapter never read `cfg.Config`, so a configured worker/orchestrator model was silently dropped and the session fell back to Kilo Code's global default.

## Fix
Kilo Code has no reliable `--model` flag for the interactive TUI AO launches (`--model` exists only on `kilo run`). It reads a per-agent model from its injected `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` config at `agent.<name>.model` (precedence: session override > per-agent config > global > auto). AO already injects that config and selects a generated agent with `--agent`, so the model is carried there:

- Add a `Model` field to `kilocodeAgentSettings`.
- Create and select the AO agent whenever a system prompt **or** a model is present. Previously the agent entry was created only for a system prompt, so a model-only role never received `--agent` and the model was dropped — this is the reported repro.
- Forward `cfg.Config.Model` (trimmed) from both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`.
- Override `GetConfigSpec` to advertise the `model` key.

Mirrors the Codex fix (#2869), adapted to Kilo Code's config-injection mechanism instead of a CLI flag.

## Tests
- Model forwarded on launch (with a system prompt) and on restore.
- Model-only / no-prompt launch still creates and selects the AO agent (the repro).
- Blank/whitespace model omitted (no agent, no `--agent`, no env prefix).
- Config-spec test updated to assert the `model` field.

`go test ./...` and golangci-lint pass. End-to-end confirmation that Kilo Code applies the model requires the `kilocode` binary and is a manual step.

title: [Frontend]: Add copy actions for board branch names and PR URLs

Today those values are visible on the card, but there is no direct copy affordance. Manual selection is fiddly in the compact board UI, and clicking the card can navigate away from the board.

title: fix(scm): re-land review-body fetch/mapping on main (recover stranded #3010)
body:
## Summary

Re-lands #3010's provider review-body fetch/mapping onto `main`. Addresses the [P1] on #3046: like #3011, **#3010 (`3da9fff85`) was merged into its stacked base (`feat/persist-pr-review-body`), not `main`** — confirmed `3da9fff85` is not an ancestor of `main`, and `SCMReviewSummaryObservation` has no `Body` field there.

So even after #3046, the pipeline was broken end to end: the API copies `review.Body` into the response, but nothing populated it — real GitHub refreshes persisted `Body == ""` and `omitempty` dropped it from the response. Reviewer/verdict showed, the summary body did not. #3046's tests injected `Body` above the missing fetch layer, so they didn't catch it (fair call by the reviewer).

This cherry-picks `3da9fff85` (the five-file fetch/mapping commit, including its provider test):

- request `body` in the GitHub review-summary GraphQL and map it in `scmReviewSummaryFromGraphQL`
- add `Body` to `ports.SCMReviewSummaryObservation`
- carry `Body` through `domainFromObservation` (observer) and `claimRowsFromSCM` (session claim)

With this + #3009 (persist) + #3046 (expose) all on `main`, the review-summary body flows end to end for the first time.

## Verification

title: bug(landing): floating nav bar GitHub badge overlaps 'Docs' link at md breakpoint
body:
## Bug

The floating navigation bar on the landing page has the GitHub star badge overlapping the "Docs" navigation link. The GitHub badge (with star count "8.5k") is rendered on top of the rightmost nav link, partially obscuring the text.

![Nav bar overlap screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-landing-nav-overlap/.issue-assets/landing-nav-overlap/nav-overlap.png)

**Source:** Discord #bug-triage | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `653c63c4`
**Priority:** medium — visual defect on public-facing landing page, no functional impact
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Open the landing page (aoagents.dev) at a desktop viewport width roughly between **768px–1024px** (the `md` breakpoint range).
2. Observe the floating nav bar at the top.
3. The GitHub star badge (right side) overlaps the "Docs" link (center).

## Root Cause

The nav links are **absolutely positioned** at the horizontal center of the container, taking them out of the flex flow:

```tsx
// frontend/src/landing/components/LandingNav.tsx:154
<nav className="absolute left-1/2 hidden -translate-x-1/2 items-center gap-7 md:flex">
```

Meanwhile, the container uses `justify-between` with only two participating flex children — the logo (left) and the right-side cluster (GitHub badge + socials + Download button):

```tsx
// line 141
<div className="relative mx-auto flex h-14 w-full max-w-4xl items-center justify-between gap-5 ...">
```

Because the centered nav is `absolute`, it **does not reserve horizontal space** in the flex layout. The `justify-between` only pushes the logo and the right-side cluster apart — neither knows about the nav's width.

At the `md` breakpoint range (768px–1024px):
- The social icons are hidden (`hidden ... lg:flex`, line 190)
- The separator is hidden (`hidden ... lg:block`, line 189)
- But the **GitHub star badge** (always visible) and the **Download button** (`md:inline-flex`, line 210) are both shown
- The centered nav with 4 links at `gap-7` (28px) has enough width that its right edge extends into the right-side cluster's space
- Result: the GitHub badge sits on top of "Docs"

At `lg`+ widths the container is wide enough (or the socials add enough right-side width) that the collision doesn't occur. Below `md`, the nav links are hidden entirely (`hidden ... md:flex`).

## Fix

**Option A (recommended):** Remove `absolute` positioning from the nav and let it participate in flex flow:

```tsx
<nav className="hidden flex-1 items-center justify-center gap-7 md:flex">
```

This makes `justify-between` space all three children correctly. The logo stays left, the nav centers itself in the remaining space, and the right-side cluster stays right.

**Option B (minimal):** Reduce the nav gap at `md` and only use `gap-7` at `lg`:

```tsx
<nav className="absolute left-1/2 hidden -translate-x-1/2 items-center gap-4 lg:gap-7 md:flex">
```

This is a band-aid — the fundamental absolute-vs-flex mismatch remains.

## Impact

- Visual overlap on the public-facing landing page at common laptop/tablet viewport widths
- "Docs" link is partially obscured/clickable area is reduced
- No functional breakage, but looks unprofessional on first impression

## Related

- [#2292](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2292) — prior landing page UI/UX audit (closed)
- Introduced by `6fb31e68` — `feat(landing): conversion-focused redesign` (#2826)

title: bug(shellterm): terminal opened from a session starts in the project root instead of the session worktree
body:
## Bug

Opening a standalone shell terminal while viewing an agent session starts the shell in the registered project's main root, not in the worktree where that session is running.

This makes the terminal look colocated with the active agent while commands actually run against a different checkout/branch. A user can easily inspect, build, or edit the wrong tree.

**Source:** user report after the standalone terminal feature landed in #2861 / #2828
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `d79977a9f5ed5b33f1b6188fe704b5d309023679` (2026-07-24)
**Confidence:** High — the current request path drops session context and resolves only the project root.

## Reproduction

1. Open a project in AO.
2. Spawn an agent session that runs in its own generated worktree.
3. Navigate to that session's terminal view.
4. Open a standalone terminal using either the `+` terminal-tab action or `Ctrl+Shift+\``.
5. Run:

```sh
pwd
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git branch --show-current
```

## Expected

When the action is invoked from a session view, the new terminal starts in that session's current workspace/worktree (`SessionRecord.Metadata.WorkspacePath`) and therefore on the same checkout/branch as the agent.

Opening a terminal from a project board can continue to use the registered project root. Opening one without project or session context can continue to use the daemon data-dir fallback.

## Actual

The new shell starts in the registered project root (the main worktree), even though it was opened from a worker session running in a different worktree.

## Root cause

The session route is reduced to project scope before the open request is made:

- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx` derives `scopedProjectId` from the current route/session and calls `openShellTerminal.mutate(scopedProjectId)`.
- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useShellTerminals.ts` sends only `{ projectId }` to `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals`.
- `controllers.OpenShellTerminalRequest` and `shellterm.OpenShellTerminalInput` have no session identifier.
- `shellterm.Service.resolveShellTerminalWorkingDir` can therefore only call `ProjectRootLocator.ProjectRoot`, so it deterministically chooses the main project root.

The UI knows which session is active, but that context never reaches the daemon.

## Fix shape

Add a session-scoped way to open a shell without accepting an arbitrary filesystem path from the renderer:

- Extend the open-shell request/input with `sessionId` (define precedence or validation if both `sessionId` and `projectId` are present).
- When the current route is a session, have both the `+` action and shortcut pass that session id.
- Resolve the id server-side through the session/service boundary and use the durable session workspace path.
- Preserve the existing project-root and data-dir fallbacks outside a session.
- Regenerate the OpenAPI spec and frontend schema after changing the DTO.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A terminal opened from a worker session starts in that worker's worktree.
- [ ] A terminal opened from an orchestrator/session with a workspace starts in that session's workspace.
- [ ] Both the terminal-tab `+` action and `Ctrl+Shift+\`` behave the same way.
- [ ] A terminal opened from a project board still starts at the registered project root.
- [ ] A terminal opened with no project/session context still uses the existing daemon data-dir fallback.
- [ ] The renderer does not send an arbitrary raw path; the daemon resolves the session id to its workspace.
- [ ] Controller/service tests cover session resolution, unknown/missing session workspace, and existing fallbacks.
- [ ] Frontend tests assert that session routes submit session scope while board routes submit project scope.

## Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues for combinations of: `terminal`, `standalone terminal`, `shell terminal`, `worktree`, `working directory`, `cwd`, `project root`, `session worktree`, `shellterm`, `workingDir`, and references to #2828/#2861. No issue covering this behavior was found. #2828 is the completed feature request and specifies project-root scope, but it does not track the session-worktree context bug introduced by the landed implementation.

title: Give every AO worker a live, session-owned browser
body:
## What

This PR turns AO’s passive Preview panel into a browser that agents can inspect, control, and verify—while the developer watches or takes over the same live page.

### Browser automation

- Adds the session-scoped `ao browser` command surface.
- Supports accessibility snapshots with short-lived element references.
- Adds navigation, clicking, filling, typing, keyboard shortcuts, hovering, scrolling, selecting, checking, and property reads.
- Adds deterministic waits for page loads, text, selectors, URLs, disappearance, and DOM stability.
- Adds non-mutating element highlighting.
- Adds screenshots, console inspection, and page-error inspection.

### Session ownership and isolation

- Gives every worker its own browser target and ephemeral profile.
- Isolates cookies, storage, tabs, references, and browser state between workers.
- Keeps the browser runtime available while the Browser panel is hidden.
- Uses the same live `WebContentsView` for both the agent and developer.

### Tabs and popups

- Adds stable logical tab IDs for agent commands.
- Captures allowed popups as tabs instead of separate OS browser windows.
- Adds a visible tab selector so developers can inspect, switch, and close tabs.
- Keeps agent actions synchronized with whichever tab the developer selects.

### Deterministic previews

- Adds session-owned development-server lifecycle management.
- Starts existing `.ao/launch.json` configurations, selects a port, waits for readiness, and cleans up the process tree with the session.
- Opens the exact preview belonging to the requesting worker instead of guessing between unrelated localhost processes.
- Opens static HTML and Markdown without introducing unnecessary npm projects or dependencies.
- Automatically opens primary browser-displayable artifacts such as Markdown, HTML, PDF, SVG, and images.

### Optional network diagnostics

- Adds explicit, temporary network-metadata capture for debugging API, CORS, authentication, caching, redirect, and loading failures.
- Keeps capture disabled by default.
- Scopes capture to the active tab, limits it to 200 in-memory entries, and expires it automatically.
- Excludes bodies, credentials, cookies, sensitive headers, fragments, and query values.
- Does not add request interception, modification, replay, or HAR export.

### Developer-facing polish

- Shows browser activity only while the agent is actually using the browser.
- Keeps annotation progress separate and clears successful delivery confirmation automatically.
- Adds concise harness guidance so agents use AO’s shared browser instead of a separate Codex IAB, browser MCP, or host-browser runtime.

## Why

Previously, an agent could build an application while AO displayed an unrelated or stale page, and meaningful verification often required the developer to manually open URLs and test the result.

This enables a smoother development loop:

1. The agent starts or opens the correct application for its worker.
2. AO automatically displays that exact page.
3. The agent inspects and operates the UI, checks errors, and verifies behavior.
4. The developer watches the same page and can take over at any time.
5. Other workers remain isolated and cannot access that browser state.

Developers can now ask an agent to build, debug, and verify a frontend without repeatedly copying URLs, describing visible failures, or switching to a separate automation browser.

## How

- Introduces a dedicated local daemon-to-Electron browser bridge.
- Uses Electron’s target-bound debugger transport instead of exposing a global remote-debugging endpoint.
- Routes every command through `AO_SESSION_ID` and validates session ownership at the daemon boundary.
- Keeps the loopback browser routes unavailable through the optional LAN listener.
- Persists session preview targets through the existing daemon API and generated TypeScript client.
- Adds platform-specific preview-process management for Unix and Windows.
- Updates AO’s embedded skill guidance and E2E fake bridge to match the expanded browser contract.

Reviewer focus:

- Browser target and worker isolation.
- Preview-process cleanup and restart behavior.
- Optional network-capture privacy boundaries.
- Daemon/Electron reconnect and command-correlation behavior.

## Testing

Passed locally:

- `go build ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- Branch-scoped `golangci-lint` — zero findings
- Race tests for the changed browser, CLI, daemon, HTTP, preview, preview-server, session lifecycle, and skill packages
- Native CLI E2E suite, including browser, network, screenshot, wait, and preview commands
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- 85 focused browser renderer/main-process tests
- OpenAPI and generated TypeScript regeneration with zero drift

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` / continuing the existing feature branch
- [x] One focused browser and preview-runtime change
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and architecture boundaries
- [x] Tests added or updated for user-visible behavior
- [ ] Relevant remote CI checks pass

title: fix(daemon): export AO_RUN_FILE into session env so hooks find the daemon
body:
## Problem

Spawned sessions receive `AO_DATA_DIR` in their environment but not `AO_RUN_FILE`. The `ao hooks` callbacks that run inside each agent session locate the daemon via `config.resolveRunFilePath`, which reads `AO_RUN_FILE` and otherwise falls back to the default `~/.ao/running.json` (see `backend/internal/cli/client.go:102-110`).

So when the daemon runs with an `AO_RUN_FILE` override — **every dev build launches its daemon with `~/.ao/dev/running.json`** (`frontend/src/main.ts` `runFilePath()` + `devExtras.AO_RUN_FILE`) — the session's hook callbacks look at the wrong run-file, find it stale or absent, and fail with:

```
AO daemon is not running (stale run-file at /Users/.../.ao/running.json) — start it with `ao start`
```

Activity tracking then silently stalls. This is the same failure mode the existing PATH-pin guard already warns about ("`ao hooks` callbacks may resolve to a different ao and activity tracking will stall").

Observed in the wild: a dev build's `hooks.log` filled with the stale-run-file error across many sessions while the daemon was in fact running.

## Fix

Thread the daemon's resolved run-file path through `sessionmanager.Deps.RunFilePath` (wired from `cfg.RunFilePath`) and export it as `AO_RUN_FILE` in `spawnEnv`, alongside `AO_DATA_DIR`. Now `ao hooks` connects to the daemon that spawned it regardless of where its run-file lives. An empty path leaves `AO_RUN_FILE` unset, so the config default behavior is unchanged for daemons that use it.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/daemon/` clean.
- New/updated unit tests in `provision_test.go`: `AO_RUN_FILE` is set to the daemon's path, project env cannot override it, and an empty path leaves it unset.
- End-to-end: ran the daemon with `AO_RUN_FILE=<custom>/custom-running.json`, spawned a session, and confirmed the session's live shell env contains `AO_RUN_FILE=<custom>/custom-running.json` (previously unset).

title: Kill button 'Killing…' state leaks across session switches (missing React key)
body:
## Bug

When killing a worker session and then switching to a different worker, the **"Killing…"** loading state persists on the new session's kill button.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open worker session A
2. Click **Kill** → click **Confirm kill**
3. While the mutation is in-flight (button shows "Killing…"), navigate to worker session B
4. Worker B's kill button **also** shows **"Killing…"** / "Confirm kill" state

## Root cause

`TopbarKillButton` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx` (line 224) is rendered **without a `key` prop**:

```tsx
<TopbarKillButton
    session={session}
    orchestratorId={orchestrator?.id}
    onKilled={...}
/>
```

Since the route pattern stays the same (`/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId`), React **reuses the same component instance** when switching sessions — it just swaps the `session` prop. But `TopbarKillButton` holds local state that doesn't reset:

- `confirming` (useState) — stays `true`
- `kill.isPending` (useMutation) — stays `true`
- `error` (useState) — can show stale error from session A on session B

There is no `key` prop and no `useEffect` that resets state when `session.id` changes.

## Impact

- The "Confirm kill" button is disabled on a session you didn't try to kill
- If the original kill mutation errors, the error message shows on the wrong session
- User could think session B is being killed when it isn't

## Suggested fix

Add `key={session.id}` to force React to unmount the old instance and mount a fresh one on session switch:

```tsx
<TopbarKillButton
    key={session.id}
    session={session}
    orchestratorId={orchestrator?.id}
    onKilled={...}
/>
```

One-line fix — the `key` makes React destroy the old `TopbarKillButton` (with stale mutation state) and create a new one with clean state.

## Severity

P2 — confusing UX state leak, no data corruption.

# Purpose

Audit and propose closure of issues and pull requests that only apply to the removed TypeScript/pnpm implementation.

The Go/Electron rewrite landed on main through #2166 on 2026-06-24 at 14:26:33 UTC.

- #2170 was the first issue opened after the landing.
- Therefore, issue numbers below #2170 form the pre-landing cohort by creation time.

## Closure standard

An issue will be recommended as **safe to close** only when its requested fix is concretely tied to code or distribution machinery removed by the rewrite, such as the old packages/* pnpm workspace, Next.js dashboard, TypeScript CLI/core/plugin implementation, or npm-first release flow.

A linked pull request will be recommended as **safe to close** only when it is still open and its diff targets that removed implementation, making it inapplicable to current main.

Conceptual feature requests and user-visible symptoms that could still apply to the Go/Electron product will not be included without revalidation.

This issue is a communication and review checkpoint. The audit will be posted below with exact counts, issue links, linked PRs, evidence, and exclusions before anything is closed.

title: feat(terminals): scope shell tabs to the session and allow renaming them
body:
## Problem

Two issues with the standalone shell terminal tabs:

1. **Tabs collide across sessions.** Shell terminals are stored as a single app-wide daemon list and carried only a `projectId`, so a shell opened in one session showed up in every session's tab strip (even in a different session of the same project). See the two screenshots in the discussion: sessions `ao-7` ("review") and `ao-13` ("work") both showed the same "AO" shell.
2. **Tabs can't be renamed.** A shell's title was fixed at creation (the working dir's base name) with no way to change it.

## Fix

**Per-session isolation**
- Shell terminals gain a nullable `session_id` (migration `0036`, FK to `sessions` ON DELETE CASCADE), threaded through query → store → service → DTO → generated TS.
- The shell layout tags a new shell with the current route's `sessionId` when one is open. `SessionView` filters its strip to `sessionId === current session`. Shells opened outside any session (from the board) have no session and live only on the standalone `/terminals` screen, which now shows only session-less shells.
- When the globally-active shell belongs to another session, the pane falls back to the session's own tab instead of rendering a shell that isn't in the strip.

**Rename**
- New `PATCH /api/v1/shell-terminals/{handleId}` with `{ "title": "..." }`, backed by `UpdateShellTerminalTitle`. Title is trimmed, must be non-empty and ≤ 80 chars; unknown handle is a 404. The title persists on the daemon and survives reload.
- Double-click a shell tab to rename inline: Enter/blur commits, Escape cancels, empty/unchanged is discarded.
- The two near-identical tab components (`CenterPane`, `ShellTerminalsView`) are unified into one shared `ShellTerminalTab`.

OpenAPI spec and generated `schema.ts` regenerated from the code-first source.

## Also included

Merged latest `main` and reformatted six agent-adapter files with go.mod's canonical Go 1.25.7 `gofmt` (import order: `ports` before `process`). PR #3006 had committed them with a newer gofmt, turning `main`'s build-test/lint red; this un-breaks CI for the branch.

## Testing

- Backend: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, golangci-lint clean, and `go test ./internal/service/shellterm/... ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/storage/sqlite/...` pass. New tests: `sessionId` round-trips through open; rename success / empty-title rejection / unknown-handle 404; controller PATCH returns the updated terminal, malformed body 400, 501-without-service.
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean; full renderer suite (1045 tests) passes. New `ShellTerminalTab` rename tests + a `SessionView` regression test asserting only the current session's shells reach the strip.
- Verified live in the dev app: shells opened in different sessions no longer share a strip; rename persists across reload.

fix(conpty): correctly implement pidAlive using processalive on Windows
body:
## What

Updates the `pidAlive` function in `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/pidalive_windows.go` to delegate to `processalive.Alive`.

## Why

Fixes #3079.

On Windows, the ConPTY runtime adapter's `pidAlive` implementation opened a handle to the process with `SYNCHRONIZE` access but never actually waited on it using `WaitForSingleObject`. Because Windows keeps process kernel objects alive until all handles are closed, `OpenProcess` succeeded for recently-terminated processes, incorrectly returning `true`. This broke the early-exit optimization during session teardown, causing the loop to always hang for the full 500ms deadline.

## How

- Replaced the flawed `OpenProcess` logic in `pidAlive` by directly calling `processalive.Alive(pid)`. 
- `processalive.Alive` is already implemented and proven elsewhere in the codebase, and correctly uses `WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0)` to check for `WAIT_TIMEOUT`.
- Replaced the `"golang.org/x/sys/windows"` import with `"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/processalive"`.

## Testing

- Confirmed that this effectively stops returning false positives for terminated processes.
- Checked that tests pass: `cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./...`

- [✓] Branched from `main`

title: feat(browser): search non-URL input, open links in-app, and glow on new links
body:
## What and why

The session Browser panel had rough edges: typing non-URL text in the address
bar coerced it to `https://<text>` and dead-ended on a blank page, terminal
links only opened in-app for localhost, and an incoming preview stole focus by
auto-opening the panel. This reworks it to behave like a real in-app browser.

Related: #2830 tackles the same "keep local pages in-app" goal from the backend
(sessions.go + AGENTS.md); this PR is the frontend side (link routing + address
bar) and does not touch those files.

## Changes

- **Address bar search.** Non-URL input (e.g. `hi`, `how do i center a div`)
  now runs a web search instead of navigating to a bogus host. Real hostnames,
  localhost, file paths, and explicit schemes are unchanged.
  (`main/browser-view-host.ts`)
- **Links open in the AO browser.** A left-click on any http/https terminal
  link opens it in the Browser panel (previously localhost only; external links
  went to the system browser). Right-click gives "Open in system browser".
  Non-web schemes (mailto:) still open externally.
  (`XtermTerminal.tsx`, `TerminalPane.tsx`)
- **No focus stealing.** An incoming preview (`ao preview`, or a link) now
  badges the Browser tab instead of auto-opening it. The badge is a glowing
  beacon and clears when the tab opens. (`SessionView.tsx`, `SessionInspector.tsx`,
  `ui-store.ts`)
- **Glow on terminal-printed URLs.** When an agent prints a URL (e.g. a
  pushed-PR link), the Browser tab glows. Detection strips ANSI, handles URLs
  split across output chunks, and dedupes (`lib/detect-urls.ts`), fed by a new
  `onOutput` seam on the terminal hook (`useTerminalSession.ts`).
- **fake harness** prints a realistic PR URL on its push line so the
  terminal-URL glow is demoable and testable end to end. (`fake.go`)

## Testing

- New `detect-urls` unit suite (detect, dedupe, ANSI strip, split-chunk join,
  non-web ignore, reset).
- Updated `browser-view-host`, `SessionView`, `TerminalPane`, and
  `XtermTerminal` suites for the new behavior.
- Full frontend suite green (1064 tests); `tsc --noEmit` clean; Go `fake`
  package test green. Rebased on latest `main`.
- Ran the built desktop app and drove the Browser panel: it renders a live URL
  and re-navigates in place when the preview command re-fires. Address-bar
  search, right-click menu, and the terminal glow rest on the unit suite; GUI
  keystroke automation was blocked by macOS assistive-access in this environment.

## Risks

- URL detection runs on every terminal output chunk for worker panes; it is
  ANSI-strip + regex + a bounded seen-set, kept cheap and skipped for non-worker
  panes.
- Behavior change: external terminal links now open in-app rather than the
  system browser (right-click restores the old behavior).

title: Follow-up to #2980: remaining session lifecycle correctness gaps
body:
## Origin

This is a follow-up derived from merged PR [#2980 — `fix: unify session state and lifecycle presentation`](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2980).

The PR's central model is sound: agent activity, terminal-runtime lifetime, durable session termination, and SCM outcome are independent facts. A deeper implementation review found the six correctness gaps below. They remain present after the final PR head and were revalidated against `main` at `f0512c885`.

This issue is not reopening the product decisions made in #2980. It tracks concrete implementation failures and missed consumers that remain after that PR.

## Shared invariant

The implementation should preserve these rules:

- An exited agent is not necessarily a terminated AO session.
- A merged PR does not by itself prove whether the session is alive.
- Once Kill accepts terminal intent, Resume must not resurrect the session.
- External runtime side effects and their durable launch generation must not disagree.
- Independently owned settings must not be overwritten by stale lifecycle snapshots.
- UI chronology and navigation must use the underlying lifetime/timestamp facts rather than construction order or a derived display label.

## Remaining failures

| # | Failure | Impact | Area |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scratch sessions can never use Resume agent | High | Daemon + desktop |
| 2 | Successful tmux respawn followed by probe failure leaves an unfenced agent running | High | Daemon |
| 3 | Resume races Kill and can undo terminal intent | High | Daemon |
| 4 | Lifecycle activity can silently overwrite the terminate-on-merge preference | Medium | Daemon/storage |
| 5 | Activity history is not actually reverse chronological | Medium | Desktop |
| 6 | Terminated merged sessions are promoted as needing attention | Medium | Desktop |

### 1. Scratch sessions can never use Resume agent

**Expected behavior**

Scratch projects are intentionally branchless. An exited scratch agent with an existing workspace and runtime handle should therefore be resumable without a Git branch.

**Why the code fails**

`DefaultSpawnBranch` deliberately returns an empty branch for scratch projects, but `ResumeAgentWithMode` rejects every empty branch before it loads the project and can apply the same scratch exception already used by Restore.

- [Scratch sessions intentionally get an empty branch](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L2049-L2059)
- [Resume treats every empty branch as an incomplete handle](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L936-L971)
- [The desktop still offers Resume based on live + exited state](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx#L324-L337)

**Real-world situation**

A first-time user chooses a scratch project to prototype a JSON-to-CSV tool without connecting a Git repository. The agent finishes and exits. Ten minutes later, the user notices quoted commas are handled incorrectly and clicks **Resume agent** to request one follow-up change.

**What the user sees**

The Resume button is present and the files and terminal still exist, but every attempt fails with `ErrIncompleteHandle`. The intentionally branchless session is being treated as corrupted state.

**Fix/proof shape**

- Load the project before validating the branch.
- Require a branch only for non-scratch project kinds, matching Restore.
- Add an exited-scratch Resume test and a controller/UI path test.

### 2. tmux can commit the respawn side effect but report failure

**Expected behavior**

Resume must leave AO in one of two coherent states: either the new agent generation did not start, or it started and the same generation is durably authoritative.

**Why the code fails**

`respawn-pane -k` kills the old pane workload and launches the new one before the separate `IsAlive` verification. If that verification has a transient error, `Restart` returns an empty handle and an error. The caller cancels the pending generation but has no successful handle with which to compensate.

- [`respawn-pane -k` runs before the fallible liveness verification](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go#L247-L283)
- [The relaunch path returns immediately on that error without committing the launch ID](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1030-L1063)

**Real-world situation**

A developer clicks **Resume agent** while their laptop is under load. tmux successfully executes `respawn-pane -k`, and the replacement Codex process begins starting, but the following `has-session` command briefly times out or returns a transient tmux error.

**What the user sees**

AO reports “Resume failed” and leaves the session in Exited even though a new agent is running. Its generation-specific hooks are rejected against the old durable generation. Clicking Resume again can replace that running process with yet another generation and discard work it already began.

**Fix/proof shape**

- Preserve ownership after the destructive respawn step.
- Either compensate by destroying the restarted handle, return an explicit “applied but unverified” result for reconciliation, or make verification/rollback part of the runtime contract.
- Add a test where respawn succeeds and only the following liveness probe fails.

### 3. Resume races Kill and can undo terminal intent

**Expected behavior**

Once explicit Kill or terminate-on-merge accepts terminal intent, a concurrent Resume must not clear termination or recreate the runtime.

**Why the code fails**

The per-session Resume exclusion only prevents a second Resume. Kill does not participate in that operation boundary. Both paths can read the same live/exited record, mutate external resources, and later commit conflicting lifecycle states. `MarkSpawned` unconditionally clears `IsTerminated`.

- [Kill has no shared arbitration with Resume](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L713-L783)
- [Resume validates once, restarts later, and is guarded only against another Resume](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L936-L987)
- [`MarkSpawned` clears termination unconditionally](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go#L790-L811)

**Real-world situation**

An agent exits just as its PR merges. The user clicks **Resume agent** to request a small follow-up while the enabled terminate-on-merge policy starts Kill. Both requests read the session as live and exited before either completes.

**Failure sequences**

1. Resume starts the replacement runtime.
2. Kill destroys runtime/workspace and marks the row terminated.
3. Resume calls `MarkSpawned`, clears termination, and leaves a live row whose resources are gone.

Or:

1. Kill destroys the old runtime and preserves a dirty workspace.
2. Resume observes no live runtime and creates a replacement.
3. Resume clears termination, defeating explicit or merge-driven cleanup.

**What the user sees**

The session may move to Archive and then reappear, remain live with a missing terminal/worktree, or continue running after the user configured it to terminate.

**Fix/proof shape**

- Share one per-session operation boundary across Resume, Kill, Restore, and replacement teardown, or use a conditional final transition tied to the expected state/generation.
- Make accepted terminal intent monotonic.
- Add deterministic tests for both Resume/Kill interleavings.

### 4. Lifecycle activity can erase the terminate-on-merge preference

**Expected behavior**

Once the merge policy update succeeds, unrelated activity callbacks must not revert it.

**Why the code fails**

The preference setter performs a narrow update, while lifecycle mutations read a complete session and later write every mutable column—including `terminate_on_pr_merge`. The store's write mutex serializes individual writes, but not the lifecycle read and later full-row commit as one atomic operation.

- [Full-row `UpdateSession` includes the policy column](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/sessions.sql#L14-L22)
- [The policy setter is a separate narrow update](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/sessions.sql#L61-L62)
- [Lifecycle performs a read-modify-full-write sequence](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go#L195-L212)

**Real-world situation**

While an agent is finishing a tool call, the user enables **Terminate on merge**. An activity callback had already read the row with the preference set to false. The narrow preference update commits true; the callback then commits its older full-row snapshot.

**What the user sees**

The switch may turn on and then silently flip back after CDC refresh. If the user navigates away before noticing, the PR later merges while the runtime and workspace remain alive, contrary to the setting they believed they saved.

**Fix/proof shape**

- Use lifecycle-specific partial update queries, a transaction spanning read/write ownership, or optimistic concurrency with an expected revision.
- Add a deterministic lost-update test that pauses lifecycle after its read, changes the preference, then releases the lifecycle write.

### 5. The Activity timeline is not reverse chronological

**Expected behavior**

Historical milestones should be ordered by their actual event timestamps, with the live current-state row kept separately at the top.

**Why the code fails**

The inspector appends events in category blocks—Created, Draft, Opened, Merged, Done—and then reverses the assembled array. It never sorts by the underlying timestamps.

- [Timeline events are assembled by category](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx#L492-L531)
- [`history.reverse()` substitutes construction order for chronology](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx#L533-L557)

**Real-world situation**

A worker owns a stacked pair of PRs. The root PR merged at 10:00, and the child PR opened at 11:45 after its dependency cleared. At noon, the user opens Activity to understand the sequence.

**What the user sees**

“Merged root PR” can appear above “Opened child PR” even though the opening happened later. The timeline implies the wrong causal sequence and can mislead stacked-PR or CI diagnosis.

**Fix/proof shape**

- Keep the raw timestamp on each historical event.
- Sort descending by parsed time with a deterministic fallback for missing/invalid values.
- Prepend the current untimestamped row after sorting.
- Add tests whose category order deliberately conflicts with timestamp order.

### 6. Terminated merged sessions still appear under Needs attention

**Expected behavior**

A terminated merged session should remain archived/search-only. `merged` describes SCM outcome; `isTerminated` describes lifetime and navigation eligibility.

**Why the code fails**

The command palette promotes every merge-zone session into `attentionSessions` without checking `sessionIsActive`. Its ID is then excluded from the later branch that would mark inactive sessions `searchOnly`.

- [Merge-zone sessions enter attention without a lifetime check](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/frontend/src/renderer/lib/command-palette.ts#L156-L170)
- [Only the later non-attention branch applies `searchOnly`](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/frontend/src/renderer/lib/command-palette.ts#L183-L188)
- [The existing test claims merged/terminated coverage but asserts only the terminated-status fixture](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0512c8857bfa2397703c0773394ad219133222c/frontend/src/renderer/lib/command-palette.test.ts#L168-L197)

This is best classified as a missed consumer exposed by #2980's explicit merged-vs-terminated model; it may predate the PR rather than being newly introduced by it.

**Real-world situation**

A user merges a payment-retry PR, terminates the session, and sees it enter Archive. The next morning they open the command palette to jump to active work.

**What the user sees**

The old terminated session is promoted under **Needs attention** without a search query. Selecting it opens archived context instead of actionable work and crowds genuinely live attention items.

**Fix/proof shape**

- Require `sessionIsActive(session)` in the attention filter.
- Add an explicit `status=merged, isTerminated=true` fixture and assert that it is search-only and absent from default suggestions.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Exited scratch sessions can resume successfully without a branch.
- [ ] A post-respawn verification error cannot leave an untracked live generation.
- [ ] Kill/terminate-on-merge cannot be undone by an overlapping Resume.
- [ ] Lifecycle writes cannot revert an independently updated merge policy.
- [ ] Historical Activity events are sorted by actual timestamps.
- [ ] Terminated merged sessions stay out of default attention suggestions.
- [ ] Deterministic regression tests cover every failure sequence above.

## Suggested implementation order

1. Resume/Kill arbitration and monotonic terminal intent.
2. tmux restart ownership after partial success.
3. Scratch Resume validation.
4. Policy lost-update protection.
5. Timeline chronology.
6. Command-palette active-session filtering.

Related merged PR: [#2980](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2980).

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

... (truncated)

title: [Tooling]: fix or remove the repo Prettier setup
body:
### Summary

  ## Problem

  The repository currently has partial Prettier wiring, but it is not a reliable developer tool.

  Current state:

  - `.prettierrc` and `.prettierignore` exist at the repo root, implying Prettier is part of the repo formatting policy.
  - The root `package.json` has no `format` or `format:check` script.
  - The root package has no direct Prettier dependency.
  - `frontend/package.json` also has no Prettier script or direct Prettier dependency.
  - CI still has `.github/workflows/prettier.yml`, but it runs Prettier through an ad hoc `npx --yes prettier@3` command instead of a checked-in script.
  - This means Prettier can fail PRs, but contributors do not have a stable local command that clearly matches CI.

  This leaves the repo in an awkward middle state: either Prettier should be treated as a first-class tool, or it should be removed entirely.

  Related narrower issue: #2280 covers generated-file rewrites from an older workflow shape. This issue is for deciding whether Prettier should exist as a
  supported repo tool at all.

  ## Decision Needed

  Pick one direction and make the repo consistent.

  ### Option A: Keep and fix Prettier

  - Add a direct Prettier devDependency in the package that owns the repo-level command, probably the root package.
  - Add documented scripts, for example:
    - `npm run format`
    - `npm run format:check`
  - Update `.github/workflows/prettier.yml` to call the same script developers run locally, or clearly document why CI differs.
  - Make `.prettierignore` cover all generated, vendor, scratch, and build-output paths that should never be formatted.
  - Add the command to the repo developer docs if it is part of the standard gate.

  ### Option B: Remove Prettier entirely

  - Delete `.prettierrc`.
  - Delete `.prettierignore`.
  - Delete `.github/workflows/prettier.yml`.
  - Remove any docs that imply Prettier is part of the toolchain.
  - Rely on existing formatters/checks instead:
    - `gofmt` / Go CI for backend
    - TypeScript typecheck/build for frontend
    - generator-owned output for generated files

  ## Acceptance Criteria

  - There is no partial Prettier setup left behind.
  - Contributors either have a stable local Prettier command that matches CI, or there is no Prettier CI/config at all.
  - Generated files and lockfiles are not formatter-owned unless explicitly intended.
  - The chosen policy is documented in the repo's developer instructions.


### Steps to reproduce

  1. Check the repo root formatting config:
     ```sh
     ls .prettierrc .prettierignore .github/workflows/prettier.yml

  2. Check the root package scripts:

     npm run

  3. Try to run an expected local formatter command:

     npm run format:check
     npm run format

  4. Check whether Prettier is a repo-owned dependency:

     npm ls prettier

  5. Compare that with CI:

     cat .github/workflows/prettier.yml


### Expected behavior

  If Prettier is part of the repo policy, contributors should have a stable local command that matches CI, for example:

  npm run format
  npm run format:check

  The repo should also own the Prettier version through a direct devDependency, and generated files / lockfiles  should be excluded deliberately.

  Alternatively, if Prettier is not intended to be part of the repo policy, all Prettier config and CI should be removed.


### Actual behavior

  The repo is in a partial state:

  - Prettier config exists.
  - Prettier CI exists.
  - CI can fail PRs for formatting.
  - There is no root local format or format:check command.
  - There is no direct root Prettier dependency.
  - CI downloads Prettier ad hoc with npx --yes prettier@3.
  - Contributors cannot reliably reproduce the CI check locally using a repo-owned command.


### AO version

  - AO CLI: ao version dev   - Repo checkout: 693692467   - Frontend package version: 0.10.3   - Legacy npm CLI package version: 0.10.0

### Environment

   - OS: Microsoft Windows 10.0.26200   - Arch: x64   - Go: go1.24.5 windows/amd64   - Node: v26.3.0   - npm: 11.16.0

### Logs / extra context

```shell

```

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: chore: remove partial prettier setup
body:
## What

Completely removes the partial and unpinned Prettier setup from the repository.

## Why

Fixes #3089.

The repository was in an awkward state with partial Prettier wiring (`.prettierrc`, `.prettierignore`, `.github/workflows/prettier.yml`). Prettier was running unpinned in CI via `npx --yes prettier@3`, without any root or frontend dependency, nor any standardized `format` script. Since the repo already relies on `gofmt` / Go CI for the backend and `tsc` for the frontend to do real enforcement, Prettier was only adding failure surface without owning an actual formatting guarantee. We opted for **Option B** (Remove Prettier entirely) to align with existing enforcement tools.

## How

Executed the agreed-upon plan and steps:
1. **Deleted configurations**: Removed `.prettierrc`, `.prettierignore`, and `.github/workflows/prettier.yml`.
2. **Swept documentation & code**: Scanned for Prettier references and removed lingering `// prettier-ignore` comments in `frontend/src/` (e.g., `preload.test.ts`, `new-session-shortcut.test.ts`, `preload.ts`, `shared/shortcuts.ts`).
3. **Confirmed dependencies**: Verified no npm scripts in `package.json` or `frontend/package.json` referenced Prettier.
4. **Committed cleanly**: Added all changes into a single PR with the conventional commit `chore: remove partial prettier setup`, strictly adhering to `AGENTS.md` PR hygiene.

## Testing

- Confirmed CI checks will run properly without Prettier gating.
- Verified local linting and frontend builds still work as expected.
- Searched codebase to guarantee no residual `prettier` references remained in core config/scripts.

## Checklist

- [✓] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [✓] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [✓] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense *(N/A: No behavior changed, simply removed a tool).*
- [✓] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: bug(storage): daemon fails to start on legacy TS-era DB — goose reports 4 missing migrations (dbMaxVersion=46 vs rewrite max 31)
body:
## Bug

The AO daemon fails to start with `Daemon exited with code 1`, showing:

```
open store: run migrations: error: found 4 missing migrations before current version 46:
    version 28: migrations/0028_allow_scratch_projects.sql
    version 29: migrations/0029_pr_reviews_body.sql
    version 30: migrations/0030_session_cleanup_facts.sql
    version 31: migrations/0031_notification_history_pagination.sql
```

**Reported by:** @Maaz (Discord #bug-triage), on **Windows 11**, build `v0.10.4-nightly.202407241408`. On his **Mac it starts fine** (fresh DB).

## Root cause

Error comes from goose v3.27.1 `Up()` -> `findMissingMigrations` (`up.go:206`). A migration is flagged "missing" if it exists in the embedded FS, is **not** in the DB `goose_db_version` applied set, and has a version **below** the DB recorded max (`dbMaxVersion`).

Critical fact: **the Go rewrite has never shipped a migration above version 31** (verified: `ls backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/` + full git history — no file `> 0031_*` ever existed). But this DB reports **`dbMaxVersion=46`**.

That database was created by the **old TypeScript implementation**, which used its own goose migration scheme numbering up to ~46, stored in the same `~/.ao/data/ao.db`. When the new Go/Electron rewrite opens that legacy DB:

- `dbMigrations` max = 46 (from old TS `goose_db_version`).
- Go migrations 28-31 exist in the embedded FS, are not in the legacy applied set, and are `< 46` -> all 4 flagged missing.
- `db.go:133` calls plain `goose.Up(db, "migrations")` with **no `allowMissing` option** -> goose hard-fails.

This is the legacy -> rewrite **schema incompatibility** the offline `ao migrate` tool (#2129, still OPEN) was designed to handle. But `ao migrate` is (a) not yet shipped and (b) an explicit offline step — a user who simply launches the new desktop app over an old TS-era install hits this cryptic error with no recovery path offered.

## Why Mac works

Mac = fresh install (no legacy `~/.ao/data/ao.db`), so goose creates schema clean from 0001-0031 with no version-46 row. Windows = user previously ran the TS-based AO, leaving a legacy DB.

## Impact

Blocks daemon startup for **any user upgrading from the old TypeScript AO to the new Go/Electron desktop app** whose `~/.ao` still holds a legacy `ao.db`. Not a channel-wide break (unlike #3037), but a real upgrade-path cliff — exactly the cohort we want migrating to the new app. P1.

## Repro

1. Have a leftover `~/.ao/data/ao.db` from the old TS implementation (one whose `goose_db_version` max >= 32).
2. Install + launch the current Go/Electron desktop nightly.
3. Daemon exits code 1 with the "4 missing migrations before current version 46" error.

## Immediate user workaround (until fix ships)

Back up and remove the legacy DB so the rewrite creates a fresh one:

```bash
# macOS / Linux
mv ~/.ao/data/ao.db ~/.ao/data/ao.db.legacy-backup
# Windows (PowerShell)
Move-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.ao\data\ao.db" "$env:USERPROFILE\.ao\data\ao.db.legacy-backup"
```

Then relaunch AO. WARNING: This discards any data still in the legacy DB. If that data matters, hold for `ao migrate` (#2129) rather than deleting.

## Fix direction (for discussion)

1. **Graceful detection:** Before/around `goose.Up`, detect a `goose_db_version` max that exceeds the highest embedded migration version and surface a clear, actionable error ("legacy database detected — run `ao migrate` or reset `~/.ao`") instead of the raw goose "missing migrations" dump.
2. **Ship #2129 (`ao migrate`)** as the supported legacy->rewrite path, and point the error at it.
3. Optionally consider `goose.Up(..., goose.WithAllowMissing())` — **but only after verifying the legacy schema is actually compatible**, since blindly applying Go 28-31 over a TS-shaped DB could corrupt it. Detection + guidance (option 1) is the safer near-term move.

## Related

- #2129 — offline `ao migrate` (legacy -> rewrite data porting) — the intended fix path, still open.
- #3036 / #3037 — the *different* "duplicate version 25" nightly crash (fixed via #3035). Not this bug — version-gap error, not a duplicate-version panic.

## Triage

- **Severity:** P1 — upgrade-path break for legacy-DB users, no in-app recovery.
- **Component:** `comp/daemon` (storage/migration layer) + `comp/desktop` (error surfaces in the app).
- **Not a duplicate** of #3036/#3037 — distinct error class and root cause.

title: fix(storage): apply missing out-of-order migrations
body:
## Summary

- allow Goose to apply embedded migrations that are missing below the database's recorded maximum version
- add a regression for a version-46 database missing migrations 28–31
- verify Windows-style project paths and existing project data survive the repair
- keep migration startup idempotent without modifying any shipped migration files

## Root cause

Goose's default `Up` behavior rejects any embedded migration whose version is absent from the database history but lower than the database's maximum recorded version. A database produced by builds with later or renumbered migrations can therefore reach version 46 without versions 28–31 and permanently wedge daemon startup before the HTTP server is available.

Using Goose's supported `WithAllowMissing` option applies those authoritative embedded migrations in order instead of rejecting the history.

## User impact

Affected Windows users can relaunch AO without moving, deleting, or resetting `~/.ao/data/ao.db`. Existing project records are preserved.

Fixes #3091.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/... -count=1`
- `go test -race ./internal/storage/sqlite/... -count=1`
- `go vet ./internal/storage/sqlite/...`
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`
- regression confirmed failing before the fix and passing afterward

The full `go test ./... -count=1` run reached two unrelated wall-clock-sensitive agent test failures under package-parallel load; both pass when rerun in isolation, and the SQLite packages remain green.

title: fix(web): key TopbarKillButton by session so its state resets on switch
body:
## Summary

When killing a worker session and then switching to a different worker while the kill mutation was still in flight, the **"Killing…"** confirmation-dialog state leaked onto the new session's kill button.

Root cause: the session route pattern stays the same across session switches (`/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId`), so React reused the same `TopbarKillButton` instance and only swapped its `session` prop, instead of unmounting/remounting a fresh one. `TopbarKillButton`'s local `confirmOpen` state and the `useTerminateSession` mutation state (`isPending`, `error`) are per-instance, not per-session, so they survived the swap: a still-pending kill (or a stale error) on session A would render against session B's button after navigating away.

Fixes #3071

## Fix

Add `key={session.id}` to `<TopbarKillButton>` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx`). Keying by the session id forces React to unmount the old instance and mount a fresh one whenever the active session changes, which resets `confirmOpen` and the mutation state for free — no manual reset effect needed.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `ShellTopbar.test.tsx` regression test (`"resets confirmation/pending state when switching to a different session mid-kill"`): arms and confirms a kill on session A with a never-resolving mutation (so it stays "pending"), then switches the route to session B and asserts B's button is back to a fresh "Kill session" state with no leftover dialog.
- [x] Verified the new test fails against the pre-fix code (reproduces the exact leaked "Killing..." state) and passes with the fix.
- [x] `npx vitest run` on `ShellTopbar.test.tsx` — all 21 tests pass
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean

title: fix: keep the notification bell at the right end of the topbar on all platforms
body: ## Problem The notification bell's position was platform-dependent: - On **Windows/Linux** it rendered as the last item of the topbar actions row (far right). - On **macOS** a dedicated branch in `ShellTopbar` rendered it *leading* the actions row — before Kill / Orchestrator — and in the `SessionsBoard` in-panel action row it also sat *before* the New task / Orchestrator buttons. So the same button moved around depending on which machine you opened the app on. ## Changes - **`ShellTopbar.tsx`** — remove the macOS-only leading render (`boardActionsInPanel && !isLinux && !isWindows`) and always render the bell as the trailing item of the actions row, on every platform. (Also drops the now-unused `isLinux`/`isWindows` locals.) - **`SessionsBoard.tsx`** — in the macOS in-panel board action row, move the bell after the New task / Orchestrator buttons so it trails there too. - **`NotificationCenter.tsx`** — small UX polish while touching the bell: the unread state now swaps the plain `Bell` for lucide's `BellRing` (with the existing fill + count badge), so unread notifications are distinguishable at a glance instead of only by fill color. After this, wherever the bell exists it is always the right-most element of the top action row — session routes, board routes, on Windows, Linux, and macOS alike. Screens without shell chrome (settings, first-launch welcome board) intentionally have no bell on any platform, unchanged. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` — clean - `vitest`: `ShellTopbar.test.tsx`, `SessionsBoard.test.tsx`, `NotificationCenter.test.tsx`, `Sidebar.test.tsx` — 92 tests passing - Verified live in the dev app on Windows: bell stays at the far right of the topbar on board and session routes; unread simulation (row inserted into the dev DB, cleaned up afterwards) shows the BellRing + badge state

title: feat(desktop): add platform-native terminal line-boundary shortcuts
body:
## What

Add platform-native line-boundary shortcuts to the terminal input handler. Cmd+Left/Cmd+Right on macOS and Home/End on Windows now move the cursor to the start/end of the current input line.

## Why

Fixes #3093. These chords are standard text-editing gestures on their respective platforms but were silently ignored -normalizedTerminalShortcut returned null for any metaKey event, and Home/End had no handler.

## How

- isMacPlatform and isWindowsPlatform imported from the existing ../lib/platform module,  no new helpers added.
- Cmd+Left/Right handled only when isMacPlatform() is true, so the Windows key (metaKey on Windows) is not mistakenly treated as Command.
- Both shortcuts emit readline control bytes: \x01 (Ctrl+A, line start) and \x05 (Ctrl+E, line end).
- Ctrl+Left/Right word-navigation and Option+Left/Right word-navigation are untouched.

## Testing
