Only an assigned contributor can work on this issue. Please do not open a PR for this unless you are explicitly assigned.

title: No cross-session merge-conflict coordination — overlapping PRs cause cascading rebase churn
body:
---

Problem

When multiple worker sessions open PRs that touch the same lines in the same repo (all targeting main), AO detects merge conflicts on each independently and nudges all affected workers simultaneously to rebase and resolve. There is no global ordering or serialization of conflict resolution across sessions.

After one worker's PR merges, main shifts, invalidating the conflict resolutions performed by the other workers. Those workers are then re-detected as conflicting and nudged again. This creates a wasteful cycle:

All PRs ready
→ Merge one
→ Remaining PRs conflict
→ Multiple workers resolve conflicts simultaneously
→ Merge one resolved PR
→ Remaining PRs conflict again
→ repeat


Root cause

The lifecycle manager's world model is per-session. The only conflict-suppression mechanism — prBlockedByOpenParent (reactions.go:309) — checks whether a PR is stacked behind an open parent via ListPRsBySession, which is scoped to a single session ID. When three workers from three different sessions each open independent PRs against main, none are considered "stacked," so none get suppressed. The sendOnce dedup (reactions.go:752) is keyed per-PR and only prevents duplicate nudges for the same PR — it has no cross-PR awareness.

There is no per-repo view of "all open PRs targeting the same base branch," no conflict arbitration to designate one PR as active while holding the rest, and no sequential re-evaluation after a merge shifts main.

Traced code path

| Step | Code location | Behavior |
|------|--------------|----------|
| Observer polls all sessions | observe/scm/observer.go:250 Poll() | Iterates all sessions, dispatches per-PR independently | (1/3)
| Conflict detected per PR | lifecycle/reactions.go:214 | if o.Mergeability == domain.MergeConflicting |
| Stack suppression check | lifecycle/reactions.go:220 → prBlockedByOpenParent | Calls ListPRsBySession(sessionID) — same-session only |
| Rebase nudge queued | lifecycle/reactions.go:225-229 | Message: "Rebase onto the base branch and resolve them" |
| Dedup | lifecycle/reactions.go:752 sendOnce | Keyed "merge-conflict:<prURL>", sig = enum string — no base SHA encoding |
| Post-merge re-evaluation | (none) | No re-sequencing of remaining conflicting PRs |

Impact

Wasted agent compute — multiple workers rebasing against main simultaneously, knowing only one can merge and the rest will re-conflict.
Increased wall-clock time — the cycle length is O(N) merge rounds for N overlapping PRs, where O(1) rounds would suffice with serialization.
Potential for repeated merge-conflict dispatch storms on repos with high PR throughput targeting the same files.

Proposed direction

The existing stack-suppression pattern in service/session/stack.go (buildStacks) and reactions.go:304-326 (prBlockedByOpenParent) is the right template — it already implements "don't nudge a PR that isn't ready to act." The gap is its visibility boundary (one session). Extending it requires:

Cross-session PR query — a store method like ListOpenPRsByRepoAndBaseBranch(repo, baseBranch) to see all sibling PRs across all sessions targeting the same base.
Conflict arbitration — when N PRs conflict against the same base, designate one as "active for resolution" and suppress rebased nudges to the rest (same !blocked gate, broader view).
Sequential re-evaluation — after the active PR merges and main shifts, re-evaluate the queue and promote the next conflicting PR.

Environment

Component: comp/daemon (lifecycle layer) (2/3)
Code path: backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go → ApplyPRObservation → prBlockedByOpenParent
Relevant files: backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go, backend/internal/service/session/stack.go, backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go
Labels: bug, comp/daemon, P1 (3/3)

title: fix(agy): honor cfg.Config.Model via --model flag on launch/restore
body:
## What
Forwards the per-role model override (`cfg.Config.Model`) to the `agy` (Antigravity) CLI as a `--model` flag on both session launch and session restore, and declares a `GetConfigSpec` entry for it.

## Why
Fixes #2901.

AO resolves a per-role model and forwards it to every adapter as `cfg.Config.Model`, but each adapter has to opt in to actually passing it to its CLI. The `agy` adapter never did, so a configured worker/orchestrator silently fell back to agy's default model instead of the one set in `agentConfig.model`.

## How
- Verified via `agy --help` that a launch-time flag exists (`--model  Model for the current CLI session`) — this was previously unconfirmed per the issue, so it settles the "does agy even support this" question in favor of applying the mechanical fix.
- Mirrors the pattern from the Codex adapter fix (#2869): an `appendModelFlag(cmd *[]string, cfg ports.AgentConfig)` helper that appends `--model <trimmed value>` only when set, called from both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`.
- Added `GetConfigSpec` (previously inherited empty from `agentbase.Base`), declaring the `model` field with the same shape used by the Codex/Copilot adapters, so the config layer/UI know this adapter now supports a model override.
- Intentional omission worth flagging: unlike the Copilot adapter (#2895), which deliberately does *not* forward `--model` on restore pending verification of `--model` + `--resume` composition, this PR forwards on both launch **and** restore. I found no equivalent warning for `agy` in `--help` or available docs, so I didn't add the same restriction — but a reviewer with a real `agy` install should sanity-check this.

## Testing
```
go build ./...
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/...
golangci-lint run ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/...
```
All pass, 0 lint issues. Covered:
- `TestGetLaunchCommand` — model set, flag appears in the right position.
- `TestGetLaunchCommandNoModel` — model unset, flag omitted entirely.
- `TestGetRestoreCommand` — model set, flag appears alongside `--conversation`.
- `TestGetConfigSpecReportsModelField` — config spec reports the `model` field.

Not yet verified locally: an actual `agy --model <x> --print "..."` run against a real `agy` binary, to confirm the flag changes model selection at runtime rather than just being accepted without erroring.

## Checklist
- [x] Branched from `main` (`fix/agy-model-override`)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue (#2901)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) — pending CI run after push

title: feat(board): agent mark registry, one card system, and lane/archive chrome
body:
Re-lands #3169 (merged then reverted in #3172) and grows well past it. Preview with `npm run dev:web`, toggle light/dark.

Five things, all on the board.

## Agent marks come from a registry

Single-colour brands vanished against one theme. The first pass fixed that by inlining each brand's SVG path as a string in `AgentAvatar` — 76 lines of path data, and the `.svg` files on disk were only half the truth.

`lib/agent-logos.ts` is now the single source: one entry per harness, pointing at the asset and saying how it has to be painted. `AgentAvatar` only renders. Adding a harness is one line in one file.

- **No background plates.** A logo on its own brand-coloured tile fights every surface it lands on, so the plate is stripped from the asset rather than hidden with CSS. `codex` keeps its gradient with the white plate path removed; `aider`, `droid` and `continue` are cleaned in place.
- **Theme-adaptive.** Single-colour marks are drawn as a mask filled with `currentColor`, so one asset stays legible on both boards instead of disappearing into one.
- Plated rasters are replaced with the upstream vectors the existing `codex` and `cursor` marks already came from — no new dependency, the files are vendored.
- `crush` deliberately keeps its background: it's an illustration whose trail bleeds off-frame, not a mark on a plate, so there's nothing to strip without a proper vector.

## Live and archived sessions share one card

The archive drew its own card — status and time on a top row, agent under the title, a different divider inset. Sitting right under the lanes, it read as a different product rather than the same board in a quieter state.

Archived sessions now use the live card's shape. Two things the live card doesn't need are kept: the **status**, because no column header names the stage down there, and **restore**, moved to the corner the live card puts Terminate in.

Task cards gain the copy button the archive already had, and name their agent in the meta row when there's no PR, diff or issue — that row was otherwise empty but for a timestamp across the whole Working lane.

## Lanes stop reserving space they aren't using

`flex-[3]`/`flex-[2]` gave the upper lane 60% of the column whatever it held, so three idle cards left a gap before the Working heading. Lanes are now content-sized under one shared scroller.

The heading also said things twice — it named both halves while the section below repeated one of them, and named an Idle lane even when nothing was idle. It now names only the lane the column starts with.

## Headings read as headings

They looked like another card footer: 10.5px, no separation from the stack under them. Now a band of their own — tint, bottom border, a colour bar in the status hue — with the title at 12px semibold and the count in a chip.

## Archive is capped and resizable

It opened at every session it held and pushed the lanes off screen. Now it opens at ~2 rows and scrolls, with a drag handle on its top edge (pointer and keyboard, persisted). Its grid is pinned `content-start`, because a grid stretches its rows to fill the container by default, which inflated every card as the panel grew instead of leaving the new room empty.

Board scrollbars were invisible: `--color-scrollbar` is `0.12` alpha and shared with the diff/file scrollbars, and `color-mix` with transparent can only *lower* alpha — no percentage could brighten it. The lanes get their own token pair; other scrollbars are untouched.

## Also

- Per-card status pill dropped entirely (author design call), with the status kept in each card's accessible name for screen readers.
- Diff size derives from the PR summaries populated by the SCM API, not the mock-only `session.changedFiles`, so it renders in the packaged app.
- Sidebar search field radius matched to the cards; label uses a new `--font-size-nano` token rather than a hardcoded value.

## Merged with main

Takes main's **grid-only archive** (#3211) — the rows/grid toggle is gone, so the unified card, height cap and drag handle all apply to the grid alone. Keeps main's orchestrator activity indicator (#3200) and daemon startup loader (#3205).

## Checks

34 files, +662/−279. Typecheck clean, **1189 unit tests pass, zero failures**. CI green: `test`, `renderer-smoke`, `scan`.

Test assertions that encoded the old layout (`flex-[3]`, dot classes, `0 working sessions`) were rewritten to the new contract rather than deleted.

title: Daemon dies of SIGPIPE when the supervisor's stdout pipe closes, leaving a stale running.json
body:
## Bug

When the Electron supervisor goes away (Ctrl-C on `ao start --source` / `npm run dev`, or any hard Electron exit), the daemon's stdout/stderr pipe loses its reader. The next log line the daemon writes gets `EPIPE`, and because Go terminates on `SIGPIPE` for fds 1 and 2 unless a handler is registered, the daemon dies **before** it can run its graceful shutdown. `running.json` is left behind pointing at a dead PID.

The daemon does exit, so this reads as "shutdown worked" — but it exited by signal, not by shutting down.

**Source:** found while verifying the daemon process-tree change for the fork's [xuelongmu/agent-orchestrator#231](https://github.com/xuelongmu/agent-orchestrator/pull/231) | **Analyzed against:** `823c29d2` (`main`)
**Confidence:** High — reproduced in isolation with the exact exit signal.
**Priority:** medium — the daemon still exits and the next start overwrites the run file; the cost is a stale handshake that makes `ao status` and CLI commands aim at a dead daemon until then.

## Reproduction

Isolated repro that removes Electron from the picture entirely — a daemon whose stdout is a pipe, a reader that goes away, then one log-producing request:

```bash
cd backend && go build -o /tmp/ao ./cmd/ao
mkfifo /tmp/aoprobe.pipe
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/aoprobe/data AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/aoprobe/running.json AO_PORT=3099 \
  /tmp/ao daemon > /tmp/aoprobe.pipe 2>&1 &
DAEMON=$!
exec 3< /tmp/aoprobe.pipe
head -c 120 <&3 > /dev/null   # consume startup lines
exec 3<&-                     # reader gone
curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3099/healthz   # forces an "http request" log line
wait $DAEMON; echo "exit=$?"
```

Observed:

```
daemon exit status: 141   (128+13 = SIGPIPE)
run file after exit: STILL PRESENT
```

Same outcome through the real path on macOS: `ISOLATE_DEV=true ao start --source`, then Ctrl-C. The daemon's log ends mid-stream with no shutdown lines, and `~/.ao/dev/running.json` survives.

## Root Cause

- `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:291` — `newLogger()` writes to `os.Stderr`, which is a pipe to Electron for every app-spawned daemon.
- `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:87` — `signal.NotifyContext(..., syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)` covers the graceful signals but not `SIGPIPE`.

Per `os/signal`: SIGPIPE is ignored for other fds, but a write to fd 1 or 2 that returns `EPIPE` raises SIGPIPE and takes the default action — terminate — unless the program registered for it via `signal.Notify`. So the first log line after Electron exits kills the daemon, skipping the graceful path that removes `running.json`.

Note the daemon *has* a correct teardown path for exactly this situation: the supervisor socket drops and it self-stops within `DefaultShutdownTimeout`. SIGPIPE just beats it to the punch.

## Fix

Register a discarding SIGPIPE handler on POSIX before serving, so a broken stdout/stderr surfaces as a write error instead of killing the process:

```go
// SIGPIPE on fd 1/2 terminates a Go program by default. The daemon's stderr is a
// pipe to whichever supervisor spawned it; when that supervisor exits, the next
// log line must not kill us before the graceful shutdown runs.
signal.Notify(make(chan os.Signal, 1), syscall.SIGPIPE)
```

Worth pairing with a test that asserts the daemon removes its run file when its stdout reader disappears.

## Impact

- Stale `running.json` after Ctrl-C, so `ao status` and CLI commands target a dead PID/port until something rewrites it.
- Shutdown work the daemon would otherwise do on the graceful path is skipped.
- Masks the real shutdown story in testing: a daemon that "exits promptly" looks correct while actually dying by signal. This is what made the Windows daemon-lifecycle verification ambiguous.

## Related
- [#2242](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2242): Electron keeps stale project actions enabled after daemon exit (same stale-state-after-exit surface).

title: fix(landing): keep the mobile app preview's proportions on small screens
body:
## Problem

The phone in `MobileAppDemo` (the "Your fleet goes where you go" feature row) is sized responsively, but its contents are absolute:

```
h-[280px] sm:h-[360px] lg:h-[390px] + aspect-[0.48]   → frame is 134px → 187px wide
text-[5px], h-7 status bar, h-11 tab bar, size-3 icons → always 100%
```

Those interior sizes were tuned for the 187px desktop frame. On mobile the frame is **72% as wide** while the UI still renders full size, so it overflows the screen: the `mergeable` stat is clipped by the bezel, `need you` wraps to two lines, the project chips are cut mid-word, only one session card fits, and the FAB sits on top of it. The fixed 28px + 44px chrome also eats 26% of a 280px phone versus 18% of a 390px one.

## Fix

Render the phone at one design size (187×390) on every breakpoint and scale the whole frame into its slot, so the interior keeps its proportions instead of overflowing:

```tsx
<div className="shrink-0 origin-center scale-[0.718] sm:scale-[0.923] lg:scale-100"
     style={{ width: PHONE_WIDTH, height: PHONE_HEIGHT }}>
```

The factors are just slot height ÷ 390 (280/390, 360/390), so the mock is pixel-identical at every width, only smaller. The section's footprint is unchanged.

## Verification

Dev server at 390×844 and 1440×900.

- **Before, 390px:** `mergeable` clipped, `need you` wrapped, chips cut at "me…", 1 card visible, FAB overlapping it.
- **After, 390px:** all three stats fit, chips read through to `adorable`, both cards visible, FAB clear.
- **1440px:** unchanged, diffed against a pre-change capture.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` green across all routes.

## Note

At mobile the phone now renders at 0.718 scale, so the 5px UI labels land near 3.6px — legible as texture, not as text. That was already true before, just clipped rather than scaled. If we want the mock to read better on a phone, the lever is now the frame's mobile height (`h-[280px]`), which scales the whole thing proportionally instead of breaking it. Left alone here to keep the section's footprint identical.

title: fix(terminal): write the initial replay as one chunk behind a cover
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3160 — opening a session showed a mid-session position and then visibly scrolled down to the tail.

The daemon pumps a pane's attach replay in 32KB reads (`attachment.go:182` `copyOut`), so the renderer receives N WebSocket frames and issues N `terminal.write()` calls. xterm parses each write atomically, but the browser paints **between** event-loop turns — so every frame boundary is a painted, further-scrolled state.

### Correction to the issue's stated root cause

The issue attributes this to xterm splitting large writes into ~15KB internal batches. It doesn't do that. In `@xterm/xterm@5.5.0`'s `src/common/input/WriteBuffer.ts`, `_writeBuffer` holds **one entry per `write()` call** and `_innerWrite` parses a whole entry atomically; `WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS = 12` is only checked *after* an entry finishes, to decide whether to yield before the next. There is no size-based splitting.

**The batch granularity is the caller's `write()` calls — i.e. our WS frames.** That distinction is what makes the fix below work.

### Measured

Real xterm 5.5.0 in real Chromium, sampling `buffer.active.viewportY` on every animation frame. Distinct consecutive values = scroll positions actually painted.

```
payload   98,528 bytes (1000 lines)   grid 200×50

  delivery              writes  frames  positions   ingest  max block
  32KB chunks, 0ms gap       4       8          1    129ms      0.1ms
  8KB chunks, 4ms gap       13      12          5    200ms      0.1ms
  4KB chunks, 8ms gap       25      22         15    367ms      0.1ms
  4KB chunks, 16ms gap      25      33         25    550ms      0.1ms
  one concatenated write     1       8          1    133ms      2.2ms
```

Severity is `frame count × inter-frame gap` and nothing else. One `write()` of 98KB painted exactly **1** position — if xterm split at ~15KB it would have painted ~7.

## Fix

Buffer the initial burst, write it once, keep the pane covered until that write is parsed.

- **`XtermTerminal.tsx`** — forward xterm's write callback, which was being dropped (`write: (data) => term.write(data)`). It fires when the chunk is parsed, giving a deterministic reveal point instead of a timer guess.
- **`useTerminalSession.ts`** — the gate opens in `connect()`, **not** on `opened`: the daemon fires `onOpen` from `setPTY` and only then starts `copyOut`, so `attached` precedes the first replay byte and gating on it would uncover a pane that hasn't drawn. A 60ms quiet window ends the burst; a 750ms cap bounds the cover and still flushes as one chunk, so the worst case degrades to a single jump rather than back to the walk. Exposes `replaySettled`.
- **`TerminalPane.tsx`** — blank terminal-coloured cover while buffering, label delayed 120ms so fast opens never flash a loader. Deliberately *not* the existing empty-state card, which would flash "Starting session" on every session switch.
- **Resize re-assert held while a burst is in flight** — the backend answers every resize frame with an explicit SIGWINCH, and that repaint would otherwise land ~250ms later, just after the cover lifts. Held, never dropped: losing it leaves the pane laid out for the old grid until the next real change.

Frontend only. No backend or protocol change, and no overlap with #3105 (all backend).

## Test plan

- `npm test` — **1107 tests / 87 files pass**
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `go build ./...`, `go test ./internal/terminal/...` — clean (toolchain bumped to Go 1.26.5 to build the daemon)
- 12 new tests: single-write flush, live passthrough after the gate closes, empty replay, cap behaviour, exit/error mid-replay, reattach re-arming, re-assert deferral, superseded-connection frames

## ⚠️ Known gap — please read before sizing this

I captured **real tmux attach replays** off a live daemon and replayed them through real xterm. They paint **1 position even without this change**:

| capture | bytes | frames | span | positions as-is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sparse screen | 1,385 | 4 | 0.3ms | 1 |
| dense colored screen | 21,083 | 23 | 1.2ms | 1 |

Structural reason: `tmux attach-session` replays only the **visible screen**, bounded by rows×cols — it never dumps scrollback. So on macOS/Linux the burst is small and lands inside a single animation frame.

The severe case is the **Windows/conpty** path, where `Ring.Snapshot()` (`conpty/ring.go:11`, `MaxOutputLines = 1000`) genuinely returns 1000 lines as one burst.

Still unmeasured:
- an **agent session** TUI attach (I used a shell terminal — same tmux path, but an agent's screen is denser and it repaints on SIGWINCH)
- the **conpty** path end to end
- behaviour under a loaded renderer

So this change is correct and cheap, but whether it's user-visible on macOS is unconfirmed. Happy to hold for an agent-session capture if reviewers would rather size it first.

## Notes

- Frontend comments throughout still say `zellij attach`; the adapters are `tmux`/`conpty`/`ptyexec`. Left alone here to keep the diff scoped.
- One pre-existing `Viewport.syncScrollArea` → `dimensions` error appears once at app startup. `XtermTerminal.tsx`'s own header documents it ("Writing before layout settles is what crashed xterm's Viewport"). It didn't recur across reloads, and this change strictly *delays* the first buffer write — but I couldn't get a clean baseline A/B, so I'm flagging rather than claiming.

title: fix(landing): keep the mobile preview's controls above the 24px target minimum
body:
Follow-up to #3184, from reviewing it.

## Problem

#3184 fixed the phone mock's proportions by rendering it at a fixed 187×390 design size and scaling the frame into its slot. That was right, but the scale applies to the controls too, and the mock is deliberately tappable (#3174 "make mobile preview interactive").

At the base breakpoint the slot was 280px tall, so scale was `280/390 = 0.718`:

| control | class | before #3184 | after #3184 | now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FAB | `size-7` (28px) | 28px ✅ | **20.1px ❌** | **24.1px ✅** |
| "Open conversation" CTA | `min-h-8` (32px) | 32px ✅ | **23.0px ❌** | 27.5px ✅ |
| bottom tabs | `min-h-10` (40px) | 40px ✅ | 28.7px ✅ | 34.4px ✅ |
| session cards | `min-h-11` (44px) | 44px ✅ | 31.6px ✅ | 37.8px ✅ |
| project chips | `min-h-5` (20px) | 20px ❌ | 14.4px ❌ | 17.2px ❌ |

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) wants 24×24 CSS px. Two controls regressed from passing to failing.

## Fix

Raise the base slot from `h-[280px]` to `h-[335px]`, which moves the scale to `0.859` and puts the smallest control (the 28px FAB) at 24.1px. One breakpoint changes; `sm` and `lg` are untouched.

335 isn't arbitrary: it's the smallest slot height where `28 × (h/390) ≥ 24`.

## Verification

Measured live in the browser at 390×844:

```
painted frame  161 × 335
FAB            24.1px
tabs / cards   46.4px
chips          17.2px   (pre-existing, see below)
horizontal overflow: none
```

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` green.

Side benefit: the 5px UI labels go from 3.6px to 4.3px, so the mock reads as a UI rather than as texture. Cost is 55px of extra section height on mobile.

## Left alone deliberately

- **Project chips (17.2px)** — `min-h-5` was already 20px and under the minimum before #3184. Raising them to clear 24px means `min-h-7`, which changes the mock's visual density. Separate call, not a regression fix.
- **~12 focusable buttons in a decorative preview** — the chips, cards, tabs and FAB are real `<button>`s with no `aria-hidden`, so keyboard users tab through a marketing mock. Pre-existing from #3174. Worth a follow-up.

title: fix: use wait-based conpty pid liveness
body:
## Summary
- make the Windows ptyregistry PID probe delegate to processalive.Alive so exited process handles are checked with WaitForSingleObject
- add Windows-only regression tests for processalive.Alive, conpty.pidAlive, and ptyregistry.defaultPidAlive against exited-but-unreaped processes

## Root cause
The ptyregistry Windows liveness probe used OpenProcess success as proof that a process was still running. On Windows, a terminated process object can remain openable while handles still exist, so the probe could preserve dead pty-host entries.

Fixes #3080.

## Validation
- go test ./internal/processalive ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/ptyregistry
- GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c -o /tmp/processalive.test.exe ./internal/processalive
- GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c -o /tmp/conpty.test.exe ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty
- GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c -o /tmp/ptyregistry.test.exe ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/ptyregistry
- git diff --check

title: fix: ignore daemon sigpipe on closed output
body:
## Summary
- Register a POSIX SIGPIPE handler during daemon startup so closed stdout/stderr pipes return write errors instead of terminating the daemon.
- Keep Windows as an explicit no-op for the platform helper.
- Add regressions for closed stderr survival and the real daemon closed-output plus supervisor-disconnect path that removes `running.json`.

## Root Cause
When Electron or a dev supervisor exits, the daemon can inherit stdout/stderr pipes with no reader. A later log write to fd 1/2 can raise SIGPIPE and terminate the Go process before `httpd.Server.Run` reaches its deferred `running.json` cleanup.

Fixes #3182.

## Tests

- `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli -run TestE2E_DaemonClosedOutputPipeShutdownRemovesRunFile -count=1 -v`

title: fix(sidebar): color session dots from the board's attention zones
body:
Fixes #3099

## Summary

Sidebar session dots rendered idle gray for any session whose agent wasn't actively running — even when its board card sat in **In Review** (blue) or **Ready to Merge** (green). `getSessionDotView` colored the dot from raw agent activity (`idle` → gray) and only consulted PR/status context while the agent was `active`, so the sidebar and board disagreed for the same session.

The dot now derives its color from `attentionZone(session.status)` — the exact mapping the board columns use — so both surfaces read from the same status source and render the same color:

- **Needs you / In review / Ready to merge** zones → the zone's dot color (`bg-status-needs-you` / `bg-status-in-review` / `bg-status-ready`), regardless of agent activity.
- **Merged** keeps the board's merged-lane tone (`bg-status-merged`), mirroring the board's split Merge lane.
- **Working zone** (no PR/attention signal) keeps the existing activity tones — idle gray, waiting/blocked needs-you, active teal — mirroring the board's split Idle/Working lane.
- Activity still controls motion: an actively-running agent pulses in every zone.

Also updated the stale `SessionDot` comment in `Sidebar.tsx` to describe the new semantics.

## Tests

- Rewrote the two tests that enshrined the regression (idle + draft → gray) and added table-driven coverage asserting the sidebar dot class equals the board zone's `dotClassName` for every attention-zone status, plus pulse/no-pulse and missing-activity cases (`session-presentation.test.ts`, `Sidebar.test.tsx`).
- `npm run typecheck` clean; full frontend suite passes (89 files, 1159 tests).

## Risks / notes

- `getSessionDotView` now requires `status` in its `Pick`; its only caller (Sidebar) already passes the full session.
- Sessions whose daemon-derived `status` is `exited`/`no_signal`/`unknown` now show the needs-you tone (their board column color) instead of exited/unknown grays — that is the intended attention-zone alignment.

title: fix(notifications): use project name in titles and sync OS badge count
body:
Fixes #3033.

## Summary

This PR addresses the two notification bugs reported in #3033:

1. **Notification titles included the session instance number** (e.g. `portfolio-10 needs input`). `sessionLabel()` in `backend/internal/notify/enrich.go` now falls back to `ProjectID` before `SessionID`, so the default title uses the clean project name while still respecting a user-set display name.

2. **The notification badge counter did not reset/read correctly across app restarts**. Added an OS-level badge that tracks the unread notification count, persists it next to `running.json`, restores it on launch, and updates it whenever the unread count changes (including on mark-read).

## Changes

- `backend/internal/notify/enrich.go`: prefer `ProjectID` over `SessionID` for the session label fallback.
- `backend/internal/notify/enrich_test.go`: tests for the new fallback behavior and title composition.
- `frontend/src/main/notification-badge.ts`: new module for setting the OS badge (`app.setBadgeCount` on macOS/Linux, `setOverlayIcon` on Windows) and persisting the count.
- `frontend/src/main/notification-badge.test.ts`: unit tests for persistence and platform-specific badge behavior.
- `frontend/src/main.ts`: restore badge count on startup and handle the `notifications:setBadgeCount` IPC.
- `frontend/src/preload.ts` + `bridge.ts`: expose `notifications.setBadgeCount` to the renderer.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NotificationCenter.tsx`: sync the badge count with the unread notification count.
- Tests updated for the new bridge shape in `NotificationCenter.test.tsx`, `SessionsBoard.test.tsx`, `shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx`, `preload.test.tsx`, and `setup.ts`.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go test ./internal/notify/... ./internal/service/notification/...` ✅ pass
- `cd backend && go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs internal/notify/...` ✅ pass
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` ✅ pass
- `cd frontend && npm run test` ✅ 1159 passed (one unrelated flaky run observed; passed on re-run)

## Known limitations

- The session instance counter in the durable session ID namespace is left unchanged. The issue notes this is by design; this PR only removes the instance number from notification titles and adds a separate notification badge counter.
- The backend CLI test suite has pre-existing failures (`internal/cli` spawn tests return HTTP 404) unrelated to these changes.

title: fix(landing): fix the design-partners roadmap accordion on mobile
body:
## Problems

Three defects in the `/design-partners` roadmap accordion (`RoadmapSlideshow.tsx`):

1. **The `−` control did nothing.** `onClick` only ever called `setActiveIndex(index)`, so clicking the open row re-set the same index. `+` opened a phase; nothing closed it.
2. **Dead space under the expanded phase (mobile).** The panel had a hard-coded height, `h-[26rem]` at mobile and `sm:h-[20rem]`. Shorter phases left roughly 300px of empty black below the last bullet; a longer phase would have clipped against the `overflow-hidden` wrapper.
3. **Content flush against the card border (mobile).** The row button was `px-0` until `lg`, so at 390px the card border sat at `x=16` and its content started at `x=17`. The `00`/`01` numbers and the `+`/`−` icons were jammed into the card's 12px rounded corner, reading as clipped.

## Fixes

**Toggle.** The image column reads `phases[activeIndex]`, so simply making the active index nullable would blank the illustration. Split the two concerns:

```ts
const [openIndex, setOpenIndex] = useState<number | null>(0); // drives the accordion
const [imageIndex, setImageIndex] = useState(0);              // drives the illustration

const togglePhase = (index: number) => {
  setImageIndex(index);
  setOpenIndex((current) => (current === index ? null : index));
};
```

Closing a row leaves the illustration on the phase you last touched.

The panel also moved out of the `<button>`. With a working toggle, a click on the body text would otherwise collapse the panel, and text selection inside a button is awkward. Outside the button it can use block elements instead of the `span` + `className="block"` workaround that phrasing-content rules forced.

**Mobile layout.** The panel sizes to its content below `lg`; `lg:h-[17rem]` stays, since at `lg` the accordion sits beside a fixed-height image column and wants a stable height. The row button gets `px-4` on mobile. The panel's padding now stands on its own instead of composing with the button's: `pl-14` / `lg:pl-16` keeps body text under the title, and `pb-5` replaces the bottom padding the button used to supply.

## Verification

Playwright against a local `next dev` build, at 390×844 and 1440×900. Both widths pass all six checks:

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Initial state | phase 00 open |
| Click the open row | collapses, `aria-expanded=false`, panel removed |
| Click it again | re-opens |
| Click the panel body text | stays open |
| Click a different row | previous closes, new one opens, illustration switches |
| Close every row | illustration persists on the last-touched phase |

Alignment measured live: title at `x=73` mobile and the panel body at `17 + pl-14(56) = 73`; desktop `145` vs `81 + pl-16(64) = 145`. Phase numbers now sit 16px inside the card border (were 1px). Desktop panel geometry is unchanged: previously `pt-5` inside a 17rem box plus the button's 20px below, now the button's 20px above plus a 17rem box containing `pb-5` — 292px either way.

`npm run frontend:typecheck` passes.

## Note

One deliberate behavior change: every phase can now be collapsed at once. At `lg` that leaves an empty band under the last row, because the image column's `min-h-[38rem]` sets the grid height. Standard accordion behavior, and the illustration stays put, but say the word if you would rather the desktop layout always keep one phase open.

No tests added — the landing app has no test harness, and this is one presentational client component. Behavior was verified with the Playwright matrix above.

title: feat: add Windows source installer
body:
## Summary

- add a native PowerShell installer for Windows source checkouts
- build and install the current checkout by default, with fetching gated behind `-Fetch`
- optionally install frontend dependencies or start the source desktop harness
- preserve PATH ordering and verify that `ao` resolves to the installed binary

## Why

The existing `scripts/daemon-build.sh` flow assumes Bash and does not provide a native Windows install path. Windows also cannot replace a running `ao.exe`, so rebuilding from source required several manual stop, build, copy, PATH, and verification steps.

This installer makes that workflow repeatable without fetching unexpectedly. It gracefully stops a running daemon before replacing the executable, installs to `~/.local/bin` by default, avoids duplicate PATH entries, and fails if the resulting `ao` resolution is not the source-built binary.

## User impact

Windows contributors can now run:

```powershell
& .\scripts\install.ps1
```

They can opt into updating `main` with `-Fetch`, reinstall dependencies with `-InstallDependencies`, or immediately launch the source harness with `-Start`.

## Validation

- parsed `scripts/install.ps1` with the PowerShell AST parser
- `go -C backend build ./...`
- `git diff --check`
- ran `& .\scripts\install.ps1` end-to-end on Windows with a live daemon and restored PTY hosts
- ran `& .\scripts\install.ps1 -Start` through dependency repair and Electron source launch
- verified `ao` resolves to `~/.local/bin/ao.exe`, reports the source `dev` version, and the source app starts a ready daemon from that path on port 3001

title: Diff viewer shows 0 changes when session branch has committed work (compares vs HEAD instead of merge-base)
body:
## Problem

When an agent creates a PR from a session branch, its changes are committed to the branch. The desktop diff viewer shows **0 files changed** / empty diffs for these committed changes.

## Root cause

All three git operations that power the workspace diff viewer compare against **`HEAD`** (the current commit), not the branch's merge base:

| File | Line | Command | Problem |
|------|------|---------|---------|
| `backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go` | 412 | `git status --porcelain` | Compares working tree vs HEAD → clean working tree = no files shown |
| same | 449 | `git diff --numstat HEAD` | Uncommitted changes only → committed changes invisible |
| same | 507 | `git diff --no-ext-diff --unified=3 HEAD` | Same — only uncommitted diff |

Once the agent commits and the working tree is clean, **everything resolves to "unmodified" against HEAD**, so the file list, numstat counts, and per-file diffs all come back empty.

## Expected behavior

The diff viewer should show the **full diff from the merge base** — the point where the session branch diverged from its upstream/base branch (typically `main`). This is the same view GitHub shows on a PR diff tab.

## Suggested approach

1. **Resolve the base ref** for the session branch. Options:
   - The upstream tracking branch (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream}`)
   - The PR base branch (if known from session/PR metadata)
   - Fall back to `origin/main` or a configured default branch
2. **Compute the merge base**: `git merge-base HEAD <base-ref>`
3. **Use the merge-base as the diff target** instead of `HEAD`:
   - `git diff --numstat <merge-base>` for the summary counts
   - `git diff <merge-base>` for the per-file diff
   - `git diff --name-status <merge-base>` for file status

## Environment

- Reproduced in discussion (Maaz + Vaibhaav + Prateek, bug-triage thread)
- Affects all sessions where the agent commits before the user opens the diff viewer

title: Auto-Review per project
body:
**Goal**

Implement **session-level auto review** for AO.

Auto review is configured per session, evaluated and triggered by the daemon, and must stay separate from agent activity state.

Auto review should:

- Be controlled by a per-session toggle.
- Be triggered only by the daemon.
- Never change or overload session activity states.
- Use the session’s selected reviewer harness, falling back to the project reviewer harness.
- Trigger only when the worker session has been idle for at least 1 minute.
- Reuse the existing review planner and review trigger flow.
- Never retrigger while a review is running.
- Never retrigger for a PR head commit that AO already reviewed successfully.
- Never repeatedly rerun the same unchanged commit after changes were requested.
- Disable manual review controls while auto review is enabled.
- Keep the reviewer harness dropdown visible but disabled while auto review is enabled.

**Non-Goals**

- Do not redesign the Kanban board.
- Do not add a new activity state like `in_review`.
- Do not move review orchestration into the frontend.
- Do not trigger auto review from the worker session.
- Do not repeatedly auto-review the same unchanged commit after `changes_requested`.

**Core Model**

Activity remains process state only:

```text
active | idle | waiting_input | blocked | exited
```

Auto review reads activity as a gate:

```text
session is idle for >= 1 minute
```

Auto review is modeled as:

```text
session auto-review toggle
+ effective reviewer harness
+ session activity facts
+ SCM PR facts
+ review planner state
-> maybe daemon triggers review
```

Not as:

```text
session status -> automation
```

**1. Add Session Auto Review Field**

Add a durable session-level field.

Suggested domain shape:

```go
type SessionRecord struct {
    ...
    AutoReviewEnabled bool `json:"autoReviewEnabled"`
}
```

Add SQLite migration:

```sql
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN auto_review_enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
```

Update:

```text
backend/internal/domain/session.go
backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/sessions.sql
backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/session_store.go
backend/internal/storage/sqlite/gen/*
frontend/src/api/schema.ts
```

Run:

```bash
npm run sqlc
npm run api
```

**2. Add Session Auto Review API**

Add a session-scoped route:

```text
PUT /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/auto-review
```

Request:

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

Response can return the updated session or a small response:

```json
{
  "sessionId": "...",
  "autoReviewEnabled": true
}
```

Recommended source files:

```text
backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go
backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go
backend/internal/service/session/service.go
backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/sessions.sql
```

Behavior:

```text
enabled=false:
  manual review mode

enabled=true:
  daemon may auto-trigger review
  frontend disables manual trigger
```

**3. Reviewer Harness Resolution**

Auto review uses the effective reviewer harness:

```text
session.reviewerHarness
else project.config reviewer harness
else missing reviewer harness -> ineligible
```

Rules:

- If missing reviewer harness use worker agent harness

**4. Frontend Behavior**

In the existing Run review section:

- Add an `Auto review` toggle.
- Toggle reads/writes `session.autoReviewEnabled`.
- Keep the reviewer harness dropdown visible.
- Disable the reviewer harness dropdown when auto review is on.
- Disable the manual `Run review` trigger when auto review is on.
- If a review is running, preserve existing running/cancel behavior.

UI state:

```text
autoReviewEnabled=false:
  reviewer dropdown enabled
  Run review enabled when no review is running

autoReviewEnabled=true:
  reviewer dropdown visible but disabled
  Run review visible but disabled
  optional helper copy: "Manual review is unavailable while auto review is on."
```

Frontend must not start auto review. It only configures and displays state.

Likely files:

```text
frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx
frontend/src/renderer/components/ReviewerSelect.tsx
frontend/src/api/schema.ts
```

**5. Add Auto Review Coordinator**

Create a daemon-side package:

```text
backend/internal/autoreview
```

Suggested shape:

```go
type Coordinator struct {
    Store Store
    Reviews reviewsvc.Manager
    Clock func() time.Time
    IdleThreshold time.Duration
}

func (c *Coordinator) EvaluateSession(ctx context.Context, sessionID domain.SessionID) (Result, error)
```

The coordinator must be:

- daemon-side
- transport-free
- UI-free
- independent from Kanban/display status
- using existing review planner behavior where possible

**6. Daemon Sweep Criteria**

The daemon periodically evaluates live worker sessions.

Sweep interval:

```text
1 min
```

Initial daemon filter:

```text
kind = worker
is_terminated = false
auto_review_enabled = true
activity_state = idle
activity_last_at <= now - 1 minute
```

This can be implemented either as a specific store query or by listing live worker sessions and filtering in Go.

Suggested query concept:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM sessions
WHERE kind = 'worker'
  AND is_terminated = 0
  AND auto_review_enabled = 1
  AND activity_state = 'idle'
  AND activity_last_at <= ?;
```

The daemon then calls:

```go
coordinator.EvaluateSession(ctx, session.ID)
```

Errors should be logged and must not crash the daemon.

**7. Full Evaluation Criteria**

A session is eligible for auto review only when all of these are true:

```text
session auto review is enabled
session kind is worker
session is not terminated
session activity is idle
now - session.activity.lastActivityAt >= 1 minute
effective reviewer harness exists
session has at least one observed PR
PR is open
PR is not draft
PR is not closed
PR is not merged
PR has non-empty HeadSHA
existing review planner says needs_review
no running review exists for the current PR/head
no approved review exists for the current PR/head/effective harness
no changes_requested review exists for the current PR/head/effective harness
```

If any condition fails, skip and return a structured reason.

Suggested skip reasons:

```text
disabled
not_worker
terminated
not_idle
idle_threshold_not_met
missing_reviewer_harness
no_pr
draft_pr
closed_pr
merged_pr
missing_head_sha
review_running
already_approved
changes_requested_same_sha
planner_ineligible
planner_up_to_date
planner_running
planner_changes_requested
trigger_failed
```

**8. Review Planner Integration**

Reuse:

```text
backend/internal/review/planner.go
```

Coordinator flow:

```text
load session
resolve effective reviewer harness
load PR facts for session
load review runs for session
call review.Plan(prs, runs)
for each planned PR:
  inspect planner status
  trigger only when status == needs_review
```

Planner state mapping:

```text
needs_review:
  auto trigger allowed if idle gate and harness checks passed

running:
  skip, do not retrigger

up_to_date:
  skip, already reviewed at this head commit

changes_requested:
  skip, wait for a new head commit

ineligible:
  skip
```

Important policy:

```text
If current head SHA has changes_requested, auto review waits for a new head SHA.
```

This prevents repeated auto-review loops on the same unchanged commit.

**9. Trigger Behavior**

When eligible, coordinator calls existing review trigger path:

```go
Reviews.Trigger(ctx, session.ID, effectiveReviewerHarness)
```

The trigger should create review runs using the same existing engine behavior as manual review.

Do not add a second review orchestration path.

**10. Duplicate / Race Protection**

Auto review must not duplicate work.

Before triggering:

```text
if any review is running for the current PR/head, skip
```

After triggering starts, existing review-run idempotency must still protect against races.

Required behavior:

```text
two daemon evaluations for the same session/PR/head/harness must not create two running reviews
```

If the existing review trigger already reuses an existing running run, rely on it and add tests. If not, add the missing idempotency at the review-run creation boundary.

**11. Same Commit Rules**

For a given:

```text
session + PR URL + head SHA + effective reviewer harness
```

Auto review should behave as follows:

```text
no run exists:
  trigger

running run exists:
  skip

approved run exists:
  skip

changes_requested run exists:
  skip until HeadSHA changes

failed or cancelled run exists:
  may trigger again, as long as no running/approved/changes_requested run exists for current head
```

When PR head SHA changes:

```text
previous changes_requested no longer blocks auto review
new head SHA may be reviewed
```

**12. Manual Review Rules**

Manual review mode:

```text
autoReviewEnabled=false
```

Behavior:

```text
Run review button available when no review is running
reviewer harness dropdown enabled
manual trigger uses effective reviewer harness
manual trigger bypasses idle gate
```

Auto review mode:

```text
autoReviewEnabled=true
```

Behavior:

```text
Run review button disabled
reviewer harness dropdown visible but disabled
daemon may trigger review after eligibility checks
```

Manual review should not be callable from the frontend while auto review is enabled.

Backend may optionally reject manual trigger while `autoReviewEnabled=true` to enforce the contract beyond the UI. If added, return a clear 422-style error.

**13. Backend Tests**

Add focused tests for the coordinator/planner flow:

```text
auto review disabled does not trigger
non-worker session does not trigger
terminated session does not trigger
active session does not trigger
waiting_input session does not trigger
blocked session does not trigger
idle less than 1 minute does not trigger
idle at least 1 minute triggers
missing reviewer harness does not trigger
session reviewer harness is used
project reviewer harness is fallback
no PR does not trigger
draft PR does not trigger
closed PR does not trigger
merged PR does not trigger
missing HeadSHA does not trigger
planner ineligible does not trigger
planner running does not trigger
planner up_to_date does not trigger
planner changes_requested does not trigger
planner needs_review triggers
existing running review does not duplicate
existing approved review for same head SHA does not rerun
existing changes_requested for same head SHA does not rerun
new head SHA after changes_requested triggers
failed review for same head SHA may retry
cancelled review for same head SHA may retry
two concurrent/near-concurrent evaluations do not create duplicate running reviews
```

Add service/controller tests:

```text
session auto-review toggle persists true
session auto-review toggle persists false
session response includes autoReviewEnabled
manual trigger is rejected while autoReviewEnabled=true, if backend enforcement is added
```

**14. Frontend Tests**

Add tests for the Run review section:

```text
auto review toggle renders from session.autoReviewEnabled
toggle on sends session auto-review update
toggle off sends session auto-review update
Run review button enabled when auto review is off and no review is running
Run review button disabled when auto review is on
reviewer harness dropdown visible when auto review is on
reviewer harness dropdown disabled when auto review is on
reviewer harness dropdown enabled when auto review is off
running review behavior still shows existing running/cancel state
```

**15. Verification Commands**

Backend focused:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/autoreview ./internal/review ./internal/service/review ./internal/service/session ./internal/httpd/controllers
```

If sqlc changed:

```bash
npm run sqlc
```

If API/schema changed:

```bash
npm run api
```

Frontend:

```bash
cd frontend
npm run typecheck
```

Broader backend check if time allows:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./...
```

**Final Design Rule**

```text
Activity answers:
  what is the worker doing?

Reviewer harness answers:
  who should review this session?

SCM facts answer:
  what PR commit exists right now?

Review planner answers:
  does this PR/head still need AO review?

Auto review answers:
  is the daemon allowed to start that review now?
```

Keep those separate.

title: feat: add controlled browser preview workflow
body:
## Summary

- keep Browser closed by default and treat URLs printed in terminal output as signal-only, showing the Browser indicator without navigating or stealing focus
- preserve explicit terminal-link navigation while safely serializing and coalescing preview requests
- open web links in AO Browser only for active workers; standalone shell, orchestrator, and terminated-session links continue to use the system browser
- extend the terminal-link context menu with Open in system browser and Copy link actions
- refresh explicitly selected static HTML, Markdown, and related assets only after worker activity becomes idle, waits for input, or exits
- never choose a preview target for a fresh worker; selection remains owned by `ao preview`, a managed preview server, or deliberate user navigation
- avoid replayed terminal output opening live previews
- document the rendered-preview workflow for framework projects: use the exact session worktree, start or reuse its development server, wait for a healthy URL, and run `ao preview <url>` near the end of UI work
- add an explicit Browser toolbar action for opening the current page externally
- merge current `main` and resolve the preview poller and Browser panel conflicts

## Review fixes

- guard every poller target mutation and refresh with a URL + target-revision compare-and-set so a stale session snapshot cannot overwrite an explicit user selection
- persist the exact revision produced by a poller-owned missing-file clear, and restore only while the blank target still has that revision
- separate explicit target revisions from static-content refresh revisions; automatic refreshes now reload the Browser's current location instead of navigating back to the selected entrypoint
- replace the per-session 250 ms recursive asset walk with a complete, uncapped fingerprint at a five-second cadence while retaining cheap entry metadata checks on each poll
- preserve current `main`'s explicit-preview ownership instead of reintroducing automatic entrypoint discovery
- restore system-browser fallback for terminals that do not have an AO Browser inspector
- route the Browser toolbar's external action through the shared error-handling policy
- remove a stale Browser layout wrapper left over from the retired viewport selector

## Tests

title: Session picker in terminal '+' dropdown is confusing and shows cross-project sessions
body:
## Summary

PR [#3138](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/3138) ("Feat/project session tabs", merged July 27) changed the terminal tab strip's **"+" button** from a direct "new shell" action to a `DropdownMenu`. The dropdown lists all worker sessions alongside the "Terminal" (new shell) option, allowing users to pin Session B's terminal as a tab on Session A's page — which is confusing.

**Reported by:** @prateek

## Decision (from triage thread)

**Remove the session picker from the "+" dropdown entirely.** The "+" should go back to directly creating a new terminal — no dropdown, no extra window.

- Swap the terminal icon with "+"
- No session picker popover
- Make sure the new terminal opens in the **correct worktree** (the current session's worktree)

## Context

The "+" in `CenterPane.tsx` currently opens a `DropdownMenu` (`isTabLauncherOpen`) with:
1. "Terminal" → creates a new standalone shell
2. A searchable list of all sessions (cross-project — see scope bug below) → pins them as terminal tabs

Users expect "+" to **create** a terminal, not browse sessions. The session-pinning entry point via "+" doesn't make sense.

## Scope bug (for reference if session tabs are kept elsewhere)

`availableSessions` in `SessionView.tsx` flattens **all** workspaces, so sessions from other projects appear:

```js
const availableSessions = workspaces.flatMap((workspace) =>
    workerSessions(workspace.sessions).filter((candidate) => candidate.isTerminated !== true),
);
```

## Affected files

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/CenterPane.tsx` — remove the `DropdownMenu`/session picker, restore "+" → direct new shell
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx` — remove `availableProjectSessions` prop wiring (and related `addSessionTab`/`removeSessionTab`/`selectProjectSession` if the "+" entry point was the only consumer)
- `frontend/src/renderer/stores/ui-store.ts` — `sessionTabsByOwner` may no longer be needed if the "+" was the only way to populate it

## Repro

2. Click the "+" button at the end of the terminal tab strip

## Problem

The **Archive** section's **list (rows) view** doesn't look great. Terminated sessions rendered as rows are visually cluttered — the dot + status + title + path + copy icon + PR status + avatar + timestamp + restart icon all compete for the same horizontal space, producing cramped, hard-to-scan rows (see screenshot).

In contrast, the grid/card layout gives each terminated session its own tile with breathing room, which reads much better for a section that's mostly historical/reference browsing.

## Proposal

**Do not support rows (list view) in the Archive section** — force grid view only for archived sessions.

This keeps the list/grid toggle for the active/review-pending sections (where rows are useful for seeing live detail at a glance) but removes the cramped rows layout from the archive, where users are scanning many historical items.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Archive section renders exclusively in grid (card) view.

- Reported by @prateek in #🧑‍🔧-bug-triage.

- Related area: `frontend/` (session list rendering, view toggle logic).

title: fix(lifecycle): stop duplicate and stale worker-idle nudges to the orchestrator (#3038)
body:
## What

Fixes the noise in the "[AO] Worker … has gone idle" nudges reported in #3038. Instead of removing the worker-idle outbox, this keeps the feature and closes the three bug classes with targeted guards.

## Why (live evidence)

Pulled from a running daemon's `worker_idle_events` table: **88 nudge events, one worker (`zero_to_one-23`) generated 25 of them in a single evening** while it was only ever `idle` (not terminated, not done). Root cause: the outbox enqueued on *every* worker `active→idle`, with no delivery-time recheck.

Three distinct symptoms (matching the issue's follow-up report):
1. **Delivery after kill** — event enqueued on idle, delivered later with no terminal check.
2. **Duplicates** — every re-idle re-enqueued (auto-mode turn boundaries, retries).
3. **Re-arm on human/orchestrator poke** — a done/`review_pending` worker flapping `active→idle` after a message re-nudged as if freshly finished.

## Changes (no schema change)

- **Report-once-per-episode** (`ApplyActivitySignal`): an in-memory `reportedIdle` set enqueues at most one nudge per attention episode. Re-idles are suppressed; a worker entering a real `needs_input`/`blocked` state reopens reporting; spawn/restore and termination reset it. A poke-induced idle never passes through `needs_input`, so it is naturally suppressed — this collapses both the duplicates (#2) and the poke re-arms (#3). In-memory by design, mirroring the existing `flights` map: a daemon restart at worst allows one extra nudge, never a lost completion.
- **Delivery-time recheck** (`DispatchPendingWorkerIdleEvents`): re-reads the worker right before sending and drains the event (marks delivered without sending) when the worker is **terminated** or owns an **open PR** (work already in review and visible to the orchestrator). Fixes #1 and stops nudging review_pending workers.

Net effect: workers still show idle in the sidebar; the orchestrator just stops being auto-poked repeatedly for the same completion.

## Tests

`go test ./internal/lifecycle/` (incl. `-race`) green. Added coverage:
- `TestActivity_WorkerReportedOncePerEpisode` — re-idle produces no second nudge.
- `TestActivity_WorkerReReportsAfterNeedsInput` — a genuine needs-input episode re-arms reporting.
- `TestDispatch_DrainsTerminatedWorkerWithoutNudge` — terminated worker's event is drained, not sent.
- `TestDispatch_OpenPRDrainsMergedPRStillNudges` — open-PR worker drained; merged-PR worker still nudges.

Pre-existing failures in `internal/cli`, `adapters/workspace/scratch`, `adapters/agent/kilocode`, and `daemon` are environment-related (macOS `/private/var` path canonicalization, spawn tests needing a live daemon) and reproduce on a clean baseline; none touch `internal/lifecycle`.

## Alternative considered

Full removal of the outbox (what the issue literally proposes). This PR is the "keep it, make it correct" option. If maintainers prefer removal, that is a larger, cleaner delete (trigger, dispatch, store, table via a new drop-migration, daemon sweep) and can be done instead.

Refs #3038

title: Keyboard Shortcuts settings modal renders blank (panel off-screen)
body: ## Summary The Keyboard Shortcuts settings modal renders blank. Opening it darkens/blurs the screen (scrim appears) but no dialog panel is visible. Esc closes it. Reproduces on all platforms. ## Screenshot ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open Settings → **Keyboard shortcuts**. 2. Screen darkens and blurs (overlay appears), but no dialog panel renders. 3. Esc dismisses the overlay. ## Expected The Keyboard Shortcuts dialog panel renders centered and visible. ## Actual Only the overlay/scrim renders. The dialog panel is pushed off-screen, so the feature is unreachable from its primary entry point. ## Root Cause `KeyboardShortcutsSettingsDialog.tsx:299` — a stray `relative` class overrides the modal's `fixed` positioning via `tailwind-merge`: ```tsx // line 299 className={cn(settingsDialogContentClass, "relative w-[min(760px,calc(100vw-var(--space-8)))]")} // ^^^^^^^^ the culprit ``` `tailwind-merge` groups all position utilities (`static`/`fixed`/`absolute`/`relative`/`sticky`) into one conflict group and keeps the last one. The base `DialogContent` class ships `fixed`, but `relative` is appended later, so `relative` wins. The panel loses its viewport pinning and lands out of view in normal flow, while the `DialogOverlay` (`fixed; inset:0; z-index:50` + scrim + `backdrop-filter: blur`) still covers the screen. Backdrop visible, content off-screen. **Why only this dialog:** `ReportProblemDialog` uses the identical `settingsDialogContentClass` but without `relative`, so it keeps `fixed` and works fine. The `relative` was added here to anchor the toast (`absolute bottom-4 right-4`, ~line 478). ## Fix (1 line) Drop `relative` — it's unnecessary. `position: fixed` from the base class already establishes a containing block for the `absolute` toast, so the toast still anchors correctly: ```tsx className={cn(settingsDialogContentClass, "w-[min(760px,calc(100vw-var(--space-8)))]")} ``` Keep the `w-[min(760px,...)]` (intentionally wider than the default settings-dialog width) — just remove `relative`. ## Regression Test Existing tests render with `open` and assert on content presence, so they pass even with the bug (the panel is in the DOM, just mispositioned). Add a computed-style assertion to lock this in: ```ts getComputedStyle(content).position === "fixed" ``` Verify: ```bash cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npx vitest run components/settings/KeyboardShortcutsSettingsDialog.test ``` ## Triage | | | |---|---| | **Area** | `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/KeyboardShortcutsSettingsDialog.tsx:299` | | **Priority** | P1 — shipped feature (#3157) unreachable from its primary entry point; non-crashing, Esc-dismissible, isolated | | **Duplicates** | None | | **OS-specific?** | No — CSS bug, hits every platform (reporter was on Windows) | | **Regression** | Introduced in #3157 — dialog was broken on first ship | ## Labels / Priority - **Labels:** `bug`, `comp/desktop`, `regression` - **Priority:** P1

title: send: GUI-typed message occasionally sits unsubmitted in worker input until next send flushes both
body:
## Summary

`POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` (and `ao send`) occasionally leaves a message unsubmitted in the worker’s TUI input area. The endpoint returns `200 OK` because `tmux send-keys` exits 0, but the agent never actually receives the prompt — the text sits in the prompt buffer as a draft, indistinguishable from an idle worker. Sending another message via the daemon API then appends to the same draft and triggers a single Enter that submits **both** messages together, looking like "the next send flushed the stuck one and the new one".

A reliable report (3 occurrences on 2026-07-28) had one session sitting idle for ~4 hours waiting on a reply that was never going to come because the prompt was never delivered.

## Repro (best-effort, intermittent)

1. Run the AO desktop app and connect to a worker session running Claude Code (or another TUI-based harness).
2. When the agent is **mid-rendering a long response** (lots of tokens streaming, agent busy), `ao send --session <id> --message "<a non-trivial prompt>"` (or the GUI equivalent) the worker.
3. In a fraction of attempts, the message sits in Claude Code’s prompt input area un-submitted. The `ao send` command returns 0 immediately. No error, no warning.
4. Issue another `ao send` (or any payload via `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send`). The chunks of the second message are appended after the stranded first message; the second message’s trailing Enter submits both messages together.

The race is timing-sensitive (depends on how saturated the TUI’s input buffer is when chunks land), so it is hard to reproduce reliably. The user impact is asymmetric: when it happens, the GUI shows no error and the user has no signal until they happen to send again.

## Root cause

The single-Enter contract still has soft edges that the existing pre-Enter pause + post-Send `confirmActive` rescue loop (introduced by #2342 / #2357) do not fully cover.

`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:411` `SendMessage`:

- Chunks are written with `r.run(ctx, ...)` over the **caller’s** `ctx`. If the caller’s HTTP request is cancelled mid-paste (renderer re-render, network blip, client disconnect), the chunk loop short-circuits on the cancellation error **before** the post-paste pause / detached Enter can run. Chunks already accepted by tmux remain in the pane as a draft, with no Enter coming to submit them.
- The detached-Enter contract (`enterCtx = context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), r.enterDelay+5s)` at line 434) only protects Enter **after** the chunk loop completes. A cancellation that lands inside the chunk loop skips the detached-Enter code entirely.

`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:1764` `Manager.Send` + `confirmActive`:

- Pre-Enter pause (`defaultEnterDelay = 300ms`, `tmux.go:31`) is fixed and small. For a large multiline paste into a busy TUI, 300ms can be too short for the TUI to absorb the chunks before Enter arrives — Enter then lands inside the pasted text and submits nothing.
- `confirmActive`’s budget (`sendConfirmAttemptDeadline = 2s`, `sendConfirmMaxAttempts = 3`, `manager.go:210-212`) gives the TUI ~6 seconds total to flip Activity.State to active. For a slow TUI that takes longer to absorb a large paste and start the agent’s user-prompt-submit hook, the rescue loop gives up silently — Send still returns nil.
- `confirmActive` is skipped entirely for harnesses that don’t implement both `EmitsSubmitActivity` AND `EmitsBlockedActivity` (`manager.go:1813` `harnessNudgeSafe` — see `adapters/agent/codex/codex.go:44` `EmitsBlockedActivity = false`). For those harnesses, a lost Enter has no rescue path at all.

The interlocking effect: when a chunked-paste races with a busy TUI, the post-Send confirmation either doesn’t run or runs out of budget, the controller returns `200 OK` to the GUI, and the message is silently stranded in the worker’s prompt input.

## Impact

- **Silent failure.** No signal to the operator (status code 200, no log, no notification). The session just sits idle.
- **Wasted user time.** A user waiting for a reply that will never come (one report: 4 hours).
- **Cross-contamination.** The NEXT send through the same daemon API path writes into the same input box. Its trailing Enter then submits accumulated drafts as one prompt, surprising the user with concatenated messages from prior un-sent sends.

## Suggested fix surface (not a proposed patch yet)

1. **`tmux.SendMessage` chunk-loop context:** once the first chunk has been written successfully, switch the chunk loop and the trailing Enter onto the same `enterCtx` (detached from the caller, bounded by a fixed timeout). This closes the "caller cancelled mid-paste, chunks stranded without Enter" hole.
2. **`sendConfirm` budget:** bump `sendConfirmAttemptDeadline` / `sendConfirmMaxAttempts` so the rescue loop has more headroom for slow TUIs. Optionally make the budget per-prompt-length scaled, not a single fixed budget.
3. **`confirmActive` telemetry:** when the rescue loop exhausts its budget without seeing ActivityActive, emit a structured `WARN` log line (session id, attempt count, observed states) so operators have a signal in telemetry even though Send returns 200.
4. **(Larger; out of scope for a small fix)** Extend `confirmActive` to non-safe harnesses with a guarded "nudge only when state is provably WaitingInput" fallback, so the rescue also works for Codex and similar adapters.

## Related

- Closes #2342 (which added Enter delay + `confirmActive`). This bug is the leftover soft edges of that fix.
- The review-nudge `sendOnce` / `MarkReviewRunDelivered` dedup-stamp path (also called out in #2342) has the same shape: a hung message becomes invisible AND locked out of redelivery.

title: feat(cloud): hosted control plane, Clerk auth, and federated bus for cloud agent sessions
body:
## What this adds

Cloud-hosted Agent Orchestrator: agent sessions can run in per-session Daytona cloud sandboxes, fronted by a hosted multi-tenant control plane on Azure, authenticated with Clerk. Local sessions are unchanged; cloud is additive and off unless a control-plane URL is configured.

Vendor-pays model: the control plane holds the single cloud provider key, so
clients never supply cloud credentials.

## Main pieces

- **Cloud sandbox stack** (`internal/cloud`): Daytona REST client (no SDK) behind a pluggable `SandboxProvider` interface (e2b/Fly/Modal drop in later); a supervisor that provisions a sandbox, boots a scoped agent-host daemon, clones the repo, and injects harness credentials. Pre-baked snapshot plus async provisioning keep spin-up around 15 to 40s.
- **Control plane** (`internal/controlplane`, `cmd/controlplane`): tenant-scoped `/api/v1/cloud/*` mirroring the daemon, Postgres registry, Clerk RS256 JWT auth (or a dev header). Cloud-agnostic: all config via env, no cloud SDK imports.
- **Federated bus**: lets an orchestrator and its workers interact across locations (laptop, sandbox A, sandbox B) by session id. A location registry plus a hub route send/spawn/kill and events to whichever host owns the target, reaching sandboxes via a signed preview URL and laptops via a held-open SSE channel. Per-sandbox scoped bus tokens (signing key from Key Vault) authorize the sandbox side; a worker token can never reach spawn or terminate.
- **Spawn delegation**: an orchestrator inside a keyless sandbox delegates `ao spawn` to the control plane to provision a new worker sandbox, with an idempotency key so a retried request never double-provisions.
- **Fleet visibility**: `ao fleet` lists every session across local and cloud with status, so an orchestrator (local or cloud) can see all its workers. The orchestrator prompt and the using-ao skill point at `ao fleet` rather than the local-only `ao session ls`.
- **Spawn-time credential injection**: the desktop app sends its current Claude credential with each cloud spawn; the control plane injects it and never stores it.
- **Per-sandbox egress allowlist**: each sandbox is provisioned with a default-deny domain allowlist (control plane host plus the harness's domains), so a cloud agent can only reach what it needs.
- **Renderer**: Clerk sign in and out (Google OAuth), Bearer attached to control-plane calls, a Local or Cloud choice on orchestrator launch and on New Task, plus session sharing and import.

## User flow

1. Sign in to cloud (Clerk, Google) from the sidebar.
2. Add a project.
3. Spawn an orchestrator: choose Local or Cloud. A cloud orchestrator runs in its own sandbox.
4. Create workers via New Task or from the orchestrator: choose Local or Cloud per worker. Cloud workers each run in their own sandbox.
5. The orchestrator runs `ao fleet` to see every worker across local and cloud with status, and `ao send <session-id>` to direct any worker regardless of where it runs. Workers report back over the bus when they go idle.
6. All coordination is by session id; sandboxes and URLs are never handled manually.

## Testing

- Backend suite green (89 packages), renderer suite green (1165 tests), tsc and gofmt clean.
- Federated bus unit-tested end to end (router, relay, transport, tokens, authz, fleet) and live-verified on Azure against real Daytona: a cloud orchestrator provisions a cloud worker via delegation, both `ao send` directions route over the bus, and `ao fleet` sees both; then teardown.

## Notes

- Off by default: without a control-plane URL, only local sessions run and the daemon behaves exactly as before.
- The control plane runs on Azure Container Apps; sandboxes run on Daytona (billed via the vendor account). Both are pluggable.

## Design doc

 https://gist.github.com/Pritom14/7e4c4075938d89de16f740b61b18916e

title: docs: ACP migration plan (Node acp-bridge, drop tmux, chat UI)
body:
## Summary

Design-only PR that lands `docs/plans/acp-migration.md`: a concrete architecture to migrate agent-orchestrator from **tmux/conpty terminal-mux** agent launch to the public **Agent Client Protocol (ACP)**, with a **Go-supervised Node acp-bridge** (`packages/acp-bridge`, official `@agentclientprotocol/sdk`) and an **AO-native React ChatPane** replacing the agent xterm pane.

Confirmed product decisions (encoded in the plan):
1. **Remove tmux** for agents (and agent conpty) — no dual-path fallback.
2. **Broad multi-agent ACP coverage** via **AO-owned** declarative adapter configs.
3. **ACP client in Node acp-bridge**, supervised by the Go daemon.

### IP / clean-room (mandatory)

See **§ IP / clean-room rules** in the design doc. Short version:

| Forbidden | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Copy/port third-party ACP product apps (code, configs, UI, PRDs, assets) | Public ACP at agentclientprotocol.com + official `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` |
| Look-alike chat UI / foreign component names | Independent design under `DESIGN.md` (`ChatPane`, …) |
| Vendor foreign adapter tables | AO catalog; flags from each agent’s public CLI docs |

Third-party ACP desktops may be mentioned only as high-level product prior art, never as code to replicate.

## Phased implementation plan (orchestrator can spawn implementers after merge)

| PR | Title | Depends on | Intent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **PR1** | feat: Node acp-bridge + detachable session workers + Go supervisor | — | `packages/acp-bridge`, worker isolation (survive HTTP *and* daemon crash on Darwin/Linux), loopback HTTP reverse-proxy + generation token, health, packaging |
| **PR2** | feat: Go AcpRuntime port + HTTP client | PR1 | `ports` + `backend/internal/acpbridge` client |
| **PR3** | feat: Declarative AO ACP adapter catalog | PR2 | AO-owned catalog schema (`command`/`args`/`connectionType`) |
| **PR4** | feat: Session spawn/kill via ACP | PR3 | SessionManager spawn/kill without tmux; metadata SQL migration |
| **PR5** | feat: send/cancel, activity+FirstSignalAt, coordination, turn busy | PR4 | `ao send` → ACP prompt; activity matrix (**end_turn → idle**); 409 on concurrent turn |
| **PR6** | feat: durable turns + chat stream SSE (timeout-exempt) | PR5 | SQLite turns (not tokens); SSE chat stream outside `middleware.Timeout` |
| **PR10a** | feat: minimum certified ACP adapters before UI flip | PR3 | Certify default harnesses before desktop default-on |
| **PR7** | feat: React ChatPane (preserve multi-session tabs) | PR6, PR10a | AO-native chat UI per DESIGN.md |
| **PR8** | feat: Permission cards + YOLO | PR7 | ACP permission UI + project YOLO mode |
| **PR9** | feat: Restore / Reconcile / ResumeAgent without tmux | PR5, PR6 | Boot reattach to surviving workers; native resume / context digest |
| **PR10b** | feat: expand adapters + upgrade UX | PR10a, PR7 | Broader certified coverage + unsupported-harness UX |
| **PR11** | feat: Shell-only PTY host + reviewer runtime migration | PR7 | Minimal PTY for user shells **and** reviewers (not agents) |
| **PR12a** | chore: delete agent tmux/conpty path and agent xterm | PR11, PR9 | Remove agent tmux/conpty, agent `/mux` attach path, agent xterm |
| **PR12b** | docs: architecture/stack/STATUS/CI cleanup | PR12a | Docs + CI reflect ACP world |

**Ship discipline:** no end-user desktop / auto-update release until **PR7 + PR10a** (prefer +PR8).

## Suggested implementer spawn order (DAG)

```
PR1 → PR2 → PR3 ─┬→ PR4 → PR5 → PR6 ─┬→ PR7 → PR8
                 │                   │
                 └→ PR10a ───────────┘
                         PR5+PR6 → PR9
                 PR10a+PR7 → PR10b
                         PR7 → PR11 → PR12a → PR12b
```

## Key architectural choices

| Decision | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Protocol source | Official ACP only (clean-room) |
| Package | `packages/acp-bridge` + `backend/internal/acpbridge` |
