title: fix: deliver Grok prompts after TUI startup
body:
## Summary

- start Grok without passing the task as a positional subcommand
- deliver the initial task through the interactive TUI after its Grok Build readiness marker appears
- preserve permission-mode mapping, appended AO rules, Grok hook wiring, and native session restore arguments
- update adapter tests to lock the current Grok CLI invocation shape

Closes #3532

## Investigation

The installed Grok Build 0.2.22 CLI uses the root grammar grok [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]. Bare prompt text is therefore parsed as an unknown subcommand. The -p/--single flag is supported, but it runs headlessly for one turn and exits, which is not a usable AO interactive worker lifecycle.

The adapter originally used -p. PR #2518 switched to a positional prompt to retain the TUI, but that positional form is incompatible with the current CLI. The supported interactive path is to launch the TUI without a task and submit the task through the terminal after startup, matching AO interactive adapters such as Kimi.

## Tests

- cd backend && go build ./...
- cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/grok
- cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/...
- cd backend && go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/grok
- cd backend && go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs
- live Grok 0.2.22 PTY probe: launched the same promptless TUI argv, submitted a test task through the terminal, received AO_GROK_PROMPT_OK, and observed session-start/user-prompt-submit/stop hooks

npm run lint reaches one unrelated existing backend test failure: internal/service/session.TestWorkspaceFilesIncludeWorkspaceProjectChildRepoDiffs receives compare ref main where the test expects empty. Running inside the live AO worker environment also requires removing AO runtime variables to keep CLI tests isolated.

## Risks

- The readiness marker depends on the Grok Build footer text. AO has an 8-second timeout and falls back to prompt delivery if the banner changes.
- Restore remains unchanged and continues to use the hook-captured native session ID.

title: fix(frontend): tighten sidebar and board layouts
body:
## Summary

- align prominent session status dots with the project-label column
- make the shared activity resolver authoritative for dot color and animation: active is pulsing blue, waiting/blocked is orange, idle is gray, exited is red
- size the project action gutter to its actual 64px footprint so project names use all available room
- reveal the smaller sidebar rename pencil only on hover/focus so session names keep its width by default
- keep project actions visible, tighten the kebab edge inset, and optically align the folder/label with the action icons
- reuse the standard session card for archived sessions so card density, PR links, and one-row PR metadata stay consistent
- align the Settings and Archive footer hairlines using the framed macOS panel geometry
- let the embedded Browser viewport use the inspector edge-to-edge instead of retaining nested content gutters
- compact auxiliary terminal tabs and strengthen the selected-tab indicator

## Why

Archived cards had a separate rendering path from active cards, which allowed their sizing and PR behavior to drift. Sidebar activity dots also had a second PR-aware color resolver, causing actively working sessions to appear yellow or green instead of consistently blue. The project row reserved 84px for a 64px action cluster, truncating names despite available space. The footer and Browser offsets depended on conflicting inset geometry; the Browser viewport then added a second inset of its own. Auxiliary terminal tabs used a 204px fixed-width formula, leaving less room for additional tabs, while the 1px selection line was too subtle.

## Validation

- `npm test -- --run src/renderer/lib/session-presentation.test.ts src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx` (156 tests)
- `npm test -- src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx` (133 tests)
- `npm test -- src/renderer/components/ShellTerminalTab.test.tsx src/renderer/components/CenterPane.test.tsx` (33 tests)
- `npm run typecheck`
- `git diff --check`
- launched the native Electron dev app from this checkout at `http://localhost:5173`, attached to the existing daemon at `127.0.0.1:3001`; no second daemon was started

## Risk

Low; changes are scoped to renderer layout and shared session/terminal presentation.

## Latest session-review polish

- redesign the inspector PR card around a title-first, single-surface hierarchy with a directly linked PR number and visible external-link affordance
- centralize compact-card status priority so CI failures, conflicts, requested changes, required reviews, and merge readiness do not produce contradictory duplicate rows
- keep the Files query and workspace-change stream warm while the inspector is open, preventing the initial false zero and first-click loading lag
- render live Kanban activity through the shared activity presentation so active workers pulse blue consistently
- improve PR metadata, review-state color semantics, contrast, hover visibility, and narrow-card density

Validation added for PR status precedence and deduplication, PR link accessibility/contrast, eager Files loading, false-zero suppression, and active Kanban pulse. Focused renderer run: 142 passing tests. Frontend typecheck passes. Full renderer run: 1,436 passing and 5 unrelated landing Markdown tests blocked because this checkout does not include the existing cheerio dependency.

title: bug(browser): in-app browser re-navigates to the session's preview URL on session switch-back, clobbering the user's manual navigation
body:
## Bug
In a session that has an active `ao preview` URL set (e.g. a dev-server preview), the in-app browser panel **discards the user's manual navigation** whenever they leave the session and return: navigate the panel to google.com, switch to another session, switch back → the panel has silently re-navigated to the session's preview URL (e.g. `http://localhost:5217/`).

**Source:** maintainer report (desktop app, macOS), reproduced on session `agent-orchestrator-81` (verify-pr-3495, previewUrl=`http://localhost:5217/`) | **Date:** 2026-08-03 | **Analyzed against:** `9ae0573` (main)
**Confidence:** High — exact effect + mechanism traced.
**Priority:** medium — the browser panel is unusable for anything other than the daemon-set preview in a previewed session; the user cannot browse elsewhere and have it stick.

## Reproduction
1. Open a session that has a preview URL set (any session where `ao preview <url>` has run — its Browser tab auto-loads that URL).
2. In the in-app Browser panel, navigate somewhere else (e.g. google.com).
3. Switch to a different session in the sidebar.
4. Switch back to the first session.
5. Observe: the Browser panel is back on the preview URL (`http://localhost:5217/`), not google.com.

## Root Cause
`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.ts`, the preview-navigation effect (~line 643):

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!viewId || viewIdRef.current !== viewId || terminated) return;
  const target = previewUrl?.trim() ?? "";
  const revision = typeof previewRevision === "number" ? previewRevision : null;
  const previous = previewTriggerRef.current;
  if (previous?.revision === revision && previous.target === target) return;   // dedup
  ...
  previewTriggerRef.current = { revision, target };
  if (target) void navigate(target);
  ...
}, [clear, navigate, previewRevision, previewUrl, terminated, viewId]);
```

- `previewUrl` is the daemon-driven target (via `ao preview`, streamed over CDC); the design intent (see the doc comment) is that the view "navigates here automatically." The dedup guard `previewTriggerRef` is meant to make it fire **only when the preview revision/target actually changes**, not on every render.
- **But `previewTriggerRef` is component-local state.** When the user switches sessions, this session's browser view is destroyed and the hook effectively remounts on return with a **fresh `viewId`** — which is in the dep array, so the effect re-fires — and `previewTriggerRef.current` has reset, so the dedup (`previous?.revision === revision && previous.target === target`) no longer short-circuits. Result: it re-navigates to `previewUrl`.
- Compounding it: the user's own last-navigated URL (google.com) is **view-local and not persisted per session**, so on return the only URL the system knows for the session is the daemon `previewUrl` — there is nothing to restore the user's navigation to.

Net: the daemon preview URL is treated as authoritative and re-asserted on every view (re)creation, and manual navigation has no persistence to win against it.

## Fix (directions)
1. Persist the "last consumed preview (revision, target)" **per session, across view remounts** (keyed by session id — a store or a ref that outlives the view), so the auto-navigate fires only on a genuine new `ao preview`, not on session switch-back.
2. And/or remember the user's **last manually-navigated URL per session** and restore that (instead of previewUrl) when returning, so manual navigation sticks. The preview URL should only take over on an actual revision bump.
3. Guard the effect against re-firing purely because `viewId` changed while `previewRevision`/`previewUrl` are unchanged.

## Impact
- In any previewed session, the browser panel snaps back to the preview URL on every return — the user cannot use it as a general browser.

## Related
- [#2698](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2698) (closed): browser panel wrongly opens when switching sessions — same subsystem
- [#2859](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2859) (closed): new session's browser auto-previews a workspace file
- [#3445](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3445) (open): browser shows wrong tab's content after switching (native view bleed-through)

title: fix(browser): stop re-asserting preview URL on session switch-back
body:
Fixes #3536.

## Problem

In a session with an active `ao preview` URL, the in-app browser panel discarded the user's manual navigation on every session switch-back: browse to google.com, switch sessions, return → the panel silently re-navigated to the preview URL.

## Root cause

The preview-navigation effect in `useBrowserView.ts` dedups `ao preview` triggers via a component-local ref (`previewTriggerRef`). On a session switch the browser view remounts with a fresh `viewId` (in the effect's dep array) and the ref resets, so the already-consumed `(revision, target)` was consumed again. Meanwhile the main process (`ensureSession`) keeps the session's native view alive across switches with the user's last URL — so the re-fired effect navigated that surviving view back to `previewUrl`.

## Fix

Persist the last consumed preview trigger per session in a module-level map that outlives the hook instance, and seed the dedup ref from it on mount when a native browser is present. Auto-navigation now fires only on a genuine revision/target change (a real new `ao preview`), never merely because the view remounted.

- A fresh `ao preview` (revision bump) still takes over the panel, including with the same URL.
- Termination still destroys the view, and drops the session's consumed trigger so a reused session ID is not suppressed.
- The non-native (web/mock) fallback keeps its old remount behavior: its view state genuinely dies with the component, so re-applying the preview is what restores it.
- Cross-session revision-collision behavior is preserved (the map is keyed by session ID).

## Tests

- New: manual navigation survives switch-away/switch-back (prop-change and full-remount variants) and a subsequent revision bump still navigates; termination frees the consumed trigger for a reused session ID; non-native remount still restores the preview.
- Full frontend suite: 110 files / 1458 tests pass; `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Manual verification (real desktop app)

Reproduced the maintainer's exact steps in the dev Electron app against an isolated daemon, driving the UI over CDP and asserting the native `WebContentsView` target URLs:

1. Session with `ao preview http://127.0.0.1:5217/` → Browser panel auto-loads it (revision 1).
2. Typed `https://www.google.com/` in the panel URL bar → native view on google.com.
3. Switched to another session and back → native view **still on google.com** (previously snapped back to `:5217`); URL bar shows google.com.
4. Re-ran `ao preview http://127.0.0.1:5217/` (revision 2) → panel navigates back to the preview.
5. Repeated navigate/switch/return after revision 2 → google.com preserved again.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(terminal): Grok/Windows history scroll with PageUp/PageDown wheel
body:
## Summary
Fixes Grok (and similar full-screen chat TUIs) history scrolling on Windows under ConPTY, with free proportional mouse-wheel scroll that does **not** hijack shell input history.

### Problem
Windows ConPTY has no tmux copy-mode fallback. Full-screen agent TUIs enable mouse tracking on the alt buffer, so wheel events were sent as SGR reports that often no-op. An intermediate attempt used ArrowUp/ArrowDown for free scroll, which made Grok recall prompt input history instead of scrolling the transcript.

### Fix (final behavior)
1. Route Windows alt-buffer / keyboard-scroll-provider wheels to **PageUp/PageDown** (not arrows).
2. Mark Grok as a keyboard-scroll provider so conversation history scrolls (alongside opencode/kilocode).
3. Free proportional mouse-wheel scroll for normal terminal content, with PageUp/PageDown for history-safe keyboard-scroll paths.

### Commits (oldest → newest)
- `fix(terminal): scroll Grok history on Windows with PageUp/PageDown`
- `fix(terminal): free proportional mouse-wheel scroll` (earlier arrows approach)
- `fix(terminal): use PageUp/PageDown for wheel, not arrows` (corrects the arrow regression)

Both intermediate and final commits are included so review can see the intentional correction; behavior of the tip is PageUp/PageDown-only for history-sensitive paths.

## User-visible impact
- Mouse wheel scrolls Grok/Windows agent history instead of no-op or prompt-history recall.
- Proportional free scroll still works where appropriate; zoom/SGR paths unchanged.

## Test plan
- [ ] Unit: `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` / `TerminalPane.test.tsx` (no frontend `node_modules` in this worktree; run CI or local frontend tests)
- [ ] Manual Windows desktop: open Grok session, wheel through history, confirm no ArrowUp prompt recall
- [ ] Manual: non-Grok shell free wheel still scrolls buffer

## Notes
- Cherry-picked onto `Untrivial-ai/main` from fork tip (excluding the fork-only merge commit).
- Topic-split PR; independent of backup/i18n/lifecycle work.

title: fix: notify orchestrator when worker turn completes (idle)
body:
## Summary
Wire the missing lifecycle dispatcher so a worker **active → idle** transition notifies the project''s live orchestrator.

### Problem
Scaffolding already existed (`ListSessions` for resolve-at-delivery, `NudgeCoordination` for busy/blocked policy), but `ApplyActivitySignal` never called it. Parents saw silence after workers finished turns — especially visible on Windows where operators rely on that signal rather than only manual `ao send`.

### Fix
- Dispatch on worker **active → idle**; skip `waiting_input → idle` and non-workers
- Deliver via `NudgeCoordination` (idle now; queue when orchestrator is busy; drop when blocked)
- Flush deferred completions when the orchestrator next becomes idle
- Regression tests for happy path, deferral, blocked, and no-orchestrator

## User-visible impact
Orchestrators receive a coordination nudge when a worker finishes a turn, so multi-agent workflows resume without manual messaging.

## Test plan

- [x] Manual multi-session: worker completes turn → orchestrator receives idle notification

title: fix(terminal): proportional history-safe wheel scroll
body:
## Summary

Smoother follow-up to **#3540** for keyboard-scroll agent panes (especially **Grok on Windows**).

#3540 made history scroll work with PageUp/PageDown (history-safe; no bare ArrowUp/ArrowDown). That baseline is correct, but every wheel notch still jumps a full page because `keyboardScrollReport()` ignored `|lines|`.

This PR restores a **proportional / 丝滑** wheel feel while remaining **history-safe**.

### Key choice

| Option | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Bare ArrowUp/Down | **Rejected** — Grok binds these to prompt input-history recall |
| SGR wheel | Ignored by these agents under AO/ConPTY |
| PageUp/PageDown only (#3540) | Works, but one key = one full viewport → jumpy |
| **Grok Ctrl+K / Ctrl+J** | **Chosen for grok** — documented line scroll; Ctrl+J is LF (`\n`), distinct from Enter CR (`\r`) |
| **OpenCode Ctrl+Alt+Y / Ctrl+Alt+E** | **Chosen for opencode/kilocode** — default `messages_line_up/down` |
| Generic alt-buffer fallback | Still one PageUp/PageDown per event (direction only) |

### Behavior

- **grok**: one Ctrl+K/J per scrolled line (small rolls move a little, large flicks farther)
- **opencode / kilocode**: one Ctrl+Alt+Y/E per line
- Unchanged: Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom, normal-buffer `term.scrollLines`, Unix mux SGR path

### Relationship to #3540

- Branch is **#3540 tip + this proportional commit** (same files: `XtermTerminal` / `TerminalPane`).
- This PR **supersedes / improves** #3540 for wheel feel while keeping the history-safe design.
- Suggested review order: review #3540 first as the baseline, then this; **or** review/merge this alone and close #3540 as fully replaced.
- Do **not** merge both as independent stacks without reconciling — they touch the same paths.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test -- src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.test.tsx` (78 passed on source branch)
- [x] Manual: Grok on Windows — wheel moves transcript gradually, does **not** recall prompt history

title: feat(telemetry): report code review outcomes
body:
## Why

Code review is a headline AO feature with **no telemetry at all**. The review service had no sink wired, so nothing can answer:

- Are reviewers actually being used?
- Do they approve or request changes?
- How long does a pass take?
- How often does triggering one fail?

Confirmed against the live project: there is no `ao.review.*` event of any kind.

## What

Four events, emitted from the service boundary where the transitions already happen:

| Event | Fields |
|---|---|
| `ao.review.triggered` | `harness`, `created_runs`, `reused` |
| `ao.review.submitted` | `harness`, `verdict`, `duration_ms`, `posted_to_provider` |
| `ao.review.cancelled` | `cancelled_runs` |
| `ao.review.trigger_failed` | `error_kind` |

`created_runs` and `reused` distinguish a genuinely new pass from reuse of a running or up-to-date one, which the engine also reports as success. Without that, adoption would be inflated by repeat triggers.

## Privacy

Enum-like fields only. Three things are deliberately excluded:

- **The review body** — reviewer prose about a user's source code
- **`PRURL`** — identifies the org and repository
- **`TargetSHA`** — identifies a commit in that repository

A test walks every emitted payload and fails if the body, repo name, SHA, a source path, or a provider host appears in any string value. That check sits at the call site rather than relying on the remote allowlist to strip them downstream, since the allowlist failing open would be silent.

## Idempotency

`ao.review.submitted` fires only on the genuine `running` → `complete` transition, matching the store's own idempotency. A reviewer retrying a submit cannot double-count a verdict. Tested by submitting three times and asserting one event.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/service/review ./internal/adapters/telemetry ./internal/daemon ./internal/httpd ./internal/review` — all passing
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean
- Four new tests: outcome fields, the privacy sweep, resubmit idempotency, and an unwired service staying silent
- **Export path verified by exercising the real PostHog sink**, not just the service. The remote allowlist drops unregistered keys, so a new event with unregistered fields would export as an empty shell. Asserted that `harness`, `verdict`, `duration_ms` and `posted_to_provider` survive export while a `body` does not.

## Notes

The sink is optional. Every existing caller constructs the service without one, so an unwired service stays silent rather than panicking, with a test for that.

Independent of #3401 and #3489. Branched from `main`, no overlapping files with either.

## Follow-ups, not in scope

- No event yet for a review reaching a **merged PR**, which is the actual value moment. That needs PR-merge instrumentation, which does not exist either.
- Reviewer harness adoption will only be comparable once builds carrying this roll out; existing installs report nothing.

title: feat(telemetry): desktop product events, retention and default-agent, daily active heartbeat
body:
## Why

We could not answer a basic product question: **do people ever configure more than one agent?**

`ao.session.spawned` carries the `harness` that ran, so it shows which agents get *used*. It says nothing about how many were available to choose from. An install with six authorized agents that always reaches for one looked identical to an install that only had that one.

## What

`ao.renderer.agents_available`, once per app launch:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `installed_count` | binary resolved |
| `authorized_count` | auth probe recently succeeded, so actually spawnable |
| `supported_count` | size of the adapter registry |
| `authorized_agents` | sorted, comma-joined ids |

`authorized_count` is the number that matters for "can this person spawn it", which is why it's tracked separately from `installed_count`.

## Why the id list is safe

Agent ids are a fixed vocabulary from AO's own registry (`claude-code`, `codex`, …), never user-supplied text. Sorted so the same set always produces the same value and can be grouped in analysis instead of fragmenting by ordering, and length-bounded so a growing registry cannot turn one property into a long string.

The renderer sanitizer allowlists only the three counts and the id list. A test asserts that a `binary_path` or a `label` passed by a future caller is dropped, so a local path cannot leak through this event later.

## Volume

Reported **once per launch**, from the shell, reading the cached agents query so it adds no request of its own. Once matters: the inventory only changes when someone installs or authorizes an agent, while the query refetches on window focus and after a manual refresh. An unguarded report would be a repeating stream, which is the shape that caused the original PostHog bill.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run` — **111 files, 1466 tests** passing
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` clean
- 5 new tests on the inventory builder: separate counts, sorted and stable ids, empty and partial catalogs, the length bound, malformed ids
- 1 new sanitizer test asserting only the contract fields survive

## Note on a test I had to touch

The shell shortcut suite mocked `../hooks/useAgentsQuery` without a `useAgentsQuery` export, so adding the hook to the shell broke 20 tests. The mock now returns `{ data: undefined }`, which means the hook reports nothing and those tests stay free of telemetry side effects.

## Scope

Independent of #3401, #3489, and #3546. Branched from `main`.

Remaining from the desktop tracking list, not in this PR: agent switching (from → to), mobile connect, get-help/report-a-problem, and an explicit stable/nightly channel property.

As with every event, this reports nothing until builds carrying it roll out.

title: feat: add durable agent switching
body:
## Summary

Adds durable worker-agent switching while preserving the AO session, worktree, branch, task, PR ownership, browser target, terminal surface, and each provider's native session.

The initial implementation is intentionally limited to switching between:

- Claude Code
- Codex

Cursor and Kimi remain available as ordinary AO agents, but are not switching sources or targets in this release.

## Hybrid handoff model

- AO always derives deterministic context from durable AO/session/workspace facts, but keeps that data in memory while constructing the handoff.
- When the source agent is healthy and its composer is provably empty, AO may request an optional semantic handoff through private, temporary `agent-handoff-candidate.json` and `agent-handoff.json` files.
- AO folds deterministic context and any verified semantic handoff into `handoff.json`, the sole long-lived handoff content artifact after a successful switch.
- The target continuation includes the verified read-only source transcript path, the latest real user request, the latest user-facing assistant update, and the optional semantic handoff.
- If semantic handoff is unavailable, AO adds a bounded transcript tail (up to 600 lines / 64 KiB); terminal output is only a final bounded fallback.
- AO never creates the superseded `prepared.*` or `handoff.md` artifacts and never translates, clips, appends, or rewrites provider-native JSON/JSONL/session files.

## Delivery and native-session retention

- Existing provider-native sessions are retained and resumed when switching back; missing or unverified native state starts a fresh provider session.
- Claude Code and Codex receive the continuation as part of the fresh/resume command, so the prompt is submitted rather than left in the composer.
- Delivery is generation-fenced and acknowledged by the exact supervised target generation before ownership is finalized.
- Tmux launches end in a safe sink so late bytes cannot reach a shell after the provider exits.
- Command-line capacity is calculated before source shutdown. Oversized continuations are compacted while preserving the protocol and latest user/assistant state.

## Durability and recovery

- Adds a durable, idempotent agent-switch saga and provider-native session registry.
- Stops the source before target activation, generation-fences lifecycle hooks, and transfers ownership only after durable target identity/delivery state is recorded.
- An unconfirmed source stop or target cleanup keeps the saga non-terminal and the input gate closed for explicit recovery.
- Recovery never resends a continuation whose delivery may already have occurred.
- SQLite migration 0083 enforces the current handoff and delivery invariants.

## Public surfaces

- Desktop: one stable `Switch agent` action, durable phase display, and switch history for Claude Code/Codex workers.
- CLI: `ao session switch-agent`, `ao session agent-switch ls`, and internal generation-fenced handoff submission.
- HTTP: switch creation, curated history/status, and generation-fenced semantic handoff submission.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` (complete backend Go test suite plus pinned golangci-lint v2.12.2)
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- Focused agent-switch renderer suites (76 tests)
- `git diff --check`

## Deliberate non-goals

- Cursor or Kimi switching in the initial release
- Orchestrator-session switching
- Automatic budget/quota switching policy
- Cross-provider transcript materialization or canonical transcript storage
- Provider compaction/checkpoint conversion

Closes #3317

Switched to registering the font as a `FontFace` built from decoded bytes on the shadow root's own `FontFaceSet` — no network fetch, so it isn't subject to the page's CSP. ## Test plan - [x] `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts annotate-preload` — 5/5 passing, including new coverage asserting the `FontFace` registration path actually runs with "Geist Variable"/"Geist Mono Variable" - [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean - [x] Manual check in the desktop app: open a project's browser preview, enter annotate mode, select an element, confirm the popup matches the diff viewer's feedback box styling and the font renders as Geist

title: fix(frontend): duplicate checkmark on selected agent in New Task modal
body:
## Bug

In the **New Task** modal, the selected agent shows a checkmark icon **twice** — once in the dropdown row and once echoed in the select trigger below it.

**Reported by:** @Dhruv Sharma (bug-triage channel)

## Screenshot

![duplicate-check](https://files.slack.com/files-tmb/placeholder.png)

## Root cause

`RequiredAgentField` (`CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx`) wraps each agent option in a Radix `SelectItem`:

```tsx
<SelectItem key={agent.id} value={agent.id} disabled={agent.disabled}>
    <AgentSelectMenuItem
        agentId={agent.id}
        label={agent.label}
        selected={value === agent.id}   // ← renders a <Check> when true
        status={agent.status}
        statusTone={agent.statusTone}
        disabled={agent.disabled}
    />
</SelectItem>
```

`AgentSelectMenuItem` (`settings/AgentSelectMenuItem.tsx:38`) renders an explicit `<Check>` (lucide-react) when `selected === true`:

```tsx
{selected ? <Check className="size-3 shrink-0 text-settings-label" aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
```

This content lives inside Radix's `SelectPrimitive.ItemText` (see `ui/select.tsx:102`). Radix's `SelectValue` in the trigger **mirrors the full `ItemText` content** of the selected item — including the `<Check>` icon. So the checkmark shows up in both places:

1. **Open dropdown** — the selected agent row renders `AgentSelectMenuItem` with `selected=true` → checkmark ✅
2. **Trigger** (closed select) — `SelectValue` echoes the same `ItemText` content → same checkmark ✅

Result: two visible checkmarks for the same selected agent.

## Affected surfaces

- `NewTaskDialog` → `RequiredAgentField` (default "stacked" variant, using Radix Select)
- Also applies to the Create Project agent sheet which uses the same `RequiredAgentField`

The `"settings-row"` variant (`SettingsOptionMenu`) is **not** affected — it uses a `DropdownMenu` with a custom `renderTrigger` that does not include the check.

## Suggested fix

Do not include the selection check inside `ItemText`. Two approaches:

**Option A (recommended):** Move the check to a Radix `Select.ItemIndicator` slot, which renders only inside the dropdown and is never echoed to the trigger:

```tsx
// select.tsx SelectItem — add an indicator slot
<SelectPrimitive.Item ...>
    <SelectPrimitive.ItemText>{children}</SelectPrimitive.ItemText>
    <SelectPrimitive.ItemIndicator className="absolute right-2">
        {/* rendered only in the dropdown, never in the trigger */}
    </SelectPrimitive.ItemIndicator>
</SelectPrimitive.Item>
```

Then remove the conditional `<Check>` from `AgentSelectMenuItem` and handle selection display via the indicator instead.

**Option B (minimal):** Give `SelectValue` an explicit children render in `RequiredAgentField` that shows avatar + label only (no check), so the trigger stops echoing the check from `ItemText`.

## Severity

**P2** — cosmetic UI issue, no functional impact. Affects every user who opens the New Task modal.

title: Terminal font-size label (12px) visually merges with agent CLI border due to transparent background

## Bug The terminal font-size indicator (`12px`) in the top-right control cluster visually overlaps/merges with the agent CLI's bordered welcome box (e.g. Claude Code's border), making it look like a stray measurement annotation. ## What happens The display controls — `[-] [12px] [+] [⛶]` — float over the terminal's top-right corner with `bg-transparent` and no backing surface (by design, "so they read as part of the terminal itself"). When the agent CLI (Claude Code, etc.) draws its bordered welcome box, the box's **top-right border corner** lands exactly where the `12px` label sits. Since the label has no background, it renders directly on top of the CLI's border line. ## Visual The `12px` text and border line overlap with no separation, making it look like a CSS measurement guide that leaked into the live UI. ## Root cause `frontend/src/renderer/components/CenterPane.tsx` (lines 217–257): ```tsx {/* Display controls float over the terminal's top-right corner with no chrome of their own, so they read as part of the terminal itself. */}
{fontSize}px ← renders "12px" (TERMINAL_FONT_SIZE_DEFAULT = 12)
``` The entire cluster is transparent — when a TUI (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) draws a border at that position, there's nothing to separate the label from the border underneath. ## Fix direction Give the control cluster a subtle backing surface so it sits *above* terminal content instead of blending into it: ```tsx
``` This preserves the "floating over the terminal" intent without overlapping agent TUI borders.

## Summary

Closes #3552

The font-size / fullscreen control cluster (`[-] 12px [+] [⛶]`) was reported in #3552 as visually overlapping with agent TUI box-drawing borders (e.g. Claude Code's bordered UI), giving the appearance of a CSS measurement artifact leaking into the live UI.

## Root cause (already fixed)

The controls were previously floating as an `absolute`-positioned overlay over the terminal surface with no background of their own, causing them to bleed into the terminal content:

```tsx
// OLD — removed by #3480
<div className="absolute right-3 top-2 z-10 flex shrink-0 items-center gap-3 font-mono text-passive/70">
  {/* no background → merged with TUI borders */}
```

## Fix

PR #3480 moved the controls into the session tab bar (`session-topbar-surface`), which provides an opaque `background-color: var(--color-bg-primary)` surface. The controls now sit clearly separated from terminal output, with no floating overlay.

This PR adds an inline comment in `CenterPane.tsx` documenting this intentional design decision so future contributors understand why the controls are not floated.

## Testing

Open a session with Claude Code or any TUI-based agent (Grok, opencode, kilocode). The `[-] 12px [+] [⛶]` controls appear cleanly in the tab bar — they do not overlap the TUI border.

- Fixed structurally by #3480

title: feat: make a missing tmux visible and fixable, in the app and the CLI
body:
Closes #3564. Related: #3434, #3435.

## Problem

A new macOS/Linux user without tmux only finds out at spawn time, via
`RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING: tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH`.
That check runs inside the daemon, which lives inside the desktop app, so it
fires in the one place with no way to tell the user anything and no terminal to
fix it from.

## The desktop app

A non-blocking banner on the board, styled as the project-health banner directly
beneath it:

- **macOS:** an **Install tmux** button that runs `brew install tmux` through the
  daemon, then re-checks PATH. Homebrew needs no password, so it is safe to run
  headless.
- **Linux:** the exact `sudo apt-get install -y tmux` line to copy. The app has
  no terminal to answer a password prompt on, so it does not offer a button it
  cannot honour.
- **Both:** a **Check again** button, so a manual install clears the banner
  without restarting the app.
- An unreachable daemon renders nothing. Not knowing is not the same as knowing
  tmux is absent.

### Why not run the install in an AO terminal pane

That was the first idea and it does not work. `daemon.go:220` wires standalone
shell terminals through the same runtime adapter as session panes, which is
tmux. No tmux means no shell terminal either, so the install cannot be hosted in
one. Hence the split above.

`pkexec` would give Linux a polkit password dialog and close that gap. Left out
deliberately: a second privilege-escalation path deserves its own change, tested
by someone who runs Linux daily.

## The CLI

`ao start` settles the same prerequisite before launching the app, which is what
#3564 asked for and mirrors the pre-rewrite `ensureTmux()`. On an interactive
terminal it prompts and installs (brew, apt-get, dnf, pacman, zypper, apk, first
match on PATH, sudo only where root is needed and reachable). Anything else gets
one warning naming the exact command.

**One deliberate deviation from the issue:** it asks for "show install hints,
exit with clear error". This warns and continues. The old `ensureTmux()` could
exit because `ao start` *was* the daemon; it is now only the app launcher, and
the app is usable without a session runtime. The CLI smoke container proved the
point: it runs `ao start` on a fresh box and asserts the failure is a download
error, and a hard tmux exit broke that check.

Not bundling tmux, per the triage thread: it would conflict with an existing
install and add a version-patching burden.

## Shape

- `internal/prereq` holds the package-manager table, so the CLI and the daemon
  cannot drift on what installs tmux. `Status.NeedsRoot` decides who may run it.
- `GET /api/v1/prerequisites`, `POST /api/v1/prerequisites/tmux/install`. The
  install endpoint refuses anything flagged `NeedsRoot` with
  `PREREQUISITE_NOT_INSTALLABLE`, so the rule holds however the request arrives,
  not just because the UI hides a button.
- A package manager can exit 0 and leave nothing runnable, so success is the PATH
  re-check, not the exit code (`PREREQUISITE_INSTALL_INCOMPLETE`).
- New `Deps.RunInteractive` in the CLI runs the install attached to the real
  terminal so `sudo` can prompt; its stdout goes to stderr so `ao start --json`
  stays a clean JSON document.
- `stdinIsInteractive` excluded `/dev/null`, which is a character device and so
  passed the old "is a terminal" test. `docker run` without `-i` hands a process
  exactly that, which made the confirmation prompt answer itself with its default
  and run an install nobody asked for. This also makes `ao import`'s confirmation
  honest in the same situation. A real tty check needs an ioctl
  (`golang.org/x/term`), which pulled an `x/sys` bump into `go.mod` for one
  boolean; `/dev/null` is the only non-tty character device that turns up as
  stdin in practice.
- `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` regenerated via `npm run api`. Copy added to all
  8 locales.

Complementary to #3435 (better error text at spawn time), which stays the
backstop for anyone who dismisses or ignores the banner.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`; `golangci-lint run` over `internal/{prereq,httpd,daemon,cli}`: 0 issues.
- `go test ./internal/prereq/ ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/cli/`: pass.
- `npx vitest run`: 109/110 test files pass. The one failure,
  `src/landing/scripts/generate-markdown-twins.test.mjs`, is a missing local
  `cheerio` install, untouched here.
- Two pre-existing backend failures
  (`TestWorkspaceFilesIncludeWorkspaceProjectChildRepoDiffs`, and six
  `TestSpawn*`/`TestBrowser*` cases that talk to a live local daemon) reproduce
  identically on `upstream/main` in a clean worktree at the base commit.

Tests added: `prereq` (platform/ordering/root rules), `PrerequisitesController`
(status per platform, install, refusal to run what it cannot, failure and
exit-0-without-tmux), `cli/tmux` (no-ops, warn-without-install per unreachable
case, the `/dev/null` regression, prompt-and-install, decline, failed install,
sudo rules), `PrerequisiteBanner` (present, unreachable daemon, install, copy,
failure, re-check).

**Not done:** I have not seen the banner render in the real app. It only appears
when the daemon reports tmux missing, and this machine has tmux. Worth a look on
a fresh box before merge.

## Summary

Ports the **AllBeingsFuture agent-stream consumer core** into AO’s renderer for ACP streaming output UX, without importing `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` or speaking raw ACP.

- **Hook:** `useAgentStream` (batcher + optional SSE + `pushEvents` for offline/tests)
- **Docs:** `frontend/docs/acp-renderer-streaming.md`

Does **not** port full fenzhi `ChatWorkspace` (out of corrected scope). SessionView / settings left untouched until backend stream API lands.

## Backend dependencies (BLOCKED for live wiring)

Provisional routes not on `main` OpenAPI yet:

1. `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/agent-stream` — SSE, `event: agent_stream`, JSON `AgentStreamEvent`
2. `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/agent-stream/permissions/{requestId}` — body `{ optionId }`

Until those exist, `connection` stays `unavailable`; UI works via `pushEvents`.

cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts \

  src/renderer/components/agent-stream

title: feat(agentstream): ABF-style sequenced agent stream over SSE
body:
## Summary

Ports the **AllBeingsFuture ACP streaming output contract** into the AO daemon as a provider-neutral wire, without a full chat-stack port.

- **Canonical stream events** matching ABF `AgentStreamEvent` (`text_delta`, `thinking_update`, `tool_call`, `tool_update`, `plan`, `status`, `permission_request`, `done`, `error`, `cancelled`)
- **Normalizer** (`BridgeEvent` → sequenced events), modeled on ABF `agent-stream-normalizer` tests
- **ACP v1 mapper** for `session/update` chunks → bridge events (SDK-free; ready for `acp-go-sdk` producers)
- **Hub** with monotonic per-session sequence + short replay buffer
- **SSE path:** `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/agent-stream?after=<seq>`
  - event name: `agent_stream`
  - `id:` = sequence
  - `data:` = `AgentStreamEventResponse` JSON
- Daemon wires `agentstream.NewHub()` into `APIDeps.AgentStream`
- OpenAPI + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated

Intentionally **out of scope** (for follow-up workers): full fenzhi chat/service storage, multi-provider chat drivers, permission-respond HTTP, durable conversation projection.

## Frontend contract

1. Subscribe: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/agent-stream` (or `?after=-1` for full buffer; reconnect with `after=<lastSequence>` / `Last-Event-ID`)
2. Reduce only `AgentStreamEventResponse` types; never import ACP SDK
3. Terminal types (`done` / `error` / `cancelled`) flush the turn
4. Producers call hub `PublishBridge` / `PublishACPSessionUpdate` when ACP drivers land

## Tests

```bash
cd backend && go test ./internal/agentstream/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/ ./internal/httpd/...
```

All green locally.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for normalizer (ABF-modeled sequences, tool diffs, permission drop, status map)
- [x] Unit tests for ACP session/update mapping
- [x] Hub subscribe/replay
- [x] SSE controller replay + live + after cursor + 501 when unwired

body:
## Bug

**Reported by:** @aditi (Discord #bug-triage)

The "Report a problem" dialog has two visual issues:

### 1. Primary action button text is invisible (white-on-white)

The primary action button (e.g. "Copy & Create GitHub Issue") uses hardcoded `text-white` instead of the design-system foreground token. In dark mode this produces white text on a nearly-white background — making the button text unreadable, and when disabled (`opacity-50`) the entire button becomes an indistinguishable gray blob.

**Root cause:** `ReportProblemDialog.tsx` line 246 uses inline Tailwind classes:
```tsx
className="settings-footer-button border-transparent bg-settings-accent text-white transition-opacity hover:opacity-90 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50"
```

It should use the existing `settings-footer-button-primary` utility class (`styles.css` line 664), which correctly uses `--color-settings-footer-button-primary-fg` → `--primary-foreground` (= `oklch(0.21)` dark in dark mode, giving proper contrast).

**Token chain (dark mode):**
- `bg-settings-accent` → `--primary` → `oklch(0.92 0.004 286.32)` (nearly white)
- `text-white` → `#ffffff` → white text on white background = **invisible**
- Correct: `--primary-foreground` → `oklch(0.21 0.006 285.885)` (nearly black) — already wired in `settings-footer-button-primary`

**Fix:** Replace the inline classes on the primary button (line 244-254) with `settings-footer-button settings-footer-button-primary`.

### 2. Footer buttons right-aligned, user expects centered

The footer uses `justify-end` (`dialog.tsx` line 125):
```
flex shrink-0 flex-wrap items-center justify-end gap-3 border-t ...
```

User expects buttons to be center-aligned (`justify-center`).

**Fix:** Consider changing `settingsDialogFooterClass` to `justify-center` — but verify other dialogs using this class (ConfirmDialog) aren't negatively impacted. Alternatively, this could be a per-dialog override.

## Repro
1. Open Settings → Report a problem
2. Observe the "Copy & Create GitHub Issue" button — text is invisible
3. Fill in title + details → button becomes enabled but text still invisible
4. Buttons are bunched to the right edge, not centered

## Files
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/ReportProblemDialog.tsx` (button classes, line 244-254)
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/dialog.tsx` (footer class, line 124-125)
- `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css` (`settings-footer-button-primary` utility, line 664-680)

title: fix(sqlite): ledger 0043 and repair is_pinned on burned migration histories
body:
## Why

`main` is red on Go / build-test at 3d782c2 ([run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/30976687994)):

```
--- FAIL: TestMigrationVersionLedger
    migration "0043_add_session_pinned.sql" (version 43) is not in the shippedMigrations ledger
--- FAIL: TestSessionListSucceedsOnBurnedMigrationHistory
    insert session mer-1: SQL logic error: table sessions has no column named is_pinned (1)
```

Two PRs, each green on its own base, neither re-run against the other:

- #3511 (merged 2026-08-04 22:09Z) added `0043_add_session_pinned.sql`.
- #3491 (merged 2026-08-05 04:58Z) added the append-only ledger and `schemaRepairs`, both stopping at 42 because the branch predates #3511.

The second failure is not ledger bookkeeping, it is the defect the guard exists to catch. The #3475/#3476 field profiles have `goose_db_version` recording versions 40 through 51 from a foreign build, so goose skips 0043 there entirely. `gen/sessions.sql.go` selects and writes `is_pinned` and `pinned_at` in create, list, get, and update, so on those installs session pinning ships as an opaque 500 on the session list while `/healthz` stays green.

## What

- Append `43: "0043_add_session_pinned.sql"` to `shippedMigrations`.
- Add `sessions.is_pinned` and `sessions.pinned_at` to `schemaRepairs`, and replay 0043's CDC trigger in `postAdd` so pin changes still broadcast on a repaired database.

The trigger replay hangs off `pinned_at`, the second column, because SQLite resolves a trigger body at `CREATE TRIGGER` time and the body references both columns. Hanging it off `is_pinned` would fail with `no such column: NEW.pinned_at`. `postAdd` runs only when the column was just added, so healthy databases are untouched.

## Verification

```
go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/ -run 'TestMigrationVersionLedger|TestSessionListSucceedsOnBurnedMigrationHistory'   ok
go test ./internal/storage/...                                                                                        ok, 88 tests, 3 packages
gofmt -l internal/storage/sqlite/                                                                                     clean
golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/...                                                                              0 issues
```

## Risks and follow-ups

- No schema change and no new migration, so nothing new to burn.
- The repair path is exercised by `TestSessionListSucceedsOnBurnedMigrationHistory`, which seeds versions 40 to 51 as applied and now creates and lists a session successfully.
- Worth considering separately: nothing forces a PR that touches `migrations/` to be re-tested against current `main` before merge, which is exactly how this landed.

Blocks the nightly. Conductor run [30976937971](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/ao-releases/actions/runs/30976937971) was cancelled at the wait step before any publish, so no release was cut from the broken SHA.

title: bug(scm): completed checks can remain pending until forced refresh
body:
## Bug

A pull request can continue to show **Checks running** in AO for roughly five minutes after every GitHub check has completed. The card corrects itself only when the SCM observer's unconditional-refresh backstop runs.

**Source:** Live AO review session on 2026-08-05 (no public chat URL)  
**Reported by:** Human reviewer in the AO desktop app  
**Analyzed against:** `c970f0d2436d770cf24bda317785ea5a8313d656`  
**AO version:** `dev` (freshly built Go rewrite; verified installed daemon ready on port 3001)  
**Observed surface:** macOS Electron development app using the same rewrite and real AO data on its development port 3002  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P2 — status is materially misleading, but self-corrects through the bounded-staleness fallback.

## Reproduction

1. Open an AO session whose attributed GitHub pull request has multiple check runs.
2. Push a commit so those checks enter the running state.
3. Keep the PR summary card visible in the session inspector.
4. Wait until every GitHub check completes successfully.
5. Observe that AO can continue to display **Checks running**.
6. Wait for the five-minute forced PR refresh; the card changes to **Checks passing** without user action.

Live instance: PR #3590 had all relevant checks complete by `2026-08-05T07:00:44Z`, while AO did not observe `ci.state: passing` until approximately `2026-08-05T07:06:05Z`. The renderer fetched and displayed the corrected daemon response immediately afterward.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go::CommitChecksGuard` requests:

```text
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs?per_page=1
```

and uses that response's ETag as the fast check-state guard. With multiple check runs, the one returned item can remain unchanged while a different workflow finishes. Since the conditional representation has not changed, GitHub can return `304 Not Modified` even though the aggregate CI state AO displays has changed.

`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go::selectRefreshCandidates` then sees both the repository guard and this single-item check guard as unchanged and skips the full GraphQL PR/check refresh. `DefaultPRMaxAge = 5 * time.Minute` eventually forces the full fetch, which explains the observed delay precisely.

The frontend event transport is not the source of the lag: once SQLite changes from `pending` to `passing`, CDC invalidates the session SCM query and the card updates.

## Suggested Fix

Make the fast check guard represent all check runs that contribute to the aggregate CI state, rather than only one item. A fix should:

- request and condition on the complete relevant check-run representation (including pagination or a better aggregate endpoint where necessary);
- preserve conditional-request savings when none of those runs changes;
- add a provider/observer regression test where the first returned run remains stable while another run transitions from running to passing;
- retain `DefaultPRMaxAge` as a safety backstop for PR metadata changes not represented by check-state guards.

## Impact

- Users can spend up to five minutes believing checks are still running.
- Ready-to-merge status and merge actions are delayed even when GitHub is already green.
- The UI appears unreliable because a later refresh changes the state without any new GitHub activity.

## Related

- [#2656](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2656): tracked PR state could remain stale after merge; established the need for bounded refresh.
- [PR #2678](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2678): added the five-minute forced-refresh backstop that eventually heals this report but does not make CI transitions timely.

title: fix: detect authenticated Kimi installs
body: ## Summary - add Kimi self-managed install path (`~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi`) to binary discovery - recognize Kimi OAuth credential files (`~/.kimi-code/credentials/kimi-code.json`) as authorized when they contain an access or refresh token - prefer valid credential tokens over empty `config.toml` `api_key` placeholders - add focused tests for Kimi binary discovery and credential auth classification ## Issue Kimi was already present in the agents dropdown, but authenticated local installs were still shown as `Needs auth`. The frontend was rendering the daemon catalog correctly; the bad state came from the Kimi adapter's readiness probe. The local Kimi install shape can be: - binary at `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` - `config.toml` containing empty `api_key = ""` placeholders - real OAuth auth stored in `~/.kimi-code/credentials/kimi-code.json` The adapter did not search the self-managed binary path, and its first OAuth credential support still stopped too early when it saw empty `api_key` values in `config.toml`, classifying the install as unauthorized before checking the credential JSON. ## Before ## After ## Fix The Kimi adapter now checks `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` during binary resolution. For auth, it treats a non-empty config API key as authorized, then checks `credentials/kimi-code.json` for an access or refresh token, and only falls back to the empty config-key unauthorized result when no credential token exists. With that, the daemon can classify this local Kimi install as installed/authorized, and the existing agents dropdown can show it as available instead of `Needs auth`. ## Tests - `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/kimi ./internal/service/agent` - `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/registry ./internal/httpd/controllers -run 'Test.*Agent|TestEveryHarnessReportsAuthStatus|TestHarnessed'`\n- `git diff --check`\n\n## Risks\nLow. The change is scoped to Kimi catalog readiness probes and does not alter launch or restore command behavior.

title: fix(frontend): strip macOS nested-radius from Windows/Linux center panel
body:
## Problem

On Windows/Linux, the right side of the app shows curved/rounded corner radii while the left side (flush with the sidebar) stays square — reported by @phylsolver in bug-triage.

## Root cause

`center-panel-surface` uses `border-radius: var(--radius-center-panel)` (= **12px**), derived from a **macOS-specific formula**:

```
inner_radius = window_radius (18px) − inset (6px) = 12px
```

This nested-radius curve only makes sense **inside a rounded macOS window**. On Windows/Linux the frameless window is **rectangular**, and the shell has **asymmetric padding**:

| Edge | Padding | Curve visible? |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Left | `0` (flush to sidebar) | hidden |
| Top  | `0` (overridden by #3083) | hidden |
| Right | `16px` | **visible** |
| Bottom | `14px` | **visible** |

So the rounded corners only show on the right/bottom, making the panel look like a floating rounded card while the left stays square.

PR #3083 (*"flush Windows center panel"*) already dropped the **top** inset on Windows but never stripped the **radius**. This finishes that job.

## Fix

Set `border-radius: 0` on `.platform-windows` / `.platform-linux` `center-panel-surface` so the framed panel has sharp corners, consistent with the flush left edge. macOS is untouched — it keeps the nested-radius curve inside its rounded window.

## Testing

- [x] CSS-only change, no logic/TS affected
- [x] macOS path (`center-panel-shell--mac`) untouched — no regression
- [ ] Manual: verify Windows/Linux center panel now has square corners on right/bottom

title: fix(ptyexec): bound Close wait after the SIGKILL fallback
body:
## Summary

`ptyexec.Spawn` opens a local PTY around a terminal attach client (`tmux attach-session` on Unix, ConPTY on Windows). Its `Close()` tears the attach process down as **SIGTERM → SIGKILL → `<-done`**, where `done` closes when `cmd.Wait()` returns.

That final `<-done` is **unbounded**. A process wedged in an uninterruptible kernel state (`D` — e.g. blocked on a dead NFS/FUSE mount in the workspace) survives **SIGKILL**, so `cmd.Wait()` never returns and `Close()` blocks forever. Because `Close()` runs on daemon shutdown and on session teardown (including via the `Spawn` ctx-cancellation goroutine), a single wedged attach terminal hangs the entire daemon shutdown indefinitely. The Windows `conPTYProcess.Close()` has the identical unbounded wait.

This matters in practice because the attach client here is `tmux attach`, which resolves its session in the workspace tree — exactly the kind of path a hung filesystem can wedge.

## Change

- Add a shared `killGrace` (2s) and a `waitForExit(done, grace)` helper that returns on `done` **or** after the grace.
- Unix `creackPTY.Close()` and Windows `conPTYProcess.Close()` now call `waitForExit(...)` after the SIGKILL fallback, then release the PTY master and return. The `cmd.Wait()` goroutine finishes whenever the kernel eventually reaps the process; `Close` stays idempotent via `closeOnce`.
- Add unit tests (`wait_test.go`) covering both the bounded-timeout escape hatch and the fast path when the process has already exited.

SIGTERM-first behavior is preserved: a cooperative attach client still detaches within `detachGrace` (250ms), and a TERM-ignoring process is still killed via SIGKILL — only the post-Kill wait is now bounded.

## Tests

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/... ./internal/terminal/...` — pass
- `go test ./...` — pass except four pre-existing `internal/cli` spawn tests that fail on a clean `main` checkout too (environment/daemon-404, unrelated to this change).

## Known risks / follow-ups

- Worst-case shutdown now adds up to ~2.25s per genuinely-wedged attach terminal instead of hanging forever (intentional tradeoff).

title: fix(scm): condition commit check guard on all check runs, not just one
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3601 — **completed checks can remain pending until forced refresh**.

`CommitChecksGuard` in `backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go` requested the per-commit check-runs endpoint with `per_page=1` and used that single-item response's ETag as the fast check-state guard. When a PR carries multiple check runs, the one returned item can remain unchanged while a **different** workflow finishes, so GitHub answers `304 Not Modified` even though the aggregate CI state AO displays has changed. `selectRefreshCandidates` then skips the full GraphQL PR/check refresh, leaving the card on **Checks running** until the five-minute `DefaultPRMaxAge` backstop.

## Change

- Request the **complete** check-run representation (`per_page=100`, GitHub's cap) so the ETag covers every run that contributes to the aggregate CI state.
- When a commit carries more than one page of runs (`total_count > 100`), fall back to a stable fingerprint over the **full** run set (paginating), so a transition on a later page still invalidates the guard. Conditional-request savings are preserved: when nothing changed, the guard reports `NotModified` and the observer skips the GraphQL refresh.
- `DefaultPRMaxAge` remains as the safety backstop for PR metadata changes not represented by check-state guards.

## Tests

- `TestCommitChecksGuard_OtherRunTransitionInvalidatesGuard` — regression: first returned run stays stable while another run transitions `in_progress -> completed`; guard must report `NotModified=false`. (Verified this test fails against the old `per_page=1` logic.)
- `TestCommitChecksGuard_PaginatedFingerprintInvalidatesLaterPageRun` — a transition on a page-2 run invalidates the paginated fingerprint guard.
- Ran `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/github/... ./internal/observe/scm/...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and golangci-lint v2.12.2 — all clean.

Pre-existing failures in `internal/cli`, `internal/adapters/agent/fake`, and `internal/adapters/agent/kilocode` reproduce on clean upstream `main` and are unrelated to this change.

## Risks / Follow-ups

None known. The guard change only affects when the fast path forces a full refresh; it can only make CI transitions arrive sooner, never later.

title: enhancement: `ao start` should detect Linux distro and install native package (RPM on Fedora/RHEL, DEB on Ubuntu/Debian) instead of always using AppImage
body:
## Problem

`ao start` on Linux unconditionally downloads and runs the AppImage, even on RPM-based distros (Fedora, RHEL, CentOS, openSUSE) where a native `.rpm` package is now available as a release asset (#3406). The CLI should detect the distro and install the native package.

Reported by @atul-upadhyay-7 in Discord (#🪲-report-bugs).

## Background

The RPM package is already built, collected, and published as a release asset (`agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.rpm`) thanks to #3406 / #3405. The `.deb` is also available (`agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.deb`). So the native packages exist — the CLI just doesn't use them.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/cli/start.go`:

```go
// assetName() — Linux branch (lines ~502–523)
case "linux":
    return "agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage", nil
```

There is **no distro detection** anywhere in the codebase — no `/etc/os-release` parsing, no `ID_LIKE` check, no `rpm`/`dnf` detection. Every Linux user gets AppImage regardless of distro.

## Proposed Solution

Make `ao start` distro-aware on Linux:

### 1. Distro detection
Parse `/etc/os-release` (fields: `ID` and `ID_LIKE`):
- `fedora`, `rhel`, `centos`, `rocky`, `nobara`, `opensuse` → RPM
- `debian`, `ubuntu`, `pop`, `linuxmint` → `.deb`
- Unknown / unparseable → **AppImage** (current behavior, always works as fallback)

### 2. Update `assetName()` in `start.go`
Select the correct asset based on detected distro instead of hardcoding AppImage.

### 3. Update `fetchAppLinux()`
Handle:
- RPM distros: download `.rpm` + install via `dnf install` or `rpm -i` (may need sudo prompt)
- Debian distros: download `.deb` + install via `apt install` or `dpkg -i`
- Fallback: AppImage (existing fetch-and-run path)

### 4. Update `knownAppLocations()` / `linuxAppImagePath()`
Scan for the appropriate installed package / binary path based on distro.

## Scope note

This issue covers **CLI-side distro-aware package selection only**. The release-asset side (building, naming, uploading RPM/DEB) is already resolved by #3406.

title: fix(update): repair the macOS update path (stale-copy clobber, baked feed owner, dead restart button)
body:
Fixes #3617. Supersedes #3523, #3525, #3527 and #3529: this is the single PR for the macOS update path, so those four can close once this merges.

The baked-owner diagnosis in #3523/#3525 is prateek's and it is correct. His #3525 is ported here verbatim, plus the piece it missed; #3529 is ported as a backstop with three corrections, noted below.

Two independent layers were breaking updates, and they ship together because either one alone still leaves the fleet broken. Layer one decides which copy of the app runs. Layer two decides which repo that copy fetches updates from. They share no files.

A third, smaller piece rides along: a backstop for the restart button, which dies silently when the app cannot be swapped where it sits.

## Layer 1: an old copy silently overwrote the updated one

`app.moveToApplicationsFolder()` ran on every packaged macOS launch, with no conflict handler and no version check. In Electron 33 that call is destructive by default: with no `conflictHandler` it trashes whatever sits at `/Applications` and copies the running bundle over it (`electron_bundle_mover.mm:404-436`, where `ShouldContinueMove` defaults to `true` when no handler is passed).

So opening a stale copy, the original download still in `~/Downloads`, or one on a mounted dmg, neither of which Squirrel ever updates, destroyed the updated install and pinned the user to the version they first downloaded. "Restart & install" appeared to work because Squirrel patches the running bundle in `/Applications` and relaunches it directly; the next cold start through the stale icon undid it.

The decision now happens up front, from versions (`frontend/src/main/relocation.ts`):

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Already in an Applications folder | stay |
| `/Applications` is empty | relocate (unchanged behaviour) |
| Install is strictly older | relocate |
| Install is equal or newer | **hand off**: open it and quit |
| Any version unreadable or not semver | stay |

The only branch that destroys anything is `relocate`, and it is now reachable only when there is nothing newer to lose. `handoff` is what fixes the reported symptom end to end: clicking the old icon launches the current install instead of overwriting it.

`ao start` was re-propagating the same downgrade. `resolveApp` (`backend/internal/cli/start.go`) was marker-first, and the app rewrites that marker on every launch, so a stale copy that got launched left the marker pointing at itself. On macOS `/Applications` now outranks the marker. Still no version comparison, so invariant 5 holds.

## Layer 2: published builds baked the wrong update feed owner

`build-artifacts.yml`, the build the release conductor dispatches, was the only release workflow that never set `AO_RELEASE_REPO` (`frontend-release.yml:97,222` and `feature-release.yml:299,367` already did). So `forge.config.ts` fell back to `DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO`, stale since the AgentWrapper to Untrivial-ai transfer, and every published build points its updater at the old owner. Those builds work today only because GitHub still honours the rename redirect. That redirect is not a contract.

Ported from #3525: the env var on the make step, the "Verify baked update feed repo" assertion, `DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO` and `feature-builds.ts`'s `DEFAULT_REPO` moved to Untrivial-ai, and the post-update baked-owner assertion in `mac-update-e2e.yml`. The build-time assertion resolves because `forge.config.ts` writes `app-update.yml` to cwd and the job sets `defaults.run.working-directory: frontend`, verified by parsing the workflow.

What #3525 missed: `backend/internal/cli/start.go` `releaseRepo` was still `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`, and that is the URL `ao start` downloads the app from. Without it the redirect dependency survives on the install path even after the updater is fixed. Now Untrivial-ai.

## Backstop: the restart button dying silently

Ported from #3529, trimmed, and explicitly a backstop rather than a primary fix. An app on a read-only App Translocation mount cannot be swapped by Squirrel, so `quitAndInstall` does nothing at all: no restart, no error. The handoff above means far fewer users ever reach that state, but a first launch with nothing installed in `/Applications` still can.

Three corrections to the original:

1. **Parent directory writability.** ShipIt swaps by moving the bundle aside and moving the new one in, so the enclosing directory has to be writable too. A user-owned app in an unwritable folder passed the original check and still failed silently. Covered by a new test.
2. **Reworded the non-writable message.** The original told the user to move the app into `/Applications`, which reads as a bug to someone already there. It now names the offending directory. A test asserts the old wording is absent.
3. **`autoInstallOnAppQuit` was left true.** The dialog guarded the button, but all three check paths set install-on-quit, and the downloaded row tells the user the build installs on quit, so quitting stayed a silent dead end. All three now set it from the same verdict, and log when they disable it.

One addition of my own: the preflight derives a bundle path from `process.execPath`, which under `npm start` and in tests is a bare node/electron binary pointing at an unrelated ancestor directory. It now fails open on anything not ending in `.app`, so a dev machine's node location cannot decide installability.

## First install: why the dmg is not fixed here

Worth recording, because it is the cause upstream of layer 1 and it surprised me.

Every macOS user installs by unzipping into `~/Downloads` and launching from there, which is the exact input condition for App Translocation and for the stale-copy clobber. A dmg avoids it: mounting one shows the app beside an `/Applications` alias, and the drag is the install.

That dmg already exists and already has the drag layout. `makers/maker-dmg.ts` has built, signed, notarized and stapled one on every darwin build since #3294, and `dmg-builder`'s default `contents` is already the two icon layout. **It has simply never been published.** Zero `.dmg` assets across the last 30 releases.

The fix does not belong in this repo. Releases are cut by the release conductor, which dispatches `build-artifacts.yml`, downloads its artifacts, and signs the app itself. It cannot use a dmg built here: the app inside is unsigned, and codesigning inside a read-only image is not possible. The container also needs its own notarization, which needs the signing identity. Local testing settled the shape:

- a signed but unnotarized dmg is rejected outright, `source=Unnotarized Developer ID`, so the app's ticket does not cover the container
- building the image before the app is stapled leaves the nested app without a ticket, so a user who drags it out depends on reaching Apple at first launch

So the dmg has to be assembled where the identity lives, from the app the conductor has already stapled. That work is tracked against the conductor, not here.

What this PR does carry is `download/page.tsx`: it now prefers the dmg and falls back to the zip. That reads the live release list, so it resolves to the zip today and switches itself over the moment a release publishes the asset, with no further change here. The static `DOWNLOAD_URL_*` constants and the README tables stay on the zip, because a `releases/latest/download/...dmg` link 404s until the asset exists.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/main` → 282 passed, 0 failed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → clean. Also what confirms `app.isInApplicationsFolder()` against Electron 33.4.11's typings (`electron.d.ts:1355`).
- `go build ./...` clean, `go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestResolveApp` → 5 passed, `gofmt -l` clean, `golangci-lint run ./internal/cli/...` → 0 issues.
- Both workflows parse as YAML, and the new steps sit in jobs whose working directory makes their paths resolve.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `frontend/src/landing` -> clean. The landing app is not covered by PR CI (`deploy-landing.yml` only runs on push to main), so this was checked locally.
- The prefer-dmg-fall-back-to-zip logic asserted against the real v0.12.2 asset payload: resolves to the zip today, to the dmg once the alias is added, and drops the row when neither exists.

`go test ./internal/cli/...` has 6 failures on this machine, in `browser_test.go` and `spawn_test.go`. They are pre-existing and environmental: I reproduced the identical 6 on a clean `upstream/main` worktree, they fail by reaching the live daemon on the dev box (HTTP 404 / SESSION_NOT_FOUND), and they touch none of these files.

Unrelated to this branch: `npm ci` fails on `main` with `Missing: encoding@0.1.13 from lock file`, so the frontend was verified with `npm install --no-save`. The lockfile is untouched here. Worth a separate look.

## Still wants a human

The relocation branch only runs when `app.isPackaged` is true, so the handoff path has not been exercised on a packaged build. One manual pass on a signed build before release: put an old copy outside `/Applications`, install a newer one, launch the old copy, confirm the new one comes up and the install is untouched.

## Deliberately not here

From #3617: the app-state.json downgrade notice, still a separate PR. The dmg half of that item turned out to live in the release conductor, not here; see the section above.

title: fix(workspace): stop leaking a descriptor per watched file on macOS
body:
## What

Bumps `fsnotify` from v1.9.0 to v1.10.1 and adds a regression test for the file descriptors held by a workspace watcher.

## Why

The kqueue backend keeps one file descriptor per watched file, so a single `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/events` stream costs roughly 1,950 descriptors on an AO checkout. fsnotify v1.9.0 never releases them:

```go
func (w *kqueue) Close() error {
	if w.shared.close() { return nil }       // closes w.done, so isClosed() is now true
	pathsToRemove := w.watches.listPaths(false)
	for _, name := range pathsToRemove {
		w.Remove(name)                       // every call...
	}
	unix.Close(w.closepipe[1])
}

func (w *kqueue) remove(name string, unwatchFiles bool) error {
	if w.isClosed() { return nil }           // ...returns here
	...
	unix.Close(info.wd)                      // never runs
```

`Close` marks the watcher closed before running its own removal loop, and `remove` bails out early on a closed watcher, so the loop that releases the descriptors is dead code.

macOS caps a process at 61,440 descriptors (`kern.maxfilesperproc`), which is about 30 workspace streams. Once the daemon is at the cap, pooled database reads still succeed while anything needing a new descriptor fails, so the user-visible symptom is `GET /workspace/files` and `GET /workspace/events` returning a bare 500 on a daemon whose `/healthz` and `/api/v1/sessions` are green. Only restarting the app clears it.

Measured on a wedged daemon, one worktree held 31,951 descriptors across only 2,126 distinct paths: 16 leaked watcher trees for a single session.

## Isolating it

```
raw fsnotify: add 342 dirs -> 1,925 fds -> Close()      leaked 1,916
workspacewatch.Watch + context cancel                   leaked 1,944
raw fsnotify, Remove() each path BEFORE Close()         leaked 0
```

The third line rules out AO's teardown: `workspacewatch` cancels correctly, the descriptors simply are not returned unless removal runs before `Close`.

Upstream tracked this as fsnotify#732 and fixed it in fsnotify#740 ("kqueue: drop watches directly in Close() instead of going through remove()"), released in v1.10.1 on 2026-05-04. The dependency was added at v1.9.0 in #3492 on 2026-08-03, three months after the fix shipped, and was not previously in `go.sum`, so nothing in the module graph required that version.

## Test

`TestWatchReleasesDescriptorsOnCancel` builds a 400-file tree, watches it, cancels, and asserts descriptors return to baseline. It pins the accounting rather than the version string:

- on v1.9.0: `FAIL ... leaked 421 of 424 opened`
- on v1.10.1: passes

`workspacewatch` is the only importer of fsnotify. `go build ./...`, the `workspacewatch` and `httpd` suites, and `golangci-lint` on the package are clean.

title: fix: preserve successful delegated task spawns
body:
## Summary

- give delegated workers an immediate provisional display name derived from the task brief
- treat orchestrator discovery and title refinement as best effort after worker spawn commits
- skip exited orchestrators while retaining the guarded send for lifecycle races
- add regression coverage for exited targets, title derivation, and title-send failure

## Why

The delegate endpoint could spawn and start a worker, then select an exited-but-not-terminated orchestrator for the optional title request. Sessionguard correctly refused that write, but the service propagated the follow-up error and returned 500 even though the worker already existed. A retry could then create a duplicate worker.

This change makes worker spawn the success boundary. Title refinement can still improve the provisional title, but it cannot revoke a completed spawn.

## Testing

- cd backend && go test ./internal/service/session ./internal/httpd/controllers
- cd backend && go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs
- native Electron dev verification with an exited, non-terminated orchestrator: delegate returned 202 and the worker appeared with its task-derived title

## Verification limitation

The repo-wide npm run lint gate was attempted but its Go test phase was not clean locally: internal/adapters/agent/fake TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination took about 6 seconds and failed its under-one-second speedup assertion. The package is unrelated to this diff; the touched package tests and golangci-lint pass.

No API contract or generated artifact changes are required.
