title: fix: handle agy model discovery pipe drain timeout
body:
## What

Fix Agy model discovery when `agy models` returns valid model output but Go reports `exec.ErrWaitDelay` while waiting for inherited stdout/stderr pipes to close.

Also add an Agy-specific parser for the current tab-separated model output format.

## Why

Agy model discovery could fail even though `agy models` had already returned a valid list of models.

The current Agy CLI outputs models in the form:

```text
gemini-3.6-flash-high    Gemini 3.6 Flash (High)
claude-sonnet-4-6        Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking)
```

Two issues prevented AO from using this output reliably:

1. The generic model parser only accepted single-field model ID lines and did not handle Agy's tab-separated ID/label format.
2. Go `os/exec` could return `exec.ErrWaitDelay` after Agy had already produced valid output because a descendant process kept the output pipes open.

This caused model discovery to fail even when usable model data was available.

Related to #3385.

## How

- Add `parseAgyModels` for Agy's tab-separated model ID and display-label output.
- Keep backwards compatibility with Agy versions that output only a model ID.
- Allow Agy discovery to parse already-produced output when the command ends with `exec.ErrWaitDelay`.
- Preserve the existing error behavior when no usable models are present.
- Keep the generic `parseIDLines` behavior unchanged for other adapters.

The `ErrWaitDelay` exception is intentionally scoped only to Agy rather than weakening model discovery behavior globally.

## Testing

Added coverage for:

- tab-separated Agy model IDs and labels
- multiple Agy model entries
- backwards-compatible model-ID-only output
- Agy model discovery behavior when valid output accompanies a pipe-drain timeout

Validated locally with the real Agy CLI and confirmed that the model catalog is discovered successfully.

Relevant tests:

```bash
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/... -count=1
go test ./...
```

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; related to #3385
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for changed behavior
- [x] Relevant Go checks pass

title: GPU process crashes 3x on startup (SIGABRT) on Wayland + hybrid GPU; no way to disable hardware acceleration
body:
## Bug

On Linux with Wayland and a hybrid Intel + NVIDIA laptop GPU, AO's GPU process crashes three times while the app starts. Chromium then gives up on the GPU and runs in software mode. The app still works, but the first ~35 seconds are unstable, and rendering stays on the slow software path afterwards.

The crash itself comes from the graphics driver, not from AO's code. The AO-side problem is that there is **no way to opt out**. AO sets no Electron GPU or Ozone options at all, so a user on a broken driver stack cannot tell the app to skip the GPU. Their only options are editing the source or living with it.

**Analyzed against:** `35da72b6c78491227fd5dbe3eaed2b8b0599f045` | **AO version:** 0.10.3
**Confidence:** High

## Environment

- OS: Omarchy (Arch Linux), kernel 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Compositor: Hyprland on Wayland, `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=wayland`
- GPU: hybrid — Intel Raptor Lake-P UHD (`8086:a7a8`) + NVIDIA RTX 5050 Max-Q (`10de:2d98`)
- mesa 26.1.5, Electron 33.4.11, node 26.2.0
- Started with `cd frontend && npm run dev`

## Reproduction

1. On a Wayland session with a hybrid Intel + NVIDIA GPU, run `cd frontend && npm run dev`.
2. Watch the terminal output for the first minute.
3. The GPU process crashes three times, about 18 seconds apart, then stops.

This happened on two separate runs of the app, so it is not a one-off:

| Run | Crash 1 | Crash 2 | Crash 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First | 22:44:34 | 22:44:52 | 22:45:09 |
| Second | 22:48:22 | 22:48:40 | 22:48:57 |

## What the logs show

Each crash is `exit_code=134`, which is SIGABRT:

```
[521942:0813/224822.770984:ERROR:gpu_process_host.cc(982)] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=134
[521942:0813/224822.771008:WARNING:gpu_process_host.cc(1416)] The GPU process has crashed 1 time(s)
[521942:0813/224840.311716:ERROR:gpu_process_host.cc(982)] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=134
[521942:0813/224840.311729:WARNING:gpu_process_host.cc(1416)] The GPU process has crashed 2 time(s)
[521942:0813/224857.825508:ERROR:gpu_process_host.cc(982)] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=134
[521942:0813/224857.825547:WARNING:gpu_process_host.cc(1416)] The GPU process has crashed 3 time(s)
```

Before each crash, the GPU process cannot allocate a buffer, and the Intel driver reports it is out of memory:

```
[ERROR:gbm_pixmap_wayland.cc(82)] Cannot create bo with format= RGBA_8888 and usage=SCANOUT
intel: the execbuf ioctl keeps returning ENOMEM
```

Those appear 9 and 3 times respectively across the run — roughly once per GPU process restart.

After the third crash, Chromium stops retrying. There are no further GPU crashes in the log, which continues normally for another 15 minutes.

## Root cause

The crash is in the driver and compositor stack, so AO cannot fix it directly.

What AO controls is whether a user can work around it, and right now they cannot:

- `frontend/src/main.ts` — searching for `commandLine`, `appendSwitch`, `appendArgument`, `disableHardwareAcceleration`, or `ozone` returns **zero** matches. No GPU or Ozone options are set anywhere.
- `frontend/forge.config.ts` — no GPU or Ozone flags.
- The only `--disable-gpu` in the repo is in a test harness (`test/e2e-pod/real-app.spec.ts:60`) and does not affect the shipped app.

## Suggested fix

Small and self-contained: let the user turn hardware acceleration off with an environment variable.

In `frontend/src/main.ts`, before `app.whenReady()`:

```ts
if (process.env.AO_DISABLE_GPU === "1") {
	app.disableHardwareAcceleration();
}
```

Then add a line to the Linux troubleshooting notes in `docs/development.md`.

I would deliberately keep it at that. Auto-detecting repeated GPU crashes and restarting in software mode is not worth the complexity, because Chromium already falls back on its own after three crashes.

## Impact

- About 35 seconds of unstable startup on affected Linux/Wayland machines, with the GPU process dying and restarting three times.
- Rendering stays on the software path afterwards. Follow-on errors continue in the log: `Automatic fallback to software WebGL has been deprecated`, `Buffer handle is null. Not creating a mailbox from it.`, and `Creation of StagingBuffer's SharedImage failed.`
- No supported way to skip the crashing startup path — no flag, environment variable, or setting.
- **Not verified:** whether crashes return under heavy GPU load. The logs only cover an idle app after the fallback, so severity beyond startup is unproven.

## Related

No duplicate found. Searches with `--state all` for `hardware acceleration`, `disableHardwareAcceleration`, and `ozone` returned nothing. `wayland` returned only [#2491](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2491) and [#2778](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2778), both unrelated.

The WebGL errors listed above also show up in [#3787](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3787), where I reproduced a separate terminal crash on this machine. They are not the cause of that crash — the two are independent, and this issue covers only the GPU process problem.

I have the affected hardware and am happy to test a fix.

title: fix: reset model scope across agent switches
body:
## What

Reset model and mode overrides when switching a conversation between agent harnesses.

- Clear the source harness model/mode before resolving the target launch configuration.
- Persist the switched conversation without retaining stale overrides.
- Reset renderer controls and cached catalog state so the target harness supplies its own defaults.
- Add backend, storage, hook, and dialog regression coverage for both switch directions.

## Why

A model selected for one agent could be reused after switching to a different agent. That stale model might not exist in the target harness and could make the next request fail.

## How

Agent switching now establishes a fresh model scope. The backend clears source overrides and resolves the target harness configuration independently. The renderer mirrors that invariant by resetting selected model/mode state and refetching the target catalog after a successful switch. Sends omit the model when the target is using its default.

The SQLite query was updated and its generated code regenerated through the repository workflow.

title: fix: update Agy hooks for current Antigravity schema
body:
## What

Update the Agy hook integration to use the current Antigravity workspace hook format.

This replaces the legacy Agy hook configuration:

```text
.gemini/hooks.json
SessionStart
SessionEnd
BeforeAgent
AfterAgent
AfterTool
```

with the current Antigravity workspace hook configuration:

```text
.agents/hooks.json
PreInvocation
PostInvocation
PostToolUse
Stop
```

AO keeps its existing internal activity commands:

```text
PreInvocation  -> ao hooks agy before-agent
PostToolUse    -> ao hooks agy after-tool
PostInvocation -> ao hooks agy after-agent
Stop           -> ao hooks agy after-agent
```

## Why

Agy workers could launch and run normally, but AO could still show them as `No signal`.

The generated worktree contained `.gemini/hooks.json`, while current Antigravity did not consume those legacy workspace hooks. AO therefore never received an activity callback, so the worker eventually became `no_signal`.

This was reproduced with a real AO-managed Agy worker:

```text
harness: agy
activity.state: idle
status: no_signal
```

After using the current `.agents/hooks.json` schema, the same session began reporting activity correctly:

```text
harness: agy
activity.state: idle
status: idle
```

A fresh worker was then validated end-to-end and created `.agents/hooks.json` automatically without any manual worktree modification.

## How

- Move Agy workspace hooks to `.agents/hooks.json`.
- Use `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, `PostToolUse`, and `Stop`.
- Preserve AO's existing internal activity event handling.
- Treat `Stop` as idle rather than process/session exit.
- Store AO hooks under a dedicated `agent-orchestrator` top-level definition.
- Preserve unrelated user-defined hooks.
- Make installation idempotent.
- Remove only AO-managed hooks during uninstall.
- Report hooks as installed only when the complete AO-managed definition is present.
- Stop generating legacy `.gemini/hooks.json`.

## Testing

Added/updated tests covering:

- installation into `.agents/hooks.json`
- current Antigravity event mappings
- absence of legacy `.gemini/hooks.json`
- idempotent installation
- preservation of user-defined hooks
- uninstall removing only AO-managed hooks
- incomplete managed definitions reporting as not installed

Validated locally with:

```bash
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... -count=1 -v
go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1
go test ./...
```

Also validated end-to-end with a fresh Agy TUI worker; the worker transitioned to `idle` instead of `no_signal` and generated `.agents/hooks.json` automatically.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch based directly on current upstream `main`
- [x] One focused Agy / Antigravity compatibility fix
- [x] Existing user hooks are preserved
- [x] Hook installation is idempotent
- [x] Legacy `.gemini/hooks.json` is no longer generated
- [x] Fresh Agy worker validated end-to-end
- [x] Relevant Go tests pass

title: [Bug]: Unset defaultBranch still forces workspace roots to main
body:
## Bug

After [#3810](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3810) was fixed for workspace children, an unconfigured workspace root still receives `main` as its base branch. A workspace whose root default branch is `trunk`, `master`, or another non-`main` branch therefore still fails to spawn with `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` unless the user manually configures that branch.

**Source:** Follow-up to [#3810](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3810) | **Reported by:** @subbu-fw | **Analyzed against:** `0f43574f20aa`

**Priority:** medium — workspace spawn is broken for non-`main` roots, but explicitly setting `defaultBranch` is a workaround.

**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Register a workspace whose root repository advertises `origin/HEAD -> origin/trunk` and has no `main` branch.
2. Leave project `defaultBranch` unset.
3. Spawn a worker or orchestrator.
4. Observe `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` for the workspace root.

A deterministic manager regression assertion reproduces the bad handoff:

```shell
cd backend
go test ./internal/session_manager -run '^TestSpawn_WorkspaceProjectRecordsRootAndChildWorktrees$' -count=1
```

Current failure:

```text
root base branch = "main", want empty so adapter infers the repo default
```

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` resolves an unset workspace root with `project.Config.WithDefaults().DefaultBranch`. `ProjectConfig` currently defaults `defaultBranch` to `main`, so the manager passes a non-empty `BaseBranch` to the git-worktree adapter. A non-empty value bypasses the adapter's per-repository `origin/HEAD` inference.

The same default leaks into settings: when config omits the field, the form falls back to the project's resolved `defaultBranch` and can persist `main` while saving unrelated settings.

## Fix

- Make automatic repository-default resolution the default branch-selection mode (`auto`).
- Translate automatic mode to an empty `BaseBranch` only at the workspace interface, where empty means infer `origin/HEAD` per repository.
- Preserve explicitly configured branch refs.
- Keep `main` only as the last-resort Git initialization/adapter fallback.
- Prevent settings saves from turning automatic mode into an explicit `main` pin.
- Cover the root plus mixed child defaults through the manager and real git-worktree adapter tests.

## Impact

- Workspace roots no longer require a `main` branch.
- Single-repository projects also follow their Git default unless explicitly pinned.
- Existing explicit branch configurations keep their current behavior.

## Related

- [#3810](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3810) / [PR #3830](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3830) — fixed per-child branch inheritance.
- [#2329](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2329) — persist child repository default-branch metadata.

title: fix(workspace): resolve automatic repository defaults
body:
## Summary

- make `auto` the default branch-selection mode without treating it as a literal Git branch
- choose each repository's primary remote using `checkout.defaultRemote`, then `origin`, then a sole remote
- resolve the live symbolic remote `HEAD`, fetch that exact branch, and fall back only to the same remote's cached `HEAD`
- allow an already-fetched request-specific remote branch to seed a session even when the remote has no symbolic `HEAD`
- resolve every repository in a workspace before creating session branches, preventing partial workspace state
- persist each repository's resolved base ref so diffs can recompute the merge base after rebases or upstream advances
- preserve explicit branch settings and AO-initialized remoteless repositories, including backfilling repositories created by older AO versions
- return `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` with repository-specific Git remediation instead of guessing the current branch, `main`, or `master`
- omit the internal `auto` sentinel from agent branch context

Fixes #3981

## Behavior

A temporary local checkout no longer changes the base branch AO selects. Workspace roots and child repositories resolve independently, so a workspace can safely mix defaults such as `trunk`, `dev`, and `main`.

The adapter returns the authoritative base ref it selected. Single-repository sessions store it in their diff metadata, while workspace sessions store one base SHA and ref per repository. Review and workspace diffs therefore remain accurate after rebases and default-branch updates.

For a single repository or workspace root with no authoritative Git default, configure `defaultBranch` explicitly. For an unresolved workspace child, configure its primary remote and cached remote `HEAD` with Git. AO-created remoteless repositories use the branch AO recorded during initialization.

## Storage

Migration `0095_session_worktree_base_ref.sql` adds the per-repository `base_ref` needed by workspace comparisons.

## Verification

- `go test -p 1 ./... -count=1`
- `go build ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- focused race tests for the resolver, git-worktree adapter, project service, session manager, session service, and SQLite store

title: fix(chat): stop freezes, attachment loss, and turn-state desync
body:
Fixes #3945, fixes #3884, fixes #3878, fixes #3749 — the P1 reliability/data-loss cluster in the Chat UI surface.

These four bugs share one theme: durable conversation state, in-memory controller state, and the disposable worktree had mismatched lifetimes and authority. This PR makes durable state authoritative for what the user sees and can act on, and stops ephemeral state (worktrees, nested provider turns, capped output deltas) from destroying or wedging it.

## #3945 — Chat UI freezes when a command exceeds the output cap; Terminal unreachable

**Root causes fixed:**
- `AppendConversationActivityOutput` (and its streamed-text sibling) kept bumping `revision`/`updated_at` on every delta after the 64K cap, firing a CDC event → SSE push → full snapshot refetch per delta for bytes that could no longer change. A vite dev server past the cap turned that into a re-render storm that froze the page. The queries now skip the row entirely once its truncation flag is set (`AND command_output_truncated = 0`), so capped deltas produce **zero** CDC traffic. The settled aggregate on `item/completed` still lands.
- An interrupt-policy chat→TUI handoff waited forever for the provider to settle the cancelled turn. If the provider is wedged on the very command the user is escaping, the switch never completed ("policy dialog that cannot complete"). `BeginHandoff` now bounds that wait (`handoffSettleWait`, 10s default) and reconciles the durable turn as interrupted so the switch always completes — the terminal is the escape hatch and must always be reachable.

## #3884 — restart recovery deletes image attachments (data loss)

Attachment bytes now have a durable owner: `$AO_DATA_DIR/attachments/<session-id>/` (new `internal/attachments` package), with the worktree `.ao/attachments` copy demoted to a projection. Follows the fix direction laid out in the issue:

- **Stage atomically:** canonical copy first (tmp+rename, 0600); a failed durable write refuses the attachment instead of accepting bytes that vanish on the next restart. The existing worktree-relative refs are unchanged.
- **Serve durably:** the preview route serves strictly-validated `.ao/attachments/<name>` references from durable storage when the worktree copy is missing; a live worktree copy still wins; ordinary preview files stay confined to the workspace.
- **Restore projection:** `RestoreAll` rematerializes the session's durable attachments into the recreated worktree (and re-adds the git exclude) before the controller relaunches.
- **Upgrade safely:** `saveAndTeardownOne` imports legacy worktree-only attachments into durable storage *before* `ForceDestroy` — the exact seam that used to delete their only bytes. Covers attachments staged by pre-fix builds, including spawn attachments.
- **Cleanup tied to durable ownership:** canonical bytes are never removed on runtime teardown or worktree recycling.
- **Security:** strict name validation (no separators/traversal/hidden files), symlinks never followed into or out of durable storage, cross-session access impossible by construction.

## #3878 — nested Codex turns drain queued automation prematurely

Applies the fix from PR #3890 by @Dhruv-Sharma01 (rebased cleanly onto main; commit authorship preserved): `ChatEvent` carries `ProviderConversationID`, only root-thread lifecycle events can claim/release primary turn ownership, in-memory ownership updates move to post-commit (`applyCommittedTurnLifecycle`), nested completions no longer report idle or drain the queue, handoff quiescence is serialized behind `sendMu`, and adapter interrupts target the root turn.

## #3749 — "Stop turn" returns CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN while the UI shows a running turn

Composes the approach from PR #3752 by @xRealBlue on top of the nested-turn lifecycle fix:

- **Durable-state fallback:** when memory says nothing is running but SQLite has a `running` turn (failed projection, restart, dispatch race), `Interrupt` reconciles it instead of refusing — serialized behind `sendMu` so a mid-dispatch state can't be misread.
- **Provider-refusal reconciliation:** `ErrChatNoActiveTurn` for a turn memory still tracks now settles the durable row rather than surfacing a bare error that leaves the user stuck on "Working".
- **`reconcileDurableTurn`** delivers the full Interrupt contract in one place: best-effort provider cancel, settle as interrupted, clear memory, cancel the queue behind it, report idle.
- **Client resilience:** the renderer and mobile clients refetch the conversation when an interrupt fails, so a stale "Working" bar is discovered instead of kept.

The projection-transaction half of the desync (memory mutated inside a rollback-able transaction) is fixed structurally by the post-commit lifecycle handling from the #3878 fix.

## Tests

New coverage (all requested seams):
- **Attachment survival across restart:** `TestAttachmentsSurviveTeardownAndRestore` (manager-level, incl. legacy import), `TestSessionsAPI_PreviewServesDurableAttachmentAfterWorktreeLoss` (HTTP incl. traversal + cross-session rejection), `internal/attachments` unit tests (validation, symlink skip, atomic store), and the lifecycle-level e2e `TestChatAttachmentSurvivesADaemonRestart` (real daemon, real codex, real restart — the exact repro from the issue).
- **Stop-turn authority under desync:** `TestInterruptReconcilesStaleRunningTurnOnDisk`, `TestProviderRefusalReconcilesTheDurableTurnAsInterrupted`, `TestInterruptReconciliationCancelsQueuedTurns`, `TestInterruptReturnsNoActiveTurnWhenNoRunningTurnAnywhere`, and `TestProjectionFailureThenStopStillStopsTheTurn` (the exact #3749 sequence: failed `turn/completed` projection, then Stop).
- **Output-cap non-wedge:** `TestCappedOutputStopsBumpingRevision` (revision frozen after truncation), `TestInterruptHandoffCompletesWhenProviderNeverSettlesTheTurn` (bounded escape to Terminal).
- **Nested-turn automation ordering:** `TestNestedTurnCompletionDoesNotDrainQueueWhilePrimaryTurnRuns`, `TestChatHandoffDrainWaitsForRootAfterNestedTurnCompletes`, plus adapter/normalizer tests (from #3890).

Validation run:
- `go test ./...` — green (the `internal/cli` spawn tests fail only when AO_* env vars from a live AO session leak into the test env; they pass with a clean env and fail identically on unmodified `main`).
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — clean.
- End-to-end: `AO_CHAT_E2E=1 go test ./e2e/ -run TestChatAttachmentSurvivesADaemonRestart` — real daemon binary, real codex session, attachment staged → daemon stop → recovery → same preview URL serves the same bytes and the resumed agent reads the same path.

## Known follow-ups (out of scope)

- #3878's "acknowledgement recovery for a dispatched provider ID that never emits turn.started" is not implemented here (nor in #3890); Stop-based reconciliation covers user recovery in the meantime.
- The `groupByTurn` presentation defect (parent activity anchored above completed child cards) from #3878's "UI clarity" section is a separate rendering change.
- #3950/#3951 (interface-switch recovery banner persistence) remain separate.

## Relationship to open PRs

- #3890 (nested turns) is included as its own commit with original authorship — this PR supersedes it only by also carrying the three sibling fixes; happy to rebase if #3890 lands first.
- #3752 (stop-turn desync) is re-implemented here on top of the nested-turn lifecycle (the two PRs conflict in `controller.go`); its author is credited as commit co-author.

title: chore(terminal): remove Clear context-menu item that never persisted on agent TUI panes
body: ## What Removes the "Clear" context-menu item from the terminal pane (`XtermTerminal.tsx`), along with its associated test coverage and now-unused i18n strings across all locales. ## Why The Clear action only cleared the local xterm.js buffer (`term.clear()`). For shell panes this looked correct, but for agent TUI panes (Codex, Claude Code, etc.) the agent process owns and continuously repaints its own transcript from memory on every redraw (resize, tick, etc.), so the cleared view would immediately repopulate — making the button appear broken/inconsistent depending on pane type. Investigated a proper fix (runtime-level scrollback truncation for tmux/conpty, plus a provider-aware "Clear conversation" action sending `/clear` to the agent). On review, decided against shipping either: - Runtime-level clear only ever fixes the shell-pane case; it can't stop a TUI from repainting its own transcript. - A "Clear conversation" button would just duplicate a command (`/clear`) every supported agent CLI already exposes natively — users can type it directly in the terminal today, no UI needed. Given that, the button wasn't earning its complexity. Removing it entirely rather than shipping a partially-working or duplicative feature. ## How - Removed the "Clear" item from the terminal context menu and its handler in `XtermTerminal.tsx`. - Removed the corresponding test case in `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`. - Removed the now-unused `terminal.clear` (or equivalent) i18n key from all locale files (`en`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN`). - No backend changes — this is a pure UI removal. - Intentional omission: no replacement action was added. Users who want to clear an agent's transcript/context can already type `/clear` directly in the terminal, which is the native, provider-supported way to do it. ## Testing - `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` - Targeted vitest run for `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` - Manual: opened the terminal context menu on both a shell pane and an agent (Codex) pane in dev — Clear item no longer appears in either. before : after: changes(suggested) - two diffrent buttons changes(approved by @illegalcall) ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): make Stop authoritative for durable running turns
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3749

## Summary

- Treat the durable running turn rendered by the UI as actionable when Stop finds no in-memory turn.
- Make Stop linearize with dispatch under `sendMu`, capture the exact pre-Stop target and queue cutoff, and wait for that turn acknowledgment without following ownership to newer work.
- Reconcile every running turn visible on the active branch, including overlapping root and nested provider turns, while keeping provider cancellation best-effort.
- Move controller-state memory changes after the durable projection commits so a rollback cannot recreate the memory/SQLite split.
- Refetch the desktop conversation after an interrupt error so stale cached Working state is not left on screen.

PR #3890 is merged into `main` and supplies the nested-turn ownership rules this recovery path relies on. This PR is based directly on current `main` and contains only the focused recovery work for #3749.

The implementation was adapted from PR #3752 by @bluwwi and extracted from the tested recovery work in PR #3986. Contributor attribution is preserved in the commit history.

## Regression coverage

- The exact #3749 projection-rollback sequence: SQLite remains `running`, the provider refuses Stop, and reconciliation settles the durable state.
- A durable running turn with no in-memory pending ID.
- A genuine absence of both durable and in-memory running work.
- Stop racing an in-progress dispatch waits for provider acknowledgment.
- Root and nested visible running turns are both settled, while Stop targets the same oldest/root turn shown by the UI.
- Queue cancellation during recovery without accidental dispatch of pre-Stop work.
- A prompt submitted after Stop survives durable fallback and provider-refusal recovery.
- A completion committed before provider refusal is not overwritten.
- Controller state changes only after projection commit.
- Recovered interrupted turns have no error message.
- Desktop interrupt errors invalidate the conversation query.

title: fix: reset model scope across agent switches
body:
## What

Apply the cross-agent model reset fix directly to `main`.

- Clear stale conversation model and reasoning overrides after an agent switch.
- Scope configured model/mode values to their configured harness while preserving harness-neutral permissions.
- Preserve an explicit target-model selection for the target launch or resume.
- Reset renderer model/mode controls and refetch the target catalog after switching.
- Add backend, storage, hook, and dialog regression coverage.

## Why

PR #3976 was merged into `codex/agent-switching-ux` after that feature branch had already been merged into `main` by PR #3770. Git does not propagate later commits from a closed feature branch into `main`, so the fix is not currently present there.

This PR ports the exact #3976 change onto current `main` as one focused commit.

## How

The backend treats an agent switch as a new model scope. Project/role model and mode settings are retained only when their configured harness matches the target; permissions remain applicable across harnesses. A non-empty model explicitly supplied by the switch request then overrides the target model.

The renderer clears local selection state and invalidates the target model/config catalog after a successful switch. The SQLite query source was applied and generated Go verified with `npm run sqlc`.

title: feat(telemetry): track per-session agent token usage and cost
body:
## What

Adds an end-to-end pipeline to capture agent LLM token usage and dollar
cost per session, sliceable in PostHog by user, session, and harness.
There is no token/cost data captured anywhere today, so this is a new
pipeline rather than a new chart.

## Events

- `ao.session.turn_usage` (aliased to `ao.v2.session.turn_usage`): one per
  model turn, with `model`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
  `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `cost_usd`,
  `model_priced`, `harness`, `kind`.
- `ao.session.usage` (aliased to `ao.v2.session.usage`): one per session at
  end, same fields plus `turn_count` and `duration_ms`.

Both auto-carry the install `distinct_id` and hashed `session_id`, which is
what enables the per-user / per-session / per-harness cuts.

## How it works

1. The claude-code `Stop` / `SessionEnd` hook payload carries
   `transcript_path`. `ao hooks claude-code stop|session-end` parses the
   transcript JSONL for per-turn usage, resuming from a persisted byte
   offset so a turn is never counted twice, and POSTs to the daemon.
2. `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/usage` decodes the report; token counts are
   clamped non-negative and the body is size-capped.
3. `Service.RecordUsage` reads harness/kind/project from the stored session
   record (so tags cannot be spoofed by the caller), prices each turn from a
   list-price table, and emits the two events. Unknown models record tokens
   with `cost_usd: 0` and `model_priced: false`.

The hook path is best-effort throughout: a missing transcript, read error,
or unreachable daemon all exit quietly so the agent is never disrupted.

## Pricing

Single editable table of Anthropic list prices (USD per million tokens),
with cache-write at 1.25x input and cache-read at 0.1x input:

| Model  | input | output | cache write | cache read |
|--------|-------|--------|-------------|------------|
| Opus   | 15    | 75     | 18.75       | 1.50       |
| Sonnet | 3     | 15     | 3.75        | 0.30       |
| Haiku  | 0.80  | 4      | 1.00        | 0.08       |

## Scope

claude-code only for now; other harnesses emit no usage until their
transcript parsers are added, so a "by harness" view shows one slice until
then. Per-turn events are unaggregated by design (both per-turn and summary
were requested); a long session emits one event per turn.

## Verification

Ran the daemon against an isolated data dir and drove the endpoint with a
real session (fake harness):
- Opus turn 1M in + 1M out reported `cost_usd: 90`; a gpt-4o turn reported
  `cost_usd: 0` / `model_priced: false` with tokens intact; summary
  `cost_usd: 90.045`, `turn_count: 2`, `duration_ms: 4200`.
- A body with `"harness":"evil"` was ignored; the event recorded
  `harness: fake` from the stored record (Sonnet priced at $3).
- Error paths: unknown session 404, empty body 400 `USAGE_EMPTY`, malformed
  JSON 400 `INVALID_JSON`, GET 405.

Unit + integration tests cover pricing, the transcript parser (partial-line
no-double-count, malformed/zero skip, single-pass summary+duration), the
service emit/pricing path, the negative-token clamp, and the CLI hook
through a test server (incremental stop reporting, offset dedup, session-end
summary, non-claude ignored). `gofmt`, `go vet`, and the OpenAPI route/spec
parity check pass.

title: feat(landing): Product Hunt launch analytics and UTM link registry
body:
## What

Adds a self-contained Product Hunt launch analytics layer to the landing
site, plus the canonical UTM link registry. Built to merge in a hurry:
**all new files under a `launch/` module + two components; the only edit
to existing code is one mount line in `app/layout.tsx`.**

## Deliberately scoped ("only the relevant things")

Most of the launch spec already exists on the site, so it is not
re-implemented:
- **PostHog autocapture** already gives page views, sessions, session
  duration, bounce, referrer, country, device, browser, unique visitors.
- **`campaign.ts`** already captures and persists `utm_*` across the tab.
- **Existing events:** `download_clicked`, `waitlist_signup`,
  `install_command_copied`, `section_viewed`, `video_*`,
  `outbound_link_clicked`.

App-side product events from the spec (`signup_completed`,
`workspace_created`, `agent_created`, `workflow_*`, `orchestrator_created`,
`*_connected`, ...) are **not** added here: they happen inside the desktop
app/daemon, which emits its own usage events. Faking them on the marketing
site would be wrong.

## What this adds (the real gap)

- **UTM link registry** (`launch/utm.ts`): one tagged `aoagents.dev` link
  per channel (Product Hunt, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Discord, GitHub, and an
  Instagram placeholder since no account exists yet).
- **Normalized attribution** (`launch/context.ts`): collapses the visit
  into `source` / `campaign` / `user_type` / `device`.
- **PH-specific events** (`launch/events.ts`): `ph_referral_visit`,
  `ph_badge_click`, `ph_upvote_cta_click`, `return_visit`.
  (`ph_comment_cta_click` is intentionally omitted until a comment CTA
  actually exists on the site.)
- **`LaunchAnalytics`** (mounted once): registers `source`/`campaign`/
  `device` as PostHog **super-properties**, so every event, including
  autocaptured pageviews and the existing CTA events, becomes attributable
  to the launch source **without touching those call sites**. Fires
  `ph_referral_visit` and `return_visit`.
- **`ProductHuntBadge`**: drop-in badge to our PH page that fires
  `ph_badge_click`.

## The funnel

`PH visit → CTA click` is covered here (`ph_referral_visit` / `source` on
the existing CTA events). `signup → workspace → first agent → first
successful orchestration` are **app-side** events in the same PostHog
project; the README explains the boundary.

## Caveat on the numbers

The site is opt-out by default behind cookie consent, so counts are "of
consenting visitors" and undercount raw PH traffic. Read rates/trends, not
absolutes. Documented in the README.

## Testing

- **Unit tests (verified passing, 14/14):** `launch/utm.test.ts` +
  `launch/context.test.ts` cover UTM link building, source/device
  classification, and the channel registry. Run:
  `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/landing/src/lib/analytics/launch`.
- **Browser:** run the landing dev server, open
  `/?utm_source=product_hunt&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=launch_day`,
  accept consent, `posthog.debug()`, and confirm `ph_referral_visit` plus
  `source: product_hunt` on every event (steps in the README).

I verified the pure logic by running the real test files under vitest. The
two React components and the `track()` wrapper follow existing conventions
and were not driven live end-to-end to PostHog (that needs the dev server +
a PostHog key); the browser steps above are how to confirm that path.

title: fix(chat): keep fitting files after an oversized batch item
body:
Fixes #4080.

## What changed

The production `useFileAttachments.addFiles` loop now skips only a file that exceeds the remaining 25 MiB budget and continues evaluating later files in the same paste, drop, or file-picker batch. The count cap intentionally still stops the loop because no subsequent file can fit once the attachment count is full.

This PR was rebased onto current `main` and narrowed during review to this one issue. The unrelated attachment-only steering fix has moved to its own issue and PR. Changes to the unused `useImageAttachments` hook were removed so this stays on the live Chat path.

## Tests

- Regression test proves a 9 + 9 + rejected 9 + later 5 MiB batch retains the first, second, and fourth files.
- Focused test: 5 passed.
- Frontend typecheck: passed.
- Full frontend suite: 191 files; 2,505 passed and 1 skipped.

title: fix(desktop): render reviewer terminal inside Chat surface instead of swapping in CenterPane
body:
## Bug

In a **Chat-mode session**, clicking the Reviewer tab in the chat header tears down the entire chat surface and swaps in the terminal UI (`CenterPane`). The chat timeline, composer, and scroll position are lost; the tab strip the user just clicked disappears from under their cursor. The design intent — chat UI stays when available, terminal is the fallback — is inverted: a terminal-only construct (the reviewer pane) replaces the whole chat surface instead of rendering inside it.

**Source:** chat report | **Analyzed against:** `1ec3acf9f353a7dfda3065f7e2931a6f600fc289`
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Open a worker session in `mode: "chat"` with a PR
2. Trigger a review (inspector → Run Review, or agent pushes with auto-review on)
3. The Reviewer tab appears in the chat header
4. Click it → the entire chat surface unmounts and `CenterPane` (terminal UI) mounts in its place
5. Chat history scroll position, composer draft, and the chat tab strip are gone; to get back you must find the worker tab in `CenterPane` and click back

Expected: the chat surface stays mounted. The reviewer tab renders the reviewer `TerminalPane` as the *content* of the chat surface, exactly like `CenterPane` renders it as content of the terminal surface. The worker chat tab remains one click away in the same header.

## Root Cause

`SessionView.tsx` gates the whole surface on the terminal target:

```tsx
// frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx
const showChatSurface = session?.mode === "chat" && routedTerminalTarget.kind === "worker";
```

When the reviewer tab (added in PR #3962) calls `selectReviewerTerminal`, `terminalTarget.kind` becomes `"reviewer"`, `showChatSurface` flips to `false`, and the ternary mounts `CenterPane` in place of `SessionChatSurface`. The reviewer tab lives in `ChatWorkspace`'s `ChatHeader` (`aria-label="Chat tabs"` tablist), so the surface it belongs to is replaced the moment it is used.

`TerminalPane` itself is surface-agnostic — it owns its xterm/mux lifecycle, works under the shell-level `TerminalCacheProvider`, and reviewer panes intentionally skip the retained terminal cache (`terminalTarget?.kind === "reviewer"` returns no cache key). Nothing structural prevents rendering it inside the chat surface.

## Fix

Make the chat surface a tabbed container:

1. `SessionView.tsx`: treat reviewer targets as part of the chat surface in chat mode — `showChatSurface` when `mode === "chat" && target.kind !== "shell"`. Pass `terminalTarget`, `daemonReady`, and `theme` into `SessionChatSurface`.
2. `SessionChatSurface.tsx`: forward those props.
3. `ChatWorkspace.tsx`: derive the active tab from `terminalTarget.kind`; render `<TerminalPane terminalTarget={...reviewer...}>` as the body when the reviewer tab is active; render the existing timeline/composer when the chat tab is active. The existing font-size controls already span 11–24px, matching the terminal range, so they apply to whichever content is active.
4. Mark the active tab properly (`aria-selected`) in the `ChatHeader` tablist.

Shell terminals keep their current behavior (they remain terminal-surface tabs in `CenterPane`).

## Impact

- **Severity:** medium — feature reachable (PR #3962), but the mode-swap UX destroys chat context
- **Affected users:** all Chat-mode sessions that run reviews
- **Workaround:** switch back via the worker tab in `CenterPane` after viewing the reviewer

## Related

- [#3939](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3939) — original report: review terminal disappears in Chat UI mode (closed by PR #3962)
- [PR #3962](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3962) — added the Reviewer tab + target-preservation guard; this issue covers the residual surface-swap UX
- [#3303](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3303) — reviewer terminal should open as a tab instead of replacing the worker terminal (TUI-mode counterpart)
- [#3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — Chat/TUI session modes design doc

title: Chat UI: command rows never show the command text (Claude Code) — 'Ran command' header + output-only body
body:
## Bug

In the Chat UI, command activity rows for **Claude Code** sessions show only the command's *output* — the command itself is never displayed anywhere: not in the collapsed row header (which just says "Ran command"), and not in the expanded body (which renders output, agent-typed input, and file diffs, but never the command string).

**Source:** Discord `#bug-triage` thread | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `ee2c58a57` (main, 2026-08-15)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced at both layers.

## Reproduction

1. Spawn/switch a session to the Chat interface with the **claude-code** harness.
2. Ask the agent to run any shell command.
3. Observe the timeline: the collapsed row says only `Ran command`; expanding it shows the output block (e.g. `(Bash completed with no output)` or the streamed output) with the caveat footer — but never *what* ran.

Screenshot (reporter's): two "Ran command" rows; first shows `(Bash completed with no output)`, second shows an `ao session`-style listing. No command text anywhere.

For comparison, the **codex** driver does populate `detail.command`, but the frontend still never renders it on a command row — so the bug has two layers.

## Root Cause

Two independent gaps compound:

### 1. Backend — ACP driver never sets `detail.command` for Claude Code execute tools

`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/client.go`, `toolEvent()` (~line 552-593): the activity detail map is built with `protocol`, `toolKind`, `locations`, `input` (the **raw** `rawInput` JSON object — for Claude Code's Bash tool this is `{"command": "...", "description": "..."}`), `output`, `content`, plus copied `claudeCode`/`terminal_info`/`terminal_exit` metadata. It never extracts a `command` string.

The neutral detail contract (`frontend/src/renderer/types/conversation.ts:182` `CommandDetail.command`) is only honored by the codex driver — `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/normalize.go:1196-1204` (`activityDetail`) sets `detail["command"] = unwrapShell(cmd)` + `rawCommand`. The ACP path (claude-code, opencode, gemini, droid, crush — every ACP-backed harness) leaves `command` undefined even though the data is present one key away in `rawInput`.

### 2. Frontend — command rows never render the command string, even when present

`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx`:

- `splitSummary()` (~line 651-660) intentionally labels command rows by category ("Ran command" / "Explored N files" / "Checked repository") and returns no `path`/target for them. That's a deliberate design (landed with the Chat UI in #3472) — but it means the collapsed header never carries the command.
- The expanded body of `GenericActivityRow` (~line 508-524) renders `files`, `detail.reason`/`detail.text`, `detail.terminalInput`, and `detail.output` — **not** `detail.command`. So even on codex sessions where the data exists, the command text is unreachable in the UI.
- `detail.command` *is* rendered for auto-review rows (~line 1169) and approval cards (~line 1470) — just not for ordinary command rows.

## Fix

1. **Backend** (`acp/client.go` `toolEvent`): for tools whose `kind` maps to `domain.ActivityKindCommand` (`ToolKindExecute`), extract the command string from `rawInput` (`command` key for Claude Code Bash; fall back to other common keys or skip) into `detail["command"]` (+ `rawCommand` for the verbatim form), mirroring `codexappserver`'s `activityDetail`.
2. **Frontend** (`ChatTimelineItems.tsx` `GenericActivityRow`): render `detail.command` in the expanded body (mono line above the output block), and include `detail?.command` in the `hasBody` check so a command row with no output is still expandable.

Step 2 alone fixes the symptom for codex; step 1 is required for Claude Code (and every other ACP harness).

## Impact

- Chat UI is unusable for auditing *what* an agent ran — a trust/safety-relevant gap for a supervisor tool. The workaround (switch to the Terminal tab and scroll) exists but defeats the point of the chat transcript.
- Affects all ACP-backed harnesses (claude-code confirmed; opencode/gemini/droid/crush share the driver).
- Rows that produced no output render as `(Bash completed with no output)` — maximally uninformative combination.

**Priority:** P2 — feature degraded, workaround exists (Terminal tab).

## Related

- #3360 — immutable Chat/TUI session modes (broader chat surface tracking)
- #3945 — chat output-cap freeze (same command-activity rendering area, different failure)

title: fix(terminal): stabilize xterm viewport, session-switch render, colors, and activity state
body:
Fixes #3803, fixes #2333, fixes #2529, fixes #2047.

## What

Four terminal-stability fixes across the renderer and the activity lifecycle.

### #3803 — disposed-viewport crash on handle replacement
`XtermTerminal` unmount cleanup disposed the xterm instance synchronously while queued write/viewport work (WriteBuffer callbacks, `Viewport.syncScrollArea` microtasks) could still land in the same task, crashing the renderer with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions')`. Cleanup now detaches all listeners/observers/timers synchronously but defers the final `term.dispose()` one macrotask, and the attachable handle drops `write`/`writeln` after disposal (still invoking `done` callbacks so attachment flow control can finish).

### #2333 — blank/glitched terminals after session switching
Two root causes:
- The retained-terminal cache became unbounded (4986af7d0), so each visited pane held a live WebGL context; past Chromium's per-page context cap the oldest contexts are force-lost and the earliest-visited panes render black. Retention is re-bounded at `MAX_RETAINED_TERMINALS = 6` with least-recently-shown eviction (evicted panes remount fresh on revisit).
- A rejected `prepareForActivation()` could leave the activation cover (`visibility:hidden`) down forever. All call sites now tolerate rejection, and a 2s activation-stall watchdog force-completes a stuck activation.

### #2529 — ANSI colors don't match a real terminal
The truecolor plumbing (tmux `-u -T RGB`, `TERM`/`COLORTERM`) already landed in #2980; the remaining gap was the palette itself. The 12 chromatic ANSI slots in `tokens.css` were a softened house mix (and the light theme darkened them further, with bright-white near-black — inverting TUI emphasis). Both themes now use the de-facto standard terminal values (VS Code integrated-terminal defaults), which agent CLIs are designed against. Neutral endpoints stay tuned to AO's terminal plate, per DESIGN.md's "terminal keeps its own palette".

### #2047 — Claude sessions misreport activity state
The `exited` activity state could pin wrongly and never self-correct (only `user-prompt-submit` could resurrect it; the reaper only transitions *into* exited). Two fixes in the lifecycle manager:
- Live-agent evidence — tool-use events and `permission-request`, which are executed by the agent process itself — now resurrects an exited state (turn-boundary callbacks like `stop`/`notification` still cannot). A wrong resurrect self-corrects on the reaper's next workload probe (~5s); a wrong exited previously pinned forever.
- The workload-dead→exited transition is skipped while a session mutation (spawn/restore/agent-switch) is in flight, matching the guard the termination path already had — probing an old process tree against new metadata mid-relaunch no longer desyncs the session to exited.

## Tests
- `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`: dispose is deferred past unmount; writes to a dead handle are dropped with `done` still invoked.
- `TerminalPane.test.tsx`: retention-cap eviction (7 visited → 6 retained, LRU evicted, fresh remount on revisit).
- `manager_test.go`: tool-use and permission-request resurrect exited; turn-boundary events do not; workload-dead observation is suppressed during session mutation.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck` and full renderer suite: 177 files, 2233 passed / 1 skipped.
- `go test ./...`: all green (AO_* session env cleared for `internal/cli`).
- Palette change verified visually via an `ao preview` before/after harness (dark + light).

## Risks / follow-ups
- Eviction cap (6) restores the pre-4986af7d0 bound; panes beyond it lose scrollback on revisit (replay repaints latest output). If unbounded retention is wanted back, it needs a non-WebGL fallback for parked panes instead.
- Exited-resurrect intentionally excludes turn-boundary hooks; delayed `stop` events after a real exit remain ignored.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Windows desktop flashes command prompt windows during startup and background probes
body:
## Bug
On Windows, AO can visibly flash transient Command Prompt windows while starting the desktop app and while the daemon performs background work. A user report included a screenshot of a black command window popping up over AO, with the note that it appears and closes repeatedly around 5-6 times while using AO.

**Source:** Local Windows user report and screenshot shared during triage on 2026-08-15. Startup logs were also provided from `frontend/npm run dev` showing daemon startup and background probes.
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction
1. On Windows, run `cd frontend && npm run dev`.
2. Wait for Electron Forge to launch the desktop app and daemon.
3. Observe transient Command Prompt windows appearing and disappearing during startup.
4. Continue using AO in flows that trigger background CLI probes; command windows can also flash during normal use.

## Root Cause
Windows GUI apps that spawn console subsystem executables without hidden process creation flags can show visible console windows. AO had two affected paths:

- Developer mode launched the daemon with `go run ./cmd/ao daemon`, which can spawn Go compiler/linker helper processes and make startup especially noisy on Windows.
- Several daemon-owned non-interactive probes used raw process spawning instead of AO's hidden-process wrapper, so downloaded Windows app users could also see command windows from Git, Docker, Tailscale, provider version probes, reviewer probes, or ACP provider processes.

A related Windows dev issue was observed after switching to a fixed prebuilt `frontend/daemon/ao.exe`: active sessions can keep that exe locked, making the next `npm run dev` fail with `EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink ...\frontend\daemon\ao.exe`.

## Fix
Use a Windows-specific dev daemon launch path and hide daemon-owned helper processes:

- Build Windows dev daemons into versioned `frontend/daemon/dev-*` directories and pass the selected exe through a dev manifest.
- Keep macOS/Linux dev startup unchanged.
- Keep packaged daemon resolution unchanged.
- Add hidden-process flags for Node build/probe spawns.
- Route daemon-owned non-interactive CLI probes through the existing backend hidden-process wrapper.
- Preserve Windows ACP process-tree cleanup while also suppressing console windows.

## Impact
- Windows developer mode should stop flashing command prompt windows during daemon startup and avoid locked fixed `ao.exe` rebuild failures.
- Downloaded Windows app users should not see background helper/probe command windows flash during normal app use.
- macOS and Linux behavior should remain unchanged.

title: fix(windows): hide daemon child process consoles
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4012

## What happened
On Windows, AO can show black Command Prompt windows for a moment and then close them again. A user reported that this happens repeatedly while using AO, sometimes 5-6 times, and it looks broken.

This is mainly a Windows problem. When a desktop app starts console programs in the background, Windows can show a command window unless the process is started with hidden-window flags.

## Why it happened
There were two places where this could happen:

1. In dev mode, `npm run dev` started the daemon through `go run`. On Windows, `go run` starts extra compiler/helper processes, so startup could flash several command windows.
2. In the normal downloaded Windows app, the daemon also starts background tools like Git, Docker, Tailscale, agent version checks, reviewer tools, and ACP provider processes. Some of these were not using AO's hidden process wrapper.

There was also a related dev-mode problem: if an old AO session was still using `frontend/daemon/ao.exe`, Windows could keep that file locked. The next `npm run dev` could then fail while trying to delete or replace it.

## What changed
- Windows dev mode now builds the daemon first and starts the built `ao.exe` instead of using `go run` at app startup.
- Windows dev builds use versioned daemon folders, so an old running session does not block the next build.
- Background helper processes launched by the daemon now use the existing hidden-process wrapper on Windows.
- ACP provider processes still keep their process-group cleanup behavior, but no longer need to show a console window.
- Mac and Linux dev behavior is unchanged.
- Packaged daemon location is unchanged.

title: fix(scm): prevent transient PR fact regressions
body:
## Summary
- separate partial PR discovery from authoritative SCM observation writes so repository listings can never erase CI, review, mergeability, metadata, or observer cursors
- identify listed PRs by the provider's canonical base repository and canonical URL, deduplicating stale remotes that redirect after repository transfers
- project successful in-app merges into durable PR state immediately, emit existing CDC, and run lifecycle reactions without waiting for the next poll
- preserve nested GitLab namespace parsing and document the durable-facts-first boundary

## Root cause
The observer used one full-snapshot upsert for two different fact strengths. A lightweight repository listing was treated as if it were an authoritative detailed observation. When both a canonical remote and a stale redirecting remote found the same PR, the partial discovery row overwrote rich readiness facts, producing a temporary **Checking merge readiness** state until the detailed refresh repaired it.

The merge action had the inverse consistency gap: it mutated the provider but did not project that confirmed result locally. Frontend invalidation therefore refetched stale SQLite facts until polling caught up.

## Verification
- `npm run sqlc`
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `npm run lint` (all AO runtime environment variables removed so CLI tests exercise their isolated harness)
- focused observer, SQLite store, SCM adapter, PR action service, and daemon tests

## Related issue

title: fix(desktop): keep shells and agent switching inside the chat surface
body:
Part of #4033 — closes its shell and agent-switch gaps.

## Summary

Two constructs that work in Terminal UI now work the same in Chat UI, without leaving the conversation:

**Shells are tabs in the chat header (Gap 1).** Previously `showChatSurface` only stayed mounted for `worker`/`reviewer` targets, so opening a shell unmounted the entire chat surface — timeline, composer draft, scroll position — and swapped in `CenterPane`. Now a shell target renders its `TerminalPane` as the tab body inside the chat surface (the routed `TerminalTarget` passed straight through, mirroring `reviewerTarget` from #4027), and the conversation panel hides with `hidden`/`inert` instead of unmounting — drafts, attachments, edits, and scroll survive.

Shell tabs use the shared `ShellTerminalTab` (already used by `CenterPane` and the terminals screen "so the three never drift"), which brings select/close/**rename** along for free. The desktop next/previous tab shortcuts (Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab) now cycle chat → reviewer → shells in strip order.

**Agent switching has an entry point in chat (Gap 2).** `CenterPane` rendered `TerminalSwitchAgentButton`; the chat surface had nothing, even though `useSwitchAgent` was already chat-aware (it invalidates conversation queries). The same control now renders in the chat header's action region. The mutation state lives in `SessionChatSurface` — which owns query wiring — so `ChatWorkspace` stays a provider-free pure view (its documented contract; enforced by existing fixture tests).

## Changes (6 files, +377/−28)

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `SessionView.tsx` | `showChatSurface` stays mounted for `shell` targets; passes the routed shell target + shell list/select/close/rename into the chat surface. |
| `SessionChatSurface.tsx` | Forwards shell props; owns the agent-switch dialog state + mutation; hands the button and a body-container ref down. |
| `ChatWorkspace.tsx` | Shell pane parallel to the reviewer pane (same `TerminalPane` target passthrough, zoom/fullscreen wiring); shell tabs via shared `ShellTerminalTab`; `timelineActive` generalization so the chat tab deactivates for either terminal pane; next-tab shortcut cycles through shells; renders the passed-down switch control. |
| tests | ChatWorkspace: shell pane hides-not-unmounts the conversation, target passthrough, Ctrl+Tab cycling. SessionView: shells-from-chat stay inside the chat surface. SessionChatSurface: switch control offered in chat. |

## What's deliberately not here

- **Full tab-strip unification (Gap 3 remainder):** the chat/reviewer tabs remain hand-rolled in `ChatHeader`; extracting one shared strip with `CenterPane` remains a follow-up on #4033.
- CenterPane's deep in-flight switch UX (input locking, source focus, announcements) — the chat surface already reflects controller transitions through its own banners; the button/dialog/mutation flow is identical.

title: Switch-agent selector fills terminal and reanimates on repeated activation
body:
## Bug

The terminal-scoped **Switch agent** selector has two related interaction regressions:

1. The provider/model card expands to the terminal panel width instead of remaining a compact centered card like the in-progress switch presentation.
2. Clicking the toolbar switch button while the selector is already open closes and immediately reopens the dialog, replaying its fade animation.

**Reported by:** @whoisasx (local desktop report)  
**Analyzed against:** `0fbe25e168b27ee35814286f541e426622f4cab0`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P2 — the workflow remains usable, but the selector presentation and repeated interaction are visibly degraded.

## Reproduction

1. Open an active Claude Code or Codex worker terminal.
2. Click the **Switch agent** toolbar button.
3. Observe that the selector card spans almost the complete terminal width.
4. Click the same toolbar button again while the selector remains open.
5. Observe the selector fade out and back in.

## Root cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/dialog.tsx` supplies `w-full` from the shared dialog primitive.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SwitchAgentDialog.tsx` also supplied the custom `w-dialog-md` utility. `tailwind-merge` does not classify the custom utility as conflicting with `w-full`, so both classes survive. Tailwind emits `.w-full` later, making the computed width 100% rather than the intended 420px.
- The selector uses a non-modal Radix dialog. A pointer-down on the toolbar button is treated as an outside interaction and emits `onOpenChange(false)`; the button's unconditional click handler then emits `onOpenChange(true)`. A focused component test records the exact `false → true` sequence.

These paths were introduced together by [PR #3770](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3770).

## Fix

- Use an unambiguous arbitrary width utility that replaces the shared `w-full` through `tailwind-merge`.
- Ignore toolbar pointer/click activation while the selector is already open, before Radix can treat it as an outside dismissal.
- Cover the computed width in the renderer Playwright harness and the repeated activation state sequence in the component suite.

## Impact

- The selector no longer visually matches the compact centered switch-progress UI.
- Repeated activation causes a distracting close/reopen animation and unnecessary remount.
- Existing tests only checked for a class name and the first open action, so neither browser-computed geometry nor repeated activation was protected.

title: fix(frontend): stabilize switch agent selector
body:
## What

- keep the terminal-scoped Switch agent selector at the 420px dialog token on wide panes and within a 16px gutter on narrow panes
- make repeated activation of the already-open toolbar control a no-op instead of closing and reopening the Radix dialog
- cover the browser-computed wide/narrow geometry and the repeated activation state sequence

## Why

Fixes #4039.

The shared dialog primitive contributes `w-full`, while the custom `w-dialog-md` class was not recognized as a conflicting Tailwind utility. Both survived merging and the later full-width rule won. Separately, the non-modal dialog treated a pointer-down on the toolbar control as an outside dismissal before the control's click handler reopened it.

## How

- use an arbitrary width utility so `tailwind-merge` replaces the shared `w-full`; cap it against the terminal containing block rather than the viewport
- intercept pointer activation only while the selector is already open, with an `onClick` guard covering keyboard and assistive-technology activation
- replace the former class-name assertion with real computed-width Playwright coverage

body:
## What

Fixes browser tabs that could not be closed after multiple tabs were opened, and improves DevTools button visibility while it is active.

## Why

UI-created tabs were added directly to AO’s Electron tab list after the native agent-browser daemon had already connected. The daemon therefore did not know about those tabs, causing close commands to fail with “Tab not found.”

The active DevTools button also inherited the ghost button’s dark hover styling, making the icon difficult to see.

## How

- Route UI tab creation through the existing native `tab-new` lifecycle so AO and agent-browser stay synchronized.
- Preserve direct tab creation as the fallback when the native runtime is unavailable.
- Give the active DevTools button a persistent high-contrast accent state, including hover.
- Expose the DevTools toggle state through `aria-pressed`.
- Add regression coverage for the seven-tab workflow and native tab lifecycle.

## Files affected

- `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`
  - Synchronizes UI-created tabs with the native browser runtime.
- `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts`
  - Covers creating multiple UI tabs after daemon initialization and closing one.
- `frontend/src/main/agent-browser-runtime.test.ts`
  - Verifies native tab creation and closure using the bundled agent-browser binary.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/BrowserPanel.tsx`

title: Linux: fixed titlebar nav cluster ghosts over Board crumb when sidebar is collapsed (broken clearance + undefined --size-titlebar-content-offset-linux token)
body:
## Bug

On Linux, with the sidebar collapsed, the fixed titlebar navigation cluster (sidebar toggle + back/forward history arrows) paints **on top of the "Board" crumb** in the framed shell topbar. The disabled back/forward arrows render at 55% opacity over the title text, producing a "ghosted chevrons bleeding through the Board label" look.

![screenshot: ghosted nav chevrons overlapping the Board title on Linux](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-linux-titlebar-ghost/.issue-assets/linux-titlebar-ghost/board.png)

**Source:** Discord `#report-bugs` thread "broken UI" | **Reported by:** Piyush (OS: Omarchy / Arch + Hyprland, Linux)
**Analyzed against:** `9a5882086` (2026-08-14) | **Confidence:** High — full geometry traced in code
**Priority:** P2 — cosmetic/layout degradation with an easy workaround (expand the sidebar); no data or functionality loss. But it also blocks a click-target: the ghosted arrows sit over where users expect to read/click the crumb.

## Reproduction

1. Run the desktop app on Linux (any distro; confirmed on Omarchy/Wayland).
2. Collapse the sidebar (PanelLeft toggle or shortcut).
3. Navigate to the root Board route (`/`) — the framed ShellTopbar shows the "Board" crumb.
4. The fixed nav cluster (sidebar toggle, back arrow, forward arrow) at `left-0` now overlaps the crumb: the toggle/grid icons sit beside the title and the two disabled chevrons ghost over the "Board" text.

Sidebar expanded → no overlap (the cluster sits over the sidebar's reserved band instead).

## Root Cause

Two layers collide because the Linux clearance path was only half-built:

**1. The nav cluster is `fixed left-0` and never moves when the sidebar hides.**
`frontend/src/renderer/components/TitlebarNav.tsx:63-67` — on Linux (`!isMac`) the cluster is `left-0`, `top-0.75`, pinned to the window's top-left "within the reserved titlebar band" (comment at lines 60-62). It is rendered once at shell level (`frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx:786-791`) precisely so it does *not* follow sidebar state — by design on macOS, where the topbar pads around it.

**2. The framed `ShellTopbar` only reserves clearance for that cluster on macOS.**
`frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx:85-90`:

```ts
const targetPaddingLeft =
    !embedded && mac && !isSidebarOpen      // ← mac only
        ? isFullScreen ? PADDING_CLEARANCE_FULLSCREEN : PADDING_CLEARANCE  // 112 / 170px
        : PADDING_DEFAULT;                  // 18px on Linux
```

When the sidebar is hidden, the center panel expands to the window edge (`.sidebar-hidden .center-panel-shell { padding-left: 16px }`, `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:456-460`), so the "Board" crumb (padding-left 18px) slides under the fixed cluster. The back/forward buttons are disabled at the board root (`useCanGoBack()` false → `disabled:opacity-55`, `TitlebarNav.tsx:134`) — hence ghosting rather than a solid overlap.

**3. A partial mitigation exists for session routes only — and it is itself broken.**
PR #3480 added `.session-topbar-titlebar-clearance-linux` (`styles.css:523-525`) applied on session routes when `!isSidebarOpen` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/CenterPane.tsx:528`, `chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx:638`). But it sets:

```css
.session-topbar-titlebar-clearance-linux {
    padding-left: var(--size-titlebar-content-offset-linux);
}
```

and **`--size-titlebar-content-offset-linux` is never defined anywhere** — the only occurrences of that token in the repo are this one usage (`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:524`) plus `--size-titlebar-cluster-left-linux: 6px` (`frontend/src/styles/tokens.css:306`), which is a different token and is never referenced. An undefined CSS custom property resolves to the guaranteed-invalid value → the declaration is ignored at computed-value time → **0 extra padding**. The session-route "fix" has been a no-op since it landed (commit `bbea40a5a`, 2026-08-03, PR #3480).

**Timeline:**
- `28c8fa284` (2026-07-26, PR #3129) introduced the Linux fixed titlebar cluster ("match mac shell chrome") — earliest version of the overlap geometry.
- `bbea40a5a` (2026-08-03, PR #3480) added the broken Linux clearance class (session routes only, undefined token).

## Fix

Two lines of defense, both small:

1. **Define the missing token** in `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` next to its siblings:
   ```css
   --size-titlebar-content-offset-linux:
       var(--size-titlebar-cluster-left-linux) + var(--size-titlebar-cluster-width) + var(--size-titlebar-content-gap);
   ```
   (6px + 92px + 12px = 110px). This repairs the existing session-route mitigation.

2. **Extend `ShellTopbar`'s `targetPaddingLeft` to Linux**: treat `!isSidebarOpen` the same as the mac branch but with the Linux offset — e.g. `mac ? PADDING_CLEARANCE : isLinux ? PADDING_CLEARANCE_LINUX : PADDING_DEFAULT`, with `PADDING_CLEARANCE_LINUX = 110` (or read the token). Apply it wherever the crumb renders (root board route and session identity), mirroring how `PADDING_CLEARANCE` is applied today. Alternatively, gate it purely in CSS via the existing `--size-titlebar-content-offset-linux` token on `topbarHeaderClass` for `.platform-linux`.

Note the arrows still overlap the crumb on **project board routes** (`/projects/$id`) where the crumb is the project name — same mechanism, so the fix should cover both (the `boardActionsInPanel` branch at `ShellTopbar.tsx:204-205` renders the crumb for Linux on all non-session routes).

## Impact

- Linux users with a collapsed sidebar see ghosted navigation chevrons over the Board/project crumb on every board visit; the cluster's hover states also light up over the title area, making the top-left of the topbar feel broken.
- The session-route mitigation shipped in #3480 is silently dead CSS (undefined token) — worth fixing regardless of the board-route work.
- macOS is unaffected (its 170px clearance path works); Windows uses its own `WindowTitlebar`, unaffected.

## Related

- [#3129](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3129) — introduced the Linux fixed titlebar cluster
- [#3480](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3480) — added the (broken) Linux session-route clearance
- [#3372](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3372) — same subsystem (sidebar hover-preview race), not a duplicate

title: Provide a global/project default to enable Auto review for new sessions
body:
## Problem

In AO 0.12.5, **Auto review** is available in the Reviews panel, but it is disabled for every newly created issue/task/worker session. Users must enable it manually for each session.

## Additional reproduction

When the worker is still in progress and no pull request has been opened, the Reviews panel only shows **Automatically send reviews**. The **Auto review** toggle is not available, so it cannot be enabled proactively. Users must wait until the work ends and/or a pull request exists before enabling Auto review, which is too late for that session review workflow.

## Request

Add a global or project-level default for auto_review_enabled, configurable through AO settings or project configuration (for example, autoReviewEnabled: true). When a session is created, it should inherit that default while retaining the per-session toggle as an override.

Please consider:

- applying the setting to all newly created sessions, including issue/task/worker sessions;
- making the setting available before or at session creation;
- preserving existing-session behavior, or providing an explicit migration/backfill option for existing sessions;
- keeping reviewer-agent selection and **Automatically send reviews** as separate settings.

## Current workaround

Enable **Auto review** manually for every session, but the control may not appear until the worker has finished or opened a pull request.

## Related

This request is for enabling the Auto review feature by default, not for the separate automatic injection/send-review-feedback setting. Related issue: #3468.
