title: Clarify token usage reporting and avoid apparent cache-token double counting
body:
## Bug

AO presents an inclusive `inputTokens` value alongside cache-read and cache-write token counts, then labels `inputTokens + outputTokens` as **Total tokens**. The arithmetic currently represents all tokens processed, but the terminology makes cache tokens appear duplicated and makes AO difficult to compare with agent-native usage reports.

**Source:** User report in an AO session on 2026-08-18  
**Analyzed against:** `78a1366310c071a5edf5d01f420c162e02e40dec`  
**Confidence:** High — the parser, aggregation query, API DTO, and renderer calculation were traced.  
**Priority:** P2 — reporting is available but materially confusing; underlying token categories are already retained.

The screenshots below are from different sessions and should not be numerically reconciled. They illustrate the terminology problem only.

### AO usage inspector

![AO usage inspector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-token-usage-reporting-20260818/.issue-assets/token-usage-reporting/ao-usage.png)

### Claude Code native usage report

![Claude Code usage report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-token-usage-reporting-20260818/.issue-assets/token-usage-reporting/claude-code-usage.png)

## Current behavior

For Claude transcripts, `backend/internal/observe/usage/parser.go` normalizes:

```text
inputTokens = uncached input + cache reads + cache writes
```

Codex reports inclusive input, so AO derives uncached input by subtracting cache reads/writes.

The inspector (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`) and compact-session query (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/usage.sql`) then calculate:

```text
totalTokens = inputTokens + outputTokens
```

This is a valid **tokens processed** measurement, but the UI shows `inputTokens`, cache reads, and cache writes as if they were independent rows. Reasoning tokens are also shown without explaining that they are included in output.

## Desired reporting contract

Use mutually exclusive user-facing categories:

- **Fresh input** — uncached input tokens
- **Cache reads**
- **Cache writes**
- **Output** — includes reasoning tokens
- **Reasoning (included in output)** — informational subset, never added again

Derive and label the aggregate explicitly:

```text
tokensProcessed = freshInput + cacheReads + cacheWrites + output
```

Do not display the inclusive internal `inputTokens` value as ordinary **Input tokens**.

Suggested summary presentation:

```text
Tokens processed                         2.2M
Estimated cost                              —

Fresh input                              86.5K
Output                                      8K
Cache reads                              2.1M
Cache writes                                 0
Reasoning (included in output)            3.1K
Cache hit rate                              96%
```

Collapsed session/agent/model rows could use `2.2M processed · 96% cached`. Once reliable pricing is available, estimated cost should be the primary comparison metric because token classes have substantially different prices.

## Proposed implementation

1. Add an explicitly named `processedTokens` derived field to detailed and compact usage responses.
2. Present `uncachedInputTokens` as **Fresh input**.
3. Stop presenting inclusive `inputTokens` in the visible breakdown.
4. Rename **Total tokens** to **Tokens processed**.
5. Label reasoning as included in output.
6. Add a cache-hit percentage with a documented denominator.
7. Keep existing API fields temporarily for compatibility and deprecate ambiguous naming rather than silently changing its meaning.
8. Ensure all pricing and telemetry formulas price/count each mutually exclusive category exactly once.

No historical data rewrite should be required: AO already persists uncached input, cache read, cache write, output, and reasoning separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visible token categories are mutually exclusive except reasoning, which is explicitly marked as a subset of output.
- [ ] `processedTokens` equals fresh input + cache reads + cache writes + output at model, harness, session, and compact-card scopes.
- [ ] Cache tokens are not counted twice in any displayed aggregate, cost calculation, or telemetry field.
- [ ] Claude raw `input_tokens` maps to Fresh input; Claude cache fields remain separate.
- [ ] Codex inclusive input is split correctly into fresh/cache categories.
- [ ] Session cards and inspector labels distinguish processed volume from fresh input and cost.
- [ ] OpenAPI and frontend generated types are regenerated together.
- [ ] Parser, aggregation, controller, and renderer tests cover the reporting contract.

## Related

- [PR #4003](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4003) — adds token cost telemetry and should use the same mutually exclusive category contract.
- [PR #2928](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2928) — introduced event-driven session token usage.

title: feat(browser): add persistent profiles with cookie and history import
body:
## What

Add opt-in persistent browser profiles to AO.

Users can now:

- Create, rename, clear, and delete named browser profiles from Settings.
- Switch profiles from the browser toolbar.
- Keep cookies and browsing history across AO restarts.
- Import cookies and history from supported Chromium-based browsers, Firefox, and Zen.
- Select one or more detected source profiles and import them into new AO profiles.
- Use imported history as address-bar suggestions.

Temporary profiles remain the default, preserving the existing ephemeral and per-worker-isolated behavior.

## Why

AO browser workers previously used temporary sessions only. This meant authentication and browsing context were lost when the worker or app restarted.

Persistent profiles let users explicitly retain useful browser state without exposing profile selection to agents or changing the default behavior for existing sessions.

## How

- Stores AO-owned profile metadata and imported history under `~/.ao`.
- Uses a dedicated persistent Electron partition for each named AO profile.
- Keeps profile selection user-controlled through Settings and the browser toolbar.
- Reads source browser databases through read-only snapshots without exposing source paths to the renderer.
- Validates source paths, realpath containment, symlinks, database sizes, record counts, and import limits before committing data.
- Creates new destination profiles instead of silently overwriting existing profiles.
- Rolls back newly created profiles and imported state when an import fails.
- Handles Chromium cookie encryption and Firefox database differences, reporting skipped or unsupported data as warnings.
- Preserves browser permission denial, renderer ownership checks, tab isolation, lifecycle cleanup, and the restriction preventing agents from choosing `--profile`.
- Packages the SQLite runtime required by the importer in production builds.

Intentional omissions:

- Bookmarks
- Passwords
- Extensions
- Full browser-profile directory copying
- Signed-in browser account synchronization
- Domain-filtered imports


## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- Focused browser, profile, settings, preload, and IPC tests:
  - 8 test files passed
  - 233 tests passed
- Import, rollback, source-validation, lifecycle, packaging, and Chromium cookie compatibility tests were added during implementation.
- Production packaging and packaged SQLite runtime verification passed before the final upstream merge.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing an existing PR branch
- [x] One focused browser-profile and import feature
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added or updated for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the final pushed commit

title: bug(agent-claude-code): session stuck working/active after a turn dies without its Stop hook (login expired) — observer skips claude-code, no TerminalActivityDetector
body:
## Bug

A claude-code worker session (live: `agent-orchestrator-139`) shows **status=working / activity=active** indefinitely while the Claude CLI is provably idle at its composer. The last turn aborted on an expired OAuth login (`Login expired · Please run /login`, `Worked for 0s`), so the turn's Stop hook never fired — and nothing else ever demotes the stale `active`.

**Source:** live observation of session `agent-orchestrator-139` (tmux pane capture) | **Reported by:** maintainer via orchestrator task | **Analyzed against:** `0e472e2b2`
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a claude-code TUI worker; let a turn start (`user-prompt-submit` → activity=active).
2. Kill the turn without a Stop hook — auth expiry mid-stream reproduces it (turn ends with `Login expired · Please run /login`, `✻ Worked for 0s`); a CLI crash or network drop behaves the same.
3. Observe `ao session get`: status stays `working`, activity stays `active` forever. Any further Enter on the logged-out CLI re-fires `user-prompt-submit` and re-asserts `active` (which is why `updated` advances on each retry while nothing runs).

## Root Cause

Claude Code's durable activity is **hook-driven only** (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/activity.go` → `lifecycle.ApplyActivitySignal`). The only transitions out of `active` are the `stop` / `notification(idle_prompt)` / `session-end` hooks. A turn that dies mid-stream emits none of them.

AO already has the exact safety net for this: the activity observer (`backend/internal/observe/activity/observer.go:103-131`) polls every 30s and, for sessions stuck `active` past `DefaultStaleAfter` (2 min), screen-proves the real state via the adapter's `TerminalActivityDetector`. But the claude-code adapter **never implemented `DetectTerminalActivity`**, so `reconcile()` returns at the type assertion (`observer.go:111-114`) and claude-code sessions are exempt from reconciliation entirely. (The adapter has `InspectTerminalSurface` — the classification logic exists — it just isn't wired to the detector port.) The prior test `TestPollLeavesOtherHarnessesUntouched` even pinned claude-code as the example of a skipped harness.

Verified against the live pane: `InspectTerminalSurface` on the stuck screen (login-expired footer, staged draft in the composer, no active chrome) correctly yields `Work=Idle` — the observer would have converged the session within one tick if the detector had been wired.

Hypotheses ruled out: hook/classifier precedence is not involved (there is simply no classifier signal), and nothing refreshes `updated` unconditionally (it stayed frozen at `15:15:56Z` for 6+ minutes of observation; it only advances when the user re-submits on the logged-out CLI).

## Fix

Implement `DetectTerminalActivity` on the claude-code plugin, delegating to `InspectTerminalSurface` — authoritative idle only when the surface positively shows an idle composer (same pattern codex shipped for #3115). Claude stays non-continuous: hooks remain authoritative while they flow; the observer only reconciles a stale `active`.

## Impact

- Users see a phantom "Working" session and wait for output that never comes; the logged-out state is hidden.
- Orchestrators treat the worker as busy and won't dispatch or escalate.
- Class bug: ANY hook turn-death (auth expiry, crash, network) strands claude-code in `working` — until now, permanently.

## Related

- [#3387](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3387) — same class for Kimi; documents that only codex implemented `TerminalActivityDetector` (this issue is the claude-code instance)
- [#3115](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3115) — codex instance (fixed by codex's `terminal_activity.go`)
- [#4048](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4048) — cline instance (fixed via continuous reconciliation)
- [#2047](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2047) — broader claude activity misreporting

title: fix(claude-code): reconcile stuck-active sessions via terminal activity detection
body:
Fixes #4142

## Summary

A Claude Code turn that dies without emitting its Stop hook (expired OAuth login, CLI crash, network loss) left the session's hook-driven activity stuck at `active`, so the app showed **status=working** forever while the CLI sat idle at its composer (live incident: `agent-orchestrator-139`, stranded on `Login expired · Please run /login`).

The activity observer already reconciles exactly this case — a session stale in `active` past 2 minutes is screen-proven against the adapter's `TerminalActivityDetector` — but the claude-code adapter never implemented that capability, so the observer skipped its sessions at the type assertion (`observer.go:111-114`).

This PR implements `DetectTerminalActivity` on the claude-code plugin, same pattern as codex (#3115): delegate to the existing `InspectTerminalSurface` and report an **authoritative idle only** when the current surface positively shows an idle composer with no active spinner/interrupt chrome and no pending decision frame. Anything else fails closed. Claude deliberately stays non-continuous: hooks remain authoritative while they flow; the observer only steps in for a stale `active`.

Scope note: this intentionally fixes claude-code only. The same class bug for other hook-only harnesses is tracked in #3387 (Kimi).

## Changes

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/terminal_activity.go` (new): `DetectTerminalActivity` delegating to `InspectTerminalSurface`, idle-only, fail-closed.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/terminal_activity_test.go` (new): fixtures reproduce the real captured stuck screen (login-expired footer + staged draft, and empty-composer variant) → authoritative idle; active spinner, active footer hint, permission dialog, unrecognizable/empty output → not authoritative.
- `backend/internal/observe/activity/observer_test.go`: `TestPollLeavesOtherHarnessesUntouched` previously pinned claude-code as exempt from reconciliation (encoding the bug) — now uses droid as the detector-less example. Added `TestPollReconcilesStaleClaudeCodeAfterAbortedTurn` (stuck screen → one `terminal-idle` signal with launch/updatedAt fence) and `TestPollKeepsGenuineLongClaudeTurnActive` (real active chrome → no signal).

## Behavior notes

Implementing the `TerminalActivityDetector` port also opts claude-code into the two existing detector consumers beyond the observer, both matching codex's shipped behavior:
- `WaitForMessageDeliveryReady` now screen-proves the composer before injecting (previously: durable idle + first-hook-or-5s fallback) — strictly stronger evidence.
- The interface-transition drain's legacy fallback (only reachable when styled output is unavailable) can now prove idle for claude-code; it additionally requires `ComposerIsEmpty`, which claude-code already implements.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/ ./internal/observe/activity/ ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/lifecycle/` — pass
- Full `go test ./...` — pass (`internal/cli` requires all `AO_*` env unset; failures with leaked env are pre-existing and unrelated)
- Classifier hand-verified against the live stuck pane of `agent-orchestrator-139` (plain `tmux capture-pane`, which is what the observer's `GetOutput` provides): `Work=Idle`, so the observer converges the session within one tick after staleness.

## Risks / follow-ups

- A genuinely active turn whose rendering momentarily lacks both the spinner row and the footer interrupt hint could be sampled as idle; the next tool hook immediately re-asserts `active`, and this is the same trade-off codex has shipped since #3115.
- Follow-up filed separately: surface the `Login expired` screen as a distinct needs-input reason so users know to run `/login` instead of seeing a silent idle.

title: feat: improve update check feedback
body: ## Summary - check automatically on launch and every hour while automatic updates are enabled - make the current update state immediately scannable, with state-specific status, progress, and actions - show the exact running version and its Stable, Nightly, Feature, or Local preview identity separately from the configured update feed - persist the last successful check across launches; failed checks keep the last known-good timestamp - record a real installed/updated timestamp when the running version changes - keep manual checking available, preserve explicit opt-outs, and respect reduced-motion and localization requirements ## UX decisions - **Automatic by default:** installed releases check on launch and hourly, matching the convention used by comparable desktop developer tools. - **Installed build is not the update feed:** the badge describes what is running; the channel selector describes where future updates come from. - **Truthful timestamps:** “Last checked” means the last successful update check. “Updated” is recorded only after a running-version change. - **Exact nightly identity:** nightly builds show the full stamped version instead of collapsing it to a generic “Nightly” label. - **Clear local-build language:** source checkouts are called “Local preview,” with a compact explanation that update checks require an installed release. ## Scenarios ### 1. Stable — up to date A successful check shows the exact installed version, Stable badge, last successful check, and when this build was installed or updated. The configured Stable feed remains visible as a separate setting. ### 2. Checking automatically Installed releases enter this state at launch and on the hourly cadence. The status and action both communicate active work, so the page never looks idle while a request is in flight. ### 3. Update available The available version is named directly and the primary action is unambiguous, while the currently installed version remains visible for comparison. ### 4. Downloading A determinate progress bar and percentage replace the primary action during download, preventing duplicate requests and making background progress visible. ### 5. Ready to restart Once downloaded, the UI says what remains and promotes the conventional final action: restart and install. ### 6. Check failed A failed request gets a visible retry action and an actionable message. The previous successful “Last checked” value remains intact instead of being overwritten by the error. ### 7. Nightly — exact installed build Nightly users see the full stamped semver for the build that is actually running, a Nightly badge, and the pre-release risk warning. This answers both “am I on Nightly?” and “which Nightly exactly?” ### 8. Automatic updates off Explicit opt-outs are preserved. Manual checking stays available, and channel controls are hidden because they have no effect until automatic updates are enabled again. ## Testing - `npm run frontend:typecheck` - `cd frontend && npm test` (2,596 passed, 1 skipped) - `cd backend && go test -p 1 ./...` - `cd frontend && npm run package` - native Electron walkthrough on macOS across every scenario above

title: fix(browser): non-disruptive preview reveal + reopen closed tabs
body:
## Summary
Phase 2 of the AO in-app browser UX overhaul (calmer, less intrusive UX):

- **Non-disruptive agent browser actions**: a new `ao preview` target used to force-switch the inspector to the Browser tab and pop it open, even if the user was looking at something else entirely (Reviews, chat, a different session). Now it just badges Browser as unseen — same pattern already used for general agent browser activity (fill/click/snapshot) — and lets the user open it when they're ready.
- **Reopen tabs closed by the agent (or you)**: closing a tab was final — the only way back was asking the agent to reopen it. Now the last 5 closed tabs (with title/url/favicon) show as a "Recently closed" section in the tabs rail, in both the popped-out list and the docked hover flyout, click to reopen. The list now survives switching sessions and back (previously renderer-only state, lost on any session switch — unlike live tabs, which are kept alive in the main process).
- **Fixed the automation runtime permanently wedging a session**: `ensureNativeActiveTab`'s convergence loop retried the identical failing `tab-select` forever once the runtime's own tab registry forgot the active tab, wedging every native browser operation for the session — not just close, but tab switching too. It now asks the runtime to refresh its own view before retrying once, and accepts the drift (with a `console.warn` breadcrumb) instead of looping forever if still stale.
- **Fixed a reopen leaving contradictory state**: reopening a closed tab pointed at a dead localhost dev server used to report failure while the tab was actually created and left open — `openTab` threw after already telling the renderer the tab existed. It now matches how navigating an *existing* tab to a dead URL already worked (tab exists, shows an error page, no throw).
- **Fixed the close fallback double-closing an already-closed tab**: the automation runtime's own `Target.closeTarget` handling can close a tab internally before the runtime still reports the overall command as failed. The fallback used to retry AO's own close regardless, throwing `TAB_NOT_FOUND` for a tab that had already, genuinely closed. It now checks whether the tab is already gone and treats that as success. The renderer's close handler also now resyncs tab state from the main process on any failure, instead of leaving a stale "ghost" row that re-fails identically on every retry.
- **Fixed reopening at the 16-tab cap silently losing the closed-tab entry**: gated on the same cap the "+" button respects, with restore-on-failure for races.
- Favicons now render in Recently Closed rows (previously captured but unused). Close/select failures surface a transient notice instead of an unhandled rejection. `closeTab`'s identity no longer churns on every tab update.

## Scope note
The original Phase 2 plan also included a "general smoothness" item (optimistic tab select/close instead of waiting on the IPC round-trip, and/or trimming a MutationObserver's overhead). Left out of this PR — the codebase's own comments show that overhead was already a deliberate, documented trade-off, and reworking tab-selection to be optimistic carries real risk of subtle state bugs that's better done as its own focused pass rather than rushed in here.

The upstream question of *why* the automation runtime's tab registry drifts from `session.tabs` in the first place is still open and deliberately out of scope here — this PR makes AO resilient to it happening, not a fix to the runtime itself. Worth its own follow-up issue.

A separate, pre-existing paper cut was flagged during review: `browser:navigate` silently rejects a URL matching the renderer's own origin (a dev-mode `localhost:517x` port) with no notice surfaced to the user. Confirmed out of scope for this PR by the reviewer.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` on `browser-view-host.test.ts`, `BrowserPanel.test.tsx`, `useBrowserView.test.tsx`, `i18n/instance.test.ts` — 163/163 passing, with regression tests for every fix above (each verified to fail against the pre-fix code before being confirmed passing)
- [x] Manual pass in the real Electron app across three rounds of review — tabs opening/closing/switching, Recently Closed (favicons, cap gating, reopen, session-switch persistence), non-disruptive preview reveal

title: fix: isolate ChatUI history by session
body:
## Summary
- prevent ChatUI from rendering a conversation snapshot that belongs to a previously selected session
- remount `ChatWorkspace` when the selected session changes so retained timeline/composer state cannot carry across orchestrators
- hide project conversation pages before the current orchestrator's `ao-context-reset:<session>` boundary, so a replacement orchestrator does not page in the previous orchestrator's history
- filter stale queued/running turns at the same reset boundary so old turn state cannot make the replacement orchestrator appear busy
- persist the fresh-context reset boundary atomically with project conversation rebinds before provider startup
- strengthen regression coverage with a stateful workspace mock and a store-level project conversation rebind/reset test

## Root cause
Project-scoped conversations are intentionally rebound when an orchestrator is replaced. The frontend-only fix reset retained React state, but the paged conversation API could still return rows from before the fresh agent context boundary. That made old orchestrator history visible again after switching/replacing orchestrators.

This PR now treats the context-reset system activity for the current project orchestrator as the first visible sequence for paged ChatUI reads. The boundary activity remains stored as internal metadata, but it is not returned in paged ChatUI reads; older turns, messages, and activities are not returned or pageable from the replacement orchestrator view. The fresh-context boundary is written in the same transaction as the project conversation rebind before provider startup, so provider-start failures do not expose old history under the replacement session.

## Tests

- `cd backend && GOCACHE=/private/tmp/go-build go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/store`

- use a temporary fixed-port 127.0.0.1 callback during WorkOS PKCE sign-in so the browser receives a final success page
- try WorkOS-configured callback ports in order: 5174, 3000, then 3001
- show "You can close this tab and return to Agent Orchestrator" after the code exchange completes
- trigger a focus-only ao-app://complete handoff from that success page so the browser still shows the native app-open prompt
- keep the existing ao-app://callback handling as a fallback for older in-flight auth redirects
- avoid relaunching WorkOS when a valid cloud session already exists

## Root cause
The sign-in flow used the custom ao-app:// callback as the primary redirect. Browsers present that as an external app launch prompt, and some OS/browser combinations pass the deep-link argument differently or leave the provider tab sitting on a page that keeps trying to hand off to Electron. Switching the token exchange to a local HTTP callback fixes the browser UX, but WorkOS requires the redirect URI to match the application settings exactly, so the callback must use one of the configured loopback ports instead of a random port. A separate ao-app://complete deep link restores the native prompt after the browser has already landed on the close-tab page.

## Validation
- npm --prefix frontend test -- cloud-auth
- npm run frontend:typecheck
- git diff --check -- frontend/src/main/cloud-auth.ts frontend/src/main/cloud-auth.test.ts frontend/src/main.ts

title: fix(terminal): reduce resize jitter by CSS-scaling during animations
body:
## What happened

The terminal flickers and jitters whenever the container resizes, especially during inspector panel open/close animations. Four things were going wrong at the same time in XtermTerminal.tsx.

## What this PR does

1. **CSS-scale during animations instead of fitting every frame** - When the live-resize attribute is active, we now scale the existing canvas with CSS transform to match the container size. One real fit() happens when the animation ends. This completely avoids the WebGL atlas rebuild storm that was causing the flicker.

2. **Gate the convergence loop behind the debounce** - Added a `debounceInFlight` flag so the onRender convergence loop skips its work while a debounced fit is pending. Before this they could run at the same time and fight over the grid size.

3. **Pin the scrollbar width permanently** - After zeroing `viewport.scrollBarWidth`, we now freeze it with `Object.defineProperty` so FitAddon cant re-read the DOM and bring back the 15px reservation on subsequent fits.

4. **Skip late settle timeouts when ResizeObserver already settled** - The 600ms and 1200ms backstop timeouts now check if the ResizeObserver already produced a stable frame and skip if so. The early 50/250ms ones still run since they help with font loading.

Closes #4155

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles clean (only pre-existing error in product-ui, unrelated)
- [ ] Open/close inspector panel, terminal should resize smoothly without flicker
- [ ] Drag sidebar, terminal should scale during drag and snap to correct grid after
- [ ] Window resize should still work correctly
- [ ] Font size change (Ctrl+=/Ctrl+-) should still refit properly
- [ ] Retained terminals (tab switching) should still restore correctly

title: feat: nudge SCM polling on agent turn end
body:
## Summary

- reduce agent-driven PR discovery and state-refresh latency from up to the 30-second fallback interval to about 2 seconds after an accepted agent turn-end signal
- cover the full mutation class: PR creation, draft→ready, close, reopen, and pushes to an existing PR branch
- add a concurrent-safe, non-blocking SCM observer nudge channel with a 2-second debounce window
- coalesce concurrent turn-end hooks into one poll and let a regular tick satisfy a pending nudge, avoiding back-to-back provider scans
- wire normalized agent stop hooks through lifecycle after session/generation fencing; terminal command parsing was intentionally avoided because one provider-neutral turn-end signal covers all supported PR mutations
- preserve the independent 30-second scheduled poll as the fallback

## Before / after

Before, a PR created or mutated by an agent could remain stale in the sidebar until the next SCM tick, adding up to about 30 seconds of latency. After, the accepted turn-end hook schedules one debounced poll, so the sidebar normally reflects the mutation in about 2 seconds.

## Tests

- added an end-to-end observer-loop test that establishes a draft PR, changes it to ready, nudges the observer, and verifies the ready state is persisted without waiting for the hourly test ticker
- go test ./... (with all AO_* environment variables unset)
- npm run lint (with all AO_* environment variables unset)
- go test -race ./internal/observe/scm ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/daemon
- repeated focused nudge, draft→ready, debounce, and lifecycle wiring tests (20 runs)

## Risk

The nudge performs the existing full observer poll. Discovery and refresh remain scoped by the observer to tracked sessions, branches, PRs, and repositories; no new provider API path, command parsing, or persisted state was added.

title: feat(cloud): deploy hardened AWS auth foundation
body:
## Summary

This is the hardened hosted-control-plane stack for #4116.

- deploys the PostgreSQL/Google-auth control plane to AWS through API Gateway, an internal ALB, ECS Fargate, and private encrypted RDS
- separates migration, runtime, auth-definer, and SCM-definer database roles; every tenant relation uses forced RLS and startup validation
- adds tenant-scoped PostgreSQL project/session/worktree storage behind the existing AO ports and shared `/api/v1` route classification
- adds the provider-neutral session execution/workspace-observation seams without moving filesystem or runtime logic into Electron
- adds the control-plane OpenAPI/client contract, including async workspace placement, worker operations, and one-time sandbox terminal-ticket redemption
- adds a first-class **AO Cloud** source to the existing desktop Projects `+` flow; tokens and generic fetch remain in Electron main
- adds the GitHub App SCM boundary: OAuth-proven installation ownership, default-deny repository allowlists, fresh scoped clone/push credentials, durable/idempotent webhook processing, and least-privilege PostgreSQL grants

## Load-bearing security properties

- the runtime database role is a separate unprivileged login and never owns tenant tables or SECURITY DEFINER functions
- SCM webhook and observation ledgers have no direct runtime CRUD; the runtime receives only exact function EXECUTE grants
- GitHub setup and user OAuth callbacks are distinct, state-bound phases; spoofed installations and failed ownership checks do not consume the AO-admin state
- credential material is mutable bytes, bounded, zeroed, never cached, and never returned through renderer IPC or persisted in the SCM ledger
- hosted `/api/v1` tenant selection uses authenticated `X-AO-Org`; org-admin routes retain explicit `orgId` membership checks
- the desktop app remains a thin supervisor; hosted filesystem and PTY bytes belong to sandbox adapters, not Electron or the control plane

## Verification

- `npm run cloud:check`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- focused Electron cloud placement/auth/preload/component tests (69 passing)
- focused cloud client tests (10 passing)
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/cloud/... ./cmd/ao-cloud ./cmd/ao-cloud-migrate`
- `cd backend && go vet ./internal/cloud/... ./cmd/ao-cloud ./cmd/ao-cloud-migrate`
- pinned golangci-lint v2.12.2 on changed cloud packages
- real PostgreSQL 16 restricted-role auth/core-storage/SCM installation/webhook conformance, including RLS, replay, lease recovery, and exact grant boundaries
- native dev Electron restarted with the staging Cloud URL and Cloud early-access flag; Projects `+` exposes the AO Cloud source

## Remaining live-staging gates

The desktop discovery/create surface and contracts are present, but this PR is **not claiming end-to-end sandbox provisioning yet**. Before calling the hosted flow production-ready, staging still needs the concrete workspace-placement/compute adapter, sandbox listener/ticket-consume implementation, and a real Daytona clone/session/mux acceptance run. Unsupported hosted application routes continue to fail closed rather than falling back to control-plane filesystem access.

title: fix(browser): keep panel resize handle draggable over the loaded page
body:
## Summary
- The inspector/terminal split's resize handle sits right at the edge of the browser panel. Electron's `WebContentsView` (the native surface that renders the loaded page) is a separate compositor layer stacked above the app's DOM, so once the drag crossed onto the loaded page's screen area, every subsequent `pointermove`/`pointerup` went straight to that native view instead of the app — killing the drag dead. Dragging over any normal DOM area (top bar, terminal, empty inspector) worked fine, matching the reported symptom.
- The codebase already has a mechanism for exactly this class of problem: `useBrowserView.ts` raises a transparent shell view above the live page (`window.ao.browser.setOverlayOpen`) whenever a dialog/menu needs input priority over the page, detected via a `MutationObserver` on `document.body`.
- This change extends that same detection to also treat `useResizable.ts`'s `is-resizing-x` body class (already toggled for the whole duration of any panel drag) as needing the shell raised, via a second lightweight `MutationObserver` scoped to `document.body`'s own `class` attribute (kept separate from the existing subtree/`data-state` observer so it doesn't fire on every className change app-wide).

## Test plan
- [ ] `ao preview <url>` into a session, open the inspector, and drag the resize handle across the loaded page — confirm the panel keeps resizing smoothly instead of the drag stopping dead.
- [ ] Confirm dragging the same handle when the inspector has no page loaded (or a blank tab) still works as before.
- [ ] Confirm opening a dropdown/dialog over the browser panel still works (regression check on the shared overlay mechanism).

title: fix(browser): crash on link click, agent-visible error signals, device-frame presets
body:
## Summary
Phase 3 of the AO in-app browser UX overhaul (agent visibility & frontend-dev ergonomics):

- **Fixed an app-crashing bug**: clicking any link with `target=_blank` (or `window.open()`) inside the browser crashed the whole app with `Invalid webContents. Created window should be connected to webContents passed with options object.` `setWindowOpenHandler`'s `createWindow` callback returned an independently-created `WebContentsView` that Electron's own `openGuestWindow` could never recognize as linked to the guest-window options it computed for that event. Now denies the guest window outright and opens (and actually navigates — it never did before, even before the crash) AO's own tab instead, entirely outside Electron's guest-window machinery.
- **Console errors and failed requests now reach the agent, always-on**: previously only visible via on-demand polling. Watches every tab's native `console-message` event (no CDP/debugger needed, so it can't conflict with agent-browser's own CDP session) and each session's shared `webRequest` for failed/errored XHR+fetch calls. Debounces a burst into one message per ~5s window and posts it through the same `POST /sessions/{id}/send` endpoint the annotation feature already uses — no new data captured beyond what's already visible in DevTools (text, method/url/status — never bodies).
- **Fixed tabs getting permanently stuck open**: reported live from a real long-running session as "Tab t5 not found; run `agent-browser tab` to list open tabs" on close. The external `agent-browser` automation binary keeps its own internal tab registry that can drift from AO's `session.tabs` over a long session; the close handler used to just propagate that failure and give up, leaving the tab stuck forever. Now falls back to AO's own close path (which only depends on `session.tabs` and the real `WebContentsView`, not the runtime's registry) for that specific failure; unrelated automation-runtime errors still surface normally.
- **Device-frame presets, redesigned**: one-click toolbar dropdown for responsive testing. Named real devices (iPhone SE/14 Pro, Pixel 7, Galaxy S22, iPad Mini/Pro) with reference dimensions shown, plus an inline custom-width field — no arbitrary "Mobile/Tablet/Desktop" buckets, no redundant Desktop option. Also fixes the dropdown rendering *behind* the live page (missing the `data-browser-native-overlay` marker that tells the shell to paint above the native view while it's open — the same mechanism the tabs-rail flyout already relies on).

title: bug(scm): allow claiming draft pull requests
body:
## Bug
`ao spawn --claim-pr` rejects draft pull requests as `PR_NOT_OPEN`, so workers cannot claim a PR until it is marked ready for review.

**Source:** reported in this AO session | **Reported by:** @whoisasx | **Observed:** 2026-08-20 | **Analyzed against:** `5240327386649625c4329fa1bb15d84ca2266e86`
**AO version:** source build `dev`; daemon status confirmed healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Environment:** macOS/Darwin arm64, zsh
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P1 — core PR/session workflow is blocked with no workaround other than changing the PR out of draft.

![AO reports PR_NOT_OPEN when claiming a draft pull request](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-draft-pr-claim-rejection/.issue-assets/draft-pr-claim-rejection.png)

## Reproduction
1. Have an open draft pull request in the registered repository.
2. Run `ao spawn --project reverb --name "pr-worker" --claim-pr <draft-pr-number>`.
3. Observe that session creation is rolled back with `PR_NOT_OPEN` / `PR is not open`.

This was reproduced consistently while attempting to claim [PR #4168](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4168).

## Root Cause
`backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go:23` documents `ErrPRNotOpen` as applying to draft, merged, and closed PRs. At `backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go:113`, `ClaimPR` returns that error whenever `obs.PR.Draft || obs.PR.Merged || obs.PR.Closed` is true. The SCM/domain model already preserves draft state and the status pipeline treats draft as a valid open-PR state, so the claim guard is stricter than the rest of the system.

## Fix
Allow draft PRs through the claim path and continue rejecting only merged or closed PRs. Preserve the draft fact in the persisted PR record and add service/CLI coverage for claiming a draft PR while retaining rejection coverage for merged and closed PRs.

## Impact
- `ao spawn --claim-pr` cannot create a worker for a draft PR.
- The generic `PR_NOT_OPEN` response obscures that draft status is the reason for rejection.
- Marking the PR ready is an inconvenient workaround and changes the PR workflow state.

## Related
- No direct duplicate found after searching all open and closed issues for `PR_NOT_OPEN`, `PR is not open`, draft PR claim, and claim PR.
- [#1618](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1618) is related to PR reattachment after a PR is closed or replaced, but does not cover draft PR claims.

title: fix(scm): allow claiming open draft pull requests
body:
Fixes #4171

## Summary
`ao spawn --claim-pr` and `ao session claim-pr` rejected draft PRs with `PR_NOT_OPEN`, so a worker could not be attached to a PR until it was marked ready for review. The claim guard in `backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go` was stricter than the rest of the system — the SCM/domain model already preserves draft state and the status pipeline (`pr_summary.go`, `prState`) treats draft as a valid open-PR state.

The guard now rejects only terminal states:

```go
if obs.PR.Merged || obs.PR.Closed {
    return ClaimPRResult{}, ErrPRNotOpen
}
```

Draft facts are preserved end to end — `claimRowsFromSCM` already sets `Draft: obs.PR.Draft` on the persisted PR row and `pullRequestFacts` carries it into the read model, so the API/CLI still report `state: "draft"` after a successful claim. The `ErrPRNotOpen` doc comment was updated to match.

## Tests
- `TestClaimPRAllowsDraftPR` (new, service): claiming a draft PR succeeds, the persisted PR row keeps `Draft: true` and is not merged/closed, and the returned read model reports the draft PR. Verified this test fails against the old guard with `session: pr not open`.
- `TestClaimPRMapsObserverAndStoreErrors` (extended): retains the `closed` rejection case and adds `merged`, `draft merged`, and `draft closed` — draft alone no longer blocks a claim, but draft + terminal still does.
- `TestSessionClaimPR_Draft` (new, CLI): `ao session claim-pr` on a draft PR succeeds and `--json` output preserves `"state":"draft"`.
- `TestSpawnClaimPR_Draft` (new, CLI): `ao spawn --claim-pr` on a draft PR keeps the spawned session — no rollback request is issued.

Test results:
- `go build ./...` — clean.
- `go test ./...` (backend) — all packages pass.
- Note: running the suite from inside a live AO worker session leaks `AO_SESSION_ID`/`AO_PROJECT_ID`/`AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID` into `internal/cli` and `internal/httpd` tests, which causes pre-existing, unrelated failures. With those variables cleared the full suite is green.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Low risk: one guard condition narrowed; merged/closed rejection is unchanged and still covered.
- Not addressed here: the generic `PR_NOT_OPEN` message remains generic, but it now only fires for merged/closed PRs, which the message describes accurately.

title: feat(diffs): render image files as before/after previews
body:
## Summary

- The diff viewer printed "Binary file preview is not available." for every image, so a changed PNG or a new screenshot in a worktree could only be reviewed by opening the file outside AO. Now it shows the images themselves, before and after.
- Added `GET /sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/file/blob?path=&side=before|after`, which serves one revision of a file as raw bytes. `before` reads it out of the compare base with `git cat-file` (following the rename source when git recorded one), `after` reads the worktree copy. Images only, 16 MB cap, `no-store`.
- Pulled the path resolution out of `GetWorkspaceFile` into a shared helper so the blob route and the file detail agree on which worktree owns a path, what prefix it carries in a workspace project, and which commit is the base.
- The detail response gained `imageMediaType`, set only when the file is binary or deleted — an SVG is text, so it keeps its line diff.
- New `ImageDiffView` draws the two sides on a checkerboard with their pixel dimensions, one pane for added/deleted files, and a fallback message if a side fails to load. Image URLs carry the detail query's load timestamp; the route is `no-store`, so without a changing URL an edited image would never refetch.

## Branch contents

This branch carries three small chrome fixes ahead of the image feature, all of which the image diff sits on top of and none of which have their own PR open:

- `refactor(frontend): remove sidebar hover preview`
- `fix(desktop): keep Linux titlebar cluster clear of the framed panel`
- `fix(board): inset the lane grid inside the framed panel`

The last commit, `fix(diffs): address review on the image preview PR`, applies the review feedback: `gitWorkspaceBlob` now asks git for the object size before reading the bytes, each image pane is keyed by its source so a failed load recovers when the file changes, and the dead `--z-sidebar-preview` / `--z-index-sidebar-preview` tokens left by the hover-preview removal are gone.

## Test plan

- Go, 8 new: media-type detection, SVG staying text, both blob sides, added → no before, deleted → no after, rename reading the previous path, non-image rejection, invalid `side`. Plus route tests for content type, `no-store`, the raw body, and the missing-`path` 400.

title: fix(ci): make gitleaks scans incremental
body:
## What

Replace the legacy gitleaks v1 wrapper with its same license-free, pinned gitleaks v7.4 container and an explicit commit list:

- pull requests scan only commits introduced by the PR;
- pushes to `main` scan only commits introduced by that push (`before..after`).

The repository's existing `.gitleaks.toml` rules and redacted output remain unchanged.

## Why

The legacy wrapper does two repository-wide things that make unrelated history break current work:

1. On pull requests it scans both sides of `base...HEAD`, so newer base-only commits can fail a queued or stale PR.
2. On every push to `main` it scans every fetched ref. Recent runs scanned roughly 8,100 commits, took about 6.5 minutes, and repeatedly failed on an old placeholder RSA header in commit `56f64bd` rather than the newly merged change.

That makes every subsequent merge inherit the same historical failure. Incremental ranges preserve secret detection for all new code without repeatedly rescanning unrelated history.

## Testing

- Reproduced the current gitleaks v7.4 failure directly against historical commit `56f64bd`.
- Replayed the previous `main` push range (`5240327..63b5ffb`): one new commit selected, no leaks found in 16 ms.
- Replayed a stale PR range: base-only commits excluded and all PR-side commits retained.
- `go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.7 .github/workflows/gitleaks.yml`
- The PR's own gitleaks workflow runs the new container path.

title: Design for the kanban columns and display status
Implement sorting sessions into Kanban Columns
body:
# Kanban Column Derivation

## Goal

Derive a stable Kanban placement for every worker session from durable facts. The column answers where the session is in its delivery lifecycle and who owns the next step. It is independent from the existing display `SessionStatus`.

```text
Building -> Validating -> Needs Review -> Ready
                                     \
                                      Archive (terminated only)
```

## Scope

This issue adds only the derived Kanban column and board grouping. It does not redesign display statuses, pills, or card content.

Review-run CDC is assumed to be available. It causes the normal workspace refresh; the backend recomputes the column from durable facts on every session-list read.

## Current Implementation

Today:
1. Backend derives one `SessionStatus`.
2. Frontend `attentionZone()` maps that status to the current `working`, `action`, `pending`, and `merge` board lanes.
3. The board separately archives terminated sessions.

The new column must be backend-derived rather than added to the frontend mapping: review-run state, PR-head freshness, and review ownership are durable-fact rules, not UI rules.

## Proposed Contract

Add a derived `kanbanColumn` to each session response:

```text
building | validating | needs_review | ready | archive
```

Do not persist this value. Derive it during `GET /sessions`, alongside the existing derived status.

## Inputs

Build a narrow internal read model from:
- Session facts: worker kind, termination, auto-review and auto-inject settings.
- PR facts: lifecycle, draft/open/merged/closed, current `headSHA`, CI, approvals, and mergeability.
- AO review-run facts: PR URL, target SHA, status, verdict, and GitHub review ID.
- Source-aware SCM review facts: external/human approvals and requested changes, separate from AO-authored reviews/comments.

A review run is current only when `reviewRun.targetSHA == pr.headSHA`.

AO-authored provider reviews must be identified through `reviewRun.githubReviewID`. Do not use aggregate `PRFacts.Review` alone to choose between Validating and Needs Review, because it combines AO and external review signals.

## Column Derivation

First, derive a placement for each PR:

```text
session terminated?
  yes -> Archive

no PR exists?
  yes -> Building

PR is draft?
  yes -> Validating

PR is merged or closed without merge?
  yes -> Ready

PR is approved or mergeable?
  yes -> Ready

AO-owned review/fix/test loop active?
  yes -> Validating

auto review enabled?
  yes -> Validating

otherwise -> Needs Review
```

An AO-owned loop includes current-head AO review work, AO CI fixing, and AO addressing AO-originated review feedback.

Once a PR is in the review lifecycle, worker activity must not move it back to Building. A new head SHA is a new validation cycle:
- Auto review on: Validating.
- Auto review off: Needs Review.

## Multiple PRs

Derive placement per PR, then select the session’s representative PR.

1. Exclude merged and closed PRs while at least one live PR exists.
2. Among live PRs, choose the highest-priority actionable placement:
   1. Ready (mergeable/approved)
   2. Needs Review
   3. Validating
   4. Building
3. Use merged/closed states only when no live PR remains.
4. Add a deterministic tie-breaker, initially latest PR update time.

This ensures a terminal PR does not hide a live PR that needs validation or human review.

## Implementation Steps

1. Define the backend `KanbanColumn` enum and add derived `kanbanColumn` to the session API DTO/OpenAPI contract.
2. Add a pure `deriveKanbanColumn(facts)` reducer next to, but separate from, existing `deriveStatus`.
3. Build the reducer input from session, PR, review-run, and source-aware SCM review facts.
4. Add/read the required review data in the session-list path with bounded queries; do not issue per-card unbounded lookups.
5. Generate API types after changing the DTO.
6. Change `SessionsBoard` to group active workers by `session.kanbanColumn`.
7. Render `archive` through the existing archive section.
8. Leave existing display-status labels and card detail untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every worker session returns one derived `kanbanColumn`.
- Terminated sessions always derive to `archive`.
- No-PR worker sessions derive to `building`.
- Draft and current-head AO validation work derive to `validating`.
- Auto-review-off review-ready PRs derive to `needs_review`.
- Approved/mergeable PRs derive to `ready`.
- A stale review run for an old SHA cannot determine the current column.
- AO and external review signals lead to the appropriate ownership column.
- Multiple PRs select the highest-priority actionable live PR, with deterministic ties.
- A review-run CDC update reaches the existing workspace refresh path and the refreshed session returns its newly derived column.
- Unit, service/API, and board-grouping tests cover the rules above.

title: Implement deriving display status for each agent session
body:
# AO Kanban Status Derivation

This document describes how AO should derive the Kanban presentation for a session from durable facts. The board should stay lifecycle-oriented and mostly unidirectional, while the display status explains what is happening right now.

The proposed active board has four columns:

```text
Building -> Validating -> Needs Review -> Ready
```

Terminated sessions should move out of the active board into a separate archive section.

## Implementation Model

Derive Kanban presentation in two stages:

1. **Derive the Kanban column** from stable lifecycle and ownership facts: session termination, PR existence, PR state, whether auto review is on, whether an internal review/fix/test loop is already active, and whether the PR is approved, mergeable, or finished.
2. **Derive the display status** from the most important current fact inside that column: worker activity, hook freshness, CI, changes requested, review runs, review verdicts, approvals, mergeability, and terminal PR state.

This keeps the column stable and user-facing, while allowing the display status to carry detailed state.

| Stage | Answers | Main inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Column derivation | Where is this session in the lifecycle, and who owns the next step? | Session termination, PR existence, PR state, auto-review setting, active internal review/fix/test loop, human approval, mergeability | `Building`, `Validating`, `Needs Review`, `Ready`, or archive section |
| Display status derivation | What is happening or needed right now? | Worker activity, hook freshness, CI status, changes requested, review run status, review verdict, human approval, mergeability | `Working`, `Blocked`, `Reviewing`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Needs human review`, `Mergeable`, etc. |

## Kanban Columns

| Column | Meaning | Typical display statuses |
|---|---|---|
| Building | AO/agent is creating the change before a PR exists. | `Working`, `Awaiting PR`, `Blocked`, `No signal`, `Exited` |
| Validating | AO is checking, reviewing, testing, or iterating on the PR. This column should be driven by PR existence and AO-owned facts: draft PRs, AO review runs, AO reviewer comments/verdicts, CI fixing, and future AO testing/artifact validation. | `Draft`, `Review scheduled`, `Reviewing`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Checks failing`, `Addressing comments`, `Blocked`, `Exited`, `Review pending`, `Needs review` |
| Needs Review | The PR is review-ready, but AO is not currently responsible for the internal review/fix loop. This column should be driven by current human/external SCM review facts, such as external comments, external requested changes, or missing human approval. | `Needs human review`, `Needs review`, `CI failing`, `Changes requested`, `Commented`, `Addressing comments` |
| Ready | The PR is approved, mergeable, merged, or closed without merge. | `Approved`, `Mergeable`, `Checks failing`, `Merged`, `Closed without merge` |

## Column Derivation Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Fetch durable facts] --> S[Session facts]
    A --> P[PR facts]
    A --> RS[Review session facts]
    A --> RR[Review run facts]

    S --> D[Derive Kanban column]
    P --> D
    RS --> D
    RR --> D

    D --> T0{Session terminated?}
    T0 -->|yes| AR[Archive section]

    T0 -->|no| PR0{Does PR exist?}
    PR0 -->|no| B[Building]

    PR0 -->|yes| PRS0{PR state}
    PRS0 -->|draft| V
    PRS0 -->|merged| RD[Ready]
    PRS0 -->|closed without merge| RD

    PRS0 -->|open| READY0{Approved or mergeable?}
    READY0 -->|yes| RD

    READY0 -->|no| LOOP0{Internal review/fix/test loop active?}
    LOOP0 -->|yes| V[Validating]

    LOOP0 -->|no| AUTO0{Auto review on?}
    AUTO0 -->|yes| V
    AUTO0 -->|no| NR[Needs Review]
```

## Display Status Derivation

After the column is selected, derive the display status with a priority list for that column.

### Building

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B[Building column] --> W0{Worker activity}
    W0 -->|active| W[Working]
    W0 -->|waiting_input or blocked| BL[Blocked]
    W0 -->|exited| EX[Exited]
    W0 -->|idle| H0{Hook signal missing past grace?}
    H0 -->|yes| NS[No signal]
    H0 -->|no| AP[Awaiting PR]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worker activity is `active` | `Working` |
| 2 | Worker activity is `waiting_input` or `blocked` | `Blocked` |
| 3 | Worker activity is `exited` | `Exited` |
| 4 | Worker is hook-capable and hook signal is missing past grace | `No signal` |
| 5 | No PR exists and worker is idle | `Awaiting PR` |

### Validating

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    V[Validating column] --> W0{Worker activity requires attention?}
    W0 -->|waiting_input or blocked| BL[Blocked]
    W0 -->|exited| EX[Exited]

    W0 -->|no| CI0{Current CI failing for PR head SHA?}
    CI0 -->|yes| ACI0{Auto CI injection on?}
    ACI0 -->|yes| FCI[Fixing CI failures]
    ACI0 -->|no| CIF[Checks failing]

    CI0 -->|no| CH0{Current unresolved AO review changes requested?}
    CH0 -->|yes| AR0{Auto review/fix on?}
    AR0 -->|yes| FCH[Addressing comments]
    AR0 -->|no| IRN[Needs review]

    CH0 -->|no| REV0{Current review run exists for PR head SHA?}
    REV0 -->|no + auto review on| RS[Review scheduled]
    REV0 -->|yes| RUN0{Review run status}

    RUN0 -->|queued or running| RV[Reviewing]
    RUN0 -->|failed| NR[Needs review]
    RUN0 -->|cancelled| RP[Review pending]
    RUN0 -->|completed changes_requested and auto-fix on| FCH2[Addressing comments]
    RUN0 -->|completed approved| DONE[Column should become Needs Review or Ready]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worker activity is `waiting_input` or `blocked` while AO owns the loop | `Blocked` |
| 2 | Worker activity is `exited` while AO owns the loop | `Exited` |
| 3 | CI is failing for the current PR head SHA and auto CI injection is on | `Fixing CI failures` |
| 4 | CI is failing for the current PR head SHA and auto CI injection is off | `Checks failing` |
| 5 | Current unresolved AO review changes are requested and auto review/fix is on | `Addressing comments` |
| 6 | Current unresolved AO review changes are requested and auto review/fix is off | `Needs review` |
| 7 | No review run exists for latest PR head SHA and auto review is on | `Review scheduled` |
| 8 | Current review run is queued or running | `Reviewing` |
| 9 | Current review run failed | `Needs review` |
| 10 | Current review run was cancelled | `Review pending` |

### Needs Review

Needs Review is entered only after AO/internal review is approved, not required, or intentionally skipped because auto review is off. Once a card is in this column, display status should be derived only from current CI state and human/external SCM review signals.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    N[Needs Review column] --> CI0{Current CI failing for PR head SHA?}
    CI0 -->|yes| CIF[CI failing]

    CI0 -->|no| EXT0{Current unresolved external review input?}
    EXT0 -->|no| NHR[Needs human review]

    EXT0 -->|yes| AUTO0{Auto-inject review comments on?}
    AUTO0 -->|yes| AC[Addressing comments]

    AUTO0 -->|no| TYPE0{External input type}
    TYPE0 -->|changes requested| CR[Changes requested]
    TYPE0 -->|comment only| COM[Commented]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CI is failing for the current PR head SHA | `CI failing` |
| 2 | Current unresolved external changes are requested and auto-inject review comments is on | `Addressing comments` |
| 3 | Current unresolved external comments exist and auto-inject review comments is on | `Addressing comments` |
| 4 | Current unresolved external changes are requested and auto-inject review comments is off | `Changes requested` |
| 5 | Current unresolved external comments exist and auto-inject review comments is off | `Commented` |
| 6 | No current unresolved external comments or changes are present | `Needs human review` |

### Needs Review Implementation Plan

1. Enter Needs Review only after column derivation has decided that AO/internal review is approved, not required, or intentionally skipped because auto review is off.
2. Do not re-check AO review existence or AO review verdict inside the Needs Review display-status resolver.
3. Fetch only current human/external SCM review signals for the selected PR head SHA.
4. Ignore resolved, outdated, or non-current review threads/comments.
5. Exclude AO-authored reviewer comments and AO review-run output from external review signals.
6. If CI is failing for the current PR head SHA, show `CI failing`.
7. If current unresolved external input exists and auto-inject review comments is on, show `Addressing comments`.
8. If auto-inject review comments is off, distinguish the external input type:
   - external changes requested wins over external comments and shows `Changes requested`;
   - external comments without requested changes show `Commented`.
9. If there is no current unresolved external input, show `Needs human review`.

### Ready

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[Ready column] --> M0{PR merged?}
    M0 -->|yes| M[Merged]

    M0 -->|no| CL0{PR closed without merge?}
    CL0 -->|yes| CL[Closed without merge]

    CL0 -->|no| MG0{PR mergeable?}
    MG0 -->|yes| MG[Mergeable]
    MG0 -->|no| CI0{Checks failing?}
    CI0 -->|yes| CIF[Checks failing]
    CI0 -->|no| AP[Approved]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PR is mergeable | `Mergeable` |
| 2 | PR has required approvals but checks are failing | `Checks failing` |
| 3 | PR has required approvals but is not mergeable yet | `Approved` |
| 4 | PR is merged | `Merged` |
| 5 | PR is closed without merge | `Closed without merge` |

### Archive Section

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Archive section] --> T0{Session terminated?}
    T0 -->|yes| T[Terminated]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Session is terminated | `Terminated` |

## State To Kanban Mapping

| Derived status | Kanban column | Display status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `awaiting_pr` | Building | `Awaiting PR` | Worker is not actively changing code and no PR exists yet. |
| `working` | Building | `Working` | Worker is actively changing code before the PR/review lifecycle starts. |
| `worker_blocked` | Building | `Blocked` | Worker is waiting for input or blocked before a review-ready PR exists. |
| `no_signal` | Building | `No signal` | Hook-capable worker has not reported activity after the grace period. |
| `exited` | Building | `Exited` | Worker process exited or is unavailable before AO owns a PR validation loop. |
| `draft` | Validating | `Draft` | PR exists but is still draft, so AO can complete internal validation before human/external review. |
| `fixing_ci` | Validating | `Fixing CI failures` | CI failed on the current PR head SHA and AO is fixing it. |
| `checks_failing` | Validating | `Checks failing` | CI failed on the current PR head SHA and auto CI injection is off, so surface the failing checks. |
| `fixing_changes` | Validating | `Addressing comments` | AO review comments or AO requested changes exist and AO is fixing them. |
| `needs_review` | Validating | `Needs review` | AO review or validation needs attention while the card is still in the internal validation loop. |
| `review_scheduled` | Validating | `Review scheduled` | Auto review is enabled and latest PR SHA has no current review run yet. |
| `reviewing` | Validating | `Reviewing` | Current AO review run is queued or running. |
| `review_failed` | Validating | `Needs review` | Current AO review run failed while AO owns the validation loop. |
| `review_pending` | Validating | `Review pending` | Review run was cancelled; the PR head still needs an AO review decision. |
| `blocked` | Validating | `Blocked` | AO owns the validation/fix loop, but the worker is blocked or waiting for input. |
| `exited` | Validating | `Exited` | AO owns the validation/fix loop, but the worker exited. |
| `ci_failed` | Needs Review | `CI failing` | CI failed and AO is not automatically fixing it, so a human/external decision is needed. |
| `changes_requested` | Needs Review | `Changes requested` | Human/external SCM reviewer requested changes. |
| `commented` | Needs Review | `Commented` | Human/external SCM reviewer commented without requesting changes. |
| `needs_human_review` | Needs Review | `Needs human review` | AO review is done, unavailable, or intentionally skipped because auto review is off. |
| `approved` | Ready | `Approved` | Required approvals exist, but PR is not mergeable yet. |
| `mergeable` | Ready | `Mergeable` | PR is approved and SCM says it can merge. |
| `checks_failing` | Ready | `Checks failing` | PR has required approvals, but checks are failing and blocking mergeability. |
| `merged` | Ready | `Merged` | PR has merged. |
| `closed_without_merge` | Ready | `Closed without merge` | PR closed without merge; the session stays visible as a final PR outcome. |
| `terminated` | Archive section | `Terminated` | Session is terminal and should be shown outside the main active board. |

## Multiple PRs Per Session

When a session has multiple PRs, derive the state for each PR independently and then pick the PR/status that best answers:

> What should the user care about next for this session?

This means actionable or landable PRs should outrank terminal PRs. A merged or closed-without-merge PR does not require user action, so it should not hide another PR that is still in validation or needs review.

For this ranking, keep review sources separate:

- **AO/internal review facts** come from AO review runs and AO-authored reviewer comments/verdicts. These can place the card in Validating.
- **Human/external review facts** come from SCM review state and non-AO reviewers. These can place the card in Needs Review.

### Selection Rule

1. Derive each PR's column and display status using the two-stage model.
2. Assign each derived PR state a priority score.
3. Pick the highest-priority actionable state for the session card.
4. Use the selected PR's column and display status as the session's Kanban presentation.
5. If only terminal PR states exist, show the best terminal state in Ready.
6. If no PR exists, fall back to session/worker facts and show Building.

### Priority Order

| Priority | Derived state | Column | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mergeable` | Ready | User can merge now. This is the highest-signal landing state. |
| 2 | `approved` | Ready | PR is close to landing, but may still need final checks or mergeability resolution. |
| 3 | `checks_failing` | Ready | PR is approved but checks are failing, so it is close to merge but still blocked. |
| 4 | `ci_failed` | Needs Review | CI failed for the current PR head SHA. |
| 5 | `changes_requested` | Needs Review | Human/external SCM reviewer requested changes. |
| 6 | `commented` | Needs Review | Human/external SCM reviewer commented without requesting changes. |
| 7 | `needs_human_review` | Needs Review | Human/external review is the next step. |
| 8 | `blocked` | Validating | AO owns the validation loop, but the worker is blocked. |
| 9 | `fixing_ci` | Validating | AO is actively fixing CI. |
| 10 | `checks_failing` | Validating | CI is failing while the card is in Validating, but auto CI injection is off. |
| 11 | `fixing_changes` | Validating | AO is actively fixing AO review comments or AO requested changes. |
| 12 | `needs_review` | Validating | AO review requested changes or validation needs attention. |
| 13 | `review_failed` | Validating | AO review automation failed and needs attention. |
| 14 | `reviewing` | Validating | AO/reviewer is currently processing. |
| 15 | `review_scheduled` | Validating | Auto review is expected for the latest PR head SHA. |
| 16 | `review_pending` | Validating | Review was cancelled or still needs an AO review decision. |
| 17 | `draft` | Validating | PR exists as a draft and is still in AO validation. |
| 18 | `working` | Building | Worker is actively building before review. |
| 19 | `worker_blocked` | Building | Worker is blocked before the review lifecycle. |
| 20 | `exited` | Building | Worker exited before the review lifecycle. |
| 21 | `no_signal` | Building | Worker signal is missing before the review lifecycle. |
| 22 | `awaiting_pr` | Building | No PR exists yet. |
| 23 | `merged` | Ready | Terminal PR state with no user action required. |
| 24 | `closed_without_merge` | Ready | Terminal PR state with no user action required. |
| 25 | `terminated` | Archive section | Terminal session state. |

### Examples

| Session facts | Selected presentation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| PR #10 is `merged`, PR #11 is `changes_requested` | Needs Review / `Changes requested` | The merged PR is terminal; the changes-requested PR still needs action. |
| PR #10 is `closed_without_merge`, PR #11 is `reviewing` | Validating / `Reviewing` | The closed PR is terminal; active AO validation work is more relevant. |
| PR #10 is `mergeable`, PR #11 is `fixing_changes` | Ready / `Mergeable` | Mergeable is immediately landable, so it wins. |
| PR #10 is `approved`, PR #11 is `review_failed` | Ready / `Approved` | Approved is closer to landing. |
| PR #10 is `merged`, PR #11 is `closed_without_merge` | Ready / `Merged` | Only terminal PRs remain, so show the best terminal outcome. |

## Notes

| Note | Detail |
|---|---|
| Column meaning | Columns represent lifecycle phase and next-action ownership, not literal agent activity. |
| Unidirectional flow | The intended movement is `Building -> Validating -> Needs Review -> Ready`. A card should not bounce back to Building just because AO is fixing review comments or CI. |
| Validating scope | Validating is the AO-owned loop: AO review, CI fixing, review-comment fixing, and future testing/artifact validation. |
| Needs Review scope | Needs Review is the human/external-review stage. For an open, review-ready PR that is not approved or mergeable, if auto review is off and no internal loop is active, the default column is Needs Review. |
| Building width | If Building has more than 5-10 visible sessions and users must scroll heavily, widen Building because many sessions naturally accumulate there. |
| Stale facts after new comments | Stale or newly-arrived facts are handled by deriving status from the current PR head SHA and current unresolved review/CI facts. For example, if CI fails while review comments are being addressed and AO owns the fix, the card stays in Validating with display status `Fixing CI failures`. |
| External comment currentness | Needs Review should only consider unresolved comments or current review threads. Resolved, outdated, or non-current external comments should not keep the card in `Commented` or `Changes requested`. |
| Review fact currentness | Review facts should be tied to the current PR head SHA or SCM's current review decision. Stale approvals, comments, or requested changes from older commits should not control the current display status. |
| External review priority | For external SCM input, `Changes requested` should win over `Commented`, and both should win over generic `Needs human review`. |
| Auto review off | If auto review is off, AO should not force adversarial review. A review-ready PR can go directly to Needs Review with display status `Needs human review`, unless it is already approved or mergeable. |
| Draft PR when auto review is on | Once the Building stage is done, or whenever a PR is raised for a session with auto review on, the PR should be opened as a draft so AO can complete internal validation before human/external review. |
| Archive section | Terminated sessions should move out of the main four-column board into a separate archive section. |

## Open Questions

| Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Multiple PR tie-breakers | If two PRs have the same derived priority, we still need deterministic tie-breakers such as most recent PR update time, highest PR number, or latest head SHA update. |

title: feat(observability): Sentry-ready error capture + triage classification (renderer)
body:
First, shippable slice of the Sentry error-handling work. **Dormant until a DSN exists**, so it can merge now and go live the moment the Sentry account is ready — no code change at ship time beyond adding the dep + setting the DSN.

## What this adds
- **`shared/observability.ts`** — pure `classifyError()` turning any failure into triage tiers: **severity** (P0 fatal → P3 expected) and **fault owner** (`ours` / `user` / `external` / `environment`), on top of the existing `category`/`code`. Additive: unknown errors fall back to a safe `P2/ours`, never unlabelled. Fully unit-tested (14 cases).
- **`renderer/lib/sentry.ts`** — a Sentry sink fed from the two **existing** telemetry seams, so there is one capture path, not two. No-op unless: (1) telemetry consent is granted (same gate as PostHog), and (2) `VITE_AO_SENTRY_DSN` is set. Scrubs local URLs/paths from messages/stacks; attaches only safe enum/id tags (`platform, surface, domain, operation, category, code, http_status, severity, owner`).
