title: fix(chat): fail fast on immutable history replay
body:
## What

- add an optional `ChatHistoryRefresher` port for history sources that can make a new authoritative provider observation
- read every native history source once, then retry only through that explicit refresh operation
- keep ACP `session/load` replay snapshot-only so an incomplete replay fails immediately instead of polling the same cache for 45 seconds
- make Codex refreshable through its real `thread/read`, preserving bounded convergence where it can actually make progress

## Why

Fixes #4123.

ACP captures replay once during `Resume`; every later `ReadHistory` returns the same frozen events. The generic settle loop nevertheless reread that cache every 100ms for up to 45 seconds when it was unsettled or missed AO's checkpoint. That delayed a guaranteed handoff failure and rollback without observing any new provider fact.

## How

This follows ACP v1's actual boundary: [`session/load` is a finite replay whose response follows the replayed entries](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol/blob/main/docs/protocol/v1/session-setup.mdx), not a standardized repeatable history read.

- `ChatHistoryReader` represents one authoritative history observation.
- `ChatHistoryRefresher` promises that `RefreshHistory` performs provider I/O or waits for a real provider signal.
- `Controller.importNativeHistory` keeps its bounded timeout around the initial read and refresh loop, but immediately returns `ErrChatHistoryUnsettled` when an incomplete source cannot refresh.
- Codex implements refresh by issuing another `thread/read(includeTurns: true)`.
- ACP deliberately does not implement refresh; the PR never reissues `session/load`, adds a grace sleep, or infers provider state from a load response.

Intentional omissions: this focused fix does not change trailing-user-only turn classification, introduce load-versus-resume intent, or adopt draft ACP v2 lifecycle/replay types. Those require separate state/evidence contracts and should not be coupled to #4123.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/chat ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver -count=1`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/ports ./internal/service/chat ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver -count=1`
- `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE=/tmp/ao-lint-cache-4123-fresh npm run lint` — full backend tests and golangci-lint, 0 issues

Regression coverage verifies:

- an immutable unsettled replay is read exactly once and fails immediately
- an immutable settled replay behind AO's checkpoint is read exactly once and fails immediately
- a refreshable unsettled source converges through one initial read plus one refresh
- a refreshable settled-but-stale source refreshes until it reaches AO's checkpoint
- cancellation before refresh preserves the typed unsettled error and context cause
- Codex refresh performs a second wire `thread/read`
- ACP conversations do not advertise refreshability

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for the changed boundary and user-visible failure behavior
- [x] Relevant build, race, test, and lint checks pass

title: feat: automate agent catalog refresh
body:
## Summary

Remove manual agent and model catalog refresh controls and move catalog freshness behind the existing cache-first daemon boundary.

The resulting read path is:

`UI → TanStack Query cache → daemon API → SQLite cache → local CLI discovery only when refresh/revalidation is due`

## What changed

### Persist the agent installation inventory

- Add a singleton `agent_inventory_cache` SQLite table containing the last successfully observed installed/authorized snapshot and its observation timestamp.
- Hydrate the daemon's in-memory inventory from SQLite on the first read after startup, without running agent CLI probes.
- Reconcile persisted IDs against the adapters supported by the current daemon build so removed adapters are not shown and current labels win over stale cached labels.
- Persist the next snapshot after a successful bounded inventory probe.
- Keep installation and authorization state advisory: session spawn remains the authoritative runtime validation boundary.

### Trigger refresh automatically

- Keep the existing daemon startup refresh so installations are reconciled in the background whenever the daemon boots.
- Refresh the inventory through `refreshAgentsIfStale()` when Project Settings opens, then update the TanStack Query cache with the result.
- Preserve the existing create-project stale refresh behavior already present on `main`.
- Continue rate-limiting and serializing inventory probes so multiple UI reads cannot stampede local agent CLIs.

### Make model revalidation actually refresh

- Continue serving cached model catalogs immediately.
- When the trust window expires, let the frontend revalidate in the background.
- Fix `RevalidateModels` so it performs discovery even when the binary/config fingerprint has not changed. This covers provider-side catalog drift that a local fingerprint cannot detect.
- Preserve stale/fallback catalog behavior and warnings when rediscovery fails.

### Remove manual catalog controls

- Remove the Project Settings “Refresh agents” row.
- Remove worker and orchestrator model refresh buttons.
- Remove the optional model-menu rediscovery action and now-unused product UI refresh props.
- Keep explicit daemon refresh endpoints/helpers for background refresh and older-client compatibility; only the manual UI controls are removed.
- Leave unrelated reload/update controls (browser reload, application update checks, retry actions) unchanged.

## Why

Catalog refresh is application bookkeeping, not a decision users should need to make. Persisting the last known inventory makes the UI useful immediately after restart, TanStack Query avoids repeated renderer fetches, and background daemon probing repairs stale installation data without blocking normal reads.

This also avoids repeatedly invoking agent CLIs during routine navigation while still converging after installs, removals, daemon restarts, or aged model catalogs.

## Failure behavior

- A missing, corrupt, or temporarily unreadable inventory snapshot falls back to the daemon's supported catalog and can be repaired by the background startup refresh.
- A failed live agent probe does not erase supported adapters; the next automatic trigger can retry.
- A failed inventory-cache write does not publish or rate-limit the probed snapshot, so the next refresh retries persistence instead of reporting a false success.
- A failed model rediscovery retains the fuller cached catalog when available and surfaces its warning.
- Spawn remains authoritative if cached installation/auth data has become stale.

## Verification

- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/go-build go test ./internal/service/agent ./internal/storage/sqlite`
- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/go-build go test ./internal/daemon`
- `npm run sqlc`
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck`
- Focused renderer tests: 44 passed
- `npm --prefix packages/product-ui run typecheck`
- Product UI tests: 61 passed

## Notes

- No API contract shape changed, so OpenAPI regeneration is not required.
- Migration `0104_agent_inventory_cache.sql` uses the next available migration number after merging the latest `main`.

title: bug(chat): transient Codex network loss is misreported as a fatal thread error
body:
## Bug

When a Codex Chat turn exhausts its reconnect attempts during a transient network outage, Codex app-server briefly reports the thread as `systemError`. AO persists that status and the desktop renders a banner claiming the provider thread is broken and future turns will usually fail. The prognosis is false: once connectivity returns, the next message succeeds on the same thread.

**Source:** AO chat report with read-only evidence from session `agent-orchestrator-140` | **Observed:** 2026-08-20 PDT | **Analyzed against:** `52fde0279` | **AO version:** locally built `dev`, daemon on port 3001
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — Chat is degraded and the banner discourages the working recovery path, but sending a new message after connectivity returns is a workaround.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Codex session in Chat mode and begin a turn.
2. Disconnect the machine from the network long enough for Codex to exhaust its response-stream reconnect attempts.
3. Observe Codex app-server emit `thread/status/changed` with `status.type = systemError`, followed by `turn/completed` with a failed turn and a transport error such as `stream disconnected before completion: error sending request for url (https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses)`.
4. Observe AO render “The agent's thread hit an internal error” and say new turns will usually fail.
5. Restore connectivity and send another message. The same thread becomes `active`, answers normally, and returns to `idle`.

Concrete incident timeline (2026-08-20 PDT):

- 14:57:26 — turn `01a0212d-d469-75c1-b54b-4707757194be` became active.
- 15:03:44 — laptop entered clamshell sleep and Wi-Fi dropped; Codex emitted two five-attempt reconnect cycles, including macOS DNS lookup failure and an error sending the responses request.
- 15:24:33 — provider emitted `systemError`, then completed the turn as failed with the transport error.
- 16:59:43 — next user turn `01a0219d-c59c-73c2-8921-d12975cef2b9` became active on the same provider conversation.
- 17:07:55 — that turn completed normally and the thread returned to idle.

## Root Cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/normalize.go` maps every Codex `systemError` thread status directly to `domain.ThreadStatusSystemError` without correlating it with the immediately following failed turn.
- The same normalizer preserves the `turn/completed` error text but does not classify transport signatures or repair the pessimistic thread state.
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` persists thread-state updates independently. Therefore the transient `system_error` is sticky until a later provider status report replaces it.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatStatusBanners.tsx` treats every `system_error` as a durable provider-thread fault and explicitly predicts that new turns will usually fail.

Read-only durable evidence from the incident shows this exact event order:

1. `thread.state = active`
2. `thread.state = system_error`
3. `turn.completed = failed`, error `stream disconnected before completion: error sending request for url (...)`
4. on the next message, `thread.state = active`
5. `thread.state = idle`
6. `turn.completed = completed`

This falsifies the theory that AO derives `system_error` from any failed turn: Codex reports it. AO's bug is interpreting and persisting that provider status without the transport-failure context it reports milliseconds later.

## Fix

- Classify known transient Codex transport failures from the failed turn's error signature.
- Preserve the turn as failed and preserve its error text.
- Correlate the transport failure with the preceding `systemError`, restore the thread to a healthy idle state, and retain a current “connection lost during this turn” notice until the next turn begins.
- Render recovery-oriented copy that tells the user to send a message again.
- Keep genuine unclassified `systemError` behavior unchanged.
- Add adapter/service and renderer tests for transient versus genuine system errors and for clearing the connection-loss notice on the next active status.

## Impact

- Users are told a healthy, reusable conversation is probably permanently broken.
- The incorrect state remains visible throughout an outage and after connectivity returns, until another turn is attempted.
- Users may abandon context or restart work unnecessarily.

## Related

- [#4120](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4120) — also involved a failed Chat turn, but concerned TUI→Chat history settlement rather than transient thread-state classification.

title: feat(chat): retry a failed turn without retyping the prompt
body:
## Problem

When a Chat turn fails after transient network loss, AO preserves the failed turn and its error correctly, but the user has no one-click way to submit the same prompt again. They must retype or manually copy the original message.

This is especially confusing when the recovery guidance says to send the message again.

**Source:** Follow-up from [#4212](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4212) | **Analyzed against:** `52fde0279`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — the core recovery path works, but avoidable re-entry friction follows a common transient failure.

## Current Behavior

- A failed turn is durable and its original human message remains in the timeline.
- The turn boundary displays `Failed` and the provider error.
- Rollback and edit/branch operations exist, but no operation means “dispatch this failed human prompt again as a new turn.”
- The composer retains attachments only when the initial send itself fails before acceptance; it does not restore content for an asynchronously failed provider turn.

## Proposed Behavior

Add a **Retry turn** action to eligible failed-turn boundaries that:

1. Reuses the durable original human message content and attachments.
2. Creates a new turn rather than mutating or relabeling the failed attempt.
3. Preserves both attempts in history and keeps provider-turn correlation explicit.
4. Uses the conversation's current next-turn settings unless product design deliberately chooses to preserve the failed attempt's settings.
5. Is disabled while another turn is running and reports daemon/provider refusals in place.
6. Is safe against double-clicks and uncertain delivery; it must not silently execute the work twice.

## Scope Notes

This should be a dedicated daemon/API operation, not renderer-side reconstruction of message text. The daemon owns ordering, attachments, delivery state, and idempotency. Reusing the existing edit/fork path would change conversation history semantics and is not equivalent to retrying after a recoverable failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Retry is offered only for an eligible failed human turn.
- Clicking once creates exactly one new queued/running turn with the same content.
- The original failed turn remains failed and visible.
- Attachments are reused or a clear validation error explains why they cannot be.
- Busy, unsupported-provider, stale-branch, and uncertain-delivery cases are tested.
- Renderer tests cover visible, hidden, disabled, pending, and error states.

## Related

- [#4212](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4212) — classifies transient Codex network failures and provides accurate recovery guidance.

title: fix(chat): classify transient Codex transport failures

## Summary

- classify narrow Codex response-stream transport signatures after the provider reports `systemError`
- preserve the failed turn and exact provider error while restoring the reusable thread to healthy `idle`
- retain a recoverable connection-loss notice until the next turn becomes active
- render accurate recovery guidance instead of predicting that future turns will fail
- leave genuine/unclassified provider `systemError` behavior unchanged
- regenerate OpenAPI and renderer API types for the optional connection-loss timestamp

## Evidence

In session `agent-orchestrator-140`, Codex emitted `thread/status/changed = systemError` immediately before a failed `turn/completed` with `stream disconnected before completion: error sending request for url (...)`. The same provider conversation accepted the next turn, became active, completed normally, and returned to idle. The durable AO event order confirms the status came from Codex; AO's fault was retaining and presenting it without the transport context reported milliseconds later.

## Tests

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_DAEMON_URL -u AO_RUN_FILE -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_PORT npm run lint`
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_DAEMON_URL -u AO_RUN_FILE -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_PORT sh -c 'cd backend && go test -race ./...'`
- `npm run api`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd frontend && npm test` — 2,630 passed, 1 skipped

## Risk / follow-up

Classification is intentionally limited to response-stream failures with known DNS/send/reset/closed/timeout transport signatures. Unknown errors continue to display the provider's genuine `systemError` state.

A one-click retry action is intentionally separate because it needs a daemon-owned, idempotent history/dispatch operation: [#4215](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4215).

title: fix(tmux): stop a destroyed session handing AO's terminal to another session
body:
## What

Set `detach-on-destroy on` for AO's own tmux sessions, so destroying one detaches AO's terminal client instead of letting tmux move it onto a session AO does not own.

## Why

Fixes #4223.

tmux's `detach-on-destroy off` — a common tmux.conf line, since it keeps you inside tmux when you kill a session — makes tmux move an attached client to **another session** rather than detaching it. AO's terminal attachment is such a client, so destroying an AO session silently reparents AO's PTY onto one of the user's own sessions. Three consequences, all silent:

* the attach stream never EOFs, so the attachment never observes the session ending and holds the PTY open;
* that unrelated session's output streams into AO's terminal view;
* **anything typed into that view executes in that session's pane.**

The third is why this is more than cosmetic — it is input crossing a session boundary the user never agreed to, into a pane that may be running anything.

Measured directly, by forking a PTY onto `tmux attach -t <ao session>` and then killing that session:

```
WITHOUT the fix (user has 'off') | client before kill: 'aosess' | after kill: 'other' | attach client exited: False
WITH  session-scoped 'on'        | client before kill: 'aosess' | after kill: ''      | attach client exited: True
```

It also makes this repo's own `TestAttachmentStreamsRealTmuxPane` (`internal/terminal`) fail on such a machine, at the `a.isExited()` assertion — that failure is what led me here.

## How

Two call sites, covering two different populations of session.

**`Create`** already sets three session options after `new-session` (`status off`, `mouse on`, `window-size largest`); this adds a fourth in the same shape. Scoped with `-t`, so the user's own sessions keep whatever they configured — verified: with the global at `off`, `show-options -t <ao session>` reports `on` while `show-options -t other` still inherits `off`.

**`Attach`** retrofits it, best-effort. tmux sessions outlive the app, so a session created by a build without the `Create` hunk still carries the user's global `off` and would keep leaking until it was recreated. My first version put this in `Destroy`; review pointed out that only covers teardowns AO initiates, and misses the user typing `exit` in the keep-alive shell or killing the session from their own tmux. Attaching is the **exact precondition** for the leak — with no client of ours attached there is nothing for tmux to reparent — so setting it there covers an adopted session for every way it can end. That makes the `Destroy` call redundant rather than merely insufficient, so it is gone and four `Destroy` call-order assertions go back to their original form.

## Testing

Two integration tests, both driving a **private tmux server** (`TMUX_TMPDIR` + `-f /dev/null` + a cleared `TMUX`) with the global set to `off`, plus a bystander session standing in for one of the user's own. tmux's default is `on`, so a test relying on the developer's tmux.conf would be green on CI and prove nothing.

- `TestRuntimeIntegrationDestroyDetachesClientUnderDetachOnDestroyOff` — attaches through the runtime's own `Attach`, destroys, asserts the stream ends with no client left behind. It waits for the client to appear in `list-clients` first, so it cannot pass by racing the attach.
- `TestRuntimeIntegrationAttachRetrofitsSessionCreatedBeforeFix` — ages a session by forcing the option back to `off` after `Create`, which is exactly the state a pre-fix build leaves behind, then attaches and destroys. Fails without the `Attach` hunk, naming the leak:

```
attach stream never ended after Destroy; tmux clients now on: "ao-dod-bystander"
```

Clearing `TMUX` is not cosmetic: tmux only honours `TMUX_TMPDIR` when it is not already inside a session, so `go test` run from inside tmux — likely, for tests about tmux — would otherwise target the developer's real server, flip its global `detach-on-destroy`, and let the cleanup `tmux kill-server` destroy their sessions, AO's own agent sessions included. I reproduced that on a throwaway server (a session named `precious_user_session` did not survive) before fixing it. Server setup and the attach/destroy assertion are shared helpers so a future test cannot reintroduce either hole.

```console
$ go test ./internal/terminal/...                       # incl. the previously-failing attachment test
ok
$ go test ./internal/observe/... ./internal/session_manager/...
ok
$ go test -race ./...                                   # whole backend
ok
$ go vet ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/...
$ golangci-lint v2.12.2 run ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/...
0 issues.
```

Note: on a box that also sets `base-index 1`, `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` still fails here — that is the separate bug in #4222, fixed by #4224, and unrelated to this change.

**Overlap:** #4224 touches the same package. The two conflict only where both append to the tail of `tmux_integration_test.go`; `commands.go` and `tmux_test.go` auto-merge. I've verified the two fixes applied together are green on both tmux configurations and across the full backend suite under `-race`, and I'll rebase whichever lands second.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (based on `52fde0279`)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go test`, `go test -race`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint`)

title: feat(kanban): add prerequisites for future column derivation
body:
## Summary

Prepare the durable facts and live-update plumbing required for a later Kanban column-derivation feature.

This issue is **prerequisite work only**. It must not add `kanbanColumn`, alter board grouping, implement column rules, or add display statuses. Those belong in a follow-on issue once the required facts can be read and observed reliably.

## Why This Is Needed

The future Kanban reducer must answer two questions from durable facts:

1. Is AO currently responsible for internal review/fix work on this PR head SHA?
2. Did a fact change that could alter the future column, so the board should refresh immediately?

Today, the answer is incomplete:

- `review_run` facts are durable, but session list assembly does not load them as a reducer input.
- `review_run` insert/update does not write a CDC event, so the desktop only discovers review-run changes through the 15-second fallback refetch or an unrelated fact change.
- The compact `PRFacts` shape contains an aggregate review decision and an any-author unresolved-comment boolean. It cannot by itself distinguish an AO-authored review result from a human/external review result.

## Scope

### 1. Create a column-derivation facts snapshot

Add a read-only internal snapshot/query surface for future session-level Kanban derivation. It must provide, for every attributed PR:

- durable PR lifecycle facts, including current `head_sha`;
- current AO review runs matched by `session_id`, `pr_url`, and current `target_sha`;
- review-run status, verdict, trigger source, `github_review_id`, and the recorded automatic-review-injection policy;
- the session's `auto_review_enabled`, `auto_inject_review`, and `auto_inject_ci` policies;
- a source-aware view of external/human review facts when required.

Do not expose this snapshot as a broad new frontend API. It is an internal service/read-model dependency for the future backend reducer.

### 2. Establish source-aware review facts

Document and implement the exact reducer-facing rule for separating AO-owned and external review facts for the current PR head SHA.

Existing facts that can participate:

- `review_run.github_review_id` identifies the SCM review posted by AO;
- `review_run.target_sha` establishes whether that AO review applies to the current PR head;
- persisted `pr_reviews` carry review ID, author, state, target SHA, and `auto_inject_review`;
- persisted `pr_comment` rows carry author, resolution, and `auto_inject_review`.

The new internal snapshot must make it possible for a future reducer to answer:

```text
AO internal review/fix work for current head?
external/human review requires attention for current head?
```

It must not rely only on `PRFacts.Review` or `PRFacts.ReviewComments`, because those are aggregate values and do not carry review ownership.

### 3. Add CDC for review-run lifecycle changes

Add SQLite-triggered CDC events for `review_run` insert and update, for example:

```text
review_run_created
review_run_updated
```

Requirements:

- resolve `project_id` through the owning session and include `session_id` in the event;
- cover review creation, completion/delivery, failure, and cancellation;
- update any `change_log.event_type` constraint/migration required by the new event names;
- add the event types to the backend CDC vocabulary and the desktop event transport watched list;
- preserve the architecture rule: database triggers write `change_log`; do not manually publish parallel CDC events from store methods.

The current path can then stay consistent:

```text
review_run write
  -> SQLite trigger writes change_log
  -> CDC poller broadcasts within its normal cadence
  -> SSE event reaches desktop
  -> workspace query refetches
```

### 4. Make the read path board-safe

The board lists many sessions. The prerequisite query shape must avoid an unbounded per-card review-run/review-detail query pattern.

Choose and test one of:

- a batch query keyed by the listed worker session IDs;
- a session-list read model query that joins/preloads the necessary current-head facts;
- a bounded lookup strategy with explicit query-count coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A future backend reducer can obtain current-head AO review-run facts without using frontend data or inferring from display status.
- The future reducer can distinguish AO-owned review/fix facts from external/human review facts; aggregate `PRFacts.Review` alone is not used for this distinction.
- `review_run` creation, completion/delivery, failure, and cancellation each create durable CDC records tied to the owning project and session.
- `/api/v1/events` replays and streams the new review-run events.
- The desktop event transport treats those events as workspace-invalidating events.
- A test proves a review-run fact change reaches the client via CDC; it must not depend on the 15-second workspace refetch interval.
- List-session reads remain bounded as the board session count grows.

## Explicit Non-Goals

- No `kanbanColumn` enum or API field.
- No `Building`, `Validating`, `Needs Review`, `Ready`, or Archive placement logic.
- No Kanban UI or Figma changes.
- No display-status work.
- No reviewer activity-hook changes. Review-run durable facts, not reviewer activity, are the prerequisite for column derivation.

## Follow-up

After this issue lands, create a separate issue to implement the pure backend column reducer, expose its result through the session API, and group board cards using that derived field.

## References

- `backend/internal/domain/pr.go`
- `backend/internal/domain/review.go`
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/review_store.go`
- `backend/internal/cdc/poller.go`
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/event-transport.ts`

body:
## What

Captures the GitHub organisation/account that owns a project so AO usage can be attributed and **ranked per org/account** (a prerequisite for connecting with the most-engaged teams and individuals for feedback).

- Adds a `github_org` property to `ao.projects.created` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added`, derived from the project's `origin` remote.

Repository name, path, branch, or full URL. Only the owner slug.

Follow-ups (separate PRs), not in this one:
- A first-run consent notice + a Settings toggle (recommended before this ships to users, since telemetry is currently on-by-default and described as "anonymous").
- Per-user `github_login` capture (needs the SCM identity resolver wired at the daemon root) for person-level outreach.
- Optionally hashing `github_org`.

## Tests

- `TestGithubOwner` covers scp/https/ssh/git forms, personal accounts, whitespace, non-GitHub, gist subdomain, and owner-only remotes.

## Risk

Low. Only adds one bounded string property on project-add events, gated by the existing telemetry consent/allowlist path. No behavior change when a project has no GitHub origin.

title: feat(packaging): make AO install properly on Linux
body:
## Making AO install properly on Linux

Today most Linux users run AO by double-clicking an AppImage wherever it landed. It works, but AO never gets *installed*: no applications-menu entry, no `ao` in the terminal, and nothing keeps a deb or rpm up to date. This makes AO install like any other Linux app.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-08-21-linux-native-install.md` (in this PR, with every step's findings recorded).

### What changes

**`ao` on PATH for deb and rpm.** The CLI and the daemon are the same Go binary shipped inside the app, but nothing ever linked it into `/usr/bin`, so `which ao` failed on a machine with AO installed and `ao preview <url>` was unavailable to every Linux user. Neither maker can carry the link in its payload (`electron-installer-debian` emits exactly one `/usr/bin` symlink; the generated rpm spec has a fixed `%files` list, so an extra file fails the build as unpackaged), so it is done with maintainer scripts in `frontend/packaging/linux/`. Each refuses to touch a `/usr/bin/ao` pointing elsewhere, and removal only fires on a real uninstall.

**No self-updating on a package-manager install.** `initAutoUpdates()` started electron-updater for any packaged build. On a deb or rpm install the app lives in root-owned `/usr/lib` with every file tracked by dpkg or rpm, so the updater tried to overwrite files it does not own. `isPackageManagedInstall()` (Linux, `APPIMAGE` unset, app directory unwritable) stops that, and the Settings panel says why instead of failing quietly. AppImage self-updates are untouched.

**A real menu entry for the AppImage.** `ao start` already wrote a `.desktop` file, but with `NoDisplay=true` — an entry deliberately hidden from the menu, which is why people hand-write launchers pointing at `~/Downloads`. It is now a real entry with an icon extracted from the AppImage itself.

**An Arch package** (`packaging/arch/`). Repackages the official deb rather than building from source: the deb is already laid out the way Arch wants, while a source build would drag a full Go build, a full npm build and a bundled Chromium download onto every user's machine. Adds a tracked `/usr/bin/ao`, restores `chrome-sandbox`'s setuid bit (without it Electron refuses to start), and installs a themed icon. `update-pkgbuild.sh` bumps it to a new release. Nothing is published to the AUR: that is a promise to bump on every release, and is a separate decision.

**Signed apt and dnf repositories** (`packaging/linux-repos/`, `.github/workflows/linux-repos.yml`), so deb and rpm users get `apt upgrade` / `dnf upgrade`. Both hosted on GitHub, no new service.

### Two constraints worth knowing about the repositories

- GitHub Pages rejects files over 100 MB and the deb is ~140 MB, so packages stay on Releases and only the signed metadata is published.
- This repo's Pages site is the landing page, and a second Pages deploy replaces the first.

So apt's metadata is uploaded to the release itself (apt resolves a package's `Filename` against the repository base, so they must share one) with users pointing at `releases/latest/download/`; dnf's metadata goes to a `linux-repo` branch served from raw.githubusercontent.com (it needs a `repodata/` subdirectory, which flat asset names cannot express), with an `xml:base` sending clients back to the release for the rpm.

Neither published package is re-signed — the chain runs through the signed metadata, which carries the package's SHA-256. Re-signing would mean overwriting published assets that the Arch PKGBUILD and the update feed pin.

### Verification

Everything below was run, not reasoned about.

- **deb** (`debian:trixie`): install, reinstall and remove; `ao --version` and `ao --help` work; the `/usr/bin/ao` link appears and disappears at the right times.
- **rpm** (`fedora:latest`): the scriptlet bodies run exactly as rpm runs them (`$1` = 1, 2, 0), including leaving a foreign `/usr/bin/ao` untouched.
- **Arch**: `makepkg` builds it, `pacman -Qlp` lists every expected path, and an installed build reports `0 altered files` under `pacman -Qkk` (setuid bit included). The app starts from `/usr/lib` with no sandbox error, an ACP chat session runs on the packaged Node runtime, the Browser panel drives a live page from the packaged agent-browser, and `pacman -Rns` leaves nothing behind. `~/.ao` is never touched.
- **Menu clash**: against a real pacman install, `ao start` resolved the packaged app, removed a planted stale AppImage entry, wrote none of its own, and left `ao-app://` pointing at the package's entry.
- **apt/dnf repositories**: built from the real v0.12.6 packages with a throwaway key and consumed in containers. Both install through the repository (dnf with metadata and package on different origins, proving `xml:base`). Both refuse a corrupted package, and both refuse metadata re-signed by an untrusted key.
- Frontend suite, `tsc --noEmit`, and `go test ./internal/cli/...` pass.

### Before the repositories can go live

A repo admin has to generate the archive signing key and add `LINUX_SIGNING_KEY` to the `release` environment; the recipe is in `packaging/linux-repos/README.md`. Until then the workflow fails fast with that instruction rather than publishing something unsigned. The one path not yet exercised is a real `apt upgrade` across two published releases, which needs that key and a release cut.

### Found on the way, deliberately not fixed here

- Release builds do not stamp a version: `ao --version` prints `ao version dev` from the deb published as v0.12.6.
- `frontend/forge.config.ts` passes `license: "MIT"` to the rpm maker, but the repo is Apache-2.0, so every published rpm claims the wrong license.

title: bug(review): sibling-named stacked PRs evade discovery and auto-review
body:
## Bug

Auto-review misses stacked child PRs whose source branch is a sibling-style name rather than a slash descendant of the owning session branch. The SCM observer never associates the child with the session, so the auto-review planner cannot see it.

**Source:** live AO bug report, 2026-08-21 | **Reported by:** maintainer | **Analyzed against:** `f739ce18d91745e356d491fef3f3ddbb57b82c63`

**Confidence:** High

**Priority:** medium — auto-review is silently skipped for a common stacked-PR shape; explicitly claiming the PR is a workaround.

## Reproduction

1. Create a worker session on branch `ao/session/parent` with auto-review enabled.
2. Open a root PR from `ao/session/parent` to `main`.
3. Open a stacked child PR from sibling branch `ao/session/parent-child` targeting `ao/session/parent`.
4. Wait for SCM discovery and for the worker to become idle.
5. Observe that only the root PR is persisted and reviewed; the child remains absent until explicitly claimed.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go` attributes discovered PRs using only the source branch. `matchSession` accepts an exact branch or slash descendant (`sessionBranch + "/..."`). It does not use the explicit stack edge carried by the provider: the child PR's target branch equals the owning session/root PR's source branch.

Live durable evidence from session `agent-orchestrator-140`:

- GitHub created stacked child PR #4166 at `2026-08-20T07:41:44Z`, with target branch `ao/agent-orchestrator-140/cloud-integration-design`.
- AO's `change_log` did not record its `pr_created` event until `2026-08-21T14:34:39Z`, more than 30 hours later.
- The automatic review at `2026-08-20T08:03:39Z` therefore saw and queued only root PR #4116.
- Session 140 was durably idle from `2026-08-21T12:21:09Z` through `14:31:27Z`, ruling out a chat-mode gate that can never pass.
- The review engine has no base-branch, CI-state, merge-state, or single-primary-PR filter; its planner and trigger already support multiple eligible PRs.
- No #4166 `review_run` existed, ruling out reviewer occupancy or notification failure (runs are inserted before notify/spawn).

Auto-review decision reasons are also effectively invisible: `Coordinator.Sweep` silently discards gate and planner results and logs only errors, so this failure initially had no daemon-log evidence.

## Fix

- During SCM discovery, fall back to an exact target-branch/session-branch match when source-prefix matching fails. This recognizes the provider-declared stacked child independent of branch naming convention while retaining author and head-repository guards.
- Add regression coverage for sibling-named stacked children.
- Log auto-review decisions when they change so skip/trigger outcomes are diagnosable without per-minute log spam.

## Impact

- Stacked child PRs can go unreviewed indefinitely despite auto-review being enabled.
- The Reviews inspector can misleadingly appear healthy because the untracked PR is absent entirely.
- Operators cannot determine the skipped decision from daemon logs.

## Related

- [#299](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/299) — original session/PR association work.
- [#3259](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3259) — related SCM attribution safety; the proposed fallback preserves authenticated-author and head-repository guards.

title: fix(review): discover sibling-named stacked PRs
body:
Fixes #4236

## Summary

- discover sibling-named stacked child PRs when their target branch exactly matches the owning session branch
- preserve source-branch precedence plus existing authenticated-author and head-repository attribution guards
- log auto-review decisions when their reason changes, including normal skips and successful triggers
- cover stacked-child discovery and deduplicated decision logging

## Root cause

AO only attributed untracked PRs when their source branch equaled the session branch or was a slash descendant. PR #4166 used a sibling-style branch name but targeted the session's root PR branch, so it remained outside AO's PR table for more than 30 hours. During the worker's idle window, the coordinator therefore saw only the already-approved root PR and skipped with `already_approved`.

## Tests

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && env -u <all exported AO_* variables> go test ./...`
- `env -u <all exported AO_* variables> npm run lint`

## Risks / follow-ups

- The target-branch fallback is exact-only and runs after source attribution, limiting it to explicit stack edges.
- The latest decision is now present in daemon logs but not yet in the desktop Reviews inspector; tracked in #4237.

title: fix: add review run CDC
body:
## Summary
- Add review-run CDC events and wire them through session read-model snapshots, HTTP SSE, and the desktop event transport.
- Build a session review snapshot that classifies AO-owned vs external review facts, but keeps only the counts Kanban needs rather than full review/comment payloads.
- Rebuild the sqlite change_log migration using a rename/view compatibility pattern so older schemas keep their existing CDC triggers working.
- Update tests for backend CDC, session review snapshot assembly, and frontend event listeners.

## Call taken in this PR
- Keep the frontend on the existing shared workspace refresh path for review-run CDC events instead of introducing targeted per-session fetches in this change.
- Do not add batching beyond the existing renderer-side debounce.
- Rely on the current `event-transport.ts` 150ms debounce to collapse bursty `review_run_created` / `review_run_updated` events into a single refresh burst.

title: feat(browser): add an act primitive that resolves an instruction and retries stale refs
body:
## Summary
Phase 4 of the browser UX plan (deliberately deferred so it would get its own design pass instead of a rushed bolt-on, inspired by browser-use's perceive-decide-act loop):

- **New `ao browser act "<instruction>"` primitive**: resolves which element to act on and performs the action, instead of the agent manually chaining a `snapshot` call, reading the accessibility tree text itself, then an explicit ref-targeted action call. Matching is fully deterministic (no new LLM call) — parses the compact snapshot's `role "name" [ref=eN]` lines and scores candidates against the instruction's role/name tokens (exact-name match > substring > fuzzy token overlap). If the match is ambiguous or absent, it returns the candidates/snapshot instead of guessing on a mutating action — exactly matching today's manual fallback.
- **One automatic retry on a stale reference**: re-snapshots, re-matches the *original* instruction, retries once. If that also fails, rethrows as-is rather than looping — mirrors `ensureNativeActiveTab`'s existing "retry once, then surface reality" convention already in `browser-view-host.ts`.
- **v1 covers the `{ref[, text]}`-shaped action family**: `click` (default), `dblclick`, `focus`, `hover`, `fill`, `type`, `check`, `uncheck`. `drag` and `select` are excluded — they need harder matching problems (two independently-resolved targets, or an option's own text within a control) and are left for a follow-up rather than a half-baked heuristic.
- **`--nth <index>`** disambiguates a tie deterministically instead of declining, for cases like "the second Add to Cart button."
- All new logic lives in the Electron main process (`browser-view-host.ts` + new `browser-act-matcher.ts`) next to the existing `snapshot`/`click` cases — the Go service layer stays a clean, business-logic-free passthrough, just adding `act` to its action allowlist and CLI wiring.
- Bundled prerequisite fix: `parseAgentBrowserJSON` used to discard the automation runtime's own error `.code`, collapsing every failure to a generic code — fixed so `STALE_REFERENCE` (among others) is a real, reachable code for the first time, which the retry logic above depends on.
- Skill doc (`browser.md`) updated to steer agents toward `act` first, reframing the manual `snapshot`→`click` flow as the fallback for `ambiguous`/`no-match` outcomes or actions `act` doesn't cover yet.

**Out of scope**: the same phase 4 plan's other item ("element-selection UX beyond click-on-page," a *human*-facing feature) is already covered by an open PR building on the annotation multiselect branch — untouched here, since this PR only touches the agent-facing accessibility-tree/ref-based automation path, which is architecturally separate from human annotation.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` — new `browser-act-matcher.test.ts` (12 tests: parsing, exact/fuzzy matching, ambiguous ties, no-match, `--nth` tie-break) and new `browser:act` tests in `browser-view-host.test.ts` (8 tests: happy path, retry-succeeds, retry-exhausted-rethrows, ambiguous, no-match, `--nth` end-to-end, argument validation) — all passing, plus the full existing suite (103/105, 2 pre-existing skips)
- [x] `go build ./...` clean; `go test` passing on `internal/service/browser`, `internal/httpd/controllers`, `internal/cli`, `internal/telemetrymeta` (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `internal/httpd/controllers` — `TestProjectsAPI_Clone` — confirmed to fail identically on unmodified `main` in this sandbox, unrelated to this change)
- [ ] Manual verification in the real desktop app — the real `agent-browser` binary's actual compact-snapshot text format was inferred from this repo's own test fixtures (which are themselves slightly inconsistent about quoting), not observed live, since a live CDP-connected target wasn't available in this environment. Recommend a manual pass before merge: open a real page, run `ao browser act "..."` against it, and separately confirm the stale-ref retry path by mutating the DOM between the internal snapshot and action.

title: feat(board): derive a Kanban column & display status per session
body:
## Summary
- Adds a daemon-derived `kanbanColumn` (`building | validating | needs_review | ready | archive`) to the session read model. It says where a session sits in its delivery lifecycle and which loop is turning it, derived at read time from durable facts alongside the existing status, and never persisted.
- The board groups by that column instead of re-deriving a lane from display status, and its lanes now carry their own labels and colours: **Building · Validating · In review · Ready**, left to right, with `archive` rendering in the existing archive sheet.
- Status pills and card content are untouched, per the issue's scope.

Rebased onto `main` after #4239 merged.

## Derivation

`contract.DeriveKanbanColumn` is a pure reducer sitting next to — not inside — `DeriveStatus`:

```
terminated                                     -> archive
no PR                                          -> building
draft                                          -> validating
merged / closed                                -> ready
human-approved, or mergeable                   -> ready
AO is turning the review-feedback loop         -> validating
auto review on and this head is unreviewed     -> validating
otherwise                                      -> needs_review
```

With several PRs, live ones win over merged/closed, then the most actionable placement wins (ready > needs review > validating > building), breaking ties on the newest PR and finally on URL so the board never flickers.

### The two middle lanes are one loop

`validating` and `needs_review` are the same review-feedback loop, split by whose turn it is. AO is turning it when a review pass is running against the current head, when it is addressing review feedback (`autoInjectReview`), or when it is fixing failing CI (`autoInjectCI`). `needs_review` is the **fallthrough**: no AO loop claimed the PR, so the next turn is a person's — giving the review, answering feedback already on it, or deciding what to do about a failing check.

That is why flipping an inject flag moves a card between the two lanes with nothing on the PR changing, and why "In review" describes the whole lane rather than only PRs awaiting a first review.

## Ownership signals

Two rules from the issue shaped the data model:

- **Review-run currency is enforced in SQL.** `ListCurrentHeadReviewRunsBySession` joins `review_run` to `pr` on `target_sha = pr.head_sha`, so a pass recorded for an earlier commit never reaches the reducer. A new head SHA starts a new cycle.
- **AO's own provider reviews are excluded from the human verdicts.** `ListPRFactsBySession` gained `external_approved` / `external_changes_requested`, computed from each human reviewer's *latest* decisive review, minus bots and minus any review id AO recorded on a run. The aggregate `review_decision` mixes both sources, so Ready requires the provider decision **and** a surviving non-AO approval.

Both ride the existing per-session reads in the session-list path; the review-run query is skipped for terminated sessions and sessions with no PR.

## Board changes

The board previously borrowed the attention-zone vocabulary for its lanes, so a column derived as `building` rendered under a header reading "Working". Columns now own their label and palette (new `column.*` keys in all eight locales), and `data-column` plus the lane aria label expose the column name.

The **idle-vs-working and ready-vs-merged split lanes are gone**. They sub-grouped a column by display status and replaced the column's own header, which is what kept "Working" and "Ready to merge" on screen. Each lane is now one flat list ordered newest first — the order the merge lane already used. Their labels and i18n keys are retired with them.

`attentionZone` itself stays: the command palette and the tray rank sessions by status urgency, which is a different question from delivery placement.

Two behaviour notes:

- A worker with **no PR** stays in Building whatever its runtime status — an exited agent no longer jumps to "Needs you" on the board. Its card still carries the Exited badge. That follows directly from the issue's `no PR exists? -> Building` rule.
- Cards in every lane are now ordered newest first. Previously only the merge lane sorted.

## Display status: what changed, and what did not

The display `SessionStatus` is **unchanged**: `backend/pkg/contract/status.go` and `internal/service/session/status.go` are not in this diff, the enum keeps all 15 values, `deriveStatus` and `DeriveSCMStatus` are untouched, and the 15 `status.*` i18n keys are byte-identical. Card pills render exactly as before.

What changed is what the board *does* with status:

- **Status no longer places a card.** Lane placement comes from `kanbanColumn`; `attentionZone(session.status)` is gone from the grid. That is the point of the PR.
- **The board's status sub-grouping is gone.** The idle-vs-working and ready-vs-merged split lanes sorted a column's cards by display status and put those names in the column header. With them removed, the board no longer surfaces those distinctions — the card's own pill is now the only place idle vs working, or ready vs merged, appears. This retires 13 `shell.*` label keys per locale (`countLabel.*`, `idleSessions`, `workingSessions`, `mergedSessions`, `readyToMergeSessions`, `idleWorkingSessions`, `readyMergedSessions`, `laneSummaryAria`, `countSessionsAria_*`).
- **`zone.*` keys stay.** All five are still used — the tray and the command palette rank sessions by status urgency, which is a different question from delivery placement, and `attentionZone` still answers it for them.

### Lane and pill can now disagree, by design

Previously a card's lane was a function of its status, so the two always agreed. They are now independent readings, and the seeded scenarios include cases where they differ on purpose:

| Card shows | Sits in | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Mergeable` | In review | Provider decision is `approved`, but the only approval is AO's own, so no person has signed off. |
| `Exited` | Building | The agent exited before opening a PR; the delivery lifecycle has not started. |
| `Merged` | Ready | Terminal PR, live session — Ready holds merged work until the session itself is terminated. |

The pill answers "what is this session's state right now"; the lane answers "where is this work, and which loop is turning it". Keeping both is deliberate — the issue scoped pills and card content as out of bounds, and nothing here narrows them.

## Review fixes in this PR

- **Superseded review verdicts.** `external_changes_requested` originally tested raw existence, so a reviewer who requested changes and later approved left both rows behind and the stale request pinned the session to Validating. The aggregate decision does not rescue this — it reads `approved` only once every required approval has landed, so a PR short of its review count stayed stuck. Both flags now come from a CTE holding each human reviewer's most recent decisive review; AO's own reviews are excluded from the superseding side too, since AO posts under an account indistinguishable from a person by author name.
- **Older-daemon fallback.** `toKanbanColumn` dropped every session without a `kanbanColumn` into Building, which moved ready and in-review cards leftward during a mixed-version upgrade — reading as work regressing rather than as a client that cannot see the field. Such a daemon still sends `status`, and mapping it through `attentionZone` reproduces exactly the lane the board used before the column existed, so the fallback preserves placement. It covers an unrecognized column too.
- **`sqlc` truncation.** An em dash in a new SQL comment tripped the parser bug already documented in `queries/sessions.sql` and `changelog.sql`: the generated SQL was silently truncated by the extra byte count, cutting `ORDER BY pr.updated_at DESC` to `DE`. It compiled and failed at runtime. The query body is ASCII-only now, with a note recording why.

## Tests

`go test ./pkg/contract ./internal/service/session ./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/domain`, `golangci-lint run` (0 issues), `gofmt` clean, `npm run typecheck`, 1920 renderer tests, 80 product-ui tests.

New coverage:
- Reducer table tests for every rule plus multi-PR selection and tie-breaking.
- Real-SQLite tests for stale-SHA filtering, the AO/external split, both supersede directions, two disagreeing reviewers, and a later AO review not dismissing a human verdict.
- Service tests for the derived column; an API test asserting `kanbanColumn` on the wire.
- Board tests that lanes group by column (not status), render in delivery order, and that an older daemon's sessions keep their status-implied lanes.

### Manual pass

Sixteen worker sessions, one per derivation rule, seeded as durable facts into a scratch database and read back through the real daemon — so the SQL, the reducer, and the board were exercised end to end rather than against fixtures. All 16 derived their expected column.

Three of them discriminate against specific wrong implementations, checked at the SQL layer too:

| Scenario | Provider decision | Review rows | `external_approved` | `external_changes_requested` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| only AO approved | `approved` | 1 | **0** | 0 |
| changes requested, then approved | `review_required` | 2 | **1** | **0** |

The first is the AO/external split: the provider says `approved`, but the only approval is AO's own. The second is the supersede fix — before it, that last cell read `1`.

## Not in this PR

`ExternalCommented` — a human COMMENTED review — is not persisted anywhere today: the GitHub query selects only `APPROVED`/`CHANGES_REQUESTED`, `pr_reviews.state` is CHECK-constrained to those, and `pr_comment` carries no review id to attribute comments to AO vs a person. Plumbing it needs a provider change, a migration, and a `ReviewDecision` enum widening, so it is filed as #4250.

## Issue
- Closes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4178

title: Persist COMMENTED provider reviews so Kanban can read an external-commented signal
body:
Follow-up to #4178 / #4249.

## Problem

The Kanban reducer's `KanbanExternalReviewFacts` carries `Approved` and `ChangesRequested` — the human review verdicts AO did not author — but has no equivalent for a reviewer who left a COMMENTED review. A human commenting on a PR is an ownership signal: the PR is not purely AO-driven, even when nobody has approved or requested changes.

It was left out of #4249 because the signal is not persisted today:

- `backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go` selects `reviews(last:N, states:[APPROVED,CHANGES_REQUESTED])`, so COMMENTED reviews never arrive.
- `pr_reviews.state` is CHECK-constrained to `('none','approved','changes_requested','review_required')` (migration 0021), so they could not be stored if they did.
- `pr_comment` rows carry no review id, so unresolved comments cannot be attributed to AO vs a human the way `review_run.github_review_id` attributes reviews.

## Work

1. Widen the GitHub GraphQL review selection to include `COMMENTED`.
2. Add a migration allowing `commented` in `pr_reviews.state`.
3. Decide whether `ReviewDecision` gains a `commented` value — it is on the public API enum for PR summaries, so this is a contract change.
4. Add `ExternalCommented` to `domain.PRFacts`, sourced like the other two (non-bot, minus any review id recorded on a review run), and feed it into `KanbanExternalReviewFacts`.
5. Decide how it should affect placement — most likely as another signal that AO does not own the next step.

title: fix(files): correctness follow-ups for the markdown Preview tab
body:
Follow-ups for #4251, branched off `feat/github-markdown-render`. Merging this into that branch folds the commits into the PR.

Seven correctness fixes, three cleanups, the first tests for the new code, and a rename plus redesign of the tab pair. One commit per item, each with its reasoning, so anything you disagree with can be dropped on its own.

## Bugs

**Relative images never reloaded after an edit.** `buildWorkspaceBlobUrl` mirrors `ImageDiffView`'s blob route but not its `v=` parameter, and that parameter is why the route works — it serves `no-store`, so as `ImageDiffView`'s own comment puts it, without a changing URL the element never refetches at all. An image an agent rewrote kept rendering from cache indefinitely. Threads the detail's load timestamp through `MarkdownFileContext`.

**A failed image rendered as a broken-image box.** The CSP allows `img-src` from `'self'`, `data:` and the loopback daemon only, so an `https://` image — a shields.io badge, a hosted screenshot, the two most common images in a real README — cannot load here at all. Falls back to alt text, the way `ImageDiffView` already handles its own failures.

**Truncated files rendered as though complete.** The daemon caps content at `maxWorkspaceFileBytes` and reports `contentTruncated`; the diff body respects it, the rendered view ignored it. The rendering is worse than the omission: a cut landing inside a fence leaves it unclosed, swallowing everything after it into one code block, with no signal that anything is missing. Adds the same warning strip behind a new `files.contentTruncated` string, translated for all eight locales.

**Heading links could scroll to the wrong file.** `rehype-slug` guarantees ids unique per rendered file, not per document, and the Files tab expands many cards at once — two open READMEs with `## Overview` put two `id="overview"` in one DOM, and `document.getElementById` answers with whichever is first. Resolves within the file's own container instead. Prefixing the slugs would also have worked but would have broken every hand-written `[link](#overview)`, which is the more common case.

**Clicking a heading overwrote the clipboard.** Silently, with no affordance saying so, and with a bare `#some-heading` that names no file and cannot be pasted anywhere and followed. Scroll only; a deliberate copy-link control can come later.

**The selection guard leaked on tab switch.** `DiffView` reports selection state up so a background refetch cannot re-render rows out from under a live selection, and that effect had no cleanup. Harmless until this PR, since the diff only unmounted with the card. Now: switch tabs with a selection active and `selectionOrMenuActive` stays `true` forever, the detail query stays disabled, and the rendered view sits on a snapshot that never refreshes while the agent keeps writing — with nothing left mounted that could clear it.

**Tab switching lost scroll position.** Not because a scroll position is discarded — an expanded file has no scroll box, the Files panel is one shared scroller. Swapping a 4,000-line diff for its rendered form shortens the column by thousands of pixels, and the browser clamps `scrollTop` to the new maximum; switching back restores the height but not the clamped-away offset.

Worth recording since it is the obvious thing to reach for: **`forceMount` does not fix this.** A hidden `TabsContent` is `display: none`, contributes zero height, and clamps identically — no benefit, and a large diff mounted for as long as the card is open. Instead a small `useViewModeScrollAnchor` records the card's offset from the scroll root when a mode is left and restores it when that mode returns, in a layout effect plus one `requestAnimationFrame`, since virtualized rows settle to their real heights a frame after mounting. No change to `useSharedScrollRowVirtualizer`. (The anchor originally rode the tab strip; the last commit moves that strip into the title row, so it rides the card's own top edge instead — see below.)

## Cleanups

- `textOf` / `fenceOf` / the `language-*` pattern arrived as byte-for-byte copies of `ChatMarkdown`'s. Both feed the same highlighter, so language sniffing had two places to drift. One copy in `lib/markdown-fence.ts`.
- `code-theme.css` had every selector written twice, once per scope. `:is(.chat-code, .markdown-code)` states it once — identical matching, ~60 fewer lines. Also corrects `HighlightedCode`'s comment, which still named `.chat-code` as the only scope.
- Notes in `MarkdownFileView` that the `prefers-color-scheme` argument holds under Electron but not `npm run dev:web`.

## Tests

`markdown-image-resolver` is pure and does the fiddliest work in the feature; it arrived untested. Eleven cases: resolution against the file's directory, a file at the workspace root, `..` walking up, `..` clamping at the root rather than escaping, query/fragment stripping, absolute passthrough, and the version reaching the URL.

The tab pair itself had no coverage at all. Two cases now: the strip renders in the title row as a sibling of the trigger rather than a descendant, and survives the panel swap — which is the `asChild` ref composition actually working at runtime — and it stays off files that cannot render as markdown.

## Rename and redesign

`Source diff` / `Rendered` → **Diff** / **Preview**, strings renamed to `files.diff` / `files.preview` and retranslated for all eight locales.

The control then moved out of the body and into the file's own title row. It had a band to itself under the title, and that band held nothing else — a right-aligned control with the whole width of the card empty to its left. It now sits beside the `+N`/`-N` badges, on the line that already names the file it acts on, and the card is a row shorter.

`AccordionTrigger` already had a `trailing` slot for exactly this: rendered inside the header row but as a sibling of the trigger `<button>`, which is what makes it legal — a `<button>` inside a `<button>` is invalid, and a nested tab would collapse the file on click. The Tabs root moves up to enclose the title row as well as the body it switches; it and `AccordionItem` both take `asChild`, so they compose onto the same single `<li>`: no wrapper element, no change in DOM depth. The strip renders only while the file is expanded.

**This costs the anchoring premise of the scroll-position commit above.** That commit chose the tab strip deliberately, because it sat at the top of the swapped body and was an element the component owned outright, with no ref composition through `asChild` in the way. The strip no longer moves with the body, so the anchor rides the card's own top edge, through a ref composed across both `asChild` roots. Since that is precisely what the earlier commit avoided, it is now covered by tests rather than resting on a typecheck.

Appearance follows the inspector rail's own tab buttons (`session-inspector__tab-button`), which is the tab language of the pane this control lives in: `text-passive` labels, `--color-interactive-*` fills one step apart on the same neutral (foreground at 4% for the track, 7% for the selected tab), and a hairline border — GitHub's segmented-control signature, and what separates this shape from a shadcn pill group. Stock shadcn's palette is dropped, and worth flagging as an actual defect rather than taste: its dark-theme active fill is `bg-input/30`, white at 1.2% over the `bg-muted` track, which is not a visible selection at this size.

Sizing is a 20px track over 16px pills — deliberately under the 20px a standalone control would get. It rides in a 36px row it does not own, beside a 28px button, and reading as the smaller thing there is the point; the labels are wide enough to keep the targets easy despite the height. Narrowing keys off the `inspector` container the shell already declares, at the 350px/300px steps it already breaks at, so the toggle changes on the same drag positions as everything else in the pane. In the centre pane there is no `inspector` container to match, so it keeps full size.

Still a judgement call, and still droppable as its own commit if you disagree.

## Not addressed

- **`github-markdown-css` vs the design system.** `CLAUDE.md` asks for explicit approval before deviating. Your reasoning is sound and I have not touched it — flagging it as the repo owner's call. Side effect worth knowing: AO's nine theme styles (dracula, nord, gruvbox…) do not reach the Preview tab, which stays GitHub-coloured.
- **Lockfile churn.** The `motion` entries under `packages/product-ui` are unrelated to this feature, but they correct a stale lock on `main` (`packages/product-ui/package.json` already lists it there). Harmless — worth a line in the PR body so a reviewer does not stop on it.

## Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Full renderer suite as of the tests commit: **2689 passed, 1 skipped, 204 files** — including your 35 `SessionFilesView` tests unmodified. Each commit typechecks on its own.

For the title-row commit on top I re-ran typecheck and `SessionFilesView` only (**37 passed**, the 35 plus the two new ones), not the full suite.

Manual verification in the Electron app is still worth doing for the scroll anchor and the image reload, which are the two that depend on real layout.

## Demo

Screen recording of the change in the desktop app: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e5T3MbyQTVrNtLqfo2ZLPWgldhwUpDQO/view?usp=sharing

title: feat(telemetry): instrument the review funnel end to end
body:
## Why

Reviews are a headline feature with almost no measurement behind them. Four `ao.review.*` events existed, and all of them sat on the manual trigger path, so an **automatic** review was invisible at trigger time: `TriggerAuto` called the engine directly and emitted nothing, which made auto-review indistinguishable from manual review in every funnel even though the two answer different product questions.

Per review feedback this PR now ships the **P0 event set only**. Everything else is listed as P1 at the bottom, with what each deferred event would have answered.

## P0 events in this PR

### Daemon

| Event | Change |
|---|---|
| `ao.review.triggered` | adds `trigger` (auto or manual). `Trigger` and `TriggerAuto` now share one instrumented path, so an automatic pass is never invisible |
| `ao.review.trigger_failed` | adds `trigger`, so a failure is attributable to the automatic or the manual path |
| `ao.review.submitted` | adds `trigger` (read from the run), `body_bytes` (review depth, never the text) and `auto_inject` (whether the session policy will let the result reach the worker) |

Payload keys are allowlisted in `remotePayloadAllowlist`; without an entry an event exports with no properties at all rather than failing loudly.

### Renderer

| Event | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ao.renderer.review_settings_changed` | project-level `auto_review` and `reviewer_harness`, plus `harness_is_default` and per-field changed flags. Emitted only when a review control actually changed, so it counts review decisions rather than every unrelated save. **This is the event that tells us whether the harness dropdown is a decision anybody makes or a checkpoint that could become a default** |
| `ao.renderer.review_auto_review_toggled` | the session-scoped auto-review switch, which duplicates the project setting. Whether anyone reaches for it decides if it stays a separate control |
| `ao.renderer.review_triggered` | manual runs, with the offered `action`, whether a per-session reviewer override was in play, and `source` (`inspector` or `command_palette`). Manual volume against auto volume is the adoption signal, and the two on-ramps stay separable |

`reviewRunActionKind` was extracted from `reviewSessionRunAction` so `review_triggered.action` reports a stable enum rather than the translated label the user happened to see. The command palette is a manual on-ramp in its own right and POSTs to the trigger endpoint directly, so it emits the same event and carries that enum on its action.

Both renderer emit sites fire before the request. That is deliberate: they count INTENT, and the daemon's `ao.review.*` events are the ground truth for what actually ran. A toggle whose save then fails still counts as the user reaching for the switch.

## One behaviour change that is not an event

While a review is running, the once-a-minute auto-review sweep calls `TriggerAuto` again, the engine reports success with nothing created, and the old code emitted another `ao.review.triggered` every time. A six-minute review produced **seven "triggers" for one real pass**, which would have inflated the headline count and spent the 200/day per-name rate limit that real triggers need.

An automatic pass that did no work (a policy race, or a reuse) now reports **nothing at all**. A manual reuse stays a trigger, because the user pressed the button and that is a real action. This was found by running the real coordinator against a real open PR, and reverting it would corrupt the very count P0 exists to measure.

## User flow, and where each P0 event fires

```
Project settings: toggle auto-review / pick a reviewer, save
  -> ao.renderer.review_settings_changed        (only if a review control changed)

Session inspector: flip the session auto-review switch
  -> ao.renderer.review_auto_review_toggled

Path A, manual: press Run / Re-review
  -> ao.renderer.review_triggered               (intent)
Path B, automatic: the coordinator sweeps an idle worker every minute
  -> (silent when there is nothing to do)

Either path reaches the engine
  -> ao.review.triggered { trigger: manual | auto }
  -> ao.review.trigger_failed { error_kind, trigger }

Reviewer agent works, then submits
  -> ao.review.submitted { verdict, trigger, duration_ms, body_bytes, auto_inject }
```

## Privacy

Counts, durations, enums and booleans only. No review body, PR URL, commit SHA, branch, PR title, repo or project name reaches any payload: review prose is reviewer commentary on someone's source, and the URL and SHA identify the repository. Project ids are hashed on the renderer side exactly as the existing settings events do, and reviewer harness ids are validated against AO's own reviewer registry so a caller mistake cannot forward free text.

Both paths keep their existing cost controls: per-event-name rate limits, the `DisabledEvents` kill switch, and an install-scoped `distinct_id`.

## Testing

Verified end to end, not just at the emit site. The payload allowlist that decides what actually reaches PostHog lives in the adapter, keyed by event name, with nothing tying it to the emit site at compile time.

- A **wire test** drives the real emit sites through the real export chain (denylist, aggregation, rate limit, PostHog) into a fake transport, then asserts the event names and properties as they leave the process. Confirmed it catches the real failure: removing one allowlist key makes it fail with `triggered.trigger = <nil>`.
- That test also scans the raw outgoing JSON for the review body, repo name, commit and review id, and fails if any appears under any key.
- Unit tests cover the auto against manual trigger split, the failure path, the submitted payload shape, a manual reuse staying counted, and six no-op automatic sweeps emitting nothing.
- Allowlist drift tests assert the review funnel's exact key sets and reject identifying keys across every `ao.review.*` entry.
- Renderer sanitizer tests cover each of the three events, including that an unknown harness or action is dropped rather than forwarded.

Backend: touched packages pass with `-count=1`, `golangci-lint` reports 0 issues. Frontend: 131 renderer test files, 1927 tests passing across three consecutive runs, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Pre-existing failures in this worktree, confirmed identical on a clean tree and unrelated to these changes: `adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver` (installed-provider conformance), `internal/cli` (spawn tests needing a live daemon), and the `landing` plus `main` frontend suites (uninstalled dependencies).

## Verified against a live daemon

The earlier full-funnel build was run on a real daemon from this branch, on an isolated data dir with a copy of live app state and remote export off, so nothing left the machine and the running app was untouched. Driving the real auto-review coordinator against a real open PR produced, for the events P0 keeps:

```
ao.review.triggered   {"created_runs":1,"harness":"claude-code","reused":false,"trigger":"auto"}
ao.review.submitted   {"trigger":"auto","verdict":"changes_requested","duration_ms":520165,
                       "body_bytes":103,"auto_inject":true,"posted_to_provider":false,
                       "harness":"claude-code"}
```

The `trigger: auto` on that first event is the fix this PR exists for: before it, that pass emitted nothing. That run is also what surfaced the per-sweep inflation described above.

## One caveat for whoever builds the dashboards

Manual and automatic passes share the single `ao.review.triggered` name, and therefore its 200/day per-name cap on the billed sink, split only by the `trigger` property. On a very high-volume install the billed count can truncate while local SQLite still keeps every occurrence, so exact auto-against-manual counts for a power user should be read from local rather than PostHog. Folding `trigger` into the aggregation tier would collapse the very split this PR adds, so the cap stands.

## P1, deferred by review decision

Removed from this PR. Listed with what each one answered, so picking them up later is a decision about priority and not a rediscovery.

| Deferred event | What goes unmeasured |
|---|---|
| `ao.review.feedback_delivered` | **Whether changes-requested feedback actually reached the worker agent.** A sent nudge, a suppressed one and an errored one look identical. The review loop (review, worker fixes, merge) is the feature's value, and P0 only observes its first half |
| `ao.review.pr_closed` | **Trust.** Whether a PR was merged over a standing changes-requested verdict, how many rounds it took, and reviewed against unreviewed time-to-merge. The override-merge flag was the only perception signal in the catalog, and the control-group data for a future default-on decision |
| `ao.review.feedback_withheld` | Why a completed changes-requested review reached nobody (`auto_inject_off`, `stale_head`, `already_delivered`). The quietest failure mode: a red verdict the worker never hears about |
| `ao.review.auto_skipped` | Why an enabled auto-review never produces reviews (draft PR, already approved, closed, missing head). "I turned it on and nothing happened" for the automatic flow |
| `ao.review.trigger_skipped` | How often automatic passes are skipped or reused. Denominator hygiene; the behaviour it guarded survives as silence |
| `ao.renderer.review_auto_inject_toggled` | Whether anyone touches the delivery switch, which is case data for merging the three review toggles |
| `ao.renderer.review_reviewer_overridden` | Whether anyone sets the per-session reviewer dropdown. Partly mitigated: `review_triggered.has_override` still shows overrides at run time |
| `ao.renderer.review_tab_opened` | Whether humans read findings or only trust the verdict |
| `ao.renderer.review_stopped` | Mid-run dissatisfaction, and the cancel against kill split that would justify merging two stop buttons |
| `ao.renderer.review_comment_sent_to_worker` | Humans hand-relaying comments, a cheap canary for automatic delivery failing |

Two smaller follow-ups, also out of scope here:

- `ao.review.rereview_requested` and `ao.review.comment_resolved` have shipped **payload-stripped** since before this PR, because their names are absent from the allowlist. The two-line fix is a bug fix rather than a new metric, so it is not in this PR either; say the word and it goes in.
- These are **change** events, not state events. A project that already had auto-review on will never emit a toggle event, so "what share of projects have auto-review on today" needs a small daily gauge (counts only, no identifiers) rather than these.

title: feat(chat): retry a failed turn without retyping the prompt
body:
## Summary

Closes #4215.

Adds a **Retry** action to eligible failed human turns so a transient failure can be retried without retyping the original prompt. The retry is a new turn; the failed source stays unchanged and visible.

## What changed

### Daemon and storage

- Adds `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/conversation/turns/{turnId}/retry`.
- Loads text and structured prompt content from durable AO rows, never from a caller-supplied retry payload.
- Applies the current next-turn model, reasoning, and approval settings.
- Persists an explicit `retry_of_turn_id` relation on the new turn in the same transaction as its message. A unique partial index makes one retry attempt per source durable and idempotent; retrying a failed retry creates the next link in the chain.
- Uses the persisted relation for replay and UI correlation, so caller-controlled client message IDs cannot impersonate or consume a retry.
- Refuses unsafe or invalid cases with typed errors: busy/handoff, stale branch, non-human or non-failed source, unconfirmed provider delivery, malformed durable content, and content unsupported by the current provider.
- Adds explicit native resource-link capability negotiation. ACP preserves resource links; a provider that cannot preserve them receives a clear refusal instead of silently dropping the attachment.
- Keeps retry consumption visible even when the retry child is rolled back or moves outside the active branch by deriving `hasRetryAttempt` from all durable retry relations.
- Includes `recovered` in replay response contracts and regenerates sqlc, OpenAPI, and frontend API types.

### Renderer

- Shows Retry only on eligible failed human turns.
- Disables it while work is running or a retry request is pending.
- Displays retry refusals beside the affected turn.
- Hides consumed retry actions using daemon-owned `retryOfTurnId` / `hasRetryAttempt` facts, including inactive-branch and rolled-back retry attempts.

## Tests

Coverage includes exact prompt/attachment replay, current settings, busy/non-human/stale/uncertain/unsupported refusals, double-click and replay idempotency, caller-ID collision, recovered replay, retry chains, resource-link provider switching, rollback, inactive-branch consumption, HTTP contracts, wire-to-renderer mapping, renderer visible/hidden/disabled/pending/error states, and Playwright behavior.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — full backend Go suite and golangci-lint: pass, 0 issues.
- Frontend typecheck and e2e typecheck: pass.
- Retry renderer + wire-mapping suites: 23 tests pass.
- Retry Playwright suite: 2 tests pass.
- Final Standards review: no findings.
- Final Spec review against #4215: no findings.
