title: bug(cursor): TUI startup MCP approval can consume AO follow-ups before hooks start
body:
## Bug

A Phoenix project configured with worker agent `cursor` and model `composer-2.5-fast` exposed two related spawn failures:

1. A normal prompted spawn failed with `chat mode unsupported for harness: cursor has no chat driver (SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED)` and created no session.
2. Explicit `--mode tui` created `phoenix-10`, but Cursor exited before accepting a follow-up. A disposable reproduction showed the underlying startup race: Cursor stops at its interactive MCP approval screen, while `ao send` returns success and the follow-up is consumed by that screen instead of reaching the agent.

**Source:** AO conversation, session `phoenix-1`, 2026-08-23  
**Reported by:** current AO user  
**Analyzed against:** `6cba6344c7081f2984927ca5f15140f99115c5c0` (`origin/main`)  
**AO CLI version:** `dev`  
**Desktop build:** `0.12.7-nightly.202608231948`  
**Priority:** medium / P2 — spawn is degraded, but manual TUI recovery exists  
**Confidence:** High for the reproduced startup-input loss; Medium for the exact `phoenix-10` exit because the Cursor process had already exited and produced no worker log

## Environment

- macOS Darwin 25.6.0 arm64
- zsh
- bundled binary only: `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`
- healthy daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001`
- Cursor Agent `2026.08.11-e8db854`, authenticated
- Cursor model `composer-2.5-fast`
- tmux 3.7c
- no Go binary in `PATH`

## Reproduction

### Original omitted-mode failure

```sh
AO_BIN="/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao"
"$AO_BIN" status --json # port 3001
"$AO_BIN" spawn \
  --project phoenix \
  --name cursor-chat-repro \
  --prompt "Reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_REPRO_OK and wait for follow-up."
```

Observed:

```text
spawn: chat mode unsupported for harness: cursor has no chat driver (SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED)
```

Exit status was 1 and no session row was created.

### Reproduced TUI startup-input loss

```sh
"$AO_BIN" spawn \
  --project phoenix \
  --name cursor-tui-repro \
  --mode tui \
  --prompt "Reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_TUI_REPRO_OK and wait for follow-up."
```

1. Cursor displays `MCP Server Approval Required` for the project MCP server before it consumes the prompt.
2. While that screen is visible, run:

```sh
"$AO_BIN" send \
  --session phoenix-13 \
  --message "Follow-up: reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_CHAT_FOLLOWUP_OK."
```

3. `ao send` exits 0, but the message is not shown or processed by Cursor.
4. After the MCP gate clears, a second `ao send` is delivered and Cursor replies normally.

For `phoenix-10`, durable state changed from idle to exited about three seconds after spawn. Its tmux shell remained alive, `cursor-agent` was gone, no Cursor native session id was recorded, and no Cursor `worker.log` was created.

## Root Cause

The CLI correctly omits `mode` when `--mode` is not passed (`backend/internal/cli/spawn.go`). The originally running packaged daemon resolved the saved Chat default but had no Cursor Chat driver, producing `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`.

Current `origin/main` already contains both protections:

- inherited Chat preflight failures fall back to TUI in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:771`
- Cursor is registered through `cursor-agent acp` in `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/registry.go:62`

After the daemon restarted, the same omitted-mode reproduction no longer errored and created a TUI session, confirming the original Chat failure was tied to the running packaged build rather than current source.

The remaining TUI race is in current source:

- Cursor TUI launches as `cursor-agent --model composer-2.5-fast -- <prompt>` and does not bypass MCP approval (`backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go:386`).
- AO Cursor hooks begin at `sessionStart` and tool/prompt events (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/hooks.go:57`), so the pre-session MCP dialog emits no blocked activity signal.
- The session therefore remains durably idle. `sessionguard.Deliver` refuses only known blocked decisions, so it permits the write (`backend/internal/sessionguard/guard.go:142`).
- tmux pastes the text and always presses Enter (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:575`). Cursor consumes that input at the approval screen.
- `ao send` has no provider acknowledgement for Cursor and returns success once tmux accepts the keystrokes (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:2887`).

## Suggested Fix

- Add a provider-neutral startup-ready gate for TUI sessions, satisfied by the first native session-start/prompt-ready signal.
- Queue or reject follow-ups with a typed not-ready error until that gate is satisfied.
- Do not auto-approve MCP servers under the default permission policy.
- Add a Cursor regression test where a pre-session dialog is present and verify that no follow-up is reported delivered until Cursor is ready.

## Workaround

- Install/restart into a build containing the merged Cursor ACP driver, then use Chat mode.
- On older builds, use `--mode tui`, answer the Cursor MCP approval screen manually, and resend the follow-up only after the Cursor prompt is visible.

## Verification and PR status

No fix PR was attempted. The machine has no Go toolchain, and repository policy requires `go build ./...` plus `go test ./...` before pushing a backend fix. No system software was installed and no unverified patch was pushed.

Dependency check: Cursor Agent `2026.08.11-e8db854` exposes the hidden `cursor-agent acp` command and matches the minimum version used by the merged Cursor Chat driver. The repository uses `github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk v0.13.5`, which is also the latest published SDK release.

## Related

- [#3712](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3712) — earlier unsupported-Chat Cursor spawn report in the desktop composer
- [PR #3715](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3715) — frontend routing of unsupported Chat agents to TUI
- [PR #4233](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4233) — inherited Chat default falls back to TUI
- [PR #4201](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4201) — merged Cursor ACP Chat driver tested against Cursor `2026.08.11-e8db854`
- [#3634](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3634) — related `ao send` success-versus-delivery semantics

title: fix(httpd): map transient DB-busy/deadline errors to 503, not opaque 500 (#4325)
body:
Fixes #4325.

## Problem
`envelope.WriteError` maps any non-`apierr` error to `INTERNAL_ERROR`/500. So transient SQLite busy/locked contention and server-side deadlines surface as genuine server faults — inflating the 5xx surface and making the true cause indistinguishable from a real bug.

## Change
- `apierr.KindUnavailable` (503) + `apierr.Unavailable(...)`.
- In `WriteError`, before the 500 fallback, detect transient conditions and return a typed **503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`** (retryable):
  - SQLite busy/locked, matched **structurally** via a `Code() int` method (primary code `5`/`6` or extended code low-byte), so `httpd/envelope` takes **no dependency** on the DB driver.
  - server-side `context.DeadlineExceeded`.
  - client `context.Canceled` is **excluded** on purpose (the response never reaches that caller; not retryable).

## Verification
- Real socket: a `database is locked` (Code 5) error returned via the production `WriteError` path yields `HTTP 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` across repeated attempts.
- Unit tests: busy / locked / extended-code / wrapped / deadline / `apierr.Unavailable` -> 503; plain error / non-busy sqlite code (constraint) / `context.Canceled` / `apierr.Internal` -> 500; existing typed kinds (400/404/409/403) unchanged. Run deterministically at `-count=100`.
- Full `internal/httpd/...` suite passes (no spec drift).

## Scope
Pure daemon HTTP classification. No route/DTO changes. Companion to #3963 (the DB contention this reclassifies) and #4323 (the SSE reconnect amplifier); #4180/#4181 (Sentry) give the remaining genuine 500s a grouped stack.

title: fix(storage): recreate tables and columns skipped by burned migration versions
body:
## What

`reconcileSchema` (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go`) only verified **columns** from the manual `schemaRepairs` list, via `pragma_table_info`. A whole missing **table** (or a column outside the list) passed the boot check as healthy: the daemon came up green, and the first query against the missing object 500'd — for `agent_inventory_cache` that is every `ao spawn` (`INTERNAL_ERROR`) while `/readyz` stays ready.

This adds:
1. `tableRepairs` — a table-level counterpart to `schemaRepairs`, checked against `sqlite_master` and recreated when absent (idempotent, same as the column path).
2. Repair entries for the two drift casualties found in the field:
   - `0104` `agent_inventory_cache` (whole table missing)
   - `0106` `pr_comment.review_id` (column missing; `preparePRCommentReviewIDMigration` only repaired the mirror case — column present, ledger entry missing)

## Why

Part of #4335: a schema drift must not survive into a green daemon whose core workflow (`ao spawn`) 500s. This is the reconciliation gap, not the WARN/`/readyz` items the issue also lists — those are separate follow-ups.

## Red → green

`TestMigrateReconcilesMissingInventoryCacheTable` and `TestMigrateReconcilesMissingPRCommentReviewIDColumn` simulate the drift by burning the version (`INSERT INTO goose_db_version`) and requiring `migrate()` to leave the object present. title: Orchestrators have no way to learn that a delegated worker finished its turn
body:
Title: Orchestrators have no way to learn that a delegated worker finished its turn

## Use case

Operator delegates a task from the project orchestrator (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`). The spawned worker completes its work — commits sitting on its `ao/<project>/<session>/root` branch — and then nothing happens until a human notices. In our session the orchestrator itself said it had to poll (`ao session get`) to discover its delegate was done. For an orchestration product, the orchestrator being the last to know is the expensive case: the whole point of delegation is that the planner picks the thread back up when the worker stops.

What exists today:

- `turn_complete` notifications reach the **human's** NotificationCenter (#4267). They do not reach any session.
- `DelegateTaskOutcome.OrchestratorID` records which orchestrator spawned the worker — but as far as I can find, **nothing consumes it**. It's bookkeeping metadata.
- W4's orchestrator view lists spawned workers with live state, but only when the human is looking at it.

## Design space

Three shapes this could take, roughly increasing in ambition:

1. **UI-level only.** Surface delegate completion more prominently (badge/ping) on the orchestrator destination view. No daemon semantics change; the orchestrator agent still learns nothing until prompted.
2. **Message injection.** When a delegate goes idle, deliver a system message into the orchestrator session's chat driver (the same path `ao send` uses), e.g. `worker <id> finished: N commits on <branch>`. The orchestrator can then react autonomously — review the diff, ask for a PR, report back. This is what made our workflow feel broken without it: the planner wanted to act on completion but had no event to act on.
3. **Session-addressable notifications.** Generalize the notification model so sessions can be subscribers/route targets. Most flexible, most machinery.

We lean toward **2**: it reuses an existing, proven transport (`ao send` into the chat driver), keeps the notification model untouched, and matches the mental model that the orchestrator is an agent, not just a view. Concerns we'd want the maintainers' read on:

- **Loop safety.** An orchestrator that reacts by delegating again must not create ping-pong; some depth/reentrancy guard seems wise.
- **Terminated/exited delegates.** Should the ping distinguish "finished cleanly" from "process died"? Lifecycle already has both facts.
- **Chat-driver availability.** Orchestrators exist only with a chat driver configured, so transport-2 has no fallback problem — but corrections welcome.

Is there a prior decision here we should know about — e.g. a deliberate choice to keep sessions out of the notification graph? Happy to turn whichever shape you prefer into a spec/PR.

title: fix(renderer): exponential backoff + jitter for workspace SSE reconnect (#4323)
body:
Fixes #4323.

## Problem
`workspace-file-events.ts` retried the SSE stream on a **fixed 5s interval** with no backoff, no ceiling reset, and no cap. A session whose stream keeps failing (e.g. the daemon briefly returns 5xx under DB contention, #3963) reconnected every 5s indefinitely, and many streams reconnected in lockstep — turning a brief hiccup into a sustained reconnect load on the daemon.

## Change (renderer-only, complementary to #4230)
- New dependency-free `sse-backoff.ts` → `computeBackoffDelayMs(failures)`: exponential growth from **5s** to a **60s** ceiling, jitter in `[0.5, 1.0]` of the step (spreads concurrent reconnects), overflow-clamped.
- The stream tracks consecutive failures, backs off per retry, and **resets to a fast first retry on a successful open**.

## Verification
- Ran the actual helper **100×** with invariant checks: monotonic growth to the cap, never exceeds 60s, never below the jitter floor, high-count clamp (no overflow). Sample progression: `4157, 6698, 14280, 39890, 43711, 54303` ms (vs the old flat 5000).
- `sse-backoff.test.ts` (vitest) covers growth, ceiling, jitter band, clamp, and NaN/negative handling.

## Scope / limitation
Native `EventSource` does not expose the HTTP status on error, so "stop reconnecting on 4xx" cannot be done from the client alone — backoff is the client-side mitigation. Daemon-side error classification (transient → 503) is handled separately in #4325. This composes with #4230 (daemon-side SSE replay cap) rather than overlapping it.

title: fix(desktop): defer agent auth probes until selection
body:

## Summary

title: Codex usage disappears after agent switches with session metadata over 64 KiB
body:
## Bug

After an AO worker switches from Claude/`claude-code` to Codex, Codex can process billable turns while **Cost & Usage continues to show only Claude**. The failure is deterministic when the first Codex rollout `session_meta` JSONL record exceeds the usage collector's 65,536-byte discovery limit.

**Source:** live local AO production audit on 2026-08-24  
**Reported by:** AO user report for `reverb-29` / `4218-subscription`  
**Production build:** `d4ae9b318e2a14748661c5b71ad589c2f1153521` (collector file byte-identical to the analyzed checkout)  
**Analyzed against:** `2fa9672c77b3c7ca8a70494d8ea38ab9a2c91906`  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced from persisted switch, native rollout, observation, ledger, API, and UI state and traced to an exact bounded-reader failure.  
**Priority:** P2 — usage accounting is omitted for affected sessions, but runtime work continues and the affected set is bounded/recoverable.

## User-visible impact

For affected sessions:

1. The harness switch completes and AO persists `harness=codex` plus the correct Codex native session ID and rollout path.
2. Codex processes later user turns and emits cumulative `token_count` observations.
3. AO leaves the Codex usage binding in `source_discovery_pending` with no `usage_sources` row.
4. No Codex model-usage ledger events are created.
5. The usage API therefore returns only the pre-switch Claude contribution, and the Summary sidebar faithfully renders Claude only.

The observations were not assigned to the old Claude harness; they never crossed the Codex source-discovery boundary.

## Reproduction

1. Start an AO worker using Claude with enough history to produce a large switch continuation.
2. Switch it to Codex.
3. Let Codex process at least one turn and emit a `token_count` rollout record.
4. Ensure Codex's first rollout `session_meta` line contains more than 65,536 bytes (a near-limit handoff naturally does this).
5. Inspect the Codex usage binding and Cost & Usage response.

Expected: the Codex rollout is registered, historical records are ingested, and both Claude and Codex appear in the session usage response.

Actual: the binding remains `source_discovery_pending`; source/event counts remain zero; the API and Summary omit Codex.

## Verified affected and control sessions

Audit scope was every persisted agent switch across all locally registered projects (`reverb`, `scratch`, and `super-30`), including active and terminated sessions. There were 14 Claude-to-Codex switch attempts across six unique sessions; six completed. No other harness-pair switches were present.

| Session | Display name | Completed switch (UTC) | First `session_meta` line | Post-switch Codex use | Codex in Cost & Usage | Classification |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| `reverb-29` | `4218-subscription` | 2026-08-23 17:52:21 | 89,596 B | 176 observations; latest cumulative 23,389,905 processed tokens | No | Affected |
| `reverb-30` | `4026-sidebar_dots` | 2026-08-24 05:38:52 | 22,177 B | 67 observations; 67 ledger events | Yes | Correct control |
| `reverb-31` | `term-select-scroll` | 2026-08-24 04:47:29 | 90,941 B | 93 observations; latest cumulative 15,927,562 | No | Affected |
| `reverb-33` | `sidebar-dnd` | 2026-08-24 04:42:21 | 91,344 B | 60 observations; latest cumulative 4,923,012 | No | Affected |
| `reverb-35` | `long-session-names` | 2026-08-24 04:46:37 | 91,546 B | 70 observations; latest cumulative 8,321,724 | No | Affected |
| `reverb-38` | `agent-system-guide` | 2026-08-23 19:50:39 | 55,410 B | 95 observations; 93 ledger events | Yes | Correct control |

The two skipped `reverb-38` observations had zero measurable token components and inconsistent `last.total_tokens`; they were correctly treated as anomalies and are unrelated to discovery.

Aggregate at the audit snapshot:

- 6 completed switches with real post-switch Codex turns.
- 4 affected, 2 correct controls.
- 561 raw Codex observations total; 399 belonged to affected sessions.
- 160 Codex ledger events total; affected sessions had zero.
- 52,562,203 cumulative processed Codex tokens were visible in affected raw observations but absent from the ledger.
- Across all 20 locally persisted Codex usage bindings, 16 had sources and these exact four remained pending. No additional active or terminated local sessions were affected.

Eight failed switch attempts are false positives if inventory code counts `target_harness=codex` without requiring a completed switch/native rollout. They did not establish comparable post-switch Codex use.

## Timeline and evidence

- The six successful switches completed between 2026-08-23 17:52 UTC and 2026-08-24 05:39 UTC.
- The daemon restarted at 2026-08-24 04:43:46 UTC. Affected switches occurred both before and after it; a correct control also occurred after it.
- Persisted session rows for all six identified Codex as the current harness and held a correct native Codex identity/rollout. `reverb-31` later resumed under a new AO launch ID while retaining the same native Codex ID and rollout; its failure persisted.
- Affected bindings were retried approximately every 30 seconds, updating their timestamps but deterministically remaining `source_discovery_pending`.
- Fresh usage API requests already omitted Codex. The result was not a stale browser cache.

The `ao send` `INTERNAL_ERROR` observed around the `reverb-29` switch is not causal. Its switch handoff timed out, but the switch completed, the persisted Codex identity is correct, seven later user follow-ups reached Codex, and 176 Codex token observations exist. This distinguishes that transient control/runtime failure from the independent usage-discovery defect.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/service/usage/collector.go` defines:

```go
maxCodexSessionMeta = 64 << 10
```

`discoverCodexPath` validates each candidate by calling `codexSessionMetaMatches`, which calls `readCodexSessionMeta`. That function uses:

```go
bufio.NewReaderSize(file, maxCodexSessionMeta+1).ReadSlice('\n')
```

When the first JSONL record is over 64 KiB, `ReadSlice` returns `bufio.ErrBufferFull`. The function returns `(false)` before unmarshalling the otherwise valid metadata, and discovery silently rejects the candidate.

The same reader participates in initial hook source attribution, startup active-session backfill, and periodic reconciliation. Every repair path therefore repeats the same deterministic rejection.

This is **before** the normal usage parser/ingestor. `backend/internal/observe/usage/ingestor.go` already permits records up to `1 << 20` (1 MiB), so the affected records are ingestible but never registered as sources.

The failed boundary is:

```text
valid Codex rollout
  -> bounded session_meta discovery (fails at 64 KiB)
  -> no usage_sources row
  -> watcher/ingestor never runs
  -> no model_usage_events or OpenAI detail rows
  -> API aggregation has no Codex rows
  -> Summary has nothing Codex to render
```

A secondary observability problem is that `source_discovery_pending` is currently treated as benign by session integrity aggregation, so these API responses reported `incomplete: false` despite missing a provider source.

## Why agent switches produce oversized first records

The switch path permits a finalized handoff continuation up to `96 << 10` bytes (`handoffContinuationMaxBytes`). It appends that continuation to the target's hidden system prompt. Codex then serializes the complete prompt into the first rollout record under `payload.base_instructions.text`.

The physical line therefore includes more than the capped handoff:

- up to 96 KiB of continuation,
- roughly 8 KiB of AO base/protocol instructions in the observed cases,
- project/agent rules,
- the JSON envelope and escaping overhead.

Observed total AO prompt sizes were 83,619–84,953 bytes for three affected controls plus 84,585 bytes for the fourth; JSON serialization expanded the physical lines to 89–91 KiB. The working controls had smaller continuations and stayed below 64 KiB.

Thus the existing limits contain an invalid invariant: a switch may legitimately generate a 96 KiB continuation while source discovery rejects the complete serialized record above 64 KiB. Project rules can also enlarge the record, so this is not inherently switch-only.

## Blast radius

Any Codex rollout whose first `session_meta` record exceeds 64 KiB can fail discovery, including:

- Claude-to-Codex switches with large continuation context,
- fresh Codex sessions with large project/agent rules,
- restored native Codex sessions,
- Codex child/subagent rollouts,
- archived/relocated rollout discovery.

The local canonical database contained no affected sessions beyond the four listed above, but the defect is product-wide and data-dependent rather than tied to those identities.

## Why tests and CI missed it

- Collector fixtures create tiny `session_meta` envelopes and omit realistic `base_instructions`.
- The existing “large rollout” test adds many records **after a small first line**, so it tests total file size rather than first-record size.
- Switch tests enforce the independent 96 KiB continuation bound using fake runtimes but never serialize a production-shaped Codex first record and pass it through usage discovery.
- Parser tests cover the 1 MiB ingestion limit independently; no cross-package test enforces `switch prompt <= discovery record <= ingestion record`.
- CI does not launch a real Codex provider, so it never observes the provider's first-record serialization shape.

## Immediate safe recovery

After deploying the reader fix, restart once to run active-session backfill or allow periodic reconciliation to run. The existing four bindings should register their rollout from byte offset zero and ingest historical records to EOF.

Do **not** truncate/copy provider rollouts, delete bindings, or manually insert usage events.

Double-counting protections already exist:

- all four affected bindings currently have zero sources/events;
- sources are unique by binding/artifact/generation;
- events are unique by binding/source event key;
- `ApplyUsageChunk` atomically validates events, inserts details, and advances cursor/baseline in one transaction;
- replaying identical events is idempotent and conflicts roll back.

If an affected session terminates before deployment, perform the same controlled targeted reconciliation against its preserved binding/source rather than manual ledger writes.

## Smallest durable fix

Raise the bounded Codex metadata-record limit from 64 KiB to **1 MiB**, matching the existing ingestion record limit. Continue reading only the first record and retain all existing provider-root, symlink, native-ID, parent-attribution, candidate-count, and cancellation checks.

A 1 MiB bound comfortably covers the permitted 96 KiB handoff plus the rest of the serialized prompt while remaining finite. Records above that limit should remain rejected; follow-up hardening can make the rejection explicit and surface persistent discovery-pending state as `incomplete: true`.

Where package boundaries allow, discovery and ingestion should derive their record ceiling from one shared contract to prevent future drift.

## Security and operational limits

- The first record may contain hidden system instructions and handoff context. Do not log or persist its text outside the provider-owned rollout; parse only identity/source fields.
- Keep a strict bounded read; do not replace it with an unbounded scanner/read-all.
- Preserve first-record-only processing, provider-root/symlink validation, native ID/parent verification, context cancellation, and the existing finite candidate search.
- Rejecting a record above 1 MiB should produce sanitized diagnostics without prompt contents.

## Regression test matrix

Focused fix coverage:

- [ ] A valid Codex `session_meta` first record above 64 KiB and below 1 MiB is matched.
- [ ] Native ID and parent thread matching still work with the large record.
- [ ] A first record above 1 MiB remains rejected without an unbounded read.
- [ ] Existing malformed JSON, wrong native ID, wrong parent, symlink/root escape, and small-record behavior remains unchanged.

Follow-up integration coverage:

- [ ] Codex session-start hook with native ID but no transcript path discovers a large-metadata rollout and clears pending state.
- [ ] Active-session backfill ingests historical token records from offset zero.
- [ ] Reconciliation is idempotent across restart/replay.
- [ ] A near-96-KiB switch continuation serialized in a production-shaped Codex envelope reaches OpenAI/model ledger rows.
- [ ] Usage API returns both pre-switch Claude and post-switch Codex contributions.
- [ ] Persistent discovery-pending state makes integrity incomplete and is surfaced by the Summary UI.

title: fix(renderer): fetch-based workspace SSE — stop on 4xx, honor 503 (completes #4323)
body:
Builds on #4340 (backoff) and completes #4323. **Stacked on `ao/ao-25/sse-backoff`** — review/merge #4340 first (or retarget to `main` after it lands).

## Why
Native `EventSource` hides the HTTP status on error, so the workspace stream could only ever blindly reconnect. #4340 added backoff to stop the *storm*; this adds the *smart stop* by reading the stream with `fetch()` + a `ReadableStream`, which exposes the status.

## Behavior
- **4xx** (session/workspace gone): stop reconnecting entirely — sticky until the daemon base URL changes (a restarted daemon still gets a fresh attempt).
- **5xx / network**: back off (reuses `computeBackoffDelayMs`) and honor a `Retry-After` header when present. This is where **#4325's typed 503 becomes usable on the client**.
- **200**: reset backoff, stream events; a healthy stream that closes reconnects promptly.
- `AbortController` drives clean teardown on unmount and base-URL change.

New dependency-free `sse-parse.ts` turns the byte stream into SSE frames (CRLF / comment-keepalive / multi-line `data` handling).

## Verification (local)
- Pure `sse-parse` and `sse-backoff` invariants: **100 runs each** via `tsx`.
- Full lib test suite — parser, backoff, and the fetch-stream integration tests (shared-stream + abort-on-unmount, event coalescing, **4xx → no reconnect**, **5xx → backed-off reconnect**) — ran **100/100 with zero flakiness**.
- Caught and fixed a real bug during testing: the retry's `connect()` was blocked by the "already connecting" guard because the aborted attempt's controller wasn't released; the 5xx→reconnect test now proves it reconnects.

## Note
Native EventSource is fully replaced here; response-body streaming works in Electron's Chromium `fetch` (the `duplex` limitation only affects request-body streaming, which this doesn't use).

title: fix(usage): accept switch-sized Codex metadata
body:
## What

Increase the bounded Codex `session_meta` discovery limit from 64 KiB to 1 MiB and add a regression fixture with a switch-sized (96 KiB) hidden system prompt.

## Why

Fixes #4343.

Agent switches can legally append up to 96 KiB of handoff continuation before Codex serializes the complete system prompt into the first rollout record. The usage collector rejected that valid first record at 64 KiB, preventing source registration, ingestion, ledger rows, API aggregation, and Summary visibility.

## How

- Keep discovery bounded and first-record-only, but align its ceiling with the usage ingestor's existing 1 MiB record limit.
- Preserve provider-root validation, native/parent identity matching, and all existing rejection behavior.
- Exercise a production-shaped `session_meta` envelope whose `base_instructions.text` is 96 KiB; this test failed against the old limit and passes with the new limit.

Intentional omissions: this focused PR does not change integrity-state reporting or add sanitized diagnostics for records above 1 MiB; those are follow-up hardening items documented in the RCA.

## Testing

title: feat(observability): daemon Sentry — capture 5xx and panics with Go stacks
body:
Third and final Sentry surface. The renderer (#4180) and mobile (#4181) slices capture what the *clients* see; this captures what the *daemon* actually threw. It is where the daemon's opaque `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500s finally get a real Go stack instead of a bare count, grouped by the same fingerprint the telemetry path already uses so an issue lines up across both.

## What this adds
- **`internal/observe/sentryobs`** — a small daemon Sentry integration. DSN-gated via `AO_SENTRY_DSN`; a blank DSN leaves it a permanent no-op, so this merges now and goes live the moment the DSN is set. Deny-by-default on privacy: PII off, `BeforeSend` clears `ServerName` and the request context and scrubs local paths (`/Users/...`, `/home/...`, `C:\...`) out of the message and every stack frame; no breadcrumbs; tracing off.
- **Capture at the seams where the real error and stack are live**, reusing the existing telemetry emit points rather than adding a second path:
  - httpd 5xx access-log branch — captures the handler's `capturedErr` with the classified `error_kind`/`error_code`.
  - panic recover middleware — captures the recovered value with its `debug.Stack()`.
- **Grouping** — the same `telemetrymeta.Fingerprint(...)` the PostHog `ao.http.5xx` / `ao.daemon.panic` events use, tagged `platform=daemon` plus `operation`, `path` (route pattern), `status`, `error_code`, and `request_id` for cross-correlation.
- **Transient 503** (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, see #4325) is deliberately excluded via `ShouldCaptureStatus` — retryable contention is not a fault and would drown the signal.

## Why no behavior change until the DSN is set
`Init` returns early on a blank DSN and every capture is a guarded no-op, so the build, tests, and runtime are unchanged today. Existing `ao.http.5xx` / `ao.daemon.panic` telemetry is untouched.

## Ship steps (when the DSN arrives)
1. Set `AO_SENTRY_DSN` in the daemon environment.
2. Release/environment are already wired from the app version + version channel.

## Verification
- Verified over a socket against a mock Sentry ingest: an event is transmitted with the local path scrubbed (no `/Users` leak), carrying the fingerprint tag and `platform=daemon`; a 503 is not captured.
- Unit tests (`scrub`, `ShouldCaptureStatus` incl. the 503 skip, no-op-when-disabled, full event scrub) pass at `-count=50`.
- `go build ./...`, `golangci-lint` clean, httpd/config/sentryobs packages green.

Completes the three-surface Sentry coverage with #4180 (desktop) and #4181 (mobile). Related error work: #4323, #4325, #4334.

title: fix(daemon): report degraded readiness and degrade spawn preflight on catalog failure
body:
## What

Follow-up to #4336, addressing the remaining items of #4335. The agent catalog is the preflight dependency of `ao spawn`, but a refresh failure was swallowed into a fire-and-forget WARN while `/readyz` kept reporting ready — so a daemon that could not spawn still passed readiness, and the CLI surfaced the failure as an opaque `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

1. **`/readyz` reflects real readiness** — new `Readiness` state in `httpd` (starts ready, can be marked degraded with a reason). `/readyz` returns `503` + `status: "degraded"` + `reason` when degraded, instead of unconditionally `200`. Nil readiness (the test default and pre-existing callers) keeps the old behavior.
2. **Daemon marks itself degraded** — when the initial agent-catalog refresh fails, the daemon records the cause on `Readiness`, so the failure is visible to the supervisor and to clients gating on the probe instead of dying in a WARN nothing reads.
3. **Spawn preflight degrades instead of blocking** — when the catalog refresh fails, `ao spawn` warns and continues, letting spawn validate runtime readiness (mirroring the existing `agentProbeUnavailable` degradation). The service-side contract ("published = cached") is intentionally encoded by `TestRefreshPublishesOnlyAfterInventoryPersistenceSucceeds`, so the fix lives in the CLI path, not the service.

## Why

Part of #4335: a failure in a core dependency must not be both invisible (`/readyz` green) and blocking (`INTERNAL_ERROR`) at the same time.

## Red → green

- `TestReadyzReflectsDegraded` — `/readyz` returned `200` for a degraded daemon; now `503` + reason.
- `TestSpawnCatalogRefreshFailureDegradesToWarning` — spawn failed on a `500` refresh; now warns and spawns.
- Both tests are killed by reverting their fix (mutation check).

title: fix(cli): carry reviewers through project set-config (#4277)
body:
Fixes #4277

## Root cause

The CLI is a thin daemon client that hand-mirrors daemon DTOs. Its mirror struct `projectConfig` in `backend/internal/cli/project.go` had no `Reviewers` field, so:

1. `ao project set-config --config-json '{"reviewers":[...]}'` unmarshals into that struct and `encoding/json` silently discards the unknown `reviewers` key.
2. The CLI then PUTs the reviewers-less config to `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/config`, which replaces the whole config.

Result: `status: ok` with reviewers never persisted, while the identical payload through the daemon API works. The daemon API was correct; this was purely a CLI DTO gap. Notably, `reviewers` pins cross-family review, so the silent drop meant the review loop quietly never ran.

## Fix

- Add `reviewerConfig` (mirrors `domain.ReviewerConfig`) and `Reviewers []reviewerConfig` (`json:"reviewers,omitempty"`) to the CLI's `projectConfig`, so `--config-json` round-trips reviewers like every other field.
- Add a repeatable `--reviewer <harness>` flag to `project set-config`, wired through `buildProjectConfig`. Harness vocabulary validation stays daemon-side per the thin-client convention.
- Tests: `TestProjectSetConfig_ReviewerJSON` (the issue's repro) and `TestProjectSetConfig_ReviewerFlags`.

## Intentional omissions

- No CLI-side validation of reviewer harness names; the daemon already rejects unknown harnesses via its error envelope.
- `--reviewer` only applies on the flags path; per existing behavior `--config-json` overrides field flags.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1` - full package passes, including the two new tests

title: Make Browser a responsive co working canvas
body:
## Issue

AO’s Browser previously behaved like the other inspector views, leaving web previews constrained to a utility-sized rail while chat absorbed most layout pressure.

The surrounding workspace did not adapt cohesively when Browser opened, and Browser maximize/minimize could expose abrupt layout or native-view handoffs.

## Fix

- Give Browser a dedicated canvas profile:
  - 900px preferred width
  - Up to 68% of the available workspace
  - 440px minimum companion-chat width
- Keep Summary, Reviews, and Files on the consistent 500px utility profile.
- Automatically compact the left sidebar when Browser and chat need more room.
- Preserve the user’s sidebar preference and respect manual expansion during automatic compaction.
- Add hysteresis to prevent the sidebar from repeatedly expanding and collapsing near layout breakpoints.
- Animate Browser growth, chat reflow, and sidebar compaction on a coordinated workspace transition.
- Remember Browser and utility-panel widths separately.
- Animate Browser maximize and minimize from the real dock geometry while preserving the live Browser instance.
- Hold the final minimize geometry briefly so Electron’s native browser bounds settle before returning ownership to the dock.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences and platform titlebar offsets.

The Browser adapts automatically when selected; no additional focus or “wide workspace” control is introduced.

## Files affected

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx`
  - Adds Browser-specific sizing, workspace transitions, adaptive demand, and geometry-aware maximize/minimize.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/BrowserPanel.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`
  - Pass dock geometry through the Browser maximize action.
- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/stores/ui-store.ts`
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/adaptive-sidebar.ts`
  - Coordinate automatic sidebar compaction without overwriting user preferences.
- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useResizable.ts`
  - Supports live sizing constraints for the different workspace profiles.
- `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`
  - Adds synchronized workspace and Browser geometry transitions.
- Associated renderer, store, sidebar, Browser, and shell tests
  - Cover entry and exit behavior, manual overrides, saved widths, responsive pressure, and maximize/minimize handoff.

## Validation

- 392 affected renderer tests passed across 11 test files.
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- `npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts`
- `git diff --check`

title: Bundled tmux cannot find terminfo database and breaks TUI attachment
body:
## Bug

Nightly `0.12.7-nightly.202608241447` prints `can't find terminfo database` repeatedly in every TUI agent session. New TUI attaches fail, and already-running TUI sessions begin showing the same error after updating because the updated daemon attaches with the newly bundled tmux client.

**Source:** User report in an AO session on 2026-08-24 (no public chat URL available)  
**Analyzed against:** `ea895fa8b` (regression introduced by `c9a0adb21`, PR [#4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293))  
**Observed artifact:** macOS arm64 desktop nightly `0.12.7-nightly.202608241447`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1 — TUI attachment is a core workflow and the packaged-app launch path has no practical in-app workaround.

## Reproduction

On macOS arm64 with the affected nightly installed:

1. Locate the staged bundled binary at `~/.ao/runtime/tmux/0.12.7-nightly.202608241447-darwin-arm64/tmux`.
2. Create an isolated session:
   ```sh
   BUNDLED_TMUX="$HOME/.ao/runtime/tmux/0.12.7-nightly.202608241447-darwin-arm64/tmux"
   "$BUNDLED_TMUX" -L ao-terminfo-repro -f /dev/null new-session -d -s triage 'sleep 30'
   ```
3. Attach using the same terminal arguments/environment as `Runtime.Attach`:
   ```sh
   TERM=xterm-256color "$BUNDLED_TMUX" -L ao-terminfo-repro -u -T RGB attach-session -t triage
   ```
4. Observe two lines of `can't find terminfo database`; the client exits with status 1.

`TERMINFO=/usr/share/terminfo` makes the same attach succeed, and `/usr/bin/infocmp xterm-256color` confirms the system entry exists.

## Root Cause

`frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:136-158` builds a private static ncurses/libtinfo under a temporary CI prefix, then `frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:184-190` statically links that library into tmux. The ncurses configuration does not specify portable system terminfo directories or embedded fallback entries.

The resulting shipped binary contains this compile-time database location:

```text
/Users/runner/work/agent-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator/.cache/bundled-tmux/darwin-arm64-r3-3.5a-2.1.12-stable-6.5-2.10.0/prefix/share/terminfo
```

That directory does not exist on an installed user's machine. Only the tmux executable and licenses are copied into `frontend/tmux`; no terminfo database is packaged.

`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:722-728` launches the bundled tmux client for every terminal attachment, and `attachEnv` at lines 768-788 forces `TERM=xterm-256color`. Initializing that terminal requires the missing database, so the error affects both new and pre-upgrade sessions whenever the nightly's client attaches.

The release smoke at `frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:108-112` runs only `tmux -V`, which does not initialize terminal capabilities and therefore cannot catch this failure.

## Suggested Fix

- Make the bundled ncurses lookup portable, either by compiling the required terminal descriptions as ncurses fallbacks (at minimum `xterm-256color`) or by packaging a minimal terminfo tree and setting an AO-owned `TERMINFO` path for bundled tmux attaches. Do not retain the CI build prefix as the runtime default.
- Add an artifact smoke test that creates an isolated tmux server and performs a real PTY attach with `TERM=xterm-256color`; checking `tmux -V` alone is insufficient.
- Verify both macOS architectures and Linux release artifacts because the same build script produces all three.

## Impact

- TUI-mode agent sessions cannot be reliably attached in the affected nightly.
- Existing sessions regress immediately after update even though their agent processes were started before the update.
- The problem is harness-independent because it occurs in the tmux client before agent output is rendered.

## Related

- PR [#4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293) introduced the bundled tmux artifact and attachment path.
- PR [#2488](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2488) is the earlier open bundled-tmux implementation in the same subsystem.

title: fix(desktop): embed tmux terminfo fallback
body:
Fixes #4382

## Summary

- build ncurses's matching `tic` and `infocmp` tools, then embed the pinned `xterm-256color` entry into the static libtinfo used by bundled tmux
- avoid host `pkg-config` dependency by pointing tmux directly at AO's pinned static utf8proc archive
- replace the version-only artifact check with a real pseudo-terminal attach while `HOME`, `TERMINFO`, and `TERMINFO_DIRS` point to nonexistent paths
- bump the native build revision so release jobs cannot reuse the broken cached artifact
- preserve pre-bundling TUI sessions by using the system tmux client for the legacy default socket while retaining AO's bundled client for the private `ao` socket
- pin every migrated legacy probe, command, and PTY attach to `-L default`, preventing inherited `TMUX` from redirecting AO to a nested or unrelated server
- distinguish conclusively absent infrastructure from an inconclusive legacy inspection: missing clients, protocol mismatches, and transient connection failures now return `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, which boot/restart/reaper paths cannot treat as session death or permission to create a replacement

## Upgrade-path coverage

- **Pre-regression → fixed:** legacy sessions are discovered and operated through the system tmux from `PATH`, avoiding tmux client/server protocol mismatches with AO's pinned bundled version. All legacy operations explicitly target the historical `default` socket. New sessions use the private socket and bundled client.
- **Broken nightly → fixed:** existing private-socket sessions continue through the bundled client, while the new app version stages the fixed binary at its own durable versioned path.
- **Mixed state:** exact private-socket probing remains first; sessions absent there are classified against the pinned legacy socket. The selected socket/client pair is cached for every subsequent operation.
- Only a conclusive `no server running` result is recoverable infrastructure absence. A missing/incompatible client or transient `error connecting` result preserves the existing controller and propagates an actionable, inconclusive error.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npm run build:tmux` (macOS arm64; real PTY attach passed with no host terminfo database)
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run forge.config.test.ts src/shared/bundled-tmux.test.ts` (12 tests passed)
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`
- clean AO environment: `npm run lint` (all Go tests and golangci-lint passed)
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux ./internal/session_manager`
- repeated tmux runtime package integration suite (`-count=3`)
- live protocol compatibility on macOS arm64:
  - system tmux 3.6b successfully queried the 16-session legacy default-socket server
  - bundled tmux 3.5a reproduced `server exited unexpectedly` against that server
  - bundled tmux 3.5a successfully queried the 11-session private `ao`-socket server
- real three-server integration regression:
  - creates isolated `default`, private `ao`, and spoof sockets
  - injects `TMUX` pointing at the spoof server with a colliding session namespace
  - verifies AO adopts the real default-socket session and rejects the spoof-only session
- unit regressions cover unavailable legacy client, incompatible-client output, transient legacy `error connecting`, client routing, and explicit `-L default` PTY attachment
- session-manager regressions prove boot reconciliation and explicit restart propagate inconclusive legacy probes without Create, Restart, Destroy, termination, or workspace changes
- `otool -L frontend/tmux/bin/tmux` (system libraries only)

## Risk

The terminfo fallback is intentionally limited to `xterm-256color`, which is the exact terminal AO forces for bundled tmux attachments. Legacy default-socket sessions depend on a compatible system tmux remaining available from the daemon's inherited `PATH`, matching the dependency that created those pre-bundling sessions. If it is unavailable or incompatible, the session and controller are preserved and AO surfaces an inconclusive runtime error; it is not archived, destroyed, or duplicated. Linux and macOS Intel release artifacts still need to pass their native release-runner attach smoke tests.

title: fix(topbar): surface the real reason when opening an editor fails
body:
## Summary

Opening a session whose worktree is gone (terminated, merged, cleaned up) put
Electron's IPC plumbing straight into the topbar actions row:

> Error invoking remote method 'editorHandoff:open': Error: Session workspace is not available

Reproduced against real local data, where 27 of the first 40 sessions have no
resolvable workspace (`/api/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/workspace` returns 404).

## What was wrong

Two separate things, and the guard that exists is not the problem.

`TopbarOpenEditorButton` already disables itself when `getState` reports
`workspaceAvailable: false`, and that works. Confirmed live: on a terminated
session the control is disabled with the tooltip "Session workspace is not
available".

What bites is staleness. `useEditorHandoffState` caches with
`staleTime: 10_000` and nothing invalidated it on failure, so a worktree that
disappears *after* the state was read leaves the button enabled. The click
fails, the state is never refreshed, and the button stays enabled to fail again.

Separately, the message shown was raw plumbing.
`TopbarOpenEditorButton.tsx` rendered `open.error.message` verbatim, which is
Electron's wrapper around anything an `ipcMain` handler throws.

## The fix

Renderer-side, in `useEditorHandoff.ts`:

- Strip the `Error invoking remote method '<channel>': Error:` wrapper and
  rethrow a clean error, so the topbar shows what the main process actually
  said. This covers the other failure paths too, which were equally buried:
  "That editor is not installed", "Could not open <name>".
- Invalidate the handoff state query on error so the control re-checks
  availability rather than inviting the same failing click.

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed in the running desktop app against real session data, not
just in tests. Before: the raw wrapper. After: the disabled control carries the
clean reason as its tooltip.

Five unit tests on the normalizer plus a component regression test that clicks
through and asserts the rendered alert. The regression test is not vacuous:
with both changes reverted it fails with `expected 'Error invoking remote
method...' not to contain 'Error invoking remote method'`.

Full frontend suite: 2867 tests across 217 files. Typecheck clean.

## Notes for review

The code being fixed came from commit 728400ca8 in #3284, which replaced an
earlier HTTP implementation with this IPC one. I did not write it, so a look
from its author is worth having.

This treats the symptom in the renderer. Arguably `open()` in
`frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.ts` should also resolve the workspace inside
its `try`/`catch` so the failure comes back as a friendly message at the source
rather than as a raw throw. Left alone to keep this change narrow; happy to
fold it in.

title: Packaged tmux can read and control user-owned tmux state
body:
## Bug

The packaged macOS/Linux app invokes AO's bundled tmux binary, but the runtime is not fully isolated from tmux state owned by the user.

**Source:** User report and follow-up design discussion in an AO task on 2026-08-24/25 (no public chat URL)
**Analyzed against:** `5e408467b`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P1 — a socket collision can direct AO input, restart, or destroy operations at a user-owned tmux session.

## Reproduction

1. Start a user tmux server using the named socket `tmux -L ao`, or keep a same-named session on the default server.
2. Configure `~/.tmux.conf` with options/hooks that are inappropriate for AO.
3. Launch packaged AO and create or restore a TUI session.
4. Observe that AO uses the fixed `-L ao` namespace, allows a newly started server to load user configuration, and probes the default tmux socket when the AO-named server does not contain a matching session.

A custom `TMUX_TMPDIR` also changes where `-L ao` resolves, so the apparently private namespace is still controlled by inherited host environment.

## Root Cause

- `frontend/src/main.ts` injects the constant `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME=ao`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go` invokes tmux with `-L ao`, without an explicit `-f` configuration.
- The adapter caches socket discovery in memory and falls back to the machine default socket using only a matching session name as evidence.
- The tmux control process inherits a surrounding `TMUX` identity.
- `backend/internal/tmuxbin/resolve.go` may fall through to a PATH tmux if a recognizable packaged layout is missing its bundled sibling.

## Fix

- Derive a stable absolute socket path from the daemon run-file identity and use `-S` for every tmux operation.
- Keep the socket inode beside the run file; use a bounded, validated `/tmp` directory alias only when macOS's AF_UNIX path ceiling requires it.
- Pass `-f /dev/null` so AO never loads system/user tmux configuration or plugins.
- Remove automatic named/default socket discovery; every control operation stays on the AO-private socket.
- Remove only tmux identity/internal selector variables while preserving the user's workload environment, and refresh that environment for every new or respawned pane.
- Fail closed when a packaged daemon's bundled tmux is missing.
- Keep Windows on the existing ConPTY adapter.

## Impact

- User tmux servers and AO can collide across socket namespaces.
- AO may inherit user hooks/plugins/options and fail unpredictably.
- A stale AO handle plus a same-named user session can cause AO to operate on foreign state.
- Machines without system tmux should continue to work through the bundled artifact; the terminfo regression in that artifact is tracked separately.

## Related

- [Issue #4382](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4382) / [PR #4385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4385) — bundled tmux terminfo artifact failure.
- [PR #4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293) — introduced bundled tmux and the fixed `-L ao` namespace.
- [Issue #2662](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2662) / [PR #2664](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2664) — broader cross-data-dir session namespace collision.

title: fix(updates): prevent stuck manual check loader
body:
Regression follow-up to #4284. This replaces the update-card styling approach attempted in #4292; the two UI diffs should not be merged together.

## Summary

- consume every updater status push before React can batch away an intermediate terminal event
- clear a manual check only from its matching request ID, while preserving a previously staged update
- simplify the status card and keep long Nightly versions readable with aligned actions
- cover the real main-process event order, the renderer race, and the reported downloaded + Nightly geometry

## Root cause

With an update already staged, a failed manual manifest check can publish these statuses synchronously:

1. `error` for the current manual request ID
2. restored `downloaded` state carrying the earlier staged request ID

The fix in #4285 cleared local loading from a React effect that only observed the latest committed status. React batches both pushes, so the matching terminal event could be discarded before that effect ran. The local request ID stayed set and forced the card back to `checking` forever, even though the updater had restored a valid downloaded state.

`useUpdateStatus` now exposes a lossless per-event callback. `UpdatesSection` uses it to clear only the matching manual request before updating the rendered snapshot, so the following staged status renders normally.

The new renderer regression test failed against the old implementation with `Checking for updates…` where `Downloaded. Restart to finish updating.` was expected.

## Visual evidence

This deterministic renderer state matches the report: dark mode, automatic updates enabled, Nightly selected, a staged download, and the long installed Nightly version. The Playwright test also asserts that the version stays on one line and both actions have equal height.

![Settings Updates after: downloaded Nightly state with readable version and aligned actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-update-loader-lost-status/.issue-assets/update-loader-lost-status/after-dark.png)

The screenshot is visual-state evidence. The updater behavior itself is proven separately by the main-process producer test and renderer regression test.

## Native Electron verification

The branch was launched in the real Electron app with isolated AO data and the real preload bridge. Settings → Updates rendered correctly, and clicking **Check for updates** completed with `Updates are only available in the installed app.`, leaving the button enabled and `aria-busy=false`.

Unpackaged Electron intentionally has no release feed, so the exact packaged staged-update sequence is reproduced at its two real boundaries in tests rather than claimed from the screenshot.

## Tests

- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run` — 218 files passed; 2,875 tests passed; 1 skipped
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/main/auto-updater.test.ts` — 152 passed
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — passed
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck:e2e` — passed
- `cd frontend && npx playwright test e2e/updates-settings.spec.ts --reporter=line` — passed
- `cd frontend && npm run package` — production Electron package completed

title: fix(runtime): isolate AO tmux state
body:
Fixes [#4391](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4391).

Complements [#4385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4385), which fixes the missing packaged terminfo database seen in the original report.

## Summary

- derive a stable per-run-file private tmux socket, force an empty tmux config, and never probe or adopt user/default tmux state
- validate socket-directory ownership and permissions, with an owner-only short alias for macOS Unix-socket limits
- refresh merged daemon/project pane environments over stdin, remove stale global/session variables, and keep configured values out of process arguments

This is an intentional strict cutover. title: feat(observability): wire Sentry DSNs into desktop + mobile builds
body:
## What

Bakes the two Sentry DSNs as committed default constants, mirroring how `DEFAULT_POSTHOG_PROJECT_KEY` already ships, so **nightly and stable both pick them up with no CI or secret setup**. Client DSNs are write-only ingest endpoints; volume is bounded by each project's Sentry-side spike protection + rate limit (both enabled: 300 events/min).

Two separate Sentry projects (`ao-desktop`, `ao-mobile`) so desktop and mobile crash waves, quotas, and native symbolication stay independent.

## Changes

- `shared/sentry-config.ts` (desktop) and `packages/mobile/lib/sentry-config.ts` (mobile) hold the two project DSNs.
- Fallbacks: renderer `VITE_AO_SENTRY_DSN`, Electron main + daemon `AO_SENTRY_DSN`, and mobile `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` all fall back to the baked constant; an explicit env still wins.
- `main.ts` stamps `AO_SENTRY_DSN` onto the spawned daemon env (**off in dev**, matching the PostHog remote gate), so the Go daemon — whose `sentry-go` SDK is already compiled in via #4346 — captures 5xx and panics on the next non-dev build.
- **Privacy:** `daemon.go` now gates `sentryobs.Init` on `cfg.Telemetry.Events`, the same consent switch as the remote telemetry sink, so a user who turned telemetry off never has daemon faults reported even though a DSN is now baked in.

## Activation status

| Surface | State |
|---|---|
| **Daemon (Go)** | **Live on next non-dev build** — SDK vendored (#4346), activates from the env stamp. This is where the ~230k INTERNAL_ERROR 500s originate. |
| Renderer / Electron main | DSN baked. Still needs `@sentry/electron` installed (it is in `package.json` but not the lockfile) and the lazy import converted to static before the packaged app resolves it. |
| Mobile | DSN baked. Still needs `npx expo install @sentry/react-native` + the config plugin + `expo prebuild` to activate. |

## Verification

- `go build`, `go vet`, and the daemon telemetry-sink test pass.
- Touched frontend/mobile files typecheck clean (unrelated cross-worktree i18n resolution noise aside).
- Not verifiable here and needs a real build: a packaged desktop/Expo build actually delivering renderer/mobile events. The daemon path is the one that goes live from this PR.

## Follow-ups (client SDK activation)

1. Desktop: `npm install @sentry/electron@7.17.0` to fix the lockfile, convert the lazy `await import(...)` in `renderer/lib/sentry.ts` and `main/sentry-main.ts` to static imports, verify a packaged build.
2. Mobile: `npx expo install @sentry/react-native`, add the config plugin, `expo prebuild`.
3. Optional: upload renderer source maps per release for readable JS stacks.

title: fix(updates): make the sidebar update row actionable and surface a failing updater
body:
## How it looks Sidebar footer, expanded. Captured from the real component driven by real click handlers. | Available (was inert, now downloads on click) | Downloading | | --- | --- | | | | | Staged (unchanged) | Checks failing (was blank) | | --- | --- | | | | The staged shot shows the pre-existing truncation noted under "Out of scope": `v0.12.8-nightly.202608…` loses the word "ready". The available row no longer does, which is the third commit here. Images live on the `assets/pr-4397` branch so they stay out of this diff; it can be deleted once this merges. ## Context Two problems that together made the sidebar's update affordance look like it had been removed. **The available state was a dead end.** Since #4285 the sidebar renders `available` as an inert `
` rather than a button. A manual check leaves `autoDownload` off, so a build discovered that way never advances to the `downloaded` state that carries the click action. The row announces an update and offers nothing to act on. **A failing updater was invisible.** The sidebar returned `null` for `idle`, `checking`, `not-available` and `error`, and automatic check failures were never broadcast at all (`restoreAutomaticCheckPreviousStatus()` returns without sending a status). The one safety net could not help: `staleCheckNudge` needs three consecutive `net::ERR_*` failures, and `recordAutomaticCheckFailure` resets that counter on any non-net error, so the manifest 404 that actually strands a nightly install never trips it. A stranded install and a healthy one were pixel-for-pixel identical. Separately, automatic nightly checks used electron-updater's plain GitHub provider, which discovers prereleases through `releases.atom`. The repo already had an API-based resolver for the newest release carrying a manifest, but only manual checks used it. ## What changed - `available` is a button in both the expanded row and the collapsed icon rail; clicking it downloads. `downloading` stays informational with the percentage; `downloaded` keeps the existing restart action and escalation treatment. - A second failure counter that does not care *why* a check failed. Past three in a row the status carries `checksFailing` and is broadcast once per streak, and the sidebar turns that into a retry row that runs a manual check. Settings gets a matching line. - Automatic nightly checks resolve the release tag through the same API helper manual checks use, failing open to the normal provider so rate limits or an outage cannot break checks. Only nightly takes the extra await, so other channels keep their existing event ordering. Two deliberate non-changes: - The suppressed automatic failure still does not overwrite the state. An error the user never asked for must not replace a truthful `idle`/`not-available`, so only the flag rides along. - The retry row ranks **below** a staged build. An update ready to install is more actionable than "checks are failing". A test covers the ordering. ## Tests - `auto-updater.test.ts`: the automatic nightly check skips an in-progress release and points the feed at the newest one with a manifest, then restores the normal provider; the failing-check streak is announced once rather than once per failure; the streak clears as soon as a check reaches an answer. Each was confirmed to fail without the production change. - `Sidebar.test.tsx`: the available row is a labelled button calling `updates.download()`; an in-flight download offers no second one; a staged build outranks the failing-checks retry; a one-off failure stays quiet. - Seven pre-existing #3526 tests asserted the old blanket silence by whole-object equality. Updated so the behaviour they were protecting (restart guidance only for a wedged network stack, never for a 404) is asserted explicitly instead of implied. Ran locally: 62/62 `auto-updater.test.ts`, 66/66 `Sidebar.test.tsx`, 161/161 across the four related files, `npm run frontend:typecheck` clean. The `src/landing/**` failures in the full suite are pre-existing and unrelated (the base branch fails more of them than this branch). ## Verified by running, not just reading The renderer path was exercised end to end against a scripted bridge: real component, real click handlers, real `updates:status` push channel. Clicking `available` really transitions through `downloading` to `downloaded`. Rendering it against real nightly version strings is what caught the third commit here, where the subline truncated to `v0.12.8-nightly.202608251200…` and lost its trailing word. ## Risks and limits The main-process updater is gated on `app.isPackaged` and cannot run in a dev build, so the actual download-and-install is covered by unit tests against a mocked `autoUpdater`, not by a packaged run. The feed change is confined to the nightly channel. ## Out of scope - The stuck manual-check loader in Settings is handled by #4392 (https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/4392). - On the staged row the version line still truncates and loses the word "ready" — the same flaw fixed here for `available`, but it predates this branch (#2381), so it is left alone. - Observed on a real install while verifying: a build already staged in `pending/` was re-downloaded in full (168MB) on a later check. Worth its own investigation; not addressed here.

title: fix(browser): stop auto-sending browser errors
body:
## What

Stops browser console and failed-request diagnostics from being injected automatically into an active agent conversation.

Browser failures remain available through an explicit `ao browser errors` query for manual or agent-driven inspection.

## Why

The always-on browser signal path posted batched errors to the daemon session send endpoint. That unsolicited message could interrupt work already in progress and wake unrelated or idle agent sessions.

## How

- Removes the daemon-port and `net.fetch` auto-send path from the browser view host.
- Retains a session-local FIFO history of the latest 200 browser failures.
- Caps each retained entry at 16 KiB before storage.
- Preserves timestamps, console/network source classification, and untrusted-content boundaries.
- Detaches webRequest listeners and clears retained diagnostics when a session is destroyed.
- Merges retained diagnostics into the existing explicit browser errors response.
- Adds regression coverage proving the former five-second window performs no outbound send.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts` — 75 passed.
- `npm run typecheck` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent code review — no remaining Critical or Important findings.
- Full frontend suite attempted on Windows: 2,823 passed, 31 failed, 2 skipped. The failures are outside the touched browser-host area and relate to macOS path assumptions, unavailable Windows Unix-socket/symlink operations, and missing landing-package dependencies.

Manual testing requested before merge: open a page that emits console errors or failed XHR/fetch requests, confirm the active agent session is not interrupted, then run `ao browser errors` and confirm the diagnostics are returned.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant frontend checks pass for the touched area

title: Keep adaptive sidebar compaction scoped to Browser

## What

Limit automatic sidebar-to-icon-rail compaction to the docked Browser workspace.

Summary, Reviews, and Files now retain the normal sidebar unless the user manually collapses it. Leaving Browser clears its workspace pressure immediately and restores the surrounding layout.

## Why

All inspector views previously published adaptive workspace pressure. On narrower windows, opening utility views such as Summary or Reviews could unexpectedly compact the sidebar even though those views did not need the additional canvas space.

title: bug(chat): Claude Plan mode promises no tool execution but writes outside the worktree
body:
## Bug

Claude Code Plan mode is described as **“Planning mode, no actual tool execution.”** In native ChatUI QA it executed tools and persisted a plan file under `~/.claude/plans`, outside the session worktree, even though the prompt explicitly prohibited tools and file changes.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419)  
**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; relevant paths rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built `ao` (`dev`), verified daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P1 — the UI presents a false safety boundary  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced natively, filesystem side effect captured, and rendering/forwarding path traced

## Reproduction

1. Open a Claude Code session in ChatUI.
2. Select **Plan** in the permission-mode menu.
3. Prompt it to produce a plan while explicitly saying not to execute tools or modify files.
4. Observe Read/Write activity and a new Markdown plan under `~/.claude/plans`.
5. Deny the later “Ready to code?” prompt; the plan file already exists.

## Expected

Either AO enforces a genuine no-tool/no-write boundary, or the menu truthfully explains provider-native Plan mode, including possible file inspection, tool use, and provider-owned plan files outside the worktree.

## Actual

AO renders an absolute “no actual tool execution” promise while passing the provider mode through without enforcing that boundary.

## Root cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/config_options.go:172` forwards provider descriptions.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.tsx:544` renders the categorical description without qualification.
- Mode changes are forwarded to ACP; AO does not currently impose a tool/write policy at this boundary.

## Fix direction

Prefer truthful provider-specific disclosure unless AO can enforce a strict read-only mode. Add a provider contract test that observes writes outside the worktree.

## Acceptance

- Plan-mode copy never promises a boundary AO does not enforce.
- Claude-specific behavior explains provider-owned plan artifacts before selection.
- `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-01` passes in strict mode.

## Evidence

![Claude Plan mode writes a plan file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/screenshots/22-plan-mode-writes-plan-file.png)

- [Full finding and expected/actual details](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/manual-qa-report.md)
- [Captured filesystem evidence](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/evidence/plan-mode-created-file.md)

## Related

- [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — local-only regression harness and QA evidence
- [#3745](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3745) — separate read-only reviewer-harness work; not a duplicate

title: bug(chat): busy Chat-to-Terminal switch interrupts work without consent
body:
## Bug

Switching from a busy Chat session to Terminal immediately selects destructive `interrupt`, cancelling the active tool/turn and queued instructions without a Finish-versus-Stop choice. The reverse Terminal-to-Chat direction already presents that policy dialog.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419)  
**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; exact hard-coded path remains on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built AO, verified daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P1 — active and queued work can be destroyed without consent  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced natively and exact transition policy traced

## Reproduction

1. Start a Chat turn that runs a long tool, such as `sleep 20`.
2. Optionally queue a follow-up.
3. Click the top-bar action to switch to Terminal UI.
4. Observe no policy dialog; the transition begins immediately.
5. The native TUI shows the tool/turn as interrupted.

## Expected

Idle/no-queue Chat may drain directly. Active or queued Chat must show **Finish work, then switch** (safe default) versus **Stop now and switch**, name affected queue/draft state, and make no interrupt request before explicit consent.

## Actual

The renderer sends `policy: interrupt` immediately and temporarily exposes a mismatched surface while the destructive transition runs.

## Root cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx:704` hard-codes `interrupt` for Chat-to-Terminal before checking busy/queued state.
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:1389` applies interrupt semantics, cancelling the durable queue and provider work.

## Fix direction

Reuse the existing policy dialog in both directions. Derive the safe default from active/queued state and prove no transition POST occurs before user choice.

## Acceptance

- Busy Chat always offers drain versus interrupt.
- Default focus is **Finish work, then switch**.
- Drain preserves accepted active/queued work.
- Interrupt occurs only after explicit **Stop now** consent.
- `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-05` passes in strict mode.

## Evidence

![Busy Chat switched directly to interrupted Terminal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/screenshots/33-busy-chat-to-terminal-transition.png)

- [Full finding](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/manual-qa-report.md)

## Related

- [PR #3671](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3671) — earlier symmetric policy-dialog behavior
- [PR #3957](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3957) — introduced unconditional Chat-to-Terminal interrupt behavior
- [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — two deterministic MQA-05 policy contracts
