title: feat(cloud): integrate the AO cloud offering into the monorepo (AWS/NodeOps, flag-gated)
body:
## Summary

Integrates the entire AO cloud offering into this monorepo so one repository serves
both the local desktop app and the hosted cloud product. The cloud control plane
(previously a separate private repo) is vendored as a `cloud/` Go module wired
through a Go workspace (`go.work`). Everything cloud sits behind a single
Developer Mode-gated Settings toggle that is off by default, so the app runs
exactly as it does today with zero behavioral change until a user deliberately
enables the offering.

## Gating (additive, zero local regression)

The cloud offering is a persisted daemon preference, off by default:

- **Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode** reveals a **Cloud** toggle; enabling it
  shows an explicit "early, highly unstable preview" confirmation first.
- The toggle is stored daemon-side (`app_settings.cloud_offering`, PATCH
  `/api/v1/settings/cloud-offering`) so desktop, mobile, and headless spawns
  resolve the same gate.
- `cloudEnabled = (toggle || AO_CLOUD_OFFERING env force-on) && control-plane URL`.
  The control-plane URL and the WorkOS client id are public client configuration
  and ship as baked defaults; the env vars remain development overrides only.
- There is no per-client entitlement in the gate anymore; abuse control is
  server-side (per-org sandbox quotas, with control-plane entitlement as a
  follow-up).

When cloud is off (the default) the daemon imports no cloud code, the renderer
skips every control-plane call, and local sessions are authoritative — the app
behaves exactly as before.

## What is included

- `cloud/` module: Postgres control plane (HTTP API, WorkOS RS256 JWT auth,
  reconciler, worker transport), sandbox provider interface with NodeOps CreateOS
  and Docker implementations, and the AWS deploy path (ECR, ECS, migration task,
  scan gate, auto rollback).
- Local vs cloud projects: local projects run local sessions; cloud projects run
  cloud sessions, each worker in its own isolated sandbox.
- Electron main process control-plane proxy so the WorkOS token stays in the main
  process and the renderer never talks to the control plane directly.
- Separate migrations by design: cloud uses Postgres migrations under
  `cloud/internal/postgres/migrations`; local keeps its SQLite migrations. The two
  are structurally disjoint (different engines, databases, directories).

## Reliability fixes in this branch

- Public repository checkout: `AO_CLOUD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_GITHUB_CHECKOUT` lets a
  worker clone a public repository directly when the checkout broker denies a grant.
  Previously only the Docker provider enabled this, so NodeOps workers on a public
  repo project without a GitHub App connection failed checkout with a 403 and
  crash-looped. GitHub App checkout for private repositories is the follow-up.
- Terminal startup ceiling: a worker that never checks in was repaired in place on
  every tick forever, which kept resetting the provider auto-pause timer and billed a
  permanently broken session indefinitely. A configurable ceiling
  (`TerminalStartupTimeout`, default 10m, clamped above the startup timeout) now
  stops the repair storm, best-effort stops the compute to halt billing, and parks
  the sandbox as `terminated`. It is gated on "never checked in" so a once-healthy
  worker that goes silent is still repaired normally.
- Sandbox `terminated` state migration: the `terminated` verdict above was written by
  the reconciler but never allowed by the `ao_sandboxes_observed_state_check`
  constraint, so every write failed (SQLSTATE 23514) and a ceiling-hit sandbox could
  never settle -- it was re-reconciled every tick and the session terminal looped
  forever on "worker is not connected". Migration `00030_sandbox_terminated_state.sql`
  adds `terminated` to the constraint so the verdict persists and the sandbox settles.
- Frontend UX: cloud auth resolves instantly on cold open (the on-disk session is
  returned immediately and the WorkOS token refreshes in the background) instead of
  blanking the sidebar for seconds; the New Project flow shows an explicit
  Local | Cloud choice with a caption for each and a sign-in prompt when
  unauthenticated; the cloud terminal shows a calm "Connecting..." on first attach
  (rather than "disconnected -- reattaching"), no longer gates on the local daemon,
  and lifts its replay cover cleanly with no blank flicker.

- Bounded sandbox deletion: a provider box that cannot be reclaimed (e.g. a
  NodeOps VM stuck in "failed", whose DELETE is accepted but never converges)
  no longer keeps the reconciler re-requesting deletion forever; past a
  deadline (default 15m) the row is released and the orphan logged.
- Sandbox quota counts only live sandboxes (terminated/failed/deleting no longer
  block new sessions) and the per-org cap default is 1000.
- Connect latency: the worker bootstraps once the sandbox is actually running
  (not at create time), within the same reconcile claim, and launches
  template-baked binaries after a hash check instead of uploading them; the
  sandbox templates come in per-harness slim variants selected by the session's
  harness; the terminal polls readiness at a flat 1s before first attach.
  Median session connect measured at ~5s (from ~60-90s), with occasional
  ~15s outliers when the provider schedules onto a host without the cached
  template.
- Cloud project/session UX: signing out hides cloud projects immediately and
  drops the cached cloud data; the orchestrator button on a cloud project spawns
  an orchestrator session in its own sandbox instead of falling through to
  project settings; coding-agent credentials are managed in-app (post-sign-in
  prompt plus a Cloud page in Settings).

## Verification

- Cloud module builds and vets clean; reconcile, config, worker, and sandbox unit
  tests pass, including new reconcile tests (terminate at the ceiling, park without
  resume, still honour deletion, repair within the ceiling) and a config test.
- Deployed to AWS staging and validated end to end: a cloud session on a public
  repository provisions a NodeOps sandbox, the worker reaches `worker.ready`, the
  agent runs the prompt, and the turn completes (returns to idle), then tears down
  cleanly.
- Local paths verified: with cloud disabled, the daemon runs the local app
  unchanged.

---

## How to test this branch (for developers)

The cloud control plane is already deployed to AWS staging, so you do **not**
deploy it, and **no environment variables are needed** — the staging control-plane
URL and the WorkOS client id ship as baked defaults. Everything below is what a
developer needs end to end.

### Prerequisites

- **Go** (per `go.mod` / `go.work`), **Node 20+** and **npm**, **git**, and **gh**.
- **A Claude Code setup token** (`claude setup-token`) or an Anthropic API key —
  the cloud sandbox runs the agent with *your* credential (step 4).
- **Free ports:** `3000` (WorkOS sign-in callback), `3002` (dev daemon), `5173`
  (Vite dev server). An installed build uses `:3001`, so it can run alongside.

### 1. Check out and run

```bash
gh pr checkout 4434          # or: git fetch <fork> && git checkout feat/cloud-offering-aws
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

`predev` builds the Go daemon, the browser runtime, and the ACP runtime
automatically. Dev state is isolated under `~/.ao/dev` (daemon on `:3002`, Vite on
`:5173`), so it never touches an installed build.

### 2. Enable the cloud offering

**Settings** (gear, bottom-left) → **Advanced** → turn on **Developer Mode** → a
**Cloud** toggle appears beneath it → turn it on and confirm the unstable-preview
warning. "Sign in to AO Cloud" appears in the sidebar immediately.

Sanity check: `curl http://127.0.0.1:3002/api/v1/settings` shows
`"cloudOffering": true, "cloudEnabled": true`.

(Env overrides still exist for CI/headless: `AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=true` force-enables,
`AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` / `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` / `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT`
override the baked defaults.)

### 3. Sign in (WorkOS auth)

Click **Sign in to AO Cloud** in the left sidebar. A browser opens WorkOS AuthKit;
after login it redirects to the loopback and the app stores the session (the token
stays in the Electron main process and never reaches the renderer). You are placed in
your **own personal org** automatically, so cloud projects are isolated per developer.

### 4. Connect your coding-agent credential (one-time, per org)

Creating a cloud session requires a validated coding-agent connection (the sandbox
worker runs the agent with your token). The app now prompts for this itself: right
after your first sign-in, a **"Connect a coding agent credential"** dialog opens
when your org has no valid connection yet. Pick the harness (Claude Code / Codex /
Cursor), paste a setup token or API key, and Connect -- expect "Credential
connected". You can reopen it any time from the sidebar account menu ->
**Coding agent credentials**.

For Claude Code, a setup token comes from `claude setup-token` (or use an Anthropic
API key). The credential is validated by the control plane and stored encrypted;
it is never shown again.

Headless/CI alternative: `python3 cloud/scripts/dev-connect-agent-credential.py`
does the same PUT from a terminal. It reads the token from `CLAUDE_CRED`, then
`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, then the macOS Keychain; signs in via WorkOS once
(loopback `:3000`, cached at `~/.ao/cloud-dev-token.json`); flags `--login`,
`--delete`.

### 5. Add a cloud project and open sessions

- **New Project** -> the **Local | Cloud** choice appears (cloud enabled + signed in)
  -> pick **Cloud**.
- Use a **public** repository, e.g. `https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World`, default
  branch `main`, and create it.
- Inside the cloud project, create one or more sessions -- **each provisions its own
  sandbox**. Create several to confirm N independent sandboxes.
- A brand-new session's terminal shows **"Connecting..."** for a few seconds
  (typically 4-6s: the sandbox template pre-bakes the worker binaries, the
  reconciler bootstraps in the provision tick, and the repo then checks out).
  A session occasionally takes 15-20s when the provider schedules its sandbox
  onto a host that has not cached the template yet (the pull happens inside the
  provider's create call); hosts warm up with use.
- **Orchestrator:** click the orchestrator button on the cloud project (sidebar
  hover, board CTA, or topbar). It spawns an orchestrator session **in its own
  sandbox** and opens its session view, exactly like a worker session (it must
  not land you in project settings -- that was the local-only fallback).

### GitHub / repositories

- **Public repos work** -- the sandbox worker clones them anonymously; no GitHub auth
  needed.
- **Private repos are not supported yet** (GitHub App integration is the follow-up).
  A private repo's worker cannot check out, so the session's worker never starts and
  its terminal keeps retrying "Connecting...". Use a public repo for now.

### Verify local is unchanged (toggle off)

Turn the Cloud toggle off (Settings > Advanced). `curl :3002/api/v1/settings` now
shows `"cloudEnabled": false`: the sidebar shows no cloud sign-in, cloud projects
disappear from the board, New Project shows no Cloud tab, and no control-plane
calls are made. The app is byte-for-byte the local app (the daemon binary imports
zero cloud code). A fresh install is in this state by default.

### Troubleshooting

- **No Cloud toggle in Settings:** Developer Mode (Settings > Advanced) is off.
- **No "Sign in to AO Cloud":** the Cloud toggle is off, or `/settings` shows
  `cloudEnabled: false`.
- **Session create returns 422 `agent_provider_required`:** your org has no valid
  coding-agent connection yet -- connect one via the account menu dialog (step 4).
- **Terminal stuck on "Connecting..." past ~3 min:** the sandbox worker never
  started -- almost always a private repo (use a public one) or a stale/dead session.
- **Port already in use:** free `3000` / `3002` / `5173` (an installed build uses
  `:3001`, so it does not conflict with the dev build on `:3002`).

## Follow-ups

- Server-side entitlement: with the per-client env check removed from the gate,
  restrict who can actually use the hosted control plane on the server (org
  allowlist or entitlement flag) before widening distribution; per-org sandbox
  quotas are the current control.

- Connect latency (accepted at 4-7s median for now): the remaining levers are a
  warm sandbox pool (sub-2s and removes the cold-host tail), per-harness slim
  templates (~770MB vs 1.4GB, halves the tail), and asking NodeOps to
  pre-distribute the template fleet-wide.
- Republish the NodeOps sandbox template when a deploy changes `ao-worker` or the

title: fix: report live workspace branch in sessions
body:
## Summary

- resolve each active git session's branch from its managed worktree when assembling session read models
- keep the durable spawn-time branch as a fallback when the worktree is unavailable or detached
- validate the workspace path against AO's managed root before running the single read-only Git probe

## Root cause

`SessionMetadata.Branch` is captured when a session is spawned, but an agent or host can change the worktree branch directly with Git. Session GET/list responses continued projecting that seed value, so the API could report `ao/<session>/root` while the worktree and claimed PR were already on a feature branch.

The fix treats the checked-out branch as mutable external state and overlays it at service read-model assembly time. This also covers spawn, restore, and resume responses that use the same assembly path. It does not perform a checkout or mutate SQLite.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/service/session ./internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree ./internal/daemon -count=1` (pass)

  - fake-agent lifecycle hook log is not created in the container
  - mobilebridge chmod-based write-failure tests run as container root and remain writable

No frontend or API schema shape changes are required.

title: optimisation on the events and sessions data to avoid failures
bug(chat): structured sessions never receive their browser capability
body:
## Bug

Chat-mode sessions launch their structured provider controller with `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` explicitly empty and never persist a `browser_capability_verifier`. As a result, `ao browser` and capability-protected preview-server commands fail for every Chat worker even when the current bundled rewrite binary and Electron browser runtime support them.

**Source:** Independently reproduced in disposable AO-managed Chat session `agent-orchestrator-214` while reassessing the externally hosted process attached to session `agent-orchestrator-211` (211 was not contacted or modified)  
**Reported:** 2026-08-25  
**Analyzed against:** [`dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99) (`origin/main`, exact match to the triage checkout)  
**AO version:** freshly built rewrite CLI reports `dev`; bundled daemon reports `dev` and SHA-256 `3bb56a325b7e10ff35560386e118b2a5d2b7c258724c1f7cc9c586d89e251fb3`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, Go `1.26.4`, daemon healthy/ready on port `3001`  
**Confidence:** **High** — reproduced with an explicit current rewrite binary and traced through issuance, persistence, provider-env injection, authorization, tests, and introducing history.  
**Priority:** **P2** — browser automation is unavailable to all Chat sessions; switching/creating as TUI is a bounded workaround.

## Scope correction: managed Chat vs externally hosted process

Session `agent-orchestrator-211` does **not** establish this managed-Chat defect. Its durable AO row is `tui`, has nonempty runtime handle/launch IDs, and already stores a 43-character browser verifier. The process reporting the missing environment variable is a separately hosted `node_repl` process carrying AO session/worktree context, not the AO-managed TUI runtime that received the launch credential. A recovered/stale bearer presented from that external process correctly failed with `BROWSER_CAPABILITY_INVALID`.

AO has no repository-owned refresh/delegation endpoint that can safely disclose a new bearer to an already-running arbitrary external process, and possession of `AO_SESSION_ID` alone must not authorize browser control. Whether hosted-process attachment should gain a separate authenticated capability-delegation protocol is outside this issue and requires an explicit security design.

This issue remains valid and is scoped only to **AO-managed structured Chat controllers**, independently proven by session `agent-orchestrator-214`: it was created through `ao spawn --mode chat`, has provider conversation and controller generation IDs, has no terminal runtime IDs, received commands through the durable Chat conversation, and reproduced both an empty verifier and missing environment bearer.

## Reproduction

1. Build the exact current rewrite CLI and verify it is talking to the Go daemon, not a legacy PATH binary:

   ```sh
   git checkout dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99
   (cd backend && go build -o /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro ./cmd/ao)
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro version
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro status --json
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro browser --help
   ```

   Observed: version `dev`; daemon state `ready`, health `ok`, port `3001`; `browser` includes `status`, `open`, `snapshot`, and the other current commands.

2. Spawn a fresh disposable Chat worker using the same absolute binary:

   ```sh
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro spawn \
     --project agent-orchestrator \
     --name triage-chat-browser \
     --harness codex \
     --mode chat \
     --prompt 'Report whether AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY is set, then run /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro browser status.'
   ```

3. The fresh controller reports:

   ```text
   AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY=unset
   ao browser requires the owning session capability (AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY is not set)
   ```

   The absolute rewrite command exits `2`.

4. Inspect only verifier lengths, never credential values:

   ```sql
   SELECT id, session_mode, length(browser_capability_verifier)
   FROM sessions
   WHERE id = '<fresh-chat-session>';
   ```

   Observed for disposable `agent-orchestrator-214`: `chat | 0`. Existing TUI rows launched on the same daemon have verifier length `43`.

The disposable session was terminated after reproduction.

## Expected

Every AO-managed Chat controller should receive a fresh, unguessable, session-scoped browser bearer in its own provider/runtime environment, while only the one-way verifier is durably stored before the worker can present the token. The owning Chat worker should pass `ao browser status`; another session, a stale launch token, an empty token, and a terminated session should remain unauthorized.

## Root cause

The shared environment builder intentionally clears all browser credentials:

- [`runtimeEnv`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3773-L3796) sets `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY`, `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN`, and `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_STDIN` to empty values.
- [`launchRuntimeEnv`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3799-L3813) is the only layer that calls the browser authority, injects the bearer, and returns its verifier.
- [`persistBrowserCapabilityVerifier`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3815-L3830) stores the verifier before process launch to close the eager-worker authorization race.

TUI spawn and restore use the secure launch path and persist the verifier:

- [TUI spawn](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L899-L905)
- [TUI restore](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1978-L1985)

Every structured-controller launch bypasses it:

- [fresh Chat spawn](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go#L128-L147) calls `runtimeEnv` and passes the cleared map to `StartChat`;
- [Chat restore/reconcile](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go#L290-L329) repeats the same call;
- [direct Chat agent switching](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/agent_switching_chat.go#L27-L40) builds the target environment with `runtimeEnv` and later hands that map to the target `StartChat`.

The provider layer faithfully passes `cfg.Env` into both driver start and resume, so the credential is already absent before the Codex/ACP boundary: [chat service dispatch](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/service/chat/service.go#L340-L370).

Authorization then correctly rejects the request because Chat has neither half of the split credential: [browser service authorization](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/service/browser/service.go#L77-L94).

### History

[PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) introduced Chat on 2026-08-06 with `runtimeEnv` as its environment seam. [PR #3473](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3473), merged on 2026-08-08 as commit [`c9e1c676b`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/c9e1c676baee8ab2e860a8110f2539a460e73a11), split browser credentials into an ephemeral bearer plus durable verifier and changed the terminal spawn/restore paths to `launchRuntimeEnv`; it did not update the already separate Chat launch paths. `git blame` still attributes both Chat calls to PR #3472.

## Affected modes and paths

- **Affected:** fresh Chat sessions for every harness whose structured driver receives `ChatStart.Env` (confirmed live with Codex; generic code path also covers ACP Chat drivers).
- **Affected:** Chat controller resume/reconcile after daemon/controller recovery.
- **Affected:** TUI → Chat interface transitions and Chat source rollback paths that relaunch through `resumeChatController`.
- **Affected:** Chat → Chat agent switching and its target/recovery launches.
- **Not affected:** normal TUI spawn/restore, which already issue, persist, and inject the credential.

## Security requirements for the fix

This is an authorization-availability omission, not evidence of an auth bypass. The existing boundary must remain intact:

- mint a fresh random bearer for each controller launch and bind its verifier to the AO session ID;
- persist **only** the one-way verifier before the provider process can run an eager browser command;
- inject the bearer only into the owning Chat provider environment; never store it in SQLite, metadata/DTO JSON, logs, error envelopes, conversation events, or frontend state;
- continue clearing privileged `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN*` values so the Electron runtime credential cannot leak to a worker;
- rotate on relaunch so stale controller tokens fail, and preserve cross-session rejection;
- sequence rotation correctly during interface/agent switching: do not invalidate a still-live source controller prematurely, and ensure rollback/recovery receives a newly matching token/verifier pair;
- do not weaken browser/preview authorization or introduce a global/shared capability to make Chat pass.

The current domain field is already `json:"-"`, and the authority uses constant-time comparison with a verifier bound to the session ID; those properties should remain unchanged.

## Required tests

1. Fresh Chat spawn issues exactly one pair, persists the verifier before `StartChat`, injects a nonempty bearer into `ChatStart.Env`, retains the verifier through `ControllerReady`, and authorizes only that session.
2. Project/inherited env cannot supply or override `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` or either privileged browser-runtime secret.
3. Issuer failure or empty credentials aborts Chat spawn before controller start and exercises the existing workspace/session rollback contract.
4. Chat resume/reconcile rotates the pair before provider resume; the new bearer succeeds and the old bearer fails.
5. TUI → Chat transition, Chat → Chat agent switch, source rollback, and restart recovery each end with one matching bearer/verifier pair without invalidating a still-running source during a reversible phase.
6. Cross-session, empty, stale, and terminated-session capabilities remain rejected; no bearer appears in stored session records, API responses, logs, or durable conversation events.
7. End-to-end regression: start the desktop/browser runtime, spawn a fresh Chat worker with an explicit rewrite binary on `:3001`, and verify `ao browser status` succeeds without relying on PATH.

Current tests cover `launchRuntimeEnv` and browser authorization in isolation, and Chat tests assert only that a generic env/session ID reaches the controller. No test asserts issuance or verifier persistence for Chat.

## PATH shadowing is separate

A bare `ao browser status` in the disposable worker also resolved to a legacy binary and returned `unknown command "browser"`. That is **not** the cause established here: the same worker reproduced the missing-capability error with the absolute current rewrite binary. This report therefore does not combine the capability defect with legacy/PATH pinning behavior.

## Recommended implementation scope

Introduce one controller-launch credential preparation boundary shared by fresh Chat launch, Chat resume/reconcile, interface transition, and Chat agent switching. It should return the provider env plus verifier, durably establish the verifier at the correct lifecycle/saga boundary before `StartChat`, preserve/rotate it through controller commits, and explicitly model rollback/recovery ordering. Reuse the existing authority and storage column; no schema/API relaxation should be necessary.

This is not a trivial one-line fix because agent/interface switching has reversible pre-stop phases and post-stop rollback/recovery. No speculative fix PR was opened during triage.

## Verification performed

```text
go build ./...                                                        PASS
go test ./internal/session_manager -run 'Test(RuntimeEnv|ChatSpawnStartsControllerAndNoRuntime|ResumeExitedChatSessionDoesNotRequireTerminalRuntimeHandle)' -count=1  PASS
go test ./internal/service/browser -count=1                          PASS
```

## Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY`, `browser_capability_verifier`, `owning session capability`, `chat ao browser`, `chat browser automation`, and `session owned browser`. No duplicate report or fix was found.

## Related

- [Issue #3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — Chat/TUI architecture and lifecycle invariants.
- [PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) — introduced the structured Chat controller paths.
- [PR #3473](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3473) — introduced session-owned browser automation and the split bearer/verifier security model.

title: fix(chat): surface normalized provider error detail and action link
body:
Fixes #4431

## Problem

`providerErrorCopy()` already unwraps Codex JSON error envelopes (including truncated, `provider error: `-prefixed ones) and returns `{ headline, detail }`, where `detail` carries the actionable part — e.g. "You have no credits remaining. Add credits to continue using the API at https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing". But `ErrorActivityRow` destructured only `headline`, so users saw the generic reconnect copy while the recovery action was silently dropped. The tests explicitly asserted that absence.

## Change

- **`ErrorActivityRow`** now renders:
  - the headline (in its own span, keeping it a single text node for queries),
  - the normalized `detail` as escaped plain text below it — unknown/untrusted provider text stays inert,
  - a constrained action link when one applies.
- **New `providerErrorAction()` helper**: scans detail for URLs but only linkifies an allow-listed host + exact path (`platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing` → "Add credits"). Arbitrary provider URLs are never made clickable (no phishing surface); look-alike paths on the real host do not trigger the action. Links open via the existing `openLinkInSystemBrowser` external-link policy.
- **Tests** flipped from asserting the credits detail is absent to asserting it renders with the correct `href`, plus two new cases: an unknown host's URL stays non-clickable, and a look-alike billing path produces no action.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/ChatProviderSignal.test.tsx` — 35 passed
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat` — 20 files, 340 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck` — only the pre-existing `motion/react` error in `packages/product-ui`, which reproduces on clean `main` and is unrelated to this change.

title: fix(chat): require consent before interrupting busy work
body: Closes #4423 ## Summary - require an explicit **Finish work** versus **Stop now** choice before a busy or uncertain Chat session switches to Terminal UI - keep ordinary sends plus Claude Edit/Retry work scoped to the initiating session from pending request through exact durable-turn observation - preserve accepted and in-flight work across navigation, same-route rerenders, and full Chat-surface unmount/remount - scope transition start/cancel/ack mutations, pending state, errors, and cache invalidation to their initiating session, including overlapping mutations in multiple sessions - prevent a deferred transition for session A from closing a newer consent dialog for session B - suppress rapid duplicate composer submissions without hiding genuine transport failures - retain the safe direct-drain path for confirmed-idle work ## Root cause and final review fix Chat-to-Terminal previously submitted destructive `interrupt` immediately, before asking the user whether active and queued work could be cancelled. During final independent review, a second race was found: each TanStack `MutationObserver` remembered only its most recent mutation. If session A started a transition, session B then started another, and the user returned to A, A could appear idle while its request was still pending. The final commit keys start/cancel/ack mutations and aggregates pending/error state by target session. Its public-hook regression was proven red before the fix and green afterward. ## Regression coverage MQA-05 and focused adversarial tests cover: - busy Chat showing the policy dialog before any transition request - **Finish work** waiting for running work before switching - **Stop now** interrupting only after explicit consent - pending and accepted Send/Edit/Retry work remaining busy through stale idle snapshots - accepted work remaining busy through full surface remount - in-flight requests remaining busy through a board round-trip - session navigation not transferring consent, pending state, errors, or cache invalidation - overlapping A/B transition mutations remaining independently pending - a deferred A completion not closing B's newer policy dialog - rapid double-submit invoking transport once ## Exact validation - product head: `ce9183ea87d18273efed6c6ac3b776fcab065927` - base: `be21597e7a24cbee2e6e9103ae669ff18c3b56b1` - opt-in harness head: `cc760a23ca74e8b110c12f11faa337064ca8d106` in draft PR #4419 - exact product+harness integration: `72c9e0f474cce9b709450a9fd7e28caefd2a6d02` - focused renderer tests: **222/222 passed** - full renderer: **3,013 passed, 1 intentional skip** - frontend typecheck: **passed** - E2E typecheck: **passed** - strict `MQA-05`: **2/2 passed** - backend suite: **passed** - GolangCI with an isolated cache: **0 issues** - `git diff --check`: **passed** - independent Standards review of the exact head: **approved, no findings** - independent Spec review of the exact head: **approved, no findings** - worktree: **clean** ## Native Electron evidence The real AO Electron app was exercised on macOS in isolated mode with `todo-app`, Codex, renderer `http://localhost:5173`, daemon `127.0.0.1:3002`, and AO state under `~/.ao/dev`. At `3e1d9cad0`, immediately before the final reviewer-only mutation-state commit: 1. a real Chat turn ran `sleep 30`; 2. clicking Terminal showed the required **Finish work** / **Stop now** dialog while the command was active; 3. **Finish work** kept Chat active until the command completed; 4. Terminal opened only afterward and displayed `QA_4423_EXACT_DONE` in the native conversation. The final `ce9183ea8` commit changes only session-keyed renderer mutation bookkeeping and its regression test; the complete focused/full/typecheck/strict-MQA matrix above was repeated on that exact head. **Busy Chat turn requires Finish/Stop consent** **Finish work completes before Terminal UI opens** **Returning to Chat shows the completed response in the earlier full round-trip capture** Local native screenshots remain under `~/.ao/qa/4423-native-3e1d9cad0/`; exact final strict artifacts remain under `~/.ao/qa/4423-mqa05-strict-ce9183ea8/`. They are outside the repository and uncommitted. ## Boundary Hard renderer reload/quit draft durability is owned by #4422. Within #4423 alone, a forced reload can lose richer renderer-local pending metadata, but it never grants interrupt consent: the automatic path remains drain-only. ## Harness separation This PR contains only the #4423 implementation and focused product tests. Draft PR #4419 owns the manually triggered ChatUI regression harness; it does not run automatically in CI. No screenshots, reports, traces, local AO state, or QA artifacts are committed. ## Review follow-up (`fb1bf9741`) The two remaining re-review edge cases are fixed on the latest `main`: - the accepted POST transition is written into the initiating session's cache before invalidation, so inactive queries or transient refetch failures cannot re-enable Chat controls while backend intake is fenced - transition settlement is keyed by session and transition, and each refresh has an attempt token; A → B → A navigation cannot leave settlement latched or let an older A refresh clear the restarted A settlement Added focused regressions for inactive invalidation, failed invalidation, navigation during settlement, and overlapping old/new settlement attempts. Exact-head validation: - hook regressions: **16/16 passed** - hook + SessionView matrix: **103/103 passed** - full renderer: **3,067 passed, 1 intentional skip** - frontend typecheck: **passed** - `git diff --check`: **passed** - mergeability against `main` at `5913376b1`: **MERGEABLE** - worktree: **clean** No screenshot, trace, report, or local evidence file is committed.

title: ci: guard the nightly feed head the way stable is guarded
body:
## Why

`release-latest-guard.yml` protects the stable channel from a `/releases/latest` that electron-updater cannot install from. Nightly had no equivalent, and nightly is the channel that actually breaks. Of the six nightlies cut between 2026-08-23 and 2026-08-25:

| Release | State | Manifests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v0.12.8-nightly.202608251410` | draft | **missing** |
| `v0.12.8-nightly.202608250759` | draft | ok |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608250031` | published | ok |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608242034` | **published** | **missing** |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608241447` | **published** | **missing** |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608241408` | published | ok |

Any one of these at the head of the feed strands **every** nightly install.

electron-updater discovers prereleases through `releases.atom`, takes the **first** entry matching the channel, fetches that release's manifest, and on 404 retries exactly one fallback before giving up. It never walks to the next entry. So one bad release at the top wedges every client even with a good release directly beneath it — which is the current state:

```
feed head:      v0.12.8-nightly.202608251410
  nightly-mac.yml -> 404
  latest-mac.yml  -> 404   (the single fallback)
  => ERR_UPDATER_CHANNEL_FILE_NOT_FOUND, gives up

one entry down: v0.12.7-nightly.202608250031
  nightly-mac.yml -> 200   (never reached)
```

The failure is invisible. Automatic check errors are suppressed by design, so affected installs show nothing at all and simply stop updating. On one machine this had been going on for two days across an app restart.

## What it does

Fails when the nightly feed head is a draft, or is missing `nightly.yml` / `nightly-mac.yml` / `nightly-linux.yml`, and says what to do about it.

It reads `releases.atom`, not the API, on purpose: the API omits drafts, the Atom feed lists them, and a draft's assets are not public, so a draft at the head 404s for everyone. Checking the API would miss exactly the case that broke this week.

Same shape as the stable guard: hourly schedule, release triggers, and the `github.repository` condition so forks do not fail red.

## Verified against the live feed

Ran the check logic against real releases:

- `v0.12.8-nightly.202608251410` (draft, no manifests) → **fails**, reports the draft
- `v0.12.7-nightly.202608242034` (published, no manifests) → **fails**, names the three missing files
- `v0.12.7-nightly.202608250031` → passes
- `v0.12.7-nightly.202608241408` → passes

So it catches both real failure modes and does not fire on healthy releases. Note this guard will fail on `main` until the current feed head is fixed — that is the point, not a defect in the workflow.

## Scope

This detects the breakage; it does not prevent it. Nightlies are cut by hand (`frontend-nightly.yml` was removed in #3070) and the manifest generation is a separate step from the artifact publish, which is what makes it easy to skip. Automating the nightly cut so the manifests cannot be forgotten is the real fix and is a larger change than this.

Related: #4397 and #4462 harden the client so it skips drafts and manifest-less releases and resolves to the newest installable one. This guards the release side; those guard the client side.

title: revert: isolate AO tmux state
body:
## Summary

- revert PR #4393 / merge commit `2aeba22c029bb6cf8980a1003ce39b2272b3bea1`
- restore the previous named `ao` tmux socket behavior for new desktop sessions
- restore legacy default-socket discovery for sessions created before that transition
- stop updates from stranding live default-socket sessions behind the hashed private socket boundary

## Incident rationale

Nightly users updating across #4393 retained live sessions on the legacy default tmux socket, while the updated daemon only classified sessions through its new hashed private socket. Reconciliation then treated the live sessions as missing and could relaunch duplicates. This revert returns to the last known-good runtime behavior while a larger terminal ownership/migration design is evaluated separately.

## Verification

title: bug(desktop): #4465's revert is backend-only — main.ts still sets AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME, so packaged builds still strand legacy default-socket sessions
body:
## Problem

#4465 reverted the backend half of the private-hashed-tmux-socket migration (#4393) — `runtimeselect.New()` now calls `tmux.New(tmux.Options{})` with no `SocketPath`, so `socketForSession`'s `r.socketName` is empty by default and legacy sessions are found directly on the machine's default socket.

However, the desktop Electron main process still independently opts every packaged launch back into the private socket:

```
frontend/src/main.ts:845
...(bundledTmuxBinary ? { AO_TMUX_BINARY: bundledTmuxBinary, AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME: "ao" } : {}),
```

`tmux.New` reads `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME` from the environment when `Options.SocketName` is empty (`tmux.go:287-289`), so any packaged desktop build with a staged bundled tmux binary — the common case — still runs with `socketName = "ao"`, and hits the exact symptom #4465 set out to fix.

## Reproduce

On a machine with tmux sessions that predate this whole migration (i.e. living only on the default socket):

```
$ /path/to/bundled/tmux -L ao has-session -t <session-id>
error connecting to /private/tmp/tmux-<uid>/ao (No such file or directory)

$ /path/to/bundled/tmux -L default has-session -t <session-id>
(exit 0 — session is alive)
```

`socketForSession` (`tmux.go`) only crosses the migration boundary to the legacy default socket when the private-socket probe output matches `sessionMissingOutput` ("can't find session"/"session not found") or `serverNotRunningOutput` ("no server running"). Neither matches "error connecting ... No such file or directory" — the exact message tmux gives when the private socket file was never created, which is guaranteed on first launch of a build with this env var reintroduced against pre-existing legacy sessions. The probe returns `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, and every legacy session's terminal pane shows "Terminal disconnected — reattaching…" indefinitely, with `reconcile: reap pass failed` / `reaper: probe error reported as failed fact` log spam for every session.

## Why this survived #4465's testing

#4465's revert is real and correct for the backend default, but its own repro/verification path (`env -u AO_TMUX_BINARY ... npm run lint` etc., per the PR body) unsets `AO_TMUX_BINARY`, which also disables the `bundledTmuxBinary` branch in `main.ts` that sets `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME`. So the revert's own verification never exercises the actual packaged-desktop code path where the symptom reappears.

## Fix options

- Drop the `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME: "ao"` half of `main.ts:845` (keep `AO_TMUX_BINARY` only) so the packaged desktop app matches the reverted backend default, or
- If the private socket is still wanted opportunistically from the desktop launcher, extend `socketForSession`'s migration-boundary check to also treat "error connecting ... no such file or directory" as definitive (this is what a private socket that was simply never created looks like — distinct from a running server going transiently unreachable, which the existing `transientServerFailureOutput`/#3475 guard is right to keep ambiguous).

## Verification after fix

On a machine with pre-existing default-socket sessions, launch the packaged desktop app and confirm the terminal pane attaches immediately instead of showing "Terminal disconnected — reattaching…", and `daemon.log` has no `reconcile reap ...: probe: ... liveness probe inconclusive: error connecting` entries for those sessions.

## Related
- #4465 (this issue's cause — the backend-only revert)
- #4393 (original migration)

title: bug(chat): selected composer text has no visible highlight
body:
## Bug

Dragging across text already typed into the Chat composer creates a real DOM selection, but the highlight is effectively invisible. Users cannot tell which part of a draft is selected before replacing, cutting, or copying it.

**Source:** AO chat report on 2026-08-26 | **Analyzed against:** `c4abb8afc4a305fbd20c6d3955a2c7808d78e7d4` | **AO version:** `dev` (desktop `0.10.3`)
**OS reproduced on:** macOS 26.5, arm64 | **Daemon:** ready on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Priority:** P2 — draft editing is significantly degraded; keyboard-only selection is possible but still has no visual confirmation.
**Confidence:** High — the exact pointer path is automated, the DOM range remains non-collapsed, and the rendered selection/surface contrast is measured.

## Reproduction

1. Open a Chat-mode session with an existing conversation.
2. Type a multi-word draft in the composer.
3. Drag the pointer across part or all of the draft.
4. Observe that no visible highlight appears, even though `window.getSelection()` contains a non-collapsed range.

The focused Playwright reproduction types a wrapped draft, drag-selects it through actual pointer events, verifies the DOM selection, then measures the composited selection-highlight contrast. On current `main` it fails:

```text
Expected: >= 1.5
Received:    1.013160847557346
```

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ComposerEditor.tsx` styles selected text with:

```text
selection:bg-accent/30
```

In Tailwind's theme bridge, `accent` is the subtle surface token (`--accent`), not the stronger product accent. In the light theme it is `oklch(0.967 0.001 286.375)` over the composer's `oklch(0.985 0 0)` card surface. At 30% alpha the composited contrast is only `1.013:1`, so the browser paints a valid selection that looks unselected.

This was introduced with the Lexical composer in [PR #4331](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4331), commit `b8e3d57f25`.

## Fix

Use a theme-aware foreground/primary selection tint with enough alpha to remain visibly distinct from the composer surface, and keep an E2E regression that proves both:

- pointer drag creates a durable selection of the typed draft;
- the composited highlight/surface contrast is at least `1.5:1`.

## Evidence

Before — the draft is selected in the DOM, but no highlight is perceptible:

![Before: invisible chat composer selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-composer-selection-visibility/.issue-assets/chat-composer-selection-visibility/before.png)

After — the same automated pointer selection is visibly highlighted:

![After: visible chat composer selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-composer-selection-visibility/.issue-assets/chat-composer-selection-visibility/after.png)

## Impact

- Users cannot safely replace or cut a portion of a drafted instruction.
- Copy/cut may operate on text with no visible confirmation of the range.
- The failure looks like pointer selection is broken even though the browser selection model is working.

## Related

- [#4268](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4268) — read-only surfaces inherit `user-select: none`; adjacent symptom, different mechanism. The composer already computes `user-select: text`.
- [PR #4443](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4443) — restores selection on read-only content surfaces; it does not change the composer's selection highlight.

title: fix(chat): make composer selection visible
body:

## TDD reproduction

Before the styling change, the new test reproduced the report: the pointer drag selected the text, but the original composited highlight contrast was only 1.013:1.

The final `selection:bg-foreground selection:text-background` pair gives the limiting Solarized dark case 4.111:1 highlight-to-surface contrast and 4.748:1 selected-text-to-highlight contrast.

title: feat(mobile): over-the-air JS updates via EAS Update
body:
## What

Adds `expo-updates` + EAS Update so JS-only changes reach installed builds without a store release. Native changes still go through the store.

- Cold start: checks in the background, applies on the next launch. Never blocks the splash.
- Back from 15+ minutes in the background: applies a downloaded update (a JS reload; sessions live in the daemon), otherwise checks silently. Same as Bluesky / CodePush `ON_NEXT_RESUME`. Shorter absences do nothing, so nobody is reloaded mid-prompt. No banner.
- Settings → About → App updates: manual check / restart. Version row and bug reports now carry update id, channel and runtime; the build number is read from the binary (with `appVersionSource: remote` the old row had none).
- Dev builds: `expo-updates` is disabled, so all of this is inert.

## Runtime version

`fingerprint` rather than `appVersion`: native modules have landed on `main` between version stamps, and a fingerprint makes any native change a new runtime automatically, so an update can't reach a build that lacks the native code it calls. `fingerprint.config.js` ignores `google-services.json`, which is gitignored and differs between a laptop, CI and EAS Build; without that the Android hash differs per machine. Verified with `runtimeversion:resolve`.

## Privacy

Each check sends platform, runtime, channel, current update id and a random per-install UUID (`EAS-Client-ID`) to `u.expo.dev`. No user or daemon data. The store privacy policy should name Expo before the next store build.

## Activation

Nothing happens until a build with this config exists. Publishing is a local, deliberate step (`eas update --channel <c> --environment <c> -m "..."`, see the README); there is no CI publish and no Expo token in the repo.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (495, 18 new); `npx expo export` for both platforms
- Release builds on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator, against a local expo-updates protocol server: cold-start download, applied on the next launch, still running after the server reports no update. On iOS a deliberately broken bundle rolled back to the embedded one.
- The Android build's runtime version matched `runtimeversion:resolve` (`2bdcb69b…`) with the placeholder `google-services.json` in place, so the ignore in `fingerprint.config.js` holds end to end
- Debug build: no requests, row reads "Off in development builds"
- Not tried on a device: the 15-minute resume path (unit-tested)

title: feat(windows,shell-terminals): selectable default shell for standalone terminals (Git Bash, PowerShell, cmd)
body:
## Feature Description

On Windows, standalone shell terminals always launch whichever shell the daemon finds first in a **hardcoded probe order** — `pwsh.exe` → `powershell.exe` → `ComSpec` → `cmd.exe`. There is no way for the user to choose a different default shell, and **Git Bash is never considered at all**.

Requested: a user-facing option (app setting and/or per-terminal picker) to select the default shell for standalone terminals, with Git Bash as a first-class choice alongside PowerShell / cmd.

## Current behavior (code anchors)

- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/loginshell.go` — `resolveUserLoginShell()` → `resolveWindowsShell()`: hardcoded candidate list `["pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe"]` then `ComSpec`/`cmd.exe` fallback. No user preference is consulted, no Git Bash probe (e.g. `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`), no override hook.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` — `OpenShellTerminalInput` has no shell/shellPath field, so `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` cannot express a shell choice per open request either.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` (`runLoginShell`, ~line 635) — login-shell env detection runs a shell too; a changed default should be honored consistently there.
- Unix already prefers `$SHELL` (`loginshell.go:24`), which is why this reads as Windows-only — but note the Unix sibling bug with non-POSIX shells: #3788 (fish).

## Motivation

- Reported by a Windows user who lives in Git Bash: **SahilG** in the `#feature-requests` Discord thread *"default terminal option"* — currently the **most upvoted feature request** there.
- Git Bash is a daily-driver shell for many Windows developers; getting PowerShell instead makes the standalone terminal pane a pane they immediately `exit` out of.
- PowerShell-first probe order also surprises cmd users the same way (SahilG perceived "only cmd is supported" — either way, the user loses).

## Proposed Solution

1. **Setting:** add a `shell` preference (e.g. `"auto" | "git-bash" | "pwsh" | "powershell" | "cmd" | custom path`) to app settings, surfaced in the desktop app's Settings UI.
2. **Resolution order:** `resolveUserLoginShell()` should consult the preference first; `"auto"` keeps today's behavior. Git Bash detection: `where git` → `<Git>\bin\bash.exe` (or `bash.exe` on PATH), launched with `--login -i`.
3. **Wire API:** optionally extend `OpenShellTerminalInput` with an optional per-request `shell` override so the UI can offer a per-terminal picker (⊞ new-terminal dropdown) without extra round-trips.
4. **Validation:** reject-with-message or fall back to `auto` when the configured shell path doesn't exist at open time (consistent with the "must not open something unusable" rule in `loginshell.go:17-19`).
5. **Regenerate API artifacts** (`npm run api`) if DTOs change.

## Alternatives Considered

- Environment-variable-only override (e.g. `AO_SHELL`) — cheap but undiscoverable; fine as a power-user extra, not a substitute for a setting.
- Doing nothing / documenting PowerShell-first — rejected: most-upvoted request, and the fix is well-bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Windows user can set Git Bash as the default shell; new standalone terminals launch in Git Bash (`--login -i`)
- [ ] PowerShell (pwsh + Windows PowerShell) and cmd remain selectable; `"auto"` preserves current behavior
- [ ] Custom shell path supported, with clear error/fallback when it's missing
- [ ] Preference honored by the login-shell env detection path (`runLoginShell`), not just terminal spawn
- [ ] Unix behavior unchanged (`$SHELL` still wins)
- [ ] OpenAPI spec + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated if request DTOs change

## Environment

- OS: Windows (feature is Windows-facing; Unix already honors `$SHELL`)
- Surface: standalone shell terminals (`/terminals` screen) — shellterm service → daemon → ConPTY

_Filed from Discord thread "default terminal option" (#feature-requests). Reporter: @SahilG; picked up by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari._

title: bug(kimi): OAuth worker starts without model in AO-managed home
body:
## Bug

AO-managed Kimi TUI workers can start without a model and reject the injected task with:

```text
Error: LLM not set, send /login to login
```

The same Kimi binary works when launched manually in the same worktree. This affects the normal Kimi device-code OAuth profile shape: `config.toml` has a `default_model`, provider/OAuth mapping, and model definitions, while the provider `api_key` is intentionally empty and tokens are stored in the referenced credential JSON.

**Source:** live same-machine reproduction in AO worker `reverb-45` on 2026-08-26  
**Analyzed against:** `c4abb3d0e` (`origin/main`)  
**AO:** packaged Go daemon `0.12.7-nightly.202608250031` on `127.0.0.1:3001` (CLI version currently reports `dev`)  
**Kimi:** `0.38.0`, macOS arm64  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced and traced to the exact config-seeding predicate  
**Priority:** P1 — the normal OAuth-backed Kimi worker path is unusable until the managed profile is manually repaired

## Reproduction

1. Authenticate native Kimi with its device-code OAuth flow.
2. Confirm the native Kimi profile contains a non-empty `default_model`, a provider with an OAuth credential reference, model definitions, and usable access/refresh credentials, but no non-empty literal `api_key`.
3. Spawn an AO Kimi worker with a non-empty task.
4. Observe that Kimi starts with no LLM, rejects the task with `Error: LLM not set, send /login to login`, and the AO session later derives `no_signal`.
5. Run plain `kimi` manually from the same worktree; it loads the native model/profile successfully.

No credential values need to be logged or exposed to reproduce this.

## Root Cause

AO intentionally isolates Kimi under its own data directory:

1. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/kimi.go` sets `KIMI_CODE_HOME=<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi` for managed launches.
2. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/hooks.go:installKimiConfigHooks` prepares `<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi/config.toml` and merges AO lifecycle hooks.
3. `seedKimiCredentials` can securely copy a usable native OAuth credential into the isolated home on first use.
4. `kimiSeedConfig`, however, copies the matching native `config.toml` only when `kimiConfigHasAPIKey(source)` finds a non-empty literal `api_key`.
5. Device-code OAuth profiles intentionally keep authentication in `credentials/kimi-code.json`; their config still carries the required `default_model`, provider/OAuth mapping, aliases, services, permissions, and model tables. The API-key-only predicate rejects that config.

The result is an inconsistent managed profile: AO has a credential and its four lifecycle hooks, but no default model or provider/model graph. Kimi therefore reports an unset LLM before it can create a native session or emit AO lifecycle hooks. `no_signal` is a downstream symptom, not a dead-process or readiness-classification bug.

Sanitized local evidence:

- native `~/.kimi-code/config.toml`: keys include `default_model`, `providers`, `models`, `services`, `permission`; the managed provider has an OAuth reference and no non-empty API key
- AO `<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi/config.toml`: contains only the four AO-managed hook entries
- both credential files exist with mode `0600`; values were not printed or compared in this report
- the AO daemon is healthy on port 3001 and the Kimi process remains live

## Correct Fix and Security/State Behavior

When the AO target config is empty or contains only AO's managed hook block, seed the **complete native config** if either:

- it has a non-empty literal API key (existing behavior), or
- its declared OAuth credential reference resolves to a locally usable access/refresh credential.

Then merge exactly one AO-managed hook block as before.

Copying the whole config is deliberate: selectively copying `default_model` would risk separating it from its provider, OAuth storage reference, model aliases, services, permissions, and related settings. This matches the existing first-use behavior for API-key profiles.

Security/state invariants:

- Keep `KIMI_CODE_HOME` under `AO_DATA_DIR`; do **not** point managed sessions at or write hooks into the native profile.
- Copy secrets only into the AO-managed home with owner-only permissions; never log or commit credential contents.
- Preserve native config/credentials byte-for-byte.
- Preserve any AO config containing non-hook user state; only merge/update AO's owned hook block.
- Preserve an existing AO-managed credential rather than overwriting an independently refreshed or explicitly logged-in managed profile.
- Do not seed OAuth-shaped config when its referenced credential is missing or unusable.

## Remaining Limitations

- Native and AO-managed credentials intentionally diverge after first seeding. If the managed credential later becomes unusable, the user must log in within the managed Kimi profile (or deliberately remove it to allow first-use reseeding); AO should not silently overwrite an existing managed secret from the native profile.
- OAuth configurations whose real token lives only in an external store and cannot be positively verified from the referenced local credential remain outside this fix; that advisory-auth variant is tracked separately in #4031.

## Duplicate Search / Related

No exact issue was found after searching all open and closed issues for the error text, `Model: not set`, `KIMI_CODE_HOME`, `default_model`, OAuth config seeding, and managed Kimi login failures.

- #4031 is related but not a duplicate: it covers OAuth configurations with empty local token fields/external storage where AO reports auth unknown or unauthorized. Here the local credential is usable and AO can report `authorized`; launch fails because the matching model/provider config is not seeded.
- PR #2960 identified the same config-seeding gap, but is currently conflicting with `main`, has no closing issue, and includes storage-layout follow-up changes beyond this exact reproduction. A current-main surgical PR should supersede only the missing OAuth-config predicate/test coverage.
- PR #3648 added first-use OAuth credential copying while intentionally preserving existing managed credentials; it did not retain OAuth profile-config seeding.

## Impact

- OAuth-authenticated Kimi installs can appear ready but fail every AO-managed task before creating a session.
- Workers can remain live while surfacing `no_signal`, obscuring the actual missing-model cause.
- Manual `kimi` remains functional, which makes the failure look terminal- or worktree-specific when it is actually managed-profile inconsistency.

title: fix(kimi): seed OAuth config into managed home
body:
## What

Seed the user's complete native Kimi config and its exact referenced OAuth credential into AO's isolated Kimi home when the source profile uses device-code OAuth, not only when it contains a non-empty literal `api_key`.

The change keeps the existing first-use boundary: only an empty or AO-hook-only managed config is seedable, after which AO merges exactly one lifecycle-hook block.

Fixes #4520.

This is a surgical current-`main` replacement for the remaining config-seeding delta in #2960, which is currently conflicting and also carries broader storage-layout work. Original contributor @serhatsayat is credited in the commit.

## Why

AO worker `reverb-45` reproduced the failure on current `main`: Kimi `0.38.0` launched by AO displayed `Error: LLM not set, send /login to login`, while the same binary launched manually in the same worktree loaded its model and worked.

### RCA

AO deliberately launches Kimi with `KIMI_CODE_HOME=<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi` so lifecycle hooks and Kimi state remain isolated under `~/.ao`. Hook preparation already copied a usable native OAuth credential into that home, but `kimiSeedConfig` accepted the matching native `config.toml` only when `kimiConfigHasAPIKey(source)` found a non-empty literal API key.

Kimi's device-code OAuth profile intentionally has empty API-key fields. Its config still carries the required `default_model`, provider/OAuth mapping, model aliases, services, permissions, and model definitions. The API-key-only gate therefore produced an inconsistent managed profile:

- credential: present
- AO lifecycle hooks: present
- default model/provider/model graph: missing

Kimi rejected AO's injected task before creating a native session or emitting lifecycle hooks, so `no_signal` was a downstream symptom rather than a process crash or readiness bug.

The regression is the untested intersection of two existing paths: API-key profile-config seeding and OAuth credential seeding.

## How

- If the native config has a non-empty API key, preserve the existing path.
- Otherwise, parse each provider OAuth reference, resolve it through Kimi's existing `kimiOAuthCredentialPath` mapping, and positively verify the exact referenced access/refresh credential before seeding the native config.
- Copy usable referenced credentials to their matching AO-managed paths; retain `credentials/kimi-code.json` only as a legacy fallback when no OAuth reference was persisted. An unrelated default credential is not copied when the config references a scoped key.
- Copy the complete config rather than cherry-picking `default_model`; the provider/OAuth reference, aliases, services, permissions, and model definitions form one internally consistent profile.
- Merge AO's hook block exactly once.

### Intentional security/state behavior

- `KIMI_CODE_HOME` remains under `AO_DATA_DIR`; managed sessions never point at or write hooks into the native `~/.kimi-code` profile.
- Credential contents are neither logged nor committed. First-use copies continue to be written owner-only (`0600`) inside AO-managed state.
- Native config and credentials remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Any AO config containing non-hook state is preserved; only AO's owned hook block is merged/updated.
- An existing AO-managed credential is never overwritten. This preserves an independent managed login or a token that Kimi refreshed inside the isolated profile.
- A token-less/missing native credential does not make an empty-key profile seedable.

### Intentional limitations

- Native and AO-managed credentials can diverge after first seeding. If an existing managed credential later becomes unusable, the user must log in within the managed Kimi profile or deliberately remove it to allow first-use reseeding; AO does not silently overwrite an existing managed secret.
- OAuth profiles whose usable token exists only in an external credential store and cannot be positively verified from local credential JSON remain outside this change; the advisory-auth variant is tracked by #4031.
- Existing AO configs with non-hook content are not repaired or replaced automatically, even if they are incomplete.

## Testing

The original OAuth regression tests and the scoped-reference review tests were run against their respective old gates and failed for the expected missing-config/missing-credential reasons; they pass with the fixes.

- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/adapters/agent/kimi -count=1`
- `cd backend && go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/kimi`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/registry ./internal/session_manager -count=1`
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" npm run lint`
  - full `go test ./...`
  - golangci-lint v2.12.2: `0 issues`
- `git diff --check`

Coverage verifies:

- OAuth config + first-use credential seeding into an empty managed home
- recovery from the exact hook-only managed config state in the reproduction
- complete default-model/provider/OAuth/model graph preservation
- exactly one AO hook block
- native config and credential immutability
- preservation of an existing, divergent AO-managed credential
- scoped OAuth keys such as `oauth/kimi-code-env-<hash>` with and without an unrelated default credential
- copying only credentials referenced by the seeded config

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Focused regression tests added with a verified red-green cycle
- [x] Relevant backend tests, build, vet, and lint pass

title: Merge-conflict nudge does not re-fire after conflict is resolved and later returns
body:
## Bug

AO notifies a worker the first time a tracked PR becomes conflicting, but does not notify it when that conflict is resolved and a later base-branch advance makes the same PR conflicting again.

**Reported from:** AO worker session `agent-orchestrator-149` while handling PR #4165
**Observed:** 2026-08-26
**Analyzed against:** `4cbb4b6ce`
**AO:** locally built `dev`, daemon healthy on port 3001
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — missed automation notification; the user can manually steer the worker as a workaround.

## Reproduction

1. Track an open PR owned by a live worker session.
2. Make the PR conflicting and allow the SCM observer to deliver the merge-conflict nudge.
3. Rebase the PR so it is clean/mergeable.
4. Advance the base branch so the same PR becomes conflicting again.
5. Observe that AO does not deliver a second merge-conflict nudge.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go` queues merge-conflict nudges with key `merge-conflict:<pr-url>` and the constant signature `conflicting`. `sendOnce` persists that key/signature in `pr.last_nudge_signature`.

A later non-conflicting observation does not clear or re-arm the merge-conflict dedup entry. When conflict returns, `sendOnce` sees the same key/signature and treats it as already delivered. The persisted state makes the suppression survive daemon restarts.

Live state for PR #4165 confirmed:

- durable mergeability: `conflicting`
- seen signature: `merge-conflict:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4165 = conflicting`
- attempts: `1`

This exactly explains why the first conflict notification arrived and the later one did not.

## Fix

Re-arm the merge-conflict reaction after a definitive non-conflicting observation (but not an `unknown` transient): remove/reset that PR-specific seen signature and attempt count, persist the updated reaction payload, and add lifecycle plus observer integration coverage for:

`mergeable -> conflicting (notify) -> mergeable (re-arm) -> conflicting (notify again)`

Identical consecutive conflicting observations must remain deduplicated, including across daemon restart.
