title: [Bug]: `ao spawn --model X` records an empty model — mergeMetadata drops Metadata.Model
body:
### Summary

`ao spawn --model <model>` succeeds, but the session records no model at all. The `sessions.model` column is written as the empty string and `GET /api/v1/sessions` omits the field, so nothing can report which model a session resolved to.

The agent itself launches correctly — this is a record/read-back defect, not a launch defect.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
export AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-model AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/ao-model/running.json AO_PORT=3095
mkdir -p "$AO_DATA_DIR"
cd backend && go run ./cmd/ao daemon
```

In a second shell, register any git repo with a resolvable default branch and spawn with an explicit model:

```bash
cd backend
go run ./cmd/ao project add --path /path/to/a/git/repo --id demo --name demo
go run ./cmd/ao spawn --project demo --harness claude-code --skip-agent-check \
  --mode tui --name m1 --model sonnet

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3095/api/v1/sessions | grep -o '"model":"[^"]*"'   # no output
sqlite3 "$AO_DATA_DIR/ao.db" "SELECT id, quote(model) FROM sessions;"
```

### Expected behavior

The resolved model is recorded and read back:

```
demo-1|'sonnet'
"model":"sonnet"
```

`domain.SessionMetadata.Model` documents exactly this — *"the agent model this session resolved to at spawn time, including any per-spawn --model override"* — and the schema carries a dedicated `model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` column for it.

### Actual behavior

```
demo-1|''
```

and the API response has no `model` key.

### Root cause

`session_manager` builds the spawn metadata with `Model: resolvedModelForMetadata(...)` and hands it to `MarkSpawned`, which merges it into the existing row:

```go
rec.Metadata = mergeMetadata(rec.Metadata, metadata)
```

`seedRecord` never sets `Model`, so the base side is empty. `mergeMetadata` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go`) copies seventeen fields by an explicit allowlist and `Model` is not among them, so the empty base value wins and the resolved model is discarded.

This is the failure mode the package already documents. `TestMarkSpawnedPersistsChatControllerFacts` carries this comment:

> mergeMetadata is an explicit allowlist, so a field added to SessionMetadata without a line here is silently dropped on every spawn and restore. That happened to the chat resume handle: the provider still held the conversation, but AO forgot its id, so no restart could ever resume it — and nothing failed loudly, the column was just empty.

`Model` is the same omission one field over.

### Scope

Only two things read `Metadata.Model` — the session DTO (`httpd/controllers/sessions.go`) and the `sessions.model` column (`storage/sqlite/store/session_store.go`). No relaunch or resume path consumes it, so no session has been running the wrong model; the value is simply never recorded.

### AO version

Built from source at `dbd87a21e` (current `main`).

### Environment

Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3, x86_64, Go 1.25.12, tmux 3.7c.

### Logs / extra context

Found by running the daemon against an isolated data dir and cross-referencing the observed behaviour with the code path. Happy to open a PR — the fix is one line in the copy-if-non-empty group, plus a regression test.

title: fix(lifecycle): carry the resolved model through mergeMetadata
body:
## What

Adds the missing `Model` line to `mergeMetadata`, so a spawn's resolved model is recorded instead of discarded.

Fixes #4716.

## Why

`ao spawn --model X` persists an empty model. `sessions.model` is written as `''` and `GET /api/v1/sessions` omits the field, so nothing can report which model a session resolved to.

`session_manager` builds the spawn metadata with `Model: resolvedModelForMetadata(...)` and hands it to `MarkSpawned`, which does `rec.Metadata = mergeMetadata(rec.Metadata, metadata)`. `seedRecord` never sets `Model`, so the base side is empty; `mergeMetadata` copies seventeen fields by explicit allowlist and `Model` is not one of them, so the empty base wins.

This is the hazard the package already warns about. `TestMarkSpawnedPersistsChatControllerFacts` says it plainly:

> mergeMetadata is an explicit allowlist, so a field added to SessionMetadata without a line here is silently dropped on every spawn and restore. That happened to the chat resume handle ... nothing failed loudly, the column was just empty.

`Model` is the same omission one field over.

## How

One line, in the `set` (copy-if-non-empty) group rather than an unconditional assignment: a relaunch that resolves no explicit model must leave the recorded value alone. That is the opposite of the neighbouring `ControllerGeneration`, which is assigned precisely because rotation is the point — the test covers both directions.

**Scope — deliberately narrow.** This is a record/read-back fix, not a launch fix. The agent already started with the correct model; `session_manager` passes the adapter its own resolved config, and `Metadata.Model` exists for the API view. Its only readers are the session DTO (`httpd/controllers/sessions.go`) and the `sessions.model` column (`storage/sqlite/store/session_store.go`), so no session has been running the wrong model — AO just forgot which one it picked.

I have not audited the rest of `SessionMetadata` for further allowlist gaps in this PR. If you would like that swept as a follow-up, say so and I will do it separately rather than widen this one.

## Testing

`TestMarkSpawnedPersistsResolvedModel` asserts both halves: the resolved model reaches storage, and a later relaunch resolving none leaves it intact. It is committed **before** the fix so the failure is in the history:

```
manager_test.go:3711: model = "", want "sonnet"; a spawn's resolved model must survive the merge
```

Verified against a real daemon on an isolated data dir, before and after:

```
ao spawn --project demo --harness claude-code --model sonnet

before   sessions.model = ''          GET /api/v1/sessions -> model absent
after    sessions.model = 'sonnet'    GET /api/v1/sessions -> model='sonnet'
```

`go test -race ./internal/lifecycle/...` passes. Full backend suite: 161 packages pass. Three failures on my machine are pre-existing and unrelated to this change, all reproducing on a clean `main` checkout — `TestCopilotClassicPATIsNotAnAuthorizationSignal` (fails whenever a classic GitHub PAT is in the environment) and `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` / `TestAttachmentStreamsRealTmuxPane` (both `base-index`, #4222).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

body:
Fixes #4728

## Summary

Implements native Linux PTY host support, mirroring the macOS (`darwin`) implementation.

### Changes
1. **Linux PTY Spawner (`spawn_linux.go`)**: Launches `ao pty-host <sessionID> <cwd> <argv...>` detached (`Setsid: true`), streaming stdout for `READY:<pid> <port>` and writing stderr to a temporary log file for startup diagnostics.

## What

Keep release discovery active for the selected stable or nightly channel even when automatic downloading is disabled, and expose the available update directly in the sidebar.

The sidebar now presents the available, downloading, ready-to-restart, and repeated-check-failure states using the AO visual language. Available releases include a plain dismiss action that hides only that version for 24 hours; a newer version appears immediately.

## Why

Users who disable automatic updates currently receive no background release discovery and can miss updates unless they visit Settings and check manually. The sidebar should make the selected channel actionable without requiring users to know where update settings live.

## How

- Separate release discovery from automatic downloading: stable checks hourly and nightly checks every 15 minutes, while `enabled` controls only `autoDownload`.
- Preserve the existing stable/nightly/feature feed configuration and serialized updater operation boundaries.
- Persist a fail-open, per-version sidebar dismissal in local storage with a 24-hour expiry.
- Make the available row download on click, retain download progress and restart actions, and offer retry after repeated automatic-check failures.

title: fix(cloud): preserve Coder workspace state across resume
body:
## Stack

- Stacked on #4624 (`ao/agent-orchestrator-211/coder-sandbox-provider`).
- This is a baseline blocker that must merge into #4624's source branch before #4624 can land.
- Keep this PR in draft; do not merge it directly to `main` or mark it ready while the parent integration is still under review.

Fixes #4731.

## Summary

- add a required, validated `AO_CLOUD_CODER_DURABLE_ROOT` template contract and persist the Coder owner, template, parameters, selected agent, and root in each session plan
- resolve every Coder reconcile/recovery operation from that durable session profile while retaining only the deployment-scoped connection credential
- reject workspace owner, deterministic name, or template mismatches during create, `FindBySession`, persisted-ID lookup, and bootstrap before worker credentials can be uploaded
- derive the repository, AO worker data, repository credential helper, `HOME`, Claude config, and Codex home from the provider-specific durable root while preserving the existing `/workspace` layout for other providers
- require a real non-symlink mount, write a session identity marker on first bootstrap, and fail closed after stop/start if the marker is missing or belongs to another session
- wait for PTY shell readiness, retry transient pre-ready closes, await the post-upload bootstrap result, and verify the detached worker remains alive so setup/launch failures reach the reconciler instead of being reported as success
- make Codex honor the configured durable `CODEX_HOME`
- extend focused tests and the opt-in live Coder lifecycle test to verify repository, Claude, Codex, restore-marker, session-profile authority, and mismatch behavior

## Template and configuration requirements

- Set `AO_CLOUD_CODER_DURABLE_ROOT` to the approved template's exact persistent-volume mount point; AO does not assume `/home/coder`.
- The path must be absolute, normalized, non-root, no longer than 1024 bytes, and free of control characters.
- The path must exist in each workspace as a non-symlink mount point and the template must provide `mountpoint`.
- Configure `AO_CLOUD_CODER_OWNER` as the canonical owner name returned by Coder, not an alias such as `me`.
- The mount must survive Coder `stop` then `start`; run the documented `TestLiveLifecycle` gate against the exact template/root before enabling idle pause.
- Hosted `coder` Secrets Manager JSON now requires `durable_root`; deployment validation fails closed when it is absent or unsafe.

## Verification

- `cd cloud && go vet ./...`
- `cd cloud && go test -race ./...`

No ECS or shared AO staging service deployment was performed.

## Risk / rollout

title: bug(daemon): reconcileLive silently ignores sessions with empty WorkspacePath, leaving them permanently stuck
body:
## What happened

After a daemon restart (app update), a previously working orchestrator session shows:

- **"The agent controller stopped"** banner with "Resume agent" / "Open shell" buttons
- **"Session is missing runtime or workspace handles (SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE)"** when clicking Resume
- **"Session workspace is not available"** in the topbar editor button area
- **"The controller is not connected"** as the composer placeholder

The session is permanently stuck. Deleting the workspace project and re-adding the same folder does not fix it because the orphaned session row persists in the database.

*(screenshot attached in comment below)*

## Reproduction

1. Add a repository as a workspace folder and spawn an orchestrator session.
2. Update AO (or force-kill the daemon mid-flight to simulate a crash).
3. Reopen the desktop app.
4. The orchestrator session shows all four error symptoms above.
5. Click "Resume agent". It fails with SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE.
6. Delete the workspace from AO and re-add it. The broken session still appears.

## Root cause

The session's `Metadata.WorkspacePath` is empty. This can happen when:
- The daemon crashed or was killed between `store.CreateSession` and `lcm.MarkSpawned` during spawn.
- A Chat controller launch failed after the seed row was created but before workspace metadata was persisted.

On daemon restart, `reconcileLive` (`manager.go:2246`) checks for empty handles and returns nil without doing anything:

```go
if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || (rec.Metadata.Branch == "" && projectKind != domain.ProjectKindScratch) {
    return nil
}
```

The session stays non-terminated, no controller starts, no cleanup runs. It sits in limbo forever.

`SaveAndTeardownAll` (`manager.go:2140`) has the same silent skip:

```go
if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || rec.Metadata.Branch == "" {
    continue
}
```

## Three distinct bugs

1. **`reconcileLive` does not terminate sessions with empty handles.** It should call `m.lcm.MarkTerminated(ctx, rec.ID)` instead of returning nil. (`manager.go:2246`)
2. **`SaveAndTeardownAll` skips sessions with empty handles without terminating them.** Same fix needed. (`manager.go:2140`)
3. **No startup sweep for spawn-orphaned rows.** If a spawn was interrupted, the half-initialized session row survives daemon restarts indefinitely. Startup should identify and terminate (or delete) these rows.

## Error chain (code references)

| UI symptom | Backend source | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| "The agent controller stopped" | `ChatWorkspace.tsx:897` | `controller.state === "stopped"` |
| "SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE" on Resume | `service/session/service.go:916` mapping `ErrIncompleteHandle` | `ResumeAgentWithMode` guard at `manager.go:1629` finds `WorkspacePath == ""` |
| "Session workspace is not available" | `service/session/workspace_location.go:28` | `WorkspacePath` empty or path doesn't exist on disk |
| "The controller is not connected" | `ChatComposer.tsx:568` | Composer disabled when `controller.state === "stopped"` |

## Suggested fix

In `reconcileLive`, terminate instead of ignoring:

```go
if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || (rec.Metadata.Branch == "" && projectKind != domain.ProjectKindScratch) {
    m.logger.Warn("reconcile: terminating session with incomplete handles",
        "sessionID", rec.ID, "workspacePath", rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath, "branch", rec.Metadata.Branch)
    return m.lcm.MarkTerminated(ctx, rec.ID)
}
```

Same pattern in `SaveAndTeardownAll`.

## Verification query

```sql
SELECT id, is_terminated, metadata FROM sessions
WHERE json_extract(metadata, '$.workspacePath') = ''
   OR json_extract(metadata, '$.workspacePath') IS NULL;
```

## Related issues

- #3649 — spawn-time `INTERNAL_ERROR` leaving orphaned worktrees (same `SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE` symptom, different trigger: spawn atomicity)
- #4700 — Restart leaving project without a working orchestrator (different trigger: restart timeout)
- #4531 — transient "workspace unavailable" flash on new sessions (frontend caching race, self-recovers)

## Environment

- macOS (darwin arm64)
- AO desktop app, latest build
- Workspace-type project with previously working orchestrator

title: fix(chat): finalize plans on successful turns
body:
## What

Finalize every remaining structured plan step when a conversation turn settles successfully, and add migration 0119 to repair completed turns that already persisted a stale non-terminal plan.

## Why

A provider can emit an initial `turn.plan` and then finish with `turn.completed` without sending a terminal plan update. AO previously stored the completed answer and turn state while leaving the plan at `0/N` or partially pending.

Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4663

## How

- Treat successful turn completion as the terminal durable fact for the turn plan.
- Update the turn plan and matching plan activity in the same transaction.
- Preserve the raw provider-event archive.
- Do not infer completion for failed, interrupted, recovered, or cancelled turns.
- Backfill only stale plans attached to already-completed turns.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/service/chat ./internal/storage/sqlite ./internal/storage/sqlite/store -count=1`

title: feat: update copy now AO Mobile is live on both stores
body:
AO Mobile is live on the App Store and Google Play, so every surface that
described a beta needed to change. Most of this is subtraction: the pre-launch
copy existed to explain multi-step workarounds that no longer exist.

**34 files, +674 / −1133.**

## Landing

The download page had two install funnels to explain — TestFlight (install
Apple's app, accept an invite) and an Android closed test (join a Google Group,
opt in, then install). Both are now one tap on a public listing, so the
walkthroughs are deleted rather than reworded, along with their phone-specific
sheets: a sheet whose job was to say "tap this other button" is pure friction
once the button goes straight to the store.

One shared `StoreQRDialog` replaces all five components. On a phone the badge
links directly to the listing; on a desktop it opens a QR, because the app
cannot install on the machine the visitor is reading this on. That handoff is
the only part of the old flow worth keeping.

The badges are Apple's and Google's own artwork, which their identity
guidelines require — the hand-drawn recreation this started with violated both
while also losing the recognition that makes a badge worth using. Their wording
differs ("Download on the" vs "Get it on") because each guideline fixes its
own; that mismatch is deliberate, not an oversight.

## Desktop — Connect Mobile

The iOS side still described a TestFlight beta. Pointing it at the App Store
made it identical to the Android side, which let the two branches collapse into
one and set off a chain of simplifications:

- **The platform dropdown is gone.** It never reached the pairing QR — the
  payload is built with `platform: ""`, and that field carries the desktop's OS,
  not the phone's — so all it selected was which of two store links to show.
  Step one now names both, each with its own hover QR.
- **The LAN step is gone.** `qrIsReady` withholds the code until the tunnel
  resolves, precisely so a scannable code always carries a tunnel endpoint, and
  the phone races every advertised endpoint. "Put your phone on the same Wi-Fi"
  contradicted a guarantee the panel already enforces, and the case where it is
  true (no cloudflared) has its own notice. Tailscale keeps its step — there,
  installing it really is a prerequisite.
- **`mobile.description` loses "over your LAN"** for the same reason, with no
  replacement qualifier: "from anywhere" would be wrong whenever the connector
  is missing.

All eight locales updated, mirroring each one's existing Google Play phrasing.
Store names stay untranslated as brand marks; the storefront name survives in
the aria labels for screen readers.

## Mobile app

The push-registration failure named an internal cause the person holding the
phone can do nothing with ("this build has no push entitlement") and sent them
to TestFlight. It now names the fix. `openStore`'s `itms-beta://` fallback
points at the real listing.

## Needs a decision before merge

**The connection-method picker (LAN/Tailscale) is commented out, not deleted**,
in three linked places so it restores as one unit. This also takes the
**secure-pairing toggle** off-screen, which iPhone-over-Tailscale requires —
iOS refuses cleartext to `100.x` addresses, and the TLS MagicDNS host is
deliberately not in the QR. LAN and tunnel paths are unaffected. The seven
tests that reached Tailscale through that picker are skipped with a matching
note rather than rewritten to bypass the UI, so they restore alongside it.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 15 suites, 99 passed / 7 skipped; mobile lib 70 passed
- Rendered on iPhone 13 and Pixel 7 viewports: no horizontal overflow, correct
  per-device badge behaviour (own store = direct link, other store = QR)

## Noted separately

On a phone the **cookie consent banner covers the store badges** on first load
— it buries the primary CTA on the page people arrive at to download the app.
Pre-existing and out of scope here, but worth its own fix.

title: bug(projects): same-basename folders at different paths collide on derived project id — desktop creation dead-ends on ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED
body:
## Bug
Registering two projects whose folders share the same basename (e.g. `~/work/api` and `~/clients/api`) fails on the second registration with an **ID conflict** — the desktop UI shows a generic "create failed" error with no path forward.

**Source:** Discord #bug-triage (Vansh), 2026-09-01 | **Reported by:** Vansh
**Analyzed against:** `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator@9997248c4` (origin/main tip)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced end-to-end
**Priority:** high — core flow (project creation) dead-ends in the UI with no in-product workaround

## Reproduction
1. Register a project for a git repo at `~/work/api` (desktop: Create Project flow, or `ao project add --path ~/work/api`). Succeeds; project id = `api`.
2. Register a second project at `~/clients/api` (same folder basename, different parent).
3. Desktop: creation fails with a generic error — no explanation, no suggested id, no retry path. Raw daemon response is `409 ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED`.

## Root Cause

Two layers combine to produce the dead-end:

**1. Daemon — project ids are derived from the folder *basename*, not the full path.**

`defaultProjectID` (`backend/internal/service/project/service.go:867` at `9997248c4`; was `:835` at `ed52364e3`):

```go
func defaultProjectID(path string) domain.ProjectID {
	id := strings.ToLower(filepath.Base(path))
	id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
	id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, " ", "-")
	return domain.ProjectID(id)
}
```

Two distinct paths → identical derived id. `Add()` then rejects the second registration at `service.go:204`:

```go
} else if ok && existing.ArchivedAt.IsZero() && existing.Path != path {
	return Project{}, apierr.Conflict("ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED", "A project with this id is already registered for a different path", map[string]any{
		"existingProjectId":  existing.ID,
		"suggestedProjectId": string(m.suggestID(ctx, id)),
	})
}
```

The daemon already computes an escape hatch — `suggestID` (`service.go:734`) returns `api1`-style suffixed candidates and returns it in `suggestedProjectId` — but it is only embedded in the error details.

**2. Desktop UI — the suggestion is dropped and no custom-id input exists.**

- `createProject` in `frontend/src/renderer/lib/shell-context.ts:11` accepts only `path`, agents, tracker intake, `asWorkspace` — **there is no field to pass a `projectId`**, so the UI can never avoid or resolve the collision.
- `projectSheetError` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx:65`) has tailored cases for `PROJECT_PATH_NOT_REPO_ROOT`, `PROJECT_BARE_REPOSITORY`, `UNSUPPORTED_GIT_REPO` — `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (and `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`) fall through to the generic "createFailedTitle / tryAgain" default. Grep of `frontend/src` for `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED` / `suggestedProjectId`: **zero matches**.

So the user hits a hard dead-end: the daemon knows the fix (`api1`), the UI never shows it, and the UI has no id field to apply it manually.

## Workaround
CLI supports explicit ids (desktop does not):

```bash
ao project add --path ~/clients/api --id api2
```

(`--id` flag: `backend/internal/cli/project.go:268`.)

## Fix Direction
Two candidate approaches (can combine):

1. **UI (minimum viable):** add an `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED` case to `projectSheetError` that surfaces "a project named X already exists" + the `suggestedProjectId` from the error details, with a one-tap "use `api1`" retry. Mirror for `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (see #4403).
2. **Daemon (structural):** make collision resolution automatic — on `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED` for a derived (not user-supplied) id, transparently register under `suggestID()`'s candidate instead of erroring (display name still defaults to the basename, so both projects *display* as "api" but have distinct ids). User-supplied ids should keep the explicit conflict error.

## Impact
- Any user with same-named folders at different paths — common with `api`, `frontend`, `backend`, client/project dirs.
- Desktop flow is a dead-end; only CLI users who know about `--id` can escape.
- Same-basename dirs also collide with display assumptions elsewhere (session prefixes derive from id — `sessionPrefix`, `service.go`).

## Related
- #4403 — the mirror conflict: same *path* re-import dead-ends on `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED` with no "go to that project" option. Same UX gap class, different trigger.
- #4479 — dotted-basename project ids (`memron.ai`) rejected by ConPTY on Windows; same `defaultProjectID` derivation, different failure mode.

title: fix(chat): refresh ACP history during TUI-to-Chat transition
body:
Fixes #4681

## Problem

ACP-backed sessions could fail immediately when switching from TUI to Chat if the first native-history replay had not yet reached the transition checkpoint. ACP exposed only a history reader, so the controller treated the snapshot as non-refreshable and returned `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`.

## Root cause

During TUI-to-Chat transition, the session manager stops the source TUI, commits the target controller epoch, and asks Chat to resume the same provider conversation with native history required. ACP's `Resume` opens the target connection and performs one `session/load`; the adapter captured that replay into an immutable slice. If Claude Code's durable transcript had not yet exposed AO's latest completed-turn checkpoint, `controller.readNativeHistory` correctly rejected the stale prefix. Because ACP did not implement `ChatHistoryRefresher`, the capability-based retry path from #4123 failed immediately instead of making another provider observation.

ACP `session/load` is repeatable for the same session ID: it resolves the existing session and replays that session's durable history again. The live adapter retains the connection and full load request needed to repeat that observation safely. The checkpoint remains proven only by the existing completed-turn/high-water matching in the Chat controller.

This differs from:

- #4120, which corrected which AO turn states may anchor the replay high-water mark;
- #4123, which introduced capability-based refresh and intentionally fast-failed ACP while its snapshot was considered immutable;
- #4424, which concerns unscoped checkpoint provenance/recovery and is unchanged here.

## Fix

Return a small `refreshableConversation` wrapper only for ACP agents that advertise `session/load`. It stores the exact initial load request and serializes repeated loads on the already-resumed ACP connection. `RefreshHistory` issues a new `session/load`, captures the new provider replay, and then exposes that snapshot to the existing controller checkpoint logic.

This is not polling the cached `historyEvents` slice: every refresh crosses the ACP protocol and causes another provider transcript observation. Resume-only ACP agents remain non-refreshable.

## Safety

- preserves history-completeness and checkpoint checks unchanged
- keeps the source TUI session intact through the existing rollback path on failure
- reloads the existing provider session; it does not create a replacement conversation
- regenerates stable provider event IDs, so identical replay prefixes remain idempotent and the existing projector deduplication remains effective
- uses the existing bounded controller retry/timeout and propagates context cancellation
- creates no target Chat controller until native history is accepted
- adds no harness-name conditional to service code and changes no Codex behavior

## Tests

Passed:

- regression-first proof: `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp -run TestACPDriverRefreshesHistoryWithAnotherSessionLoad -count=1` failed before implementation because ACP did not advertise refreshable history
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/... -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/... ./internal/service/chat/... ./internal/session_manager/... -count=1` (ACP and Chat packages passed; session-manager Windows baseline failures noted below)
- `go test ./internal/session_manager -run InterfaceTransition -count=1`
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/... ./internal/service/chat/... -count=1`
- `go test -race ./internal/session_manager -run InterfaceTransition -count=1`
- `go vet ./...`
- pinned golangci-lint against the diff: `... golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs --new-from-rev=origin/main --timeout=10m` — 0 issues

The final test-only assertion proving a third identical replay performs another wire `session/load` passed in the normal ACP suite. A post-assertion race rerun could not start after Windows cleaned the temporary checksum-verified Go/MinGW toolchain; the race suite above passed with the same production implementation.

Repository-wide Windows limitations:

- `npm run lint` and its `go test ./...` step encounter existing POSIX-path, shell/tmux, symlink-privilege, `/tmp`, and environment-sensitive test failures on Windows.
- The representative session-manager failures were reproduced in a clean `origin/main` worktree at `9aadfc8ae` with the same results.
- Running pinned golangci-lint globally on Windows reported 1,033 baseline findings (1,022 repository-wide goimports reports plus existing Windows errcheck/gosec findings) and timed out; diff-only lint reports 0 issues.

No live Claude Code/ACP provider validation was performed; coverage is deterministic fake-provider replay plus code-path verification.

## Intentional omissions

- No change to #4424's unscoped-checkpoint behavior.
- No controller timeout, replay-completeness, error-mapping, migration, frontend, or Codex app-server change.
- No retry by rereading an immutable cached snapshot and no arbitrary sleep.

title: [Bug]: codexappserver conformance test fails when the installed Codex is older than the pinned ProviderVersion
body:
### Summary

`go test ./...` fails on a clean checkout when the Codex installed locally is older than the version the checked in protocol file was generated from. Nothing in AO is actually broken. The test cannot tell the difference between "someone added a method that does not exist" and "this developer has an older Codex build".

`TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` compares the generated method table in `codexproto/protocol.gen.go` against the schema that the `codex` binary on PATH emits. It treats the two directions differently:

| Direction | Handling | Line |
|---|---|---|
| Installed provider has methods the generated file lacks | `t.Logf`, test passes | `conformance_test.go:202` |
| Generated file has methods the installed provider lacks | `t.Errorf`, test fails | `conformance_test.go:209` |

Failing on the second case is correct when the generated file has genuinely drifted, because calling a method the provider does not have breaks at runtime. But the same condition is also true when the generated file is fine and the developer simply has an older Codex, which is not a defect.

The test is already tolerant of an unusable environment. It skips when `codex` is not installed (`conformance_test.go:169-171`) and when the provider refuses to emit a schema (`conformance_test.go:176-177`). Being strict only in the "installed Codex is older" case looks like something that was missed rather than a decision.

`protocol.gen.go` pins `ProviderVersion = "codex-cli 0.146.0"` and has been regenerated once, in [PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472). Codex keeps releasing, so the distance between the pinned version and whatever a contributor has installed grows over time.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a Codex CLI older than the pinned `ProviderVersion`. I have `codex-cli 0.142.5` and the file pins `codex-cli 0.146.0`.
2. Clone the repo and check out current `main`.
3. From `backend/`, run the documented local gate:
   ```
   go test ./...
   ```
4. Or run just the one test:
   ```
   go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/ -run TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider
   ```

### Expected behavior

A contributor whose Codex is simply an older build should not get a red suite. The test should separate the two causes. One way is to compare the installed provider version against `codexproto.ProviderVersion` and skip or log when the installed build is older, the same way the test already skips when Codex is absent, while still failing when the versions line up and the generated file has actually drifted.

### Actual behavior

The test fails at `conformance_test.go:209`:

```
--- FAIL: TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider (0.84s)
    conformance_test.go:209: generated protocol declares 5 method(s) the installed
    provider does not: [externalAgentConfig/import/recordHistory
    thread/environment/connected thread/environment/disconnected
    app/installed app/read]
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver	0.843s
```

![conformance test failing against codex-cli 0.142.5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mukulkatewa/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-conformance-older-provider/.issue-assets/codex-conformance-older-provider/conformance-fail.png)

`go test ./...` is what `docs/development.md` and `docs/STATUS.md` present as the local gate, and `npm run lint` runs `go test ./...` as well. So a new contributor running the documented command for the first time sees a failure that has nothing to do with their changes.

### AO version

`0.10.3`, commit `92990fd3`, current `main` at time of filing.

### Environment

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS x86_64, kernel 6.14.0-37, Go 1.26.5, `codex-cli 0.142.5`

### Logs / extra context

```shell
$ codex --version
codex-cli 0.142.5

$ grep "ProviderVersion =" internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/codexproto/protocol.gen.go
const ProviderVersion = "codex-cli 0.146.0"

$ go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/ -run TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider
--- FAIL: TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider (0.84s)
    conformance_test.go:209: generated protocol declares 5 method(s) the installed provider does not: [externalAgentConfig/import/recordHistory thread/environment/connected thread/environment/disconnected app/installed app/read]
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver	0.843s
FAIL
```

The method names print in a different order on each run because Go iterates a map. The set itself is stable.

title: test(codexappserver): tolerate a provider older than the generated protocol
body:
## What

Makes `TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` version aware. When the installed Codex is older than the build `protocol.gen.go` was generated from, the missing methods are reported with `t.Logf` instead of failing the test. When the installed build is not older, the existing `t.Errorf` is unchanged.

Fixes #4773.

## Why

`go test ./...` fails on a clean checkout for anyone whose Codex predates the pinned `ProviderVersion`, and nothing in the checkout is wrong.

The test compares the generated method table against the schema the installed `codex` emits, then splits the result two ways. A provider that declares methods the generated file lacks is only logged, because AO does not have to use everything. A generated file that declares methods the provider lacks is failed, because calling one of those breaks at runtime.

That second rule is right when the generated file has drifted. The problem is that an older provider produces exactly the same condition without anything having drifted: every method a later Codex added is a method the older build does not declare. The test could not tell the two apart, so it reported a version gap as a defect.

The test is already deliberate about not failing on an environment it cannot use. It skips when `codex` is absent and when the provider refuses to emit a schema. Failing only in the "your Codex is older" case was the gap.

This is not a rare state. `protocol.gen.go` pins `codex-cli 0.146.0` and has been regenerated once, in #3472, while Codex keeps releasing. My machine has `codex-cli 0.142.5` and reports five methods. `go test ./...` is what `docs/development.md` and `docs/STATUS.md` present as the local gate, and `npm run lint` runs it too, so this is the first command a new contributor runs.

## How

Test-only change. No production code is touched.

The comparison already exists in this package, so nothing new was introduced: `parseCodexVersion` and `codexVersion.less` in `driver.go` do the work. The new `providerOlderThanGenerated` helper only joins them and decides the one question the test needs answered.

Unparseable output on either side returns false and keeps the strict comparison. A version that cannot be read is not evidence that the gap is benign, so the safe direction is to keep failing rather than to quietly pass.

The version is read with `exec.Command(bin, "--version")` to match how this file already invokes the provider, rather than `installedCodexVersion`, which carries the driver's process environment that a schema comparison does not need.

The two `len(extra) > 0` arms are a `switch` rather than a nested `if` so the strict path stays visible at the same level as the tolerant one.

## Testing

```
go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/ -run TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider -v
```

Before this change, on `codex-cli 0.142.5`:

```
--- FAIL: TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider (0.84s)
    conformance_test.go:209: generated protocol declares 5 method(s) the installed provider does not: [...]
FAIL
```

After:

```
=== RUN   TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider
    conformance_test.go:220: installed provider (codex-cli 0.142.5) predates the generated "codex-cli 0.146.0", so it does not declare 5 method(s) this file has; update codex or regenerate to compare them: [...]
--- PASS: TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider (0.91s)
```

`TestProviderOlderThanGenerated` covers the decision directly: older, equal, newer, and unreadable version output on either side.

I could not verify the strict path against a real Codex at or above `0.146.0`, since the only build available to me is older. The equal and newer cases are covered by the table test, and that path is unchanged from the current behavior.

Also run: `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet` clean, full `go test ./...`.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(settings): render the pairing QR dark-on-light so Android can scan it
body:
## The bug

The pairing QR could not be scanned by the AO Android app. It scanned fine from iOS, from Android's system camera, and from Google Lens — which is why it read as a flaky per-device camera problem rather than a rendering bug, and why it survived this long.

`StyledQRCode` took its colour from `--color-text-settings-title` over a `transparent` background. In the dark theme that renders **light modules on dark** — an inverted code.

Apple's AVFoundation and Google Lens both decode inverted codes. The bundled `com.google.mlkit:barcode-scanning` that `expo-camera` uses on Android does not. So the code was readable by every scanner except our own app's.

## How it was isolated

A single-variable sweep, scanned in the AO app on a device that reproduced the failure. Module size, logo size and finder shape were each held constant so only one factor varied at a time, with a known-failing and a known-passing control bracketing the round:

| variant | polarity | logo | finders | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (control) | inverted | 0.45 | round | fail |
| V1 | inverted | 0.25 | round | fail |
| V2 | inverted | **none** | round | fail |
| V3 | inverted | 0.45 | **square** | fail |
| V5 | inverted | 0.25 | square | fail |
| V4 | **light** | 0.45 | round | pass |
| V6 | **light** | 0.25 | square | pass |
| V7 (control) | **light** | 0.25 | square | pass |

Every inverted variant failed; every dark-on-light variant passed. Nothing else predicted the outcome.

This rules out the plausible suspects: **not** the logo (V2 has none and still fails), **not** finder shape (V3 fails), **not** module size (V6 passes at the original 240px panel), and **not** the device (its system camera reads all of these).

## The fix

Render dark-on-light with an opaque background. The logo, rounded dots, round finder corners and EC level M are all left alone — the sweep showed none of them mattered.

Because `StyledQRCode` is shared, this also fixes the TestFlight and Play Store QRs, which were equally unreadable on that device.

## Also included

**Quiet zone measured in modules, not as a fraction of rendered size.** Modules are the unit a scanner reads clearance in, and a short payload has fewer, larger modules — so a percentage tuned on the long pairing code left the small store codes badly short:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Pairing (v18) | 4.0 | 4.0 |
| Pairing (v23, long payload) | 3.1 | 4.1 |
| Play Store (v5) | **2.4** | 4.2 |
| TestFlight (v3) | **1.9** | 4.3 |

The pairing QR hit the required 4 modules by coincidence. The store codes — the ones people scan to install the app — did not.

**Panel 240px → 320px, and the code fills its card.** Not required for the fix. The card was insetting the code on top of the quiet zone `StyledQRCode` already draws, stacking two margins and shrinking the modules for nothing. Removing the inset halves the white border *and* takes a full-length payload from 0.47mm to 0.66mm per module, so it scans at arm's length instead of needing the phone against the screen.

## Verification

- **Paired a real Android and a real iOS device** against a dev daemon; both completed the full `identity` → `endpoints` → `push/devices` handshake and went on to poll sessions and events.
- Every code type (pairing at 516/652/780 chars, Play Store, TestFlight, placeholder) decodes, rendered from the component's own constants.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; 80 tests pass across 15 files.

## Follow-ups, not in this PR

- **Payload length is unbounded.** It grows with endpoint count and hostname length, so some machines get a denser code than others. A CI assertion capping the QR version for a representative payload would stop this silently regressing — which is how the original problem arrived.
- **A slim v3 pairing format** (516 → ~267 chars, v18 → v12) is the real structural win for weak cameras, but it is a wire-format change: `parsePairingCode` hard-rejects any version but `2`, so it needs sequencing with a mobile release.
- **Upstream `expo-camera` bug:** `startFocusMetering()` builds its metering point at `createPoint(1f, 1f)` — the bottom-right corner, not the centre (`ExpoCameraView.kt:640`). Dormant today because the pair screen never sets `autofocus`, but it will bite whoever enables it.

title: feat(cloud): full Docker-local sandbox testing (no NodeOps)
body:
## What

Makes the **entire AO cloud flow runnable on local Docker** — orchestrator/worker sessions, terminals, repo checkout, agent launch, browser panel — with **zero NodeOps sandboxes and zero credits burned**. The Docker sandbox *provider* was already implemented; this closes the two real gaps: **local bring-up tooling** and **desktop-app local auth**.

Combines two pieces (cherry-picked, disjoint files):

### Phase A — one-command local bring-up
- New `cloud/scripts/cloud-local-up.sh`: interactive, stays-up (no self-teardown), fixed loopback ports (CP `127.0.0.1:8081`, PG `54329`), persists stable keys under `~/.ao/cloud/` so `down`/`reset` match, builds the worker + CP images, `docker compose up`, waits for `/readyz`, and prints the desktop launch hint.
- Restored the missing `cloud:local` / `:down` / `:reset` / `:smoke` / `cloud:staging` npm aliases (lost in the #4434 vendoring).
- Fixed stale docs (Docker provider is shipped; corrected the removed `:3000` UI claim + submodule note).

### Phase B — Electron dev-mode local auth (the real unlock)
- The desktop app only spoke WorkOS; the local Docker CP runs `AO_CLOUD_LOCAL_AUTH` and accepts only email/password `/auth/local/*` opaque tokens. Added a **dev-only, loopback-gated** local-auth path: `cloud-auth-local.ts` (register/login/logout + one gate predicate), routed `getCloudSession`/`getCloudAccessToken` to return the local opaque token (so the CP proxy and ticketed terminal WS authorize unchanged), a shadcn sign-in dialog, IPC/preload wiring, and i18n across all 8 catalogs.
- **Gate:** permitted only when unpackaged (or `AO_CLOUD_LOCAL_AUTH_DEV=1`) **and** the CP host is loopback — enforced authoritatively in the IPC handlers and again before any fetch, so an email/password can never be sent to a remote host. WorkOS path untouched.

## Testing — E2E verified on real Docker, no NodeOps

Ran the full flow against a live Docker-backed CP (`cloud-local-up.sh` → `/readyz` 200):
```
register (local-auth) → ao_local_ opaque token       ✓
credential connect → project (public repo) → session ✓
Docker worker container spawned                      ✓
session runtimeState = running                       ✓
worker: bootstrapped → anonymous checkout → repo cloned (/workspace/repository)  ✓
agent terminal: state=open, output_bytes=951         ✓   ← agent launched + producing output
```
That last line is the same milestone that was broken on staging's #4683 build (0 bytes) — here it works. Plus: Phase B's 126 renderer unit tests pass + clean typecheck; Phase A validated live (stack up/down/reset, idempotent, keys persisted 0600).

## Dev loop after this

```bash
npm run cloud:local                                   # Docker CP + workers up on 127.0.0.1:8081
cd frontend && AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on \
  AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 npm run dev
# in-app: SIGN IN with the seeded account (dev@local.test / localdevpass123)
#         → create a cloud project on a public repo → session → terminal
npm run cloud:local:down                              # stop (data retained)
```

Provider capability gaps vs NodeOps (in-place resume, idle auto-pause, public per-port ingress) are by-design and don't affect this testing flow — the browser panel proxies through the CP, and the terminal rides the CP transport, not ingress.


---

## How to test it (step by step)

1. **Bring up the Docker control plane** (builds images the first time, then reuses them):
   ```bash
   npm run cloud:local
   ```
   Waits for `/readyz` on `http://127.0.0.1:8081` and prints the launch hint. Nothing hits NodeOps.

2. **Launch the desktop app pointed at it** (dev mode — the local-auth path is gated to unpackaged + loopback):
   ```bash
   cd frontend
   AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 npm run dev
   ```

3. **Sign in — no register step needed.** `npm run cloud:local` seeds a default account after the CP is ready, and the success banner prints the credentials. The cloud sign-in opens the local email/password dialog (only under the dev+loopback gate); just use the **Sign in** tab:

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Email | `dev@local.test` |
   | Password | `localdevpass123` |

   Tokens are opaque `ao_local_…`, valid 720h.

   > The seed is best-effort and idempotent (201 creates it, 409 means it already exists — the bring-up never fails on it). The **Register** tab is still there if you want a second account; it needs email, display name, password (**≥ 12 chars**), org slug (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,62}$`), and org name.

4. **Create a cloud project on a PUBLIC repo** — e.g. `https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World` (default branch `master`). Private repos need a GitHub App and won't check out locally by design.

5. **Connect a coding-agent credential.** For just exercising the *infrastructure*, any string works (the local CP skips credential validation). For **real agent output**, paste a valid `claude setup-token` in the credentials dialog — otherwise claude launches but shows an auth prompt (the terminal still renders).

6. **Create a session** → a Docker worker container spawns (`docker ps` shows `ao-worker-…`), checks out the repo, and the **terminal renders** with the agent. Orchestrator sessions can `ao spawn` workers; the browser panel works too — all local.

7. **Tear down:**
   ```bash
   npm run cloud:local:down    # stop, keep data
   npm run cloud:local:reset   # stop + wipe the local DB
   ```

> Note: the local-auth dialog appears **only** when running from source (`npm run dev`) against a loopback CP. Packaged nightly/stable builds have `app.isPackaged = true`, so this path is off and users get WorkOS as normal.

title: fix(lifecycle): ignore stale TUI metadata for Chat activity
body:
Fixes #4696

## Problem

A structured Chat session could retain terminal runtime metadata from an older TUI ownership epoch. Chat activity signals correctly carried the current `controller_generation`, but lifecycle applied the generic `runtime_launch_id` fence first. Because Chat signals intentionally have no terminal launch id, the reducer silently discarded `chat.turn.started` and `chat.turn.completed`, leaving durable activity stuck at `idle`.

## Root cause

The SQLite activity write fence was already mode-aware: TUI writes compare `runtime_launch_id`, while Chat writes compare `controller_generation`. The in-memory lifecycle reducer was not. It applied the terminal fence to every mode before checking the optional Chat generation.

Current Chat startup already clears `runtime_launch_id` through metadata merging, and interface-transition epoch commits clear both runtime fields. However, `runtime_handle_id` was merged only when non-empty, so a legacy/recovered Chat row could retain a stale terminal handle across another successful Chat startup.

## Fix

- Make lifecycle ownership checks mode-specific:
  - TUI signals remain fenced by the current runtime launch id.
  - Chat signals must carry the exact current controller generation and ignore irrelevant stale terminal metadata.
  - controller-generation signals remain invalid for TUI mode.
- Clear stale runtime handle and launch metadata whenever a current Chat controller is successfully committed.
- Document `ControllerGeneration` as the required Chat activity ownership fence.

## Safety

- Preserves existing TUI launch-generation fencing.
- Preserves stale/foreign Chat-controller rejection and additionally rejects generationless inherited provider hooks.
- Does not infer activity, bypass the durable owner CAS, change interface-transition sequencing, or add a second activity source.
- Cleanup occurs only when a Chat controller with a non-empty generation is successfully committed; a failed controller commit leaves the previous durable owner untouched.
- CDC behavior is unchanged: the existing SQLite session update and trigger remain the only durable/event path.

## Tests

Passed locally with Go 1.26.5:

- `go test ./internal/lifecycle -run 'Test(MarkSpawnedPersistsChatControllerFacts|ActivitySignalFencesChatByControllerGenerationDespiteStaleRuntimeMetadata)$' -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/lifecycle -count=1`

The regression proves that a Chat row containing stale runtime handle/launch metadata:

- accepts `active` and `idle` from its current controller generation;
- rejects a generationless stale TUI hook even when its launch id matches the stale value;
- rejects a foreign Chat generation; and
- scrubs stale terminal ownership metadata on successful Chat startup.

Broader `internal/service/chat` and `internal/session_manager` validation was attempted with build/module/tmp caches moved to a secondary disk because the host system drive was full. Dependency preparation did not complete within a bounded 15-minute local wait under concurrent builds, so those results are not claimed; CI remains the authoritative broad run. A focused `go vet ./internal/lifecycle` attempt likewise did not complete within the bounded local wait.

## Related scope

PR #4204 / issue #4125 address the separate sticky-`exited` resurrection and controller shutdown ordering problem. This PR deliberately does not copy those controller/interrupt changes. It aligns the ownership terminology with #4204 while fixing #4696's distinct ordering defect: terminal launch fencing must not precede and veto current Chat generation ownership.

title: fix(renderer): bounded exponential backoff for SSE reconnects
body:
## Problem

The renderer schedules its own `EventSource` rebuild once the browser gives up (`readyState` CLOSED), and every consumer used a flat delay: 5s in `event-transport.ts` and `notifications.ts`, 5s +/- 1s in `workspace-file-events.ts`. Nothing grew the delay and nothing capped the attempts, so a stream the daemon keeps refusing knocked every ~5s indefinitely.

That is the amplification in #4323. When the daemon returns a transient 5xx during stream setup, every open session's stream fails at once and they all retry in lockstep. The retry traffic is itself what keeps the daemon from recovering, so a brief hiccup sustains itself.

## Change

New `sse-backoff.ts` with `computeSseRetryDelayMs(retries)`: doubles from 5s to a 60s ceiling, scaled by jitter in `[0.5, 1)` so streams that failed together desynchronise, with the exponent clamped so a long-dead stream cannot reach `Infinity`. All three consumers track consecutive scheduled rebuilds and reset on a successful open, so a one-off failure still reconnects fast. This mirrors the bounded backoff `main/supervisor-link.ts` already uses for the daemon links.

Two details worth calling out, both from review of the first commit here:

- The exponent is driven by a `retries` counter, not the existing `failures` counter. `workspace-file-events` also increments `failures` on non-terminal `onerror` (readyState CONNECTING, where the browser retries on its own) to drive the "degraded" label. Those are not rebuilds we scheduled, and counting them made the first real failure wait the 60s ceiling instead of ~5s, which is slower to recover than the flat delay being replaced.
- All three consumers reset the counter when the API base URL changes. A daemon that comes back on a different port is a fresh target and should not serve the delay the dead port earned. `workspace-file-events` already did this; the other two did not.

## Verification

`sse-backoff.test.ts` covers growth, the ceiling, the jitter band, reset, and non-finite input. Stream-level tests assert that each wait is longer than the last, that a successful open drops back to the initial delay, that the browser's own non-terminal retries do not inflate the delay, and that a new daemon port starts over.

Every new test was mutation-tested rather than just observed passing. Reinstating the flat delay fails 4 tests; breaking the reset-on-open fails 1; reinstating the conflated counter fails the non-terminal test; dropping either port reset fails the corresponding test.

Full renderer suite: 3389 passed. The 5 failures in `src/landing` reproduce identically on `origin/main` and are unrelated to this change. `tsc --noEmit` is clean for every file touched here.

Two existing tests hardcoded the flat 5s and now derive the expected delay from the helper.

## Scope

Renderer only. The optional daemon-side `Retry-After` from #4323 is not included.

Supersedes #4340, whose branch predates the #4388 rewrite of `workspace-file-events.ts` and no longer applies.

Refs #4323, #3963
